By simulating a range of future CDR pathways including afforestation, BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage), and biochar, we assess their technical feasibility, economic viability, and interaction with Germany’s energy and land systems. The results demonstrate that achieving high levels of negative emissions to address residual emissions in Germany requires a combination of engineered and nature-based CDR pathways rather than reliance on a single technology class. Natural sinks provide a reliable removal baseline of approximately 45 Mt CO2/year by 2050 and BECCS is the scalable lever to exceed the threshold of 60 Mt CO2 removal required for climate neutrality in Germany.

title: Metals as energy carriers: Unlocking a hydrogen economy through established logistics
summary: A future energy system centred on renewables and hydrogen requires reliable, high-density storage and cost-effective transport at scale. Metals (and metal oxides) offer a compelling pathway for a fast integration of hydrogen into a sector c
content: A future energy system centred on renewables and hydrogen requires reliable, high-density storage and cost-effective transport at scale. Metals (and metal oxides) offer a compelling pathway for a fast integration of hydrogen into a sector coupled energy system: circular energy carriers that provide safe and dispatchable energy. This review discusses the role of hydrogen in metal reduction processes for renewable energy storage, with subsequent metal oxidation delivering heat and hydrogen for industry and grids. Metal-based energy carriers could be the tipping point for integrating hydrogen into a truly global energy system by enabling safe, scalable, and cost-effective interregional transport that interconnects continents using existing bulk materials infrastructure. Five candidate metals: aluminium, iron, magnesium, silicon, and zinc are evaluated across fundamentals, production and recycling and system-level integration. The biggest identified research gaps are ensuring durability under repeated redox cycles, and achieving seamless coupling with electrolysers, industrial heat, and grid service.

title: POSSIBLE PATHWAYS FOR THE TRANSFORMATION OF COAL-FIRED THERMAL POWER PLANTS IN UKRAINE: SCENARIOS, MODELLING AND RECOMMENDATIONS
summary: This article examines possible pathways for transforming coal-fired thermal power plants (TPPs) in Ukraine in the context of European integration, post-war recovery, and climate commitments. Most Ukrainian coal-fired generating units were c
content: This article examines possible pathways for transforming coal-fired thermal power plants (TPPs) in Ukraine in the context of European integration, post-war recovery, and climate commitments. Most Ukrainian coal-fired generating units were commissioned between the 1960s and 1980s, so equipment is characterised by low efficiency, high greenhouse gas emissions, and physical deterioration. According to various estimates, in 2022–2025 up to 70–80 % of thermal generation capacity was destroyed or damaged. At the same time, thermal generation remains critically important for power system stability and balancing under increasing penetration of renewable energy sources. The study aims to perform a comparative techno-economic and environmental assessment of alternative transformation scenarios for coal-fired TPPs. Six scenarios are analysed: (A) continued operation of existing coal-fired units; (B) cofiring coal with biomass; (C) full conversion to biomass; (D) replacement with combined-cycle gas turbine (CCGT) units; (E) installation of flue-gas desulphurization and nitrogen oxides reduction systems; and (F) efficiency-oriented technical modernization. The assessment is based on a levelised cost of electricity (LCOE) model incorporating capital expenditures, fuel costs, operation and maintenance expenses, and costs associated with CO2 emissions. Publicly available statistical and analytical data from international organizations are used as input. The results indicate that CCGT units provide the lowest LCOE under current assumptions, while biomass-based scenarios ensure the most significant reduction in carbon emissions. The findings can support the development of a national strategy for the transformation of coal-fired thermal generation in Ukraine. Bibl. 24, Tab. 4.

title: Tailoring Cathode Interphase with Cyclic Ethers toward Stable Lithium‐Metal Batteries
summary: Lithium‐metal batteries (LMBs) require stable electrode–electrolyte interphases to achieve long‐term cycling stability. Ether electrolytes are attractive for LMBs due to their excellent compatibility with lithium‐metal anodes. However, the
content: Lithium‐metal batteries (LMBs) require stable electrode–electrolyte interphases to achieve long‐term cycling stability. Ether electrolytes are attractive for LMBs due to their excellent compatibility with lithium‐metal anodes. However, the influence of cyclic ether molecular structures on cathode interphase chemistry remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that cyclic ether ring structure governs ring‐opening thermodynamics and thereby regulates cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and electrochemical durability. Two representative cyclic ethers, 1,3‐dioxolane (DOL) and 1,3‐dioxane (DOX), exhibit markedly different performance in Li||LiFePO 4 and Li||NCM811 cells through distinct interfacial reaction pathways. On LiFePO 4 cathodes, DOL forms a thin LiF‐rich inorganic–organic hybrid CEI, enabling 84.6% capacity retention after 1200 cycles. By contrast, DOX delivers superior stability on high‐voltage NCM811 by forming a more stable CEI. These findings establish interfacial reactivity matching as an important design principle for ether‐based electrolytes in LMBs.

title: The Role of University Leadership in Enhancing the Concept of Sustainability among Students of the Islamic University of Madinah
source: University of Bisha Journal for Educational Sciences
summary: The study aims to identify the role of university leadership in fostering the concept of sustainability among students at the Islamic University of Madinah. Furthermore, it examines their level of awareness regarding national initiatives an
content: The study aims to identify the role of university leadership in fostering the concept of sustainability among students at the Islamic University of Madinah. Furthermore, it examines their level of awareness regarding national initiatives and university-led sustainability programs, as well as the impact of university leaders in influencing and modifying their behavior. Also, whether there were statistically significant differences between Saudi and non-Saudi students in behavior or awareness of initiatives. The research employed a descriptive survey methodology, used a questionnaire as a research tool, and was applied to a sample consisting of (325) students. The study results concluded that university leadership plays a positive and active role in promoting sustainability concepts and practices, as the general index achieved an average of (3.76), indicating a “high” evaluation level. The leadership role of the university administration in encouraging sustainable behaviors within the campus ranked second with an average of (3.81), confirming students’ conviction in the tangible practices and initiatives adopted by the leadership. The results revealed a high level of student awareness regarding university policies for rationalizing resource consumption (energy and water) in its facilities, with an average of (3.72). The researcher recommends establishing a committee or center for sustainability, integrating sustainability concepts into curricula, and enhancing student participation in activities related to sustainability.

title: Proxy-Based Identification of Heating, Ventilation, and Air-Conditioning-Related Carbon Emission Drivers in Commercial Building Energy Operation
summary: Abstract Energy conservation and carbon reduction in commercial buildings are essential for achieving carbon neutrality targets, but carbon emission drivers may change under operational disruptions. This study investigates phase-dependent H
content: Abstract Energy conservation and carbon reduction in commercial buildings are essential for achieving carbon neutrality targets, but carbon emission drivers may change under operational disruptions. This study investigates phase-dependent HVAC-related carbon emission drivers in a large shopping mall using 23 monthly observations of energy consumption and meteorological data from February 2021 to December 2022. To avoid mechanical overlap between total electricity consumption and HVAC-related carbon emissions, non-HVAC electricity consumption was constructed as a proxy for operational intensity. Four progressive regression models were developed, including a temperature-only baseline model, a proxy-augmented model, a phase-dummy model, and a phase-interaction model. The results show that the phase-interaction model achieved the best in-sample explanatory performance, with the adjusted R² increasing from 0.3705 to 0.9641 and the RMSE decreasing from 231.2226 to 49.7036 compared with the temperature-only model. The marginal effect of temperature increased from 10.3703 in the restricted phase to 26.0975 in the recovery phase, indicating a stronger temperature–HVAC carbon emission association during the recovery phase. Robustness analyses using residual diagnostics, HC3 robust standard errors, leave-one-month-out sensitivity analysis, leave-one-out cross-validation, expanding-window time-series validation, and phase-stratified bootstrap resampling supported the stability of the temperature–phase interaction, although the simpler phase-dummy model showed better strictly chronological predictive performance than the interaction model. In contrast, the non-HVAC electricity proxy and its phase interaction were not statistically significant under HC3 robust inference, indicating that the proxy-related associations were less robust and should be interpreted cautiously. The proposed framework is intended for retrospective carbon accounting and exploratory driver identification in data-constrained commercial buildings, rather than real-time HVAC control or peak-load forecasting.

title: Smart Biovoltaic System for Integrated Soil-crop-energy Management Strategies
summary: In the current global energy and environmental environment, the need for a biomass management system with renewable energy production has become a central challenge for sustainable development towards the goals of decarbonization and carbon
content: In the current global energy and environmental environment, the need for a biomass management system with renewable energy production has become a central challenge for sustainable development towards the goals of decarbonization and carbon neutrality. The transition to low-carbon energy systems, accelerated by the European Green Deal by 2050, requires innovative land use strategies that incentivize agricultural and energy production. Agrivoltaic systems are a promising solution, enabling the simultaneous generation of green energy and agricultural production on the same land surface. Furthermore, by integrating renewable energy production with sustainable agricultural practices, agrivoltaics can promote resource efficiency, soil health and carbon sequestration for a circular, climate-resilient bioeconomy. The main objective of the work is to verify through environmental monitoring (chemical-physical analysis and bioindicators) the adaptation of the soil-culture system in the presence of agrivoltaic plant, depending on the different characteristics and different plant configurations to evaluate their effects on crop growth, soil health and energy yield related to the specific site conditions.

title: Greenwashing detection using natural language processing uncovering deceptive green signaling and linguistic obfuscation
summary: Corporate sustainability communication has intensified as firms seek legitimacy amid rising stakeholder pressure and global sustainability agendas. However, the rapid growth of environmental marketing claims has increased concerns regarding
content: Corporate sustainability communication has intensified as firms seek legitimacy amid rising stakeholder pressure and global sustainability agendas. However, the rapid growth of environmental marketing claims has increased concerns regarding deceptive sustainability communication or greenwashing. This study investigates the linguistic mechanisms underlying greenwashing by decoding deceptive green signaling and linguistic obfuscation in environmental marketing claims using Natural Language Processing. Despite increasing regulatory attention, greenwashing detection remains largely reactive and subjective, relying mainly on qualitative assessments. This study examines whether linguistic patterns and institutional signals can be used to explore the feasibility of NLP- Based greenwashing classification in corporate marketing narratives. This research introduces the concept of linguistic biomarkers of greenwashing, shifting the literature from perception-based evaluation toward exploratory NLP framework for greenwashing screening while integrating Signaling Theory and Construal Level Theory. The study analyzes 91 corporate environmental marketing claims using Natural Language Processing to extract linguistic features such as lexical vagueness and sentiment. Statistical tests and a Random Forest model were applied to identify linguistic patterns and predict greenwashing probability. Basic linguistic indicators such as word count and sentiment do not significantly distinguish greenwashing from authentic claims. However, environmental certification functions as a strong costly signal separating credible sustainability communication. Greenwashing detection requires combining textual analysis with institutional credibility signals. The study provides a computational framework for detecting deceptive sustainability communication.

title: Impacts of the digital economy on industrial employment and CO2 emissions: a comparison between developed and developing countries
summary: This article assesses the impact of the digital economy on industry and the environment by comparing 15 countries (7 developed and 8 developing) over the period 2000–2021. Using the System Generalized Method of Moments (SYS-GMM), the analys
content: This article assesses the impact of the digital economy on industry and the environment by comparing 15 countries (7 developed and 8 developing) over the period 2000–2021. Using the System Generalized Method of Moments (SYS-GMM), the analysis reveals contrasting results between country groups. For developed countries, a 1% increase in ICT imports is associated with a 0.159% reduction in CO₂ emissions (p-value < 0.01) and a marginal 0.038% decrease in industrial employment (p-value < 0.10), consistent with automation-driven labor reallocation toward high-value-added sectors. In developing countries, the same 1% increase in ICT imports yields an insignificant effect on CO₂ emissions (− 0.008, p-value = 0.676) and industrial employment (− 0.016, p-value = 0.113), reflecting structural constraints including outdated energy infrastructure and limited absorptive capacity for green technologies. Industrial value-added positively influences employment in both groups, though the elasticity is higher in developed economies (0.048 vs. 0.031). The results underscore the need for developed countries to sustain investments in advanced digital infrastructure and innovation policies that accelerate the green digital transition. For developing countries, priorities should include strengthening green digital infrastructure, fostering international technology-transfer partnerships, and implementing targeted workforce retraining programs to maximize the employment and environmental co-benefits of digitalization.

title: Methanol — flexible energy and carbon vector for the achievement of the dual goals of decarbonization & carbon circularity
summary: In a world with geopolitical conflicts and uncertainties, numerous import-dependent nations are facing a dilemma in achieving a parallel carbon transition from (1) fossils to renewables, (2) a linear to a circular carbon economy, and (3) re
content: In a world with geopolitical conflicts and uncertainties, numerous import-dependent nations are facing a dilemma in achieving a parallel carbon transition from (1) fossils to renewables, (2) a linear to a circular carbon economy, and (3) reliance on imported to domestic carbon resources. Methanol could fill this critical role as both an energy and carbon vector for carbon-dependent industries. Based on the example of the German chemical industry, the potential of methanol for chemical production via chemical recycling with focus on gasification of anthropogenic (e.g. plastic-containing refuse-derived fuel and mixed plastics) and biogenic (e.g. bioresidues) carbon waste materials, as well as Power-to-X, to enable the achievement of the dual goals of decarbonization and carbon circularity is discussed. Potential opportunities and challenges of Methanol-based synthesis technologies are qualitatively assessed. With its reference to literature, this article aims to raise awareness of the untapped potential of methanol for the global sustainability transformation.

title: Zigzag Graphene Nanoribbons as a Majorana Platform
summary: Abstract Graphene nanoribbons support a variety of electronic phases that can be tuned via external stimuli. In particular, zigzag graphene nanoribbons exhibit an antiferromagnetic insulating ground state which can transition to a half-meta
content: Abstract Graphene nanoribbons support a variety of electronic phases that can be tuned via external stimuli. In particular, zigzag graphene nanoribbons exhibit an antiferromagnetic insulating ground state which can transition to a half-metallic phase under a transverse electric field or when embedded in hexagonal boron nitride. Here, we develop a simple model of a heterostructure composed of a half-metallic zigzag graphene nanoribbon coupled with an Ising superconductor. We demonstrate that an Ising superconductor's s-wave spin-singlet pairing gap component can induce a spin-triplet, odd-parity pairing gap in the half-metallic phase of the nanoribbon via proximity coupling. The resulting superconducting phase is topologically nontrivial, with gate-tunable transitions that enable the emergence of Majorana zero modes.

title: Towards Common Ground: Perspectives on Energy Transitions in Canadian Oil and Gas Producing Municipalities
summary: Abstract Oil and gas producing municipalities host Canada's highest‐emitting industries while facing economic and social risks as the country pursues carbon neutrality. Understanding how these communities envision their economic futures, an
content: Abstract Oil and gas producing municipalities host Canada's highest‐emitting industries while facing economic and social risks as the country pursues carbon neutrality. Understanding how these communities envision their economic futures, and the barriers and enablers they encounter in pursuing low‐carbon opportunities, can inform decision‐makers seeking both emissions reductions and more resilient local economies. This study engages ten municipal economic development staff in British Columbia and Alberta to capture their perspectives on transition pathways. Findings demonstrate that staff are exploring diversification but face substantial barriers, including limited staff, technical, and fiscal capacity and the absence of a coherent transition vision. Addressing these challenges requires governance transformation. We argue that transition strategies must move beyond top‐down, universal mandates and embrace more locally grounded approaches. Community‐supported, place‐relevant visions for low‐carbon transitions, co‐created with municipal actors, must be supported by integrated policy packages built on whole‐systems modalities rather than narrow green jobs or sectoral focuses.

title: Designed for a secure transition – a systematic review of supply security in energy system models
summary: While renewable electricity has gained traction, the transition to a low-carbon energy system is still subject to large uncertainties about future energy use and supply portfolios. In the light of recent disruptive events such as geopolitic
content: While renewable electricity has gained traction, the transition to a low-carbon energy system is still subject to large uncertainties about future energy use and supply portfolios. In the light of recent disruptive events such as geopolitical tensions and trade restrictions, it is evident that energy transition strategies should consider unforeseen disturbances. In this paper, we conduct a systematic review of 179 energy system modelling studies from Scopus and Web of Science based on the PRISMA guidelines. We include articles considering various aspects of energy security, focusing on large-scale system models with a long-term techno-economic design perspective. Our analysis reveals significant variation among studies in three key areas: the security aspects evaluated, the types of disruptions considered, and the methodological approaches employed. While weather variability is commonly examined, other security threats such as climate change or geopolitical disruptions receive less attention.

title: The bioremediation of some heavy metals by using of some blue green algae isolated from the Al-Gharraf River in the Al-Shatra City
summary: For this study, two blue-green algae species (Spirulina platensis and Anabaena sp.) were isolated from the Al-Gharraf River in Al-Shatra city of the Iraq in 2025, and were exposed to two types of heavy metals chromium (Cr) and lead (pb) at
content: For this study, two blue-green algae species (Spirulina platensis and Anabaena sp.) were isolated from the Al-Gharraf River in Al-Shatra city of the Iraq in 2025, and were exposed to two types of heavy metals chromium (Cr) and lead (pb) at several concentrations 1.0, 2.0, 0.25, 0.50, and 0.10 mg/l for two weeks in order to determine their capacity to accumulate.The study results indicated that the algal Spirulina platensis collected the highest amount 1.726 µg/gm dry weight for chromium element at the same treatment 2 mg/l whereas the algal Anabaena sp collected the highest amount 1.535 µg/gm dry weight for chromium element at the same treatment 2 mg/l.In contrast, the algal Spirulina platensis accumulated 0.59 µg/gm of dry Anabaena sp weight of the same element at the same treatment 2 mg/l while the algal accumulated more of the element 1.28 µg/gm of dry weight.The statistical analysis showed some significant differences between the two types of algae with respect to concentration of chromium and lead elements for the different treatments.There was also a gradient in the concentrations of the elements added between the treatments; The higher the concentration added the higher was the concentration of the heavy metals on the algal.

title: Thermodynamic regulation promotes in situ repair of oxide films in the damaged regions of 70/30 copper-nickel alloy and enhances corrosion resistance
source: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
summary: This study proposes a thermodynamically regulated in situ repair strategy for scratched regions of 70/30 copper-nickel alloy. The strategy is controlled by NiCl 2 addition. It aims to enhance the corrosion resistance of the regenerated film
content: This study proposes a thermodynamically regulated in situ repair strategy for scratched regions of 70/30 copper-nickel alloy. The strategy is controlled by NiCl 2 addition. It aims to enhance the corrosion resistance of the regenerated film and reduce the risk of localized corrosion failure. Pourbaix diagram analysis and potentiodynamic polarization tests identified NiCl 2 as the repair additive. A concentration of 0.1 wt% was determined to be optimal. Subsequently, 0.1 wt% NiCl 2 was added to a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, serving as the formation medium for the regenerated film in the scratched regions. SVET measurements show that after 216 h of immersion repair, the regenerated film in the NiCl 2 containing system exhibited significantly higher corrosion resistance than the system without NiCl 2 . Microstructural characterization indicates that NiCl 2 addition transformed the regenerated film from a conventional bilayer structure to a denser single layer structure. Its thickness was approximately twice that of the original inner protective oxide layer, with evident Ni enrichment on the outer side of the film. Combined experimental characterization and DFT calculations reveal that Ni 2+ promotes the formation of a Ni enriched protective regenerated film and enhances its barrier capability against corrosive media.

title: Hierarchical multi-market coordination of virtual power plants via multi-factor differentiated bidding
summary: With the increasing participation of distributed energy resources and the growing importance of carbon and flexibility services, virtual power plants (VPPs) require market bidding and revenue-allocation mechanisms that reflect heterogeneous
content: With the increasing participation of distributed energy resources and the growing importance of carbon and flexibility services, virtual power plants (VPPs) require market bidding and revenue-allocation mechanisms that reflect heterogeneous operating characteristics. Conventional uniform bidding cannot adequately represent differences in device cost, carbon emissions, storage intertemporal value, and peak-shaving capability. This study therefore proposes a hierarchical market–VPP coordination framework based on multi-factor differentiated bidding. The market-clearing layer determines energy procurement and clearing outcomes according to system supply–demand conditions, resource bids, and peak-shaving requirements. Given these market outcomes, the VPP-response layer optimizes internal resource dispatch, portfolio profit, and subsequent bids. The two layers are coordinated through sequential feedback of bidding and clearing information. Device output, storage opportunity cost, stepwise carbon burden, carbon-capture effects, and technically feasible peak-shaving capacity are incorporated into resource-specific bids, while a two-stage allocation mechanism transfers bidding competitiveness and system-support contributions to internal resources. Compared with the single-level benchmark, the proposed framework reduces market procurement cost by 3.43% while improving VPP profit and controllable-resource revenue. Under the complete multi-factor bidding scenario, total CO 2 emissions decrease by 19.52%. In addition, differentiated bidding improves the revenue position of controllable units such as gas turbines in the tested cases. Profile-perturbation and scalability analyses further indicate consistent economic, low-carbon, and computational performance under the tested conditions.

title: Pomegranate peel-derived Cu/hydrochar nanocomposites: a sustainable catalyst for biodiesel production via oleic acid esterification
summary: Abstract Transforming pomegranate peel waste into a biodiesel catalyst advances waste-to-resource circularity. A facile hydrothermal carbothermal reduction method was used to synthesize copper-decorated hydrochar nanocomposites derived from
content: Abstract Transforming pomegranate peel waste into a biodiesel catalyst advances waste-to-resource circularity. A facile hydrothermal carbothermal reduction method was used to synthesize copper-decorated hydrochar nanocomposites derived from peel bio-waste and CuSO 4 , with Cu(II) concentrations of 10, 25, and 50 mmol/L (denoted as Cu10/HC, Cu25/HC, and Cu50/HC, respectively). The physicochemical properties of the nanocomposites were characterized by FTIR, XRD, BET, XPS, SEM-EDX, and NH₃-TPD, and their catalytic performance was evaluated for biodiesel production via the esterification of oleic acid (OA) with ethanol. Structural analysis confirmed highly pure, crystalline zero-valent copper (Cu⁰) with an FCC nanostructure and spherical morphology (average size ~ 25–63 nm), well-dispersed throughout the hydrochar-derived carbon matrix. XPS verified oxygen functionalities (–COO⁻, > C = O, C–OH) alongside Cu⁰ on the nanocomposite surfaces. Moreover, textural analysis revealed that Cu25/HC exhibited the highest surface area (29.6 m²/g) and pore volume (0.099 cm³/g), whereas Cu50/HC showed reduced porosity but introduced significant acidity (54.9 µmol/g, according to NH 3 -TPD). Catalytic efficiency increased with higher Cu dispersion density (Cu atoms/nm 2 ; R² =0.996): Cu50/HC achieved the best performance (97.4% conversion), followed by Cu25/HC (96.6%) and Cu10/HC (96.0%), outperforming bulk Cu content and BET surface area. Under optimal conditions (70 °C, 5 h, 1.0 wt% catalyst relative to OA, and an ethanol/OA molar ratio of 15:1) the Cu50/HC catalyst attained complete OA conversion. Thermodynamic parameters were determined and indicated an endergonic and thermodynamically non-spontaneous reaction. Notably, the catalyst retained 97.1% of its initial activity after six consecutive cycles, demonstrating excellent operational stability, as confirmed by the FTIR, XRD, and Cu content. These findings position the Cu50/HC nanocomposite as a cost-effective, sustainable, and efficient catalyst for biodiesel production.

title: Cation-Deficient Tantalum Oxide–Zinc Tantalate Nanocomposite for Photocatalytic Carbon Dioxide Conversion
summary: Artificial photosynthesis offers a promising route to close the anthropogenic carbon cycle, yet efficient photocatalytic CO2 conversion with H2O as an electron donor remains challenging.ZnTa2O6 (ZTO0.50) is one of the most active photocatal
content: Artificial photosynthesis offers a promising route to close the anthropogenic carbon cycle, yet efficient photocatalytic CO2 conversion with H2O as an electron donor remains challenging.ZnTa2O6 (ZTO0.50) is one of the most active photocatalysts, but the origin of its activity remains unclear.In this study, we show that Ta-rich ZnTa2O6 (ZTOn, n = Zn/Ta) inherently contains a rutile-type tantalum oxide phase, identified as cationdeficient Ta0.8O2, whose role has been largely overlooked.By tuning the ZnO/Ta2O5 precursor ratio, we obtain ZTO0.43 with the highest Ta0.8O2 content.Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal atomically intimate interfaces between Ta0.8O2 and ZnTa2O6 that promote charge separation and H2O oxidation.Density functional theory calculations show that Ta vacancies stabilise a semiconducting electronic structure and induce wavefunction localisation on adjacent O atoms, enhancing their reactivity towards H2O oxidation.Consequently, ZTO0.43 modified with the Ag@Cr cocatalyst achieves a CO formation rate exceeding 1 mmol h -1 , with a 95% selectivity; to the best of our knowledge, this is the highest CO formation rate obtained via photocatalytic conversion of CO2 with H2O as the electron donor.

title: Proactive Carbon Management in Asian Manufacturing SMEs: Insights from a Dual-Driver Case Study in Taiwan
source: Advances in management and applied economics
summary: This study examines why resource-constrained Asian manufacturing SMEs initiate proactive carbon management before direct regulatory enforcement and how internal strategic intent interacts with external institutional pressures. A qualitative
content: This study examines why resource-constrained Asian manufacturing SMEs initiate proactive carbon management before direct regulatory enforcement and how internal strategic intent interacts with external institutional pressures. A qualitative-dominant mixed-methods case study of an export-oriented Taiwanese powder metallurgy SME combines a 2024 ISO 14064-1:2018 organizational greenhouse gas inventory with three semi-structured executive interviews. Managerial assessment preceded domestic enforcement, while customer ESG requirements, evolving carbon policy, and ISO 14064-1 provided legitimacy and an operational framework. Total 2024 emissions were 3,074.026 tCO₂e, with Scope 2 accounting for 87.40%, making energy efficiency and renewable energy the priorities of a three-phase decarbonization pathway. Interviews identified inconsistent regulatory guidance, limited supplier support, and regulatory knowledge gaps. Integrating the natural resource-based view and institutional theory, the dual-driver model shows that proactive strategic intent initiates carbon action, while institutional frameworks enable systematic and legitimate implementation. The findings qualify portrayals of Asian SMEs as passive compliance seekers, demonstrate the value of triangulating standardized inventory and managerial evidence, and identify potential spillover implications across firm, industry, and societal levels. Practically, the study highlights regulatory guidance, supplier capability development, and industry-academia collaboration as priorities for SME decarbonization support. JEL classification numbers: M14, M21, Q56, Q58. Keywords: Carbon management, Small and medium-sized enterprises, Natural resource-based view, Proactive environmental strategy, Institutional theory.

title: Load-matched multi-evaporating pressure control in multi-split heat pumps for improving energy efficiency and thermal comfort
summary: Multi-split heat pumps (MSHPs) are powerful tools for achieving carbon neutrality in the building sector. However, all the indoor units (IDUs) in MSHPs have the same evaporating pressure, causing overcooling and frequent on-off operations u
content: Multi-split heat pumps (MSHPs) are powerful tools for achieving carbon neutrality in the building sector. However, all the indoor units (IDUs) in MSHPs have the same evaporating pressure, causing overcooling and frequent on-off operations under varying loads. Thus, multi-evaporating pressure (MEP) control is essential for obtaining a matched capacity for each IDU with the zone load, thereby achieving high energy efficiency and thermal comfort. This study proposes a flow control valve (FCV)-based MEP system and quantitatively evaluates its performance advantages over conventional single-evaporating pressure (SEP) systems in MSHPs. A simulation model for MSHPs with the FCV-based MEP system was developed using Dymola TIL Library, and parametric and dynamic-load scenario-based analyses of MSHPs with MEP and SEP systems were conducted using the validated simulation model. Based on the parametric analysis performed under various part-load ratios (PLRs) and sensible heat ratios (SHRs), the MEP system improved the coefficient of performance (COP) by 3.59% and temperature control precision by 40 percentage points (%p), with the greatest gains at mid-PLRs (0.5–0.7) and high SHRs (0.8–1.0). Additionally, the dynamic-load scenario analysis revealed that the MEP system reduced the energy consumption by 4.7%–7.5% and improved the COP by 8.5%–10.7% while maintaining a temperature control precision of 90%. These results demonstrate that the FCV-based MEP system simultaneously improves the energy efficiency and thermal comfort of MSHPs under realistic multi-IDU operations.

title: Anthropogenic aerosol reduction contributes to faster flash drought onset in a changing climate
summary: Flash droughts have emerged as severe hazards, posing growing challenges to natural and socioeconomic systems, yet the influence of recent aerosol reductions on their onset remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impacts of aerosols and t
content: Flash droughts have emerged as severe hazards, posing growing challenges to natural and socioeconomic systems, yet the influence of recent aerosol reductions on their onset remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impacts of aerosols and their underlying mechanisms using multi-source observations and large-ensemble climate simulations. Lower aerosol levels are increasingly linked to severe soil moisture deficits, with aerosol effects on onset-speed variability intensifying across 69.2% of regions. During the onset stage, air temperature pathways associated with aerosol variability account for a larger fraction of onset-speed variability than pathways linked to atmospheric demand. Aerosols have long acted to dampen flash drought development; however, their reduction, acting within a warming climate, contributes to faster flash drought onset. As aerosol emissions decline in the future, the area at higher risk of flash drought acceleration in aerosol-forced simulations is projected to increase by 11.7% during 2070–2099 relative to the historical period of 1990–2019. Anthropogenic aerosol reduction contributes to faster flash drought onset by enhancing soil moisture depletion induced by higher temperature and increased shortwave radiation.

title: Bibliometric Study of the Intersection Between Green Energy and Artificial Intelligence: Business- and Economy-Related Studies
summary: The rapid convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and green energy (GE) is transforming sustainable business practices, energy management, and economic development. Although research in this interdisciplinary field has expanded consider
content: The rapid convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and green energy (GE) is transforming sustainable business practices, energy management, and economic development. Although research in this interdisciplinary field has expanded considerably, its intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and business implications remain insufficiently understood. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of AI and GE research from a business and economics perspective. Publications were retrieved from the Scopus and Web of Science databases using an expanded, transparent, and reproducible search strategy. Following PRISMA guidelines and predefined inclusion criteria, a final dataset of 7,301 publications was analyzed using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer to examine publication trends, influential authors, institutions, countries, journals, collaboration networks, and thematic structures. The results reveal a marked increase in scientific production after 2022, reflecting the growing integration of AI into renewable energy systems and sustainable development research. Scientific output is concentrated in countries with strong research capacity, sustained investment in digital innovation, and ambitious sustainability agendas. Keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies four dominant research themes: sustainability and energy policy, AI-driven forecasting and optimization, smart energy systems, and digital transformation for energy efficiency. The findings demonstrate that the field has evolved from predominantly technical applications toward a multidisciplinary research domain integrating business strategy, innovation management, sustainability, and energy economics. Unlike previous bibliometric studies based on narrower search strategies or smaller datasets, this study provides a transparent, large-scale mapping of the field and offers a more comprehensive understanding of its intellectual structure and emerging research directions. The findings provide valuable insights for researchers, policymakers, managers, and investors seeking to accelerate sustainable energy transitions and support long-term economic resilience.

title: Hydrogen gas response of quartz crystal microbalance sensors coated with nitrogen-containing and nitrogen-free amorphous carbon films
summary: Abstract A safety-conscious hydrogen society requires new hydrogen gas (H2) sensors with simple structures, using no precious metals, and capable of room-temperature operation. We focused on the quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) method, cap
content: Abstract A safety-conscious hydrogen society requires new hydrogen gas (H2) sensors with simple structures, using no precious metals, and capable of room-temperature operation. We focused on the quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) method, capable of low-temperature operation, and proposed a novel H2 sensor utilizing amorphous carbon (a-C) and nitrogen-containing amorphous carbon (a-C:N) films as the detection layer. Four types of a-C:N films with different thicknesses ranging from 25 to 270 nm and one type of a-C film were deposited onto QCM elements. The test results showed that the uncoated QCM element exhibited no H2 response, whereas the QCM elements coated with a-C or a-C:N films demonstrated a noticeable H2 response. Furthermore, the H2 response increased approximately linearly with increasing a-C:N film thickness. Surface roughness also increased with increasing film thickness. These results demonstrate the potential application of such thin films in QCM-type sensors.

title: A global, temporally continuous, hourly CO 2 concentration dataset at GAW monitoring stations for 2000–2024: Enabling fine-scale carbon dynamics analysis
summary: Abstract. Global Atmosphere Watch (GAW) carbon dioxide (CO2) observations provide high-precision constraints on surface CO2 variability, but many station records remain temporally incomplete because of flask sampling, instrument interruptio
content: Abstract. Global Atmosphere Watch (GAW) carbon dioxide (CO2) observations provide high-precision constraints on surface CO2 variability, but many station records remain temporally incomplete because of flask sampling, instrument interruptions, and quality-control exclusions. Such gaps can limit the representation of diurnal variability, bias daily, monthly, and annual mean CO2 estimates, and reduce the ability to detect short-lived events. Here, we present a global, temporally continuous hourly reconstruction dataset of GAW station CO2 concentrations for 2000–2024. The dataset was generated using a two-stage reconstruction framework that integrates GAW observations with Carbon Tracker (CT) and Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) CO2 fields, together with anthropogenic, vegetation, meteorological, and spatiotemporal predictors. In the intra-day gap filling stage, missing hours on days with at least one valid observation were reconstructed using hour-pair models to produce complete daily profiles. In the full-sequence reconstruction stage, the remaining periods with no valid observations were reconstructed using a globally trained initial prediction model followed by station-specific post-correction. The framework showed robust validation performance at the hourly scale, with R2 = 0.96 and RMSE = 3.65 ppm for intra-day gap filling and R2 = 0.93 and RMSE = 4.76 ppm for full-sequence reconstruction. Across all stations, the mean filling rate was 68.9 %, and the mean reconstruction uncertainty was 2.80 ppm. Applying the World Data Centre for Greenhouse Gases (WDCGG) global analysis framework showed that reconstructed global monthly mean CO2 concentrations were, on average, 0.54 ± 0.21 ppm higher than those derived from the original GAW records, indicating that incomplete temporal coverage can measurably affect global monthly estimates. Compared with grid-cell CT and CAMS simulations, the reconstructed dataset retained stronger station-scale diurnal variability and captured CO2 enhancements during the 2023 Canadian wildfire period. This dataset can support long-term assessments of global and regional surface CO2 changes, fine-scale analyses of CO2 variability, and regional carbon emission inversion and evaluation. The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21306261 (Mi et al., 2026).

title: Analysis of Nigerian Newspapers' Portrayal of Climate Change Effects on Food Security
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION STUDIES
summary: This study explored how Nigerian newspapers—The Guardian and Daily Trust—report climate change and its impact on food security, using framing theory as a guide. It specifically examined the patterns of story types, use of different frames a
content: This study explored how Nigerian newspapers—The Guardian and Daily Trust—report climate change and its impact on food security, using framing theory as a guide. It specifically examined the patterns of story types, use of different frames and representation of voices in the newspapers. A content analysis of 394 articles revealed that feature articles were predominant, with limited presence of editorials and interviews. Findings also revealed that economic factors were the most dominant frame on climate change reports. It was also found that government officials were the most frequently mentioned sources of information, while farmers, women, youth, and scientists were given little attention. Thus, the narrative about climate change tends to be less inclusive and supportive of internal stakeholder participation. The paper concludes that climate issues were given moderate attention by Nigerian newspapers, which can only influence the public’s knowledge about climate-related food shortages to some extent. This highlights the need for a wider range of stories and reliable information, along with more responsible reporting, for national stability and sustainable system for food security.

title: Life-cycle incremental cost-benefit model for passive buildings and a case study in Zhejiang Province, China
source: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
summary: Passive buildings (PBs) offer substantial advantages in reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, making their promotion a strategic priority for China’s carbon goals. However, high upfront costs, unclear long-term benefits
content: Passive buildings (PBs) offer substantial advantages in reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, making their promotion a strategic priority for China’s carbon goals. However, high upfront costs, unclear long-term benefits, and long payback periods hinder adoption. This study develops a Life-Cycle Incremental Cost-Benefit Model (LCICBM) covering design, construction, and operation. The model quantifies and monetizes economic, environmental, and social benefits. A dynamic evaluation framework using ENPV and EIRR is proposed. The model is validated using the first PHI-certified passive residential district in Zhejiang, China. Results confirm economic feasibility: ENPV is positive (6.67 million CNY), EIRR (8.5%) exceeds the social discount rate (8%), and the payback period (43 years) is within the 50-year design life. Sensitivity analysis shows electricity price as the most influential factor, yet the project remains robust under most pessimistic scenarios. This research provides a practical tool for PB economic evaluation, supporting policy, investment, and technical decisions for large-scale PB deployment in China and beyond.

title: Dynamics of Production‐ and Consumption‐Based Carbon Dioxide Emissions in China: The Influential Role of Energy Imports and Monetary Policy
summary: ABSTRACT As the world's largest CO 2 emitter and one of the largest energy importers, China encounters significant challenges in achieving its carbon neutrality target whilst ensuring environmental sustainability. Understanding how macroeco
content: ABSTRACT As the world's largest CO 2 emitter and one of the largest energy importers, China encounters significant challenges in achieving its carbon neutrality target whilst ensuring environmental sustainability. Understanding how macroeconomic and energy‐related factors influence different dimensions of carbon emissions is therefore essential for designing effective climate policies. This study examines the effects of monetary policy and energy imports on aggregate carbon emissions, consumption‐based carbon emissions (COC) and production‐based carbon emissions (COP) in China over the period 1990–2020. The study employs the novel augmented autoregressive distributed lag (AARDL) approach to examine short run and long run relationship amongst variables. The empirical evidence demonstrates that monetary policy (i.e., real interest rate) has a positive relationship with aggregate CO 2 emissions and COC in the long run, whilst the relationship between monetary policy and COP is negative but statistically insignificant. Energy imports have a positive and significant impact on aggregate CO 2 emissions, COC and COP, in both the short and long run. Economic growth also contributes positively to all three emissions accounts, reflecting the environmental impact of China's energy‐intensive growth model. Therefore, the findings suggest that the integration of environmental goals into monetary policy, the promotion of green finance and the acceleration of the transition to renewable energy sources will be necessary to reduce CO 2 emissions and meet China's long‐term carbon neutrality.

title: Social and labour policies can unlock the climate deadlock
summary: Every five years, signatory countries to the Paris Agreement update their Nationally Determined Contributions, outlining national climate policies and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission targets. We propose a simulation modelling framework levera
content: Every five years, signatory countries to the Paris Agreement update their Nationally Determined Contributions, outlining national climate policies and greenhouse gas (GHG) emission targets. We propose a simulation modelling framework leveraging data from the system of national accounts, national GHG emission inventories, and household and labour force surveys. With supply-and-use tables at its core, the framework assesses how structural changes in economies, driven by climate policies such as the adoption of low-emission energy technologies, affect direct, indirect, and induced employment by industry. We apply this approach to seven economically diverse countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, examining policies related to renewable energy, industrial processes, sustainable agriculture and tourism. Estimates of technological change are informed by national statistical data, expert knowledge and secondary literature. We find that climate policies generally lead to net-positive nationwide employment gains. The findings can support governments in designing complementary Just Transition policies that maximise gains and improve fairness.Highlights – We analyse ‘what-if’ NDC climate policies using country-specific inter-industry trajectory models for seven different Sub-Saharan African countries.– We find that most climate policies yield net-positive nationwide employment gains.– However, job losses occur in carbon-intensive sectors, with industry-level impacts depending on the nature of the policies.– Climate policies may disproportionately impact low-income households, as induced effects of higher energy prices raise costs of food, housing and transport, for which low-income households have higher propensity to spend.– The modelling results indicate where climate policies generate negative implications, an information that is essential for designing Just Transition policies as stipulated in the preamble of the Paris Agreement to fit the aims of the UNFCCC workstream on the ‘Impacts of the implementation of response measures.’

title: Influence of blend ratio and particle size on the physiochemical and fuel properties of briquettes from water hyacinth, bagasse, and sludge
summary: Converting abundant, underutilized wastes into densified solid fuels offers a promising pathway for renewable energy generation and circular waste management. Such wastes include invasive water hyacinth ( Eichhornia crassipes ), sugarcane b
content: Converting abundant, underutilized wastes into densified solid fuels offers a promising pathway for renewable energy generation and circular waste management. Such wastes include invasive water hyacinth ( Eichhornia crassipes ), sugarcane bagasse ( Saccharum officinarum ), and wastewater sewage sludge. Prior studies have largely focused on single-feedstock briquetting, with limited attention to hybrid formulations that combine municipal sludge, invasive aquatic weeds, and agro-industrial residues. The literature also lacks systematic evaluation of how blend ratio and particle size influence physicochemical and fuel quality properties under controlled compaction conditions. To address this gap, the present study employed a Taguchi L25 orthogonal design with ANOVA and regression diagnostics to investigate the effects of feedstock blending ratio and particle size on the physicochemical and fuel properties of hybrid briquettes produced under a compaction pressure of 20 MPa. The properties included calorific value, moisture content, ash content, volatile matter, fixed carbon, and bulk density. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) revealed that the feedstock blending ratio was the dominant factor governing all measured properties. Particle size showed no statistically significant effect on fuel quality within the investigated range. The bagasse-rich blend of ratio 1:2:7 was the highest-performing formulation among the five tested ratios. It achieved a peak calorific value of 19.00 MJ/kg, a maximum bulk density of 1004 kg/m³, and a fixed carbon content of 21.40%, as well as a low ash content of 9.50%. Sludge-dominated formulations resulted in a higher ash content of 13.70% and a lower calorific value of 16.90 MJ/kg. It was concluded that increasing the biomass proportion progressively improved fixed carbon from 8.70% to 21.40% and bulk density from 760 kg/m³ to 1004 kg/m³. Future research should focus on evaluating their other mechanical properties and conducting comprehensive flame temperature and gaseous/particulate emissions measurements. to support practical application and commercial upscaling of these hybrid biofuels.

title: Carbon source and pollutant matching shapes microbial succession and removal regimes under electrochemical redox control
summary: Electro-assisted bioreactors provide redox-controlled platforms for removing recalcitrant industrial organics, yet empirical co-substrate dosing often causes carbon–pollutant mismatch, diverting electrons and carbon fluxes into non-producti
content: Electro-assisted bioreactors provide redox-controlled platforms for removing recalcitrant industrial organics, yet empirical co-substrate dosing often causes carbon–pollutant mismatch, diverting electrons and carbon fluxes into non-productive sinks. Here, we systematically pair three carbon sources with three representative pollutants to determine how carbon identity shapes microbial succession, interaction networks, and removal performance under coupled resource–stress gradients. Across nine pairings, successional trajectories and network configurations diverge reproducibly, yielding up to ~4-fold differences in pollutant removal. Co-substrates reshape niches and interspecies dependencies, redirecting metabolic routing and resulting in three succession regimes: pollutant-dominated, co-dominated, and carbon-dominated. Removal is most strongly associated with niche occupancy and ecological interactions (r = −0.853, p < 0.01), supporting network-level emergence. Overall, this study provides an ecology-informed basis for tailoring carbon dosing to pollutant context, shifting from degrader-focused dosing to a network-centric strategy that supports decision-oriented control for smart, low-carbon wastewater management in electro-assisted and related anaerobic systems. Decision-oriented carbon supplementation in electro-assisted and related anaerobic wastewater treatment systems reshapes niches and interspecies dependencies, leading to around 4-fold increase in pollutant removal, based on experiments pairing three carbon sources with three pollutants.

title: Decoding Hydrogen-Affinity-Controlled Surface State Evolution in Sn-Based Single-Atom Alloys for CO2 Electroreduction
summary: Abstract The catalytic role of heteroatom dopants in Sn-based electrocatalysts remains elusive because the dynamic evolution of surface states under electrochemical conditions is rarely considered. Herein, density functional theory calculat
content: Abstract The catalytic role of heteroatom dopants in Sn-based electrocatalysts remains elusive because the dynamic evolution of surface states under electrochemical conditions is rarely considered. Herein, density functional theory calculations combined with pH-dependent microkinetic simulations reveal that hydrogen affinity governs the evolution of catalytic surface states in Sn-based single-atom alloys (SAAs) during electrochemical CO2 reduction to formate. We demonstrate that hydrogen preferentially occupies either dopant or neighboring Sn sites depending on the electronic structure of the dopant and identify simple electronic descriptors based on the dopant d-band and p-band centers that enable the screening of preferential H adsorption sites. Surface Pourbaix analysis further reveals that Sn-based SAAs tend to evolve into nearly monolayer hydrogen-covered surfaces under practical CO2RR conditions, indicating that the catalytic performance should be evaluated on reconstructed rather than pristine surfaces. By incorporating dipole–field interactions, explicit potential of zero charge, and pH-dependent electric-field effects into microkinetic modeling, a predictive pH-dependent activity volcano is established, showing excellent agreement with experimental benchmarking. The resulting framework identifies promising catalysts with distinct pH-dependent activity windows and, more importantly, establishes hydrogen affinity as a fundamental descriptor governing surface-state evolution and thereby influencing catalytic performance, providing a general strategy for the rational design of p-block-metal-based electrocatalysts.

title: Intelligent Concrete: AI-Driven Design and Optimization of Reinforced Concrete Structures
summary: Traditional reinforced concrete (RC) design has historically relied on time-consuming, iterative manual calculations to ensure structural safety. While effective for maintaining security, this method often hampers efficiency and innovation.
content: Traditional reinforced concrete (RC) design has historically relied on time-consuming, iterative manual calculations to ensure structural safety. While effective for maintaining security, this method often hampers efficiency and innovation. Consequently, it has struggled to fully meet modern demands for sustainable and optimized construction. These approaches rely heavily on conservative assumptions, standardized material properties, and empirical rules. As a result, they lead to time-intensive design cycles, over-reinforced sections, and suboptimal outcomes in complex or non-standard scenarios. The inherent limitations in exploring high-dimensional design spaces and integrating multi-objective criteria (e.g., cost, durability, and environmental impact) restrict the potential for performance-based, adaptive, and resource-efficient structures. This chapter introduces artificial intelligence (AI)-driven design and optimization as a transformative paradigm shift. With the help of machine learning (ML), deep neural networks, genetic algorithms, and hybrid computational frameworks, it enables data-driven, predictive, and highly optimized RC systems. By automating generative design, topology optimization, and lifecycle performance forecasting, AI produces intelligent concrete structures that are stronger, lighter, and more sustainable. Despite its promise, the chapter also reviews key challenges such as data scarcity, interpretability of AI models, computational costs, regulatory compliance, and ethical concerns, underscoring the need for explainable AI and human–AI collaboration. Real-world case studies and meta-analyses highlight measurable environmental and economic benefits, advocating AI as a transformative paradigm for future sustainable construction. The chapter closes by calling for interdisciplinary efforts to advance reliable, transparent, and equitable AI adoption in structural engineering.

title: Leading early, losing later? Responsible leadership and the lifecycle dynamics of circular economy adoption
summary: Purpose This study examines how responsible leadership (RL) influences the adoption of circular economy (CE) practices in the construction sector, with particular attention to how leadership effects vary across project lifecycle stages and
content: Purpose This study examines how responsible leadership (RL) influences the adoption of circular economy (CE) practices in the construction sector, with particular attention to how leadership effects vary across project lifecycle stages and institutional contexts. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative design was used to explore how responsible leadership influences circular economy adoption in construction. Data from 21 semi-structured interviews with construction professionals were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis to identify key leadership behaviours and decision-making processes shaping CE outcomes. Findings The findings show that responsible leadership supports circularity, but its effectiveness depends on structural conditions such as project initiation processes, procurement systems, regulatory environments, and supply chain maturity. Its influence is strongest in early project stages, where circular principles and contractual mechanisms can be embedded, but diminishes during delivery due to technical complexity, commercial pressures, and path-dependent design constraints. Practical implications The study emphasizes embedding circular economy requirements early through procurement reform, explicit contractual obligations, and regulatory alignment, alongside strengthening the capacity of technical teams and supply chain actors to enable effective implementation of responsible leaders' circular economy goals. Originality/value This study extends responsible leadership theory by framing RL as a contingent, institutionally embedded process rather than an individual trait. It advances understanding of leadership in sustainability transitions in project-based contexts by offering a process-oriented explanation of how institutional conditions shape sustainability outcomes.

title: Ab Initio Insights into the Interfacial Interactions of Emerging Two-Dimensional Nanomaterials with C-A-S-H Geopolymer Matrices
summary: Abstract The development of sustainable construction materials has positioned geopolymer concrete as a promising alternative to conventional Portland cement due to its reduced carbon footprint and utilization of industrial byproducts. In th
content: Abstract The development of sustainable construction materials has positioned geopolymer concrete as a promising alternative to conventional Portland cement due to its reduced carbon footprint and utilization of industrial byproducts. In this context, two-dimensional (2D) materials have emerged as versatile reinforcing fillers that enable the precise tuning of interfacial interactions, thereby improving the mechanical and physicochemical performance of geopolymer systems. Herein, we present a systematic first-principles investigation of a diverse class of two-dimensional (2D) materials, including Xenes (silicene, germanene, stanene, arsenene, tellurene, and blue phosphorus), transition metal dichalcogenides (MoS2 and WS2), MXenes, graphene derivatives (including graphdiyne), and ceramic/covalent systems such as SiC, boron phosphate, boron nitride, and CrO2 by examining their interfacial interactions with a structurally ordered calcium aluminosilicate hydrate (C-A-S-H) model using density functional theory (DFT). DFT-guided calculations reveal a clear hierarchy in interfacial binding, ranging from strong chemisorption (≈−1.5 to −4.0 eV) for MXenes and functionalized graphene derivatives, to moderate interactions (≈−0.8 to −1.5 eV) for Xenes and carbides, and weak physisorption (≈−0.2 to −0.8 eV) for transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and ceramic surfaces. MXenes and functionalized graphene exhibit the strongest adhesion, driven by covalent bonding, Ca2+ mediated bridging, and charge transfer, leading to improved load transfer and microstructural densification. In contrast, graphdiyne and h-BN are dominated by van der Waals interactions, contributing mainly to durability and stability. Overall, this study establishes that surface functionality and electronic structure govern interfacial strength and reinforcement efficiency in 2D material-geopolymer systems. Therefore, this DFT-guided comparative study establishes a unified structure–interaction–property relationship and highlights that surface functionality and electronic structure are the key descriptors governing reinforcement efficiency. The findings establish clear design principles for the rational selection of 2D reinforcements, positioning MXenes, Xenes, and functionalized graphene as leading candidates for the development of next-generation, high-performance, and durable geopolymer concretes.

title: An Analysis of Outdoor Recreation on Land Slated for Development; Implications for a Social-Ecological System in Boulder, Colorado
summary: Robust evidence shows that outdoor recreation in natural areas, i.e. places that retain native, ecological character with minimal human intervention, produces public health benefits including physical benefits from exercise, reduced mental
content: Robust evidence shows that outdoor recreation in natural areas, i.e. places that retain native, ecological character with minimal human intervention, produces public health benefits including physical benefits from exercise, reduced mental stress, increased community connections, heightened place identity, and even increased ecological awareness. But land use planners don’t always formally consider these benefits in their planning, which can create tension amongst recreationalists, public health experts, planners and developers. We were interested in the benefits related to outdoor recreation at a popular, community-regulated natural area in Boulder, Colorado, USA, called CU South, that is slated to be closed to the public for the development of a flood mitigation project and university campus. Using mixed methods from recreation ecology and social-ecological systems framework theory, we showed that visitors highly value recreating at CU South for a wide range of health and community benefits, including customary off-leash dog access in a natural setting. We also showed how this site serves as a community hub where locals gather as part of their daily routine. Finally, we demonstrated that the governing institutions, the University of Colorado Boulder and the City of Boulder, acknowledge recreation occurs on CU South, but have not publicly considered the full suite of current recreation benefits in their development plans.

title: Prioritizing decarbonization technologies for climate-neutral railway systems: A qualitative technology assessment of Korea’s rail sector
summary: Railways are widely recognized as a low-carbon transport mode, but achieving climate-neutral railway systems requires a broader transition beyond modal shift, spanning propulsion technologies, energy supply, infrastructure management, digit
content: Railways are widely recognized as a low-carbon transport mode, but achieving climate-neutral railway systems requires a broader transition beyond modal shift, spanning propulsion technologies, energy supply, infrastructure management, digital operation, and climate resilience. This study develops a document-informed, interpretive technology assessment framework to examine railway decarbonization technologies, using Korea as a case study. Global technology and policy agendas were reviewed and classified into four domains—low-carbon propulsion and electrification, energy optimization and renewable integration, digital and AI-based operation, and climate-resilient infrastructure—and assessed against environmental relevance, technological maturity, operational applicability, policy/regulatory readiness, and R&D urgency. Korea has relatively mature conventional railway technologies, but significant gaps remain in hydrogen and battery-based propulsion, renewable energy–rail integration, standards and certification, and decarbonization-specific demonstration infrastructure. The assessment identifies distinct implementation conditions and R&D priorities across the four domains. Regenerative braking, energy storage systems, energy management systems, and AI-based operation optimization are classified as near-term priorities because of their relatively high operational applicability and potential for integration into existing railway systems. Renewable energy–rail integration, battery-electric trains, hydrogen fuel-cell trains, and digital twin-based asset management are classified as medium-term priorities, reflecting their requirements for further system integration, demonstration, or regulatory alignment. Climate-resilient infrastructure, low-carbon construction materials, and international standards and certification systems are identified as long-term strategic priorities. The main contribution of this study is an integrated, document-informed assessment that connects technology characteristics and implementation gaps in Korea’s railway sector with a staged R&D portfolio, providing a structured basis for coordinating technology development, demonstration, and institutional readiness.

title: Scaling paludiculture: stakeholder perspectives on adoption and enabling conditions in England
summary: Paludiculture, the cultivation of wetland species on rewetted peatlands, is increasingly promoted as a nature-based solution for climate mitigation, biodiversity restoration and peat conservation; however, its adoption remains limited in th
content: Paludiculture, the cultivation of wetland species on rewetted peatlands, is increasingly promoted as a nature-based solution for climate mitigation, biodiversity restoration and peat conservation; however, its adoption remains limited in the United Kingdom. This study examines stakeholder perspectives on the adoption of paludiculture and the enabling conditions required to support its scale-up. Drawing on 36 photo-elicitation interviews with farmers, land managers, conservation organisations, researchers, and policymakers, the study explores how stakeholders interpret the ecological, economic, and socio-cultural implications of transitioning from drained peatland agriculture to wetland-based systems. Results indicate widespread recognition of environmental benefits, including greenhouse gas mitigation, flood regulation, and habitat restoration. However, adoption is constrained by concerns related to food security, land valuation, regulatory complexity, and underdeveloped markets. Stakeholders also highlight gaps in policy frameworks, with existing financial mechanisms perceived as short-term and poorly adapted to peatland systems. Market development, long-term policy support, and a strengthened evidence base emerge as critical enabling conditions, requiring coordinated policy, sustained investment, and cross-sector collaboration to support viable supply chains and demand. Aligning policy design with locally grounded knowledge and stakeholder needs is essential to enable effective environmental management.

title: Pathways for the integration of bioenergetic and food production: An artificial intelligence-assisted review
summary: ABSTRACT The application of agricultural biomass as a renewable energy source is garnering global attention, particularly for its contribution to the circular economy. However, the production pathways needed to harmonize agricultural produc
content: ABSTRACT The application of agricultural biomass as a renewable energy source is garnering global attention, particularly for its contribution to the circular economy. However, the production pathways needed to harmonize agricultural production for alimentation and/or as a bioenergy resource remain unclear. Despite growing literature on renewable energy, a research gap persists in the integration of bioenergy into the food security framework. This research aims to identify the conditions under which bioenergy can be produced without jeopardizing food production. A methodology was developed that combined bibliometric clustering with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), providing a systematic framework for sustainable agricultural biomass and bioenergy co-production. To determine potential pathways for integrated agricultural-bioenergy production, a bibliographic analysis was conducted using the Web of Science (WoS) database and VOSviewer software. A GenAI tool and diagramming software were then used to address the question: Is it possible to produce bioenergy without affecting food production? Two groups of keywords with the highest occurrence and citations, were obtained by data mining and clustering analysis. A total of 10 pathways were identified, supported by AI, able to balance bioenergy and food production. All pathways use agricultural crop residue, food waste, manure, algae, sludge, and torrefied biomass as energy sources. This study corroborates the use of GenAI to identify bioenergetic-food integration pathways and presents a novel methodology for identifying and integrating them into the current food security framework.

title: Solution‐processable cross‐linked poly(ethylene oxide) ultrathin composite membranes via ultraviolet polymerization for CO 2 capture
summary: Abstract Cross‐linked poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) synthesized via free radical polymerization is one of the most promising polymer membrane materials for CO 2 capture. However, it remains a major challenge to obtain soluble cross‐linked PEO
content: Abstract Cross‐linked poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) synthesized via free radical polymerization is one of the most promising polymer membrane materials for CO 2 capture. However, it remains a major challenge to obtain soluble cross‐linked PEO polymers via facile and controllable methods, so as to fabricate solution‐coated ultrathin composite membranes with high CO 2 permeance. To address this issue, we proposed an intermittent ultraviolet (UV) irradiation strategy that enables precise control over the free radical polymerization process of PEO monomers and improves polymerization uniformity. Consequently, we successfully synthesized a soluble PEO polymer sufficiently cross‐linked and fabricated it into an ultrathin (~45 nm), defect‐free selective layer via simple solution coating methods. The optimized membrane achieves an ultrahigh CO 2 permeance of 3074 gas permeation units (GPU), along with a desirable CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 38.3, outperforming current cutting‐edge membrane materials. More importantly, this membrane exhibits good scalability and operational stability, offering great promise for continuous large‐scale fabrication and practical carbon capture applications.

title: Effects of Executive Sustainability Compensation on Nonexecutive Employee Behavior
summary: ABSTRACT In response to growing awareness of climate change and increasing regulatory sustainability requirements, many companies now link executive compensation to specific sustainability criteria. Although prior research has examined the
content: ABSTRACT In response to growing awareness of climate change and increasing regulatory sustainability requirements, many companies now link executive compensation to specific sustainability criteria. Although prior research has examined the effects of such incentives on executive behavior, this study explores how executive sustainability‐linked compensation and leadership tone influence the sustainable behavior of nonexecutive employees. Using an online experiment, I find that informing nonexecutive employees about executive bonuses tied to sustainability targets significantly increases their likelihood of making sustainable decisions. In contrast, tone from the top information does not have a statistically significant effect. The results have important implications for theory, practice, and policy by highlighting transparent communication of sustainability‐linked executive incentives as a simple yet powerful tool for fostering sustainable change among nonexecutive employees as well. Ultimately, this study contributes to advancing the understanding of employee‐level sustainability efforts and offers practical strategies to support the sustainable transformation of business and society.

title: Aerial Seeding for Forest and Landscape Restoration: A Systematic Review of Technology, Challenges, and Future Directions
summary: ABSTRACT Land degradation is a critical global challenge, threatening biodiversity, food security, and livelihoods. Ecological restoration has therefore become a priority, with aerial seeding emerging as a key method to address issues of sc
content: ABSTRACT Land degradation is a critical global challenge, threatening biodiversity, food security, and livelihoods. Ecological restoration has therefore become a priority, with aerial seeding emerging as a key method to address issues of scale, accessibility, and efficiency. By dispersing seeds from aircraft or drones, aerial seeding complements ground‐based approaches and is especially effective in remote or degraded areas. First applied in agriculture during the 1940s, its role has expanded with technological advances that allow greater precision, though challenges such as seed predation and uneven distribution remain. A systematic literature review (SLR) of studies published between 2000 and 2024 synthesized current evidence and identified research gaps. A total of 34 articles were analyzed, showing increased interest since 2017, with China contributing 29% of publications. Highly cited studies emphasized unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications in forest regeneration. The literature was stratified into two primary domains: environmental constraints and associated mitigation strategies, and technological innovations designed to overcome technical barriers in aerial seeding. Findings show that aerial seeding is an effective, low‐cost method for large‐scale restoration. It is particularly valuable for degraded and postfire landscapes, where it enhances carbon recovery and reduces costs compared to manual planting. However, outcomes depend on seed traits, site conditions, timing, and predation pressure. Future success will rely on technological advances, ecosystem‐specific strategies, and adaptive responses to climate change. By enhancing seed resilience and precision delivery, aerial seeding could become a cornerstone of global reforestation and restoration efforts.

title: Synthetic Methodologies and Structural Engineering of Biomass‐Derived Adsorbents for CO 2 Capture
summary: ABSTRACT Developing sustainable, scalable, low‐cost adsorbents constitutes a core prerequisite to realize practically viable CO 2 capture technologies. Biomass‐derived porous carbons represent attractive candidate sorbents owing to renewabl
content: ABSTRACT Developing sustainable, scalable, low‐cost adsorbents constitutes a core prerequisite to realize practically viable CO 2 capture technologies. Biomass‐derived porous carbons represent attractive candidate sorbents owing to renewable raw feedstocks, tailorable pore architecture, intrinsic hydrophobic character, and moderate regeneration energy demand. This review adopts a methodology‐ and engineering‐driven perspective to examine rational design principles, scalable fabrication routes, and structural engineering strategies of biomass‐derived adsorbents for high‐efficiency CO 2 capture.
