Material‐level links between manufacturing pathways, physicochemical features, and resultant CO 2 adsorption performance are critically analyzed, covering a broad suite of carbonization, activation, and surface‐modification approaches. Beyond material characteristics, engineering‐relevant aspects are addressed, including pelletization of powdered sorbents, reactor configuration, and practical implementation within PSA (pressure swing adsorption), VSA (vacuum swing adsorption), and TSA (temperature swing adsorption) cyclic adsorption workflows for industrial‐scale deployment. Key existing bottlenecks are outlined, such as lack of standardized synthesis workflows, insufficient anti‐contamination performance, barriers for large‐scale manufacturing, and absence of unified performance‐assessment benchmarks. Corresponding future research avenues are suggested to promote the translation of lab‐scale biomass‐derived adsorbent research toward real‐world CO 2 ‐capture practice.

title: State‐Initiated Climate Intermediaries Shaping Climate Governance–Needed Facilitators of Dialogue for Societal Transition to Net Zero?
summary: ABSTRACT As governments intensify efforts to achieve net zero goals, they increasingly rely on forms of indirect governance to mobilise societal actors and facilitate climate action. Governance literature focuses on orchestration by organis
content: ABSTRACT As governments intensify efforts to achieve net zero goals, they increasingly rely on forms of indirect governance to mobilise societal actors and facilitate climate action. Governance literature focuses on orchestration by organisations and governments that engage intermediaries to pursue shared governance goals. While intermediaries are recognised in climate governance as go‐between organisations operating between governance levels to affect climate policy, less is known about states that establish and design intermediaries for steering climate action. This paper unpacks policy characteristics of what we call state‐initiated climate intermediaries (SICI) to gain a nuanced understanding of this dynamic. It examines cases of SICIs in Sweden and the Netherlands using grey literature analysis. Case analysis is guided by a novel conceptual framework that bridges orchestration theory with mission‐oriented innovation policy. The analysis indicates that mission‐oriented policy of SICIs that encourages cross‐sectoral participation and dialogue with the wider public facilitates inclusive climate action. However, neither intermediary provides systematic mechanisms for tracking participants' implementation of voluntary commitments. The available evidence therefore indicates facilitation and stakeholder mobilisation, but does not permit conclusions about the resulting climate outcomes. This paper makes a conceptual contribution to climate governance literature by defining SICIs as a distinct climate intermediary type with mission‐oriented policy characteristics. It contributes to an empirical understanding of states as orchestrators of SICIs and mission‐oriented innovation policy to steer these intermediaries' climate initiatives towards mission goals.

title: A Land-Sea integrated ecological compensation framework based on carbon sequestration service flows: Evidence from a Coastal City
summary: Ecological compensation (EC) is an important policy instrument for coordinating ecological conservation and economic development and promoting carbon neutrality. However, existing EC policies in coastal regions remain largely terrestrial-or
content: Ecological compensation (EC) is an important policy instrument for coordinating ecological conservation and economic development and promoting carbon neutrality. However, existing EC policies in coastal regions remain largely terrestrial-oriented, making it difficult to identify cross-regional dependence on land-sea carbon sequestration services (CSs) and the corresponding compensation responsibilities. Using Qingdao, China, as a case study, this study develops a land-sea integrated EC framework that combines random forest, the IPCC inventory method, and a spatial interaction model to identify land-sea CSs supply-demand patterns and carbon sequestration service flows (CSF), and to allocate EC responsibilities accordingly. The results show that: (1) from 2004 to 2023, the imbalance between CSs supply and demand continuously intensified, with pronounced spatial mismatches; (2) CSF exhibited clear land-sea coupling, with the sea area and coastal mountainous area (Laoshan District) serving as the major CSF sources. CSF outflows from the sea area accounted for 29.02%–47.81% of the total positive regional CSF and primarily flowed to the rapidly urbanizing area of Huangdao District; and (3) actual EC payments differed markedly from ideal responsibilities across county-level administrative units, while the sea area received 78.10% of total inter-county compensation receipts. The Ecological Compensation Priority Index (ECPI) further indicated that the sea area and key terrestrial CSs supply areas should be prioritized for compensation. By integrating land-sea ecological contributions, external CSs dependence, compensation responsibilities, and implementation priorities into a unified analysis, the framework can support more equitable and efficient EC decision-making in coastal regions.

title: Journal of Ballistics
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping agribusiness by integrating advanced technologies into production, processing, marketing, and supply chain management, thereby creating more efficient, resilient, and sustainable food systems.In India, in
content: Digital transformation is reshaping agribusiness by integrating advanced technologies into production, processing, marketing, and supply chain management, thereby creating more efficient, resilient, and sustainable food systems.In India, increasing demand for food, climate variability, shrinking landholdings, and resource constraints have accelerated the need for smart agricultural solutions.This review examines the emerging role of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence, precision agriculture, the Internet of Things, blockchain, big data analytics, drones, and digital platforms, in modernizing agribusiness and strengthening food value chains.It synthesizes recent scientific evidence on technological innovations, adoption patterns, opportunities, barriers, and sustainability outcomes across the agricultural sector.The review highlights that digital technologies improve productivity, resource-use efficiency, traceability, market connectivity, and climate resilience while supporting informed decision-making.However, challenges related to digital infrastructure, affordability, data governance, and digital literacy remain significant.The paper concludes that supportive policies, inclusive innovation, capacity building, and multi-stakeholder collaboration are essential to accelerate India's transition toward smart, resilient, and sustainable food systems.

title: Analisis Penguasaan Konsep dan Kesadaran Perubahan Iklim Siswa Kelas X SMA PGRI 1 Pati
source: JagoMIPA Jurnal Pendidikan Matematika dan IPA
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis penguasaan konsep, kesadaran perubahan iklim, serta hubungan keduanya pada siswa kelas X SMA PGRI 1 Pati. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain deskriptif-korelasional. Subjek pene
content: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis penguasaan konsep, kesadaran perubahan iklim, serta hubungan keduanya pada siswa kelas X SMA PGRI 1 Pati. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain deskriptif-korelasional. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 380 siswa kelas X yang dipilih menggunakan teknik sampling jenuh (total sampling). Data dikumpulkan melalui tes penguasaan konsep berupa 16 soal pilihan ganda yang mencakup kemampuan mengingat (C1), memahami (C2), mengaplikasikan (C3), dan menganalisis (C4), serta angket kesadaran perubahan iklim berupa 20 pernyataan skala Likert yang mencakup aspek pengetahuan, sikap, dan tindakan. Data dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif dan korelasi peringkat Spearman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan rata-rata penguasaan konsep sebesar 70,9 dengan variasi kemampuan antarsiswa yang cukup besar. Capaian tertinggi terdapat pada kemampuan mengingat dan mengaplikasikan, sedangkan terendah pada kemampuan menganalisis interaksi sains, teknologi, dan masyarakat. Kesadaran perubahan iklim memiliki rata-rata 76,9 dan berada pada kategori tinggi, dengan aspek tindakan sebagai capaian tertinggi. Analisis korelasi menunjukkan hubungan yang sangat lemah dan tidak signifikan antara penguasaan konsep dan kesadaran perubahan iklim. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa penguasaan konsep tidak secara otomatis berkaitan dengan kesadaran siswa. Pembelajaran perubahan iklim perlu mengintegrasikan penguatan konsep, pengalaman kontekstual, refleksi nilai, dan aksi lingkungan berbasis masalah lokal.

title: Electrification reshapes BRICS vehicle urban mining: Material flows and circularity by 2050
source: Transportation Research Part D Transport and Environment
summary: Vehicle electrification is increasing demand for critical battery materials and shifting end-of-life management from whole vehicle scrap toward component-level streams, especially retired vehicle batteries. The five BRICS founding countries
content: Vehicle electrification is increasing demand for critical battery materials and shifting end-of-life management from whole vehicle scrap toward component-level streams, especially retired vehicle batteries. The five BRICS founding countries—Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa—represent a critical and diverse testing ground for this transition because they combine large and growing vehicle markets, divergent electrification pathways, and uneven recycling capacities. Here, we develop a stock-driven dynamic material flow model to project vehicle electrification, end-of-life vehicle generation, and retired battery generation from 2025 to 2050. By combining material intensity data with country-specific end-of-life parameters, we estimate secondary material re-supply and vehicle-to-vehicle circularity for major vehicle and battery materials. By 2050, circularity for recoverable battery materials under current systems ranges from approximately 3 % to 24 % across countries and materials, indicating continued dependence on primary supply. Improved collection and refining can raise circularity for these materials to 24 %–56 %, with NiSO 4 reaching approximately 49 %–56 % in China, South Africa, Russia, and Brazil; however, FeSO 4 , graphite, and carbon black remain unrecovered under the modeled conditions. Our analysis shows the need to synchronize electrification with formal collection, component-level dismantling, quality-preserving refining, and targeted policy support.

title: Integrating ideals and urban datasets for sustainable city monitoring
summary: This study highlights the potential of connecting ideals and semantic web technology to overcome challenges in urban sustainability monitoring. City governments generally employ abstract concepts to communicate sustainability goals. Moreove
content: This study highlights the potential of connecting ideals and semantic web technology to overcome challenges in urban sustainability monitoring. City governments generally employ abstract concepts to communicate sustainability goals. Moreover, siloed monitoring systems are often used to track a multitude of metrics and indicators. However, the absence of an overarching strategy in cities’ monitoring frameworks and the incompatibility between various datasets and indicators can result in fragmented approaches. By using “Ideals”, actors can collaborate to achieve important objectives and share a unified understanding of the concepts employed. The authors propose the use of ideals to bridge different disciplines and achieve comprehensive insights through indicator-based monitoring systems. The City of Amsterdam is used as an exploratory case study to demonstrate how a domain ontology that combines the examination of coalition agreements, urban datasets, and monitoring systems can provide insights into how a city operationalizes and monitors its own interpretation of sustainable development.

title: Low-carbon day-ahead joint market clearing for integrated energy systems with high renewable energy penetration
summary: Driven by carbon-neutrality targets and the rapid growth of renewable generation, improving wind and photovoltaic (PV) accommodation has become a central requirement for integrated energy systems (IESs). This paper proposes a low-carbon day
content: Driven by carbon-neutrality targets and the rapid growth of renewable generation, improving wind and photovoltaic (PV) accommodation has become a central requirement for integrated energy systems (IESs). This paper proposes a low-carbon day-ahead joint electricity-heat market-clearing model that coordinates combined heat and power (CHP) units, gas boilers, wind power, PV generation, grid transactions, and shiftable demand. The model minimizes total operating cost and monetized direct-emission cost while satisfying fixed electricity and heat demand. Electricity and heat balances, unit operating and ramping limits, tie-line capacity, energy-neutral demand shifting, and fixed-load requirements are represented within a linear-programming framework. A 96-period numerical case is constructed from publicly available electricity-demand, renewable-generation, electricity-price, and heat-demand profiles. The results show that the renewable-curtailment rate in Scenario 1 is 12.70% under a 350 kW tie-line and a 1000 kWh/day shiftable-energy limit. Increasing shiftable energy to 2000 kWh/day reduces curtailment to 9.96%, whereas increasing tie-line capacity to 800 kW enables complete renewable accommodation. At the reference carbon price of 505 yuan/tCO2, emissions are monetized but the physical dispatch remains unchanged because the heat balance and tie-line constraint are binding. At 1500 yuan/tCO2, curtailment decreases to 0% and direct emissions decline from 13.873 to 13.333 tCO2. Increasing the CHP heat-to-power ratio from 1.0 to 1.6 further reduces curtailment from 33.10% to 1.23%. These results show that carbon pricing, demand flexibility, CHP coupling, and tie-line capacity jointly determine renewable accommodation and should therefore be coordinated in day-ahead market design.

title: Applications of bio-enhanced cementitious composites for sustainable building materials: emission-reduction and carbon-sequestration pathways
summary: This article uses knowledge mining to examine microbial strengthening mechanism in cementitious composites. Knowledge graphs and large language models (LLMs) support literature collection and curation to link established findings with recen
content: This article uses knowledge mining to examine microbial strengthening mechanism in cementitious composites. Knowledge graphs and large language models (LLMs) support literature collection and curation to link established findings with recent advances in the development of bio-cement. The review covers pathways of microbially induced calcite precipitation (MICP), microbial species, reinforcement/delivery strategies, metabolism under cementitious environments, and functional properties (i.e., self-healing, and carbon sequestration). The review article discusses the microbial physiology within cementitious matrices that consist of high alkalinity, restricted mass transport, and biomineralization. The article examines engineering limitations, including multistage and relatively slow production, dependence on moisture and nutrients, treatment byproducts, nonuniform precipitation, and uncertain long-term viability. Priorities include standardized field testing, protective delivery systems, omics-based analysis of microbial responses in cement, and machine learning ready databases. Coupling transcriptomics, metabolomics, metabolic flux analysis, and genome-scale models with AI/ML or digital twins may support strain selection and prediction of mineralization and self-healing. However, these approaches require interoperable datasets and field validation. The paper elaborates that bio-enhanced cementitious composites can support emission reduction and durable carbon sequestration. Whereas net negative performance must be demonstrated through complete life cycle analysis that accounts for greenhouse gases and microbial survivability in cementitious environments.

title: Study on freeze–thaw resistance and equivalent service-life prediction of alkali-activated desert sand concrete
summary: To help address the limited availability of natural river sand (RS) resources and evaluate the feasibility of using desert sand (DS) in alkali-activated concrete for cold regions, alkali-activated desert sand concrete (AA-DSC) was prepared
content: To help address the limited availability of natural river sand (RS) resources and evaluate the feasibility of using desert sand (DS) in alkali-activated concrete for cold regions, alkali-activated desert sand concrete (AA-DSC) was prepared by partially or fully replacing RS with DS. Its frost resistance was evaluated, and its equivalent service life was predicted. The influence of the DS replacement level was assessed using compressive strength, relative dynamic elastic modulus (RDEM), mass loss evolution, NMR, SEM, XRD, and Weibull-based modeling. The DS replacement level produced a pronounced nonlinear influence on the mechanical behavior and frost resistance of AA-DSC. The 40% DS replacement group (DS40) exhibited better overall performance. Its 91 d compressive strength reached 71.25 MPa. After 200 freeze–thaw cycles, its RDEM retention was 94.56%, and its mass loss rate was 0.23%. Combined with the microstructural analysis results, moderate DS incorporation improved particle gradation and pore-structure stability. It reduced pore connectivity and delayed microcrack propagation. Excessive DS replacement reduced workability and aggravated interfacial damage and freeze–thaw deterioration. The Weibull model developed based on RDEM attenuation could characterize the freeze–thaw degradation process of AA-DSC. Model comparison and uncertainty analysis showed that DS40 had the highest model-predicted equivalent service life under the present test conditions. These results should be used primarily for relative durability assessment among different mix proportions. This study indicates that a 40% DS replacement ratio can serve as a reference mix proportion for optimizing the freeze–thaw durability of AA-DSC.

title: Reactivity‐Guided Janus Graphene With Asymmetric Interfacial Electrostatics for Tunable Charge Transport
summary: ABSTRACT Breaking out‐of‐plane symmetry in graphene is essential to realize electrostatic control in next‐generation electronic devices. While Janus graphene, which bears chemically distinct top and bottom faces, is a promising architecture
content: ABSTRACT Breaking out‐of‐plane symmetry in graphene is essential to realize electrostatic control in next‐generation electronic devices. While Janus graphene, which bears chemically distinct top and bottom faces, is a promising architecture, establishing a controllable fabrication route and directly linking asymmetric chemistry to electronic transport remains challenging. In this study, we present a resist‐free, interface‐selective laser‐writing strategy that facilitates stepwise bottom‐to‐top covalent functionalization of graphene and enables controlled access to top‐, bottom‐, and asymmetric dual‐side configurations. Raman spectroscopy verifies that this Janus configuration reaches a substantial degree of functionalization, exhibiting a Raman‐derived defect distance ( L D ) of approximately 1.5 nm. Kelvin probe force microscopy reveals configuration‐dependent electrostatic responses, with a change of contact potential difference of approximately 225 mV for Janus graphene. Back‐gated field‐effect transistors further reveal pronounced changes in charge transport, with the residual carrier density increasing to 5.92 × 10 12 cm −2 in Janus graphene. Notably, comparison of the investigated configurations reveals a configuration‐dependent relationship between interfacial electrostatics and charge transport. Furthermore, lithographically pre‐patterned substrates enable spatially programmable Janus architectures via single‐step laser writing, providing a scalable platform for engineering symmetry‐broken two‐dimensional electronic materials.

title: An analysis of climate-related disclosures in South African listed mining firms: challenges and opportunities
summary: The study evaluates South African listed mining companies’ climate-related disclosure practices, with a perspective of both challenges and opportunities of complying with ESG reporting standards. A PRISMA protocol was employed for the selec
content: The study evaluates South African listed mining companies’ climate-related disclosure practices, with a perspective of both challenges and opportunities of complying with ESG reporting standards. A PRISMA protocol was employed for the selection of relevant articles on climate-related disclosures from Scopus databases. The screened articles were then used for content analysis, with secondary data collected from integrated reports of the top ten listed mining companies on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. The research found that there is a gradual and consistent climate-related disclosure by the top ten listed mining firms in South Africa over the years. There are substantial differences between the structure, content, metrics and level of compliance among mining firms. The practical implications of the research findings include offering insights to policymakers, investors and regulators in promoting transparency and accountability in environmental impact, as well as informing the formulation of regulations in South Africa’s corporate reporting environment. In addition, mining companies in South Africa are encouraged to align with international climate report models and dimensions to ensure business competitiveness and to boost stakeholder trust. A climate disclosure alignment framework was presented to guide researchers on the usefulness of a structured manner of evaluating current climate reporting practices in the mining sector. The study is limited to the sample size of the top 10 JSE-listed mining companies. This may not fully represent the broader mining sector, particularly small-scale miners or non-listed mining firms that may have different disclosure practices.

title: Production and Fuel Property Characterization of Biodiesels from Waste Swine Oil and Waste Cooking Oil
summary: Biodiesel fuels were produced from waste swine oil (WSO) and waste cooking oil (WCO) and evaluated in terms of fuel properties, blend characteristics, and purification requirements. The WSO feedstock had an acid value of 0.54 mg KOH/g and a
content: Biodiesel fuels were produced from waste swine oil (WSO) and waste cooking oil (WCO) and evaluated in terms of fuel properties, blend characteristics, and purification requirements. The WSO feedstock had an acid value of 0.54 mg KOH/g and an FFA content of 0.27%, indicating low free fatty acidity and allowing direct base-catalyzed transesterification without acid esterification pretreatment, while the higher-FFA WCO required acid esterification. Transesterification was investigated over methanol-to-oil molar ratios of 5:1–12:1 and KOH loadings of 0.5–2.5 wt.%, with 7:1 and 1.0 wt.% KOH selected as the optimum conditions. The biodiesels generally satisfied the evaluated ASTM D6751 requirements. WSO biodiesel contained 96.4 wt.% FAME, marginally below the EN 14214 minimum of 96.5 wt.%, while WCO biodiesel achieved 97.2 wt.%. WSO biodiesel exhibited a cetane number of approximately 65, viscosity of 5.9 mm²/s, density of 886 kg/m³, and cloud point of 14 °C, consistent with its higher saturated FAME content. WCO biodiesel exhibited a cetane number of approximately 54, viscosity of 4.7 mm²/s, density of 880 kg/m³, and improved low-temperature properties, with a cloud point of approximately 2 °C. GC–MS analysis showed that WSO FAMEs were predominantly C16:0 and C18:0, while WCO contained higher proportions of C18:1 and C18:2. ULSD blends from B20 to B80 showed improved lubricity, higher flash points, and lower sulfur levels, while calorific value decreased with increasing biodiesel content. These findings demonstrate the viability of WSO and WCO as biodiesel feedstocks, with WSO providing higher ignition quality but requiring more intensive post-reaction purification and washing.

title: Inverse CeO 2 /Cu Catalysts with Engineered Cu + ‐O V ‐Ce 3+ Interfacial Sites for Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction
summary: ABSTRACT The reverse water‐gas shift (RWGS) reaction can serve as a pivotal hub for converting CO 2 into value‐added chemicals. However, conventional Cu/CeO 2 catalysts are constrained by a limited metal‐oxide interfacial perimeter, sufferi
content: ABSTRACT The reverse water‐gas shift (RWGS) reaction can serve as a pivotal hub for converting CO 2 into value‐added chemicals. However, conventional Cu/CeO 2 catalysts are constrained by a limited metal‐oxide interfacial perimeter, suffering from both inadequate low‐temperature activity and poor stability. Herein, a series of CeO 2 /Cu‐x catalysts (where x is the Ce/Cu molar ratio) were synthesized via an oxalic acid‐assisted sol‐gel coprecipitation method, and tested for RWGS at 400°C and atmospheric pressure. The optimal inverse CeO 2 /Cu‐0.1 achieves an intrinsic reaction rate of 197.0 µmol·g cat −1 ·s −1 , which is 3.7 times higher than that of the conventional CeO 2 /Cu‐10 (53.1 µmol·g cat −1 ·s −1 ) and is much more stable. Structural analyses revealed that the CeO 2 /Cu‐0.1 is characterized by an inverse architecture of tiny CeO 2 crystallites (4.6 nm) on larger Cu particles (12.7 nm), which is distinct from conventional architecture of Cu clusters (3.3 nm) on larger CeO 2 particles (7.1 nm) for CeO 2 /Cu‐10. The inverse architecture significantly improves the density of Cu + ‐O V ‐Ce 3+ sites at the interfacial perimeter of CeO 2 /Cu, which facilitates the synergistic activation of H 2 and CO 2 as well as subsequent reaction, leading to lower reaction orders and a much higher intrinsic rate. This work demonstrates the inverse oxide/metal architecture with engineered oxide‐metal interfacial sites for enhancing RWGS.

title: Distributive Justice in Social Guarantees for Workers in Hazardous Working Conditions
summary: The system of social guarantees for workers engaged in harmful and dangerous working conditions remains an important element of social protection. The purpose of the study is to assess the distributional fairness of the current system of so
content: The system of social guarantees for workers engaged in harmful and dangerous working conditions remains an important element of social protection. The purpose of the study is to assess the distributional fairness of the current system of social guarantees in Kazakhstan, compare it with foreign models and determine the possibilities of transition from a list–based to a risk-based mechanism for providing guarantees. The research methods include comparative institutional and legal analysis, targeted content analysis of legislation, descriptive statistical analysis, as well as an assessment of the financial and incentive effects of the proposed reform. The initial data cover the legislation of 11 countries — six CIS countries (Kazakhstan, Russia, Belarus, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Armenia) and five OECD countries (USA, Germany, Great Britain, France, Canada), as well as data from the form of the Bureau of National Statistics of the Republic of Kazakhstan for 2021-2025. The results showed that the number of employees receiving at least one social guarantee remained virtually unchanged, while the share of those covered by guarantees decreased from 41.54% to 38.75% (-2.79 percentage points). Employers' expenses increased from 167.9 to 341.9 billion tenge, that is, by 2.04 times in nominal terms and by 26.4% in real terms the expression. The proposed transition to the differentiation of guarantees according to the measured risk level and the contribution scale of 3-9% allows maintaining fiscal neutrality and at the same time creating an economic incentive for the employer to reduce occupational risk.

title: Accounting for short-term durability in carbon offsetting
summary: Durability, the length of time carbon dioxide is stored before potential re-release to the atmosphere, is a critical yet underdeveloped dimension of carbon offset quality.While the voluntary carbon market trades both short-term and long-ter
content: Durability, the length of time carbon dioxide is stored before potential re-release to the atmosphere, is a critical yet underdeveloped dimension of carbon offset quality.While the voluntary carbon market trades both short-term and long-term carbon storage as fungible "one tonne" credits, the climate implications of these two classes of removal differ fundamentally.In this commentary, we examine the conceptual and practical challenges of accounting for shortterm durability in carbon offsetting.We distinguish between two strategies for reconciling temporary storage with robust neutralization claims: horizontal stacking, in which credits are sequentially renewed as they expire, and vertical stacking, in which multiple short-term credits are purchased upfront to approximate the climate benefit of permanent storage.We evaluate the assumptions, trade-offs, and market constraints associated with each approach and argue that transparent, science-grounded frameworks for durability accounting are essential to the integrity of corporate net-zero claims.We conclude by recommending portfolio-based approaches that pair near-term, high-quality temporary removals with investments in durable engineered storage.

title: GlycoMAC: A Multiscale Metabolic‐Glycosylation Framework for Predicting Glycosylation Across Conditions in Mammalian Cell Cultures
summary: Antibody productivity and glycosylation quality in CHO cell cultures emerge from a dynamically evolving metabolic environment, yet existing models often work in isolation or at a single scale. Here, we present a multiscale mechanistic frame
content: Antibody productivity and glycosylation quality in CHO cell cultures emerge from a dynamically evolving metabolic environment, yet existing models often work in isolation or at a single scale. Here, we present a multiscale mechanistic framework linking molecular, cellular, and macroscopic scales to predict how inputs shape bioprocess trajectories. The framework combines a single-cell kinetic model of metabolism and glycosylation with a stochastic population model that captures environment-dependent transitions among growth, production, and decline states. To characterize metabolic adaptation, we introduce the cumulative variation in oxygen uptake rate, a trajectory-based biomarker that quantifies the total metabolic adjustment experienced during culture. Unlike population-averaged approaches, the model propagates cell-resolved metabolic states-including ammonia-regulated Golgi pH, nucleotide sugar availability, manganese cofactors, and synthesis rates-into glycan processing. The framework was evaluated using CHO-K1 fed-batch cultures producing VRC01 IgG1 under targeted ammonia stress, matched control conditions, and a pyramid-feeding strategy with tighter control. It accurately reproduced trajectories of cell growth, metabolites, productivity, and harvest glycosylation, including increased G0F abundance and reduced galactosylation under ammonia stress. By mechanistically linking process conditions to cell-state dynamics and glycosylation outcomes, the framework provides a unified foundation for digital bioprocessing, predictive biomanufacturing, and advanced process control.

title: A Study on North-South Rule Conflicts in the Global Climate Governance System
summary: Frequent extreme climate events across the globe underscore the urgency of the global climate governance system. Within the current global climate governance system centered on the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFC
content: Frequent extreme climate events across the globe underscore the urgency of the global climate governance system. Within the current global climate governance system centered on the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), several principles and mechanisms coexist: differentiated responsibilities, Kyoto flexibility mechanisms, and the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. Nevertheless, divergences persist between developed and developing countries regarding the delineation of historical responsibilities, guarantee of financial inputs, transfer of green technologies, and the right to development. Some unilateral climate measures have prompted debate about their compatibility with multilateral frameworks, which may widen the North-South trust gap and fragments the global climate governance system. After analyzing the dilemmas embedded in the existing governance regime, this paper proposes three pathways for reforming the global climate governance system: accelerating the establishment of a more equitable accounting system, strengthening the coordination and binding force of existing rules, and promptly addressing the shortfalls in finance and technology transfer.

title: From point-to-point to hub-and-cluster: a systematic review of co-optimization of source–sink matching and transport networks for large-scale CO2 sequestration
summary: Large-scale carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) requires coordinated source–sink matching (SSM), transport infrastructure, and geological storage planning. This review examines how published studies couple source allocation, net
content: Large-scale carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) requires coordinated source–sink matching (SSM), transport infrastructure, and geological storage planning. This review examines how published studies couple source allocation, network topology and capacity, CO 2 flow, and storage availability. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, a reproducible Web of Science and Scopus search identified 17 studies for direct evidence synthesis. The evidence shows that integrated models can jointly represent source–sink allocation, transport-network investment, operational flow, and storage constraints, whereas sequential approaches may overlook system-wide trade-offs. Mathematical programming remains the most auditable basis for strategic planning because it provides explicit feasibility constraints and, in some cases, optimality bounds. Hub-and-cluster and multimodal configurations can improve infrastructure sharing, but their value depends on utilization, phased connection, access conditions, and cost recovery. Evidence for metaheuristics and AI-enabled methods remains case-specific; their comparative value cannot be established without common instances and complete reporting of feasibility, solution quality, and computational effort. Future research should develop physically valid large-scale benchmarks, adaptive planning models, and governance-aware mechanisms for shared CCUS infrastructure.

title: The FAST tool for synthetic SXR calculations and determination of impurity density and effective charge (Z eff )
summary: Abstract A new soft x-ray (SXR) synthetic tool has been developed: it is called FAST for FLYCHK-based Atomic physics and SXR Tomography. It is based on FLYCHK SXR emissivity spectra calculated for a variety of elements, from deuterium to tu
content: Abstract A new soft x-ray (SXR) synthetic tool has been developed: it is called FAST for FLYCHK-based Atomic physics and SXR Tomography. It is based on FLYCHK SXR emissivity spectra calculated for a variety of elements, from deuterium to tungsten. FAST creates 2D plasma emissivity for arbitrary plasma compositions and plasma profiles. It computes line-integrated SXR profiles based on a specific detector geometry and response. This tool is used to reproduce signals from an absolutely calibrated multi-energy SXR (ME-SXR) camera at WEST. Thanks to its energy-resolved measurement capability, the ME-SXR camera is able to separate spectral regions dominated by impurity line emission from others containing only continuum emission. At WEST, FAST and the ME-SXR camera are employed to determine impurity density profiles for tungsten and nitrogen (used as a proxy for low-Z impurities), as well as the plasma effective charge (Zeff), through SXR measurement reproduction at different energies, from 2 to 14 keV. Tungsten density is determined in two plasma scenarios at WEST: lower hybrid heating in the X-point radiator regime and lower hybrid heating with modulations of ion cyclotron resonance heating. In the first scenario the tungsten profile is found to be moderately peaked in the core with a concentration of 0.8‒1×10-4. This concentration is found to increase up to 1.4×10-4 during ion cyclotron resonance heating. Tungsten peaking factor in steady-state conditions is also retrieved and compared to theoretical predictions. It is found to be slightly lower than the combined neoclassical and turbulent transport prediction.

title: Advancing 100% renewable electricity in Tunisia: techno-economic pathways for integrating solar PV, hydropower, and pumped hydro energy storage
summary: Introduction Although Tunisia has a large potential for renewable energy, it is still heavily reliant on traditional biomass and fossil fuels, with each resident consuming only 0.5 MWh of electricity annually. This low level of consumption
content: Introduction Although Tunisia has a large potential for renewable energy, it is still heavily reliant on traditional biomass and fossil fuels, with each resident consuming only 0.5 MWh of electricity annually. This low level of consumption highlights the need for a long-term electrification strategy that would enable a more significant energy transformation. Methods This study explores the path to 100% renewable energy by directing final consumption sectors toward electricity, using a daily energy balance model of Tunisia’s electrical future until 2050. Solar photovoltaic (PV) and hydroelectric power are modeled as primary energy sources, while pumped hydro energy storage (PHES) and transboundary electricity imports are used for system equilibrium. Two scenarios are analyzed for 2050, including three levels of electricity demand (2.6 and 9.1 MWh per inhabitant and annually), two hydroelectricity development trajectories (ambitious and established), and scenarios with or without electricity imports. Results The results show that solar photovoltaic energy is the main source of production in most scenarios, but PHES plays a crucial role in daily and seasonal equilibrium. According to the main theories put forth, the levelised cost of electricity (LCOE) ranges from 17 TND/KWh to 24 TND/KWh. The sensitivity analysis revealed that photovoltaic costs, actualization rates, and hydroelectricity production scenarios are economic determinants. These results show that Tunisia’s future energy needs may be largely met by proven and developed renewable technology. Discussion These lessons are useful for long-term energy planning and provide guidance to other countries with similar low electricity consumption. They also support the realization of long-term development goals (SDG), such as SDG 13 (Fighting climate change) and SDG 7 (Clean and affordable energy).

title: Hydrogen valleys: Advancing the hydrogen economy through decarbonization, energy flexibility, and sector coupling
summary: To support the energy-system transition toward climate neutrality, scalable solutions that enable renewable electricity integration, multi-sector coupling, flexibility, and carbon-emission reduction are increasingly required. However, no ex
content: To support the energy-system transition toward climate neutrality, scalable solutions that enable renewable electricity integration, multi-sector coupling, flexibility, and carbon-emission reduction are increasingly required. However, no existing review provides a cross-project assessment of hydrogen valleys as an integrated deployment model. This review addresses this gap by developing an Integrated Hydrogen Valley Systems Framework grounded in Industrial Ecology, Energy Hub theory, and Technological Innovation Systems theory. Using an evidence-based approach, we systematically analyse all 90 hydrogen valley projects listed in the Clean Hydrogen Partnership's H2V database. Peer-reviewed studies, official project databases, technical reports, and policy documents are synthesised to compare renewable-energy integration pathways, electrolyser technologies, hydrogen storage and transport options, sector-coupling strategies, and supporting policy frameworks. The findings indicate that hydrogen valleys can facilitate the integration of wind and solar power, enhance energy-system flexibility, enable long-duration energy storage, and contribute to carbon-emission reductions of up to 30%, with a levelised cost of hydrogen of approximately €5.6/kg under an optimal sector-coupling scenario. Proton exchange membrane and alkaline electrolysers account for most deployments, particularly in Europe. Nevertheless, project development remains constrained by renewable-resource variability, high capital costs, limited infrastructure, regulatory gaps, and supply-chain constraints. The review identifies key policy priorities, including technology-neutral investment support, harmonised cross-border hydrogen-trade frameworks, accelerated permitting, and expanded electrolyser manufacturing capacity, to strengthen the scalability and global development of hydrogen valleys.

title: Sensitivity of biogenic carbon and heat fluxes to urban vegetation parametrisations in the urban land surface model SUEWS
summary: Abstract. As cities are taking actions to reduce their carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, the potential of urban vegetation to act as a carbon sink has received increasing attention. Carbon sequestration, however, has large uncertainties due t
content: Abstract. As cities are taking actions to reduce their carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, the potential of urban vegetation to act as a carbon sink has received increasing attention. Carbon sequestration, however, has large uncertainties due to the highly variable and mosaic nature of urban vegetation. For land surface models to realistically estimate carbon sinks in urban areas, they need to be able to describe various urban vegetation types and their responses to environmental controls. One such model is the Surface Urban Energy and Water balance Scheme (SUEWS), which is an urban land surface model that can simulate energy, water and CO2 exchanges in cities. For SUEWS to accurately simulate the biogenic CO2 fluxes, it requires information on surface conductance controlling stomatal opening, maximum photosynthesis values, and parameters for soil and vegetation respiration. The main aims of this study are to provide a more comprehensive set of vegetation parameters derived from eddy covariance and chamber observations to extend the usability of SUEWS in different cities, and to evaluate the selection of the specific vegetation parameters on SUEWS model performance in two mid-latitude cities: Swindon (UK) and Minneapolis (US). The results highlight the importance of appropriate selection of surface conductance, maximum photosynthesis, and soil and vegetation parameters for different types of vegetation to be able to accurately simulate the biogenic and net carbon fluxes at monthly and annual level. Surface conductance parameters are most affected by soil moisture and specific humidity, rather than radiation and air temperature. The model performs better with tree surface conductance parameters (R = 0.62–0.70 in Swindon, R = 0.61–0.74 in Minneapolis) than lawn or low vegetation parameters (R ≤ 0.48 in Swindon, R ≤ 0.72 in Minneapolis), even in areas with smaller tree cover, highlighting the significance of urban trees in controlling overall stomatal conductance. The sensitivity of CO2 fluxes to parameter selection is greater than that of latent heat fluxes with R ranging between -0.26–0.74 when compared to 0.60–0.90. Carbon balances are influenced by traffic levels, air temperatures, and rates of photosynthesis and soil respiration. Overall, the findings emphasize the necessity for accurate observations of urban vegetation to effectively parameterise urban vegetation and soil, as using inappropriate reference vegetation can lead to substantial errors in estimating biogenic exchanges.

title: Microstructure-transport coupling in titaniferous magnetite pre-reduction: Porosity evolution, Ti-phase effects, and modelling for low-carbon ironmaking
summary: Titaniferous magnetite (TTM) is among the largest reserves of underexploited iron ore resources. Titanium-bearing minerals including ilmenite, pseudobrookite, and enriched titanium spinel phases alter reduction mechanisms, pore structure de
content: Titaniferous magnetite (TTM) is among the largest reserves of underexploited iron ore resources. Titanium-bearing minerals including ilmenite, pseudobrookite, and enriched titanium spinel phases alter reduction mechanisms, pore structure development, and transport phenomena in ways that traditional iron oxide models cannot capture. This review addresses that gap by consolidating recent developments in the solid-state, packed-bed pre-reduction of TTM, a process whose literature remains comparatively scarce relative to conventional hematite, with emphasis on the coupling between microstructural evolution and transport processes across particle, pellet, and reactor scales. Topics covered include porosity transitions from uni-modal to bi-modal pore structures, the competing roles of sintering and pore formation in controlling permeability, the effect of Ti-phase enrichment on the transition from chemical to diffusion control, reaction-front progression, the influence of carbonaceous and gaseous reductants, and multiphysics computational fluid dynamics modelling of heat, gas-phase transport, and phase transformation across scales. Since direct TTM evidence remains sparse relative to conventional ore, this review also develops testable, semi-quantitative hypotheses linking Ti-phase persistence to permeability loss, percolation-threshold shifts, and whisker-versus-dense-shell morphology, alongside three outstanding gaps: the absence of data linking titanium-phase formation to permeability under realistic flowing-gas conditions, the lack of pore-scale investigation under titaniferous conditions, and the absence of a multiphysics CFD model incorporating Fe-Ti-O multicomponent thermochemistry in packed-bed reactors. Insights from synchrotron visualization, thermogravimetric kinetics, and reactor simulation provide a foundation for efficient, low-carbon pre-reduction of titaniferous magnetite.

title: Flexible energy management of hybrid hydrogen-electric power system considering temperature-induced characteristics in unmanned aerial vehicle applications
summary: In hybrid hydrogen-electric unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications, efficient energy management for the hybrid hydrogen-electric power system (HEPS) combining the hydrogen fuel cell (HFC) module with the lithium battery (LiBa) module is
content: In hybrid hydrogen-electric unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications, efficient energy management for the hybrid hydrogen-electric power system (HEPS) combining the hydrogen fuel cell (HFC) module with the lithium battery (LiBa) module is vitally important for the long-term and steady power supply. However, conventional energy management strategies (EMSs) generally assume a constant ambient temperature and employ fixed control thresholds for power allocation. This assumption is unsuitable for UAV missions involving rapid altitude changes, during which the time-varying ambient temperature alters the operating characteristics of both power sources, particularly the maximum power point (MPP) of the HFC and the maximum available capacity (MAC) of the LiBa. Consequently, fixed-threshold EMSs may result in inappropriate power allocation and hinder efficient cooperative operation of the two power sources under changing flight conditions. In this study, a flexible energy management strategy for the hybrid HEPS considering its temperature-induced characteristics is proposed for UAV applications. At first, the hybrid HEPS architecture for the UAV is analyzed, and models of the HFC module and the LiBa module are established. Then, to accurately reflect the variations in the MPP and the MAC of the two energy sources under dynamic ambient temperature conditions, nonlinear compensation schemes are constructed in accordance with temperature-induced characteristics of the two energy sources, respectively. Moreover, to achieve efficient energy management for the HEPS, the flexible EMS with nonlinear compensation schemes is developed. Finally, simulations and experiments are carried out to validate the effectiveness of the flexible EMS for the HEPS in UAV applications. Compared with the traditional rule-based EMS, the proposed flexible EMS improves the UAV endurance by 11.6% and 14.6% under two operating conditions, respectively.

title: Mitigation of potential-induced degradation phenomena using Li in crystalline Si photovoltaic modules
summary: Abstract This study investigated on mitigation methods for shunting-type potential-induced degradation (PID-s) of wafer-based standard p-type crystalline silicon technology. Lithium did not cause PID-s and only sodium caused substantial PID
content: Abstract This study investigated on mitigation methods for shunting-type potential-induced degradation (PID-s) of wafer-based standard p-type crystalline silicon technology. Lithium did not cause PID-s and only sodium caused substantial PID-s. To quantitatively explore the relationship between them, we used a module without a cover glass and an additional encapsulation material on the solar cell light-receiving surface and performed PID tests with lithium and sodium contamination. Moreover, we measured the current density-voltage characteristics and captured electroluminescence images during the test, and we performed secondary ion mass spectrometry on certain modules. When sodium was present, the performance degradation of the solar cell remained the same as that of typical PID-s, although introducing lithium substantially decelerated performance degradation. Concurrently, the long-term PID test showed that performance degradation, occurred even with a low sodium concentration (< 0.1 mmol∙L-1). This indicates that lithium can only mitigate, but not inhibit PID-s when sodium is present.

title: Single‐Atom Active Sites in Polymeric Phthalocyanine Hybrid Electrocatalysis for High‐Efficiency Lithium–Carbon Dioxide Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Lithium–carbon dioxide (Li–CO 2 ) batteries represent a compelling dual‐function technology that simultaneously enables electrochemical energy storage and CO 2 capture for carbon neutrality. However, the inherent insulating nature
content: ABSTRACT Lithium–carbon dioxide (Li–CO 2 ) batteries represent a compelling dual‐function technology that simultaneously enables electrochemical energy storage and CO 2 capture for carbon neutrality. However, the inherent insulating nature and high thermodynamic stability of lithium carbonate (Li 2 CO 3 ) discharged product impose excessive charge overpotentials and rapid capacity fade that limit practical deployment. Here, we demonstrate polymerized copper phthalocyanine immobilized on carbon nanotubes (CuPPc@CNT) as a noble‐metal‐free cathode electrocatalyst that harnesses atomically dispersed Cu–N 4 single‐atom active sites to overcome these limitations. The in situ polymerization of copper phthalocyanine units through triethylene glycol linkers enables conformal, non‐aggregated coating on the CNT surface via strong π–π interactions, ensuring efficient charge transfer and long‐term interfacial stability. The CuPPc@CNT cathode delivers a markedly reduced overpotential of 1.06 V and sustains capacity‐limited cycling up to 120 cycles, outperforming both pristine CNT and lithium polyphthalocyanine‐based counterparts. Ex situ surface characterization and in situ differential electrochemical mass spectrometry confirm highly reversible Li 2 CO 3 formation and decomposition, while theoretical calculations reveal that the Cu–N 4 coordination center provides a moderate binding strength for Li 2 CO 3 and reduces the discharge–charge potential gap to 1.43 V. These findings establish polymeric metal phthalocyanine–carbon nanotube hybrids as an advanced electrocatalyst platform for next‐generation Li–CO 2 battery technologies.

title: Structure Selection in Ionic Colloidal Crystals via Independent Charge Tuning
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Colloidal building blocks can assemble into many different crystal structures, yet selecting a specific lattice without redesigning the particles remains a central challenge in programmable self-assembly. Here we demonstrate that i
content: Abstract Colloidal building blocks can assemble into many different crystal structures, yet selecting a specific lattice without redesigning the particles remains a central challenge in programmable self-assembly. Here we demonstrate that independent tuning of colloidal surface charge enables deterministic structure selection using a fixed pair of oppositely charged colloids. Micromolar additions of simple ionic surfactants independently adjust the surface charge of each colloidal species without significantly altering solution ionic strength, allowing the same building blocks to assemble into Th3P4-, CsCl-, Cu3Au-, and Li3Fe-like crystals, the last of which represents a previously unreported colloidal crystal structure. Experiments and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that structure selection is governed by the competition between Coulombic attraction and lattice-specific like-charge repulsion. Experiments across different particle-size ratios further demonstrate the generality of this approach, with additional surfactant-induced transitions between Th3P4-, AlB2-, and Cr3Si-like structures. These findings establish charge asymmetry as a general design parameter for ionic colloidal assembly.

title: SCHEMA FOR AI DRIVEN MUNICIPALITY
summary: Many municipalities adopt artificial intelligence without knowing if their supporting data is accurate, turning municipal decision-making into an opaque "black box." To address this, we introduce the AI Flow for Municipalities, an evidence-
content: Many municipalities adopt artificial intelligence without knowing if their supporting data is accurate, turning municipal decision-making into an opaque "black box." To address this, we introduce the AI Flow for Municipalities, an evidence-led orchestration system developed under the Czech CESMOD project. Built upon the national Smart Cities Concept, the system utilizes the 4-Diamonds framework and an expert-curated Information and Data Platform (IDP) to map unstructured municipal queries into multi-sectoral, policy-compliant recommendations. By providing auditable data provenance and clear contextual logic, this transparent framework enables genuinely data-driven territorial development and offers a scalable model for explainable AI governance.

title: The schism of strategic planning in the climate crisis
summary: Strategic planning is traditionally defined as a broader, more flexible process compared to statutory spatial planning. It most often involves investments and partnerships in urban development projects, increasing carbon emissions as a resu
content: Strategic planning is traditionally defined as a broader, more flexible process compared to statutory spatial planning. It most often involves investments and partnerships in urban development projects, increasing carbon emissions as a result. This creates a schism between the stated sustainable development objectives and the actual consequences of strategic planning. This study first tracked this schism in academic discourse across three different approaches to strategic planning. It revealed that the focus on ‘strategic’ in planning literature contrasts with the urgent commitments required for climate change mitigation. Second, the study investigated how this schism manifests in the two case studies of the tourism strategy and mobility planning in Copenhagen, Denmark. Given their significant role in urban development, tourism and mobility planning have major consequences for carbon emissions. Through a critical policy analysis, the case studies reveal how the schism unfolded – not only as a schism between vision and practice but also as contradictions within policy documents. The findings highlight the critical need to rethink strategic planning to effectively address the challenges of the climate crisis. Effective climate change mitigation requires a fundamentally different kind of strategic planning that is focused on reducing activities that produce carbon emissions.

title: Scope 3 emissions reporting as an instrument for accelerating sustainable aviation fuel deployment
summary: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a key near-term option for aviation decarbonisation, but its large-scale deployment is constrained by high production costs. At the same time, governance mechanisms, such as ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Re
content: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is a key near-term option for aviation decarbonisation, but its large-scale deployment is constrained by high production costs. At the same time, governance mechanisms, such as ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and Scope 3 emissions reporting under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, are reshaping incentives across the aviation value chain. This study conducts a systematic literature review of Scope 3 reporting, aviation decarbonisation technologies, and sectoral governance. Based on these insights, it proposes a conceptual financing framework showing how Scope 3 reporting can enable cost-sharing business models for SAF. The framework identifies emerging practices where corporates pay the SAF premium in exchange for Scope 3 credits, airlines cover conventional fuel costs and retain Scope 1 credits, and producers gain demand certainty.

title: Biomass and plastic waste-derived pyrolysis oils for asphalt pavement applications: A review of technology readiness levels and future perspectives
source: Journal of Analytical and Applied Pyrolysis
summary: Rising demand for sustainable infrastructure makes pyrolysis oils a promising renewable alternative to petroleum asphalt. This review critically evaluates the conversion of biomass and plastic waste into pyrolysis oils and their heavy fract
content: Rising demand for sustainable infrastructure makes pyrolysis oils a promising renewable alternative to petroleum asphalt. This review critically evaluates the conversion of biomass and plastic waste into pyrolysis oils and their heavy fractions, focusing on feedstock composition, pyrolysis conditions, upgrading requirements, binder-asphalt performance and technology readiness. Pyrolysis is generally conducted at 300–700 °C, and maximum oil yield is commonly reported within 400–600 °C. Liquid yields vary widely. Intermediate pyrolysis gives roughly 40–50% liquids; individual studies report 10.6% for the organic fraction of municipal solid waste and 50.2% for Prosopis juliflora at 450 °C. In waste-tyre studies, thermal and microwave pyrolysis produced comparable liquid yields (40.4 and 39.1 wt%), but microwave heating cut reaction time from 80 to 18 min and calculated energy demand by 73.02%. Biomass heavy bio-oil can hold up to 45 wt% oxygen, causing high acidity, poor stability and limited compatibility with conventional bitumen, so it usually needs fractionation, catalytic upgrading or controlled blending. The most viable near-term route is not replacing bitumen outright but aromatic-enriched heavy bio-oil fractions from lignin-rich feedstocks via established fast pyrolysis, followed by fractionation or catalytic stabilisation and controlled partial blending with bitumen. Conventional pyrolysis is commercially mature (TRL 8–9), but catalytic upgrading and asphalt applications are still developing (TRL 3–6). Large-scale adoption is limited by product instability, high water/oxygen content, catalyst deactivation, and a lack of standardized specs and field performance data. Commercial success requires integrated pilot production, consistent binder formulation, and full-scale pavement trials.

title: A forecast-to-dispatch workflow for day-ahead operation of a regional natural gas transmission network based on station-level load prediction and linepack target setting
summary: Day-ahead operation of regional natural gas transmission networks requires station demand forecasts and their translation into inventory-preparation references. This study evaluated a sequential forecast-to-dispatch workflow for the Chongqi
content: Day-ahead operation of regional natural gas transmission networks requires station demand forecasts and their translation into inventory-preparation references. This study evaluated a sequential forecast-to-dispatch workflow for the Chongqing regional gas network. Six forecasting models were assessed under a leakage-controlled 30-day walk-forward protocol. Across nine routine stations, mean station-level MAPE was 8.61% for SARIMAX, 8.95% for XGBoost, and 9.78% for GRU. The corresponding values were 10.93% for LSTM, 11.63% for BPNN, and 11.77% for CNN-BiLSTM-Attention. Station G was assessed separately as a data-quality boundary case; Station K was excluded because only 62 observations were available. An independent archived 18-day hourly dataset reported reconstruction MAPE of 6.7%-8.1% and peak-timing deviations of 1.0-1.5 h. A retrospective West-pipeline case for 22 April 2023 traced historical station forecasts through weighted aggregation, intermediate rounding, hourly reconstruction, and reduced-order linepack calculation. Its LFFX preparation target and the separate NGXDD and DLFX targets were 1.272, 4.702, and 1.571 × 10⁶ m³, respectively. All three targets passed case-specific deterministic inventory checks. The results support station-specific forecast-model selection and an explicit interface between daily prediction and segment-level inventory preparation.

title: Quantifying hydrogen production policy in the Middle East: Distance-to-frontier diagnostics and policy design
summary: This paper develops a transparent, auditable benchmark of hydrogen policies across five leading Middle Eastern countries, focusing solely on production-stage indicators. Based on a hydrogen production projects database, seven binary indicat
content: This paper develops a transparent, auditable benchmark of hydrogen policies across five leading Middle Eastern countries, focusing solely on production-stage indicators. Based on a hydrogen production projects database, seven binary indicators are coded under four policy pillars: Strategy/Targets, Funding & Market, Standards & Certification, and Permitting & Administration, restricted to enacted instruments (laws, decrees, or rulebooks). Three complementary metrics quantify policy performance: pairwise Hamming Distance ( D HAM ) for structural similarity, pillar-vector L 1 Distance ( D L 1 ) for policy intensity, and Distance-to-Frontier ( G ) for missing frontier features. Under the specified seven-indicator rubric, the observed country-policy vectors form two groups: Egypt and Oman lie on the empirical regional frontier ( Composite = 0.625 ; D L 1 = 0.375 ; G = 0.000 ), whereas the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia share a second policy configuration ( Composite = 0.250 ; D L 1 = 0.750 ; G = 0.286 ), characterized by gaps in implementing authority and production permitting. Enacting either missing instrument reduces the frontier gap by half, while enacting both achieves frontier parity. Weighting sensitivity shows that the country ordering remains unchanged under ±20% pillar-weight variations, conditional on the fixed indicator set. The framework offers a reproducible, data-driven method to evaluate and guide hydrogen policy reforms, supporting transparent assessment and reform of enacted hydrogen-production policy instruments in the Middle East.

title: Green Fiscal Policy and Sustainable Development in ASEAN Countries: Evidence From a Bayesian Spatial Regression Approach
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between green fiscal policy and Sustainable Development in 10 ASEAN countries during 2002–2024, focusing on the moderating role of Institutional Quality and spatial spillovers. It analyzes Green
content: ABSTRACT This study examines the relationship between green fiscal policy and Sustainable Development in 10 ASEAN countries during 2002–2024, focusing on the moderating role of Institutional Quality and spatial spillovers. It analyzes Green Public Expenditure, Environmental Tax, Green Public Investment, and a PCA‐based Green Fiscal Policy Index using a Bayesian Spatial Durbin Model. The study contributes to the literature by integrating multiple green fiscal instruments, testing the moderating role of Institutional Quality, and identifying cross‐country spillovers within a unified Bayesian spatial framework. The results show that all green fiscal policy measures are positively associated with Sustainable Development, while stronger Institutional Quality reinforces these relationships. Positive direct and indirect effects indicate both domestic and regional benefits. CO 2 emissions and Inflation are negatively associated with Sustainable Development, whereas Technological Capacity, Trade Openness, and Financial Development are positively associated. The findings support stronger institutions, coordinated green fiscal policies, and greater regional cooperation in green investment and sustainable infrastructure.

title: Review: design, function, and translation of next-generation nanocomposite materials for energy conversion and storage applications
summary: The urgent transition towards sustainable energy technologies has intensified interest in nanocomposite materials that combine complementary physicochemical properties beyond those achievable with individual components. By integrating multi
content: The urgent transition towards sustainable energy technologies has intensified interest in nanocomposite materials that combine complementary physicochemical properties beyond those achievable with individual components. By integrating multiple nanoscale constituents, nanocomposites enable tailoring of electrical, mechanical, thermal, and interfacial properties, making them promising materials for next-generation energy technologies. This review critically examines recent advances in the rational design, synthesis, and characterisation of nanocomposites for energy conversion, including solar cells and fuel cells, and energy storage, including supercapacitors (SCs) and lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). This review emphasises structure–interface–property–performance relationships and the mechanisms by which nanocomposite architecture influences charge and ion transport, reaction kinetics, structural stability, and device performance. Beyond summarising recent developments, this review critically evaluates emerging material architectures, interfacial engineering strategies, and scalable fabrication approaches, together with the trade-offs between laboratory-scale performance and practical implementation. Finally, it assesses key challenges related to long-term durability, reproducibility, cost, environmental sustainability, and end-of-life considerations. Future research priorities are proposed to guide the development of nanocomposite materials towards durable, scalable, and sustainable energy conversion and storage technologies.

title: Binary phosphonium ionic liquids induced synergistic modulation of electrochemical performance in polymer electrolytes for dual energy devices
summary: The advancement of cost-effective, efficient and sustainable electrochemical devices has garnered significate interest, leading to an aggressive expansion of research aimed at enhancing their performance across various dimensions, including
content: The advancement of cost-effective, efficient and sustainable electrochemical devices has garnered significate interest, leading to an aggressive expansion of research aimed at enhancing their performance across various dimensions, including electrode, electrolytes and even computational perspectives. Ionic liquids infused with polymer electrolytes have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for advanced devices, owing to their high conductivity and electrochemical stability. In this study, we present a binary system comprising a polymer electrolyte and phosphonium ionic liquids (PIL), employing polyethylene oxide (PEO) as host matrix and two phosphonium ionic liquids—specifically, tributylmethylphosphonium iodide (TMPI) and tributylmethylphosphonium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TBMP-TFSI) at various compositions, with the aim of significantly enhancing ionic conductivity and wettability. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals that the incorporation of a binary ionic liquid (IL) leads to a maximum ionic conductivity of 2.04 × 10⁻³ S/cm. Structural analyses confirmed the optimization of the amorphous phase and segmental motion within the polymer matrix. The optimized polymer electrolyte was subsequently evaluated in an electric double-layer capacitor (EDLC), achieving a specific capacitance of 138 F/g at a scan rate of 10 mV/s. The EDLC achieved a maximum specific discharge capacitance of 109 F/g, with a coulombic efficiency of 90%, an energy density of 17.7 Wh/kg and a power density of 5.4 kW/kg. Furthermore, its application in a dye-sensitized solar cell resulted in a power conversion efficiency of 1.48%. These results demonstrate that the optimized polymer electrolyte exhibits enhanced photovoltaic efficiency in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) and high capacitive performance in electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), thereby illustrating its dual functionality.

title: Copper Recovery from Metallurgical Slags Using Biomass in the Form of Fruit Seeds/Stones as a Reducing Agent
summary: Civilizational development, which depends on the availability of raw materials, has accelerated tremendously in recent decades. This is due to globalization and the growth of emerging markets. It represents a huge opportunity for an innovat
content: Civilizational development, which depends on the availability of raw materials, has accelerated tremendously in recent decades. This is due to globalization and the growth of emerging markets. It represents a huge opportunity for an innovative approach to both production and consumption. Along with civilizational growth, we also face negative consequences that lead to climate change. To meet the demands regarding climate neutrality, people have started analyzing the possibility of running production processes using substrates that either eliminate or significantly reduce the use of non-renewable resources. Considering the specifics of metal extraction and production, it is important to note that chemistry and thermodynamics play a key role here. This involves, on the one hand, understanding how carbon or its oxides are absorbed, which is essential for plant growth, and on the other, using components of so-called biomass for controlled chemical reactions. These regulations regarding climate neutrality and the type of raw materials are reflected in detail in the relevant European Union directives. Copper production in Poland is a strategic sector of the economy. Considering the scale of production and the consumption of natural resources, developing the possibility of partially replacing them will constitute a process innovation. Research into copper recovery from slag to date has focused primarily on improving the efficiency of the slag reduction process by intensifying bath mixing and improving the mass transfer process in the liquid phase. Given that biomass contains a significant proportion of volatile matter, this may additionally have a beneficial impact on the efficiency of using this type of material in the process. Many parameters still need to be investigated before the obtained results can be tested on a larger scale, enabling transfer to industrial conditions. The study presented the results of research on the potential use of biomass to reduce secondary raw materials coming from the copper industry. A Gibbs free enthalpy analysis was carried out for possible chemical reactions and their likelihood of occurring. As a source of metals, a material similar in composition to slag generated in the copper industry was used. Considering that copper ores contain about 1 wt. %, it makes even more sense to use secondary slag, which contains up to 10 wt. % copper. As part of the work, tests of the pyrometallurgic slag reduction process were carried out with the use of selected types of biomass. The tests were carried out in a metallurgical aggregate, at a temperature of 1300 °C in the time range from 1 to 5 h. The main parameters determining the efficiency of the process were to determine the degree of removal of the main metals, i.e., Cu and Pb, as well as to determine the content of these elements in the secondary slag. title: Circularity measures enhance resilience of net zero pathways for agriculture
summary: Abstract Reducing environmental impact of agriculture is paramount for sustainable food production. Development of a circular bioeconomy can contribute to environmental objectives, yet the interaction of circularity measures with net zero s
content: Abstract Reducing environmental impact of agriculture is paramount for sustainable food production. Development of a circular bioeconomy can contribute to environmental objectives, yet the interaction of circularity measures with net zero strategies is poorly understood. Using integrated modelling and 12 key performance indicators, we assess the sustainability and resilience of two simulated circular strategies implemented within a business as usual and three net zero greenhouse gas emission pathways for Ireland’s land sector. Two circularity strategies were designed: Energy-focused circularity maximised domestic feedstock utilisation for bioenergy production via anaerobic digestion. Feed-focused circularity minimised imported (overseas) inputs to national livestock systems. Net zero requires large-scale transformation across the land sector. Circularity moderately enhances greenhouse gas emission reductions through energy and livestock feed substitution but considerably strengthens the resilience of net zero pathways by lowering dependence on imported fertilisers, feeds and/or energy (depending on the circularity strategy). This work highlights opportunities to embed circularity within net zero land use strategies to improve resilience.

title: Resource-efficient use of industrial residue for multifunctional cacao nanofibers
summary: This study evaluates cacao residue from chocolate production for resource-efficient production of multifunctional nanofibers. The underlying hypothesis is that preserving non-cellulosic constituents during processing can enable resource-eff
content: This study evaluates cacao residue from chocolate production for resource-efficient production of multifunctional nanofibers. The underlying hypothesis is that preserving non-cellulosic constituents during processing can enable resource-efficient nanofiber production while contributing unique functionalities. Cacao residue yielded 30% after bleaching, with the main components being fat and holocellulose. Fibrillation produced cacao nanofibers at an energy demand of 3.9 kWh/kg, compared with the reference, a commercial wood pulp, with 8.2 kWh/kg after the same processing time. The cacao nanofibers displayed bioactivity, hydrophobic behavior, and excellent redispersibility not observed for the reference material, which has cellulose as the main component. The bioactivity of cacao nanofibers included strong antioxidant, mild antibacterial, and moderate anti-collagenase activity. Utilization of the natural composition offers a resource-efficient approach to unlock the potential of cacao residue into specific multifunctional nanofibers with potential for further development of coating, cosmeceutical, and biomedical applications.

title: Evaluating the global economy-wide impact of energy efficiency policies in buildings
summary: The building sector accounts for nearly one-third of global final energy use. A range of energy efficiency policies can help reduce energy consumption in the sector. These policies include building energy codes, which improve energy efficie
content: The building sector accounts for nearly one-third of global final energy use. A range of energy efficiency policies can help reduce energy consumption in the sector. These policies include building energy codes, which improve energy efficiency in new buildings, as well as retrofit programs and whole-building performance standards, which address efficiency of existing buildings. In this study, we use the Global Change Analysis Model to assess the impacts of these policies on building energy use and other key outcomes globally and across regions. Additionally, we explore how compliance rates influence policy effectiveness and examine the interactions between building efficiency policies, socioeconomic development, and related policy issues. Our study shows that energy demand from the building sector will rise significantly through 2050, absent policies. Socioeconomic development and population gains will be the dominant contributors to this growth. The sector’s energy use could be considerably reduced by implementing effective building efficiency policies. We find that universal adoption and high compliance of advanced building efficiency policies could reduce building energy use by approximately 44% by 2050. Low policy compliance, however, could reduce their effectiveness by nearly half. Furthermore, the impacts of these policies vary by region. Our study indicates that emerging economies in South Asia and Africa would benefit the most from policies targeting new buildings, with gross savings at nearly 1% of GDP in 2050. Meanwhile, China and countries in Europe and North America would benefit the most from a combination of policies addressing both new and existing buildings.

title: Reconciling the role of clay mineral formation on net alkalinity generation during rock weathering: Insights from reactive transport models of shale, granite, and basalt
summary: Abstract. Clay minerals, while ubiquitous in soil, have wide-ranging and countervailing impacts on global biogeochemical cycles. Their compositional diversity makes predicting their formation conditions and impacts on soil solution chemistr
content: Abstract. Clay minerals, while ubiquitous in soil, have wide-ranging and countervailing impacts on global biogeochemical cycles. Their compositional diversity makes predicting their formation conditions and impacts on soil solution chemistry a grand challenge.
