content: The present study aimed to isolate, purify, characterize, and evaluate the physicochemical properties of pectin obtained from orange peel, an agro-industrial waste material.Pectin was extracted by aqueous extraction at different temperatures (40°C, 70°C, and 100°C) followed by acetone precipitation.The percentage yield of isolated pectin was found to be 15%.Phytochemical screening confirmed the presence of carbohydrates, while proteins, tannins, fats, volatile oils, and glucose were absent, indicating the purity of the isolated polymer.Organoleptic evaluation revealed a brown-colored powder with characteristic odor and taste.Solubility studies showed that pectin was soluble in hot water, formed a gel in cold water, and was insoluble in organic solvents.Physicochemical characterization demonstrated pH values ranging from 4.36 to 4.56, swelling index from 77.26% to 188.18%, viscosity from 8.43 to 10.18 poise, and ash content from 5.6% to 9.0%.The P3 batch (100°C) exhibited the highest swelling capacity, whereas the P1 batch (40°C) showed superior flow properties and viscosity.FTIR analysis confirmed the characteristic functional groups of pectin.The results indicate that orange peel-derived pectin possesses desirable physicochemical properties and can serve as a promising natural polymer for pharmaceutical and biomedical applications.

title: Energy Storage Integrated RPC Compensation System and Its Optimization Research
summary: Abstract In electrified railway systems, traction loads exhibit strong randomness, fluctuation, and nonlinear characteristics, which may cause power quality problems such as negative-sequence current, reactive power fluctuation and voltage
content: Abstract In electrified railway systems, traction loads exhibit strong randomness, fluctuation, and nonlinear characteristics, which may cause power quality problems such as negative-sequence current, reactive power fluctuation and voltage unbalance. Meanwhile, regenerative braking energy may be wasted if it is not effectively absorbed and reused. To address these issues, this paper proposes an energy-storage-integrated Railway Power Conditioner (RPC) compensation system incorporating a supercapacitor. The RPC transfers active power between the two feeding sections and supports reactive power compensation, while the supercapacitor connected to the DC link performs peak shaving and valley filling. To further reduce residual reactive power, a Fungal Life Cycle Particle Swarm Optimization (FLC-PSO) algorithm is developed to optimize the control parameters of the Static Var Compensator (SVC). A MATLAB/Simulink model of the electrified railway traction power supply system is established, and 20 typical operating conditions are simulated. Across the 20 operating conditions, FLC-PSO achieves an average power factor of 0.9903 and an average voltage unbalance factor of 0.7327%, compared with 0.9858 and 0.7791%, respectively, for conventional PSO. This corresponds to a 5.96% reduction in the average voltage unbalance factor. Among the four compared algorithms, FLC-PSO provides the best overall average trade-off between power factor and voltage unbalance. All 20 FLC-PSO operating conditions satisfy the limits of power factor (PF) ≥ 0.95 and voltage unbalance factor (VUF) < 1.30%. The proposed RPC–SC–SVC coordinated compensation strategy improves power quality and enables SC-based peak shaving and valley filling within the specified charging/discharging-power and SOC limits.

title: Rapid Interfacial Reconfiguration Via Microwave Air Plasma Enables Durable Superamphiphobic Coatings
summary: ABSTRACT The structural and chemical instability of liquid‐repellent coatings remains a major limitation to durable surface protection under harsh conditions. Here, an atmospheric‐pressure microwave air plasma (MAP)‐induced interfacial reco
content: ABSTRACT The structural and chemical instability of liquid‐repellent coatings remains a major limitation to durable surface protection under harsh conditions. Here, an atmospheric‐pressure microwave air plasma (MAP)‐induced interfacial reconstruction strategy is reported, converting a PFDTES‐modified SiO 2 /epoxy precursor layer into a consolidated hierarchical superamphiphobic interface within 60 s. MAP induces controlled matrix etching to expose and reorganize the fluorosilane‐modified SiO 2 framework, thereby coupling hierarchical roughness, fluorinated surface chemistry, and structural stabilization. The resulting coating exhibits water and oil contact angles of 168° and 155°, respectively, and repels diverse solutions, suspensions, and emulsions. It retains superhydrophobicity after thermal treatment at 500°C and resists sandpaper abrasion, tape peeling, water‐jet impact, sand impact, 1440 h of UV exposure, and 240 h of chemical immersion. It also delays droplet freezing and facilitates the removal of nanoscale powders and liquid stains. This work establishes MAP‐induced interfacial reconfiguration as a rapid route toward durable multifunctional liquid‐repellent coatings.

title: Degradation of graphene oxide-silver nanoparticles by hypochlorite: impacts on physicochemical properties, antimicrobial activity and ecotoxicity
summary: Graphene oxide-silver nanoparticles (GO-AgNPs) represent a promising hybrid material for developing composites, sensors, catalysts, and antimicrobial systems. However, their degradation and life cycle remain poorly understood. Herein, this
content: Graphene oxide-silver nanoparticles (GO-AgNPs) represent a promising hybrid material for developing composites, sensors, catalysts, and antimicrobial systems. However, their degradation and life cycle remain poorly understood. Herein, this study investigated the chemical degradation of GO-AgNPs by sodium hypochlorite (NaClO) and evaluated the resulting impacts on their colloidal stability, antimicrobial activity, and ecotoxicological effects. This oxidative degradation was monitored over 10 days at room temperature, revealing a progressive transformation of both hybrid components. The process induced structural defects and pores within the GO flakes, while simultaneously altering the AgNP surfaces, with both components exhibiting a reduction in size as the reaction progressed. These transformations significantly compromised colloidal stability—as evidenced by a decrease in zeta potential magnitude—leading to particle aggregation even in ultrapure water. Although pristine GO-AgNPs exhibited exceptional activity against microorganisms, this efficacy was entirely lost post-degradation. Furthermore, while degradation mitigated the acute aquatic toxicity toward Daphnia similis , the transformed material significantly affects the feeding behavior of this model organism. Overall, this study provides crucial insights into the degradation mechanisms of GO-AgNPs, directly contributing to life cycle assessment frameworks and safe-and-sustainable by design approaches for nanomaterials.

title: Z ‐Direction Weld Zone: Microstructural and Mechanical Inhomogeneity in 140‐mm Ultra‐Thick Ti Alloy Double‐Sided Electron Beam Welded Joints
source: Fatigue & Fracture of Engineering Materials & Structures
summary: ABSTRACT TC4 titanium alloy is widely used in aerospace, biomedical, chemical, and marine engineering due to its high specific strength, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility. Existing studies on thick titanium alloy EBW joints mainly
content: ABSTRACT TC4 titanium alloy is widely used in aerospace, biomedical, chemical, and marine engineering due to its high specific strength, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility. Existing studies on thick titanium alloy EBW joints mainly focus on welded joints, while through‐thickness fatigue behavior of double‐sided welds remains underexplored. This work systematically studies the distribution of microstructure and mechanical properties along the thickness direction in double‐sided electron beam welded joints. Experimental results indicate that the weld zone of ultra‐thick Ti alloy joints shows significant heterogeneity in microstructure and mechanical properties through thickness. The average ultimate tensile strengths of the welds without and with the overlapping zone are 955 and 1007 MPa, respectively. The high‐cycle fatigue properties of welds with and without overlapping zones are compared, with fatigue strengths measured as 544 and 498 MPa, respectively. All welds contain abundant acicular martensite, and the overlapping region exhibits finer microstructure and higher microhardness. These results provide experimental support for the safe application of ultra‐thick titanium alloy welded structures.

title: Resonance-Tuned Plasmon–Phonon Hybridization in Continuous Bilayer Graphene
summary: Abstract Bilayer graphene hosts an infrared-active antisymmetric (Eu) optical phonon whose spectral response is strongly influenced by electronic excitations. While carrier-density control of this phonon has been widely studied, its interac
content: Abstract Bilayer graphene hosts an infrared-active antisymmetric (Eu) optical phonon whose spectral response is strongly influenced by electronic excitations. While carrier-density control of this phonon has been widely studied, its interaction with collective electronic excitations, graphene plasmons, at nominally fixed carrier density remains less explored. Here we show that resonant plasmonic excitation in chemically doped AB-stacked BLG reshapes the optical phonon response through plasmon–phonon hybridization. A grating-coupled resonator enables efficient far-field excitation of plasmons in a continuous BLG sheet, while a built-in photonic cavity modulates the plasmonic resonance strength. We observe systematic changes in Fano asymmetry, apparent resonance position, spectral weight, and effective line width near the plasmon-strength maximum. Correlation analysis and numerical simulations support plasmon–phonon hybridization as the dominant origin of the observed spectral evolution, with possible intrinsic phonon–electronic coupling. Our findings identify resonance tuning as a distinct route to control plasmon–phonon hybridization and engineer nanoscale mid-infrared light–matter interactions.

title: Correlation between Fe/Mn/Ni Ratio and Structural Properties in P2-Na2/3Mn2/3Fe1/3– x Ni x O2 ( x = 0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, and 1/3)
summary: Abstract P2-type layered oxides, particularly those based on Mn/Fe/Ni, are promising cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries but have structural instability caused by phase transitions during sodiation/desodiation. We show that the phase
content: Abstract P2-type layered oxides, particularly those based on Mn/Fe/Ni, are promising cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries but have structural instability caused by phase transitions during sodiation/desodiation. We show that the phase behavior of the P2-type material Na0.66Mn2/3Fe1/3–xNix series (x = 0, 0.02, 0.05, and 1/3) is strongly influenced by the Fe/Mn/Ni cationic ratio, which is directly coupled to the Mn3+/Mn4+ ratio. Powder X-ray diffraction reveals a systematic variation in the lattice parameter as a function of cation distribution, reflecting the corresponding changes in cation radii. Furthermore, the two binary systems exhibit different structural behaviors, with the Ni/Mn system forming a superstructure, whereas the Fe/Mn system does not exhibit such a phenomenon. The progressive narrowing of the linewidth determined by electron paramagnetic resonance indicates that the proportion of Mn3+ cations decreases as Ni2+ substitution in the P2 lattice increases. In situ XRD between 1.5 and 4.2 V vs Na/Na+ shows that, in the absence or at low amounts of Ni2+ (x < 0.05), the P2 phase coexists with an undesired, Jahn–Teller-distorted orthorhombic P′2 phase. Notably, no high-voltage structural transformations to O2 or OP4/Z phases are observed above 4.0 V. At x ≥ 0.05, the Mn3+ fraction is sufficiently reduced to suppress the formation of the P′2 phase in the low-voltage regime during discharge. These findings underscore the structural stabilization of Fe/Mn-based P2-type layered oxides achieved through minimal Ni substitution.

title: Modified negative thermal expansion heterointerface engineering for thermally compatible La0.6Sr0.4Co0.2Fe0.8O3–δ-ZrW2O8 composite oxygen electrodes for solid oxide electrolysis cells
summary: SOECs are promising for efficient green hydrogen production owing to high energy conversion efficiency and no requirement for precious-metal catalysts. However, interfacial stress associated with thermal-expansion mismatch remains a critica
content: SOECs are promising for efficient green hydrogen production owing to high energy conversion efficiency and no requirement for precious-metal catalysts. However, interfacial stress associated with thermal-expansion mismatch remains a critical barrier to long-term durability. Herein, a modified negative thermal expansion (NTE) heterointerface engineering strategy is proposed by incorporating ZrW 2 O 8 (ZWO) into La 0.6 Sr 0.4 Co 0.2 Fe 0.8 O 3– δ (LSCF) oxygen electrodes. During fabrication and operation, thermally driven reactions between LSCF and ZWO are associated with interfacial reconstruction, accompanied by the formation of SrWO 4 -related phases at the interface. This interfacial regulation mitigates thermal expansion mismatch and is associated with improved electrode durability and oxygen electrode polarization performance. The optimized LSCF-20ZWO oxygen electrode shows a 22.73% lower thermal expansion coefficient than pristine LSCF, delivering 2.61 A cm −2 at 1.4 V and 750°C with improved durability and thermal cycling tolerance. This work presents a feasible strategy for thermally compatible oxygen electrodes via modified NTE heterointerface engineering.

title: Chiral Cycloparaarylenes Incorporating Binaphthyl Units: Dramatic Effects of Peripheral Functionalization on (Chir)Optical Properties
summary: ABSTRACT Axially chiral [12]cycloparaarylenes 1 and 2 , consisting of three each of 1,1′‐binaphthyl and biphenyl units, were synthesized. Their characteristics were distinct from those of [12]cycloparaphenylene and depended on whether the 2
content: ABSTRACT Axially chiral [12]cycloparaarylenes 1 and 2 , consisting of three each of 1,1′‐binaphthyl and biphenyl units, were synthesized. Their characteristics were distinct from those of [12]cycloparaphenylene and depended on whether the 2,2′‐substituents on the binaphthyls were methoxy groups or a methylenedioxy bridge. 1 with methoxy groups adopted a D 3 ‐symmetric structure with transoid binaphthyls, whereas 2 with methylenedioxy groups existed as an equilibrium mixture of C 3 ‐ and C 1 ‐symmetric structures with cisoid binaphthyls. This difference arises from modulation in binaphthyl dihedral angles and the intrinsic preference of cycloparaarylenes (CPAs) for cylindrical arene arrangements. 1 displayed strong aggregation‐induced emission enhancement (AIEE) with Φ fl of 0.85 at 5°C and blue emission in the solid state. 2 showed weaker but more redshifted AIEE and solid‐state green emission. Trifluoroacetic acid molecules stabilized the highly symmetric conformations of 1 in the excited state, leading to a ninefold enhancement in fluorescence (FL) and intense circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) with | g lum | of 0.028 and B CPL of 820 M −1 cm −1 at −60°C.

title: Interpretable structure–spectrum mapping via manifold learning in amorphous In–Ga–Zn oxide
summary: Amorphous materials offer unique functionalities but remain poorly understood because structural disorder obscures links between local environments and macroscopic properties. Electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) probes local chemistry,
content: Amorphous materials offer unique functionalities but remain poorly understood because structural disorder obscures links between local environments and macroscopic properties. Electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) probes local chemistry, yet fine structure is often broadened and overlapping, limiting interpretation. Here we present a manifold-learning framework in which a variational autoencoder (VAE) embeds paired structural descriptors and O K-edge spectra in amorphous In–Ga–Zn oxide (a-IGZO) into a shared latent space. Gradient-guided latent perturbations quantify conditional spectral sensitivities and descriptor interdependencies on a data-constrained manifold, recapitulating established O K-edge fingerprints, including cation-specific modulations consistent with In-, Ga-, and Zn-oxide–like local environments and enhanced pre-edge features associated with peroxide-like O–O configurations. An auxiliary network maps experimental spectra to this space and enables descriptor-level inference, allowing spatial mapping of local descriptors that are difficult to access directly from experiment. Applied to a-IGZO devices, the approach resolves interfacial and growth-condition trends that are independently corroborated by EDS and EELS edge-integral quantification. This work establishes an interpretable platform for systematic, data-driven exploration of a-IGZO.

title: Potential for Carotenoid and Other Bioproducts Production by a Brazilian Dunaliella salina Isolate Using a High Photon Flux Density Strategy
summary: ABSTRACT Dunaliella species are among the most significant biological sources of carotenoids, notably beta‐carotene. Given that chemical synthesis offers a more cost‐effective alternative to biotechnological cultivation, optimizing producti
content: ABSTRACT Dunaliella species are among the most significant biological sources of carotenoids, notably beta‐carotene. Given that chemical synthesis offers a more cost‐effective alternative to biotechnological cultivation, optimizing production strategies is essential for economic viability. This study investigated the optimization of bioproduct synthesis in a Brazilian strain of Dunaliella salina by evaluating the effects of high photon flux density (PFD) and temperature under low‐salinity conditions (1 mol L −1 NaCl) to facilitate downstream processing. Batch cultivations were conducted at 26°C across a PFD gradient ranging from 100 to 2000 µmol photons m −2 s −1 , with additional cultivations performed at 30°C under maximum irradiance. The results demonstrated that increasing PFD to 2000 µmol photons m −2 s −1 significantly enhanced metabolic performance, yielding a 25% increase in biomass concentration, a 62% rise in biomass productivity, and an 82% surge in total carotenoid production. Furthermore, carbohydrate content increased by 61%, whereas lipid levels remained stable, exhibiting a fatty acid profile conducive to biodiesel production. The temperature variation up to 30°C had no effect on biomass concentration or biomass composition, affecting only the fatty acid composition. These findings underscore the robust potential of this strain for the large‐scale biotechnological production of carotenoids and other high‐value compounds within a biorefinery framework.

title: Source node management in complex water network based on cascading failure and bidirectional risk transmission: The case of Henan Province
summary: Water source nodes within water network are subject to dual pressures: the propagation of failure risks and reverse feedback from fluctuations in user demand. As the connectivity of water network and the relationship between water supply an
content: Water source nodes within water network are subject to dual pressures: the propagation of failure risks and reverse feedback from fluctuations in user demand. As the connectivity of water network and the relationship between water supply and consumption become increasingly complex, there is an urgent need to elucidate the patterns of bidirectional risk transmission in complex water network and to effectively manage water source nodes. Taking the water network of Henan Province as a case study, improved forward and reverse cascade failure models were established respectively. The criticality of water source nodes in forward risk propagation and their sensitivity to pressure in reverse feedback were comprehensively identified. Spearman correlation analysis and K-means clustering were employed to classify water source nodes into 'criticality+sensitivity' two-dimensional clusters. The results indicate that forward risk transmission exhibits distinct head-concentration characteristics, with a small number of critical reservoir nodes dominating cascade failure. Spatially, risk first propagates through the structural layer before permeating to the functional endpoints.Temporally, it follows a non-linear evolution pattern, initially intensifying and subsequently attenuating. Reverse risk propagation exhibits characteristics of 'source-proximity priority' and hierarchical feedback: as the degree of demand deviation and the number of affected users increase, reservoirs closest to the source are the first to reach their pressure limits and transmit pressure to secondary reservoirs. The two-dimensional classification criteria combining the criticality and sensitivity of reservoir nodes more comprehensively reflect the characteristics of reservoir nodes within the water network, enabling more precise, differentiated management of these nodes. This study broadens the research perspective on risk propagation in complex water network and provides theoretical support and decision-making guidance for the precise management of water source nodes to enhance the water supply security of water network.

title: In silico discovery and cellular validation of PBM-342: a novel PPAR-β/δ modulator for skeletal muscle differentiation
summary: Modulation of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor beta/delta (PPAR-β/δ) holds therapeutic potential for skeletal muscle regeneration and metabolism. However, the clinical development of classical agonists has been hampered by sev
content: Modulation of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor beta/delta (PPAR-β/δ) holds therapeutic potential for skeletal muscle regeneration and metabolism. However, the clinical development of classical agonists has been hampered by severe issues of non-specificity and metabolic toxicity. In this study, we implemented an in-silico strategy coupled with in-vitro functional validation to discover selective and safe modulators. Through a ligand-based virtual screening of the ZINC database, using the crystallographic agonist 'Compound 9' (PBM-0) as a structural template to favor isotype selectivity, and molecular docking analysis, PBM-342 was identified as the top-ranked candidate, exhibiting a favorable docking score (ΔG = −12.86 kcal/mol by flexible docking). Subsequent molecular dynamics simulations revealed that PBM-342 constrains the conformational dynamics of Tyrosine-437 in Helix-12, the structural determinant of the receptor transcriptional activation. Pharmacokinetic (ADME) profiling confirmed its optimal lipophilicity (Log P = 3.86) and the absence of inhibition of the critical hepatic isoenzyme CYP2D6. Consequently, in murine C2C12 cultures, the working concentration of PBM-342 (100 nM) promoted morphologically and transcriptionally, myotube fusion index (p < 0.0001) and fiber-type reprogramming, as evidenced by selective upregulation of the specific oxidative muscle fibers, myosin isoform MHCIIa (p < 0.01).

title: Organic fertilizer levels regulate Fusarium graminearum colonization by reshaping soil microbial community
summary: Soil immunity is defined as the capacity of soil to defend against diseases and sustain plant health, which is fundamentally driven by soil microbial communities. Wheat Fusarium head blight, which is caused mainly by Fusarium graminearum ,
content: Soil immunity is defined as the capacity of soil to defend against diseases and sustain plant health, which is fundamentally driven by soil microbial communities. Wheat Fusarium head blight, which is caused mainly by Fusarium graminearum , threatens agricultural sustainability. Topsoil is a major pathogen habitat because of straw return, thus reducing soil pathogen abundance is critical for the environmentally sustainable management of soil-borne diseases. Organic management is regarded as a potential way to inhibit pathogen proliferation by shaping complex microbial interactions in soil to prevent plant diseases. Therefore, determining the optimal amount of organic fertilizer for improving soil immunity to cultivate disease-suppressing soils is imperative. A six-year field trial with a 28-d experiment was conducted to determine the effects of organic fertilizer rates (CK, 0 t/ha; 1TSM, 15 t/ha; 2TSM, 30 t/ha; 4TSM, 60 t/ha) on crop yields, soil fertility, and microbial traits. The results revealed that compared with the CK, the 2TSM and 4TSM increased crop yields, soil fertility, and network complexity and enhanced the inhibitory effect on Fusarium graminearum abundance. However, the soil microbial community remained highly stable only under the 2TSM after Fusarium graminearum inoculation. Microbial co-occurrence network and topological role analyses both suggested that Mortierella may be the keystone taxon involved in soil immunity. Furthermore, plant coleoptile infection and another 28-d incubation experiments revealed that Mortierella alpina inoculation not only increased network complexity in soil but also reduced plant diseases. Overall, 30 t/ha organic fertilizer application is a reasonable strategy for increasing soil productivity. Changes in soil C:N ratio induced by fertilization may account for the alterations in soil immunity. Incubation combined with plant coleoptile infection assays revealed a potential mechanism: 2TSM-stimulated Mortierella alpina -driven Fusarium graminearum suppression and network complexity improvement represent feasible pathways to achieve plant and soil health.

title: Boosting Methyl Orange Removal via Hydrothermal Engineering of CuZnAl LDHs
summary: Abstract Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are promising adsorbents for dye-contaminated water owing to their tunable layer charge and exchangeable interlayers. In this study, ZnAl, CuAl, and CuZnAl LDHs were synthesized under identical urea
content: Abstract Layered double hydroxides (LDHs) are promising adsorbents for dye-contaminated water owing to their tunable layer charge and exchangeable interlayers. In this study, ZnAl, CuAl, and CuZnAl LDHs were synthesized under identical urea-assisted hydrothermal conditions using metal ratios corresponding to those of compositionally related co-precipitated materials reported previously. Their structural, textural, adsorption, and regeneration properties were systematically evaluated using methyl orange (MO) as an anionic model pollutant. In batch tests, CuZnAl exhibited near-quantitative removal across pH 2–11, CuAl achieved near-quantitative removal at pH ≥ 3, whereas ZnAl showed a narrower effective pH range with a marked decline under alkaline conditions. Adsorption kinetics ( C 0 = 50–500 mg L −1 ) were well described by the pseudo-second-order model. Equilibrium analysis indicated high adsorption capacities, with Langmuir monolayer capacities of 497.5 mg g −1 (ZnAl), 609.8 mg g −1 (CuAl), and 666.7 mg g −1 (CuZnAl), while Freundlich fitting suggested favorable adsorption on heterogeneous sites. Regeneration by alkaline Na 2 CO 3 /NaOH washing enabled efficient reuse: CuZnAl and CuAl maintained MO removal efficiencies of 98.2% and 97.2%, respectively, after five cycles, whereas that of ZnAl decreased to 69.3%. Post-adsorption XRD and FTIR results indicated retention of the LDH framework and partial interlayer participation of MO, while SEM revealed composition-dependent changes in aggregate morphology. The adsorption behavior reflected the combined effects of metal composition, basal spacing, textural properties, aggregate architecture, and surface/interlayer chemistry. Among the investigated materials, hydrothermal CuZnAl provided the most favorable balance of adsorption capacity, pH tolerance, and regeneration performance.

title: Study on the thermal damage evolution law of granite considering mesoscopic fabric characteristics
summary: Introduction The intrinsic fabric heterogeneity of granite gives rise to the inherently scattered nature of its thermal damage behavior. Therefore, accurately evaluating thermal damage in granite is essential for engineering safety. Methods
content: Introduction The intrinsic fabric heterogeneity of granite gives rise to the inherently scattered nature of its thermal damage behavior. Therefore, accurately evaluating thermal damage in granite is essential for engineering safety. Methods This study explores the relationship between thermal damage and granite fabric using a polycrystalline damage model. Thermal damage tests were conducted on granite specimens with distinct fabrics, and crack propagation was characterized using microscopic imaging and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Thermo-mechanical numerical simulations were then performed using the discrete element method (DEM) coupled with a thermo-mechanical model to investigate mesoscale crack propagation and damage evolution. Results (1) The microcracks in granite propagated progressively with increasing temperature and coalesced into observable macroscopic cracks within the 400 °C–600 °C range range. (2) The thermal damage behavior of granite was correlated with its fabric characteristics through a functional relationship f * (temperature damage characteristic function), which followed a power-law growth trend with increasing temperature. (3) Microcrack damage, macroscopic damage, and theoretical damage exhibited consistent variation trends, although microcrack damage values were lower than the other calculated damage values at relatively small crystal sizes. Conclusion The fabric characteristics of granite govern microcrack development, thereby generating distinctive thermal damage patterns. Constructing a multi-parameter thermal damage model and solving for f * can deepen the understanding of thermal damage evolution in granite. From a microcrack-damage perspective, the thermal damage of granite is more strongly influenced by fabric characteristics at smaller crystal sizes. These findings provide a mesoscopic-fabric-based framework for evaluating thermal damage in granite and offer practical insights for temperature-related underground engineering.

title: Nearly ninety percent of Indonesian coffee area is classified as deforestation-free under the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR)
summary: Abstract Indonesia is the third-largest coffee producer globally and exports a substantial share of its production to European Union (EU) countries. Recent implementation of the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which requires deforestati
content: Abstract Indonesia is the third-largest coffee producer globally and exports a substantial share of its production to European Union (EU) countries. Recent implementation of the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), which requires deforestation-free supply chains, highlights the need for spatially-explicit coffee mapping to support the assessment of coffee-associated deforestation. In this study, we utilized multitemporal and multi-sensor remote sensing to produce annual maps of coffee distribution from 2016 to 2024. We analyzed the spatial patterns of annual coffee distribution during this period, and evaluated the potential implications of EUDR for coffee production in Indonesia. Our maps of coffee agroecosystems demonstrate an overall classification accuracy exceeding 80%, and are broadly consistent with independent coffee datasets (i.e., national statistics and coffee probability maps from the Forest Data Partnership). We detected a net increase of ~15% in coffee area over the eight-year period, although the patterns of change vary across provinces. Based on these maps, we estimate that 87.9% of the coffee area in 2024 meets the EUDR deforestation-free criterion, and only a relatively small proportion of agroecosystems are classified as non-deforestation-free. These findings highlight opportunities for spatially targeted EUDR implementation, where deforestation-free coffee agroecosystems can be supported towards meeting broader EUDR requirements, while areas associated with forest conversion can be supported towards other pathways, such as sustainable agricultural practices, restoration, and forest conservation.

title: Harnessing Anion Perturbation for Self‐Limiting Decomposition for Durable Argyrodite‐Based Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Argyrodite‐type electrolytes Li 6‐a PS 5‐a X 1+a (LPSX, X = Cl, Br) are attractive for All‐solid‐state lithium metal batteries (ASSLMBs) due to their high ionic conductivity and processability, yet their inherent chemical instabili
content: ABSTRACT Argyrodite‐type electrolytes Li 6‐a PS 5‐a X 1+a (LPSX, X = Cl, Br) are attractive for All‐solid‐state lithium metal batteries (ASSLMBs) due to their high ionic conductivity and processability, yet their inherent chemical instability with Li metal causes interfacial degradation. Conventionally, this has been tackled by suppressing electrolyte decomposition. Herein, we harness controlled decomposition to construct a protective interphase. Fluorozirconate incorporation induces localized anion perturbation of PS 4 3− , which directs the initial reductive decomposition toward rapid formation of a self‐limiting solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Theoretical calculations and experimental results reveal that the strong electron‐withdrawing character of fluorozirconate redistributes the electronic environment of adjacent PS 4 3− , making interfacial sites preferentially active and enhancing reduction susceptibility. The resulting interphase is rich in Li 2 S/Li x P and F‐containing species which is mechanically robust and electronically insulating and effectively facilitates charge transfer, thereby suppressing continuous electrolyte decomposition. Li||Li cell with optimized electrolyte can cycle steadily for 7000 h at 0.5 mA cm −2 and 0.5 mAh cm −2 . Furthermore, the full cell can retain 81.3% of its capacity after 1200 cycles at 1 C. The anion‐perturbed electrolyte delivers excellent ultra‐long cycling stability, which provides a facile regulation strategy for interfacial modification and performance optimization of ASSLMBs.

title: Overcoming the trade-off between electrical conductivity and densification in Al 2 O 3 –TiC Ceramics via particle size grading
summary: Abstract Electrically conductive composite ceramics face a critical trade-off where increasing the phase domain size ratio between the insulating matrix and the conductive phase theoretically enhances conductivity but practically hinders de
content: Abstract Electrically conductive composite ceramics face a critical trade-off where increasing the phase domain size ratio between the insulating matrix and the conductive phase theoretically enhances conductivity but practically hinders densification. The resulting porosity inevitably degrades both mechanical and electrical properties. To address this limitation, a matrix particle size grading strategy is proposed using the Al2O3–TiC system as a model. The incorporation of nano-Al2O3 into a micro-Al2O3 matrix triggers a synergistic microstructural evolution. Specifically, nano-Al2O3 particles fill interparticle spaces to promote densification and may pin TiC grain boundaries, thereby contributing to the refinement of the conductive phase domains. Concurrently, the micro-Al2O3 phase domains coarsen at the expense of nano-Al2O3, maximizing the phase domain size disparity and favoring the formation of a continuous three-dimensional TiC network. With 10 vol% nano-Al2O3 addition, the calculated effective percolation threshold drops from 15.54 vol% to 10.20 vol%, achieving an electrical conductivity of 4.02 × 104 S/m. Consequently, the composite exhibits enhanced electrical discharge machining (EDM) performance, achieving a material removal rate of 9.50 mm2/min alongside high surface quality. This strategy offers a robust framework for developing advanced conductive ceramics tailored for EDM applications.

title: Global burden and trends of smoking-related low back pain in women of childbearing age and projections to 2032: A secondary dataset analysis of Global Burden of Disease 2021
summary: INTRODUCTIONThis study used Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data to examine trends in smoking-related low-back pain (LBP) among women of childbearing age (WCBA) and project future trends.METHODS This study is a secondary analysis of the GBD
content: INTRODUCTIONThis study used Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data to examine trends in smoking-related low-back pain (LBP) among women of childbearing age (WCBA) and project future trends.METHODS This study is a secondary analysis of the GBD 2021 data.This study analyzes the temporal trends in the disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) caused by smoking-related LBP between 1990 and 2021 across 204 countries and territories.We evaluated the changing trends in the burden of smokingrelated LBP in WCBA using the estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and percentage change and Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling to forecast the burden to 2032.RESULTS Globally, smoking-related low-back pain DALYs among women of childbearing age declined by 3% from 1990 to 2021, with the age-standardized rate falling from 84.58 to 56.54 per 100000 (EAPC= -1.39%).Regional disparities were pronounced: high-SDI regions accounted for 40.8% of the 2021 burden but saw a 22% decline, whereas low-SDI regions experienced a 54% increase.The largest national increases occurred in Qatar (733.3%) and the UAE (715.4%).Eastern Europe showed the greatest regional EAPC increase (1.85%), while Tropical Latin America declined most sharply (-2.68%).The age group of 45-49 years exhibited the highest 2021 DALY rate (140.2 per 100000), increasing 22% since 1990, contrasting with a 20% decline among those aged 30-34 years.Frontier analysis identified Greece, Chile, and Slovenia as having the greatest improvement potential.BAPC modeling projects a 17.24% decline in the global age-standardized DALY rate by 2032.CONCLUSIONS The burden of smoking-related LBP in WCBA is shifting from high-income to low-and middle-income regions, with middle-SDI countries and older reproductive-age women facing escalating risks.

title: Dilemmas and Actions for Tropical Cyclone Risk Insurance under Climate Change: Governmental Bodies, Market Entities, and Scientific Communities
summary: Abstract. Faced with the increased frequency of tropical cyclones (TCs) amid climate change, insurance plays a pivotal role in disaster response and adaptation. Current research on TC risk insurance exhibits a trend of multidisciplinary int
content: Abstract. Faced with the increased frequency of tropical cyclones (TCs) amid climate change, insurance plays a pivotal role in disaster response and adaptation. Current research on TC risk insurance exhibits a trend of multidisciplinary integration and multi-stakeholder participation. Using a large language model, this paper systematically reviews 890 TC risk insurance publications. Spatio-temporal distribution analysis reveals growing research attention yet persistent spatial imbalances. Co-authorship network analysis uncovers varying but still insufficient degrees of collaboration among three stakeholder groups: governmental bodies, market entities, and scientific communities. Generally, the literature mainly converges on four interlocking dilemmas that constrain the current insurance system: Can TC risk remain insurable under climate change? Is insurance comprehensive enough? Is insurance accessible to those who need it most? Will people purchase insurance even when it is available? In response, the paper proposes a dilemma-aligned tripartite collaboration framework that specifies joint actions for the three stakeholder groups. This framework aims to strengthen cooperation and innovation, advancing the TC risk insurance system toward greater fairness, efficiency, and resilience in a changing climate.

title: Practical Applications of Machine Learning in Manufacturing: Virtual Power Plants and Coordinated Computing and Power Management
summary: This paper uses publicly available UCI electricity consumption data to examine how machine learning affects day-ahead load forecasting and energy storage dispatch. Hourly loads from 20 large electricity users are aggregated to simulate a vi
content: This paper uses publicly available UCI electricity consumption data to examine how machine learning affects day-ahead load forecasting and energy storage dispatch. Hourly loads from 20 large electricity users are aggregated to simulate a virtual power plant. The experiments compare naive baselines with direct regression models and use the weekly load pattern to develop residual models that predict deviations from the load at the same hour of the previous week. The gradient boosting residual model achieves a mean absolute percentage error of 3.49%, a 13.2% reduction from the baseline of 4.02%, and reduces root mean squared error by 28.0%. The error in the period of peak falls from 1.69% to 1.22%, and the mean absolute error in daily peak load falls by 25.4%. By using a 15 MW/30 MWh storage system, assumed the rates are based on the time it uses, and a fixed peak-shaving target, peak-shaving not only effectively increases from 78.2% to 79.0% over the roughly 38-day test period but also the saves more electricity cost rise from CNY 511,000 to CNY 515,000. Weekly residual learning improves the accuracy forecasting with a larger error reductions during peak periods than the full test period. Better forecasts bring additional peak-shaving and cost benefits although the storage capacity and dispatch rules limit gains. This paper also shows that how the approach can potentially support coordinated computing and power management through shifts in task execution times; However, the performance in computing task scheduling might requires more validation.

title: Penetrant-Triggered Responsiveness in Carboxylate Polymer of Intrinsic Microporosity
summary: Abstract While complex mixture fractionation has become a primary focus in membrane science, the mechanisms behind penetrant-penetrant and penetrant-polymer interactions governing molecular separations require deeper investigation. Of equal
content: Abstract While complex mixture fractionation has become a primary focus in membrane science, the mechanisms behind penetrant-penetrant and penetrant-polymer interactions governing molecular separations require deeper investigation. Of equal importance, how the external environment dictates these interactions remains poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, we elucidate the molecular mechanisms that control how microporous polymers structurally adapt to their external environment. Resolving previous speculations, we show that upon reaction with carboxylic acid groups in carboxylate polymer of intrinsic microporosity (cPIM), ammonia forms ammonium carboxylate adducts. This chemical modification alters small-molecule sorption, local chain organization, free volume distribution, and, ultimately, penetrant diffusion. Notably, ammonia-modified cPIM rapidly reacts with carbon dioxide, causing in situ polymer ionic cross-linking. Using a suite of advanced experimental methods, including transport measurements, FTIR, PALS, and NMR, we uncover the mechanisms behind the observed responsiveness and its time-evolution. Ultimately, we demonstrate that accounting for coupled interactions is crucial for accurate performance prediction and optimal design of responsive membranes.

title: Reduced semi-arid summer carbon dioxide efflux from agrivoltaic compared to conventional horticultural soil
summary: Abstract Agrivoltaic (AV) systems that combine horticultural crops with photovoltaic (PV) infrastructure on the same land parcel can provide mutual benefits for crop performance, electricity production, and water use in semi-arid climates.
content: Abstract Agrivoltaic (AV) systems that combine horticultural crops with photovoltaic (PV) infrastructure on the same land parcel can provide mutual benefits for crop performance, electricity production, and water use in semi-arid climates. Whether semi-arid AV systems provide additional benefits for soil development and carbon (C) accumulation remains unclear. Larger aboveground biomass and yield production, which has been observed in semi-arid AV for certain crops, may accelerate C loss by supporting more continual and extensive microbial and root respiration, resulting in net zero or negative change in soil C over a growing season. Alternatively, AV systems may retain more soil C by reducing stress-induced respiration losses. To test these contrasting hypotheses, we compared crop biomass and yield, soil carbon pools, and semi-continuous microclimate and respired carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions for two horticultural crops grown in an experimental AV site in southern Arizona, USA. Over one summer growing season, we observed an approximately 9% reduction in daily mean soil CO2 efflux from legume (cowpea, Vigna unguiculata) and 48% reduction from aromatic herb (basil, Ocimum basilicum) beds, with the strongest impacts of AV appearing during the early monsoon season when plants were mature. On diel timescales, AV soil CO2 efflux peaked later in the day compared to conventional horticultural beds, corresponding to lagged increases in soil temperature under solar panels. Smaller CO2 efflux in AV coincided with a doubling of aboveground crop biomass. Both crops and cover types experienced similar declines in soil C over the growing season, however, suggesting soil C transformation pathways other than CO2 respiration (e.g. methanogenesis) may dominate in AV at this site. Complementing its well-described food-water-energy benefits, we find potential for AV to reduce soil CO2 losses and urge future research to identify changes to soil C cycling that result from the addition of PV to horticultural landscapes.

title: Coupled Bulk‐Interfacial Modulation Enables Suppressed Conduction Loss in High‐Temperature Polymer Capacitors
summary: ABSTRACT Polymer film capacitors are widely used in electronic devices and power systems, yet their energy storage performance (ESP) deteriorates significantly under harsh operating conditions. Here, we propose a synergistic strategy that i
content: ABSTRACT Polymer film capacitors are widely used in electronic devices and power systems, yet their energy storage performance (ESP) deteriorates significantly under harsh operating conditions. Here, we propose a synergistic strategy that integrates bulk physical crosslinking with interfacial plasma regulation to suppress conduction loss and enhance high‐temperature dielectric performance. 4‐cyanobenzaldehyde (4‐CZ) is incorporated into a polyetherimide (PEI) matrix to construct a noncovalent, electrostatically crosslinked network, which simultaneously constrains polymer chain dynamics and introduces charge‐transport barriers, thereby effectively inhibiting carrier migration. In parallel, plasma surface treatment further enhances interfacial trap density and suppresses charge injection. Owing to this synergistic regulation of bulk and interface, the optimized film delivers a discharge energy density ( U d ) of ∼7.6 J·cm −3 with an efficiency ( η ) of 91.8% at 150°C and 670 MV·m −1 , markedly outperforming pristine PEI. This work establishes a generalizable design strategy for high‐performance all‐organic polymer dielectrics toward high‐temperature energy storage applications.

title: Tube-in-tube hollow RuCrMn oxide nanofibers for noble-metal-efficient oxygen evolution via Cr/Mn-regulated Ru active sites
summary: Reducing the Ru content while maintaining high oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity remains a major challenge. In this study, single phase Ru 0.30 Cr 0.31 Mn 0.39 O 2 nanofibers were prepared through electrospinning process followed by
content: Reducing the Ru content while maintaining high oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity remains a major challenge. In this study, single phase Ru 0.30 Cr 0.31 Mn 0.39 O 2 nanofibers were prepared through electrospinning process followed by temperature-regulated heat treatment. The temperature regulation process induces a unique formation of a hollow tube-in-tube structure while simultaneously influencing crystallinity and defect distribution. Among the prepared samples, the material treated at 400 °C shows the most favorable performance for OER. This behavior is associated with improved transport properties and increased accessibility of catalytically active sites. The catalyst reaches an overpotential of only 211 mV at 10 mA cm − 2 and maintains stable operation in alkaline electrolyte. The mass-normalized activity and turnover frequency (TOF metal ) are significantly 293- and 104-fold higher than those of commercial RuO 2 , respectively, highlighting its superior catalytic efficiency with reduced Ru content. Theoretical calculations based on density functional theory suggest that the incorporation of Cr and Mn modulates the electronic structure of RuO 2 , particularly near the Fermi level, and adjusts the d-band center position. These changes lower the energy barrier associated with the O* to OOH* step. The results thus demonstrate that simultaneous control of composition and morphology can improve OER performance in alkaline media.

title: Isoetin and luteolin glycosides from Leontodon crispus and Leontodon hispidus (Cichorieae, Asteraceae)
summary: A phytochemical investigation of the aerial parts of Leontodon crispus and leaves of L. hispidus yielded seven flavonoids. Two compounds were determined to be already known luteolin glycosides, whereas five compounds were determined to be i
content: A phytochemical investigation of the aerial parts of Leontodon crispus and leaves of L. hispidus yielded seven flavonoids. Two compounds were determined to be already known luteolin glycosides, whereas five compounds were determined to be isoetin glycosides. Of these five isoetin derivatives, two were determined to be previously unreported isoetin di- O -glucosides, isoetin 2′,5′-di- O - β - d -glucopyranoside and isoetin 4′,5′-di- O - β - d -glucopyranoside. The structures of the isolated compounds were determined by means of HRMS/MS, 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy, and UV spectroscopic analyses. The absolute configurations of the glucose moieties of the two previously unreported isoetin derivatives were determined by octylation of the glucose moieties and subsequent GC-MS analyses. Additionally, the occurrences of the isolated compounds in related taxa (two species of Hypochaeris and six species of Leontodon ) were investigated by semi-quantitative UHPLC-HRMS analysis. The distribution of the compounds within the investigated species was discussed with a focus on chemophenetics.

title: New approach for deciphering polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-based plastics’ diols: Application on PET daily-life packaging objects paving their chemical modifications
summary: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a thermoplastic polyester synthetized from a terephthalic diacid and a diol which is generally ethylene glycol. Given PET prominence in food packaging industry, a detailed study of this polymer is of utmo
content: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a thermoplastic polyester synthetized from a terephthalic diacid and a diol which is generally ethylene glycol. Given PET prominence in food packaging industry, a detailed study of this polymer is of utmost importance. The identification of the initial diols constituting PET-based bottles and containers along with their structural modifications, due to recycling procedures and/or weathering, is still a challenging research subject. In this study, PET diols were derivatized using a new approach combining an innovative methanolysis-benzoylation methodology with analysis by Orbitrap MS. First, a transesterification with methanol for freeing diols and/or polyols was performed followed by a derivatization with 4-dimethylaminobenzoyl chloride (DMABC) used as benzoylation agent under specific conditions. After reaction post-treatment, the derivatized products were analyzed using ESI ionization on an Orbitrap MS hyphenated to liquid chromatography LC−MS. This method was applied to PET-based daily-life bottles and containers in comparison to authentic diols and copolyesters used as references, showing extra new data on their diols’ composition that may be affected by recycling, manufacturing procedures and/or natural weathering. These PET-based packaging objects were differentiated according to the detected diols along with their oxidized compounds and hydroxy acids. Other polyesters and copolyesters can be studied using this same new strategy.

title: Andamiaje nanofibroso de acción dual para la cicatrización tendinosa: un nuevo biomaterial de PLGA/PCL para la liberación local de fármacos y la protección del tejido
summary: Objectives: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a bilayer nanofiber scaffold consisting of methylprednisolone (MT)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) and polycaprolactone (PCL) to reduce peritendinous adhesion while minimizing
content: Objectives: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a bilayer nanofiber scaffold consisting of methylprednisolone (MT)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) and polycaprolactone (PCL) to reduce peritendinous adhesion while minimizing steroidinduced tendon atrophy.Methods: A dual-layer scaffold was fabricated via electrospinning, comprising a 25% MP-loaded PLGA outer layer for sustained drug delivery and a PCL inner layer to block steroid exposure to the tendon.The scaffold was characterized using scanning electron microscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, mechanical testing, water contact angle measurement, drug release kinetics, and biodegradability analysis.An in vivo study was conducted on 42 Wistar rats across four experimental groups.Outcome assessments included macroscopic adhesion scoring, histopathology, biomechanical testing, tendon length measurements, and systemic glucose level monitoring.Results: The scaffold demonstrated uniform fiber morphology and reliable mechanical properties.MP release followed Korsmeyer-Peppas kinetics.In vivo, the scaffold significantly reduced fibrosis, inflammation, and adhesions without altering tendon length or systemic glucose levels.The bilayer design effectively prevented corticosteroid-related atrophy and preserved tendon biomechanical integrity.Conclusions: The 25% MP-loaded PLGA/PCL scaffold appears to be a safe and effective barrier for post-surgical tendon healing, offering localized delivery and dual protection against adhesion and atrophic complications.

title: Van der Waals Gap‐Confined Molecular Engineering of MoS 2 for Selectivity‐Enhanced and Humidity‐Tolerant Gas Sensing
summary: ABSTRACT Controlling interactions between sensor surfaces and target molecules is central to achieving high selectivity and stability in chemical sensing. However, in two‐dimensional (2D) material‐based sensors, unintended adsorption, parti
content: ABSTRACT Controlling interactions between sensor surfaces and target molecules is central to achieving high selectivity and stability in chemical sensing. However, in two‐dimensional (2D) material‐based sensors, unintended adsorption, particularly of water molecules, often disrupts these interactions, degrading selectivity and long‐term stability. Here, we exploit molecular confinement within van der Waals (vdW) gaps of MoS 2 to engineer sensor–analyte interactions. Ethanol (EtOH) confinement induces electron doping and hydrophobicity, whereas water confinement produces negligible doping and hydrophilicity. This combined modulation suppresses H 2 O adsorption while promoting selective NO 2 adsorption, enabling the EtOH‐confined sensor to detect NO 2 from 200 ppb to 5 ppm, with a maximum response of 48% at 60% relative humidity and a detection limit of 36 ppb. Under highly humid conditions, it exhibits a sevenfold higher NO 2 response and retains 95% of its initial response after 5 weeks, compared with 44% for H 2 O‐confined films. First‐principles calculations reveal that molecular confinement regulates sulfur‐vacancy (V s ) configurations: EtOH favors isolated and lined V s , which promote NO 2 adsorption while suppressing H 2 O binding, whereas H 2 O stabilizes clustered V s , which increase H 2 O affinity. This vdW‐gap confinement provides a design strategy to tune surface chemistry, electronic structure, and defect configurations for selective, humidity‐tolerant, and reliable 2D chemical sensors.

title: CFD-Based Numerical Optimization of the Thermal Performance of PCM-Integrated Hollow Bricks: Combined Effects of Cavity Geometry and Phase-Change Temperature under Hot-Climate Conditions
summary: Abstract This study presents a two-dimensional transient CFD investigation of the thermal performance of hollow bricks incorporating air, glass wool, and phase change materials under the hot-climate conditions of Kairouan, Tunisia. Five bri
content: Abstract This study presents a two-dimensional transient CFD investigation of the thermal performance of hollow bricks incorporating air, glass wool, and phase change materials under the hot-climate conditions of Kairouan, Tunisia. Five brick geometries and three PCMs-RT26, RT30, and RT34 were evaluated over a 24-h thermal cycle using ANSYS Fluent R19. The numerical model, based on the enthalpy-porosity method, was validated against experimental data from the literature, with a maximum deviation below 3%. The solid brick exhibited the highest thermal load, with an energy demand of 191.78 Wh·m⁻², whereas the air- and glass-wool-filled bricks reduced this value to 84.90 and 73.80 Wh·m⁻², respectively. Among the investigated PCMs, RT30 achieved the best balance between latent-heat activation and thermal regulation, with an energy demand of 77.90 Wh·m⁻² and a maximum liquid fraction of 0.45. RT26 melted completely but activated too early, while RT34 reached a maximum liquid fraction of only 0.27 and increased energy demand to 96.50 Wh·m⁻². Increasing the cavity number from 8 to 12 reduced the transmitted heat flux by up to 57.65% under the investigated configurations. Overall, glass wool provided the lowest energy demand, while PCM performance depended strongly on the compatibility between its melting range, cavity geometry, and imposed thermal cycle.

title: Spinel MnFe2O4 nanoparticles with improved surface area and charge transfer characteristics for next-generation supercapacitors
source: Journal of Sol-Gel Science and Technology
summary: The growing demand for sustainable and efficient energy storage devices has accelerated the development of advanced electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors. In this work, MnFe₂O₄ nanoparticles were successfully synthesized
content: The growing demand for sustainable and efficient energy storage devices has accelerated the development of advanced electrode materials for high-performance supercapacitors. In this work, MnFe₂O₄ nanoparticles were successfully synthesized through a novel green co-precipitation approach using Curcuma longa extract as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of highly crystalline spinel MnFe₂O₄ with an average crystallite size of 19.9 nm and excellent phase purity. Raman spectroscopy further validated the characteristic vibrational modes of the spinel ferrite structure, while BET analysis revealed an enhanced surface area with mesoporous characteristics favorable for ion diffusion. SEM images demonstrated porous cauliflower-like interconnected morphology, and EDX confirmed the homogeneous distribution of Mn, Fe, and O elements without impurities. Electrochemical studies exhibited remarkable pseudocapacitive behavior with a high specific capacitance of 295 F g⁻¹ at 0.8 A g⁻¹ and 87.3% capacitance retention after 5000 charge–discharge cycles. Furthermore, EIS analysis revealed low charge transfer resistance and enhanced ion diffusion kinetics, confirming the strong potential of green-synthesized MnFe₂O₄ for sustainable next-generation supercapacitor applications.

title: Global distributions and environmental correlates of community leaf length and width in forests
summary: Leaf length and width are key dimensions of tree leaf size and can influence leaf boundary-layer development and leaf-environment heat exchange. However, their global patterns and environmental correlates remain poorly understood. By integr
content: Leaf length and width are key dimensions of tree leaf size and can influence leaf boundary-layer development and leaf-environment heat exchange. However, their global patterns and environmental correlates remain poorly understood. By integrating tree leaf traits and community data, we mapped community leaf length and width and identified their environmental correlates in global forests. Both community leaf length and width decreased toward higher latitudes, although leaf width showed an additional peak at mid-latitudes. These asynchronous patterns contributed to geographic variation in leaf shape, with more elongated leaves in tropical and boreal forests and relatively rounder leaves in temperate forests. Soil variables and mean annual temperature were the main correlates of leaf length, whereas leaf width was mainly associated with temperature. Our results reveal distinct environmental correlates of community leaf length and width, highlight the value of multiple leaf dimensions for predicting forest distributions and function, and identify tropical regions where additional trait data are needed to reduce uncertainty.

title: Towards standardised development of palaeofire charcoal reference sets via muffle furnace pyrolysis for Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
summary: Background The application of Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to subfossilised charcoal preserved in natural archives has been shown to be a useful technique to better understand historical fire (i.e. palaeofire) conditions.
content: Background The application of Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) to subfossilised charcoal preserved in natural archives has been shown to be a useful technique to better understand historical fire (i.e. palaeofire) conditions. The reliability of FTIR analyses in palaeoecological studies is contingent on the robustness of charcoal reference sets, many of which are produced via muffle furnace pyrolysis under varying methodologies. Aim We tested how various methodological approaches influence FTIR spectral signatures, using dried plant material (leaves and branches) derived from Eucalyptus camaldulensis. Methods Methods evaluated included the preparation (e.g. milled or unmilled), containment (e.g. aluminium foil or container) and cooling (e.g. internal or external) of the modern reference material. Key results We found that methodological approaches substantially influence FTIR signatures and subsequent classification accuracies, determined via leave-one-out centroid matching, varying by nearly 30% between approaches. Conclusions We suggest that loosely containing samples in aluminium foil, using sand mediums (e.g. 50.00 ± 0.05 g and a grain size of 250–500 μm) for thermal buffering and immediately removing samples from the muffle furnace for cooling are preferred protocols for generating reference sets via muffle furnace pyrolysis. Implications This study highlights the critical importance of methodological transparency and standardised methodological protocols in developing charcoal reference sets for palaeofire analyses.

title: Proteomic profiling of Camelus dromedarius blood leukocytes using protein sequence database searches and de novo peptide sequencing
source: Journal of King Saud University - Science
summary: There is a lack of studies on the crude leukocyte proteome of camels. Therefore, we hypothesized that camel leukocytes could be a source of bioactive peptides that have not been studied before. Here, we present the first comprehensive prote
content: There is a lack of studies on the crude leukocyte proteome of camels. Therefore, we hypothesized that camel leukocytes could be a source of bioactive peptides that have not been studied before. Here, we present the first comprehensive proteomic analysis of dromedary camel crude leukocyte-derived polypeptides (CLDP) using both protein sequence database searches (PSD) and de novo peptide sequencing (DPS) to improve peptide identification and coverage. The crude protein was extracted and analyzed by LC-MS/MS, followed by identification of protein and peptide sequences through PSD and DPS. PSD identified 120 proteins based on the Camelus dromedarius and Sus scrofa databases, while DPS identified a total of 830 peptides with an average local confidence (ALC) of 95% or higher. Gene Ontology (GO) annotation and KEGG analysis highlighted terms associated with stress adaptation, extracellular signaling, and immune response. However, DPS exhibited a broader and more pronounced enrichment trend, particularly in relation to the immune system.

title: Grayscale Photomasks Enable Noncontact Optical Patterning of Hydroxypropyl Cellulose Gels for Dynamic Art
summary: ABSTRACT Hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) forms cholesteric photonic gels with dynamic structural color, but most HPC systems are tuned globally or patterned through serial fabrication. Here we report a mask‐encoded parallel photonic manufactu
content: ABSTRACT Hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) forms cholesteric photonic gels with dynamic structural color, but most HPC systems are tuned globally or patterned through serial fabrication. Here we report a mask‐encoded parallel photonic manufacturing strategy that locally regulates the reflected wavelength of acrylamide‐containing HPC (AM‐HPC) photonic gels. UV‐induced photopolymerization produces a dose‐dependent blueshift consistent with cholesteric‐pitch compression, yielding a 204 nm (662–458 nm) tuning window in 68 wt.% AM‐HPC under time‐controlled exposure and spatial features down to 50 µm. To translate this response into programmable manufacturing, we combine Gaussian‐process active‐learning calibration with an experimentally measured mask‐opacity‐to‐UV transfer function. This workflow converts two‐dimensional target wavelength fields into grayscale optical masks, enabling spatially varying UV doses to be delivered simultaneously across a continuous, unsegmented gel. A single 10 s exposure produced multilevel structural‐color images with an 85 µm mask‐pixel pitch (13 840 pixels cm − 2 ) in a continuous gel. The patterned gels retain thermally responsive structural color, allowing dynamic modulation of encoded images. These results establish a proof‐of‐concept digital‐to‐material workflow for parallel, composition‐specific programming of apparent structural color in continuous HPC photonic gels.

title: Modifications of Fiber Surface and Resin Matrix on Enhancing Interfacial Strength of UV ‐ CIPP Materials
summary: ABSTRACT Ultraviolet‐cured‐in‐place‐pipe (UV‐CIPP) technology is widely used for trenchless rehabilitation of urban pipelines. However, the multilayered liner structure is prone to debonding and delamination due to weak interfacial bonding
content: ABSTRACT Ultraviolet‐cured‐in‐place‐pipe (UV‐CIPP) technology is widely used for trenchless rehabilitation of urban pipelines. However, the multilayered liner structure is prone to debonding and delamination due to weak interfacial bonding between fibers and the resin matrix. To address this issue, microdroplet pull‐out tests were conducted on glass fiber/UV‐curable resin systems to investigate the effects of fiber surface silanization and resin matrix filler modification on interfacial properties. The surface morphology, roughness, and chemical composition of glass fibers were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Three‐point bending tests were performed on laminated specimens to validate the translation of microscale interfacial improvements to macroscopic bending performance. The preferred curing parameters were determined as 150 s and 60 mW/cm 2 . For the three strategies, interfacial shear strength (IFSS) exhibited a non‐monotonic trend with increasing modification extent. KH560 treatment for 9 h yielded a maximum IFSS of 20.63 ± 1.63 MPa among the silane‐modified groups, accompanied by an increase in surface roughness Ra from 0.273 to 0.396 nm, as revealed by AFM, and successful silane grafting, as confirmed by XPS. For resin matrix modification, the preferred MgO content was 3.5 wt%, achieving an IFSS of 20.80 ± 1.88 MPa, while the preferred nano‐SiO 2 content was 3 wt%, achieving an IFSS of 22.70 ± 1.39 MPa. The bending tests confirmed that enhanced interfacial bonding translated into improved flexural performance, with the ranking of reinforcing effectiveness consistent with the microscale results.

title: Tailoring Carbon Vacancies by Conformational Pre‐Organization Enables Hard Carbon Anodes Toward Ultra‐Long Cycle Life
summary: ABSTRACT Hard carbon is regarded as the most promising anode material for sodium‐ion batteries; however, its intrinsically sluggish kinetics and unstable electrode/electrolyte interphase during cycling fundamentally restrict its rate capabi
content: ABSTRACT Hard carbon is regarded as the most promising anode material for sodium‐ion batteries; however, its intrinsically sluggish kinetics and unstable electrode/electrolyte interphase during cycling fundamentally restrict its rate capability and cycling stability. To overcome these issues, we propose a strategy for tailoring carbon vacancies via conformational pre‐organization of the precursor architecture. Specifically, impurity atoms in the precursor serve as anchoring sites to introduce carbon vacancies that facilitate rapid Na + diffusion. Owing to their localized negative charges, these vacancies preferentially capture Na + while excluding coordinating solvents, homogenizing the interfacial electric field, and diminishing the charge‐transfer resistance. This synergistic effect reinforces interfacial stability and promotes low‐temperature ion‐transport kinetics, leading to markedly improved rate capability and cycling durability. Consequently, the optimized hard carbon anodes deliver an ultra‐long cycle life, achieving 16 000 and 10 000 cycles at 1.0 and 5.0 A g −1 , respectively. Even at −20°C, the advanced anode maintains a capacity retention of 92.40% after 800 cycles at 0.1 A g −1 , further demonstrating its excellent cycling stability. Furthermore, the full cells assembled with Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 retain 79.74% of their initial capacity after 3200 cycles at 10C. This work establishes a design paradigm for engineering hard carbon anodes with ultra‐long cycling durability.

title: Tuning the structure-piezoelectric property relationship in electrospun PLLA nanofibers through collector-induced fiber alignment
summary: Electrospinning has become one of the most common methods to fabricate piezoelectric polymer nanofibers for flexible electronics, sensors, energy harvesting devices, and bioelectronic scaffolds. Fiber alignment is one of many parameters tha
content: Electrospinning has become one of the most common methods to fabricate piezoelectric polymer nanofibers for flexible electronics, sensors, energy harvesting devices, and bioelectronic scaffolds. Fiber alignment is one of many parameters that can impact nanofiber performance attributes since alignment affects mechanical anisotropy, crystal organization, and piezoelectric response. Nonetheless, few published works provide an in-depth discussion of collector rotation speed as it impacts nanofiber alignment, leaving detailed and reproducible methods for tuning alignment-dependent piezoelectric performance largely unreported. Here, we report a standardized electrospinning protocol to reproducibly fabricate piezoelectric nanofibers with controlled alignment through tuning the speed of a rotating collector. The steps in this protocol include preparing polymer solutions, setting up an electrospinning system, determining collector speed, collecting fibers, performing optional post-processing steps, and quantitatively evaluating fiber morphology and piezoelectric response. The protocol was validated through quantification of fiber alignment using scanning electron microscopy coupled with image-based orientation metrics, and piezoelectric performance through quantification of electrical output and piezoelectric coefficients. We demonstrated that increasing collector rotation speed from 1000 to 4000 rpm reduced orientation spread from 19.57° to 11.23°, and showed this increase in alignment was associated with an increase in the effective piezoelectric coefficient (d33) from 3.37 pC/N to 5.92 pC/N and an increase in open-circuit voltage output from 15 mV to 35 mV. These results highlight how the provided protocol enables users to reproducibly tune nanofiber orientation and associated piezoelectric performance. This protocol can aid in the design of scaffolds with tunable properties, wearable sensors, and mechanically-triggered energy harvesting devices.

title: System‐Local Axes and Metabolic Reprogramming From Health to Response in House Dust Mite‐Specific Subcutaneous Immunotherapy for Allergic Rhinitis
summary: ABSTRACT Allergic rhinitis (AR) features mucosal inflammation and systemic immune activation; the coordination of local and circulating metabolism during disease and immunotherapy is unclear. We performed untargeted LC‐MS metabolomics on pa
content: ABSTRACT Allergic rhinitis (AR) features mucosal inflammation and systemic immune activation; the coordination of local and circulating metabolism during disease and immunotherapy is unclear. We performed untargeted LC‐MS metabolomics on paired plasma and nasal secretion samples from 28 house dust mite (HDM)‐induced AR patients before and after 6 months of subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT), together with 19 healthy controls. Over 1800 annotated metabolites revealed compartmentalized metabolic reprogramming in AR. Nasal secretions displayed disrupted lipid, steroid, and redox metabolism linked to epithelial injury and local inflammation, while plasma had altered nucleotide and NAD + metabolism reflecting systemic type 2 inflammatory stress. After clinically effective SCIT, metabolic profiles shifted toward healthy status, with nasal metabolites showing stronger treatment‑associated changes. Two exploratory candidate axes were observed: a plasma nucleotide/NAD + axis potentially reflecting systemic immunometabolic burden, and a nasal lipid‐steroid‐redox axis possibly linked to mucosal remission, yielding candidate features that may support future longitudinal surveillance. Combined local and systemic metabolomics reveals asynchronous yet coordinated immunometabolic remodeling throughout AR onset and SCIT intervention, providing candidate features for future development of noninvasive strategies to assess disease activity and therapeutic response.

title: Multifunctional Fe, N Co-Doped Microporous Carbons Derived from Conjugated Microporous Polymer Containing Tetraphenylethylene and Iron-Chelated 1,10-Phenanthroline Units as Platforms for CO2 Uptake, Supercapacitor, and Oxygen Evolution Reaction
summary: Abstract The development of multifunctional microporous carbons for integrated electrochemical energy storage, CO2 capture, and oxygen evolution electrocatalysis (OEECs) is an attractive approach for sustainable energy applications. In this
content: Abstract The development of multifunctional microporous carbons for integrated electrochemical energy storage, CO2 capture, and oxygen evolution electrocatalysis (OEECs) is an attractive approach for sustainable energy applications. In this work, Fe/N codoped porous carbons (TPE-PhenFe-CMP-700 and TPE-PhenFe-CMP-800) were synthesized from a tailor-made conjugated microporous polymer (CMP) precursor prepared through a Sonogashira–Hagihara cross-coupling reaction between an ethynyl-functionalized tetraphenylethylene (TPE-T) linker and an iron-chelated 3,8-dibromo-1,10-phenanthroline (Phen-Fe-2Br) monomer. The molecularly engineered precursor enables well-distributed Fe and N species throughout the carbon framework after carbonization. Among the materials obtained, TPE-PhenFe-CMP-800 exhibits a SBET of 411 m2 g–1 and a well-developed porous graphitic structure. The synergistic combination of porosity-enhanced graphitic carbon networks and the presence of Fe–N active sites endows the material with outstanding multifunctional performance. The TPE-PhenFe-CMP-800 delivers high specific capacitance (Cs) of 892 F g–1 at 0.5 A g–1, in a three-electrode supercapacitor (SCs) configuration, together with excellent CO2 adsorption of 4.01 mmol g–1 at 273 K. Furthermore, TPE-PhenFe-CMP-800 exhibits outstanding OER electrocatalytic activity, demonstrating an overpotential as low as 530 mV to reach 10 mA cm–2, along with a favorable Tafel slope of 82 mV dec–1 and an extensive electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of 76 cm2. These results demonstrate that molecular engineering of CMP precursors provides an effective strategy for constructing multifunctional Fe/N codoped porous carbons, offering a versatile platform for advanced electrochemical energy storage, CO2 capture, and electrocatalytic applications.

title: High-resolution reconstruction of redox changes using XRF core scanner: depth-transect redox changes in the Japan Sea during the Quaternary
source: Progress in Earth and Planetary Science
summary: Abstract The reconstruction of past marine bottom-water redox conditions are crucial because it reflects changes in ocean circulation, surface productivity, and the precipitation–evaporation balance. However, long-term (Myr scale), high-res
content: Abstract The reconstruction of past marine bottom-water redox conditions are crucial because it reflects changes in ocean circulation, surface productivity, and the precipitation–evaporation balance. However, long-term (Myr scale), high-resolution (mm scale), redox reconstructions remain scarce because traditional discrete-sample analyses are highly time-consuming. While the Japan Sea is known for past high-frequency fluctuations of deep-water redox conditions, the existing records are limited to the past 640 kyr at a relatively low resolution. In this study, we propose a novel method for estimating deep-water redox conditions using high-resolution XRF core scanning data and apply it to reconstruct Quaternary deep-water redox changes in the Japan Sea. First, we developed an XRF core scanner-based, high-throughput method that drastically accelerates the estimation of past deep-water oxygenation. We utilized XRF core scanner-derived Br/S, Fe/Ti, and Fe/S ratios, which are substitutes for the conventional redox-sensitive parameters C/S ratio, Fe/Al ratio, and degree of pyritization (DOP) respectively, for classification of deep-water redox conditions into four ranks. Then, we applied this method to a depth transect in the Japan Sea consisting of three sediment cores (~ 1000, ~2000, and ~3000 m water depths) from the Japan Sea. Our ultra high-resolution (mm scale) data reveal that deep-water redox conditions fluctuated from euxinic to oxic at ~cm scales.
