"Sampling Frequency Distributions Plotter.py" is used to plot the data pruning analysis. "TIC TOC and Base Sat Plotter.py" is used to plot the carbon pool and base saturation data.

title: Rational Control of Antibody Orientation for Enhancing Sensitivity and Specificity in Lateral Flow Immunoassays With Clinical Validation
summary: Lateral flow assays (LFAs) are widely used for point-of-care diagnostics, but their sensitivity is often limited by inefficient antibody orientation and poor signal transduction. Herein, we report a universal strategy integrating orientatio
content: Lateral flow assays (LFAs) are widely used for point-of-care diagnostics, but their sensitivity is often limited by inefficient antibody orientation and poor signal transduction. Herein, we report a universal strategy integrating orientation-controlled antibody conjugation at the immunoprobe with a biotin-streptavidin-modified test line to enhance LFA sensitivity, specificity, and analytical reliability. Using an orientation-controlled conjugation approach (P-6, Scheme 1), antigen accessibility was maximized while nonspecific adsorption and false-positive signals were suppressed. Compared with conventional randomly conjugated probes (P-3, Scheme 1) on unmodified test lines, the combined P-6/biotin-streptavidin configuration achieved limits of detection of 0.0352 ng/mL for cytokeratin 19 fragment (CYFRA21-1) and 0.0808 ng/mL for carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), corresponding to sensitivity enhancements of approximately 14-19 fold. However, probe rankings get inverted across capture chemistries, indicating the importance of dual-site orientation. The universality of this strategy was further validated using alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA125), carbohydrate antigen 15-3 (CA15-3), and prostate-specific antigen (PSA). Furthermore, multiplexed LFAs using fluorescent polymer dots enabled simultaneous detection of CYFRA21-1 and CEA with minimal cross-reactivity and were validated in 28 clinical serum samples against the hospital reference method.

title: Methodologies for Developing Consumption-Based Urban GHG Emission Inventories: A Systematic Review
summary: As cities emerge as the primary drivers of global consumption-based emissions, the need for greenhouse gas (GHG) accounting methods that model multisectoral urban interactions has become paramount. In this context, consumption-based (CB) ur
content: As cities emerge as the primary drivers of global consumption-based emissions, the need for greenhouse gas (GHG) accounting methods that model multisectoral urban interactions has become paramount. In this context, consumption-based (CB) urban GHG emission inventories have arisen as a useful tool for political decision-makers. This systematic literature review was carried out across three databases, covering al-most 20 years of publications strictly related to the elaboration of CB GHG emission inventories, reaching a total of 100 publications. More than a third of the articles ex-plored Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), 34% used Environmentally-Extended In-put-Output Analysis (EEIOA), with only 10% delving into hybrid methodologies. A case study comparison was performed for cities that applied different methodologies, in terms of carbon footprint. The strengths and weaknesses of each framework were also assessed. The results showed that both EEIOA and LCA were useful to model complex carbon flows and accounted for the majority of emissions associated to urban activity. EEIOA excelled for its operational simplicity and speed in the calculation of carbon footprint when input-output matrices are available, but it was not as suitable for policy-making. LCA required a larger volume of information and its processing was more time-consuming, but it was also capable of identifying hotspots. Hybrid approaches obtained carbon footprint results similar to those of EEIOA or LCA, while covering certain weaknesses of these standalone methodologies.

title: ECCSEL ERIC Profile
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: ECCSEL ERIC (European Carbon Dioxide Capture and Storage Laboratory – European Research Infrastructure Consortium) is the European research infrastructure for CO2 Capture, Utilisation, Transport and Storage (CCUS), Carbon Dioxide Removal (C
content: ECCSEL ERIC (European Carbon Dioxide Capture and Storage Laboratory – European Research Infrastructure Consortium) is the European research infrastructure for CO2 Capture, Utilisation, Transport and Storage (CCUS), Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR), Low Carbon Energy Storage (LCES) and Geothermal. Our vision is to enable net zero CO2 emissions from industry and energy systems, and accelerate research and innovation. ECCSEL is a permanent, distributed, integrated research infrastructure encompassing interlinked transnational scientific facilities and national nodes.

title: Synthesis and Preliminary Biological Evaluation of a Structurally Modified Niraparib-Based PARP-Targeted PET Tracer for Tumor Imaging
summary: Abstract Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) is highly expressed in various malignancies and represents an important therapeutic target. Noninvasive evaluation of PARP expression is therefore of potential clinical significance for patient st
content: Abstract Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) is highly expressed in various malignancies and represents an important therapeutic target. Noninvasive evaluation of PARP expression is therefore of potential clinical significance for patient stratification. In this study, we developed and evaluated [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-MK-4827, a structurally modified PARP-targeted radiotracer derived from niraparib, featuring a two-carbon linker between the DOTA chelator and the pharmacophore. [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-MK-4827 demonstrated high uptake in MDA-MB-231 and OE-19 tumors with elevated PARP-1 expression, which was significantly reduced by blocking, supporting a PARP-related component of tumor accumulation. The tracer exhibited favorable pharmacokinetics, including high hydrophilicity and predominantly renal clearance, resulting in low abdominal background activity. Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging enabled clear tumor visualization with good contrast, supported by biodistribution findings. Preliminary clinical imaging further showed notable uptake in an esophageal cancer lesion, with immunohistochemical confirmation of PARP-1 expression in the biopsied tissue. These results suggest that [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-MK-4827 has potential as a PARP-targeted PET tracer for tumor imaging and merits further investigation in larger clinical cohorts.

title: Stock market reaction to the announcement of Morocco’s voluntary carbon market: An event study
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe growing development of voluntary carbon markets has raised increasing interest in understanding how financial markets respond to climate-related policy announcements, particularly in emerging
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThe growing development of voluntary carbon markets has raised increasing interest in understanding how financial markets respond to climate-related policy announcements, particularly in emerging economies. This study investigates the stock market reaction to the official announcement of the operational launch of Morocco’s voluntary carbon market on September 24, 2024. The analysis applies the event study methodology to a sample of the eight largest companies listed on the Casablanca Stock Exchange to estimate expected returns and abnormal returns over an event window of [–4; +5].The results indicate that the announcement did not generate statistically significant abnormal stock market reactions. On the event day (t = 0), the average abnormal return (AAR) was –0.238% (t = –1.006; p = 0.348), while the cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over the [–4; +5] event window reached 1.00% (t = 0.615; p = 0.550), indicating the absence of a statistically significant market response. A robustness analysis using an alternative event window [–3; +3] produced similar results (CAR = 1.52%, t = 1.494; p = 0.186), confirming the stability of our finding.Overall, the evidence suggests that the operational launch of Morocco’s voluntary carbon market did not constitute value-relevant information capable of significantly influencing investors’ expectations or short-term market valuation, reflecting the early stage of development of the country’s voluntary carbon market.

title: Code for: Overestimated CO2 emissions from dryland lakes challenge global lake carbon budgets
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The code calculates lake-water pCO2 and uses a random forest model to estimate CO2 fluxes from global dryland lakes. 01_CO2SYS (MATLAB) calc_pCO2_main.m: calculates pCO2 from pH and DIC with CO2SYS (K1/K2 of Cai & Wang, 1998; NBS pH scale).
content: The code calculates lake-water pCO2 and uses a random forest model to estimate CO2 fluxes from global dryland lakes. 01_CO2SYS (MATLAB) calc_pCO2_main.m: calculates pCO2 from pH and DIC with CO2SYS (K1/K2 of Cai & Wang, 1998; NBS pH scale). calc_pCO2_input_pairs_constants.m: calculates pCO2 from three input pairs (pH + DIC, TA + DIC, TA + pH) with 17 sets of K1/K2 constants. 02_RandomForest (Python) rf_grid_search_cv.py: 5-fold cross-validation over the number of trees and maximum tree depth. rf_cv_predictions.py: cross-validated predictions with the selected model (200 trees, maximum depth 13). rf_permutation_importance.py: permutation importance and relative contributions of the predictors. rf_global_prediction.py: prediction of CO2 fluxes for global lakes.

title: Two-Stage Combustion of Ammonia/Hydrogen Blends: An Experimental Approach to Low-Carbon Fuel Utilisation
summary: This study presents an experimental investigation of a laboratory-scale two-stage RQL-based combustor burning NH3/H2 fuel blends at a thermal input of 8.0–8.5 kW and atmospheric pressure using fuels containing 70–100% ammonia by volume in t
content: This study presents an experimental investigation of a laboratory-scale two-stage RQL-based combustor burning NH3/H2 fuel blends at a thermal input of 8.0–8.5 kW and atmospheric pressure using fuels containing 70–100% ammonia by volume in the first stage and 80–100% in two-stage operation. The first stage operated under fuel-rich conditions (ϕ1 = 1.2–1.4), while the second stage operated under globally lean conditions (ϕG = 0.5–0.9). Unlike conventional rich–quench–lean combustors, the secondary stage allows controlled hydrogen injection upstream of the secondary air inlet to enhance ammonia burnout. Temperature profiles and exhaust NH3, NOx and O2 concentrations were measured with and without secondary fuel injection. The burner operated stably over a wide range of fuel compositions, including pure ammonia, while maintaining reduced NOx emissions in the rich stage. Two-stage operation exhibited a clear trade-off: secondary hydrogen reduced ammonia slip, but NOx emissions increased above the 59 ppm and 24 ppm reference benchmarks under most conditions and exceeded 200 ppm in some cases. Incremental secondary hydrogen injection, tested with pure ammonia at ϕ1 = 1.3, ϕG = 0.6, identified an operating window of approximately 100–300 W, within which ammonia slip decreased to 10–20 ppm with a moderate increase in NOx above 300 W. Further reduction in ammonia slip was limited while NOx emissions continued to increase.

title: A sensitivity analysis of insulation material and thickness in a timber frame external wall
summary: Low-carbon design policy, including the Welsh Housing Quality Standard 2023, increasingly pushes designers toward higher-performance insulation to reduce operational carbon. This study asks whether this assumption holds once the whole life
content: Low-carbon design policy, including the Welsh Housing Quality Standard 2023, increasingly pushes designers toward higher-performance insulation to reduce operational carbon. This study asks whether this assumption holds once the whole life embodied carbon cost of that insulation is considered. A sensitivity analysis compared mineral wool (Rockwool) and PIR (Celotex) across four thicknesses (100–220mm), with U-values from BR 443, operational carbon from SAP, and embodied carbon from ICE V3 factors. Embodied carbon ranged 7.3–7.7 tCO₂e for mineral wool versus 8.4–10.1 tCO₂e for PIR, yet even at maximum thickness, PIR cut operational emissions by only 34 kgCO₂/year. The resulting carbon payback period is approximately 71 years, exceeding the 60-year reference period. This confirms material choice outweighs thickness: minimum-thickness PIR generates more embodied carbon than maximum-thickness mineral wool. Mineral wool insulation, across the thicknesses assessed, is therefore recommended as the more robust whole-life carbon strategy within the scope of this study.

title: Occupant Perceptions of Indoor Air Quality Determinants, Monitoring Awareness and Mitigation Priorities in Near-Road Purpose-Built Student Accommodation: An Exploratory UK Case Study
summary: Purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) is characterised by prolonged residential occupancy, compact spatial arrangements and managed building systems. Yet comparatively little evidence addresses how residents understand indoor air quali
content: Purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) is characterised by prolonged residential occupancy, compact spatial arrangements and managed building systems. Yet comparatively little evidence addresses how residents understand indoor air quality (IAQ) determinants and prioritise monitoring and mitigation. This exploratory cross-sectional case study examined occupants’ perceptions of environmental and building-related IAQ determinants, awareness of IAQ monitoring technologies, endorsement of mitigation strategies, and overall self-rated IAQ in a near-road PBSA in Bolton, United Kingdom. Seventy-seven survey records were returned, with two respondents under 18 years who provided no substantive IAQ responses, leaving 75 complete cases. Composite scores showed satisfactory internal consistency for environmental-determinant recognition (α = .841), building-related determinant recognition (α = .708), monitoring awareness (α = .838) and mitigation-strategy endorsement (α = .950). Respondents generally recognised the listed determinants and supported the mitigation strategies, and monitoring-awareness scores were positively correlated with mitigation endorsement. In a multiple linear regression, the three predictors jointly explained 63.5% of the variance in mitigation-strategy endorsement (R² = .635; adjusted R² = .620). Residual diagnostics indicated heteroscedasticity, so HC3 robust inference was used. Monitoring awareness showed the strongest independent association with mitigation endorsement (standardised β = .434, p < .001), followed by building-related determinant recognition (β = .292, p = .004). The environmental-determinant association was positive but borderline under robust inference (β = .205, p = .053). Overall self-rated IAQ was analysed separately and was not the dependent variable in this regression. The study therefore contributes context-specific evidence on occupant IAQ awareness and management priorities. Future multi-site research should combine occupant surveys with direct environmental and ventilation measurements.

title: Should food finance carbon removal? A comment
summary: This commentary focuses on the public acceptance prospects of Moberg, Lyngfelt and Fridahl's proposal for a climate fee on food consumption to finance carbon removal. On the negative side, the fee raises household costs and falls disproport
content: This commentary focuses on the public acceptance prospects of Moberg, Lyngfelt and Fridahl's proposal for a climate fee on food consumption to finance carbon removal. On the negative side, the fee raises household costs and falls disproportionately, if modestly, on low-income groups, both factors known to weaken support for climate policy instruments. On the positive side, several design features work in the proposal's favour: earmarking revenue into a dedicated fund outside the state budget, rather than the general treasury, has been shown to increase acceptance and reduce the political risk of erosion during fiscal strain, while a clear, measurable link between payment and carbon removal may support perceived effectiveness. The commentary also discusses whether the fund should finance carbon removal alone or broader climate measures, as well as how the fee relates to the EU's forthcoming new Emissions Trading System.

title: Novel Microparticulation of Pea Protein: Structural Transformation, Enhanced Gelation, Dispersion Stability, and Off‐Taste Masking
summary: ABSTRACT Pea protein isolate (PPI) suffers from poor solubility, weak gel‐forming ability, and undesirable sensory attributes that limit its wider adoption in plant‐based food products. This study reports a novel three‐stage process for pro
content: ABSTRACT Pea protein isolate (PPI) suffers from poor solubility, weak gel‐forming ability, and undesirable sensory attributes that limit its wider adoption in plant‐based food products. This study reports a novel three‐stage process for producing plant protein microparticulate by combining pH shift, high‐pressure homogenization, and heat treatment. The microparticulated pea protein isolate (MPPI) demonstrated substantially improved functional properties relative to native PPI. Microparticulation reduced the volume‐weighted median particle diameter ( d 50 ) approximately 10‐fold (from ∼61.8 to ∼6.2 µm) and apparent particle density by ∼1.9‐fold (from 1.07 to 0.57 g/cm 3 ). The taste profiling further revealed that microparticulation altered the taste profile of PPI, with notable shifts in off‐taste like astringency and bitterness. Dispersion analysis of 15% (w/w/) solution of MPPI using LUMiSizer showed an 85.5% reduction in sedimentation velocity and a 99.6% reduction in sediment height relative to PPI, reflecting markedly improved colloidal stability. Structural characterization revealed a significant reduction in surface hydrophobicity and intrinsic fluorescence intensity of MPPI compared to PPI, while free sulfhydryl content increased markedly (from 320.26 to 1571.20 nmol/mg), confirming extensive structural destabilization of MPPI due to protein unfolding and subsequent hydrophobic‐core burial as well as thiol exposure. Rheological analysis demonstrated that MPPI exhibited approximately one order of magnitude higher storage modulus ( G ′) and consistency index ( K ) than native PPI, with superior structural resilience under oscillatory deformation. In situ gelation experiments showed that MPPI formed denser, mechanically stronger elastic gels upon heating and cooling, with substantially higher final G ′ values. These findings therefore confirm microparticulation as an effective strategy for unlocking the structural and functional potential of PPI for wider plant‐based food applications.

title: Catalyzing sustainable development through digitalization: the nexus between government digital transition and green total factor productivity
summary: Green total factor productivity (GTFP) represents a cornerstone for sustainable development; however, previous scholarship has primarily concentrated on market-based or technological determinants, frequently ignoring the impact of instituti
content: Green total factor productivity (GTFP) represents a cornerstone for sustainable development; however, previous scholarship has primarily concentrated on market-based or technological determinants, frequently ignoring the impact of institutional governance. Comprehending the mechanisms through which digital public administration drives GTFP is vital for facilitating a profound ecological shift in both society and the broader economy. By utilizing the 2018 e-government comprehensive pilot as a quasi-natural experiment, we evaluate the impact of government digital transition on GTFP via a difference-in-differences (DID) framework, analyzing panel data from 285 Chinese municipalities spanning 2013 to 2021. The findings demonstrate that digital governance significantly improves GTFP, with the effect operating primarily through technological progress rather than technical efficiency change. These findings are robust across various specifications and validity checks. Heterogeneity results reveal that the positive impact is more noticeable in ordinary prefecture-level and inland urban centers, suggesting a compensatory role of institutional intervention. Mediation analyses reveal that digital government improves GTFP by enhancing government information transparency and fostering technological innovation. Moderation analyses further show that this positive effect is amplified where factor marketization and digital economy development are more advanced. By shifting the focus from traditional drivers to institutional governance, this paper offers novel perspectives on the digital government-GTFP nexus and provides policymakers concrete evidence on viable pathways to sustainable development.

title: Prefabrication of structural walls from large mineral rubble
summary: Abstract This paper presents a new, low-carbon prefabrication process for load-bearing structural walls. It reuses large flat concrete and stone rubble sourced from demolition waste, is readily scalable, and operates under controlled factor
content: Abstract This paper presents a new, low-carbon prefabrication process for load-bearing structural walls. It reuses large flat concrete and stone rubble sourced from demolition waste, is readily scalable, and operates under controlled factory conditions, combining the structural logic of masonry with industrialized concrete prefabrication methods. The process begins by sourcing the mineral rubble pieces from demolition sites or recycling centers. Each piece is digitally inventoried by processing pictures taken on the worksite. The pieces are then virtually selected and arranged to determine their best assembly geometry, maximizing load-bearing capacity while minimizing void volume. Next, the pieces are placed horizontally on a tilting table according to the generated layout. A low-impact recycled concrete is poured into the voids. Once the material has hardened, the wall is tilted and lifted in its vertical orientation. Four full-scale walls have been built to assess technical feasibility, environmental performance, and structural behavior, and to provide relevant insights into productivity and potential process improvements. Preliminary compression testing demonstrates sufficient resistance for structural walls in low- to mid-rise buildings under conventional loads. Prototypical fabrication highlighted lower fabrication speed and higher labor demand than for traditional precast concrete walls, while optimistic estimates of batch processing suggest similar fabrication rates. A Life Cycle Assessment shows reductions of up to 83% in CO 2 eq emissions compared with recycled concrete walls, while significantly increasing the circularity of concrete.

title: Quantum-Dot-Containing Photopolymer Materials: Surface Chemistry, Optical Loss, Cure Interaction and Emission Stability
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Quantum dots can give photocurable polymers wavelength-selective absorption, tunable photoluminescence and, in some formulations, a direct role in photoinitiation. Their integration is not a simple filler-addition problem. The nanocrystal s
content: Quantum dots can give photocurable polymers wavelength-selective absorption, tunable photoluminescence and, in some formulations, a direct role in photoinitiation. Their integration is not a simple filler-addition problem. The nanocrystal surface controls dispersion, electronic states and interactions with monomers, initiators and propagating radicals; aggregation can increase scattering and spectral heterogeneity; and the optical field used to cure the resin can itself alter the emitter or the surrounding network. This review treats a quantum-dot photopolymer as a coupled colloidal, photochemical and optical system. It distinguishes nanocrystal identity from ligand-shell identity, separates absorption by the quantum dot from absorption by the photoinitiator, and links printability to the concentration-dependent balance among attenuation, radical generation, quenching, local heating and network formation. Published work on quantum-dot phase transfer into acrylate monomers, quantum-dot photoinitiation and carbon-dot-assisted vat printing demonstrates that stable dispersion and effective cure can be achieved, but also shows that the successful route is formulation-specific. A qualification framework is proposed around dispersion stability, spectral attenuation, cure response, photoluminescence quantum yield or relative emission, spatial uniformity, ageing and device-level optical performance. ER-421.

title: Bi-Level Coordinated Optimal Operation of a Multi-Microgrid System with Shared Energy Storage
summary: To improve sustainable operation of multi-microgrid (MMG) systems with high penetration of renewable energy, this paper proposes a bi-level coordinated optimization method based on Stackelberg and cooperative games to address wind–photovolt
content: To improve sustainable operation of multi-microgrid (MMG) systems with high penetration of renewable energy, this paper proposes a bi-level coordinated optimization method based on Stackelberg and cooperative games to address wind–photovoltaic output fluctuations, stakeholder coordination, and low-carbon dispatch under shared energy storage (SES). At the upper level, the shared energy storage operator (SESO) acts as the leader and the MMG coalition as the follower, forming a Stackelberg model for time-of-use service pricing and coordinated response. At the lower level, the coalition dispatch integrates tiered carbon trading, power-to-gas (P2G), and carbon capture and storage (CCS), together with a time-correlated continuous-budget uncertainty set and a two-stage robust scheduling model for wind power, photovoltaic output, and electricity prices. Marginal economic contribution is defined by the change in total system cost caused by an MG joining the coalition and is used to construct an asymmetric Nash benefit-allocation mechanism. Particle swarm optimization (PSO), the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMMs), and column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) form a hierarchical nested solution framework: PSO searches the upper-level service prices, ADMM coordinates the coalition’s continuous coupling variables, and C&CG generates adverse scenarios for the coalition-level two-stage robust problem. Tests on the IEEE 33-bus system show that, relative to deterministic optimization, robust scheduling incurs an 11.33% nominal operating-cost premium but reduces carbon emissions from 1478.55 to 1318.46 kg and improves adaptability under uncertain scenarios. The marginal-contribution-based Nash allocation keeps every MG’s allocated cost below its stand-alone cost. The proposed method, therefore, balances operating economy, robustness, low-carbon performance, and stakeholder benefits.

title: Forest Ecosystems and Sustainable Management in the Era of Climate Change
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Sustainable forest management under climate change requires protection of existing ecological assets, recovery of degraded forests, and management that can adjust as environmental conditions change. Forest area and tree growth alone are ina
content: Sustainable forest management under climate change requires protection of existing ecological assets, recovery of degraded forests, and management that can adjust as environmental conditions change. Forest area and tree growth alone are inadequate measures of success. Management must also sustain biodiversity, soils, water regulation, and the people who depend on forests. The literature supports a portfolio of responses tailored to forest type, disturbance history, and local objectives, with explicit attention to uncertainty and competing demands. Climate change affects forests through physiological stress, altered regeneration, and changes in disturbance regimes. Drought, fire, pests, and land-use pressures can interact, making forest recovery and carbon storage less predictable. Nevertheless, responses differ among regions, and global averages can conceal both deterioration and recovery. Forest carbon uptake remains substantial, but it should not be confused with the net climate benefit after deforestation emissions and other effects are considered. The management implications are conditional. Natural regeneration is valuable where recovery processes remain functional; planting and other interventions become more important where those processes are constrained. Fuel treatments can reduce subsequent wildfire severity in particular forest systems, but evidence from those systems does not justify indiscriminate treatment elsewhere. Community involvement can improve outcomes, yet participation alone does not guarantee equitable benefits. Decisions therefore need ecological diagnosis, secure and legitimate governance, long-term monitoring, and revision when outcomes diverge from expectations.

title: Accelerated weathering of limestone for CO2 capture and storage: a critical review of unbuffered, buffered, and modified pathways
summary: Accelerated weathering of limestone (AWL) converts CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate by reacting calcium carbonate and water, an alternative to geological storage. This review examines AWL as a branching family spanning the unbuffered concept,
content: Accelerated weathering of limestone (AWL) converts CO2 into dissolved bicarbonate by reacting calcium carbonate and water, an alternative to geological storage. This review examines AWL as a branching family spanning the unbuffered concept, buffered AWL (BAWL), and modified routes (potable-water, construction-grade waste limestone, promoter-assisted, utilization-based, ship-based, and electrochemical AWL), grouped into six classes covering reactor configuration, feedstock, dissolution promotion, effluent conditioning, downstream utilization, and electrochemically driven alkalinity generation. AWL has progressed from concept to bench-scale, pilot-scale, modeling, and techno-economic work, but remains pre-commercial, limited by water demand, slow dissolution, reactor size, weak permanence, discharge concerns, and BAWL's calcination cost. Unbuffered AWL is simple but degasses CO2 after discharge. BAWL improves permanence at greater complexity and upstream emissions, relocating rather than resolving the trade-off. Each route targets one bottleneck without resolving the system; cross-study comparison is difficult given differing objectives, water sources, and boundaries. A mass-balance framework separates gross gas-phase capture, dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) conversion, carbon retained, net stored CO2, and storage duration. The ΔTA/ΔDIC ratio, not capture efficiency alone, governs post-discharge degassing. Carbonic anhydrase raises capture up to 2.2-fold under 20 % CO2 and 4-fold under atmospheric contact, at bench scale. Future progress needs cleaner buffering, industrial-condition pilot testing, and standardised life-cycle accounting.

title: Review of essd-2026-587
summary: Abstract. The global geography, behaviour, and impact of fires are shifting, as spatially varying human influences interact with a visibly changing climate. The State of Wildfires project systematically tracks global and regional fire activ
content: Abstract. The global geography, behaviour, and impact of fires are shifting, as spatially varying human influences interact with a visibly changing climate. The State of Wildfires project systematically tracks global and regional fire activity, analyses the causes of prominent extreme wildfire events for three focal regions, and projects the likelihood of similar events under future climate scenarios. During the March 2025–February 2026 fire season, global burned area (BA) was 18 % below the 2002–2024 average and global fire carbon (C) emissions were also 20–31 % below average, making it one of the lowest years on record. Yet this globally low fire year still produced widespread regional impacts. Canada experienced a third consecutive extreme fire year, with national fire C emissions at nearly triple the average since 2002, 70,000 evacuations, and reported direct losses of USD 360 million. In the Midwestern Canadian Shield Forests, the epicentre of Canada’s anomalous season, we find that anthropogenic climate change has doubled the likelihood of extreme fire weather in this region and made the observed BA around 61 times more likely during July–August 2025, while BA extent in the region is 46 times greater. Many parts of Europe also experienced record or high-ranking BA and fire C emissions, including in Spain, Portugal, and the UK, and a record USD 4.11 billion of physical assets were exposed to fire across the continent. Direct fatalities occurred in Türkiye (17), Spain (8), Portugal (6), Cyprus (2), Greece (1) and France (1), and evacuations in Türkiye, Spain, and Greece totalled over 110,000. In the Northwest Iberian Peninsula, we find that extreme fire weather over August 2025 was around 3 times more likely due to climate change. Under a high-emissions scenario (SSP3-7.0), fires of the same return interval are likely to burn about 78 % more area by the end of the century, with some projections within the same scenario suggesting increases of around sevenfold. In Chile and northwest Argentina, January–February 2026 fires caused 23 fatalities, displaced 55,000 people and threatened a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the Chilean Temperate Forests and Matorral, the epicentre, we find that BA was around 36 % larger due to anthropogenic climate change. Across all focal regions in this report, the conditions for extreme fire developed gradually through months of precipitation deficits, cumulative drying and, in the case of Northwest Iberia, antecedent fuel accumulation aided by preceding wet periods. Continued climate change is expected to intensify these hydroclimatic extremes, yet mitigation has already reduced projected end-of-century wildfire risk: under a high-end emissions pathway (SSP3-7.0), the extreme BA events in our focal regions are projected to be 4–23 % smaller than they would have been under a worst-case emissions scenario no longer considered credible (SSP5-8.5). Meeting the Paris targets (SSP1-2.6) would further reduce BA during thes

title: Participant Mobility as a Temporary Urban Transport-Energy System: Energy Use, Carbon Emissions and Low-Carbon Scenarios for the 2024 Wuhan Marathon
summary: A mass-participation marathon assembles tens of thousands of people from many origins for a single morning, so its energy demand is dominated by a temporary transport system, not a venue. Event footprints are usually reported as one carbon
content: A mass-participation marathon assembles tens of thousands of people from many origins for a single morning, so its energy demand is dominated by a temporary transport system, not a venue. Event footprints are usually reported as one carbon total built on average travel assumptions, hiding both the heterogeneity of participant mobility and its uncertainty. This study builds an activity-based transport-energy account for the 30,000 participants in the 2024 Wuhan Marathon over nine modes and nine energy-intensity parameters, calibrates the one unobserved travel parameter against the event’s third-party certified inventory (a consistency check, not an independent measurement), and propagates sixteen parameters through 10,000 Monte Carlo runs and a Sobol decomposition. Participant mobility consumes 9097 GJ of final energy and emits 965.7 t CO2e, 32.2 kg per participant, at 33.7 g CO2e per passenger–kilometre. Aviation is 1.5% of mode users but 27.9% of energy. Travel distance carries 59% of output variance, energy intensity 18% and the much-debated aviation mode comprises 6%. Integrated operational measures cut energy by 21.8% but emissions by only 6.5%, whereas decarbonizing the regional grid cuts emissions by 56.6%: for this catchment, reducing transport energy and reducing transport carbon are not equivalent objectives.

title: Plants, silicon, and climate change
summary: Abstract This chapter considers some quite diverse topics that coalesce around the theme of climate change. It begins by looking at enhanced weathering as a method of drawing carbon down from the atmosphere. Here ground silicate rock is use
content: Abstract This chapter considers some quite diverse topics that coalesce around the theme of climate change. It begins by looking at enhanced weathering as a method of drawing carbon down from the atmosphere. Here ground silicate rock is used to react with atmospheric carbon dioxide, and the product can subsequently be stored in carbonate rocks. The chapter then briefly considers recent research on the effects of silicon (Si) on carbon (C) turnover and emissions from the soil. At present this is inconclusive. The potential role of phytoliths in C sequestration is the next area of discussion. It has now been studied for over twenty years and has been a controversial topic. Despite some progress, problems remain in determining the concentration of C in phytoliths and in assessing phytolith residence times in the soil. This chapter also investigates some of the ways in which Si affects plant response to climate change, particularly looking at the effect of increasing carbon dioxide concentrations in the atmosphere. Finally, drought is a major effect of climate change, and the chapter looks at recent work on Si and nutrient availability under conditions of water stress.

title: Environmental proactivity relates to perceived sustainability performance through green innovation and resource efficiency in Vietnamese manufacturing
summary: Manufacturers in emerging economies face simultaneous pressure to reduce environmental impacts and preserve operating competitiveness, yet a proactive environmental orientation does not automatically translate into broad sustainability gain
content: Manufacturers in emerging economies face simultaneous pressure to reduce environmental impacts and preserve operating competitiveness, yet a proactive environmental orientation does not automatically translate into broad sustainability gains. Drawing on the natural-resource-based view, dynamic capability theory, and institutional theory, this study examines two internal conversion mechanisms green innovation capability and resource efficiency and the contextual role of perceived environmental institutional pressure. Survey data from 278 knowledgeable informants in Vietnamese manufacturing firms were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, bootstrap mediation and moderation tests, robustness analyses, and 10-fold cross-validation. The findings show that environmental proactivity is associated with perceived sustainability performance both directly and indirectly through two complementary routes: renewal through green innovation capability and operational optimization through resource efficiency. Institutional pressure is positively associated with green innovation capability, but it does not significantly amplify the proactivity–innovation relationship. The study contributes by specifying how strategic environmental intent is converted into sustainability-oriented capabilities rather than treating orientation as a self-executing resource. For managers and policymakers, the results support a balanced portfolio that combines innovation capability building with resource-efficiency improvement, while using external pressure together with technical support, implementation capacity, and green-finance access.

title: Timber buildings and indoor air quality : evaluating the relationship between measured environmental conditions and occupant perception
summary: The use of timber in modern construction is increasing due to its low embodied carbon and contribution to net zero goals. However, concerns remain regarding its impact on indoor air quality (IAQ), particularly through volatile organic compo
content: The use of timber in modern construction is increasing due to its low embodied carbon and contribution to net zero goals. However, concerns remain regarding its impact on indoor air quality (IAQ), particularly through volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, while the relationship between measured IAQ and perceived air quality (PAQ) remains underexplored. This study compares measured IAQ and PAQ in the WIP Pavilion at Robotics Living Lab, MMU, a timber-frame building, and the Student Centre at UCL, a concrete-frame building with timber interior finishes. Temperature, relative humidity, CO2, TVOC and Formaldehyde were monitored and analysed against occupant questionnaire responses. Both buildings maintained IAQ within recommended guidelines, where ventilation strongly influenced pollutant concentrations. The WIP Pavilion received the most consistent positive comfort ratings. Overall, timber did not compromise IAQ under typical operating conditions, but enhanced occupant experience through sensory and psychological effects.

title: Decomposing the divergence in reported carbon footprints of urban and peri-urban crop production: a meta-regression Description
summary: A preregistered meta-analysis and meta-regression of reported greenhouse gas emission intensities from urban and peri-urban crop-producing systems. The review treats the dispersion among published carbon footprint estimates as the object of
content: A preregistered meta-analysis and meta-regression of reported greenhouse gas emission intensities from urban and peri-urban crop-producing systems. The review treats the dispersion among published carbon footprint estimates as the object of analysis rather than as a caveat. It quantifies how much of that dispersion is attributable to methodological choices — functional-unit metric, system boundary, and boundary-component inclusion — relative to system attributes such as cultivation system, supplementary lighting, and climate zone. Livestock, poultry and aquaculture systems are outside scope.

title: Magnetically recyclable CoFe₂O₄@HKUST-1 nanocatalyst for sustainable carbon–nitrogen coupling, and structure-affinity relationship study of the synthesized products via molecular docking
summary: α-Ketoamides and their derivatives serve as critical foundational components in the fields of natural products, pharmaceutical research, and organic synthesis. In this investigation, we developed an environmentally sustainable Metal–Organic
content: α-Ketoamides and their derivatives serve as critical foundational components in the fields of natural products, pharmaceutical research, and organic synthesis. In this investigation, we developed an environmentally sustainable Metal–Organic Framework (MOF)-based nanocomposite that functions as a multifunctional catalytic system for the production of α-Ketoamide derivatives. This heterogeneous nanocomposite, referred to as CoFe₂O₄@HKUST-1, was synthesized through a series of steps. In this regard, CoFe₂O₄ Magnetic Nanoparticles (MNPs) were synthesized by the co-precipitation process. Then, HKUST-1 was synthesized via an in-situ process. Afterward, CoFe₂O₄@HKUST-1 was functionalized by thioacetamide to obtain a Thioacetamide@CoFe 2 O 4 @HKUST-1 nanocatalyst. Various analytical techniques, including Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy, field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and vibrating sample magnetometer (VSM) have been employed to validate the structure of the synthesized catalyst. The Thioacetamide@CoFe 2 O 4 @HKUST-1 nanocatalyst system, characterized by the magnetic properties of CoFe 2 O 4 MNPs, allows for easy separation from the reaction mixture through the application of an external magnet. Notably, a modest quantity of the synthesized nanocatalyst (15 mol%) has demonstrated remarkable catalytic efficacy in the production of α-Ketoamide derivatives (63–98%) within a brief reaction period (1 h) at a temperature of 60 °C. The observed catalytic performance may be attributed to the cooperative contribution of the composite components and the surface functionalization induced by thioacetamide treatment. Overall, it can be contended that Thioacetamide@CoFe 2 O 4 @HKUST-1 warrants greater focus owing to its non-toxic nature, straightforward preparation process, excellent recyclability, and impressive catalytic efficiency. Molecular docking studies of the synthesized α-ketoamide compounds with aldose reductase (AR) revealed binding affinities ranging from − 5.72 to − 9.485 kcal/mol, with compound 1-(naphthalen-1-yl)-2-(piperidin-1-yl)ethane-1,2-dione (3bg) exhibiting near-equivalent affinity (− 9.485 kcal/mol) to the reference inhibitor Tolrestat (− 9.523 kcal/mol). These results demonstrate the potential of α-ketoamidesbased scaffolds to serve as competitive AR inhibitors, consistent with Tolrestat's mechanism of targeting catalytic residues (Tyr48, His110, Trp111, Cys303) via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions.

title: Lagrangian μ-Particle Tracking Velocimetry Analysis of Microscale Flow over Structured Surfaces
summary: Abstract This work aims to provide an experimental basis for the improvement of (bio)reactors by studying flow over micro- and nanostructured surfaces, with a focus on microscale mass transport toward and away from the surface. μ-Particle t
content: Abstract This work aims to provide an experimental basis for the improvement of (bio)reactors by studying flow over micro- and nanostructured surfaces, with a focus on microscale mass transport toward and away from the surface. μ-Particle tracking velocimetry is employed in a microreactor to experimentally obtain Lagrangian trajectories of flow-following tracer particles. The method also resolves three-dimensional, time-dependent velocity fields. The derived mean velocity profiles agree well with the theory of flow over porous walls. Beyond averaged Eulerian velocities, the Lagrangian framework captures near-surface interactions. The Lagrangian analysis of different surfaces indicates that rectangular structured microgrooves increase the wall contact of the tracer particles, especially when the flow is oriented perpendicular to the microgrooves. Particularly, this approach enables resolution of trapping phenomena and localized recirculation dynamics. Nanostructuring by growing a carbon nanotube forest increases surface area and modifies local fluid dynamics, thereby enhancing contact with (bio)catalysts that are potentially functionalized on the nanotubes in future applications.

title: Contracting as Sensemaking Infrastructure: Enacting Sustainability Strategy in Business‐to‐Business Relationships
summary: ABSTRACT Firms articulate sustainability objectives but depend on suppliers and business partners to enact them. As commitments cross organizational and professional boundaries, their meaning may fragment even when parties agree in principl
content: ABSTRACT Firms articulate sustainability objectives but depend on suppliers and business partners to enact them. As commitments cross organizational and professional boundaries, their meaning may fragment even when parties agree in principle. This theory‐synthesis article examines B2B contracting as sensemaking infrastructure for enacting sustainability strategy across interorganizational relationships. Integrating sensemaking, proactive contracting, and contract design, it develops the sensemaking‐based contracting framework. The framework identifies four interdependent functions: framing clarifies what the relationship seeks to govern; translation connects that understanding to responsibilities, data, and routines; adaptation organizes legitimate revision; and signaling connects relationship‐level performance to external credibility. The article repositions contracting from downstream compliance to strategy enactment. It shows that preserving contractual wording is insufficient when purpose becomes disconnected from performance and directs managerial attention to connections among purpose, responsibility, capability, review, and evidence. Whether this infrastructure supports shared meaning depends on power, network position, and actors' ability to question established interpretations.

title: 2016–2023 China’s land-sea environmental extended input-output dataset
summary: China is a key driver of global marine economic growth, and a critical region for advancing the synergistic governance of pollution reduction and carbon mitigation. The environmentally extended input-output table serves as the core foundati
content: China is a key driver of global marine economic growth, and a critical region for advancing the synergistic governance of pollution reduction and carbon mitigation. The environmentally extended input-output table serves as the core foundation for research on industrial environmental impacts. However, existing dataset do not effectively distinguish between land-based and marine industries, and thus cannot adequately support research on land-sea synergistic pollution and carbon reduction. To this end, this study constructs China’s land-sea environmentally extended input-output (CLSEEIO) dataset covering the period from 2016 to 2023. This dataset covers input-output data of 42 land-based industries and 13 marine industries. It integrates emission inventories of a total of 30 environmental pollutants, including greenhouse gases, 10 water pollutants and 19 atmospheric pollutants. It can provide standardized foundational data support for various studies related to land-sea environmental footprints and green low-carbon development.

title: ECCSEL ERIC Value Proposition
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: ECCSEL ERIC's mission is To enhance open national and transnational access to world-class research facilities, fast-track innovation from TRL1 to TRL7, and propel industries and power generation toward net-zero CO₂ emissions. Maintaining an
content: ECCSEL ERIC's mission is To enhance open national and transnational access to world-class research facilities, fast-track innovation from TRL1 to TRL7, and propel industries and power generation toward net-zero CO₂ emissions. Maintaining and expanding a pan-European network of state-of-the-art research facilities focused on Carbon Capture, Transport, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS), Carbon Dioxide Removal with BECCS and DACCS (CDR), Subsurface Low Carbon Energy Storage (LCES) and Geothermal technologies. The ECCSEL advantages include: • Unparalleled open access: Gain access to over 165 world-class research facilities across Europe, covering the entire value chain from capture to storage and utilization, and Low Carbon Energy Storage.• Powerful collaboration: Join a leading network of researchers, industry and policymakers.• Enhanced funding opportunities: Increase success rates for EU & national funding applications.• Strategic influence: Shape the future of CCUS, CDR, LCES and geothermal research and policy.• Safeguard knowledge sovereignty: Maintaining European-controlled platforms foradvanced research and testing.

title: TIMES Ireland Model with Extended Aviation Modeling
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Aviation module update This model version includes the updated aviation module used to assess the role of aviation in Ireland's national carbon budgets. It represents aviation demand by route distance and aircraft category, with short-haul
content: Aviation module update This model version includes the updated aviation module used to assess the role of aviation in Ireland's national carbon budgets. It represents aviation demand by route distance and aircraft category, with short-haul (<500 km), medium-haul (500-3,000 km) and long-haul (>3,000 km) demand categories. The model was used to generate the aviation scenarios presented in the study. Updates: New demand- and distance-specific aviation module Aviation demand scenarios expanded for BAU and LED pathways Bio-SAF, e-SAF and fossil kerosene pathways included Hydrogen and electric aircraft options represented Aviation fuel prices updated Fuel import requirements explicitly represented International aviation CO2 emissions from departing flights included in the national carbon budget assessment Extended model horizon to 2070 Sensitivity of results to fuel availability and technology adoption assessed What's Changed The following was expanded by @vahid-aryanpur and @BakytzhanSuleimenov in: Expanded the aviation module from final energy demand (PJ of fuel) to service demand (Revenue Passenger Kilometres), with associated assumptions in the TIM Added aviation-specific demand, technology, fuel and emissions parameters Updated scenario files used for the aviation carbon budget analysis

title: Unlocking the green power of the North Sea: Identifying key energy infrastructure synergies for 2030 and 2040
summary: The North Sea will play a key role in providing clean and secure energy for Europe. This not only requires the development of new offshore wind farms, but also their successful integration into the onshore system. In this work we analyze an
content: The North Sea will play a key role in providing clean and secure energy for Europe. This not only requires the development of new offshore wind farms, but also their successful integration into the onshore system. In this work we analyze and compare three key integration options and their preferred siting (onshore vs. offshore): grid expansions, electricity storage, and the production, storage and transport of low-carbon hydrogen. We focus on their potential to reduce emissions and energy system costs – individually and in combination with each other. Additionally, we study the consequences of constraints on their implementation. We analyze the years 2030 and 2040, starting from the projections of installed energy infrastructure and demand from the Ten Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) 2022 of the European Network of Transmission System Operators (ENTSO-E). Results show that cross-border electricity grid expansions across the North Sea are a no-regret measure, resulting in significant reductions in system costs and emissions compared to national grid expansions. By comparison, the production, storage and transport of hydrogen have a lower cost and emission reduction potential. In both the short and long term (2030 and 2040), electricity storage can help to reduce emissions, but it is not cost competitive unless emission reduction targets are enforced. Combining the three integration measures at optimal capacities provides additional benefits. Overall, the highest emission reductions can be achieved by combining electricity storage with an expansion of the grid, while the highest economic benefits can be achieved with a combination of grid expansions and hydrogen production for direct use in industry.

title: Far from the Factory Gate: A Scope 3 Performance Index for Measuring Agribusiness Value-Chain Emissions
summary: Upstream carbon pricing, supply chain disruptions, and future resource scarcity can all increase costs. On the other hand, comprehensive Scope 3 accounting enables firms to anticipate regulatory and reputational risks, guide procurement and
content: Upstream carbon pricing, supply chain disruptions, and future resource scarcity can all increase costs. On the other hand, comprehensive Scope 3 accounting enables firms to anticipate regulatory and reputational risks, guide procurement and design decisions, and align value chains with climate targets. This approach drives decarbonisation across supply networks, strengthens corporate credibility, and reduces carbon leakage and greenwashing risks — all critical policy priorities for achieving net zero transitions.

title: Precise polymerization of phenolic pollutants by a nanoconfined reactor with Fe-Mo dual-site
summary: The conversion of aquatic pollutants into polymers presents a significant opportunity for wastewater resource recovery. However, the precise synthesis of polymers with controlled molecular weight and narrow dispersity remains challenging. H
content: The conversion of aquatic pollutants into polymers presents a significant opportunity for wastewater resource recovery. However, the precise synthesis of polymers with controlled molecular weight and narrow dispersity remains challenging. Herein, we design a spatially decoupled Fe-Mo dual-site catalyst (FeMo-NC), which synergistically regulates phenolic pollutant transformation through enhanced peroxymonosulfate activation and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), thereby reducing the C-H bond dissociation energy barrier by 18.3% and redirecting phenolic pollutant removal toward controlled oligomerization. By tuning the pore size of the carbon framework, we confine polymer growth, yielding polymers with molecular weights of 418–1142 g·mol−1 and narrow dispersity (PDI < 1.2). Compared to conventional Fe₃O₄/PMS systems, PMS consumption decreases by 96.7% and carbon emissions are significantly reduced. An integrated FeMo-NC/ceramic membrane (FeMo-NC/CM) system achieves 100% phenol (PhOH) removal over continuous operation exceeding 144 h. This work highlights confinement engineering as a strategy for selective organic polymerization and wastewater resource recovery. This work demonstrates a Fe-Mo dual-site catalyst that redirects phenolic pollutant transformation toward controlled oligomerization. The resulting membrane system achieves near-complete pollutant removal over 144 h with reduced oxidant usage and carbon emissions.

title: Interventions to reduce desflurane use in hospitals: A systematic review
summary: Desflurane is a potent greenhouse gas (GHG) and major contributor to healthcare carbon emissions. Clinician-led interventions to reduce its use have been implemented, but their effectiveness has not been systematically reviewed. We aimed to
content: Desflurane is a potent greenhouse gas (GHG) and major contributor to healthcare carbon emissions. Clinician-led interventions to reduce its use have been implemented, but their effectiveness has not been systematically reviewed. We aimed to synthesise available evidence on the effectiveness of hospital-based interventions designed to reduce desflurane use. Four databases were searched from inception to 3 July 2025. Randomised and non-randomised controlled trials (RCTs), interrupted time series (ITS) and controlled or uncontrolled before-and-after studies were included. Outcome measures were desflurane consumption (primary), GHG emissions, costs, alternate anaesthetic consumption and staff outcomes. Paired authors independently screened studies, extracted data, assessed risk of bias and certainty of the evidence. Due to heterogeneity, results were synthesised using a structured summary of intervention effects with no meta-analysis. Twenty-three studies were included: 13 uncontrolled before–after studies, seven ITSs and three RCTs. Common interventions were environmental changes ( n = 20) and education ( n = 19). No study was rated at low risk of bias across all criteria. All studies that reported impacts on desflurane consumption (17/17), GHG emissions (16/16) and costs (14/14) found reductions. Use of alternative anaesthetics was inconsistent for sevoflurane ( n = 15) and isoflurane ( n = 7) but increased for propofol ( n = 7). Staff knowledge (3/4) and behaviour (3/3) improved; however, attitudes were unfavourable (1/1) and acceptability was inconsistent (1/1). The evidence was very uncertain for all outcomes. Hospital-based interventions targeting desflurane use may reduce consumption, GHG emissions and costs, with inconsistent effects on alternative anaesthetic use and staff outcomes. However, the evidence is very uncertain.

title: Professionalizing deliberation: a Social Network Analysis of UK climate mini-publics
summary: Abstract Deliberative mini-publics have become an increasingly prominent feature of climate governance across advanced democracies. In the United Kingdom, their rapid expansion has been accompanied by the emergence of a professional deliber
content: Abstract Deliberative mini-publics have become an increasingly prominent feature of climate governance across advanced democracies. In the United Kingdom, their rapid expansion has been accompanied by the emergence of a professional deliberative field composed of facilitators, recruitment agencies, advisory bodies, expert witnesses, and network organizations. While existing scholarship debates whether professionalization enhances deliberative quality or introduces risks of marketization and elite capture, there is limited empirical evidence on how influence, standards, and authority are structured within this field. This article addresses that gap by mapping the actors involved in the design and delivery of UK climate mini-publics using qualitative social network analysis. The analysis examines how professional ties shape the circulation of expertise, standards, and backstage decision-making. The findings identify important and influential actors within the network, and their place within the wider industry. Here, we highlight the unequal concentration and clustering within the network. Rather than finding clear evidence of elite capture, the analysis reveals a form of structural dependency. Responsibility and authority are frequently transferred from commissioning bodies to facilitators, concentrating influence in a small number of actors. While these actors often act as safeguards of deliberative integrity, this reliance also introduces fragility, risks of stagnation, and uneven standards across the field. The article concludes that professionalization is neither inherently corrosive nor unproblematic. By foregrounding the networked architecture of deliberation, the study contributes a new perspective on how democratic innovations are governed, stabilized, and constrained in practice.

title: Rooftop photovoltaic potential in data-scarce regions using open-source geospatial information: Scenario-based approach for a Mediterranean coastal city
source: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development
summary: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems can support urban decarbonization, yet data scarcity limits city-scale assessments in developing regions. This study develops an open-source 2D GIS workflow for five central districts of Antalya, Turkiye, u
content: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems can support urban decarbonization, yet data scarcity limits city-scale assessments in developing regions. This study develops an open-source 2D GIS workflow for five central districts of Antalya, Turkiye, using Overture Maps building footprints. A three-stage procedure combined spatial and size filters, geometry and land-use screening, and targeted image inspection to retain the continuous urban building stock while excluding rural settlements, greenhouses, and structures smaller than 60 m 2 . Planimetric agreement was evaluated against 60 manually delineated reference structures totaling 93,070 m 2 . Structure-level mean absolute percentage error was 8.48%, whereas total-area relative error was 0.13%; leave-one-out values ranged from −0.43% to +0.96%, demonstrating sensitivity to sample composition. After screening, 130,458 structures with 38.97 million m 2 of gross rooftop footprint remained. Because verified building-use labels and citywide 3D height data were unavailable, rooftop availability was represented by literature-supported utilization factors of 0.20 and 0.50, incorporating obstructions, access, setbacks, layout constraints, and inter-row spacing. With annual plane-of-array irradiation of 2084.62 kWh m −2 , module efficiency of 21%, and a performance ratio of 0.75, technical generation was estimated at 2.56 to 6.40 TWh yr −1 . Under an average-grid displacement factor of 0.430 tCO₂ MWh −1 , this corresponds to 1.10 to 2.75 MtCO₂ yr −1 . These estimates represent screening-level technical potential, not building-specific deployment forecasts, because source-data omissions, inter-building shading, structural suitability, permitting, and grid constraints remain unresolved. The workflow separates footprint error, preprocessing decisions, and rooftop-utilization uncertainty, providing a transparent screening framework for data-scarce cities.

title: CO2 Sensing Performance of Carbon Black-Doped Europium Oxide Thick-Film Sensors
summary: In this study, a carbon black-doped europium oxide (Eu2O3) thick-film gas sensor was developed and systematically evaluated for CO2 sensing applications. The sensing layers were fabricated using a screen-printing technique, with Eu2O3 paste
content: In this study, a carbon black-doped europium oxide (Eu2O3) thick-film gas sensor was developed and systematically evaluated for CO2 sensing applications. The sensing layers were fabricated using a screen-printing technique, with Eu2O3 paste prepared with an organic binder, followed by the incorporation of carbon black at different doping concentrations (0.1-5 wt.%). The structural and compositional characteristics of the films were investigated using field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), while their electrical properties were evaluated through current-voltage (I-V) measurements. Gas-sensing performance was investigated in a controlled chamber with CO2 concentrations ranging from 1000 to 5000 ppm. The results revealed that the carbon black incorporation significantly improved the microstructure of the sensing film by reducing particle agglomeration and generating a more porous, uniform morphology, thereby facilitating gas diffusion and charge transport. Among the tested samples, the sensor with 2 wt.% carbon black doping exhibited the best performance, achieving high linearity (97.66%) and enhanced sensitivity of 0.05327 mV/ppm compared with the undoped Eu2O3 sensor (0.01476 mV/ppm). The optimized sensor exhibited good repeatability, satisfactory stability, and reduced hysteresis during successive CO₂ exposure cycles. These improvements may be attributed to the formation of conductive pathways and the increased availability of active surface sites introduced by carbon black within the Eu2O3 matrix. The results establish carbon black-modified Eu2O3 thick films as promising candidates for room-temperature CO₂ gas sensing, with competitive sensing performance.

title: Exciton-driven optics and molecular recognition in carbon nanotube nanosensors: from single-molecule detection to living plant diagnostics
summary: Fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) have emerged as uniquely powerful optical probes for biosensing owing to their stable near-infrared emission, excitonic sensitivity to local perturbations, and compatibility with scatterin
content: Fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) have emerged as uniquely powerful optical probes for biosensing owing to their stable near-infrared emission, excitonic sensitivity to local perturbations, and compatibility with scattering biological media. This plenary will highlight how nanoscale optical phenomena—specifically one-dimensional exciton transport and quenching—enable single-molecule detection through discrete, stochastic fluorescence modulation events. By engineering the corona phase surrounding SWCNTs, including DNA, polymers, and aptamer-functionalized coatings, molecular recognition can be programmed without perturbing the nanotube’s intrinsic photophysics. These corona phase molecular recognition (CoPhMoRe) strategies produce highly selective and reversible optical responses to analytes ranging from nitric oxide and hydrogen peroxide to proteins and neurotransmitters. Combined with analytical frameworks such as hidden Markov modeling and birth–death kinetics, these optical nanosensors extract quantitative molecular dynamics from fluorescence trajectories, enabling real-time, label-free measurements of single-molecule adsorption, desorption, and cellular efflux processes. This presentation will further describe advances in optical instrumentation and signal processing, including wavelength-induced frequency filtering (WIFF), which enhances signal-to-noise ratios in highly scattering environments and extends nanosensor imaging to centimeter-scale tissue depths. These developments have enabled unprecedented applications in living systems, from mapping reactive oxygen species signaling at single-cell resolution to detecting protein secretion from individual microorganisms in real time. The convergence of near-infrared photonics, nanoscale molecular recognition, and in vivo-compatible sensing culminates in recent breakthroughs in plant biology, where SWCNT-based optical nanosensors non-invasively track hormonal and oxidative signaling dynamics across intact tissues. Applications including real-time imaging of wound-induced hydrogen peroxide waves, multiplexed detection of stress signaling molecules, and direct measurement of plant hormones such as auxin illustrate a new paradigm for precision agriculture. By enabling continuous, spatially resolved biochemical monitoring in crops, these optical nanosensor platforms open pathways toward early stress diagnostics, climate-resilient agriculture, and next-generation biointegrated sensing technologies.

title: Data from: Microbial mechanisms underlying the shift of net global warming potential in a maize field under organic amendments
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset supports an original research article published in Frontiers in Microbiology entitled "Microbial mechanisms underlying the shift of net global warming potential in a maize field under organic amendments". It was generated from
content: This dataset supports an original research article published in Frontiers in Microbiology entitled "Microbial mechanisms underlying the shift of net global warming potential in a maize field under organic amendments". It was generated from a replicated field experiment located in suburban Beijing established in 2007 and sampled in 2021 and 2022, comprising seven treatments each with three replicate plots (21 plots in total): an unfertilized control (CK); 100% conventional urea N (CN); 75% urea N plus 25% composted poultry manure N (CNM); 75% urea N plus 25% composted slurry N (CNS); 100% composted poultry manure N (CM); and 75% urea N plus 25% straw N applied under deep tillage (CT) or no tillage (NT). The dataset contains two linked worksheets. The first, "Soil+Yield+GHG", reports nine plot-level variables for each year: soil total nitrogen content (TN, 0.47–0.98 g kg⁻¹), soil organic carbon stock (SOC, 14.7–28.2 t C ha⁻¹), soil nitrate-N content (NO3-N, 8.0–18.9 kg N ha⁻¹); soil ammonium-N content (NH4-N, 0.77–1.91 kg N ha⁻¹), soil pH (7.65–8.13), soil electrical conductivity (EC, 0.087–0.165 mS cm⁻¹), maize yield (4.3–14.0 t ha⁻¹), and plot-scale N2O and CO2 emissions (0.53–2.26 kg N ha⁻¹ and 1.14–6.73 t C ha⁻¹, respectively). The second worksheet, "Functional gene abundance", quantifies absolute functional gene abundances (gene copies per gram of dry soil, 0–2.88 × 10⁶) of 48 functional genes measured by high-throughput qPCR across the same 21 plots, grouped into C degradation (17 genes), C fixation (12 genes), and N cycling (19 genes) genes. Non-detect gene-abundance values are recorded as zero. Reuse potential includes meta-analyses of fertilization effects on soil C and N cycling, coupling functional-gene abundances to greenhouse-gas fluxes and crop yield, and benchmarking high-throughput qPCR data. The data are field measurements containing no human, animal, or personally identifiable information; no ethical, legal, or privacy restrictions apply, and the dataset can be shared openly under a CC BY 4.0 license.

title: Depth‑Dependent Molecular Responses of Fresh Root Input and Pre‑Existing Soil Carbon to Simulated Soil Warming in a Temperate Forest
source: Zurich Open Repository and Archive (University of Zurich)
summary: Soils constitute the largest terrestrial organic carbon reservoir, storing more than 2000 Pg of organic carbon globally. Climate change has already increased global mean surface air temperature by about 1.29 °C since pre-industrial times, a
content: Soils constitute the largest terrestrial organic carbon reservoir, storing more than 2000 Pg of organic carbon globally. Climate change has already increased global mean surface air temperature by about 1.29 °C since pre-industrial times, and continued warming is expected to further raise soil temperatures. Because soil temperature strongly regulates microbial activity, plant productivity, and soil moisture, warming has the potential to substantially alter soil carbon cycling. Although recent soil warming studies demonstrated enhanced carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions and soil organic carbon (SOC) loss, most of them only warmed topsoils (< 30 cm). Despite their low carbon concentrations, subsoils (> 30 cm) store roughly half of total SOC to 1 m depth. As a result, neglecting subsoil responses may lead to an incomplete or underestimated assessment of whole-profile SOC change. Subsoil carbon is often assumed to be relatively persistent to environmental changes because of slow turnover and stronger mineral protection, yet evidence for its long-term (decadal) response to warming remains limited. Additionally, warming may alter productivity and root vertical distribution, with potentially important cascading effects on SOC dynamics. This thesis addresses these research gaps using an ongoing whole-soil warming experiment at Blodgett Forest Research Station (CA, USA). First, I examined the fate of simulated root growth at three depths (10–14, 45–49, and 85–89 cm) during a three-year field incubation by molecular analysis. Second, I investigated the effects of 9.5 years of warming on SOC dynamics, with particular emphasis on subsoils. To move beyond bulk soil measurements, soils were separated into three density fractions—free particulate organic matter (fPOM; large, partially decomposed fragments of plant litter), occluded particulate organic matter (oPOM; small, particulate plant residues that are enclosed within soil aggregates), and mineral-associated organic matter (MAOM; highly microorganism-processed products that are associated with mineral surfaces)—at 10–20, 40–50, and 80–90 cm depth. Because these fractions differ in composition, turnover, and stabilization mechanisms, they provide a more mechanistic basis for identifying which carbon pools drive bulk soil responses to warming. The fractions were subsequently analyzed using infrared spectroscopy and molecular approaches to characterize their chemical composition. After 3-year incubation, the decomposition of root-derived hydrolysable lipids showed a clear depth-dependent response to warming. In warmed plots, decomposition was accelerated at 10–14 cm but suppressed at 45–49 and 85–89 cm. The slower decomposition in subsoils was likely driven by warming-induced reductions in soil moisture together with low microbial abundance and spatial heterogeneity, which may have limited contact between microorganisms and fresh substrates.
