title: Green Inventory Model under Carbon Emission Sensitive Demand with Preservation Technology Investment and Advance Payment Scheme
summary: Growing awareness of climate change and environmental issues, purchasing behaviour of the customers. Nowadays, designing of inventory policy affected due to the presence of sustainable products, electric vehicles, etc., in the market. Furth
content: Growing awareness of climate change and environmental issues, purchasing behaviour of the customers. Nowadays, designing of inventory policy affected due to the presence of sustainable products, electric vehicles, etc., in the market. Further, advance payment scheme also affected the inventory policy designed by decision-maker as this is one of the financing schemes offered by non-financial institution. Focussing, all these challenging issues, this paper presents a green inventory model that includes advanced payment policy and preservation technology investment. In the model, decision-maker designed the inventory policy considering carbon emission dependent demand. Further, preservation technology investment reduces the rate of deterioration. A credit period has been offered by supplier to retailer under advance payment scheme to pay purchased cost. The objective of the present paper is to reduce the impact of carbon emissions and minimize the business investment of retailers. In the model, two different scenarios: one where advance payment scheme is considered and other where is no scheme of advance payment is offered by supplier have been discussed. Under each case, two subcases are also derived based on preservation technology investment either applied or relaxed. Numerical examples have been illustrated to test the practical applicability of the model. Model's sensitivity depending upon key parameters and managerial insight have been also presented. Numerical study reveals that cost is at minimum when no advance payment scheme is offered and there is no investment made in preservation technology. More investment in preservation technology results 25% reduction in deterioration rate.

title: The impact of agricultural socialized services on grain farmers’ agricultural eco‑economic efficiency
summary: Developing agricultural socialized services (ASS) while promoting green and low-carbon grain production is an important component of agricultural modernization in China. Although previous studies have examined the effects of ASS on agricult
content: Developing agricultural socialized services (ASS) while promoting green and low-carbon grain production is an important component of agricultural modernization in China. Although previous studies have examined the effects of ASS on agricultural productivity, farm income, and individual input use, it remains unclear whether ASS improve household-level agricultural eco-economic efficiency (AEE), which jointly accounts for economic output, resource use, and environmental costs. Evidence is also limited regarding the factor-allocation channels and production conditions underlying this relationship. Using survey data from 5,992 grain-producing households across 14 provinces in China, this study examines household-level AEE and examines its relationship with ASS adoption using OLS and an instrumental-variable two-stage least squares specification. The results indicate that: (1) ASS adoption is positively associated with grain farmers’ AEE; (2) the estimated relationship varies across farm sizes and crop types, with a more pronounced positive estimate among farmers operating at least 2 ha, but a negative estimate among wheat-growing households; and (3) ASS adoption is associated with a lower share of fertilizer and pesticide expenditure in total variable production costs, whereas no statistically significant labor-reallocation channel is identified. These findings suggest that ASS policies should improve service quality, reduce smallholders’ barriers to service access, develop crop- and production-stage-specific service packages, and promote more precise management of agricultural inputs.

title: Climate stress, energy shocks and carbon-market connectedness in the European emissions trading system
source: International Journal of Climate Change Strategies and Management
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine state-dependent connectedness in the climate-energy uncertainty-carbon system surrounding the European Union Emissions Trading System. It asks whether average connectedness differs from carbon-market stres
content: Purpose This study aims to examine state-dependent connectedness in the climate-energy uncertainty-carbon system surrounding the European Union Emissions Trading System. It asks whether average connectedness differs from carbon-market stress states and extreme-heat states. Design/methodology/approach This study constructs a monthly data set for 2011–2024 covering heat anomalies, geopolitical risk, energy transportation uncertainty, crude oil returns, European gas returns and carbon allowance returns. It combines correlation and tail-dependence evidence, partial-correlation networks and generalized forecast error variance decomposition to compare contemporaneous dependence and directional spillovers across average and stressed states. Findings The average monthly system is only modestly connected, with carbon allowances mainly receiving shocks. Connectedness rises in both lower- and upper-tail carbon-return states and during extreme-heat months, indicating that stressed conditions reveal stronger energy-carbon-uncertainty transmission than full-sample averages suggest. Under upper carbon-return states, carbon allowances also become more active in transmitting shocks. Originality/value This study integrates physical climate stress, energy shocks and uncertainty indicators into a state-dependent connectedness framework for the European carbon market. The evidence shows that average-state monitoring can understate spillover intensity when carbon-market or heat-stress conditions become extreme.

title: Coal Consumption Optimization through Performance Gap Analysis and Heat Rate Improvement in Thermal Power Plants
summary: India coal fired thermal power is still playing an important role in electricity generation in the country. To enhance plant performance, economic competitiveness and environmental sustainability, therefore, the efficient use of coal is ess
content: India coal fired thermal power is still playing an important role in electricity generation in the country. To enhance plant performance, economic competitiveness and environmental sustainability, therefore, the efficient use of coal is essential. Coal is the major component of the generation cost, and it plays a significant role in the plant heat rate and plant efficiency in Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah Thermal Power Station (SDSTPS). There have been several studies on heat-rate analysis, energy audit, and auxiliary power optimization, but little focus has been paid to the plant-level approach to optimize coal consumption with actual plant data. The present work is to optimizing coal consumption by considering technical and operational performance of the plant, in particular combustion efficiency and turbine heat rate, which are important parameters of specific consumption of coal. The study utilizes performance gap analysis, evaluation of operational data, energy audit and heat-rate analysis to determine the significant performance deviations and set appropriate optimization parameters to increase plant efficiency. The analysis indicates that optimizing the coal use systemically can lead to improved efficiency and reliability and reduce coal consumption overall. The results indicate that streamlined operational practices together with advanced energy management systems can significantly enhance plant performance. Such an approach will help SDSTPS operate more efficiently and serve as an example of sustainable and high-performance thermal power plant operation.

title: Catechol as a Co‐Polymerization Mediator for Programmable Surface Chemistry Structure Synthesis of Carbon Dots
summary: ABSTRACT Red‐emissive carbon dots (R‐CDs) hold promise for bioimaging and optoelectronics, yet their synthesis under mild, scalable conditions remains challenging. Conventional hydrothermal routes demand high temperature and pressure, while
content: ABSTRACT Red‐emissive carbon dots (R‐CDs) hold promise for bioimaging and optoelectronics, yet their synthesis under mild, scalable conditions remains challenging. Conventional hydrothermal routes demand high temperature and pressure, while ambient‐pressure alternatives rely on strong acids and yield limited quantum yields without programmable surface control. This work reports a catechol‐assisted ambient‐pressure strategy that achieves hundred‐gram‐scale preparation of R‐CDs by simple heating at ∼90°C. Catechol acts as a co‐polymerization mediator, participating in formation of carbon dots while its dual hydrogen‐bonding network suppresses functional‐group detachment, stabilizes radical intermediates, and lowers the steric barrier for cyclization. This mechanism enables programmable tuning of hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity and emission wavelength by varying the precursor substituents. The hydrophobic carbon dots exhibit a solid‐state quantum yield of 45.26% (encapsulated in polyvinylpyrrolidone), the highest reported, and enable white light‐emitting diodes (WLED) with a color rendering index (CRI) of 94. The hydrophilic carbon dots (quantum yield 37.86%) are directly applied to deep‐tissue in vivo imaging without surface modification. This work provides a versatile molecular engineering platform for sustainable synthesis of functional aromatic carbon nanomaterials.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINABLE HIGH-PERFORMANCE CONCRETE USING SUPPLEMENTARY CEMENTITIOUS MATERIALS: EVALUATION OF MECHANICAL STRENGTH, DURABILITY, AND ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The rapid expansion of the construction sector has increased demand for concrete while intensifying concerns regarding the environmental impact of Portland cement production. High-performance concrete (HPC) provides superior mechanical stre
content: The rapid expansion of the construction sector has increased demand for concrete while intensifying concerns regarding the environmental impact of Portland cement production. High-performance concrete (HPC) provides superior mechanical strength and durability, but its conventional production may require high cement contents, resulting in increased embodied energy and carbon dioxide emissions. The incorporation of supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs), including fly ash, ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBFS), silica fume, metakaolin, and other industrial or agricultural by-products, provides an effective pathway for developing more sustainable high-performance concrete. This article evaluates the influence of SCM incorporation on the mechanical, durability, and environmental performance of HPC through a literature-based analytical approach. Particular attention is given to compressive strength, flexural performance, permeability, chloride resistance, carbonation, shrinkage, and embodied carbon. The reviewed literature demonstrates that appropriately selected and proportioned SCMs can reduce Portland cement consumption while maintaining or improving long-term mechanical and durability characteristics. Fine SCMs such as silica fume and metakaolin can significantly refine the pore structure, whereas slag and fly ash can provide substantial reductions in clinker content and environmental impact. Recent studies indicate that optimized binary and ternary SCM systems can achieve a favorable balance between strength, durability, and carbon reduction. However, excessive replacement levels may negatively influence early-age strength, workability, and carbonation resistance. Therefore, sustainable HPC should be designed through performance-based optimization rather than maximizing SCM content. The article proposes an integrated framework for selecting SCMs and optimizing concrete mixtures according to mechanical, durability, and environmental criteria.

title: An AutoML Approach for Multi-Echelon Forecasting of Semiconductor Stock Prices Using Recurrent-Based Models: A Study of Financial Dynamics and Demand Shock Propagation
summary: Similar to supply chains (SCs), where bullwhip effect shocks spread backward, financial time series exhibit volatility driven by investors’ choices, macroeconomic context, and technological development, among other factors. While deep learn
content: Similar to supply chains (SCs), where bullwhip effect shocks spread backward, financial time series exhibit volatility driven by investors’ choices, macroeconomic context, and technological development, among other factors. While deep learning has enhanced the predictive performance for stock prices, limited research has examined the impact of multi-echelon forecasting and shock propagation on predictive performance. This paper presents a reliable predictive framework based on RNNs, transformers, and XGBoost, combined with Automated Machine Learning (AutoML), to design a customizable pipeline for forecasting stock prices and indices throughout the semiconductor SC, from manufacturing and hardware assembly to final demand and carbon emissions. The Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) used Tree Parzen Estimator (TPE) and BOHB to simultaneously tune hyperparameters in a high-dimensional space. The feature set of each echelon incorporates the previous echelons’ close prices, in addition to the autoregressive components of the current echelon’s target, without leakage. To foster users’ interactivity, the performance analysis gauges the models’ accuracy and complexity per hyperparameter landscape and determines, through SHAP analysis, the hyperparameters and the features driving optimal performance. Moreover, a shock propagation is performed to follow the impact of volatility in upstream variables on forecasts of the final demand and carbon emissions.

title: Low-Frequency Magnetic Field Mitigation Using Recyclable Sintered Pure-Iron Powder Compacts for Safer Power and Sensor Infrastructure
summary: High-current carrying conductors, electrical machines, power-electronic systems, and sensors generate low-frequency magnetic fields that can cause electromagnetic interference and may result in higher magnetic-field exposure in occupied or
content: High-current carrying conductors, electrical machines, power-electronic systems, and sensors generate low-frequency magnetic fields that can cause electromagnetic interference and may result in higher magnetic-field exposure in occupied or sensitive environments. This study proposes a new low frequency shielding material in the form of sintered pure-iron powder compacts as an alternative to the conventional high-permeability magnetic shielding alloys. This material is manufactured by following controlled environment annealing, green compaction and sintering of high purity iron powder. The magnetic properties of the compacted specimen were determined by characterization according to IEC 60404-4 standard, and scanning electron microscopy was used to study the microstructural features, and chemical analysis was performed by using energy dispersive spectroscopy to validate purity of the iron powder. Experimentally determined magnetic properties were used in finite element simulations to evaluate the shielding performance when different shielding geometries manufactured from the proposed material are placed around a current-carrying conductor. Analysis was done when the conductor carries current of 1000 Amp with focus to evaluate different shielding topologies, including open, square, hexagonal and circular shapes. Analysis indicated that the circular closed-shielding geometry can achieve better shielding effectiveness by ensuring a low-reluctance flow path for magnetic-flux shunting. Finite element simulation results indicated that the proposed pure-iron compact based shielding can ensure shielding effectiveness of 12.6 dB, as compared with 13.35 dB for Mu-metal and 11.24dB for Fe–Si steel. There will be 79% attenuation of the magnetic field at radial distance of 1 m from the conductor with use of the proposed shielding material. The proposed material has several sustainability advantages beyond providing shielding performance, which includes use of recyclable pure iron, reduced dependence on expensive Ni-based alloys, geometry flexibility, and repairability. The proposed material can provide safer, reliable, and more sustainable low-frequency magnetic shielding for use in power infrastructure, sensor systems, medical instrumentation, electric vehicle modules, and industrial equipment.

title: Impact of Ganga Sludge-derived Organic Nutrient Management on Soil Fertility, Productivity, and Resource-use Efficiency in Wheat-Pea Intercropping Systems under a Humid Subtropical Climate
summary: Introduction/Objective This study evaluated the effects of Ganga sludge-based organic manures on soil nutrient availability, growth, yield attributes, and land-use efficiency of wheat ( Triticum aestivum ), pea ( Pisum sativum ), and their
content: Introduction/Objective This study evaluated the effects of Ganga sludge-based organic manures on soil nutrient availability, growth, yield attributes, and land-use efficiency of wheat ( Triticum aestivum ), pea ( Pisum sativum ), and their intercropping system under a humid subtropical climate. Methods A field experiment was conducted using a randomized block design with seven nutrient management treatments, comprising a conventional fertilization control and single or combined applications of Jaivik Prom, Pori Potash, Dharti ka Chaukidar, Jaivik Poshak, and Jaivik Khad. Growth attributes, Crop Growth Rate (CGR), yield components, Land Equivalent Ratio (LER), competition indices, and correlations between soil properties and crop performance were evaluated under sole and intercropping systems. Data were analyzed using ANOVA and LSD tests ( p ≤ 0.05). Results Integrated organic nutrient management significantly enhanced crop performance compared with conventional fertilization. In pea, the combination of Pori Potash and Jaivik Poshak produced the highest grain yield under both intercropping (4.67 kg plot −1 ) and sole cropping (6.81 kg plot −1 ). In contrast, Jaivik Prom combined with Jaivik Khad markedly improved pod production and biomass. In wheat, the combined application of Pori Potash and Jaivik Khad resulted in the highest grain yield under sole (1.71 kg plot −1 ) and intercropping (1.00 kg plot −1 ), while Jaivik Khad alone enhanced crop growth rate, leaf area, and chlorophyll content. Pea performed better under sole cropping, whereas wheat benefited from intercropping. LER values (1.35–2.32) confirmed superior land-use efficiency of intercropping, and available phosphorus and potassium showed strong positive correlations with crop growth and yield. Discussion Improved crop performance was primarily associated with enhanced nutrient availability and complementary interactions between wheat and pea, particularly the legume component's facilitation of nitrogen availability. Conclusion The results indicate that integrated application of Ganga sludge-based organic manures, particularly combined formulations, offers a sustainable approach for nutrient recycling, soil fertility improvement, and enhanced productivity in organic and low-input cereal-legume systems.

summary: Replication package for a multi-period, multi-objective MILP that sites inspection, repurposing and recycling capacity for end-of-life EV batteries across 15 Saudi cities, optimising discounted profit, net life-cycle carbon and a mass-based
content: Replication package for a multi-period, multi-objective MILP that sites inspection, repurposing and recycling capacity for end-of-life EV batteries across 15 Saudi cities, optimising discounted profit, net life-cycle carbon and a mass-based circularity index. NOTE: all economic, technical and emissions coefficients are synthetic and are not forecasts; see README.

title: Climate finance, innovation, and the low-carbon transition in Portugal: Evidence from a nonlinear ARDL approach
summary: Balancing economic development with environmental sustainability remains a critical challenge for many European economies pursuing low-carbon transitions. Although Portugal has made substantial progress in renewable energy deployment and te
content: Balancing economic development with environmental sustainability remains a critical challenge for many European economies pursuing low-carbon transitions. Although Portugal has made substantial progress in renewable energy deployment and technological innovation, the environmental impacts of economic growth, urbanization, and trade openness remain complex. They may exhibit asymmetric responses to policy and market shocks. Therefore, this study investigates the asymmetric and dynamic relationships among urbanization (URB), trade openness (TRD), economic growth (EG), renewable energy (RE), innovation (INNO), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions in Portugal using the Nonlinear Autoregressive Distributed Lag (NARDL) framework. Annual time-series data covering the period 1990–2023 were employed to examine both long-run and short-run asymmetries in the environmental effects of these macroeconomic factors. The empirical findings reveal that positive shocks in EG and URB significantly increase CO₂ emissions, whereas increases in RE consumption and INNO substantially reduce environmental degradation. TRD exhibits mixed effects; while trade expansion initially increases emissions through higher production activity, it contributes to long-run emissions reductions through technology diffusion and cleaner trade composition. The results further indicate that negative shocks to RE and INNO have disproportionately adverse environmental consequences, highlighting the fragility of sustainability gains. These findings demonstrate Portugal’s progress in aligning economic development with RE transition and INN-driven climate strategies. The study provides novel evidence on the asymmetric effects of economic and policy shocks on environmental quality. It offers policy recommendations that support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 9, 11, and 13.

title: How Can Degrowth and Democratic Planning Policies be Implemented? An Empirical and Theoretical Investigation
summary: Despite the 2015 Paris Agreement targets, global greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise, highlighting the need for more radical action. Degrowth, as a planned reduction in resource use, seeks to balance economic goals with ecological sus
content: Despite the 2015 Paris Agreement targets, global greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise, highlighting the need for more radical action. Degrowth, as a planned reduction in resource use, seeks to balance economic goals with ecological sustainability, improve well-being, and reduce inequality. This study empirically examines the implementation of degrowth and democratic planning policies to address escalating ecological crises and socioeconomic inequalities. It explores the structural transformations needed to support degrowth, especially their viability beyond capitalism. Using an environmentally extended multi-regional input–output dataset, the study models the impact of a degrowth policy mix in six countries: the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, China, Turkey, and South Africa. The four key policies considered include reducing output in ecologically destructive sectors, reducing work hours, redistributing income, and implementing guaranteed minimum income. These policies, set within a democratic planning framework, target both demand and supply sides to reduce emissions and income inequality. Collectively, the six countries contributed 24,044,285 kilotons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions in 2021. Under the proposed degrowth policies and “business as usual” technological advances, emissions are projected to decrease by 56%, aligning with recommendations of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change for a 60% reduction by 2035. Results indicate that these policies could significantly mitigate emissions but would require complementary measures (e.g., work-hour reductions) to manage employment impacts. This study argues that such policies may be difficult to reconcile with capitalism’s growth imperative and proposes a democratic planning framework as an alternative approach for prioritizing social and ecological well-being over profit.

title: EMOCS-CRO: a hybrid multi-objective optimization framework for sustainable construction planning and execution-mode selection
summary: The construction industry significantly contributes to global carbon emissions, creating pressure to reduce the Embodied Carbon (EC) of buildings without compromising structural integrity or construction-related quality. However, most exist
content: The construction industry significantly contributes to global carbon emissions, creating pressure to reduce the Embodied Carbon (EC) of buildings without compromising structural integrity or construction-related quality. However, most existing optimization approaches address only one or two objectives, such as cost, energy, or carbon, rarely integrating dataset-derived quality and construction-related quality within a unified multi-objective framework. This study proposes a hybrid metaheuristic framework, Enhanced Multi-Objective Cuckoo Search (MOCS)-tuned Coral Reefs Optimization (EMOCS-CRO), to simultaneously optimize dataset-derived quality and EC reduction in sustainable building design. The framework combines the global exploration capability of MOCS with the adaptive local refinement of Coral Reef Optimization. The Sustainable Architecture Optimization Dataset from Kaggle, comprising 69 office building activities and 29 highway construction activities, was used for evaluation, with the model developed in Python 3.11. EMOCS-CRO was benchmarked against MOSGO and eMOGOA using Diversification Measurement (DM), Mean Ideal Distance (MID), Spread (SP), and Hyper-Volume (HV) metrics. The proposed method achieved higher DM (30.137 for Case 1, 50.137 for Case 2) and HV (0.927 and 0.948), with lower MID (0.655 and 0.555) and SP (0.374 and 0.574), outperforming existing methods in both cases. EMOCS-CRO offers a scalable, practical decision-support tool bridging surrogate structural-performance engineering with sustainable architectural design.HighlightsProposes hybrid EMOCS-CRO for sustainable architectural optimization.Simultaneously optimizes strength, esthetics, and embodied carbon.Achieves higher DM and HV with lower MID and SP values.Enhances carbon reduction in office and highway projects.Outperforms MOSGO and eMOGOA in multi-objective performance.

title: Closed-Loop CO2-Mediated Ultrafast and Controlled Synthesis of Amino Acid Polymers toward a Circular Carbon and Polymer Economy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract The development of chemically recyclable polymers via net-zero CO2 emission is considered one of the ideal solutions to alleviate carbon imbalance and advance a circular polymer economy. Amino acid (AA) polymers, an important class
content: Abstract The development of chemically recyclable polymers via net-zero CO2 emission is considered one of the ideal solutions to alleviate carbon imbalance and advance a circular polymer economy. Amino acid (AA) polymers, an important class of polyamides, provide an attractive molecular platform for constructing recyclable polymer systems. However, classical synthetic methods for AA polymers typically involve CO2 emissions and suffer from slow polymerization rate, poor controllability, and difficulty in achieving high molecular weight. Herein, we develop a CO2-mediated synthetic strategy for AA polymers using carbamates as reactive intermediates. This strategy not only enables the ultrafast synthesis of N-carboxyanhydride (NCA) monomers from CO2 and amino acids within 1 min under mild conditions, but also realizes a robust carbamate initiation strategy for the ultrafast and controlled NCA polymerization to afford AA polymers in a short time with predictable molecular weights. The carbamate initiator exhibits high reactivity and superior stability, enabling the facile synthesis of 21-block copolymers and high-molecular-weight AA polymers with diversified structures. Mechanistic studies revealed a distinct “concerted nucleophilic addition and decarboxylation” polymerization pathway. Notably, the CO2 released during polymerization is simultaneously recycled for monomer and carbamate regeneration, forming a “fixation–release–reuse” closed-loop carbon cycle. The resulting AA polymer exhibited excellent processability with a high mechanical strength of 25.7 MPa, and could be efficiently depolymerized into amino acids with a recovery rate of 91.2%, demonstrating great potential as sustainable engineering plastics and biomaterials for circular polymer economies.

title: Eco-mechanical performance of fly ash-modified concrete blocks: strength development and CO2 emission assessment
source: Journal of Applied Materials and Technology
summary: Fly ash is a waste product from coal combustion and can be used as a partial substitute for cement, thereby aiding in the production of lower-carbon-footprint concrete. Most studies have focused only on mechanical or environmental performan
content: Fly ash is a waste product from coal combustion and can be used as a partial substitute for cement, thereby aiding in the production of lower-carbon-footprint concrete. Most studies have focused only on mechanical or environmental performance, and fewer studies are available that integrate properties of fly ash concrete in terms of mechanical performance, water absorption and CO2 emissions at low replacement rates (£20%). Accordingly, this study aims to meet this need by developing an integrated eco-mechanical evaluation to identify a practical replacement criterion based on three indicators. Five mixtures with varying amounts of fly ash (0%, 5%, 10%, 15% and 20%) were developed. The compressive strength, splitting tensile strength and water absorption after 28 days were tested in the laboratory, while the cradle-to-gate CO2 emission was calculated by calculating the CO2 emission from every constituent of the concrete. These results indicate that the 5% fly ash was able to achieve about 94.3% compressive strength of the control mixture, while also reducing CO2 emissions by 4.71%, yielding the best strength–carbon balance of the mixtures. Increased replacement levels resulted in higher emission reduction, up to 18.85% at 20% fly ash, while producing more significant strength reductions. The findings serve as the basis for policy and specific specifications that would be associated with appropriate utilization of locally available fly ash in accordance with strength and durability requirements. It could be encouraged through material availability, transport, processing, quality control and the possibility of cement savings at the project level, through financial incentives or procurement preferences and performance-based standards.

title: Hazardous Gas Dispersion in Tunnels: Full-Scale Experiments within the CHEMATUN Project
summary: Abstract Tunnel safety research has traditionally focused on fire scenarios, while incidents involving hazardous chemical releases remain comparatively under-researched, despite being governed by different physical processes and emergency-r
content: Abstract Tunnel safety research has traditionally focused on fire scenarios, while incidents involving hazardous chemical releases remain comparatively under-researched, despite being governed by different physical processes and emergency-response objectives. The CHEMATUN project addresses this gap by combining full-scale gas-release experiments with the development of a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) framework for hazardous gas dispersion in tunnels. This contribution reports a progressive full-scale experimental programme at the Zentrum am Berg research facility, comprising preliminary tests with carbon dioxide and helium in the Southern Road Tunnel and two main series in the Northern Road Tunnel. Carbon dioxide and helium releases were investigated under still-air and longitudinal ventilation conditions. Furthermore, hydrogen releases were investigated under longitudinal ventilation, and carbon dioxide was additionally tested under semi-transverse ventilation. The results indicate that gas properties govern the fundamental buoyancy-driven dispersion regime, while ventilation state and strategy strongly influence the transport, direction, and persistence of the resulting gas cloud. The findings highlight the need for ventilation strategies tailored to the specific hazard and provide a full-scale experimental basis for the subsequent development and validation of CFD models for additional release and ventilation scenarios.

title: Technical note: How well do evapotranspiration partitioning approaches perform in moss-covered wetlands?
summary: Abstract. Evapotranspiration (ET) is the dominant hydrologic flux in wetlands, and partitioning into transpiration (T) and evaporation (E) is essential for understanding water and carbon dynamics, guiding sustainable water management practi
content: Abstract. Evapotranspiration (ET) is the dominant hydrologic flux in wetlands, and partitioning into transpiration (T) and evaporation (E) is essential for understanding water and carbon dynamics, guiding sustainable water management practices, and predicting responses to climate change in these systems. However, the presence of moss layers in many wetlands challenges the assumptions of commonly used partitioning methods. This study evaluates the performance of nine eddy covariance (EC)-based ET partitioning approaches across multiple moss-covered wetland sites located in boreal and the Canadian Rocky Mountains. The partitioning results from each approach were compared against independent measurement-based estimates, which were obtained using flux chamber, micro-lysimeters, sap flow sensors, and EC systems. Results showed that none of the evaluated methods provided both accurate and precise estimates of ET partitioning (T:ET), and no single method emerged as the most suitable for studied ecosystems. Despite this, the general agreement between modelled and measured T:ET values indicates that many of these approaches still provide valuable insights. Applying multiple methods concurrently is recommended, where possible, to enhance confidence in partitioning results. For researchers with access to high-frequency EC data, priority should be given to high-frequency EC-based methods due to their more consistent performance across sites. The findings also highlight the limitations of current partitioning approaches under evaporation-dominated conditions, and underscore the need to examine the mechanistic role of mosses, as well as to improve how optimal stomatal conductance theory is conceptualized and implemented in model formulations.

title: The ECOSENSE forest: a distributed sensor and data management system for real-time monitoring of ecosystem processes and stresses
source: Geoscientific instrumentation, methods and data systems
summary: Abstract. Forests provide crucial ecosystem services, but are vulnerable to climate-related physical and biological stresses, such as droughts, pests and pathogens. The rapid climate change currently observed increases the pressure on fores
content: Abstract. Forests provide crucial ecosystem services, but are vulnerable to climate-related physical and biological stresses, such as droughts, pests and pathogens. The rapid climate change currently observed increases the pressure on forest ecosystems, with already drastic consequences, e.g., widespread tree mortality across Central Europe. However, we fall short of understanding underlying process dynamics and their impacts on the Earth system. To better understand and predict forest ecosystem dynamics and the associated energy, carbon and water fluxes, detailed knowledge of ecosystem structure, processes and functioning under constantly varying conditions and across different spatial and temporal scales is needed. The ECOSENSE project brings together engineers, environmental and data scientists to establish novel environmental monitoring approaches and to capture distributed forest carbon and water flux dynamics in space and time with a wide range of established measurement technologies and newly developed sensors. Here, we describe the required infrastructure – called ECOSENSE forest – with regard to physical structures, power supply, communication network and data management, that supports such novel environmental sensor networks. We established a comprehensive monitoring system in this ECOSENSE forest, spanning from below-ground to above-canopy with three large scaffold-towers in different plots. More than 670 commercial and 430 self-built sensors monitor over 90 distinct parameters, fluxes, or processes generating upwards of 4,500 time series that capture soil, tree and atmosphere processes with high spatial and temporal resolution. In particular, our design objective is to provide a stable, flexible and secure forest research infrastructure with power, communication and data management using low-cost and commercially available components that meet the needs of various research disciplines. Our considerations and experiences provide impulses and practical solutions for establishing robust, low-cost distributed field research infrastructures and thus increase data continuity and resilience to disruptions at remote locations. The ECOSENSE forest may thus serve as a blueprint for future projects with similar goals and challenges.

title: Benchmarking Faradaic Efficiency and O2 Quantification during Water Oxidation under Mild Conditions Using a 3D-Printed Cell and Clark Electrode
summary: Abstract Producing green hydrogen via water electrolysis offers a potential pathway for achieving a sustainable energy transition. Despite its potential, it is limited by the sluggish kinetics of OER, which motivates the development of effi
content: Abstract Producing green hydrogen via water electrolysis offers a potential pathway for achieving a sustainable energy transition. Despite its potential, it is limited by the sluggish kinetics of OER, which motivates the development of efficient catalysts. In addition, the field still lacks standardized and reproducible approaches for evaluating catalyst faradaic efficiency (FE) and monitoring the oxygen production. Therefore, we present a 3D-printed electrochemical cell coupled with a Clark sensor for in situ oxygen quantification during OER, while measurement uncertainties were examined to confirm the precision and reproducibility of the methodology. The effects of electrolyte concentration (0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 mol L–1 KNO3), different electrolytes (KNO3 and PBS), electrode surface area (0.071 and 0.195 cm2), and applied constant current (1, 5, and 10 mA) were investigated. Statistical validation demonstrated high reproducibility and robustness. At 10 mA in 0.1 mol L–1 KNO3 using a 0.071 cm2 electrode area, Pt exhibited higher oxygen evolution and FE (4.55 ± 0.5 mg L–1, 85.6 ± 10.8%) than GC (2.32 ± 0.3 mg L–1, 43.6 ± 6.1%). The methodology was subsequently applied to Prussian blue (FePBA), and its respective cobalt and nickel Prussian blue analogues (CoPBA and NiPBA, respectively). Among the investigated materials, NiPBA exhibited the highest OER activity (0.40 ± 0.03 mg L–1 with 76.5 ± 5.7% FE), and was comparable to CoPBA, while both outperformed FePBA at 1 mA. A trend in the NOP was observed among the PBAs, following the order NiPBA ≥ CoPBA > FePBA. This approach provides a reproducible platform for dissolved oxygen quantification and the standardized benchmarking of OER electrocatalysts.

title: Alkalinity generation and trace metal dynamics during olivine-based marine enhanced rock weathering in bioturbated sediments
summary: Abstract. Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) via marine enhanced rock weathering (mERW) of olivine is a proposed strategy for atmospheric carbon dioxide removal (CDR). However, the potential co-release of trace metals to marine ecosystems,
content: Abstract. Ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) via marine enhanced rock weathering (mERW) of olivine is a proposed strategy for atmospheric carbon dioxide removal (CDR). However, the potential co-release of trace metals to marine ecosystems, most notably nickel (Ni) and chromium (Cr), raises environmental concerns. Here, we investigated total alkalinity (AT) release, trace metal dynamics and metal bioaccumulation during mERW using two complementary approaches. First, a 28-day microcosm experiment showed that bioturbation by the lugworm Arenicola marina in pure olivine sand enhanced AT release nearly fivefold and more than doubled the release of dissolved Ni (DNi). Second, in a long-term (> 1 year) mesocosm experiment, we added fine-grained olivine at sediment loading levels of 6% and 10%, and coarse-grained olivine at 10%, to natural intertidal sediments inhabited by A. marina. We quantified sediment–water fluxes and porewater concentrations of AT, DNi, and DCr, and assessed metal accumulation in lugworm tissues. Olivine amendment increased sediment–water AT fluxes approximately two- to threefold, without significant effects of grain size or loading level. Fine-grained olivine treatments resulted in the highest DNi fluxes and the greatest Ni bioaccumulation in lugworms. Lugworm Ni concentrations increased up to tenfold relative to controls. In contrast, olivine amendment did not increase DCr fluxes and Cr bioaccumulation was minor compared to Ni. These results show that bioturbation can enhance olivine weathering and that olivine amendment can increase AT release from natural coastal sediments. However, finer grain size disproportionately increased Ni release and bioaccumulation without a detectable additional AT benefit. This decoupling suggests that AT generated by olivine weathering may have been partly offset by suppression of natural sedimentary AT generation. Under the conditions tested here, coarse olivine therefore provided a more favourable balance between net AT release and ecotoxicological risks from Ni exposure during mERW.

title: Estimating the Hidden Sustainability Contributions From Food Sharing Initiatives at the Municipal Scale
summary: Establishing the impacts of municipal food systems is essential for guiding policy, ensuring accountability and promoting just, resilient, and sustainable food system transformation at this scale. However, knowledge of these systems remains
content: Establishing the impacts of municipal food systems is essential for guiding policy, ensuring accountability and promoting just, resilient, and sustainable food system transformation at this scale. However, knowledge of these systems remains partial. While the goals of food sharing initiatives (FSIs), such as community gardens, kitchens, and surplus food redistribution organisations, often support more equitable and sustainable food systems, their impacts are rarely documented and therefore remain invisible to municipal food governance. In response, this article presents a methodology for estimating sustainability impacts from FSIs and applies this to the municipality of Dublin, Ireland. Using FSI mapping, surveys, and a sample of sustainability impact assessments from growing, cooking, and redistribution initiatives, the approach enables estimations of social, economic, and environmental impact for municipalities. This gives greater visibility to the impacts FSIs create collectively, but alone cannot guarantee that these impacts are considered by decision-makers. In the context of developing a post 2030 sustainability agenda, we call for the development of municipal governance systems that both incentivise impact data collection for all food organisations and ensure the resulting impact data is meaningfully considered in decision-making.

title: Crude Oil Theft and Environmental Degradation in Oil-Producing Communities of Rivers State, Nigeria: Evidence from Bodo And Rumuekpe
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: This study examines crude oil theft as a direct driver of environmental degradation in Bodo (Gokana LGA) and Rumuekpe (Emuoha LGA), two oil-producing communities in Rivers State, Nigeria, using a descriptive survey design anchored on Strain
content: This study examines crude oil theft as a direct driver of environmental degradation in Bodo (Gokana LGA) and Rumuekpe (Emuoha LGA), two oil-producing communities in Rivers State, Nigeria, using a descriptive survey design anchored on Strain Theory, Resource Curse Theory, and Environmental Justice Theory. Two communities were purposively selected for their contrasting exposure profiles; within them, 200 respondents were drawn through stratified random sampling across six occupational categories. Structured questionnaires were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics (chi-square). Respondents perceived poverty and unemployment as the leading facilitators of oil theft and associated the practice with widespread air, water, and soil pollution, which in turn undermined farming, fishing, and health. Government enforcement, corporate remediation, and compensation were perceived as slow, profit-driven, and inadequate, respectively. The findings support a theoretically grounded, mutually reinforcing relationship between environmental harm and continued oil theft, though the cross-sectional design cannot establish causal direction. The article recommends coordinated regulatory enforcement, logistics-chain surveillance, community-based environmental governance, and targeted youth economic empowerment.

title: Domain‐Wall Circulation Gating and Pinning via Compositional Engineering of Cylindrical Nanowires
summary: Spintronic devices based on cylindrical magnetic nanowires have been proposed as a route toward three-dimensional (3D) information storage and processing by harnessing the controlled motion of domain walls (DWs). In this geometry, the Bloch
content: Spintronic devices based on cylindrical magnetic nanowires have been proposed as a route toward three-dimensional (3D) information storage and processing by harnessing the controlled motion of domain walls (DWs). In this geometry, the Bloch-point wall (BPW) is the characteristic DW type. It features a curling of magnetization around a Bloch Point singularity, a topology that has been predicted to enable propagation at high speed without undergoing a Walker breakdown. We demonstrate that compositional modulations of larger magnetization, which host spontaneous curling states while the rest of the wire remains axial, fulfil a dual role: they act as deterministic pinning sites and as active gates for BPW circulation. Combining magnetic transmission X-ray microscopy and micromagnetic simulations, we reveal that DW-modulation interactions are the result of a superposition of long-range magnetostatic repulsion and short-range, circulation-dependent exchange contributions: parallel circulation produces an attractive well, while opposite circulation generates a repulsive barrier. This results in DW pinning at or near a compositional modulation. A DW's internal circulation can be inverted upon traversing a modulation, enabling on-demand switching of its circulation state. This dual mechanism demonstrates that both DW position and circulation can be tuned in a controlled manner, with potential implications for multistate spintronic devices.

title: Enhanced lipid production from acetate by oleaginous yeast co-cultivation and transcriptomic characterization
summary: Microbial lipids are promising alternative oil sources, particularly for biodiesel production, but their industrial application is limited by high fermentation costs and low lipid yields. Volatile fatty acids (VFAs) derived from organic was
content: Microbial lipids are promising alternative oil sources, particularly for biodiesel production, but their industrial application is limited by high fermentation costs and low lipid yields. Volatile fatty acids (VFAs) derived from organic waste represent potential low-cost substrates for microbial lipid production. This study investigated the co-cultivation of oleaginous yeasts using acetic acid as a carbon source to enhance lipid production. Four oleaginous yeast strains were evaluated under mono- and co-cultivation conditions, and the combination of Yarrowia lipolytica and Rhodotorula glutinis showed the highest lipid production performance among the tested combinations. Response surface methodology was applied to optimize cultivation parameters, including acetate concentration, C/N ratio, and inoculation ratio. Under the optimized conditions, co-cultivation achieved a lipid concentration of 1.04 ± 0.05 g/L, with increases of 18.07% and 26.83% in dry cell weight and lipid concentration, respectively, compared with Y. lipolytica mono-cultivation, and increases of 47.47% and 30.00%, respectively, compared with R. glutinis mono-cultivation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed co-cultivation-associated changes in lipid metabolism-related gene expression in Y. lipolytica . Genes associated with fatty acid and triglyceride biosynthesis, including HTD2, MECR, FAS1, FAS2, AGPAT1_2, and DGAT1, showed increased transcript abundance, whereas TGL3 and TGL4 showed decreased expression. These transcriptional changes were associated with enhanced lipid accumulation under co-cultivation and provide insights into the metabolic responses of oleaginous yeasts during co-cultivation.

title: Optimizing temperature prediction in automotive lithium-ion battery discharge cycles using machine learning and SHAP analysis
summary: Background Effective thermal control is essential for lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles and energy storage systems, as uncontrolled heat generation accelerates degradation, reduces performance, and increases safety risk. Conve
content: Background Effective thermal control is essential for lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles and energy storage systems, as uncontrolled heat generation accelerates degradation, reduces performance, and increases safety risk. Conventional temperature-prediction studies often report high accuracy using random data splitting; however, such evaluation may not adequately represent performance on unseen battery cells. Objective This study aims to develop an accurate, stable, and interpretable machine-learning framework for predicting lithium-ion battery temperature during discharge cycles under unseen-battery conditions. Methods The NASA lithium-ion battery ageing dataset was used to train and evaluate Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine models. Five input features were considered: measured voltage, measured current, power, cumulative discharged energy, and voltage drop, with measured temperature as the target. Battery-wise validation was performed using cells B0005, B0006, B0007, and B0018, where each battery was used once as an independent test set. Model performance was assessed using root mean square error, mean absolute error, and coefficient of determination. Uncertainty analysis, residual diagnostics, and SHapley Additive exPlanations were used to examine prediction stability, error behaviour, and feature influence. Results Light Gradient Boosting Machine achieved the strongest overall generalization, with a mean root mean square error of 1.070 °C and a mean coefficient of determination of 0.910. Random Forest showed closely comparable performance and achieved the lowest mean absolute error of 0.893 °C, while Linear Regression showed weaker predictive performance. SHAP analysis identified power, cumulative discharged energy, and measured voltage as the dominant predictors. Conclusion The proposed framework provides a reliable and interpretable approach for battery temperature prediction and supports data-driven thermal monitoring in battery management systems. Future work should validate the model using broader datasets, real-time sensor data, ageing indicators, and physics-informed learning under dynamic operating conditions.

title: Beyond Linear Paths: Configurations of Networks, Knowledge, and Dynamic Capabilities for Sustainable MSMEs
summary: ABSTRACT Despite extensive research on entrepreneurial business networks (EBNs), knowledge management (KM), and dynamic capabilities (DC), three questions remain theoretically underdeveloped and empirically unexplored in resource‐constraine
content: ABSTRACT Despite extensive research on entrepreneurial business networks (EBNs), knowledge management (KM), and dynamic capabilities (DC), three questions remain theoretically underdeveloped and empirically unexplored in resource‐constrained MSMEs. These concern the integrative mechanisms through which EBN and KM jointly cultivate DC, the differential mediation logic of DC across sustainability outcome types, and the configurational pathways through which these constructs collectively produce sustainability outcomes. Using PLS‐SEM and fsQCA on data from 316 manufacturing MSMEs in Uttar Pradesh, India, this study finds that DC fully mediates the effects of EBN and KM on sustainable competitiveness (SComP), whereas sustainable performance (SP) retains direct network and knowledge effects, reflecting its operational proximity to resource inputs. The necessity analysis confirms no single condition is individually necessary for high SP, and fsQCA reveals nine equifinal configurations, showing that high SP is achievable through multiple strategic routes. These findings offer actionable insights for managers and policymakers in emerging‐economy contexts.

title: Feature Quality Adaptive Attention Transformer: A Transformer-Based Model for Multi-Horizon EU ETS Carbon-Price Forecasting
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Forecasting the carbon price of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) supports energy planning, risk assessment, and climate-policy evaluation. The price is non-stationary and responds to several energy markets, so medium-hor
content: Forecasting the carbon price of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) supports energy planning, risk assessment, and climate-policy evaluation. The price is non-stationary and responds to several energy markets, so medium-horizon forecasts are difficult to evaluate without information leakage. This protocol describes a leakage-controlled workflow and the Feature Quality Adaptive Attention Transformer (FQA-ATT) for forecasting at 5, 10, and 21 trading days. A Feature Quality Gate scales each input by a prior that combines mutual information (MI) and random forest (RF) importance computed on training data. A Quality-Adaptive Attention module adds a learnable per-head temporal decay and a quality-energy bias to scaled dot-product attention. Depth-wise convolutions with 1-, 3-, and 5-day kernels extract local patterns. The trading-day panel covers November 2017 to 29 December 2025 and contains 41 lagged features. Each input window ends at the forecast origin, and every target lies after it. Over five random seeds, FQA-ATT gave the lowest validation mean absolute error (MAE) of ten models at all three horizons. On the 2024–2025 test period, its MAE was 2.37, 3.19, and 4.79 EUR, which ranked second, third, and second. FQA-ATT was significantly more accurate than XGBoost, LightGBM, and PatchTST at short horizons. FQA-ATT and a linear FITS-style model were the only learned models whose accuracy never differed significantly from the persistence benchmark. These results show that the protocol gives realistic accuracy estimates and that the feature-quality prior helps attention-based models remain competitive with persistence on carbon returns.

title: Evolving role of cardiac magnetic resonance in cardiac amyloidosis
summary: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA), characterized by misfolded transthyretin (ATTR) or immunoglobulin amyloid light-chain (AL) proteins, has shifted from a rarely diagnosed, near fatal or fatal condition, to a recognized and treatable cause of heart
content: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA), characterized by misfolded transthyretin (ATTR) or immunoglobulin amyloid light-chain (AL) proteins, has shifted from a rarely diagnosed, near fatal or fatal condition, to a recognized and treatable cause of heart failure.This transformation has been enabled in large part by advances in non-invasive multimodality imaging, with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) occupying a prominent diagnostic and prognostic role.Late gadolinium enhancement, native T1 and T2 mapping, and extracellular volume quantification allow detection of amyloid infiltration with high sensitivity, often before overt phenotypic expression.CMR also provides robust and reproducible prognostic information that complements biomarkers and bone-avid scintigraphy.This review summarizes the established CMR diagnostic yield, its role within contemporary diagnostic algorithms for ATTR and AL amyloidosis, the prognostic value of quantitative tissue characterization, and the expanding evidence base for using CMR to monitor response to the new generation of disease modifying therapies.It also examines emerging evidence, including artificial intelligence assisted interpretation, non-contrast diagnostic strategies, extracardiac tissue mapping, and refinement of tissue mapping thresholds, that is likely to shape CMR practice in amyloidosis over the coming years.

title: Patent review on revolutionary electrochemical CaCO 3 conversion for cement manufacturing
summary: Abstract Sustainable development has become a necessity in conventional cement production to reduce environmental impact. Global demand needs to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The transition to green cement manufacturing plays a key
content: Abstract Sustainable development has become a necessity in conventional cement production to reduce environmental impact. Global demand needs to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The transition to green cement manufacturing plays a key role in achieving net-zero carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions and carbon-neutral concrete by 2050. This patent review highlights the importance and potential of green cement manufacturing through an electrochemical process, converting calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) into calcium hydroxide Ca(OH) 2 to produce ordinary Portland cement. This study reveals the entire patent landscape in green cement production and electrochemical green cement production. It highlights and describes the notable patents and their methodology. In addition, this review assesses the innovation of electrochemical technology in cement manufacturing and its potential and feasibility. A roadmap with efficient and effective polices and a framework can enhance the production of green cement. It can be expected that incorporation of electrochemical technology for calcium hydroxide production, when paired with renewable resources, cannot only reduce the overall emission and carbon footprint of cement products but also contribute toward achieving sustainable development goals, mitigate climate change, and regulate the market trend toward more sustainable products. It has been proven that interdisciplinary collaboration is indeed a necessity to overcome the technical and regulatory barriers.

title: Framing nature‐based solutions in Norwegian public media: A critical discourse analysis of public narratives
summary: Abstract Nature‐based solutions (NbS) have become central to environmental governance. Yet, their societal legitimacy depends on how they are framed in public discourse. This study investigates how Norwegian media actors construct narrative
content: Abstract Nature‐based solutions (NbS) have become central to environmental governance. Yet, their societal legitimacy depends on how they are framed in public discourse. This study investigates how Norwegian media actors construct narratives around NbS, whose voices are amplified, and the extent to which plural and Indigenous epistemologies are represented. We conducted a critical discourse analysis of 57 articles published between 2018 and 2025 across five major Norwegian media outlets. Articles were coded abductively, drawing on typologies of values (instrumental, relational and intrinsic) and dimensions of environmental justice. The sample primarily included opinion pieces and expert contributions, most of which were authored by non‐journalist experts. Four dominant narratives emerged: (1) Nature as infrastructure , emphasising technical and cost‐effective climate services; (2) Win‐win optimism , framing NbS as universally beneficial; (3) Nature as relationship , depicting nature as a partner but remaining marginal; and (4) Commodification critiques , primarily in progressive outlets. In addition, we identified a patterned absence of Indigenous epistemologies , with Sámi perspectives almost entirely absent. Outlet‐specific patterns reflected editorial ideologies, with instrumental framings dominating across the corpus. Our findings highlight that Norwegian media discourses on NbS remain strongly anthropocentric, which may contribute to reinforcing perceptions of nature as a resource for human use and constrain transformative imaginaries. The limited representation of relational values and Indigenous knowledges could risk perpetuating epistemic injustices. We suggest reflexive and pluralistic media practices that move beyond narrow technocratic narratives to foster inclusive public conversations about nature, climate and justice. title: Trace metals contamination in freshwater fish in Brazil: related factors, environmental impacts, and risks to human health
summary: Freshwater fish are essential components of the aquatic food chain and an important source of protein and nutrients for various communities, especially riverine populations. However, water pollution is one of the main causes of metal bioacc
content: Freshwater fish are essential components of the aquatic food chain and an important source of protein and nutrients for various communities, especially riverine populations. However, water pollution is one of the main causes of metal bioaccumulation in the organs of these animals. This study conducted a systematic review of the scientific literature on trace metal contamination in freshwater fish in Brazil. The methodological procedure was structured in three stages: definition of the research problem, application of a relevance test with inclusion and exclusion criteria, and selection of eligible studies for the review. Regional heterogeneity was observed in the scientific production on metals in freshwater fish in Brazil, with a higher concentration of studies in the Northern region. The studies indicate a predominance of native species and demonstrate that trophic level, feeding habits, and interaction with the habitat influence the bioaccumulation of metals in freshwater fish in Brazil. There was also consensus that the metals of greatest toxicological and environmental relevance are Pb, Cd, Cr, and Hg, which were the most frequently identified in the studies. The contamination profile of metals in fish varies regionally and is directly related to anthropogenic activities such as mining, intensive agriculture, urbanization, and effluent discharge. Health risk assessment studies indicate that the daily intake of some potentially toxic trace metals (cadmium, lead, and mercury) may exceed the maximum limits established by legislation, mainly affecting populations with high fish consumption, such as Amazonian riverine and Indigenous communities.

title: A Recyclable Coconut‐Shell‐Carbon‐Based Photocatalyst for Robust Antimicrobial Activity and Enhanced Wound Repair
summary: ABSTRACT Acinetobacter baumannii ( A. baumannii ) is a notorious nosocomial pathogen for its extensive drug resistance and adaptability. This study developed a novel heterojunction photocatalyst (PC), PTQ10‐SY1, supported on coconut shell c
content: ABSTRACT Acinetobacter baumannii ( A. baumannii ) is a notorious nosocomial pathogen for its extensive drug resistance and adaptability. This study developed a novel heterojunction photocatalyst (PC), PTQ10‐SY1, supported on coconut shell charcoal (CSC), a carbon material derived from natural biomass. The CSC matrix ensures efficient dispersion of PTQ10‐SY1 and enhances its recoverability, thereby synthesizing the reusable, environmentally friendly, white light‐responsive material CSC@PTQ10‐SY1. Under 13.2 mW/cm 2 of light excitation, the material efficiently generates reactive oxygen species (ROS), which disrupt the cell wall and membrane integrity of A. baumannii , inhibit ATP synthesis, and leading to bacterial death. It achieves significant elimination of A. baumannii within 30 min and also demonstrates effective activity against Methicillin‐resistance Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ). In mammalian safety assessments, CSC@PTQ10‐SY1 shows minimal adverse effects under the tested conditions. In a wound‐associated infection model, topical application of CSC@PTQ10‐SY1 significantly reduces bacterial burden and inflammation, resulting in improved wound healing outcomes compared to the control group. Furthermore, the material retains its composition and shows no evidence of tolerance to photodynamic therapy (PDT) after 10 cycles. This work highlights an innovative strategy for designing antimicrobial PC materials and promotes the application of antimicrobial PDT for the A. baumannii .

title: Tailoring Piezoelectric Materials for High Energy Density Batteries: Fundamentals, Advances, and Perspectives
summary: High-energy-density rechargeable batteries are plagued by electrode polarization, unstable interfaces, and parasitic side reactions, which severely restrict their electrochemical performance across diverse battery chemistries. Piezoelectric
content: High-energy-density rechargeable batteries are plagued by electrode polarization, unstable interfaces, and parasitic side reactions, which severely restrict their electrochemical performance across diverse battery chemistries. Piezoelectric materials can construct dynamic built-in electric fields via mechanical or electrochemical excitation, showing great potential to modulate ion migration, interfacial charge behavior, and reaction kinetics for optimized battery performance. In this review, we first outline the fundamental physical principles and material classification of piezoelectric materials, followed by a comprehensive summary of how the piezoelectric effect manifests differently when piezoelectric materials are integrated into a variety of battery components. Within electrode materials, piezoelectricity can accelerate interfacial ion diffusion, enhance redox reaction kinetics, and suppress undesirable side reactions through built-in electric fields. On the anode side, the piezoelectric polarization field serves as an additional driving force to regulate ion flux and promote homogeneous metal deposition, thereby mitigating dendrite growth. In electrolytes and separators, piezoelectric materials can enhance ionic conductivity, stabilize electrode/electrolyte interfaces, and homogenize ion distribution, leading to improved electrochemical stability and reaction reversibility. Finally, current challenges and future perspectives are discussed to guide the rational design and practical implementation of piezoelectric-enabled strategies for rechargeable energy-storage systems featuring enhanced safety, prolonged service life, and high energy density.

title: Blockchain Management Empowering Green and Climate Finance: Mechanisms, Real‑World Dilemmas and Optimization Paths
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: Against the background of China's dual-carbon strategic goals, green and climate finance have achieved rapid scale expansion as critical instruments for low-carbon economic transition. Nevertheless, the whole market is still plagued by prom
content: Against the background of China's dual-carbon strategic goals, green and climate finance have achieved rapid scale expansion as critical instruments for low-carbon economic transition. Nevertheless, the whole market is still plagued by prominent governance risks, including intentional environmental data manipulation, and repeated double-counting of carbon assets, as well as poor traceability of green project capital flows. As an innovative trust-rebuilding management paradigm rather than simple technical tools, blockchain management leverages distributed ledgers, data immutability and smart-contract functions to deliver credible technical support for green-climate finance. This paper adopts qualitative analytical research, including literature review and dual-case comparison, to investigate how blockchain management functions within green credit, carbon trading and green bond scenarios. It identifies major practical obstacles and puts forward coordinated institutional-technical optimization proposals. The study reveals that blockchain can effectively mitigate information asymmetry in green-financial practice. Nevertheless, its large-scale commercial deployment is hindered by on-chain-off-chain data fragmentation, insufficient unified regulatory standards and relatively high technical operation costs. Therefore, collaborative governance mechanisms, unified industry-wide standards and lower access thresholds for small- and medium-sized enterprises are urgently required for future development.

title: Optimization, microstructure, and durability of sawdust ash concrete modified with Conplast SP430 superplasticizer
summary: The use of sawdust ash (SDA) as a supplementary cementitious material offers an opportunity to valorize biomass waste and reduce dependence on Portland cement, but its incorporation can affect workability, strength development and durabilit
content: The use of sawdust ash (SDA) as a supplementary cementitious material offers an opportunity to valorize biomass waste and reduce dependence on Portland cement, but its incorporation can affect workability, strength development and durability. This study investigates the combined effects of SDA replacement and Conplast SP430 dosage on the fresh, hardened and durability performance of concrete. SDA replacement levels of 0–40% and Conplast dosages of 0–7.6 L/m 3 were investigated, followed by microstructural and elemental characterization of the resulting concrete using BSE-SEM and EDS. The optimum formulation, identified within the investigated mixture range, was 10% SDA with 5.7 L/m 3 Conplast SP430, which achieved a 28-day compressive strength of 24.7 MPa, representing a 51.5% increase relative to the control. Continued strength development was observed at later curing ages, with the optimum mixture reaching 25.8 MPa at 90 days. SEM observations showed comparatively favourable matrix morphology at 10% SDA, while higher SDA replacement levels were associated with increasing morphological discontinuity and interfacial defects. EDS analysis showed a progressive increase in the Ca/Si ratio from 0.345 in the control to 0.586 at 40% SDA, with the 10% SDA mixture exhibiting an intermediate value of 0.422. The increase in Ca/Si was negatively associated with compressive strength within the investigated mixtures. Durability assessment of the optimum mixture after 56 days showed 76.7% strength retention in Na₂SO₄, whereas MgSO₄ and the acidic environments produced substantially greater deterioration. Overall, the results indicate that 10% SDA with 5.7 L/m 3 Conplast SP430 provided the most favourable balance of mechanical, microstructural and durability performance within the experimental range investigated. The findings provide experimentally based guidance for SDA–Conplast concrete while recognizing that the observed microchemical relationships are specific to the materials and exposure conditions examined.

title: Kurumlar, Kurallar ve Krizler
summary: ÖNSÖZFakat sanırım Cemil Serhat hocanın hatırasına yakışacak olan, yalnızca geçmişi anlatmak değil; düşünmeye devam etmektir.Bu nedenle Kurumlar, Kurallar ve Krizler: Dayanıklılığın Kurumsal Temelleri başlığını taşıyan bu armağan kitabın en
content: ÖNSÖZFakat sanırım Cemil Serhat hocanın hatırasına yakışacak olan, yalnızca geçmişi anlatmak değil; düşünmeye devam etmektir.Bu nedenle Kurumlar, Kurallar ve Krizler: Dayanıklılığın Kurumsal Temelleri başlığını taşıyan bu armağan kitabın en kıymetli tarafını, geçmişte bırakılmış bir akademik mirası yalnızca anmak yerine onu yeni araştırma sorularıyla geleceğe taşımasında görüyorum.Kitaptaki her bölüm aynı şeyi söylemiyor; zaten söylememeli de.Akademinin gücü, herkesin aynı sonuca ulaşmasında değil, aynı büyük meseleye farklı pencerelerden bakabilmesindedir.Bu esere düşünceleri ve emekleriyle katkı sunan bütün bölüm yazarlarına, hazırlanmasında görev alanlara ve Cemil Serhat Akın'ın akademik hatırasının yaşatılmasına katkı sağlayan herkese başta Prof. Dr. Cengiz Aytun hocama olmak üzere; kardeşi olarak gönülden teşekkür ediyorum.Bu kitabın yeni araştırmalara, yeni tartışmalara ve özellikle genç akademisyenlerin soracağı yeni sorulara vesile olmasını diliyorum.

title: Green Criminology: The Urgency of Applying Strict Liability to Corporate Environmental Crimes Following the Constitutional Court Decision
source: International Journal of Law and Society
summary: This article examines the urgency and constitutional limits of strict liability as a mechanism for addressing corporate environmental pollution in Indonesia through the perspective of green criminology and recent Constitutional Court jurisp
content: This article examines the urgency and constitutional limits of strict liability as a mechanism for addressing corporate environmental pollution in Indonesia through the perspective of green criminology and recent Constitutional Court jurisprudence. The study addresses an accountability gap arising from cumulative, technically complex, and organizationally dispersed ecological harms that are difficult to attribute to individual decision-makers. Article 88 of Law No. 32 of 2009 on Environmental Protection and Management primarily establishes civil strict liability, while corporate criminal liability follows a different attribution structure. This study employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, case, and comparative approaches. It analyzes the Environmental Protection and Management Law as amended by Law No. 6 of 2023, Supreme Court Regulation No. 13 of 2016, Constitutional Court Decisions No. 91/PUU-XVIII/2020, No. 35/PUU-XXI/2023, and No. 119/PUU-XXIII/2025, as well as twenty-five recent Scopus-indexed studies published from 2022 to 2025. The findings indicate that removing the phrase expressly dispensing with proof of fault creates interpretive uncertainty but does not necessarily eliminate the strict character of absolute liability. However, transforming Article 88 into automatic criminal liability would conflict with legality and proportionality. The study proposes a dual-track model combining genuine civil strict liability for restoration and compensation with an expressly legislated organizational criminal-liability framework for high-risk environmental offences, supported by restoration orders, compliance supervision, evidentiary rules, and anti-retaliation protection.

title: Just transition, profit margins and investment protection
summary: Abstract This article assesses whether the interpretation and treatment of profit margins in investment treaty renewable energy disputes may interfere with just transition goals by safeguarding strong profit margins as legal entitlements fo
content: Abstract This article assesses whether the interpretation and treatment of profit margins in investment treaty renewable energy disputes may interfere with just transition goals by safeguarding strong profit margins as legal entitlements for ‘green’ investments. There is an ongoing academic and policy debate about the role of investment treaties in shaping climate action. As far as climate-friendly investments are concerned, the focus of the debate has largely been on the role of investment treaties in incentivising renewable energy investments. Whether relying on investment treaties to protect RE investments can be conducive to just transition outcomes has not been the subject of much academic discussion. This article analyses the role of profit rates in renewable energy arbitral awards and situates investment treaties within the ‘de-risking’ ecosystem dominating energy transition policies. Situating investment treaties within this de-risking ecosystem enables a more holistic assessment of their role within energy transition and their impact on just transition goals. The article calls for the integration of profitability and burden-sharing considerations into proposals for rethinking the future of sustainable investment governance.

title: From concept to action: Driving impact through responsible research practices in the International Polar Year 2032–2033 An early career perspective
summary: Regions at the poles are warming at rates two to four times higher than the global average, driving profound environmental, societal, and geopolitical changes. As Polar Early Career Researchers with careers extending into and beyond the 5th
content: Regions at the poles are warming at rates two to four times higher than the global average, driving profound environmental, societal, and geopolitical changes. As Polar Early Career Researchers with careers extending into and beyond the 5th International Polar Year in 2032–2033, we have a responsibility to shape research practices that are impactful, ethical, and sustainable. We argue that current definitions of research impact often prioritize narrow, quantifiable metrics, overlooking cultural, environmental, and long-term consequences. Building on interdisciplinary workshops held in 2025 at the Polar Early Career World Summit (USA) and the Centre for Ecology and Hydrology (UK), this paper redefines research impact for polar science and presents tangible action for integrating responsible practices ahead of the next IPY. We outline priorities across three levels: 1) individual researchers, who should practice reflexivity, promote interdisciplinarity, and implement environmentally responsible methods; 2) regional and national institutions, which must provide equitable funding, training, and inclusive protocols; 3) international IPY planning bodies, which should strengthen communication, publish guidelines, and implement regulations to prevent exploitative practices. Our call to action emphasizes collaboration, transparency, and improved impact evaluation frameworks to ensure that polar research delivers societal and environmental benefits while minimizing unintended consequences. This vision begins now and extends beyond the IPY, offering a roadmap for responsible polar science.

title: Reduced Carbon Emissions and Chain Elongation during Mixotrophic Fermentation of a Biomass Feedstock
