summary: Abstract Anaerobic fermentation of biomass feedstocks using open cultures is a promising technology to produce platform carboxylates. Syngas, a mixture of H2, CO2, and CO, can be sourced sustainably and used to supplement biomass feedstocks
content: Abstract Anaerobic fermentation of biomass feedstocks using open cultures is a promising technology to produce platform carboxylates. Syngas, a mixture of H2, CO2, and CO, can be sourced sustainably and used to supplement biomass feedstocks as a source of acetyl-CoA, an intermediate for carboxylate chain elongation. To test this, syngas and corn silage were provided to a 10-L semicontinuous fermenter for 208 days of operation in a first-of-a-kind study at this scale. After acclimation to syngas, a 2-fold reduction in average CO2 production rate (0.097 vs 0.21 g L–1 d–1) was observed over a period of 42 days in comparison to a control. Syngas cofeeding also increased average production rates of n-butyrate (C4) and n-caproate (C6) by 74 and 27%, respectively, although these effects were observed at relatively low C6 concentrations up to 4 g L–1. Abundances of Megasphaera and Dialister showed significant correlation (p < 0.05) to consumption of H2, CO2, and CO as well as production of C3, C4, C5, or C7, suggesting involvement of these genera in mixotrophic metabolism. A feasibility analysis showed that syngas recirculation could return additional 1.54 USD mbroth–3 while costing 1.26 USD mbroth–3 and avoiding 1.81 kg CO2 eq. mbroth–3 in emissions compared to heterotrophic fermentation. With still much room to increase syngas consumption and carboxylate production, we propose mixotrophic fermentation as a “low-tech” technology to turn fermenters into decentralized industrial carbon sinks.

title: Beyond radiotheranostics: how imaging modality defines theranostics
summary: Theranostics integrates diagnostic imaging and therapy within a single platform, enabling image-guided treatment delivery, real-time monitoring, and therapeutic optimization. The choice of imaging modality fundamentally shapes the design, f
content: Theranostics integrates diagnostic imaging and therapy within a single platform, enabling image-guided treatment delivery, real-time monitoring, and therapeutic optimization. The choice of imaging modality fundamentally shapes the design, functionality, and clinical maturity of theranostic systems. This review examines the theranostic concept through the lens of major imaging modalities employed in clinical and preclinical practice, including positron emission tomography (PET), single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), ultrasound (US), optical imaging (OI), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and computed tomography (CT). Beyond modality-specific approaches, the review highlights emerging multimodal theranostic strategies that integrate complementary imaging technologies to overcome individual limitations, enhance biological specificity, and improve treatment guidance. For each modality, we discuss the structural components of theranostic agents, their mechanisms of action, and the balance between diagnostic sensitivity and therapeutic efficacy. The review also highlights current and emerging clinical applications across major disease areas, while critically addressing limitations, such as spatial resolution, depth penetration, toxicity, and translational barriers. Overall, this article underscores that theranostics are expanding from modality-defined implementation toward integrated, multimodal strategies that are likely to shape the next generation of personalized and precision imaging-guided therapies. RELEVANCE STATEMENT : Imaging modality-driven theranostic design enables more precise, adaptive, and personalized image-guided therapies by aligning diagnostic sensitivity with therapeutic mechanisms, thereby improving treatment selection, response monitoring, and translational integration across clinical disciplines. KEY POINTS: Theranostics is determined by the underlying imaging modality rather than by a unified theranostic framework. Imaging modality dictates integration strategy. Nuclear medicine theranostics are clinically established, while MRI-, CT-, ultrasound-, and optical-based theranostics remain largely translational or function primarily as image-guided therapies. Multimodal theranostics address modality-specific limitations. Future progress depends on imaging-driven design and standardization.

title: CMIP6-driven deep-learning downscaling dataset of historical and future daily precipitation over the Loess Plateau, China
summary: Under global warming, intensified droughts and rainfall extremes pose serious threats to water resources, ecosystems, agriculture, and geological safety in the semi-arid Loess Plateau. However, the coarse resolution and large systematic err
content: Under global warming, intensified droughts and rainfall extremes pose serious threats to water resources, ecosystems, agriculture, and geological safety in the semi-arid Loess Plateau. However, the coarse resolution and large systematic errors and uncertainties of global climate models (GCMs) limit their effectiveness for assessing regional precipitation changes and related impacts. This study employs a deep-learning (DL) downscaling approach by applying an attention-based Laplacian pyramid network to CMIP6 atmospheric variables to generate a high-resolution precipitation dataset over the Loess Plateau. The dataset provides daily precipitation at 0.1° spatial resolution for 1950–2100, based on historical simulations and two Shared Socioeconomic Pathway scenarios (SSP2-45 and SSP5-85) from four CMIP6 GCMs. Evaluation shows that the DL-downscaled data better characterize spatial details and extreme features in precipitation than the original GCM outputs, and successfully captures local probability density functions of daily precipitation across the region. With its long temporal coverage and fine spatial resolution, this dataset provides a crucial data foundation for projecting future regional precipitation changes and extremes, and for assessing the attendant impact.

title: Moral obligation or personal benefit? Explaining consumers' regular use intentions for digital product passports
summary: Abstract Digital product passports (DPPs) are a product-service innovation designed to increase transparency on product sustainability and support circular economy practices by providing consumers with lifecycle-wide information on material
content: Abstract Digital product passports (DPPs) are a product-service innovation designed to increase transparency on product sustainability and support circular economy practices by providing consumers with lifecycle-wide information on materials, repairability, and end-of-life options. However, empirical evidence on which factors drive not only initial uptake but also regular use of DPPs is scarce. Building on the norm activation model (NAM) and UTAUT2, this paper investigates antecedents of consumers’ regular use intentions for DPPs and examines differences between pre-purchase and post-purchase scenarios. We conducted two scenario-based online surveys with German ( n = 344) and Spanish ( n = 195) consumers and analyzed the data using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), necessary condition analysis (NCA), and a qualitative analysis of open-ended responses. Personal norms, performance expectancy, and anticipated habit emerge as main drivers of regular use intentions, with performance expectancy particularly relevant in the post-purchase phase. The NCA identifies anticipated habit as a necessary condition for regular use across scenarios and samples, whereas the necessity of effort expectancy and performance expectancy is scenario-specific; qualitative responses likewise highlight usability as a key prerequisite. Overall, regular use intentions are stronger in the post-purchase context. This study contributes to research by (1) providing the first theoretically grounded examination of consumers’ regular use intentions for DPPs across pre- and post-purchase stages, (2) showing that normative beliefs explain regular use intentions alongside technology acceptance constructs, and (3) identifying both sufficient and necessary conditions for regular DPP use. Our findings offer actionable implications for policymakers and practitioners advancing DPP implementation.

title: Entrepreneurship-Based Green Finance Model: Optimizing the Role of Regional-Owned Enterprises (BUMD) in Achieving Jakarta’s Net Zero Emission 2060 Target
source: Indonesian Journal of Environmental Management and Sustainability
summary: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of willingness to innovate, proactive attitude, and risk-taking propensity on green finance and sustainability performance among Regional-Owned Enterprises (BUMD) in DKI Jakarta. The resear
content: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of willingness to innovate, proactive attitude, and risk-taking propensity on green finance and sustainability performance among Regional-Owned Enterprises (BUMD) in DKI Jakarta. The research employs a quantitative method using Structural Equation Modeling with Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) analysis, based on primary survey data collected from 23 BUMDs in Jakarta in 2025. The findings reveal that willingness to innovate and proactive attitude positively contribute to strengthening green finance; however, only the proactive attitude consistently enhances sustainability performance. Conversely, the willingness to take risks shows a negative effect on green finance and an insignificant impact on sustainability performance. Furthermore, green finance exerts a positive, though not yet significant, influence on sustainability performance. These findings underscore the need for operational strategies such as strengthening green innovation, establishing sustainability teams, implementing green risk management, and developing sustainability reports as integral components of transparent and accountable governance. Such strategies are essential to reinforce the strategic role of BUMDs in supporting the transition toward a green economy and achieving Jakarta’s Net Zero Emission 2060 target.

title: Agricultural Industry Agglomeration and Carbon Emission Intensity: A Systems Perspective on Resilience and Digital Development
summary: Decarbonizing agriculture depends not only on the efficiency of individual production activities but also on coordination among production, processing, and service activities. From a systems perspective, this study treats provincial agricul
content: Decarbonizing agriculture depends not only on the efficiency of individual production activities but also on coordination among production, processing, and service activities. From a systems perspective, this study treats provincial agriculture as an interconnected industrial system and examines the relationship between agricultural industry agglomeration and agricultural carbon emission intensity. Moving beyond conventional measures of production concentration, agricultural industry agglomeration is measured as coordination between horizontal agglomeration in agricultural production and vertical agglomeration across production, processing, and agricultural services. Based on a balanced panel of 390 observations across 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2023, the study uses province and year fixed effects, mediation and moderation analyses, robustness checks, and an endogeneity check. Results show that agricultural industry agglomeration is significantly associated with lower agricultural carbon emission intensity. The mediation results are consistent with a partial intermediary role for agricultural industry resilience in this relationship. The interaction and simple slope results show that the positive association between agricultural industry agglomeration and agricultural industry resilience is larger at higher levels of digital village development. These findings connect subsystem coordination, adaptive capacity, digital conditions, and carbon performance, thereby extending research on agricultural transformation toward lower carbon intensity from a systems perspective.

title: Aligning Biofuels Policy with the Sustainable Development Goals in the UAE: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: The United Arab Emirates is actively making efforts to shift the current dependence on fossil fuels to a more cleaner and sustainable energy direction, and biofuels are a prospective part of this amendment. The practicality, opportunities,
content: The United Arab Emirates is actively making efforts to shift the current dependence on fossil fuels to a more cleaner and sustainable energy direction, and biofuels are a prospective part of this amendment. The practicality, opportunities, policy framework, and sustainability compatibility of biofuel production in the UAE have been estimated in this systematic review. It distinctly focuses on the waste-based feedstocks that do not compete with food sources. This review also points out UAE’s optimal position in terms of production of biofuels using used cooking oil, agricultural waste, municipal and sewage waste, animal waste and local microalgae adapted to the desert and coastal environment, which has been compiled from various research works. This review followed PRISMA guidelines that included 26 studies to analyze the technical, economic and social feasibility of biofuels. Biofuels are highly compatible with the national clean energy agenda as they help significantly reduce carbon emission (in comparison to traditional fossil fuels) and grow the renewable energy market. However, as shown in this review, there are many policy constraints that limit the growth of this sector. Waste based biofuels have the potential to benefit UAE’s transition to renewable energy, as shown in this review. Improved policies and governance systems, financial support, and increased social awareness/participation is needed to assist biofuels to have the necessary impact on national sustainability objectives.

title: Forensic source classes and toxic-equivalent concentrations of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in soils and sediments: a systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: Diagnostic-ratio source attribution is routine in environmental forensics, but whether the assigned source class predicts the benzo[a]pyrene toxic-equivalent concentration (TEQBaP) of a contaminated solid matrix has not been evaluated quant
content: Diagnostic-ratio source attribution is routine in environmental forensics, but whether the assigned source class predicts the benzo[a]pyrene toxic-equivalent concentration (TEQBaP) of a contaminated solid matrix has not been evaluated quantitatively. We conducted a systematic review (PRISMA 2020) of soil and sediment studies published from 2013 to 2026 that reported TEQBaP together with a diagnostic-ratio source classification. A structured search of Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science conducted on 2 July 2026 returned 2,119 records, which were reduced through successive screening to a review corpus of 105 full texts; with a supplementary search, 67 studies were included in the review. A total of 16 studies met the quantitative criteria after a primary-source audit of every extracted value, of which 12 yielded a directly derivable sampling variance (primary model) and 14 yielded a variance with imputation. The outcome was the reported BaP-equivalent concentration, a carcinogenic-potency metric, not a measured biological effect. ln(TEQBaP) was pooled by restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung–Knapp–Sidik–Jonkman intervals. The pooled TEQBaP was 104.2 ng g -1 (95% CI = 32.4–335.6; k = 12), essentially unchanged under DerSimonian–Laird, Paule–Mandel, and equal weighting, with τ 2 = 3.27 (95% CI = 1.58–9.44), I 2 = 99.9%, and a 95% prediction interval of 1.6–6,942 ng g -1 . Pyrogenic and mixed assemblages differed by a factor of 0.57 (95% CI = 0.04–8.0; p = 0.639): no difference was detected, but the interval is compatible with anything from a substantial decrease to a roughly 20-fold increase, so this is an absence of detected association rather than evidence of equivalence. Petrogenic evidence remained insufficient for class-level inference (k = 3 overall; k = 1 in the primary model) even after the search was widened. Secondary moderators, including sampling environment, are reported as exploratory and hypothesis-generating only. A concentration-normalized mixture potency factor (MPF = TEQBaP/ΣPAH) is proposed as a reporting convention and evaluated as exploratory feasibility work; it remains unvalidated. The principal finding is that the available study-level evidence is too sparse and too heterogeneous to determine whether forensic source class predicts toxic-equivalent concentration—an evidence gap, not a demonstrated null.

title: Virus ΨM2 enters a non-lytic lifecycle alternative to lysogeny during infection of Methanothermobacter marburgensis
summary: Methanogens, a diverse group of archaea that produce methane during energy metabolism, are prevalent in anoxic habitats where they are exposed to viral infections. The head-tailed virus ΨM2 is one of few virus isolates that infect a methano
content: Methanogens, a diverse group of archaea that produce methane during energy metabolism, are prevalent in anoxic habitats where they are exposed to viral infections. The head-tailed virus ΨM2 is one of few virus isolates that infect a methanogen host and was described as a lytic virus that lyses its host, Methanothermobacter marburgensis . Here, we present evidence that ΨM2 does not exclusively follow the classic lytic lifecycle but can also enter an alternative, chronic infection-like state. Growth experiments showed that infected cultures in minimal medium, optimized for the methanogen host (MS medium) did not exhibit complete lysis but continuously released infective virions. In contrast, in a suboptimal complex medium (SAB medium), the ΨM2-infected culture released virions in the exponential growth phase and eventually lysed after 14 hours post infection. Although the genome of ΨM2 encodes a putative integrase, a prerequisite for lysogeny, whole genome sequencing of ΨM2-infected M. marburgensis cultures revealed that the viral DNA remained extrachromosomal rather than integrating into the host genome, likely due to a mutation in the integrase gene. These findings suggest that ΨM2 enters a non-lytic lifecycle alternative to lysogeny under suboptimal host growth conditions. Sequencing further identified a heterogeneous viral population including previously undescribed variants. A high density of non-synonymous mutations and frameshift-inducing insertions was observed within ORFs predicted to encode a capsid protein and a major spike protein, suggesting these viral variants to differ in host recognition and infectivity. Overall, our results show more complex viral behavior and greater genetic variability than previously described.

title: Training tools, clinical decision support tools, and evaluation methods promoting environmentally sustainable inhaler prescribing in asthma management: a scoping review protocol
summary: BACKGROUND. The healthcare sector is a substantial contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, notably through the use of inhalers in asthma management. Although several initiatives aim to promote more environmentally sustainable inhaler presc
content: BACKGROUND. The healthcare sector is a substantial contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, notably through the use of inhalers in asthma management. Although several initiatives aim to promote more environmentally sustainable inhaler prescribing, their implementation remains limited by a lack of suitable training tools, clinical decision support resources, and standardised methods for evaluating their effectiveness. The knowledge currently available on these practice-support tools remains scattered across the literature, which limits their integration into clinical practice and into training programmes for health professionals. OBJECTIVE. This scoping review aims to map the scientific knowledge on training tools, clinical decision support tools, and evaluation methods that promote environmentally sustainable inhaler prescribing. Specifically, it will identify the characteristics of training tools that support the acquisition of clinical competencies among prescribers, respiratory therapists, nurses, and pharmacists; catalogue the decision support tools that assist in selecting low-carbon-footprint inhalers without compromising patient safety; and describe the methods used to evaluate their effects on knowledge, prescribing patterns, and the carbon footprint of care. METHODS. This scoping review will be conducted in accordance with the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley, enhanced by Levac and colleagues, and following the guidance of the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI). Reporting will follow the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Literature searches will be conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase (Ovid), CINAHL Complete (EBSCOhost), and Web of Science Core Collection, supplemented by a targeted search of the grey literature and of documents published by major professional organisations and health institutions. Studies addressing training tools, clinical decision support tools, or methods for evaluating the effectiveness of such tools on environmentally sustainable inhaler prescribing will be eligible. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection and data extraction. Findings will be synthesised descriptively and thematically, organised according to the three research axes of the study. EXPECTED RESULTS. This review will produce a comprehensive picture of the training and clinical decision support tools currently available to support environmentally sustainable inhaler prescribing. It will highlight the characteristics of training tools, the components of clinical decision support tools, and the approaches used to evaluate their effectiveness. Gaps in the literature and priority research needs will also be identified. CONCLUSION. The findings of this review will provide the scientific foundation for developing a training programme and clinical decision support tools to promote environmentally sustainable inhaler prescribing in paediatric asthma management. They will help inform continuing education strategies, clinical practice, an

title: Perceptions of Climate Change, Health Impacts, and Climate Resilience, among Urban Residents Living with Asthma: An Exploratory Qualitative Study
summary: Abstract In the US, rates of asthma, and in particular, uncontrolled asthma, are disproportionately high among historically marginalized racial/ethnic groups and among urban residents. Against the backdrop of climate change and its known co
content: Abstract In the US, rates of asthma, and in particular, uncontrolled asthma, are disproportionately high among historically marginalized racial/ethnic groups and among urban residents. Against the backdrop of climate change and its known consequences, which can exacerbate the environmental triggers of asthma, these inequities are further magnified. This qualitative study explored perceptions of climate change, health impacts, and climate resilience among historically marginalized urban adults with asthma. Black/African-American, Hispanic/Latino, and/or multiracial adults ( $$\ge$$ ≥ 18 years) diagnosed with asthma, and residing in the Chicagoland area, were recruited. Semistructured interviews informed by the capability, opportunity, motivation, and behavior (COM-B) model were conducted, and data were transcribed for thematic coding. Data from 20 interviews revealed four primary themes: (1) climate change awareness, (2) perceived harms of climate change, (3) climate resiliency: barriers and strategies, and (4) perceived outlook on climate change. Participants consistently associated extreme weather with adverse asthma management consequences and highlighted the negative impacts of climate-related events on their outdoor time, physical activity, and social life. Virtually all participants emphasized significant financial burden resulting from their daily living adaptations for managing their condition in the context of climate change. Participants showed variable levels of climate preparedness and reported limited community-level engagement in climate action activities. This study supports enhancing climate resilience as a potentially effective strategy for improving asthma management among historically marginalized urban residents, warranting future research. Findings emphasize the need to strengthen both individual- and societal/environmental-level climate resilience to optimize health and well-being for all.

title: Input Parameter Dataset for Stochastic Multi-Carrier SSCEE Scheduling with Electric-Drone Mobility
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Input Parameter Dataset for Stochastic Multi-Carrier SSCEE Scheduling with Electric-Drone Mobility This dataset provides a structured numerical input specification for a stochastic multi-carrier energy scheduling benchmark incorporating car
content: Input Parameter Dataset for Stochastic Multi-Carrier SSCEE Scheduling with Electric-Drone Mobility This dataset provides a structured numerical input specification for a stochastic multi-carrier energy scheduling benchmark incorporating carbon-emission trading (CET), renewable portfolio standards (RPS), peer-to-peer (P2P) electricity trading, hydrogen conversion, and electric-drone mobility. The accompanying Microsoft Excel workbook contains 27 numerical parameter tables corresponding to Appendix C of the supplementary material. The dataset covers the following subsystems and modeling components: Multi-carrier distribution networks: IEEE 33-bus electrical distribution system, 7-node natural-gas network, 14-node district-heating network, and 20-node hydrogen distribution network, including branch characteristics, operating limits, and network parameters. Energy conversion and storage: Input specifications for combined heat and power units, gas boilers, electrolyzers, hydrogen fuel cells, methanation, and stationary energy storage. P2P electricity trading: Participant configurations, bilateral trading connections, and associated operating parameters. Electric-drone mobility: Fleet characteristics, battery parameters, charging and discharging limits, mobility-distribution parameters, and stochastic scenario inputs. Scheduling and learning parameters: Hourly demand and renewable-generation profiles, electricity tariffs, scenario-generation settings, and deep reinforcement learning configuration parameters. The benchmark adopts a 24-hour scheduling horizon with hourly resolution. Its mobility-scenario specification comprises 1,000 initial realizations and 10 representative scenarios, with scenario probabilities assigned according to the prescribed reduction procedure. The workbook includes separate machine-readable worksheets for the numerical tables and selected structured input categories.

title: Highly oxidized products from the atmospheric reaction of hydroxyl radicals with toluene
summary: Abstract Simple aromatics, largely toluene (C 7 H 8 ) and benzene (C 6 H 6 ), are emitted into Earth´s atmosphere by different sources. Their degradation initiated by the gas-phase reaction with hydroxyl radicals (OH) forms mainly bicyclic
content: Abstract Simple aromatics, largely toluene (C 7 H 8 ) and benzene (C 6 H 6 ), are emitted into Earth´s atmosphere by different sources. Their degradation initiated by the gas-phase reaction with hydroxyl radicals (OH) forms mainly bicyclic peroxy radicals (BCP) besides phenol-type compounds. The formation of highly oxidized products with at least 6 O atoms (HOMs) starting from BCP is currently controversial. Here, the experimental observation of HOMs and other products is reported for near-atmospheric conditions focusing on OH + toluene. Autoxidation processes starting from BCP generate C 7 H 9 O 7 and C 7 H 9 O 9 radicals with molar yields of $${0.25}_{\,-0.13}^{\,+0.25}\, \%$$ 0.25 − 0.13 + 0.25 % and $${0.12}_{\,-0.06}^{\,+0.12}\, \%$$ 0.12 − 0.06 + 0.12 % , respectively. Labeling experiments revealed that the ring H atoms are involved in autoxidation. The atmospherically relevant reaction of C 7 H 9 O 7 and C 7 H 9 O 9 with NO almost exclusively forms organic nitrates as HOM products, C 7 H 9 O 6-8 NO 2 , with a total molar yield ≤ 0.1%. Other HOMs, such as C 7 H 8 O 8 and C 7 H 8 O 10 , represent only small trace products. Results from OH + benzene confirmed the findings from the toluene system pointing to a minor relevance of both aromatics for HOM generation.

title: Plasma-Assisted and Green Routes to Silicon and Carbon Quantum Dots: A Critical Comparison of Synthesis–Structure–Property Relationships
summary: Silicon quantum dots (SiQDs) and carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are often discussed as related heavy-metal-free luminescent nanomaterials, although the mechanisms governing their formation and emission differ fundamentally. Rather than combinin
content: Silicon quantum dots (SiQDs) and carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are often discussed as related heavy-metal-free luminescent nanomaterials, although the mechanisms governing their formation and emission differ fundamentally. Rather than combining two parallel bodies of literature, this review uses SiQDs and CQDs as contrasting model systems to determine which synthesis–structure–property relationships are transferable and which remain material-specific. We critically compare nonthermal gas-phase plasma, plasma–liquid, and solution-phase synthesis, including green routes, with respect to precursor activation, nucleation and growth, crystallinity, surface chemistry, purification, photoluminescence, reproducibility, and scalability. Low-pressure continuous-flow radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma (RF-CCP) is treated as the reference plasma architecture for free-standing Si nanocrystals, while atmospheric-pressure and plasma–liquid approaches are discussed according to their distinct product forms, formation mechanisms, and technological maturity. For crystalline SiQDs, quantum confinement provides a physically defined framework for interpreting size-dependent optical behavior, although oxidation, ligands, and interfacial defects remain critical. In CQDs, emission may arise from carbon-core states, surface or defect states, and molecular fluorophores, making structural assignment and fraction-resolved characterization essential. Across both material families, reported record photoluminescence efficiencies are less informative for technological translation than reproducibility, purified product yield, long-term stability, and application-specific performance. Hybrid plasma–liquid processing, operando diagnostics, standardized optical characterization, and data-guided process optimization are identified as promising directions toward scalable and reproducible quantum-dot manufacturing.

title: Laser-etched Molybdenum metasurfaces as refractory broadband solar absorbers
summary: Abstract Broadband solar absorbers (BSAs) are essential for efficient solar thermal energy harvesting. Among them, metasurface absorbers have attracted significant attention owing to their high absorption efficiency, compact footprint, and
content: Abstract Broadband solar absorbers (BSAs) are essential for efficient solar thermal energy harvesting. Among them, metasurface absorbers have attracted significant attention owing to their high absorption efficiency, compact footprint, and compatibility with integrated energy systems. However, easy fabrication of metasurface solar absorbers remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a novel BSAs based on laser-etched refractory molybdenum (Mo) metasurfaces fabricated using a nanosecond laser processing technique. Fourier imaging spectroscopy measurements, supported by finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations, reveal broadband absorption spanning 400–1100 nm, wide-angle operation, and high average absorptance. To evaluate the robustness of the fabrication technique, metasurfaces were produced under different laser repetition frequencies and power settings. The corresponding reflectance spectra and calculated average absorptances show consistently high performance across all fabrication conditions, indicating excellent process tolerance. The combination of broadband absorption, angular stability, scalability, and fabrication simplicity highlights the potential of laser-etched Mo metasurfaces as practical, broadband solar absorbers for high-temperature solar thermal energy conversion applications.

title: ARISE: an urban political economy-informed resilience indicator framework for south asian metropolitan cities
summary: Introduction Existing urban resilience indicator frameworks combine literature-derived pooling, expert validation, and multi-criteria weighting independently of any explicit theory of why some urban conditions, rather than others, are polit
content: Introduction Existing urban resilience indicator frameworks combine literature-derived pooling, expert validation, and multi-criteria weighting independently of any explicit theory of why some urban conditions, rather than others, are politically constituted as resilience priorities. Methods This paper’s contribution is methodological: it demonstrates how Urban Political Economy (UPE) theory can condition an indicator-development pipeline, from category structure through to how weighting outcomes are interpreted against theoretical commitments. ARISE, the Adaptive Resilience Indicator System for Equity, operationalises this UPE-conditioned approach through five stages: identification, categorisation, reduction, validation, and prioritisation. Drawing on 75 studies and 193 indicators, ARISE applies Pareto analysis and Staticized Group Technique consultation to produce 32 Resilience Indicators across seven dimensions, weighted via the Analytic Hierarchy Process by 18 experts. Results Urban Design and Spatial Planning carries the highest weight (36.04%); sensitivity analysis confirms stability for four dimensions, with Ecosystem and Resources (5.96%) the most panel-sensitive. Discussion The contribution is theory-conditioned indicator-development methodology: a UPE-derived categorisation structure, a two-track mechanism protecting under-cited indicators from elimination, and an explicit interrogation of the divergence between theoretical commitments and empirical outcomes, rather than a claim that the underlying AHP, Pareto, and SGT instruments are themselves novel. The indicator set illustrates what this conditioning produces, transferable in logic to other theory-grounded efforts. ARISE is not a validated scoring instrument at this stage; it is an expert-prioritised indicator-development framework whose empirical application to real cities constitutes the next research phase.

title: The Power Behind the Prompt
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Book 1 of the Power and Responsibility in the Age of AI series. Every AI prompt is processed in a physical building that draws power, needs cooling and depends on the grid. This book follows the chain from the productivity organisations exp
content: Book 1 of the Power and Responsibility in the Age of AI series. Every AI prompt is processed in a physical building that draws power, needs cooling and depends on the grid. This book follows the chain from the productivity organisations expect from AI, through the computation, data centres, electricity, water and materials that adoption demands, to the grid, carbon and cost consequences that follow. Written for chief executives, board members and the finance, technology, procurement and sustainability leaders who work alongside them, it sets out how organisations can capture the benefits of AI while governing its physical costs. The Power and Responsibility in the Age of AI series examines the choices organisations make when they put artificial intelligence to work. Book 1 asks what AI consumes: the electricity, water, materials and grid capacity behind every prompt. Book 2 asks what AI is allowed to do, and who answers for it when AI agents act on our behalf. Each book stands alone, and together they offer leaders a complete view of the costs and responsibilities that come with AI. About the author. Adrian Summers is Group Director, Data and AI at one of Saudi Arabia's largest construction and engineering groups, leading AI strategy and governance across 14 subsidiaries while building AI systems himself, including an agentic platform with human oversight. His background spans investment banking, funds management and defence advisory. He holds degrees in finance, management and AI, and is a PhD candidate in AI and technology.

title: Estimation of the Impact of the Formal Implementation of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism on the Implicit Carbon Costs of China's Exports and Identification of Trade Transfer Effects
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: After the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered the formal stage, the implicit emissions of products began to form the compliance costs at the import stage. This paper examines how this cost affects the destination selectio
content: After the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered the formal stage, the implicit emissions of products began to form the compliance costs at the import stage. This paper examines how this cost affects the destination selection of China's exports. The study calculates the industry costs based on the default path and uses annual panel estimation to estimate the changes in EU exports. In the first year of the formal period, the required clearance ratio is only 2.5%, and the cost is less than 1.5% of the export value to Europe. Under the benchmark setting, the export coefficient to Europe is -0.152, and to the third market is 0.127, with opposite signs. The adjustment term direction also points to market substitution caused by carbon costs. The current expenditure is difficult to explain this combination. The expected quota reduction and compliance preparations are more likely to be the main drivers. Therefore, the assessment of export adjustment must separate the scale compression effect of costs from the order reallocation effect. Research shows that whether or not reliable emission data can be provided is as important as market selection.

title: Fostering conceptual understanding of organic solar cells through immersive augmented reality: a quasi-experimental study in chemistry education
summary: Organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly important in modern chemistry and sustainable energy education; however, undergraduate students often struggle to understand their molecular structure, charge generation, charge transport, and ope
content: Organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly important in modern chemistry and sustainable energy education; however, undergraduate students often struggle to understand their molecular structure, charge generation, charge transport, and operating mechanisms because these processes are abstract, invisible, and difficult to convey using conventional instructional approaches. This study investigated whether an immersive augmented reality (AR) learning application could improve conceptual understanding of OSCs and reduce students’ misconceptions. The AR application was developed through a needs assessment with chemistry educators and incorporated interactive three-dimensional visualizations, molecular- and device-level explanations, and simulations of key OSC processes. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, combining a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test study with semi-structured student interviews. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) revealed that the instructional method had a significant effect on post-test performance after controlling for pre-test scores (F(1,117) = 214.67, p < .001, partial η² = 0.823), indicating a large educational effect. Students who used the AR application demonstrated substantially greater improvements in conceptual understanding than those receiving conventional instruction, particularly regarding OSC structure, operating mechanisms, molecular interactions, and charge transport, while misconceptions were markedly reduced. Student interviews further confirmed that immersive visualization enhanced understanding by making abstract molecular and device-level processes more accessible and engaging. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of immersive AR for improving conceptual learning in chemistry education and highlight its potential for teaching emerging sustainable energy technologies.

title: Low-carbon power system scheduling via nodal marginal carbon intensity-driven synergy between generation and demand sides
summary: Nodal marginal carbon intensity (NMCI) quantifies the marginal change in system carbon emissions caused by nodal load variations and provides a potential signal for coordinating generation- and demand-side decarbonization. Because demand re
content: Nodal marginal carbon intensity (NMCI) quantifies the marginal change in system carbon emissions caused by nodal load variations and provides a potential signal for coordinating generation- and demand-side decarbonization. Because demand response (DR) changes nodal loads, it may alter the optimal solution and the active constraints of the generation-side scheduling problem, thereby changing the NMCI. This paper proposes a two-stage low-carbon scheduling framework that coordinates the generation and demand sides through NMCI. In Stage I, a DC-power-flow-based generation scheduling model jointly considers operating costs and carbon-emission costs of generators, and the NMCI and its corresponding invariance constraints are analytically derived for each scheduling interval. In Stage II, a low-carbon DR model incorporating an NMCI-based demand-side carbon tax is solved iteratively. The NMCI and its invariance constraints are updated whenever DR drives the system into a transition state, thereby enabling further exploitation of the demand-side emission-reduction potential while maintaining the feasibility of Stage I scheduling problem. Compared with traditional day-ahead generation-side scheduling without user-side DR, the NMCI-guided DR strategy reduces carbon emissions by 1.63% and 4.79% in the IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 39-bus systems, respectively, and outperforms the nodal static carbon intensity (NSCI)-based strategy in coordinating generation- and demand-side decarbonization.

title: Variability in blue carbon stocks across mangrove forest types in Jamaica
summary: Mangroves are among the most carbon-rich tropical forests, with much of their carbon stock located in underlying sediments. They play a vital role in climate mitigation and adaptation by offsetting carbon dioxide emissions linked to global
content: Mangroves are among the most carbon-rich tropical forests, with much of their carbon stock located in underlying sediments. They play a vital role in climate mitigation and adaptation by offsetting carbon dioxide emissions linked to global warming. Despite their importance, blue carbon ecosystems remain poorly represented in climate policy across the Caribbean, with Jamaica and Belize being the only Caribbean countries to incorporate blue carbon stock values into their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). Limited standardized information on mangrove carbon stocks across representative forest types in the region, further constrains the development of national baselines and their integration into climate policies. We conducted comprehensive mangrove carbon assessments across seven sites within four forest ecotypes: riverine, fringing, cay and lake to establish a national carbon baseline. The national mean total ecosystem carbon stock was determined to be 387.8 ± 18.6 Mg C ha -1 . Recent island-wide mapping of mangrove forests determined Jamaica’s total mangrove extent to be 11,978 ha. Using these values, a total national carbon stock of 4.7 ± 0.2 Tg C was determined for Jamaican mangrove forests, with 3.5 Tg C stored as sediment stocks, 1.1 Tg C as above and below-ground tree biomass and 0.08 Tg C as standing dead tree biomass. Results indicate that forests within freshwater systems had the greatest carbon stored as living biomass (79.5 ± 15.7 Mg C ha -1 ), while forests on small mangrove cays, had the highest sediment carbon (344.6 ± 13.1 Mg C ha -1 ) despite influences from tidal flows. The random forest regression predictor identified sediment pH as important predictors across all carbon components, while forest type was important for standing dead and sediment carbon. Water salinity was a strong predictor of standing dead carbon and a weak and negative predictor for biomass carbon. This study provides valuable insight on the variability of mangrove carbon in different forest types potentially supporting sustainable management and conservation strategies necessary to inform policy. It represents the most extensive mangrove carbon assessment done in Jamaica with results informing the 2025 update of the island’s NDCs, a commitment under the Paris Agreement.

title: Forest Fire Area, Industrial GRDP, Population Density, and Environmental Quality in Indonesia
summary: Purpose— This study examines how forest fire area, industrial-sector gross regional domestic product (GRDP), and population density are associated with Indonesia’s Environmental Quality Index (Indeks Kualitas Lingkungan Hidup, IKLH) at the
content: Purpose— This study examines how forest fire area, industrial-sector gross regional domestic product (GRDP), and population density are associated with Indonesia’s Environmental Quality Index (Indeks Kualitas Lingkungan Hidup, IKLH) at the provincial level. Research Methodology— A quantitative panel-data design uses 150 province-year observations from 30 Indonesian provinces during 2020–2024. Common-, fixed-, and random-effects specifications are considered, with the Chow and Hausman tests supporting a fixed-effects model. Results— Forest fire area is not statistically associated with IKLH in the selected model, whereas industrial GRDP and population density show positive conditional associations. The full fixed-effects specification is statistically significant, but its overall model test includes province effects and therefore does not isolate the joint contribution of the three substantive regressors. Research limitations/Implications— The analysis covers three predictors, 30 provinces, and five years; omitted time effects, spatial dependence, and robust inference limit generalization. The findings support continued fire prevention, cleaner industrial development, and environmental infrastructure in densely populated areas. Originality— The study integrates ecological, industrial, and demographic pressures within one provincial panel framework while controlling for time-invariant provincial heterogeneity.

title: Dynamic baselines with blended BAU scenarios ensure conservative mitigation estimates for improved forest management accounting
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Introduction Improved forest management (IFM) is vital for climate change mitigation. Yet, precise carbon accounting to ensure credible attribution is a challenge. Current accounting protocols vary in their analytical approaches, leading to
content: Introduction Improved forest management (IFM) is vital for climate change mitigation. Yet, precise carbon accounting to ensure credible attribution is a challenge. Current accounting protocols vary in their analytical approaches, leading to substantial differences in mitigation outcomes. Methods We evaluated four common decision points in baseline design—modeled versus measured, static versus dynamic, matched versus random, and single versus blended business-as-usual (BAU) scenarios— across diverse regions and forest types in the eastern United States (US) using Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) and the Forest Vegetation Simulator (FVS). Results Dynamic baselines that integrate blended BAUs produced, on average, 63% more conservative estimates of net climate mitigation benefits than static, single BAU models, highlighting how baseline design choices can substantially influence results, with estimated mitigation varying by more than fivefold across accounting approaches, regions, and forest types. Stand characteristics, such as stand density, also affected outcomes. Conclusion Since the true BAU counterfactual cannot be directly observed, adopting dynamic baselines with blended BAU scenarios can reduce the risk of overestimation, strengthen the credibility of carbon accounting, support more informed investment in IFM projects, and reinforce the integrity of carbon accounting for natural climate solutions.

title: Contrast-enhanced T2-fluid-attenuated inversion recovery magnetic resonance imaging for radiotherapy target delineation in brain metastases: A narrative review
summary: Brain metastases (BM) are the most common type of brain tumor, with diagnosis, pretreatment evaluation, and follow-up relying on imaging.Radiotherapy, including whole brain radiotherapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, is a key treatment moda
content: Brain metastases (BM) are the most common type of brain tumor, with diagnosis, pretreatment evaluation, and follow-up relying on imaging.Radiotherapy, including whole brain radiotherapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, is a key treatment modality for BM, and its efficacy is closely related to the precision of target delineation, which depends on clear and accurate multimodal imaging.The target delineation for BM is typically performed using a fusion technique combining computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).In routine MRI, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (T1WI + C) is considered the basic sequence, but it has certain limitations, such as the interference with lesion signals adjacent to large vessels and the cerebral cortex caused by enhanced vascular signals.T2-fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (T2-FLAIR) sequence suppresses the signal of free water [cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)] while highlighting the signal of bound water (intracranial edema).Contrast-enhanced T2-FLAIR (T2-FLAIR + C) sequence further improves visualization, thereby addressing the limitations of T1WI + C. Specifically, T2-FLAIR + C effectively suppresses CSF signals while clearly delineating enhanced lesions, particularly those on the brain surface and adjacent to the cerebral cortex.Additionally, its heightened sensitivity to low concentrations of gadolinium allows for indirect assessment of the vascularity of brain and meningeal tumors.However, the use of MRI simulation in radiotherapy for BM is not widespread, and the application of the T2-FLAIR + C sequence is not yet common.This narrative review elaborates on the technical principles of the T2-FLAIR + C sequence and current guidelines for BM radiotherapy target delineation, summarizes its clinical applications in BM radiotherapy, and discusses existing evidence gaps and future research directions.Notably, direct evidence supporting the benefit of T2-FLAIR + C for contouring accuracy, dosimetric optimization, and patient clinical outcomes remains limited.This review aims to provide a comprehensive reference for further research and clinical application of T2-FLAIR + C in BM radiotherapy.

title: Photosynthesis: Nature's Answer to Climate Change?
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This article explains the connection between photosynthesis and climate change in simple scientific language. It covers how plants, algae and bacteria absorb carbon dioxide, why forests and oceans act as carbon sinks, how deforestation wors
content: This article explains the connection between photosynthesis and climate change in simple scientific language. It covers how plants, algae and bacteria absorb carbon dioxide, why forests and oceans act as carbon sinks, how deforestation worsens global warming, and how heat, drought and floods reduce photosynthesis and crop yields, with a focus on Pakistan's agriculture. It concludes with practical solutions: protecting forests and oceans, reforestation campaigns, biotechnology for climate-resilient crops, and reducing fossil fuel emissions. Self-written based on my Biology (FSc) studies.

title: Soil emission measurement
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Soil greenhouse gas flux measurement is essential for evaluating carbon and nitrogen exchange between soil and atmosphere. This SOP describes a chamber-based procedure for measuring CO2, CH4 and N2O emissions from field or pot experiments.
content: Soil greenhouse gas flux measurement is essential for evaluating carbon and nitrogen exchange between soil and atmosphere. This SOP describes a chamber-based procedure for measuring CO2, CH4 and N2O emissions from field or pot experiments. The method is mainly based on the closed static chamber combined with gas chromatography, which is widely used because it is simple, low-cost, sensitive and suitable for cropland, paddy fields and low-vegetation ecosystems. The SOP is useful for researchers and technicians who need standardized and repeatable measurements of soil greenhouse gas emissions under different fertilization, irrigation, crop or soil amendment treatments. It supports comparison among treatments, sites and monitoring campaigns.

title: Giving the Emperor clothes: operationalizing AI ethics principles in corporations
summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies raise enormous questions for society and how we should live. For corporations, AI raises questions about how organizations ought to incorporate principles and other forms of ethical guidanc
content: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies raise enormous questions for society and how we should live. For corporations, AI raises questions about how organizations ought to incorporate principles and other forms of ethical guidance into their work. The movement from theory to practice, or “the operationalization question” demands that organizations not only have good intentions, but actual institutionalized approaches towards ethical problem solving. In this paper, we look at the movement from theory to practice, and particularly at the use of principles as a way to guide ethical behavior, considering, first, why implementation of principles is difficult, second, how to move from abstract principles to actionable principles, and third, illustrating this progression through seven real-life AI cases. These seven cases each relate to an ethical principle: (1) protecting human dignity and rights, and the International Baccalaureate exam replacement by algorithm, (2) promoting human well-being, and Amazon warehouse worker injuries, (3) investing in humanity, and the Partnership on AI’s work to bring together AI corporations and civil society, (4) promoting inclusion, and IBM’s response to the Gender Shades study, (5) protecting the environment, and Hugging Face’s tracking AI energy use, (6) maintaining accountability, and the Christchurch, New Zealand mass shooting response by Facebook and Western Digital, (7) and, lastly, promoting transparency, and AI model cards. The cases model the movement from abstract principle to concrete action, and collectively illustrate a pattern that can be repeated in many contexts, thus demonstrating a new possible solution for organizations implementing ethics.

title: Modeling optimal incentives for the electric vehicle market
summary: Governments face increasing pressure to meet legally binding net-zero targets, requiring a rapid transition from internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles to electric vehicles (EVs). Designing effective incentive schemes is challenging beca
content: Governments face increasing pressure to meet legally binding net-zero targets, requiring a rapid transition from internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles to electric vehicles (EVs). Designing effective incentive schemes is challenging because vehicle fleets adjust slowly, policy interventions are fiscally costly, and electrification erodes fuel-tax revenues. This paper develops a dynamic policy evaluation framework that combines cross-country evidence on EV adoption with long-run fleet dynamics under uncertainty. Using both the United Kingdom and France as case studies, we simulate optimal time paths of EV purchase incentives under alternative policy objectives, including terminal fleet targets, sales-based penalties, and fiscal revenue considerations. The results reveal three core findings. First, stock-based (terminal) penalties may delay intervention but strongly stabilize long-run fleet outcomes, while sales-based penalties induce earlier but less targeted action. Second, dependence on fuel-tax revenues creates a fiscal lock-in mechanism that weakens optimal electrification incentives. Third, the effectiveness of subsidy programs depends critically on consumer responsiveness to price incentives. Overall, the analysis shows that EV transition policy is best evaluated jointly with fiscal reform and long-run fleet dynamics. Well-timed and fiscally coherent intervention can substantially reduce emissions while limiting long-term budgetary risks.

title: HOMER-Based Techno-Economic Analysis of a Solar-Powered EV Charging Station for Campus Use
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
summary: The electrification of campus transportation requires charging infrastructure capable of accommodating variable charging demand while controlling energy cost, grid dependence and environmental impact. This paper presents a HOMER-based techn
content: The electrification of campus transportation requires charging infrastructure capable of accommodating variable charging demand while controlling energy cost, grid dependence and environmental impact. This paper presents a HOMER-based techno-economic analysis of a solar-powered electric vehicle (EV) charging station for campus use. The proposed architecture, derived from the supplied thesis, integrates a 60 kW DC solar photovoltaic (PV) array, maximum-power-point-tracking and DC–DC conversion, a 70 kW power-conversion/inverter stage, a 100 kWh lithium-iron-phosphate battery energy storage concept, Level-2 EV charging, utility-grid support and an energy-management strategy. The HOMER results report annual EV charging consumption of 1,09,500kWh/year [300kW×365] out of total campus consumption of 884,852 kWh, solar PV production of 115,588 kWh and grid purchases of 774,118 kWh. The model reports 37.4 kWh/year of excess electricity, zero unmet electric load and zero capacity shortage. The annual renewable fraction is 12.5% w.r.t total load & 100% w.r.t EV Charging load, while maximum instantaneous renewable penetration reaches 93.2%. The reported economic indicators are a total net present cost (NPC) of $1,633,301, levelized cost of energy (LCOE) of $0.1428/kWh, annual operating cost of $90,771.55, ROI of 16.78% and payback period of 5.95 years. The emissions output is 489,243 kg CO₂/year, 2,121 kg SO₂/year and 1,037 kg NOₓ/year. The paper also performs transparent consistency checks on the reported economic and energy-balance values and identifies modeling issues requiring clarification before practical deployment, particularly the relationship between the stated 100 kW charging envelope and the higher instantaneous load peaks shown in the time-series output, the treatment of the 100 kWh BESS in the base-case results, and the use of an effectively unconstrained grid connection. The study provides a structured simulation-based assessment of solar-assisted campus EV charging and establishes a basis for future validation using measured campus charging data.

title: IQTISODIY O'SISH VA EKOLOGIK BARQARORLIK KO'RSATKICHLARINI EKONOMETRIK MODELLAR YORDAMIDA PROGNOZLASH
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Maqolada O'zbekistonda iqtisodiy o'sish va karbonat angidrid (CO₂) chiqindilari o'rtasidagi bog'liqlik 1990–2024-yillar ma'lumotlari asosida ekonometrik modellar yordamida tahlil qilingan hamda 2030-yilgacha prognoz qilingan. Kuznetsning ek
content: Maqolada O'zbekistonda iqtisodiy o'sish va karbonat angidrid (CO₂) chiqindilari o'rtasidagi bog'liqlik 1990–2024-yillar ma'lumotlari asosida ekonometrik modellar yordamida tahlil qilingan hamda 2030-yilgacha prognoz qilingan. Kuznetsning ekologik egri chizig'i gipotezasi O'zbekiston uchun statistik jihatdan tasdiqlanmadi. ARIMA(1,1,0) modeli yordamida real YaIM 2030-yilda 235,9 mlrd dollarga yetishi prognoz qilindi. 2016–2024-yillarda CO₂ chiqindilarining YaIMga nisbatan elastikligi 0,545 ni tashkil etgani sababli joriy tendensiya saqlansa, chiqindilar 2030-yilga borib 22,4 foizga oshadi. Natijalar iqtisodiy o'sishdan chiqindilarning nisbiy ajralishi ro'y berayotganini, biroq mutlaq kamayishga erishilmayotganini ko'rsatadi.

title: Research review on vehicle energy recovery technology for energy savings
source: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part C Journal of Mechanical Engineering Science
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive review of the research progress in vehicle energy recovery technologies. It synthesizes regenerative braking systems, with an in-depth exploration of their control strategies and efficiency optimization s
content: This paper presents a comprehensive review of the research progress in vehicle energy recovery technologies. It synthesizes regenerative braking systems, with an in-depth exploration of their control strategies and efficiency optimization schemes, alongside regenerative suspension systems—covering both hydraulic and electromagnetic pathways—and waste heat recovery systems. Furthermore, the study analyzes passive aerodynamic energy recovery in vehicle platoons, focusing on the variations in aerodynamic drag and their positive impact on energy recovery. Aerodynamic drag reduction during platooning is specifically defined as “passive energy recovery.” By efficiently recovering braking kinetic energy, suspension vibrational mechanical energy, and vehicle waste heat, while leveraging aerodynamic optimization, various forms of energy dissipated during conventional vehicle operation can be converted into usable electrical power. This integration significantly enhances overall energy efficiency, extends driving range, and reduces carbon emissions. Finally, the paper provides an outlook on future research directions, emphasizing that the collaborative optimization and intelligent control of multi-source energy recovery systems are pivotal to advancing the sustainability of green transportation.

title: Economic succession: an ecology-informed diagnostic framework for sustainable urban transformation
summary: Cities around the world face the difficult task of transforming their economies to decarbonize, use resources more efficiently, strengthen resilience, and broaden access to opportunity. Yet a transition that progresses in one city may stall
content: Cities around the world face the difficult task of transforming their economies to decarbonize, use resources more efficiently, strengthen resilience, and broaden access to opportunity. Yet a transition that progresses in one city may stall in another, and urban economics offers limited practical guidance for explaining why. To address this gap, this Conceptual Analysis develops urban economic succession as a middle-range framework for ordered but non-deterministic change in an urban economy's portfolio of activities. It translates the causal architecture of ecological succession into six economically observable components: opportunity availability, access to potential activities, local capability fit, interactions among activities, historical legacies and feedback, and extra-local connectivity. The framework brings together insights from sectoral transition, urban scaling, relatedness, economic complexity, production networks, and urban metabolism, while distinguishing changes in economic composition from judgments about what counts as sustainable. Five falsifiable propositions and a seven-step diagnostic workflow show how it can identify different barriers to green industrial diversification, circular production, low-carbon buildings, resilience, and other sustainable transformations. The framework does not treat cities as biological ecosystems, assume that urban economies follow a universal sequence, or equate greater internal cycling with greater sustainability. Instead, it offers a comparative research program for identifying recurrent transition pathways, explaining why cities depart from them, and matching interventions to the specific constraints operating in particular city-regions.

title: From Bulk Hygroscopicity to Nanoscale Water Activity: Breakdown of Continuum Theories in Sub-4 nm Secondary Organic Aerosols
summary: Interactions between water and organic molecules in sub-10 nm clusters surrounded by air play a key role in the chemistry and microphysics of secondary organic aerosol (SOA). However, water-organic interactions in such small clusters are di
content: Interactions between water and organic molecules in sub-10 nm clusters surrounded by air play a key role in the chemistry and microphysics of secondary organic aerosol (SOA). However, water-organic interactions in such small clusters are difficult to probe experimentally and remain poorly constrained. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations to examine morphology, molecular interactions, and water evaporation energetics of nanoclusters formed by nine representative SOA compounds across sizes and water contents. Nanocluster water affinity depends on size and water content, with distinct controlling mechanisms emerging during RH-driven drying. At high and moderate water contents, clusters larger than 4 nm follow a Kelvin baseline based on their bulk-mixture surface tension. In contrast, sub-4 nm organic-shell clusters sometimes retain water much less strongly than expected based on the Kelvin relation as their phase-mixing state changes with cluster size. At low water content, loss of water-network connectivity fragments the water domain into isolated pockets, shifting control of water retention to specific water-organic and water–water interactions, ionic coordination, and steric accessibility, producing species-dependent water affinity that bulk hygroscopicity cannot predict. These results identify where continuum descriptions break down and inform the representation of water in SOA nanoclusters in atmospheric models.

title: A Visual Analysis of the Uneven Contribution Towards Sustainable Climate Action: An Analysis of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 13
source: International Journal of Sustainable Development Goals
summary: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita is a measure of a country's economic capacity. Hence, the correlation between GDP pc and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the present study, Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG 13), provid
content: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita is a measure of a country's economic capacity. Hence, the correlation between GDP pc and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the present study, Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG 13), provides a clear indication of the extent to which individual countries comply with the goal. SDG 13 comprises four subgoals: CO₂ emissions from fossil-fuel combustion and cement production; greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions embodied in imports; and CO₂ emissions embodied in fossil-fuel exports. The fourth goal, addressing carbon prices, is not studied due to missing data. All three studied components should be considered to give a truthful picture of the single country’s contribution to climate change, as they all play a part in the overall picture in relation to sustainability and, as such, an indication where, mainly the more affluent countries, should focus to achieve better compliance with the SDG, in this respect not neglecting the ethical issues of not complying.

title: Exchange rate dynamics and economic growth in Bangladesh: Revisiting the evidence through the real effective exchange rate
summary: This study revisits the relationship between exchange rate dynamics and economic growth in Bangladesh, with particular emphasis on the real effective exchange rate (REER) rather than the nominal exchange rate. Using annual data from 1975 to
content: This study revisits the relationship between exchange rate dynamics and economic growth in Bangladesh, with particular emphasis on the real effective exchange rate (REER) rather than the nominal exchange rate. Using annual data from 1975 to 2024, the study examines the relationship between REER and economic growth while incorporating key macroeconomic factors, namely world gross domestic product (GDP), interest rates, money supply, and inflation. The autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) framework bounds testing approach, and the error correction model are used to assess the long-run and short-run relationships among the variables, while the Toda–Yamamoto causality test is applied to determine the direction of causality. The results show that REER appreciation is associated with higher GDP growth in the short run but lower GDP growth in the long run. In addition, the causality analysis indicates a unidirectional relationship running from the REER to GDP growth. These findings highlight the time-sensitive role of exchange rate dynamics in shaping economic growth in Bangladesh and offer useful insights for policymakers.

title: Wetland restoration enhances ecological quality in urbanizing regions
summary: Abstract Introduction Rapid urbanization and climate change drive widespread wetland degradation, yet it remains unclear whether wetland restoration improves ecological quality (EQ), a composite indicator reflecting vegetation, thermal, hyd
content: Abstract Introduction Rapid urbanization and climate change drive widespread wetland degradation, yet it remains unclear whether wetland restoration improves ecological quality (EQ), a composite indicator reflecting vegetation, thermal, hydrological, environmental, and soil conditions at regional scales in highly urbanized landscapes. Objectives This study aimed to quantify the spatiotemporal dynamics of wetland extent and EQ in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region, assess the contribution of wetland restoration to EQ improvement, and disentangle its effects from climatic, edaphic, topographic, and anthropogenic influences. Methods Using annual 30‐m Landsat‐based wetland maps and 500‐m EQ data (2001–2021), we quantified wetland dynamics and restoration effects using regression, spatial comparisons, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Model. Results Areas with expanding wetland coverage showed improved EQ, with every 1% increase in wetland area corresponding to a 0.034 rise in EQ. Wetland restoration was especially effective in core areas, substantially enhancing local EQ. Although indirect effects of climate, soil, terrain, and human disturbance were detected, they did not weaken the positive relationship between wetland restoration and EQ improvement. Wetland loss was most pronounced in coastal and near‐coastal areas, and some regions lost wetlands completely. In contrast, inland areas exhibited a moderate increase in wetland coverage, with the average wetland fraction increasing by 2.18%. Notably, a shift in wetland dynamics was observed after 2015, with the previous declining trend reversing. Conclusions These findings highlighted the pivotal role of wetland restoration in enhancing EQ.

title: Pitfalls in industrial policy
summary: The term “industrial policy” refers to government interventions with market outcomes in economic activity. By the 1990s, advanced countries had rejected almost all industrial policies and relied on competition policy and the free market. Bu
content: The term “industrial policy” refers to government interventions with market outcomes in economic activity. By the 1990s, advanced countries had rejected almost all industrial policies and relied on competition policy and the free market. But recently, industrial policy has become more popular. This paper covers some of the cautions applicable to industrial policy. Crucially important is the need for careful evaluation of proposed interventions, prevention of political interventions in management and engineering decisions, and ongoing willingness to evaluate performance in targets of industrial policy relative to intended purposes.

title: Optimizing Stocking Density for Enhanced Tilapia and Lettuce Production in NFT Aquaponics
summary: Water is an essential resource in arid regions; therefore, its management and use must be rational. Aquaponics, which integrates aquaculture and hydroponics, represents an innovative approach to efficient water use, particularly in arid env
content: Water is an essential resource in arid regions; therefore, its management and use must be rational. Aquaponics, which integrates aquaculture and hydroponics, represents an innovative approach to efficient water use, particularly in arid environments. The objective of this study was to determine the effect of fish stocking density on the growth performance of lettuce (Lactuca sativa) and Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) in a nutrient film technique (NFT)-based aquaponic system under arid conditions. A randomized block design was adopted with three fish stocking densities (1.5, 3.0, and 4.5 kg m-³), expressed as Nile tilapia biomass per unit volume of water. Water temperature remained within the optimal range across all treatments and did not differ significantly among them. However, pH and dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations were significantly influenced by stocking density, with DO concentrations decreasing as stocking density increased. Higher stocking densities also resulted in increased nitrate, nitrite, and total ammonia nitrogen concentrations, whereas potassium and soluble reactive phosphorus concentrations remained stable. Tilapia reared at the lowest stocking density (1.5 kg m-³) attained significantly greater final weight, weight gain, and specific growth rate, whereas survival rates did not differ significantly among treatments. In contrast, lettuce grown at the highest fish stocking density (4.5 kg m-³) had significantly greater biomass, head weight, and leaf and root lengths, possibly due to greater nutrient availability. These findings highlight the need to balance fish and plant production objectives to optimize the efficiency of NFT-based aquaponic systems.

title: Tryptophan-induced nanometrization and hydrophobization of Fe 2+ /Fe 3+ oxyhydroxide green rust crystals enable their insertion into lipid particles
summary: Compartmentalization and metabolic activity are recognized as intrinsic and essential to both extant life and the first protocells. Minerals found in early-Earth hydrothermal settings, such as the Fe 2+/3+ oxyhydroxide green rust (GR), are
content: Compartmentalization and metabolic activity are recognized as intrinsic and essential to both extant life and the first protocells. Minerals found in early-Earth hydrothermal settings, such as the Fe 2+/3+ oxyhydroxide green rust (GR), are not only expected to have promoted the formation and assembly of amphiphiles into vesicles, but also to have acted as precursors of current membrane-embedded bioenergetic enzymes. In a previous paper, we identified nanometric size and surface hydrophobicity as two crucial properties for the embedment of GRCO 3 crystals in amphiphile-based vesicles, and demonstrated their acquisition upon exposure to two components of early hydrothermal settings: nickel and tryptophan. Here, we used lipids as model amphiphiles to systematically investigate how the evolution of size and hydrophobicity parameters in GRCO 3 crystals affects their interaction with free lipids and lipid-based particles, and identify the nature of the resulting GRCO 3 -lipid hybrid systems. By leveraging cryo-electron microscopy as well as zeta potential and Laurdan generalized polarization measurements, we demonstrate that modulations of two parameters are sufficient to drastically modify the fate of GRCO 3 -lipid hybrid systems. Size alone defines the directionality of adsorption processes between electrostatically-compatible GRCO 3 crystals and liposomes, yielding intricate mineral-organic interfaces. Subsequent variations in the surface hydrophobicity of the crystals not only orient the assembly of interacting lipids towards either liposomes or lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), but also enable their embedding within the hydrophobic core of both these lipid-based particles. These results suggest that GRCO 3 would have played numerous roles in the emergence of the first energized protocells, from promoting the synthesis of amphiphiles and their assembly into vesicles to embedding within the latter, thus enhancing them with redox and proto-metabolic properties. These new hybrid systems constitute both ideal tools to experimentally assess the proton-coupled electron transfers that were theorized to happen in the interlayers of GR, and promising platforms for therapeutical or depollution applications.

title: From reform to compliance: Unveiling the efficacy of green finance policy in curbing firm financial fraud
summary: As an institutional arrangement transitioning from blueprint to practice, green finance holds significant potential in shaping firm behavior; however, its mechanisms remain underexplored. Using a multi-period DID design and taking the estab
content: As an institutional arrangement transitioning from blueprint to practice, green finance holds significant potential in shaping firm behavior; however, its mechanisms remain underexplored. Using a multi-period DID design and taking the establishment of the Pilot Zones for Green Finance Reform and Innovation as a quasi-natural experiment, this study explores the effect of the pilot policy on firm financial fraud. The results indicate that the pilot policy significantly reduces firm financial fraud, with the policy effect exhibiting a certain degree of lag. This finding remains valid after a series of robustness tests, including variable substitution, alternative model specification, and PSM-DID analysis. The pilot policy effectively targets the core elements of the fraud triangle, reducing the motive for firm financial fraud by lowering firm risk-taking and negative public sentiment pressure while also reducing the opportunity for fraud by alleviating information asymmetry. This study provides a reference for evaluating the effectiveness of green finance policies and offers insights into using institutional means to combat illegal firm activity.

title: Beyond the Conditional Mean: Digital Economy Development and Logistics Carbon Intensity—Evidence from Chinese Provincial Panel Quantile Analysis
summary: Whether the relationship between digital economy development and logistics carbon intensity varies across the conditional distribution cannot be determined from average estimates alone. Using panel data for 30 Chinese provincial-level regio
