title: BIOLOGICAL, NUTRITIONAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS AFFECTING GROWTH AND PHYSIOLOGICAL PRODUCTIVITY IN POULTRY: A REVIEW
source: Jana Nexus Journal of Health and Medicine
summary: Poultry work period and productivity are of paramount importance for a successful, efficient and sustainable contemporary poultry industry. The magnitude of genetic progress achieved in poultry during recent decades, which has improved grow
content: Poultry work period and productivity are of paramount importance for a successful, efficient and sustainable contemporary poultry industry. The magnitude of genetic progress achieved in poultry during recent decades, which has improved growth potential, is primarily limited by biological, nutritional and environmental constraints. This paper provides an overview of the recently available information of the biological drivers affecting growth, primarily the genetic make-up, endocrine balance, muscle development, immunity and gut health. It emphasizes the significance of nutrition: energy consortium of the diet and balanced provision of amino acids, lipid quality and functioning, and sufficiency of micronutrients and applications of functional feed additives. Furthermore, attention is paid to other environmental effectors such as temperature, humidity, air quality and stocking density as well as lighting programs housing system and hygiene on growth performance and feed efficiency. The evidence support that the integrated management system will provide optimal performance in poultry through precision nutrition and a controlled environment to optimize the genetic potential. Knowledge about the mechanism these interacting factors can be impacted is crucial in elevating productivity, animal welfare and sustainability within poultry production.

title: Thermostability and pH Differentiation in Geobacillus Hydrolases: A Comparative Perspective
summary: Thermostable enzymes are central to high-temperature industrial processes because they combine catalytic efficiency with structural resilience under demanding conditions. Among thermophilic bacteria, Geobacillus has emerged as a prominent s
content: Thermostable enzymes are central to high-temperature industrial processes because they combine catalytic efficiency with structural resilience under demanding conditions. Among thermophilic bacteria, Geobacillus has emerged as a prominent source of industrially relevant enzymes, particularly hydrolases such as proteases, lipases, and carbohydrate-active enzymes. Although many individual enzymes have been characterized in detail, comparative synthesis across catalytic classes within the genus remains limited. In this review, we integrate biochemical data and structural evidence to explore whether thermostability in Geobacillus reflects isolated enzyme-specific traits or recurring functional patterns across enzyme classes. Reported Tmax and pHmax values from purified and partially purified hydrolases were systematically compiled to assess class-level tendencies. Temperature optima cluster within a relatively narrow thermophilic range across enzyme groups, supporting high-temperature activity as a common feature within the genus. In contrast, pH optima display clearer functional differentiation, with proteases and lipases consistently shifted toward alkaline values relative to carbohydrate-active hydrolases. Recurrent stabilizing elements, including reinforced hydrophobic cores, expanded electrostatic interaction networks, and a balanced rigidity-flexibility profile, are observed across multiple enzyme classes, indicating shared structural trends rather than independent enzyme-specific variation. By situating catalytic optima within a comparative framework and relating them to shared structural determinants, this review provides a comparative interpretation of patterns observed across Geobacillus-derived enzymes, linking structure, catalysis, and functional adaptation.

title: Avaricia: concentrar el poder, los datos y los beneficios
summary: Technological greed appears when the adoption of artificial intelligence concentrates power, data, and benefits while distributing costs, labor, and dependency unevenly.This chapter examines the conditions needed to evaluate a fair distribu
content: Technological greed appears when the adoption of artificial intelligence concentrates power, data, and benefits while distributing costs, labor, and dependency unevenly.This chapter examines the conditions needed to evaluate a fair distribution of value in institutional settings.The analysis connects infrastructure, investment, data, human labor, access, maintenance, portability, and exit capacity, avoiding the assumption that availability of a tool is equivalent to an effective ability to benefit from it.It distinguishes partial efficiency, task productivity, and distributed benefit, as well as global concentration and local dependence on providers.Studies of literacy, participation, and well-being provide situated questions and qualify universal promises; differences among countries, institutions, and territories make it inappropriate to treat AI adoption as a homogeneous process.The conceptual synthesis identifies capacities to understand a technological relationship, influence its conditions, and modify it when it produces unjustified burdens.It also examines who contributes data, labor, infrastructure, and knowledge, and who retains control over outputs and service continuity.An illustrative procurement scenario for student guidance shows how to review data purpose, accessibility, portability, oversight workload, and the possibility of changing providers.Its implementation has not been evaluated.The chapter concludes that defensible adoption must explain who receives benefits, who bears costs, and what mechanisms can correct their distribution.Technological justice requires access, but also bargaining power, understanding, practical alternatives, and institutional capacity to prevent dependency from becoming a persistent form of inequality.The analysis therefore links fairness to both distribution and the practical capacity of institutions and users to influence the technological arrangements on which they depend.

title: Analytical Strategies for the Determination of Rhodamine B: A Review of Extraction Techniques and Detection Methods
summary: Rhodamine B is a xanthene dye with demonstrated genotoxic and other adverse toxicological effects in experimental studies, banned from cosmetics and food, yet it remains widely and illegally used for its low cost and vivid color. This revie
content: Rhodamine B is a xanthene dye with demonstrated genotoxic and other adverse toxicological effects in experimental studies, banned from cosmetics and food, yet it remains widely and illegally used for its low cost and vivid color. This review examines analytical methods published between 1998 and 2025 for determining Rhodamine B in cosmetic and related matrices. Extraction strategies are traced from classical solid-phase and cloud-point extraction through miniaturized liquid-phase and dispersive liquid–liquid microextraction to greener alternatives such as deep eutectic and supramolecular solvents and magnetic nanomaterial-based sorbents. Detection platforms span UV-Vis spectrophotometry and fluorimetry, liquid chromatography, capillary and microchip electrophoresis, high-performance thin layer chromatography (HPTLC), and digital image colorimetry. Reported methods typically achieve sub-µg L−1 to ng mL−1 detection limits, preconcentration factors up to several hundred-fold, and recoveries of 85–105%, with recent studies increasingly benchmarked against various greenness metrics. However, validation practices remain inconsistent, and no unified guideline is widely applied. This review synthesizes these developments to highlight the field’s shift toward greener, nanomaterial-enabled, field-deployable methods and to identify standardized validation as a priority for future research.

title: Harnessing Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria for the Biocontrol of Phytopathogens in Sustainable Agriculture: A Review
summary: Plant diseases significantly reduce worldwide agricultural production, causing yield declines of 21-30% for major crops, while excessive use of pesticides and chemicals poses serious health and environmental risks. Plant growth-promoting rh
content: Plant diseases significantly reduce worldwide agricultural production, causing yield declines of 21-30% for major crops, while excessive use of pesticides and chemicals poses serious health and environmental risks. Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) offer an environmentally acceptable, efficient biocontrol approach against phytopathogens. Through direct mechanisms, such as the synthesis of phytohormones and nutrients, and indirect mechanisms, including the synthesis of antibiotics and siderophores and the establishment of induced systemic resistance (ISR), PGPR support plant development and suppress infections. This paper examines the role of PGPR in sustainable agriculture, focusing on their interactions with plant roots, rhizosphere dynamics, and the rhizosphere microbiome, as well as their biocontrol efficacy against fungal, bacterial, and nematode diseases. Key mechanisms include niche exclusion, competition for resources, and the release of antimicrobial compounds. Large-scale PGPR application is hindered by limitations such as inconsistent field performance, environmental acceptability concerns, and regulatory issues. Breakthroughs in microbial ecology, molecular biology, and bioinformatics offer new opportunities to optimize PGPR formulations and enhance crop-specific compatibility. Future studies should focus on developing microbial consortia, enhancing their stress tolerance, and integrating them into organic farming systems to achieve sustainable biocontrol. Within the framework of the green revolution, sustainable agriculture can increase crop yields, enhance soil health, and reduce the use of synthetic agrochemicals by leveraging PGPR-plant associations. This review highlights the promise of PGPR for the biological control of agricultural diseases and discusses the challenges and future directions for its global commercialization.

title: Calculating Distributive Justice: Reconstruction of Fidyah Calculation Based on Rice Price Index (IHPR) in the Perspective of Contemporary Fiqh and Humanist Economics
source: International Journal of Islamic Thought and Humanities
summary: This research aims to reconstruct the calculation of fidyah based on the Rice Price Index (IHPR) by integrating contemporary fiqh perspectives, applied mathematics, and humanist economics to maintain the real value equivalence of fidyah ami
content: This research aims to reconstruct the calculation of fidyah based on the Rice Price Index (IHPR) by integrating contemporary fiqh perspectives, applied mathematics, and humanist economics to maintain the real value equivalence of fidyah amidst food price fluctuations. Employing a qualitative documentary case study design, the methodology utilizes content analysis, comparative document evaluation, and mathematical formulation of institutional guidelines, fiqh texts, and empirical rice pricing data. The core novelty lies in shifting from static nominal-based calculations to a dynamic value-equivalence model using the index adjustment formula , ensuring transparent and proportional updates. The findings indicate that fidyah functions as an essential instrument for Islamic socioeconomic redistribution rather than a mere ritual substitution, bridging normative obligations with economic realities. The implications suggest that religious and zakat management institutions must adopt adaptive, data-driven determination mechanisms to strengthen transparency, accountability, and distributive justice in alignment with maqāṣid al-syarī'ah principles.

title: Validating national reuse indicators from regional demolition data: a Swedish example
summary: Construction accounts for a substantial share of global emissions and waste, highlighting the need to shift from linear to circular resource flows and to prioritise deconstruction and reuse over demolition and disposal. Enabling this transi
content: Construction accounts for a substantial share of global emissions and waste, highlighting the need to shift from linear to circular resource flows and to prioritise deconstruction and reuse over demolition and disposal. Enabling this transition requires reliable methods for identifying and quantifying products embedded in existing buildings. This Swedish study examines whether key performance indicators (KPIs) derived from demolition‑permit documentation can be generalised across regions to support product‑level stock estimation for circular construction. Using a bottom‑up method, regional similarities and differences were assessed using data on product quantities from preschool and multifamily‑building demolitions (n = 38) in Umeå and Stockholm. Six product categories were compiled from demolition permits and compared statistically with Greater Gothenburg values. The results show that while several products exhibit modest regional variation, others—gypsum boards and clay roof tiles in preschools, and wooden windows in multifamily buildings—display statistically significant differences, indicating that national KPIs would misrepresent regional building stocks. Where no significant differences were found, regional datasets were aggregated to propose national KPIs. Improved demolition‑permit documentation would enhance KPI robustness, underscoring the need for standardised, higher quality data. Expanding datasets and validating the results against demolition outcomes will be essential to strengthen KPI applicability. PRACTICE RELEVANCE When can national KPIs serve as a reliable forecast of reusable building products from demolition? When must regional differences be considered? For products with limited regional variation, such as roofing felt and timber frameworks, national KPIs can inform circular-construction planning. In contrast, gypsum boards, clay roof tiles and certain window types show substantial regional differences, likely driven by construction traditions and documentation practices, making region-specific KPIs necessary. Until greater stability from further data collection is demonstrated, regional KPIs should remain the basis for quantifying products, with national indicators applied only where consistency is evident. To improve data quality, policymakers should promote harmonised pre‑demolition audits, standardised reporting and digital documentation. Practitioners can use KPIs in early‑stage planning, while municipalities could integrate them into permit processes and make the data publicly accessible to strengthen regional reuse capacity.

title: Optimizing Logistics Ecosystems: Evaluating the Performance of Smart Port Enterprises
summary: Abstract The rapid development of smart ports has revolutionized the maritime industry, leveraging advanced technologies and data analytics to enhance efficiency, productivity, and sustainability. However, assessing and optimizing the perfo
content: Abstract The rapid development of smart ports has revolutionized the maritime industry, leveraging advanced technologies and data analytics to enhance efficiency, productivity, and sustainability. However, assessing and optimizing the performance of smart ports remains a complex challenge. This study proposes a comprehensive framework for evaluating and improving smart port efficiency using a Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) approach. The methodology integrates the Malmquist Index, which measures productivity changes over time, and the Super Slacks-Based Measure (Super SBM) model, which identifies specific areas of inefficiency. The study aims to assess changes in smart ports' overall efficiency and productivity, identify sources of inefficiency, and propose targeted optimization strategies. The research methodology involves a comprehensive literature review, with a particular emphasis on the application of Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) models in the logistics sector. The empirical analysis uses data from a representative sample of smart ports, and the findings are examined in light of their implications for port management and decision-making. The results reveal that Evergreen Marine Corp (P6) and Westports Holdings Bhd (P9) consistently exhibited high efficiency levels throughout the study period. This observation underscores their remarkable resilience and adaptability as they navigate evolving market conditions. The sustained efficiency performance of these two ports serves as a testament to their robust operational strategies and effective resource management practices. The proposed framework offers a data-driven approach for port authorities, logistics service providers, and policymakers to benchmark performance, identify best practices, and allocate resources effectively. The study advances smart port research by offering a novel methodological approach and practical insights for optimizing logistics systems in the era of digitalization.

title: Organo-mineral Fertilizer: Waste to Wealth Economy
summary: The document discusses the urgent need for sustainable agricultural practices to ensure global food security amid rising population and rising fertilizer costs. It highlights the environmental and economic challenges posed by conventional m
content: The document discusses the urgent need for sustainable agricultural practices to ensure global food security amid rising population and rising fertilizer costs. It highlights the environmental and economic challenges posed by conventional mineral fertilizers, emphasizing the potential of organo-mineral fertilizers (OMFs) as eco-friendly alternatives. OMFs combine organic waste materials with mineral nutrients to improve soil health, enhance nutrient use efficiency, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The paper explores various organic feedstocks and processing techniques for OMF production, noting their benefits in waste valorization and circular economy models. It underscores the importance of technological advancements, regulatory frameworks, and scientific validation for widespread adoption of OMFs. The authors advocate for further research into OMF effectiveness across diverse soil types and conditions to promote sustainable, balanced nutrient management in agriculture.

title: “The Guy(s) from California”: Race, the Tax Code, and the Relational Geographies of Rental Housing in Memphis
source: Annals of the American Association of Geographers
summary: This article examines how high net worth, individual investors from coastal markets have reshaped the rental market in Memphis, Tennessee, and could be playing a growing role in housing markets across the United States. Drawing on interview
content: This article examines how high net worth, individual investors from coastal markets have reshaped the rental market in Memphis, Tennessee, and could be playing a growing role in housing markets across the United States. Drawing on interviews with local “turn-key” real estate companies and a computational analysis of property data across Memphis, I show how the historical trajectory of racial capitalism, coupled with the fallout of the 2008 financial crisis, has enabled local property managers to channel out-of-state investment from high-cost markets like California into Memphis neighborhoods. Californian investors, I show, own roughly 10 percent of the Memphis single-family rental market and accounted for nearly 24 percent of all out-of-state home sales between 2020 and 2022. I argue that this form of financialization maps onto two dueling currents in the political economy of housing. First, “the guy(s) from California” capitalize on the city’s racial appreciation gap, funneling speculative investment into the uneven, relational geographies of value between housing markets in Memphis and high-cost, coastal markets like California. Second, it shows how fiscal geographies have shaped this relational connection, initially through monetary policy that allowed coastal investors to cheaply debt-finance rental property, and now through provisions within the tax code that allow for the deferral of capital gains tax on high-value property sales in California. The article concludes by questioning whether the rapid appreciation and concentration of wealth in California (and other coastal housing markets) might be driving speculation in markets across the Midwest and Southeast.

title: Agroecological practices, perceived benefits, and determinants of adoption in the Yayu Coffee Forest Biosphere Reserve, Southwest Ethiopia
summary: Agroecology offers a promising pathway for reconciling forest conservation with rural livelihoods in biodiversity-rich tropical landscapes, yet empirical evidence on the breadth, intensity, and determinants of adoption remains limited, part
content: Agroecology offers a promising pathway for reconciling forest conservation with rural livelihoods in biodiversity-rich tropical landscapes, yet empirical evidence on the breadth, intensity, and determinants of adoption remains limited, particularly in UNESCO biosphere reserves. This study investigates agroecological practices, perceived contributions, and determinants of adoption in the Yayu Coffee Forest Biosphere Reserve (YCFBR), Southwest Ethiopia. A cross-sectional concurrent mixed-methods design was employed, combining 293 randomly selected households, complemented by key informant interviews, focus group discussions, and field observations. Binary logistic regression identified determinants of adoption (extensive margin), while ordinal logistic regression examined adoption intensity using the Agroecological Adoption Index (AAI) (intensive margin). Number of Practices Adopted (NPA), Weighted Adoption Intensity (WAI), and Duration of Adoption (DUR) provided complementary insights into adoption breadth, intensity, and persistence. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically to contextualize quantitative findings. Results showed that 72% of households adopted at least one agroecological practice, including coffee agroforestry, homegarden agroforestry, soil and water conservation, climate-smart agriculture, intercropping, crop rotation, mixed tree planting, afforestation and reforestation, organic soil fertility management, and biological pest and disease management. Adoption intensity varied: 34.6% low, 41.2% moderate, and 24.2% high. Practices were perceived to improve soil fertility, biodiversity conservation, climate resilience, forest management, and livelihood diversification while reducing pressure on natural forests and strengthening ecological connectivity and adaptive capacity. Sex, education, farm size, extension services, training, credit access, and cooperative membership significantly determined adoption and intensity, whereas age, household size, farming experience, and distance to forest were non-significant. Agroecology provides a multifunctional, context-specific pathway for advancing sustainable forest management, biodiversity conservation, and livelihood resilience. Strengthening agroecology-oriented extension, gender-responsive training, access to finance, indigenous knowledge integration, and policy mainstreaming are essential for long-term environmental sustainability and community resilience in the YCFBR and comparable forest-dependent landscapes.

title: Statistical Modeling of yarn quality in hemp-recycled Fiber blends: A textile waste valorization approach for circular economy
summary: Harnessing eco-friendly and renewable fibers in textiles is increasingly important for advancing circular and resource-efficient production. Hemp, a regenerative and low-input fiber, offers a sustainable alternative to conventional cotton w
content: Harnessing eco-friendly and renewable fibers in textiles is increasingly important for advancing circular and resource-efficient production. Hemp, a regenerative and low-input fiber, offers a sustainable alternative to conventional cotton with comparable textile functionality and lower environmental impacts. Meanwhile, incorporating recycled cotton (r-cotton) supports circularity by valorizing textile waste and maintaining cotton fibers within the textile value chain. However, the coarse and stiff nature of hemp, coupled with the shorter length and higher nep content of r-cotton, can impair spinnability, necessitating blending with virgin cotton. Herein, an eco-conscious tri-blend yarn comprising hemp, r-cotton, and virgin cotton was developed to maximize the utilization of hemp and r-cotton while maintaining yarn quality suitable for fabric production. Because identifying an optimal blend ratio through conventional trial-and-error approaches is complex and time-consuming, MATLAB was used to generate a comprehensive set of blend combinations, while artificial neural network (ANN) and multiple linear regression (MLR) models were employed to establish relationships between fiber composition and yarn properties. The ANN was evaluated using repeated composition-grouped leave-one-composition-out cross-validation, whereas MLR demonstrated better predictive accuracy and was therefore selected for multi-objective optimization. Experimental validation showed prediction errors of approximately ≤5% for five of the six yarn properties, confirming the reliability of the optimization approach. The optimized blend achieved approximately 42% combined utilization of hemp and r-cotton while maintaining desirable yarn quality and reducing manufacturing cost by around 7.7% compared with the hemp/virgin-cotton reference yarn. Overall, the developed tri-blend yarn provides a practical pathway for balancing renewable and circular fiber utilization, yarn performance, and economic feasibility in textile production.

title: The Accountability Pathway: Linking ESG Disclosure, Integrated Reporting Quality, and Value Creation in Southeast Asia
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how listed firms in Southeast Asia translate internal environmental, social, and governance (ESG) commitments into accountable practices, transparent reporting, and organizational value creation. Focusing on fir
content: ABSTRACT This study examines how listed firms in Southeast Asia translate internal environmental, social, and governance (ESG) commitments into accountable practices, transparent reporting, and organizational value creation. Focusing on firms in the ASEAN‐6 countries over the period 2020–2024, the study proposes and empirically tests a framework in which ESG disclosure enhances integrated reporting quality and, ultimately, value creation, as measured by investment efficiency, while accounting for macro‐level energy transition pressures and firm‐level corporate governance mechanisms. Using panel data from 2605 firms, the study employs maximum likelihood structural equation modeling within a moderated mediation framework, while controlling for country‐level fixed effects. The findings indicate that ESG disclosure significantly enhances integrated reporting quality and that reporting quality serves as a key mechanism through which ESG disclosure contributes to value creation. The results further demonstrate that the accountability pathway is context‐dependent: energy transition pressures strengthen the importance of sustainability accountability, whereas corporate governance influences firms' capacity to implement ESG strategies effectively. This study contributes to the literature by conceptualizing corporate social responsibility as a multistage process that links ESG knowledge, disclosure and reporting infrastructure, and value creation. The findings offer practical implications for managers, investors, and policymakers seeking to enhance corporate transparency and promote sustainable capital allocation across ASEAN economies.

title: From trade-off to paradox: a configurational theorizing and “quantum” approach to the resilience–sustainability tension in global sourcing
summary: Abstract Global sourcing is increasingly caught between two persistent pressures: to be sustainable and resilient. While this relationship is often framed as a trade-off, we draw on paradox theory to conceptualize it as a persistent paradox
content: Abstract Global sourcing is increasingly caught between two persistent pressures: to be sustainable and resilient. While this relationship is often framed as a trade-off, we draw on paradox theory to conceptualize it as a persistent paradox, especially for MNEs coordinating complex supplier networks. Most paradox research addresses either how tensions are embedded in organizational systems or how they are socially constructed by managers, but rarely both. Drawing on the "quantum" approach to paradox, we bridge these ontological and epistemological perspectives, arguing that the resilience–sustainability tension is rooted in the structure of global sourcing systems and made salient through how managers interpret and combine sourcing decisions. Following a configurational roadmap of three stages—scoping, linking, and naming—we theorize five systemic sourcing factors (location choice, supplier redundancy, inventory buffer, green certification, and the sustainability premium) and examine how they are evaluated by 72 Italian procurement managers through a factorial survey, a fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, and interviews. Managers favor coherent bundles over standalone levers, combining certification-based sustainability assurance alongside resilience-oriented levers such as proximity, redundancy, and buffers. We conceptualize three archetypal sourcing logics— integrator , resilience-first , and cost-only —offering managers a practical vocabulary for framing and legitimating sourcing choices when both pressures collide.

title: Thioiminium Salt Catalyzed Chemoselective Late Stage Halogenation Using N-Halosuccinimides
summary: C−H halogenation plays a central role in drug discovery. It enables rapid molecular diversification and provides a direct means to tune the metabolic and biological properties of drug candidates. However, selective halogenation of less reac
content: C−H halogenation plays a central role in drug discovery. It enables rapid molecular diversification and provides a direct means to tune the metabolic and biological properties of drug candidates. However, selective halogenation of less reactive arenes remains challenging, particularly when aromatic and benzylic C−H bonds coexist in the same molecule. Here, we introduce a thioiminium salt-based Lewisbase catalyst that activates readily available N-halosuccinimides for selective aromatic and benzylic halogenation with complementary control. Notably, the method enables late-stage aromatic bromination of natural products, pharmaceuticals, peptides and heterocycles and can be extended to aromatic chlorination using N-chlorosuccinimide. The practicality of this method is demonstrated by four gramscale syntheses, catalyst recycling and post-synthetic diversification. Mechanistic and computational studies reveal distinct electrophilic and radical pathways, with the catalyst counter anion acting as a molecular switch for chemoselectivity between aromatic and benzylic bromination.

title: A review of remote sensing for agricultural drought: technologies, indices, modelling advances and future prospects
summary: Agricultural drought is a complex hazard that jeopardises food security and progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed English-language literature published between 2015 and 2025, focusing on
content: Agricultural drought is a complex hazard that jeopardises food security and progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed English-language literature published between 2015 and 2025, focusing on Remote Sensing (RS)-driven agricultural drought monitoring and prediction. Eligible studies were identified from the Web of Science and Scopus databases (last searched in August 2025); review articles, duplicates, and irrelevant studies were excluded, resulting in 181 articles. This review critically examined the evolution of sensors, drought indices, modelling approaches, and emerging technologies used to assess agricultural drought across diverse agro-ecological regions. Specifically, we (1) systematically evaluated the use of optical, thermal, and microwave RS platforms, along with satellite-based, model-based, and reanalysis products for agricultural drought monitoring; (2) reviewed widely used RS-based drought indices, including single indices grouped into nine categories, as well as composite indices; (3) reviewed software or programming languages applied; (4) assessed the progression of modelling approaches from traditional statistical and time-series methods to machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) frameworks; and (5) examined validation strategies applied to agricultural drought assessment. The analysis reveals a growing research interest in this topic, with a strong geographic concentration in Asia, particularly China. Optical and thermal platforms (e.g. MODIS and Landsat) dominate the literature (~54%) due to their accessibility, followed by satellite-derived precipitation products (17%), while microwave soil-moisture missions remain underutilized (~7%). Regarding RS-based indices, most studies employed more than one index: 44% analysed multiple individual indices, 51% used composite indices (either alone or in combination with individual indices), and only 5% relied on a single index. Vegetation indices, such as NDVI, remain workhorses; however, their sensitivity to soil background effects and canopy saturation has driven increased adoption of thermal composites (e.g. VHI), as well as adaptive weighting schemes and principal component analysis-based approaches. Moreover, computational tools used in drought research can be broadly grouped into geospatial and RS platforms for large-scale data processing and analysis (e.g. QGIS, GEE), and general-purpose programming languages (e.g. R, Python) for model development and advanced analytics. Regarding the methodology, statistical and time-series approaches account for 64% of the reviewed studies, followed by ML models (20%) and DL methods (15%), while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) remains nascent. Techniques, such as random forests, support vector machines, and CNN and LSTM architectures, generally outperform traditional models but require large training datasets and raise concerns related to interpretability and ethics. title: Research on Human Resource Management and Training in Electric Power Companies
source: International journal of educational teaching and research.
summary: The current situation is that the Chinese electric power industry is entering an important stage of transformation: the in-depth construction of smart grids, the acceleration of the iteration of energy structures and the full implementation
content: The current situation is that the Chinese electric power industry is entering an important stage of transformation: the in-depth construction of smart grids, the acceleration of the iteration of energy structures and the full implementation of the "dual-carbon", the traditional power system will be transformed and upgraded comprehensively and profoundly into a new power system. Electric power companies, as the main body ensuring the national energy security and guaranteeing the stable operation of power grid, require new development needs such as intelligent production, digitalized operations, refined operation and maintenance and standardized safety control, which brings higher level challenges and demands on their human resource management systems and employee training mechanisms. In this paper, we systematically analysed the existing problems in human resource management and employee training in electric power companies, put forward corresponding optimization strategies which are scientific, digitalized and scenario-based to improve the talent cultivation system of electric power enterprises, matching the development of talent teams with the trends of smart grids and new energy industries, providing solid talent support for the high quality transformation and upgrading of the electric power industry and green and low-carbon development of the energy sector.

title: Agronomic and nutritional performance of lentil–hull‐less barley mixtures under temperate Swiss conditions: protein content, protein yield stability, β‐glucan content and separation ability
source: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
summary: Abstract BACKGROUND Intercropping of legumes with cereals enhances resilience, resource efficiency, and nutritional quality in food systems, yet few studies have integrated yield stability with grain quantity and post‐harvest processability
content: Abstract BACKGROUND Intercropping of legumes with cereals enhances resilience, resource efficiency, and nutritional quality in food systems, yet few studies have integrated yield stability with grain quantity and post‐harvest processability. Lentils ( Lens culinaris Medik.) and hull‐less barley ( Hordeum vulgare L. var. nudum ) represent a promising mixture for temperate climates. Here, we provide the first multi‐year evaluation of protein content, protein yield stability, β‐glucan concentration, and grain separation, across 3 years (2022–2024), two sites, and 22 treatments. RESULTS Mixed stands increased barley protein content by 18–26 g kg −1 dry matter (DM) compared with pure unfertilized and fertilized systems, whereas lentil protein content was marginally higher in pure stands. Mixed systems buffered environmental variability (Finlay–Wilkinson bᵢ ≈ 1.1), with variability substantially lower (CV = 38%) than in pure barley stands (63% CV), approaching that of pure lentil stability (29% CV). The lentil cultivar Beluga paired with the barley cultivar AF Cesar achieved the highest protein yield stability, recording a weighted absolute score of 94.5 via the AMMI (additive main effects and multiplicative interaction) yield stability index. β‐glucan content (17–76 g kg −1 DM) was highest in fertilized pure AF Cesar and was influenced by year and site. Grain separation showed partially high impurity levels (>1%), due to similar seed sizes, but mixtures with contrasting seed sizes (e.g., Beluga–AF Cesar) improved separation ( r = 0.38). CONCLUSION Intercropping of lentils with barley increases barley protein content and yield stability under Swiss conditions, providing the first evidence of effects on β‐glucan content and seed‐size‐driven impurity reduction. Selecting cultivar pairs with contrasting seed sizes and optimizing sowing time can improve both agronomic and post‐harvest performance in legume‐cereal systems. © 2026 The Author(s). title: The Transparency‐Capability Dilemma: Configuring Stakeholder‐Engagement to Overcome Scope‐3 Inertia in Net‐Zero Supply Chains
summary: ABSTRACT Scope‐3 decarbonisation is central to a credible net‐zero strategy. However, firms face a difficult transparency‐capability dilemma. They are under immense pressure to disclose supply chain emissions, while the collaborative capabi
content: ABSTRACT Scope‐3 decarbonisation is central to a credible net‐zero strategy. However, firms face a difficult transparency‐capability dilemma. They are under immense pressure to disclose supply chain emissions, while the collaborative capabilities needed to act are slow‐building, relational, and unevenly distributed across supplier systems. This paper explains how firms can configure stakeholder engagement so that Scope‐3 transparency supports collaborative decarbonisation rather than becoming a source of unmanaged exposure. Drawing on a structured conceptual review and interpretive synthesis, we develop a stakeholder engagement architecture comprising carbon‐intelligence sourcing, collaborative carbon co‐design, and carbon‐governance commons. It theorises these as interdependent engagement configurations, explaining how supplier emission information becomes decision‐useful carbon intelligence, how such intelligence supports collaborative implementation with suppliers, and how repeated collaboration can be stabilised through accountable governance. The paper develops propositions, diagnostic configurations, and boundary conditions explaining why Scope‐3 engagement may become substantively coupled, weakly coupled, or symbolically claimed.

title: Breaking Scaling Relations to Achieve an Electrochemical Potential Window Strategy for Highly Selective Urea Electrosynthesis From N 2 and CO 2
summary: ABSTRACT Electrochemical co‐reduction of nitrogen (N 2 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) under ambient conditions offers a sustainable route for urea synthesis, while this desirable pathway suffers from selectivity challenge because of an inferi
content: ABSTRACT Electrochemical co‐reduction of nitrogen (N 2 ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) under ambient conditions offers a sustainable route for urea synthesis, while this desirable pathway suffers from selectivity challenge because of an inferior competition with numerous parallel reactions. Available strategy to selectively boost urea electrosynthesis and suppress the competitive reactions is absent, because they share the same intermediates which are limited by the well‐established scaling relations. Herein, we design a multi‐site NbCo 3 intermetallic compound, which imposes a dynamic strain effect on intermediates to break the scaling relations, achieving to gather radical intermediates to participate in C−N coupling while preventing their further protonation. Based on constant potential density functional theory (CP‐DFT) computations, an electrochemical potential window is evolved that NbCo 3 (001) obtains a prior selectivity toward urea electrosynthesis when the electrode potential is below −0.25 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). This work provides an available strategy to improve the catalytic selectivity of urea electrosynthesis, which accelerates the development of highly efficient catalysts.

title: The Use of Nanoparticles for Enhanced Heavy Crude Oil Recovery
summary: Heavy crude is a type of crude oil possessing a high viscosity and density. It is usually produced from oil sands, and as the name suggests, it is heavy and hard to extract. It is referred to as “heavy” because it has a higher specific grav
content: Heavy crude is a type of crude oil possessing a high viscosity and density. It is usually produced from oil sands, and as the name suggests, it is heavy and hard to extract. It is referred to as “heavy” because it has a higher specific gravity and is also much denser when compared with conventional (light) crude. Although some variations still exist, heavy oil is classified as crude with API gravity less than 200. Light crude oil primarily produces fuels such as gasoline, diesel and aviation fuels, heavy crude (which also yields these transportation fuels) also provides feed stock for plastics, petrochemicals and road surfacing to name a few, therefore it is safe to say adequate heavy crude oil investment is necessary for the security of the oil and gas industry. Compared to its lighter counterpart, there is more unexploited heavy crude oil reserves around the world with several reasons responsible, most of which are associated with the difficulty encountered in recovering these heavy crude oils.

title: TURNING FIELD, SOIL, WEATHER AND CROP DATA INTO A PREDICTIVE CULTIVATION PLANNING PIPELINE FOR SMARTER AGRICULTURAL DECISIONS - (FARM2FORECAST)
source: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
summary: Farmers in India make most of their cultivation decisions, such as which crop to sow, when to sow it, how much fertiliser to apply, and when to irrigate, on the basis of experience and advice passed on informally. These decisions are becomi
content: Farmers in India make most of their cultivation decisions, such as which crop to sow, when to sow it, how much fertiliser to apply, and when to irrigate, on the basis of experience and advice passed on informally. These decisions are becoming harder because rainfall has grown less predictable, soil fertility varies considerably between neighbouring fields, and market prices change from season to season. This paper presents Farm2Forecast, a data pipeline and predictive analytics system that combines field records, soil test results, weather observations and forecasts, and historical crop data to support cultivation planning for small and medium farms. The system collects data from several sources. Field details such as location, area, irrigation source, and past crops are registered by farmers or extension workers through a mobile application. Soil Health Card results provide nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, pH, organic carbon, and micronutrient values. Daily weather observations and medium-range forecasts are fetched from public meteorological services, and district-level crop yield and market price records are loaded from government open data portals. A batch and incremental ETL pipeline cleans these data, aligns them to a common field and season key, and stores them in a partitioned analytical warehouse. Three models are built on the integrated data. A crop suitability model ranks candidate crops for each field and season based on soil, climate, and water availability. A yield prediction model, using gradient boosting on soil, weather, and management features, estimates the expected yield of the recommended crops. A sowing window model combines forecast rainfall and soil moisture estimates to suggest the most favourable dates for sowing. A rule-based nutrient module converts soil test values into fertiliser recommendations, and an economic layer uses expected yield and recent prices to estimate the likely return from each option.

title: Towards parahydrogen-induced polarization of acetoacetate
summary: Abstract Hyperpolarized acetoacetate is a promising probe for the detection of redox status inside mitochondria using 13 C MRI. In this pilot study we used parahydrogen-induced polarization by means of a side arm hydrogenation (PHIP-SAH) ap
content: Abstract Hyperpolarized acetoacetate is a promising probe for the detection of redox status inside mitochondria using 13 C MRI. In this pilot study we used parahydrogen-induced polarization by means of a side arm hydrogenation (PHIP-SAH) approach for the hyperpolarization of [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate. The propargyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate precursor was synthesized and subjected to homogeneous hydrogenation with parahydrogen. After optimization, the observed 1 H polarization was 25.5% while achieving 100% chemical conversion of the propargyl moiety, and 80% selectivity to allyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate product. After hydrogenation, a linear magnetic field sweep was performed for the 1 H-to- 13 C polarization transfer in allyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate, with maximum observed 13 C polarizations: P( 13 C-1) = 4.1% and P( 13 C-3) = 2.7%. Next, we analyzed the products of allyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate hydrolysis under different conditions. Alkaline hydrolysis results in the formation of stereoisomeric enolates of allyl [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate, which can then be converted into hyperpolarized [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate under harsh alkaline conditions with a subsequent decomposition to hyperpolarized [2- 13 C]acetone and [ 13 C]carbonate. These results expand PHIP-SAH studies beyond pyruvate to the metabolically relevant acetoacetate probe and identify the key chemical factors that currently limit the direct probe production. Beyond the achieved polarization levels, this work provides a useful mechanistic insight into allyl acetoacetate hydrolysis and offers guidance for future PHIP-SAH development of β-ketoacid-derived probes.

title: Reimagining Tourism Education Through Transformative Learning and Systems Change: Fast-Tracking Curriculum Reform to Close the Sustainability Competency Gap
summary: Tourism accounts for approximately eight per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions and faces increasing pressure to transition toward low-carbon, regenerative development pathways. However, evidence from recent studies across Ireland, the
content: Tourism accounts for approximately eight per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions and faces increasing pressure to transition toward low-carbon, regenerative development pathways. However, evidence from recent studies across Ireland, the United Kingdom and five European countries reveals a persistent sustainability competency gap within tourism higher education, where graduates often lack the systems thinking, ethical reasoning, digital literacy and applied decarbonisation skills required to support Net-Zero transitions. This paper examines how tourism education can respond to this challenge by integrating transformative learning and systems change approaches into curriculum design. Drawing on a conceptual analytic synthesis informed by three complementary empirical studies of tourism programmes across Europe, the research develops a Transformative Systems Change Framework for curriculum reform. The framework conceptualises educational transformation as a multi-level process operating across four interconnected spheres: individual reflexivity, pedagogical innovation, institutional integration and systemic collaboration. The study argues that incremental curriculum adjustments are insufficient to address the sustainability competency gap. Instead, tourism education must shift from transmissive, management-oriented models toward experiential, digitally enabled and co-creative pedagogies that embed sustainability competencies throughout programme structures. The framework highlights the importance of authentic assessment, industry–university partnerships and institutional alignment with sustainability strategies to accelerate this transition. By positioning tourism education as a leverage point for systemic transformation, the paper contributes a practical and theoretically grounded model for fast-tracking curriculum reform. It demonstrates how higher education can move beyond producing skilled workers to developing reflective, ethically grounded professionals capable of supporting a just and regenerative tourism future.

title: Impact of Foreign Direct Investment on Economic Growth: A Disaggregated Approach for Policy Discourse in Developing Countries
source: International Journal of Social Science and Human Research
summary: The study examines the impact of foreign direct investment on economic growth in Nigeria spanning over 1984 to 2025. The study utilized a secondary data source and adapts the Augmented Dickey-Fuller Unit Root Test, the Granger causality tec
content: The study examines the impact of foreign direct investment on economic growth in Nigeria spanning over 1984 to 2025. The study utilized a secondary data source and adapts the Augmented Dickey-Fuller Unit Root Test, the Granger causality technique, and the Autoregressive Distributed Lag model which is robust to heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation. The study divided foreign direct investment into inward foreign direct investment and outward foreign direct investment. Finding indicated that inward foreign direct investment was significant and positively influenced economic growth in Nigeria. However, outward foreign direct investment had significant and negative impact on economic growth in Nigeria. Further findings indicated that outward foreign direct investment is positive however, not significant on economic growth within the study period in Nigeria. The evidence indicate that foreign direct investment granger caused economic growth and also economic growth granger caused foreign direct investment. Therefore, the study recommended that Nigerian government should formulate and implement policies that can attract more foreign direct investment and policies that would discourage outflow of foreign direct investment.

title: REScoops acting as intermediaries, influencing the scaling of energy communities; a multi-case analysis of five pilots in Europe
summary: There is increasing scholarly attention to the scaling of energy communities (EC). Intermediaries have an important role here. Energy communities themselves, especially in the form of renewable energy cooperatives (REScoops), can take on th
content: There is increasing scholarly attention to the scaling of energy communities (EC). Intermediaries have an important role here. Energy communities themselves, especially in the form of renewable energy cooperatives (REScoops), can take on this role very well. This paper addresses the question how REScoops, acting as intermediaries, influence the scaling of ECs. A longitudinal multi-case research design is adopted to answer this question. Five cases of EC pilots in different EU countries receiving intermediary support from REScoops were selected and researched over a three-year period. Data collection involved interviews, text documents, a quantitative longitudinal survey, and pilot project data. Results show that EC organisations use various forms of scaling: scaling-up, -out, and -deep. Regarding REScoops acting as an intermediary influencing the scaling of ECs, the analysis presents moderate support for positive impact. The relationship appears positive for scaling-deep and fairly positive for scaling-out. For scaling-up the relationship there was mostly within-case evidence. Scaling-up appears related to contextual factors. A fairly challenging context seems correlated to ECs deploying scaling-up strategies, using REScoop intermediary agency with the aim of changing key institutional structures, regulatory and policy frameworks that have a negative impact on ECs. This paper ends with suggestions for future work.

title: Removal of carbofuran from aqueous solutions using activated carbon derived from Pistacia khinjuk stocks (bıttım) shell waste
summary: Abstract Pesticides are important environmental pollutants that require effective removal to protect ecosystems and human health. This study investigated carbofuran removal from water using KOH-activated carbon derived from Pistacia khinjuk
content: Abstract Pesticides are important environmental pollutants that require effective removal to protect ecosystems and human health. This study investigated carbofuran removal from water using KOH-activated carbon derived from Pistacia khinjuk Stocks (bıttım) shell waste. The resulting adsorbent exhibited a high specific surface area (1552 m² g⁻¹). Under the selected conditions (50 mg L⁻¹ carbofuran, 0.01 g adsorbent, 0.25 L solution, pH 4.0, 25 min, and 298 K), the highest experimental adsorption capacity was 324.3 mg g⁻¹. In synthetic water, the adsorption capacity was 276.5 mg g⁻¹, retaining approximately 85.3% of that obtained in ultrapure water. The apparent thermodynamic parameters and the decrease in adsorption capacity with increasing temperature were consistent with favorable adsorption and an exothermic temperature dependence under the investigated conditions. The Langmuir isotherm best described the equilibrium data. Adsorption appeared to involve hydrophobic and π–π electron donor–acceptor interactions, while electrostatic attraction likely played a limited role. These findings demonstrate the potential of bıttım shell-derived activated carbon as a biomass-derived adsorbent for carbofuran removal from water.

title: Coordinated dispatch of virtual power plants in distribution systems under ramping constraints and uncertainties
summary: This paper proposes a coordinated dispatch framework for distribution systems with virtual power plants (VPPs) that addresses both substation ramping constraints and load-ramping uncertainty. A data-driven quantile-regression temporal convo
content: This paper proposes a coordinated dispatch framework for distribution systems with virtual power plants (VPPs) that addresses both substation ramping constraints and load-ramping uncertainty. A data-driven quantile-regression temporal convolutional network (QR-TCN) is developed to produce multi-quantile probabilistic forecasts of both the load and its ramping boundaries. Using the resulting prediction intervals, a second-order cone programming (SOCP) dispatch model is formulated to jointly minimize upstream substation operating costs, VPP regulation costs, and network losses. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate that the proposed framework ensures system economic, flexibility, and security adequacy across diverse operational boundaries and system constraints.

title: Redefining fuel poverty: Introducing the temporal equity framework (TEF)
summary: The definition and quantification of fuel (or energy) poverty remain contentious, particularly within the English policy landscape. The current official definition—Low Income Low Energy Efficiency (LILEE)—systematically underestimates the c
content: The definition and quantification of fuel (or energy) poverty remain contentious, particularly within the English policy landscape. The current official definition—Low Income Low Energy Efficiency (LILEE)—systematically underestimates the condition in low- and middle-income households, effectively obfuscating changing energy affordability norms. This paper presents a sensitivity analysis of fuel poverty trajectories in Nottingham, UK, across competing definitions and diverging ‘optimistic’ (domestic efficiency upgrades) and ‘pessimistic’ (energy price inflation) scenarios. Results demonstrate that LILEE overstates the efficacy of efficiency upgrades while failing to adequately reflect the impact of price shocks. To address these deficiencies, we propose the Temporal Equity Framework (TEF), a budget standard-based approach paired with a proportional energy expenditure indicator that captures shifting affordability norms more equitably. The TEF also introduces continuous expenditure-based depth indicators to evaluate the entrenchment of fuel-poor households (the ‘fuel poverty gap’) and the resilience of non-fuel-poor households (the ‘fuel poverty buffer’). We argue that responsive definitions which also recognise fuel poverty as a continuum of vulnerability, rather than a static, dichotomous state, are paramount to ensuring the equitability of energy transitions. Further, we suggest that the early identification of fuel poverty and spatial targeting of remedial resources could be markedly improved by adopting the TEF. We conclude that the adoption of a multidimensional budget standard-based definition is essential to facilitate a more accurate and just evaluation of energy transitions in England.

title: Stable Transfer Geometry of the Substituted Chrysene Network: H-Infinity Transformation Metrics, Dissipative Well-Posedness, and Survival Under Persistent Disturbance
summary: We construct a family of distances on the admissible domain of the Chrysene Formalism and determine which metric axioms each satisfies. The central object is the unitary-orbit H-infinity distance between the transfer realizations of two str
content: We construct a family of distances on the admissible domain of the Chrysene Formalism and determine which metric axioms each satisfies. The central object is the unitary-orbit H-infinity distance between the transfer realizations of two structural forms, together with its path closure over admissible transformations; it is an extended pseudometric, and its zero set is exactly the relation of transfer isomorphism, which is shown to be logically independent of isomorphism of the underlying molecular graphs. The construction requires a well-posedness result: the worst-case norm of a transfer operator built from the directional Hamiltonian is generically infinite, and we prove that it is finite precisely when the active region carries no mode that is energetically embedded in the continuum of a second fibration yet orthogonal to every channel into it. The dissipation making this possible is not postulated but computed, as the coupling-weighted density of states of that fibration, and the norm it removes from the admissible sector is shown to be transferred rather than destroyed. Two statements follow: a radius within which a form may be transformed and remain robustly stable, and a common-storage condition under which arbitrary admissible switching among forms preserves a uniform gain bound. Frozen-form stability is shown by counterexample not to imply the latter. The choice of the worst-case over the mean-square norm is justified by four independent arguments, including an explicit resonance family inside the axioms' own data; a self-adjoint perturbation class for which the worst-case norm is instead the wrong measure is identified, and an exact margin supplied for it. Invariance of the admissible domain is shown to be a peak-gain statement not controlled by the worst-case norm, so that survival, the conjunction of robust stability with that invariance, is certified here in two separate halves and by no single certificate. An explicit witness realization with closed-form values is given, the formalism's own explicit model being shown to have infinite gain. Fourteen non-implications, twelve new deferred targets, a concordance table recording five corrections to the prior corpus, and a self-identified defect ledger are stated.

title: Single-vacancy engineering of blue phosphorene for suppressing the shuttle effect and enhancing conversion kinetics in Na-Se batteries: A computational investigation
summary: The development of high-performance sodium-selenium (Na-Se) batteries is critically hindered by the dissolution and migration of intermediate polyselenide species, which induce severe shuttle effects and degrade cycling stability. In this w
content: The development of high-performance sodium-selenium (Na-Se) batteries is critically hindered by the dissolution and migration of intermediate polyselenide species, which induce severe shuttle effects and degrade cycling stability. In this work, first-principles density functional theory calculations are employed to systematically investigate single-vacancy blue phosphorene (SVBlueP) as an effective host material for sodium polyselenides. The structural stability, adsorption behavior, electronic properties, charge-transfer characteristics, and reaction thermodynamics and kinetics of Na 2 Se n (n = 1, 2, 4, 6, 8) species on SVBlueP are comprehensively analysed. The results reveal that introducing single-vacancy defects significantly enhances polyselenide binding through higher interfacial charge transfer and orbital hybridization, while preserving the metallic character of the host surface. Charge density difference and Bader analyses confirm pronounced electron donation from Na 2 Se n clusters to the vacancy phosphorene surface, indicative of chemisorption-dominated interactions, particularly for low-order polyselenides. Electron localization function analysis further demonstrates the coexistence of covalent and ionic bonding characteristics, rationalizing the observed adsorption strength hierarchy. Thermodynamic calculations show that SVBlueP markedly lowers the Gibbs free energy along the Na-Se conversion pathway relative to the vacuum reference, thereby promoting favorable polyselenide transformation reactions. In addition, climbing image nudged elastic band calculations reveal a substantially reduced energy barrier for Na 2 S decomposition on SVBlueP, highlighting its catalytic role in accelerating electrochemical kinetics. These findings elucidate the critical role of vacancy-induced surface electronic modulation in regulating polyselenide adsorption and conversion and establish single-vacancy blue phosphorene as a promising surface-engineered host for mitigating shuttle effects and enhancing the performance of Na-Se batteries.

title: A Hybrid TOPSIS–PIV Method with Compromise Weighting of SWARA and MEREC for Supplier Selection in the Indonesian Leather Industry
source: RSF Conference Series Engineering and Technology
summary: Supplier selection constitutes a critical decision in the leather industry, as supplier performance directly influences material quality, production continuity, cost, and product competitiveness. Nevertheless, supplier evaluation in this se
content: Supplier selection constitutes a critical decision in the leather industry, as supplier performance directly influences material quality, production continuity, cost, and product competitiveness. Nevertheless, supplier evaluation in this sector involves multiple, often conflicting criteria, which complicates efforts to obtain reliable rankings through a single weighting or ranking method. Existing approaches tend to rely either on subjective expert judgments or objective data characteristics, neither of which fully captures the complexity inherent in supplier selection. This study addresses this gap by offering an integrated supplier selection framework that combines subjective and objective weighting with complementary ranking techniques. The proposed framework integrates the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) and Proximity Indexed Value (PIV) methods with a compromise weighting scheme derived from the Stepwise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (SWARA) and the Method based on the Removal Effects of Criteria (MEREC). The Delphi method identifies and validates the supplier evaluation criteria. A case study in an Indonesian leather manufacturing company demonstrates the framework's applicability. The findings indicate that the hybrid approach yields consistent supplier rankings and facilitates more robust decision-making by integrating expert judgments with objective data characteristics. The proposed framework thus offers a practical and reliable decision-support tool for supplier selection in the leather industry.

title: Common Interest Groups as Institutional Spaces for Gendered Empowerment Within a Food System Innovation Platform: Evidence from Kenya
summary: Community-based organizations are increasingly recognized as institutional mechanisms for inclusive and regenerative food-system transformation, yet evidence on their gendered empowerment outcomes within Food System Innovation Platforms (FS
content: Community-based organizations are increasingly recognized as institutional mechanisms for inclusive and regenerative food-system transformation, yet evidence on their gendered empowerment outcomes within Food System Innovation Platforms (FSIPs) remains limited. This study examined CIG members’ perceptions of voice and agency, gender-responsive institutional practices, participation, and empowerment within the Nakuru Living Lab FSIP, Menengai Local Initiative, Kenya. A cross-sectional survey of 129 CIG members was conducted using a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and gender-disaggregated Welch’s t-tests were applied, with empowerment interpreted using the Reach-Benefit-Empower-Transform (RBET) framework. Participation was high (M = 4.21), particularly in training, meetings, and activity implementation. Women perceived stronger anti-discrimination mechanisms than men (4.32 vs. 3.79; p = 0.007). RBET analysis showed significantly greater benefits among women (4.56 vs. 4.20; p < 0.001), including income opportunities and household well-being, while men reported greater confidence in influencing governance decisions (4.39 vs. 4.04; p = 0.004). Women also perceived stronger long-term structural change (4.54 vs. 4.32; p = 0.025). The findings reveal a participation-benefit-power paradox: CIGs are perceived as strengthening inclusion and women’s livelihood benefits, but gender gaps in governance influence persist. Gender-responsive FSIPs should therefore complement participation and livelihood support with stronger mechanisms for women’s leadership, decision-making authority, and institutional influence.

title: The Effect of Digital Payments on Currency in Circulation Mediated by Digital Financial Inclusion
source: American Journal of Economic and Management Business (AJEMB)
summary: The rapid growth of digital payment systems has transformed Indonesia’s payment behavior; however, currency in circulation remains substantial despite the increasing adoption of cashless instruments. This study aims to examine the effect of
content: The rapid growth of digital payment systems has transformed Indonesia’s payment behavior; however, currency in circulation remains substantial despite the increasing adoption of cashless instruments. This study aims to examine the effect of digital payments, represented by Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS), electronic money, and card-based payment instruments (APMK), on currency in circulation, both directly and indirectly through Digital Financial Inclusion as a mediating variable. This study employs a quantitative approach with a causal associative design using monthly time-series data from January 2020 to December 2025, consisting of 72 observations obtained from Bank Indonesia publications. The data were analyzed using the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model, Error Correction Model (ECM), and Sobel test to evaluate short-term, long-term, and mediation relationships. The results indicate that QRIS and electronic money significantly strengthen Digital Financial Inclusion in the long term, while APMK has a weaker contribution. However, Digital Financial Inclusion does not significantly mediate the relationship between digital payment instruments and currency in circulation. Electronic money shows a positive and significant long-term effect on currency circulation, indicating that digital payments have not replaced cash but continue to coexist within the payment ecosystem. The study concludes that Indonesia remains in a complementary cashless society phase, where digital payment development advances alongside the continued role of physical currency.

title: EFFECT OF HARVEST TIME, STORAGE METHOD AND DURATION ON BIOCHEMICAL CONSTITUENTS OF GINGER (Zingiber officinale L.) RHIZOME
source: International Journal of Agriculture and Agricultural Technology
summary: This study investigated the effect of harvest time, storage methods and storage length on biochemical constituents, including anti-nutritional factors and oleoresin content, of ginger rhizome (Zingiber officinale L.). Fresh ginger rhizomes
content: This study investigated the effect of harvest time, storage methods and storage length on biochemical constituents, including anti-nutritional factors and oleoresin content, of ginger rhizome (Zingiber officinale L.). Fresh ginger rhizomes harvested at 5, 6 and 7 months after planting were subjected to three storage methods (pit, heap and ambient storage) for 1, 2 and 3 months. The experiment was a 3 × 3 × 3 factorial arranged in completely randomized design with three replications. Biochemical parameters including carotenoids, tannin, total phenolics, saponin, alkaloids, steroids, terpenes, trypsin inhibitor activity, DPPH radical scavenging activity, flavonoids and oleoresin content were determined using standard analytical procedures. Results showed that harvest time, storage method and storage length significantly (P ≤ 0.05) influenced all parameters assessed. Ginger harvested at 7 months recorded the highest values for carotenoids (0.03 mg/100g), tannin (0.05 mg/100g), total phenolics (0.04 mg/100g), saponin (0.16 mg/100g), steroids (0.06 mg/100g), terpenes (0.04 mg/100g), trypsin inhibitor activity (7.74 TIU/g), DPPH radical scavenging activity (0.18 mg/100g), flavonoids (0.32 mg/100g) and oleoresin (17.35 mg/100g) compared to 5 and 6 months harvests. Pit storage preserved oleoresin, DPPH activity and flavonoids better than other methods, while ambient storage promoted alkaloid accumulation. Storage for 1 month produced the highest biochemical constituent values, with progressive decline after 2 and 3 months. The three-way interaction (H7 × Pit × L1) gave the best oleoresin retention (21.30 mg/100g), indicating that harvesting at 7 months after planting and pit storage for 1-2 months is most suitable for maintaining ginger biochemical quality. Conversely, immature harvest (5 months) combined with ambient storage for 3 months resulted in the lowest values for most parameters. The study demonstrates that delayed harvest (7 months) enhances secondary metabolite accumulation and oleoresin content, while pit storage provides a favourable microenvironment that slows biochemical degradation. It is recommended that ginger intended for nutritional, medicinal and industrial use should be harvested at physiological maturity (7 months after planting) and stored in pits for not more than 2 months to preserve its quality attributes.

title: Risk-Constrained Optimal Energy Management of Multi-Carrier Microgrids Under Uncertainty
source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: The introduction of multi-carrier microgrids (MCMGs) is a paradigm shift in the decentralised energy system, allowing for coordinated dispatch of coupled electrical, thermal, and natural gas subsystems. Despite this, the economic challenges
content: The introduction of multi-carrier microgrids (MCMGs) is a paradigm shift in the decentralised energy system, allowing for coordinated dispatch of coupled electrical, thermal, and natural gas subsystems. Despite this, the economic challenges of MCMGs are quite sensitive to multi-dimensional uncertainties such as the intermittent generation of renewable energy, the volatile market electricity prices, and the multi-energy load demands. Traditional deterministic or risk-neutral energy management systems optimise average performance, but are not designed to buffer microgrid operators from operational gaps and tail risks with high impact from low-probability events. In this paper, a new risk-constrained optimal energy management approach for multi-carrier microgrids is presented, which aims to minimise risk by employing a twostage stochastic mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) approach. The Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) is incorporated as a primary operational objective function to capture and mitigate financial exposure during worst cases. Extensive uncertainty profiles are computed using Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS), while being downscaled by a fast forward scenario-reduction technique. A modified IEEE 33-bus electrical network and a 6-node district heating system are used for the validation of the proposed model. It is shown that the proposed framework strategically sacrifices a marginal increase in the expected daily operating costs while offering a significant decrease in the tail-risk financial losses through tuning the risk-aversion parameter.

title: Foundational Fracture: Failing to Reform the World Trade Organization in an Age of Geopolitics
summary: ABSTRACT The World Trade Organization (WTO) is at the crossroads, with a principal challenge raised to the organization by the United States in 2025 and a series of related, largely unsuccessful reform attempts over the last several years.
content: ABSTRACT The World Trade Organization (WTO) is at the crossroads, with a principal challenge raised to the organization by the United States in 2025 and a series of related, largely unsuccessful reform attempts over the last several years. To shed new light on why recent WTO reform attempts have been proving so difficult, we leverage evidence from close to 40 interviews conducted in Geneva in 2024 and 2025, and an array of recent reform‐related WTO documents. We argue that the main reform failures do not result from design inefficiencies or specific well‐defined disagreements. Rather, we propose that the situation in the WTO is best described as a foundational fracture , a deep split among WTO's principal members about the very purpose of the organization, combined with a long‐term inability of the WTO to update its institutional framework, and the mutual reinforcement of these two challenges. We only identify modest reform progress achieved over the last years in activities that are predominantly informal and focused on information exchange, without binding commitments and the ability to address the deep‐seated institutional issues. These findings contribute to broad debates on global governance transformation, beyond the WTO itself.

title: Recognized but displaced: Uranium mill tailings and the sustainability accounting of nuclear energy
summary: Nuclear-energy sustainability is usually debated through reactor performance, carbon intensity, fuel availability, operational safety and spent-fuel disposal. Less visible are the front-end residues generated by uranium production, especial
content: Nuclear-energy sustainability is usually debated through reactor performance, carbon intensity, fuel availability, operational safety and spent-fuel disposal. Less visible are the front-end residues generated by uranium production, especially uranium mill tailings (UMT), likely the nuclear fuel cycle's largest long-lived radioactive residue stream by volume. This Perspective argues that UMT are not merely neglected; they are recognized and displaced through nested governance boundaries. It develops the concept of volume-based leniency and identifies three linked mechanisms: classification displacement, infrastructural pragmatism and sustainability-accounting displacement. Historical regulation, current naturally occurring radioactive material (NORM) and remediation frameworks, the Wismut programme, written clarifications from Nordic radiation-safety authorities, and uranium-mining legacies show how competent institutions can each address a bounded part of the problem without assembling the long-term radioactive, chemical, ecological, financial and distributive liability as a whole. The resulting issue is not whether all tailings should be reclassified as conventional radioactive waste. It is whether nuclear-energy sustainability can be judged credibly when front-end liabilities remain outside, or only weakly attached to, the system boundary used to assess the electricity they enable. Whole-system accounting should not predetermine whether nuclear energy is sustainable; it should ensure that the judgement is made with its material liabilities inside the boundary of analysis. Uranium mill tailings illustrate how a recognized, long-lasting material liability can be displaced through nested governance boundaries. Specialist regimes can reduce impacts and achieve partial administrative closure, while the underlying inventory and stewardship obligations persist. Whole-system nuclear sustainability assessment should therefore keep front-end uranium liabilities within the accounting boundary. • Uranium mill tailings are recognized yet displaced from sustainability accounting. • Volume-based leniency captures special governance of enormous, low-activity residues. • Nested governance boundaries allow partial closure while liabilities persist. • Wismut shows remediation success can still require continuing stewardship. • Whole-system nuclear sustainability should include front-end uranium liabilities.
