title: INCLUSIVE BUSINESS MODEL INNOVATION IN COMMUNITY BASED HERITAGE TOURISM: A CASE STUDY OF HERITAGE WALKING TOURS IN SURABAYA USING THE FLOURISHING BUSINESS CANVAS
source: Proceeding of The International Seminar on Business Economics Social Science and Technology (ISBEST)
summary: Global economic fragmentation has heightened attention to inclusive and sustainable business models across industries, including tourism. While social entrepreneurship has been widely discussed in prior research, much of the literature has
content: Global economic fragmentation has heightened attention to inclusive and sustainable business models across industries, including tourism. While social entrepreneurship has been widely discussed in prior research, much of the literature has remained centered on small traditional enterprises, leaving community-based initiatives built around local heritage and experience relatively underexplored. This study examines the business model development of a community-based heritage walking tour in Surabaya, Indonesia, using a qualitative singlecase study design. The case was selected because it represents a grassroots initiative that seeks to preserve local culture while also generating economic value. Data were drawn from publicly available sources, including social media content, community publications, and user-generated interactions. The analysis is informed by the Flourishing Business Canvas (FBC), which offers a holistic lens for assessing economic, social, and environmental value creation. The findings suggest that the community has developed in ways that resemble an emerging social enterprise, with revenue-generating activities closely linked to social objectives such as heritage preservation and local empowerment. The study also shows that digital platforms play an enabling role by broadening access and supporting wider participation. This study contributes to strategic management research by illustrating how grassroots community initiatives can evolve into sustainable and inclusive business models while retaining their core social purpose. It also highlights the relevance of the Flourishing Business Canvas as a practical framework for analyzing community-based social enterprises.

title: Distant water fishing and its effects on domestic food security
summary: Governments around the world have identified distant water fleets (DWFs) as a key threat to ecosystem health, domestic economic opportunities, and food security. With a high prevalence of undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in cou
content: Governments around the world have identified distant water fleets (DWFs) as a key threat to ecosystem health, domestic economic opportunities, and food security. With a high prevalence of undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in countries where DWFs operate, the aquatic foods caught by DWFs represent a vital opportunity to shift policy and improve nutrition outcomes. To better understand this issue, we conducted a literature review and expert interviews to develop a framework of relationships between DWFs and food security. We then applied the framework to three unique case studies to describe the mechanisms underlying DWF-food security interactions. Our findings highlight the potential for diverse policy pathways to improved food and nutrition outcomes. The research suggests that integrating food systems expertise and nutrition metrics into management and licensing negotiations could serve to illuminate the true tradeoffs of DWF access and steer policy to ensure an equitable flow of benefits to local communities.

title: Mobilizing Dynamic‐Capability Microfoundations for Sustainability‐Oriented Innovation: The Role of Innovation Champions
summary: ABSTRACT Organizations face growing pressure to respond to environmental and social challenges, yet research has not sufficiently explained how organizational actors mobilise dynamic‐capability microfoundations across the development of sus
content: ABSTRACT Organizations face growing pressure to respond to environmental and social challenges, yet research has not sufficiently explained how organizational actors mobilise dynamic‐capability microfoundations across the development of sustainability‐oriented innovations. Drawing on 68 semistructured interviews conducted between March and November 2024 across 18 EU and UK marine firms, this qualitative study examines how innovation champions and related actors support sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring. The analysis identifies an interconnected process: market exposure and network relationships support sensing sustainability‐oriented opportunities; perceived product–capability fit shapes whether those opportunities progress to seizing; and managerial mobilization, cross‐functional problem‐solving, and relationship coordination support reconfiguration. Rather than treating every influential manager as an innovation champion, the study distinguishes championing activities—persistent advocacy, boundary spanning, resource mobilization, and coordination—from formal organizational positions. The study contributes by explaining how actor‐level mechanisms connect successive dynamic‐capability stages in a sustainability‐oriented innovation context. Product–capability fit is presented as an emerging transition mechanism that requires further testing rather than as an entirely novel construct.

title: Groundwater Security in the Pacific Islands: Bridging Knowledge Systems for Climate Adaptation
summary: The Pacific Islands are among the regions most exposed to climate change impacts, and their limited groundwater resources are particularly vulnerable to these impacts. This transdisciplinary review aims to inform the design of effective ada
content: The Pacific Islands are among the regions most exposed to climate change impacts, and their limited groundwater resources are particularly vulnerable to these impacts. This transdisciplinary review aims to inform the design of effective adaptation measures for sustainable groundwater management in the Pacific Islands. The review is guided by the question: What approaches are most relevant and effective for investigating groundwater resources and for designing adaptation strategies in the Pacific Islands? Based on a synthesis of the hydrogeological context, projected climate change impacts on groundwater, and adaptation strategies, we identify three key considerations for groundwater security and climate adaptation. First, bridging knowledge systems through equitable dialogue between traditional knowledge and contemporary science, including hydrogeology and climate science, is essential for developing adaptation strategies for groundwater security. Traditional knowledge refers to cumulative, place-based, and culturally grounded ways of knowing developed through generations of lived experience and close interaction with ancestral territories, including orally transmitted understandings of environmental change and human–environment relationships. Second, adaptation measures should be tailored to the diverse social and cultural contexts of Pacific Island communities to avoid maladaptation and ensure culturally appropriate and socially acceptable outcomes. Third, adaptation efforts should proceed despite irreducible uncertainties in climate projections and hydrogeological conditions, using approaches such as robust and collaborative decision-making. Ensuring groundwater security in a changing climate therefore requires moving beyond inclusive stakeholder engagement toward the equitable co-production of knowledge and adaptation strategies through transdisciplinary and inter-epistemic dialogue.

title: Diagnóstico de cultivos agrícolas y diversidad vegetal en sistemas agroforestales finca "Lucero", parroquia Teniente Hugo Ortiz
summary: Los sistemas agroforestales constituyen una alternativa para integrar producción, conservación de la biodiversidad y resiliencia socioecológica en la Amazonía. El objetivo del estudio fue diagnosticar los componentes agrícolas y la diversid
content: Los sistemas agroforestales constituyen una alternativa para integrar producción, conservación de la biodiversidad y resiliencia socioecológica en la Amazonía. El objetivo del estudio fue diagnosticar los componentes agrícolas y la diversidad vegetal del sistema agroforestal de la finca Lucero, parroquia Teniente Hugo Ortiz, Pastaza, Ecuador, para sustentar estrategias de mejoramiento productivo y ambiental adaptadas a las condiciones locales. Se realizó un estudio de caso descriptivo y observacional. El componente agrícola incluyó georreferenciación y delimitación de las áreas productivas, recorridos técnicos, observación directa y entrevista semiestructurada a un productor, además del registro de prácticas de manejo, fertilización, enfermedades y rendimiento de la producción. El componente forestal se evaluó en tres parcelas de 20 × 20 m, con una superficie total muestreada de 1.200 m², donde se registraron 35 individuos arbóreos. Se determinaron variables dasométricas, riqueza, abundancia y frecuencia relativas, dominancia, índice de valor de importancia, Shannon-Wiener, Simpson, equidad e Índice Compuesto de Conservación. La finca presentó una superficie delimitada aproximada de 470.000 m² y una producción agrícola diversificada, con predominio del cacao y limitaciones nutricionales y fitosanitarias. La diversidad y estructura variaron entre parcelas; Shannon-Wiener fue 0,695, 0,669 y 0,579 para P1, P2 y P3, respectivamente. A partir del diagnóstico se propusieron intensificación agroecológica, regeneración natural asistida, enriquecimiento selectivo y monitoreo adaptativo como estrategias de manejo, cuya efectividad deberá evaluarse posteriormente.

title: Does competitive advantage strengthen the value relevance of ESG disclosure?
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleIn the evolving landscape of ASEAN capital markets, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure is increasingly recognized as a strategic driver of corporate value, with competitive advantage
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleIn the evolving landscape of ASEAN capital markets, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure is increasingly recognized as a strategic driver of corporate value, with competitive advantage determining the extent to which its benefits are realized. This study aims to examine how competitive advantage moderates the relationship between ESG disclosure and firm value in the ASEAN emergent context. The study applies panel data comprising 2,801 observations from 726 listed companies in ASEAN during 2015-2023. Regression analysis was conducted using the two-step System Generalized Method of Moments, accompanied by a series of robustness tests. The findings emphasize ESG reporting benefits, as ESG disclosure positively influences all firm value proxies in baseline models (βESG_Tobin’sQ = 0.0034, p-value < 0.05; βESG_LogMC = 0.0040, p-value < 0.01; βESG_PB = 0.0047, p-value < 0.05). The interaction between ESG disclosure and competitive advantage is also positive and significant across the three measures (βESGxCA_Tobin’sQ = 0.0545, p-value < 0.05; βESGxCA_LogMC = 0.0254, p-value < 0.01; βESGxCA_PB = 0.0678, p-value < 0.01). These results suggest that the valuation implications of ESG disclosure are contingent on firms’ competitive advantage, with the estimated marginal effect generally increasing as competitive advantage improves. Accordingly, the study enriches the literature by resonating with the intersection between stakeholder theory and the resource-based view (RBV), demonstrating how competitive advantage conditions the link between ESG disclosure and firm value in ASEAN capital markets. The study suggests that managers should align financial objectives with stakeholder expectations and integrate ESG disclosure into broader corporate strategies to enhance valuation purposes.

title: Effect of Sustainability-Themed Advertising on Consumer Purchase Intention for Guinness Nigeria Plc in Benin City, Edo State
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MARKETING AND COMMUNICATION STUDIES
summary: This study examines the effect of sustainability-themed advertising on consumer purchase intention for Guinness Nigeria Plc in Benin City, Edo State. The study assessed four dimensions of sustainability communication: eco-friendly packaging
content: This study examines the effect of sustainability-themed advertising on consumer purchase intention for Guinness Nigeria Plc in Benin City, Edo State. The study assessed four dimensions of sustainability communication: eco-friendly packaging communication, green advertising creativity, green brand image, and perceived sustainability value. An analytical survey design was adopted. From a population of 154 staff of Guinness Nigeria Plc in Benin City, a sample of 111 was drawn using the Taro Yamane formula and selected through stratified random sampling; 103 valid responses (92.79%) were retained for analysis. Data were gathered with a structured questionnaire measured on a five-point Likert scale; whose internal consistency was confirmed by Cronbach's alpha coefficients ranging from 0.812 to 0.883. We used descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis to test the hypotheses. The results show that all four dimensions exert a significant positive effect on consumer purchase intention: green advertising creativity emerged as the strongest predictor (β = 0.512; p = 0.000), followed by green brand image (β = 0.269; p = 0.009), eco-friendly packaging communication (β = 0.231; p = 0.010), and perceived sustainability value (β = 0.204; p = 0.004). The study concludes that sustainability themed advertising is a meaningful driver of purchase intention in the Nigerian beverage sector, and recommends that Guinness Nigeria Plc sustain and expand credible sustainability messaging across its packaging, advertising, and community engagement platforms in order to strengthen brand trust, loyalty, and patronage.

title: Barrier model selection alters apparent diclofenac permeation parameters: a controlled in vitro comparison of Strat-M® and a HaCaT-based epidermal construct
summary: Introduction Synthetic membranes and keratinocyte-based constructs are both used as accessible alternatives to ex vivo skin in in vitro permeation testing (IVPT), but they have not been compared directly for the same marketed products under
content: Introduction Synthetic membranes and keratinocyte-based constructs are both used as accessible alternatives to ex vivo skin in in vitro permeation testing (IVPT), but they have not been compared directly for the same marketed products under identical conditions. This pilot study directly compared the synthetic Strat-M® membrane and a HaCaT construct under identical IVPT conditions using Voltaren® and Olfen®, two marketed, nominally dose-equivalent diclofenac gels. The aim was to determine whether the two barrier models yielded consistent apparent permeation parameters and led to the same comparative interpretation of the two formulations. Methods Permeation studies were performed using Franz diffusion cells in an internally controlled experimental design. Both formulations were tested in triplicate under identical conditions, including receptor medium, temperature, sampling protocol, and analytical method. Steady-state flux (Jss), permeability coefficient (Kp), lag time ( t lag), and cumulative permeation profiles were determined and compared between barrier models. Results Barrier model selection affected the apparent permeation behavior of diclofenac. Strat-M® detected a statistically significant difference in steady-state flux between Voltaren® and Olfen®, whereas no statistically significant between-formulation difference was detected with the HaCaT construct under the same experimental conditions. Lag time was the parameter most strongly influenced by barrier selection and was consistently shorter with the HaCaT construct than with Strat-M®. Discussion Under identical IVPT conditions, Strat-M® and the HaCaT-based epidermal construct generated different apparent permeation profiles and yielded different comparative assessments of Voltaren® and Olfen®. This model-dependent divergence underscores the need to justify barrier selection explicitly and to consider its limitations when interpreting comparative IVPT data.

title: Radon Concentration Assessment and Potential Health Impact in Selected Wetlands of Warri, Delta State
source: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF PURE SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
summary: This study establishes a baseline radiological profile of radon-222 (²²²Rn) in surface water from eight wetlands-Ajamimogha, Esisi Road, Iyara, Market Road, McDermott Road, NPA Axis, Okere, and Okumagba, within Warri South Local Government
content: This study establishes a baseline radiological profile of radon-222 (²²²Rn) in surface water from eight wetlands-Ajamimogha, Esisi Road, Iyara, Market Road, McDermott Road, NPA Axis, Okere, and Okumagba, within Warri South Local Government Area, Delta State, Nigeria. Sixteen samples were collected during a single dry-season campaign in March 2026 and analyzed using a RAD7 electronic radon detector with closed-loop protocols. Decay-corrected concentrations were evaluated through descriptive statistics, Kruskal–Wallis testing, Spearman correlation, and exploratory GIS mapping, while annual effective dose and excess lifetime cancer risk were modeled using ingestion dose coefficients of 3.50 × 10⁻⁹ and 6.90 × 10⁻¹⁰ Sv/Bq. Of sixteen samples, fourteen yielded quantifiable concentrations of 3.87–53.70 pCi/L (≈0.143 1.987 Bq/L), with a mean of 20.10 pCi/L (≈0.743 Bq/L). The relatively highest readings occurred at Iyara and Esisi Road, though all values remained far below the 100 Bq/L WHO/Euratom parametric limit. The Kruskal–Wallis test showed no significant differences among locations (p = 0.161), reflecting limited sample size, while GIS contouring suggested localized clustering of comparatively higher values. Spearman correlation indicated a moderate negative association between radon and temperature (ρ = –0.503, p = 0.067) and a moderate positive association with relative humidity (ρ = 0.458, p = 0.100), with negligible spatial correlations. Radiological assessment confirmed that annual effective doses (≈0.49–4.92 µSv/y) were well below the 0.1 mSv/year reference, and excess lifetime cancer risks (≈2.02 × 10⁻⁶–2.03 × 10⁻⁵) were negligible compared to the UNSCEAR benchmark of 0.29 × 10⁻³. These findings demonstrate that Warri wetlands exhibit low dissolved-radon concentrations and do not pose significant radiological hazards if consumed directly, while underscoring the importance of continued monitoring, seasonal sampling, and hydrogeological follow-up to strengthen long-term environmental risk evaluation.

title: Nanoparticle-Based Zinc Fertilizer Enhances Rice Growth and Micronutrient Uptake
summary: In many agricultural soils around the world, zinc deficiency is one of the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies affecting rice productivity and nutritional quality of rice grain.Nano-fertilizers have proven to be a new strategy to enha
content: In many agricultural soils around the world, zinc deficiency is one of the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies affecting rice productivity and nutritional quality of rice grain.Nano-fertilizers have proven to be a new strategy to enhance nutrient use efficiency and nutrient availability.Thus, in the present investigation, the growth, physiological performance, uptake of macro and micronutrients, yield and resource use efficiency of rice in the field were evaluated upon application of zinc nanoparticle fertilizer.The experiment was laid out in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with five treatment and three replications.The growth parameters, physiological traits, nitrogen and zinc uptake, yield attributes and nutrient-use efficiency were evaluated during the crop growth period.The use of zinc nanoparticles led to a marked improvement in plant growth and physiological activity.The height of the plants was 62 cm in the control and 82 cm in the maximum zinc nanoparticle treatment, whereas the biomass accumulation was 18 to 34 g plant⁻¹ in control to highest zinc nanoparticle treatment, respectively.The chlorophyll content was raised from 32 to 45 SPAD units and the photosynthetic rate was raised from 14 to 22 units.The grain yield was enhanced from 3.2 to 5.1 t ha⁻¹ and also improved grain number and grain weight.The amount of nitrogen in leaves, roots and grains rose significantly, leaving behind greater nitrogen-use efficiency, from 38% to 65% among the treatments.Even though there were minor variations in water use, water productivity also improved.In general, the overall findings of this study showed that the use of zinc nanoparticles for fertilization led to the improvement of growth, physiological efficiency, nutrient use efficiency and grain yield of rice crop.Based on the findings, it is concluded that the application of NPFZ is a promising and sustainable approach to enhance rice production, nutrientuse efficiency and nutritional quality of its grains in modern farming systems.

title: Medicinal and Aromatic Plants of the Indian Himalayas
summary: The Indian Himalayan Region (IHR), covering 16.16% of the geographical area, forms the most significant world biodiversity hotspot, characterized by fragile ecosystems and high endemism. Endemic diversity mainly includes ecologically, econo
content: The Indian Himalayan Region (IHR), covering 16.16% of the geographical area, forms the most significant world biodiversity hotspot, characterized by fragile ecosystems and high endemism. Endemic diversity mainly includes ecologically, economically, and culturally important medicinal and aromatic plants (MAPs). These plants are progressively gaining recognition in international herbal markets for their utilization in the development of modern pharmaceuticals, besides the traditional utilization in Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, and Amchi practices for a long time. Nonetheless, overharvesting threatens their existence severely due to enhanced pressure in terms of demand, climate change resulting from enhanced carbon emissions, and expanding anthropogenic pressures. MAPs in the IHR have been categorized in various International Union for Conservation of Nature extinction risk categories owing to their sensitivity and limited occupancy, which further aggravates the issue these species are already experiencing. The present chapter demonstrates a complete overview of MAPs in the IHR, with details of their diversity, utilization, and conservation issues. This mainly discusses their traditional and modern uses, functional significance, and climate change implications. Moreover, existing conservation strategies such as habitat conservation, cultivation, and community engagement are deliberated in association with policy structures. Focus is given to the sustainable use and incorporation of traditional knowledge into scientific progress. The combined strategy is crucial for preserving the intact, diverse, and culturally rich MAPs of the Himalayas and maintaining their role in livelihoods, medicine, and biodiversity conservation.

title: Urban land-use dynamics and changing landscapes in Kano, Nigeria (1950–2020)
summary: Kano is one of the rapidly urbanizing cities of sub-Saharan Africa, characterized by a growing population, sprawling development, and weak planning controls. Understanding the city’s land-use dynamics is vital for its sustainability. This s
content: Kano is one of the rapidly urbanizing cities of sub-Saharan Africa, characterized by a growing population, sprawling development, and weak planning controls. Understanding the city’s land-use dynamics is vital for its sustainability. This study examines the decadal land-use dynamics of the Municipality, between 1950 and 2020. Using unsupervised classification, topographic sheets, and multi-date satellite imagery, the city’s growth patterns were quantified geospatially. The results show that Kano expanded from 27.50 km 2 in 1950 to 355.25 km 2 in 2020, an increase of 1,192.73% over 7 decades, and the average annual growth rate of 3.71%. The highest growth was recorded between 1975 and 1990 (72.75 km 2 to 162.00 km 2 ), with an annual growth rate of 5.53%, while the slowest growth was recorded between 1990 and 2000 (1.66% per year). Corridor-based analysis reveals pronounced variability, with the Kano–Panshekara (5.47%), Kano–Gwarzo (4.95%), and Kano–Dawanau (3.13%) corridors emerging as the fastest-growing axes, while Kano–Hadejia–Nguru (1.52%) and Fanisau (1.08%) corridors record lower growth. The study concludes that transportation development has played a significant role in shaping Kano Municipality’s spatial expansion. It also highlights the need to integrate transport investment with land-use planning, infrastructure provision, and environmental management to promote a more connected, resilient, and sustainable urban system.

title: Analysis halal information disclosure for firm value and performance
summary: Indonesia, as one of the countries with the largest Muslim populations, places considerable importance on halal-related information associated with products. This study aims to examine the impact of halal information disclosure on firm valu
content: Indonesia, as one of the countries with the largest Muslim populations, places considerable importance on halal-related information associated with products. This study aims to examine the impact of halal information disclosure on firm value and performance by introducing halal information disclosure as a novelty. Using a sample of consumer non-cyclicals companies in the food and beverage subsector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2019–2023 period, this study finds that halal information disclosure has no significant effect on earnings per share (EPS), sales, price-to-book value (PBV), or Tobin's Q. These findings indicate halal information disclosure has not yet generated measurable economic benefits for firms. One possible explanation is that the observation period coincided with the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent economic recovery, during which stakeholders were more concerned with firms' operational resilience and financial stability than with halal-related disclosures. Consequently, the potential value of halal information disclosure may not have been fully recognized by investors and other.

title: The Leadership CODE for AI Transformation: Unlocking Economic Value through Change Management and Human-Centred Design
source: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Smart Business and Innovation
summary: INTRODUCTION: Despite heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure and talent, an estimated 70–85% of digital transformation projects fail, partly because human-focused leadership models are lacking.OBJECTIVES: This study deve
content: INTRODUCTION: Despite heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure and talent, an estimated 70–85% of digital transformation projects fail, partly because human-focused leadership models are lacking.OBJECTIVES: This study develops and illustrates the CODE Framework, an integrative leadership model combining change management, behavioural economics, human-centred design and ethical governance.METHODS: A qualitative theoretical synthesis was combined with a comparative case study of two organisations, JPMorgan Chase and Lenovo.RESULTS: The four pillars (Clarity of Vision, Organisational Alignment, Design for Humans and Ethical Governance) proved mutually reinforcing, with measurable outcomes evident in both organisations.CONCLUSION: The framework offers leaders an integrated roadmap for artificial intelligence-driven transformation, and the case evidence is preliminary and exploratory rather than a validation.

title: Who should pay for energy transition costs? Political ideology and distributive fairness in Alberta
summary: Public support for energy transition does not necessarily imply agreement over how its costs and benefits should be distributed. As governments accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy, political conflict increasingly centers not on w
content: Public support for energy transition does not necessarily imply agreement over how its costs and benefits should be distributed. As governments accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy, political conflict increasingly centers not on whether the transition should occur, but on whether its economic burdens and benefits are allocated fairly. This paper examines how left–right political ideology shapes perceptions of distributive fairness in Alberta's energy transition. Using original survey data from 1527 Alberta residents, multivariate regression models analyze four dimensions of distributive fairness: funding mechanisms, responsibility for transition costs, the regional distribution of costs, and the regional distribution of benefits. The findings show that political ideology exerts selective rather than universal effects. Ideological differences are strongest when policies explicitly redistribute economic costs or benefits, particularly through higher taxes on the oil and gas industry and the regional distribution of transition benefits. By contrast, other dimensions of distributive fairness are more consistently associated with household energy burden, local energy dependence, institutional confidence, climate concern, and broader political value orientations. These findings demonstrate that distributive fairness is a distinct and multidimensional aspect of public opinion, with different distributive questions activating different political and contextual considerations. Rather than serving simply as a proxy for support for energy transition, distributive fairness reflects how citizens evaluate the political legitimacy of allocating transition costs and benefits. The study suggests that the long-term political durability of energy transition depends not only on reducing emissions but also on designing policies that citizens perceive as distributively fair.

title: Volumetric Waste: Containing Polymorphous Plastic in Bangkok’s Circular Economies
summary: This paper examines how volumetric reasoning permeates everyday practices in Bangkok’s circular economies. While circular economies calculate, value, and contain plastic waste, mobile waste flows are hidden from view and often evade regulat
content: This paper examines how volumetric reasoning permeates everyday practices in Bangkok’s circular economies. While circular economies calculate, value, and contain plastic waste, mobile waste flows are hidden from view and often evade regulation. As a result, circular economy initiatives struggle to account for low-value waste, microplastics, and chemicals that proliferate through land, water, air, and blood in bodies. In these instances, waste travels and transforms volumetrically without a traceable latitude and longitude. Similarly, the actual dimensions of plastic objects impact their ability to be valued in the circular economy. Drawing on seventeen months of ethnographic fieldwork in Bangkok, Thailand, this paper documents how circular economy practitioners manage waste that takes on new materialities as it moves through plastic circularity loops. Nonstate waste practitioners invoke volumetric reasoning as they grapple with circular economy solutions (e.g., recovering, repurposing, and upcycling plastics). My argument is twofold: first, I argue that practitioners’ everyday volumetric practices expose the limits of formal circular economy policy. Second, I argue that volumetric reasoning gives practitioners a set of techniques for reclaiming agency over the everyday management of waste. By attending to commonplace yet novel spatial dimensions of plastic circularity, this paper contributes to emerging scholarship at the intersection of political ecology and volumetric analyses of plastic pollution in Asia.

title: Drivers of blockchain technology adoption in construction supply chains: a systematic literature review and scientometric synthesis
source: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications
summary: Purpose Blockchain technology (BT) has attracted growing attention in construction supply chain management (CSCM), yet existing research predominantly emphasises applications, technical architectures and barriers, providing limited understa
content: Purpose Blockchain technology (BT) has attracted growing attention in construction supply chain management (CSCM), yet existing research predominantly emphasises applications, technical architectures and barriers, providing limited understanding of the pressures motivating adoption. This study, therefore, systematically identifies and synthesises the drivers of BT adoption in construction supply chains (CSCs). Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review, conducted using the Scopus database, yielded 493 records. Following screening, 145 publications were retained for scientometric analysis, with 40 subsequently selected for qualitative content analysis. Findings The findings identify five interrelated driver themes: information governance; transactional and operational pressures; digital integration; sustainability and institutional pressures; and strategic and contextual pressures. Information fragmentation, limited visibility, trust and accountability deficits, coordination inefficiencies and unreliable provenance emerged as the most prominent motivations. However, driver salience varies across clients, contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, regulators and other supply-chain actors, demonstrating that adoption is a negotiated network-level decision rather than a uniform organisational response. Originality/value The findings provide a theoretically grounded basis for empirical research and help practitioners and policymakers align BT investments, governance arrangements and procurement interventions with clearly defined supply-chain problems rather than technology-led experimentation.

title: Impacts of anticipated changes in the operational environment on forest resources and potential timber supply in Europe
summary: European forests and forestry are facing multiple changes now and in the coming decades. Understanding how these changes may alter forest resources and timber supply is crucial for anticipating future risks and guiding sustainable forest po
content: European forests and forestry are facing multiple changes now and in the coming decades. Understanding how these changes may alter forest resources and timber supply is crucial for anticipating future risks and guiding sustainable forest policy and management. Based on the literature, we identified eight factors stemming from political, economic, social, technological, and environmental developments and mapped experts’ and stakeholders’ views via a survey. Respondents were asked to assess both the directional trend and the magnitude of the anticipated changes in forest resources and potential timber supply across Europe by 2040. In addition to natural disturbances and extreme events, respondents perceived changes in trees’ growing conditions due to climate change to be the most significant factors. However, most expected the impacts to remain minor by 2040. The perceived effects varied in direction: nearly all factors were expected to either decrease or have no impact on the forest area available for wood production. On average, respondents anticipated an increase in dead wood volume per hectare and an increase in tree species richness across all change factors. Furthermore, generally, respondents anticipated a reduction in the volumes of conifer sawlogs and veneer logs, and conifer pulpwood resulting from nearly all change factors.

title: Norfloxacin-loaded chitosan–zinc phthalocyanine hydrogels for photodynamic antibacterial therapy
summary: Antimicrobial resistance and infected wounds require localized systems capable of combining controlled antibiotic delivery with light-activated antibacterial action. Here, norfloxacin-loaded chitosan hydrogels containing an aldehyde-functio
content: Antimicrobial resistance and infected wounds require localized systems capable of combining controlled antibiotic delivery with light-activated antibacterial action. Here, norfloxacin-loaded chitosan hydrogels containing an aldehyde-functionalized zinc phthalocyanine (ZnPc) were developed as dual chemo-photodynamic platforms. ZnPc was covalently incorporated through Schiff-base formation, acting simultaneously as a photosensitizer and secondary crosslinker. Formulations containing 1–10 mg ZnPc and 10 mg norfloxacin were evaluated structurally, morphologically, thermally, mechanically, rheologically, and biologically. FTIR and XRD supported covalent ZnPc incorporation and homogeneous, predominantly amorphous component distribution. ZnPc strengthened the hydrogel network, reduced swelling, and enabled composition-dependent tuning of mechanical and release properties. Norfloxacin loading efficiencies remained above 94%, while 24-h release was greater at pH 5.8 (up to 96%) than at pH 7.7 (25–56%). All ZnPc-containing systems generated singlet oxygen under 660-nm irradiation, with relative efficiencies increasing with ZnPc content. Cs-ZnPc-3-Norf showed the strongest antibacterial response, producing 1.09-log and 0.52-log reductions in Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus , respectively. However, its extract reduced L929 fibroblast metabolic activity even after dilution, indicating that formulation optimization is required before further biomedical evaluation.

title: DETERMINANTS OF ADOPTING CLIMATE-SMART AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES AMONG SOYBEANS FARMERS IN TORO LOCAL GOVERNMENT AREA, BAUCHI STATE, NIGERIA
source: International Journal of Agriculture and Agricultural Technology
summary: This study investigates the Determinants of Adopting Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices among Soybeans Farmers in Toro LGA, Bauchi State, Nigeria. The study employed a descriptive survey research design utilizing a structured questionnair
content: This study investigates the Determinants of Adopting Climate-Smart Agricultural Practices among Soybeans Farmers in Toro LGA, Bauchi State, Nigeria. The study employed a descriptive survey research design utilizing a structured questionnaire to collect data from 160 smallholder soybean farmers. Data were analysed using descriptive (frequency, percentages, mean, standard deviation and rank) and inferential (multivariate probit regression model) statistical techniques. Findings revealed that mixed cropping rank first among the practices they adopted, followed by adopting early maturing varieties, whereas irrigation rank the lowest among the practices. Furthermore findings reveal that level of education, access to extension service delivery, farm size, income level positively influence smallholder soybean farmers potentials to adopt to climate smart agricultural practices. The findings underscore the necessity of tailored interventions that foster the adoption of effective climate change adaptation strategies to enhance food security among soybean farmers in the Toro Local Government Area. The study advocates for policies that prioritize access to resources, education, and innovative agricultural practices to strengthen the resilience of smallholder farmers against the adverse effects of climate change.

title: Agroecology in West Africa: the pathway towards a sustainable transition of agri-food systems? A review
summary: This article reviews the state of the art on the potential of agroecology to contribute to the sustainable transformation of agrifood systems in West Africa. Data were retrieved from Scopus, PubMed, Google Scholar and grey literature. The 4
content: This article reviews the state of the art on the potential of agroecology to contribute to the sustainable transformation of agrifood systems in West Africa. Data were retrieved from Scopus, PubMed, Google Scholar and grey literature. The 484 publications reviewed span the last 25 years, focusing primarily on West Africa, while selected studies from other regions were included where relevant to the analysis. Over the past two decades, agroecology has gained a growing interest in different scientific fields, and is increasingly discussed as an alternative approach to conventional agricultural models. The reviewed evidence suggests that several agroecological practices are rooted in local knowledge and may contribute to addressing some of the environmental and food-systems challenges facing the region. However, the nature and the magnitude of these contributions remain context-dependent and unevenly documented across the region. Existing studies point to potential benefits for agricultural resilience, food security and nutrition, biodiversity, socioeconomic viability, human values, but the available evidence remains insufficient to highlight the potential of agroecology for food systems transformation. Scaling up agroecology is further constrained by interrelated challenges, including limited training and advisory services, restricted access to inputs and markets, and policy support. In many regions, research on agroecology has covered only a limited range of topics, highlighting the need for more context-specific and multidimensional science. Future studies should investigate the conditions under which agroecological transitions are most likely to succeed, including the interactions among policy support, training, resource access, markets, and economic incentives. Greater attention is also needed to its socioeconomic viability and to the development of locally adapted advisory and support services.

title: Environmental Plasticity and Protein Potential of Soybean Varieties Developed by LLP ‘Oil Crops Experimental Farm’ under the Conditions of the East Kazakhstan Region
summary: Soybean productivity and seed quality are strongly influenced by hydrothermal conditions, making the identification of environmentally adaptable varieties essential for stable production under changing climatic conditions.This study evaluat
content: Soybean productivity and seed quality are strongly influenced by hydrothermal conditions, making the identification of environmentally adaptable varieties essential for stable production under changing climatic conditions.This study evaluated the yield, protein and oil content, protein productivity, and environmental plasticity of soybean varieties developed by LLP "Oil Crops Experimental Farm" in the East Kazakhstan Region during 2021-2025.Eight varieties were evaluated under contrasting agroclimatic conditions and compared with the standards Annushka and Berlik.Hydrothermal conditions were characterized using Selyaninov's hydrothermal coefficient (HTC), while yield stability and environmental responsiveness were assessed using analysis of variance and the Eberhart-Russell model.The study years ranged from dry conditions in 2022 (HTC = 0.46) to wet conditions in 2025 (HTC = 1.32).Mean protein content among the evaluated varieties ranged from 39.9% to 40.8%, with Otan plus (40.8%) and Nur plus (40.7%) recording the highest values among the early-maturing varieties.Atameken had the highest mean yield among the early-maturing varieties (23.0 dt/ha), whereas Zhaz achieved the highest overall mean yield (25.7 dt/ha).Based on regression coefficients, Atameken (bi = 1.30),Nur plus (bi = 1.06), and Otan plus (bi = 1.02) were highly responsive to favorable environmental conditions, while Zhaz (bi = 0.89), Progress (bi = 0.81), and Eurasia (bi = 0.76) demonstrated lower environmental sensitivity and greater stability.Zhaz and Eurasia also produced high mean protein yields of 1038.9 and 1018.6 kg/ha, respectively.Overall, the results identified distinct groups of intensive and stable soybean varieties, providing useful breeding and production material for soybean cultivation under the sharply continental conditions of East Kazakhstan.

title: Development of Lipid-Polymer combined Oral micelles for Enhanced Oral Delivery of Lovastatin
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Lovastatin is a Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) Class II drug characterized by poor aqueous solubility and limited oral bioavailability, resulting in variable therapeutic performance.The present study aimed to develop, optimize
content: Lovastatin is a Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) Class II drug characterized by poor aqueous solubility and limited oral bioavailability, resulting in variable therapeutic performance.The present study aimed to develop, optimize, and evaluate lovastatin-loaded nanoparticulate carriers for enhancing solubility, dissolution rate, and oral bioavailability.Oral micelles were prepared using a nanoprecipitation technique employing poly(lactic-coglycolic acid) (PLGA) as the polymeric carrier and Poloxamer 188 as a stabilizer.A Box-Behnken design was utilized to optimize formulation variables including polymer concentration, surfactant concentration, and stirring speed.The optimized formulation was characterized for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, drug entrapment efficiency, surface morphology, in vitro dissolution, stability, and pharmacokinetic performance.The optimized oral micelles exhibited a mean particle size of 145.6 ± 4.2 nm, polydispersity index of 0.221 ± 0.03, zeta potential of -31.4 ± 2.1 mV, and entrapment efficiency of 89.3 ± 1.8%.Scanning electron microscopy revealed spherical and uniformly distributed particles.In vitro dissolution studies demonstrated a significant increase in drug release compared with pure lovastatin, with more than 90% release within 60 min.Pharmacokinetic studies indicated a 2.3-fold increase in oral bioavailability compared with the marketed formulation.Stability studies confirmed the physical stability of oral micelles over three months.The findings suggest that nanoparticulate carriers represent a promising strategy for improving the biopharmaceutical properties and therapeutic efficacy of lovastatin.

title: Are domestic long-distance travel and international flying complementary? Evidence from England’s National Travel Survey, 2015–2019
summary: Research on the demand and climate impacts of domestic and international long-distance travel (LDT) has expanded rapidly, yet comparatively little is known about whether these two domains are behaviourally interlinked; that is, whether part
content: Research on the demand and climate impacts of domestic and international long-distance travel (LDT) has expanded rapidly, yet comparatively little is known about whether these two domains are behaviourally interlinked; that is, whether participation in one is associated with participation in, or the intensity of, the other. This paper addresses that gap by examining the relationship between domestic LDT and international flying at both the extensive (participation) and intensive (frequency) margins within a common analytical framework. Using pooled National Travel Survey data for England (2015–2019), the study estimates zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) models of annual trips per person with cross-domain participation as a key explanatory variable and a control-function correction for potential endogeneity across both domains. Conditional mixed process (CMP) simultaneous-equation models provide a broader robustness check. Descriptively, among respondents aged 16 and above, those who had taken at least one international flight in the previous year (fliers) were substantially more mobile domestically than those who didn’t. Fliers travelled around 50 % further in total but nearly twice as far in domestic long-distance trips, generating proportionally higher emissions than non-fliers, suggesting the main divide lies in longer-distance rather than everyday travel. ZINB models show a positive bidirectional association between domestic LDT and international flying at the extensive margin, where participation in one domain is associated with a higher likelihood of participation in the other. At the intensive margin, however, the association becomes asymmetric, as international flying participation is not associated with higher LDT frequency among its participants. CMP models point to modest shared unobserved drivers of entry across both domains and identify another directional asymmetry, as domestic LDT frequency is not associated with international flying participation. Together these patterns indicate asymmetric co-variation rather than symmetric patterning and support treating domestic and international long-distance travel as interconnected components of individual mobility.

title: Green Versus Sustainable Loans: The Impact on Firms' ESG Performance
summary: ABSTRACT This paper studies the development of a firm's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance following the issuance of “green loans” earmarked for green projects versus “sustainable loans” benchmarked by ESG criteria. Fir
content: ABSTRACT This paper studies the development of a firm's Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance following the issuance of “green loans” earmarked for green projects versus “sustainable loans” benchmarked by ESG criteria. Firms issuing green loans improve environmental performance, particularly by reducing emissions, but experience declines in social performance, suggesting a trade‐off between environmental and social objectives. In contrast, sustainable loans are associated with broader ESG improvements, enhancing environmental and governance outcomes without a comparable social decline. Overall, loan design shapes corporate sustainability behaviour: green loans generate targeted environmental gains, whereas sustainable loans foster more balanced and holistic ESG performance improvements.

title: Diverse coupling between climate change, socio-economic factors and climate potential productivity in Africa
summary: Africa’s accelerating climate warming has rendered its climate potential productivity (CPP) increasingly vulnerable, raising global concerns over biodiversity, water resources, and food security. Understanding the long‑term evolution of CPP
content: Africa’s accelerating climate warming has rendered its climate potential productivity (CPP) increasingly vulnerable, raising global concerns over biodiversity, water resources, and food security. Understanding the long‑term evolution of CPP and its driving mechanisms has therefore become an urgent research priority. This study analyses the spatiotemporal patterns and correlates of CPP across Africa, using the Thornthwaite Memorial model in combination with trend detection, correlation, and econometric analyses. The results reveal a declining CPP trend over 1901–2019, with a distinct latitudinal zonal distribution. CPP is highly sensitive to both temperature and precipitation. Continued deterioration is a likely consequence of future warmer and drier conditions. During 2000–2019, the predictive associations between CPP and industrialization, energy consumption, and PM2.5 emissions are directionally heterogeneous. CPP exhibits a unidirectional association with industrialization and PM2.5 emissions, while maintaining a bidirectional association with energy consumption. The industrialization‑CPP relationship follows an environmental Kuznets curve pattern, while CPP correlates positively with energy consumption and weakly negatively with PM2.5. These findings provide a scientific basis for understanding the dynamic evolution of Africa’s CPP and the socio‑ecological factors, and offer quantitative insights into the trade‑offs and synergies among environmental health, climate suitability, and industrial development in the region.

title: Design and Tunability of Thermochromic Polymers Based on Dye–Developer–Solvent Systems: Toward Non-Toxic Materials
summary: Abstract Thermochromic polymers have had significant development over the years through consistent research. Specifically, polymers that involve an embedded ternary thermochromic compound, which consists of a dye, color developer, and cosol
content: Abstract Thermochromic polymers have had significant development over the years through consistent research. Specifically, polymers that involve an embedded ternary thermochromic compound, which consists of a dye, color developer, and cosolvent, have garnered a lot of attention for the tunability of their color-changing properties. These compounds exhibit color changes through the mechanism of proton transfer between the dye and developer species, and the presence of a solvent is crucial to facilitating this phenomenon. By manipulating the type of each component within the dye-developer-solvent (DDS) compound, the color, direction of color change, and phase transition temperature can be adjusted. The fabrication of thermochromic polymers with DDS compounds can be done through encapsulation, impregnation into a porous material, coating, or a combination of encapsulation and compounding with a polymer matrix. Potential applications of temperature-sensitive polymers include temperature sensors and heat regulators in packaging, clothing, medical devices, and architecture. Research efforts are being continuously made on DDS compounds to make them safer and more eco-friendly with the replacement of conventional components with biobased materials. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the working principle of ternary thermochromic DDS compounds, the tunability of the thermochromic properties, the current progress of research on utilizing DDS compounds in polymers, and the prospects in developing nontoxic thermochromic polymers for food packaging and medical applications.

title: Performance limits and stability horizons in next-generation anion exchange membrane water electrolysis for hydrogen production
summary: In this paper, we reviewed the performance boundaries and operational stability horizons governing next-generation AEMWE platforms. This review study indicates that standard state-of-the-art AEMWE configurations achieve industrially relevan
content: In this paper, we reviewed the performance boundaries and operational stability horizons governing next-generation AEMWE platforms. This review study indicates that standard state-of-the-art AEMWE configurations achieve industrially relevant cell voltages of 1.7–1.9 V at 1.0 A cm⁻², with optimized systems reaching current densities up to ~2.0–2.7 A cm⁻² at ~1.8 V as reported in literatures. Membrane hydroxide conductivity typically spans 50–100 mS cm⁻¹ at 60–80 °C with water uptake levels between 20 wt.% and 80 wt.%. While hydrogen Faradaic efficiencies consistently exceed 95–99% under steady-state, transient operating conditions can drop this metric to 90–95% due to gas crossover. Operational stability remains the primary commercialization bottleneck; reported cell degradation rates vary significantly from 10 μV h⁻¹ to >1000 μV h⁻¹ under continuous testing, driven by quaternary ammonium functional group decay, backbone cleavage via nucleophilic attack, catalyst dissolution, support corrosion, and electrode delamination. Addressing these constraints through advanced hydrocarbon membrane chemistries, tailored ionomer cross-linking, optimized porous transport layers, and standardized AST protocols is essential to meet the Clean Hydrogen Partnership target of degradation rates below 0.5% per 1000 hours at current densities above 1.5 A cm⁻².

title: Firm-Level Digital and Sustainability Indicators and Sustainability Outcomes: Evidence from Chinese Listed Industrial Firms under Environmental Regulation
summary: This study examined the associations between digital and organizational capabilities and sustainability outcomes among 200 industrial firms listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in China from 2013 to 2023. The study applied the theory of Dy
content: This study examined the associations between digital and organizational capabilities and sustainability outcomes among 200 industrial firms listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in China from 2013 to 2023. The study applied the theory of Dynamic Capabilities and Institutional Theory to explore the digital transformation, corporate sustainability culture, cultural capital and digital media literacy, and their relationship with environmental performance and sustainability innovation. Media coverage intensity and the financial support of sustainability initiatives were investigated as possible indirect pathways and environmental regulation as a moderating institutional condition. Firm and year fixed-effects models were supplemented with dynamic System GMM and bootstrapped indirect-effect analysis, moderation analysis, and robustness specifications. The findings indicate that digital transformation, corporate sustainability culture, and digital media literacy were positively associated with both environmental performance and sustainability innovation, whereas cultural capital was positively associated with sustainability innovation but not environmental performance. Media coverage intensity and financial support for sustainability initiatives showed statistically supported indirect associations for digital transformation, corporate sustainability culture, and digital media literacy, but not cultural capital. Environmental regulation generally strengthened the positive capability–sustainability associations, while its negative interaction with cultural capital for sustainability innovation provided only tentative evidence of a weakening association, as the interaction was significant only at the 10% level. These findings contribute to the Dynamic Capabilities Theory by bringing into focus capability-specific sustainability associations and the Institutional Theory by establishing differentiated regulatory conditions. The indirect effects and relationships estimated are therefore viewed as associative in nature for the purpose of the observational panel design.

title: Aligning clean energy innovations with the SDGs: sectoral dynamics of green bonds and sustainability-enhanced equities across market conditions
source: Journal of Environmental Economics and Policy
summary: This study examines the dynamic interconnections among clean energy innovations, green bonds, and sectoral sustainability-enhanced equities, and their implications for advancing SDGs 7, 9, 11, 12, and 13. Using a Quantile VAR model and dail
content: This study examines the dynamic interconnections among clean energy innovations, green bonds, and sectoral sustainability-enhanced equities, and their implications for advancing SDGs 7, 9, 11, 12, and 13. Using a Quantile VAR model and daily data from 31 October 2016–27 December 2024, we decompose systemic spillovers across extremely adverse (5th quantile), typical (50th quantile), and highly favourable (95th quantile) market conditions. Our results reveal a pronounced U-shaped pattern in systemic integration: the Total Connectedness Index surges to near-peak levels of approximately 89–95% at both tails, indicating that diversification benefits collapse during crises and market exuberance alike. Clean energy, green bonds, and utilities consistently act as net receivers, absorbing shocks transmitted by cyclical sectors. In contrast, industrials and consumer discretionary emerge as persistent net transmitters that drive systemic risk. Defensive sectors, notably healthcare and consumer staples, remain relatively resilient across all regimes. Importantly, green bonds, often perceived as safe-haven assets, exhibit state-dependent vulnerability to tail shocks, challenging their unconditional stabilising role. These findings imply that portfolio managers must abandon reliance on average-correlation diversification and instead adopt tail-risk-aware, dynamically allocated strategies. For regulators, the results underscore the need to integrate climate-aligned, quantile-dependent stress testing into macroprudential frameworks to safeguard financial stability during the low-carbon transition. By linking sectoral spillover dynamics to SDG outcomes, this research provides actionable guidance to enhance the resilience of sustainable finance ecosystems.Key Policy HighlightsSystemic connectedness rises to 89–95% during market stress and exuberance, sharply reducing diversification benefits.Industrial and consumer discretionary sectors are the main transmitters of shocks and should be prioritised in systemic risk monitoring.Clean energy, utilities, and green bonds primarily absorb shocks, making them vulnerable to spillovers from other sectors.Green bonds do not consistently act as safe-haven assets during extreme market conditions.Quantile-based climate stress testing and tail-risk-sensitive regulation can strengthen financial resilience and support SDGs 7, 9, 11, 12, and 13.

title: Performance of sweet cherry trees trained to a central leader and pergola system
summary: Sweet cherry (Prunus avium (L.) L.) cultivation has expanded remarkably in Chile, surpassing 80 000 ha, driving the need for orchard management strategies that enhance precocity, profitability, fruit quality, and operational efficiency.This
content: Sweet cherry (Prunus avium (L.) L.) cultivation has expanded remarkably in Chile, surpassing 80 000 ha, driving the need for orchard management strategies that enhance precocity, profitability, fruit quality, and operational efficiency.This study evaluated the effect of two training systems with permanent wood renewal: Central leader and pergola, on light interception, leaf gas exchange, vegetative growth, and fruit production of 'Lapins'/'Colt' sweet cherry trees.Light interception by the trees was higher in pergola (83%) than in central leader (36%).Leaf transpiration rate and stomatal conductance in trees trained in the pergola system were 32% and 39% lower, respectively, compared with the central leader, although no differences were observed in photosynthetic rate.The leaf area per tree was 66% higher in the pergola system than that observed in central leader.Fruit production per tree did not differ between systems; however, pergola produced 49% more fruit per branch and 73% more leaf area per fruit than central leader.Fruit from trees trained on pergola were larger, but showed slightly less intense color and higher acidity compared to those from central leader, suggesting delayed ripening.These results provide relevant production indicators for decision-making in the establishment of new commercial sweet cherry orchards.

title: Regional coordination and industrial green total factor productivity: evidence from the yangtze river delta economic coordination council
summary: Introduction Fragmented local governance can limit productivity-based industrial greening in urban agglomerations, especially when production activities, environmental externalities, and innovation flows extend across administrative boundar
content: Introduction Fragmented local governance can limit productivity-based industrial greening in urban agglomerations, especially when production activities, environmental externalities, and innovation flows extend across administrative boundaries. This study examines whether formal regional coordination improves industrial green total factor productivity by alleviating institutional fragmentation. Methods Using panel data for Chinese cities from 2004 to 2024, we use the staggered accession of cities to a regional coordination institution as a quasi-experimental setting and estimate its effects with staggered-adoption difference-in-differences models. Cities outside the coordinated region that were never exposed to the institution serve as an external comparison group for later-period identification. Results Regional coordination significantly improves industrial green total factor productivity, and the effect becomes stronger over time. Further analysis suggests that this improvement is related to reduced capital and labour misallocation, stronger environmental regulation, smaller regulatory differences across jurisdictions, and greater green innovation. The effect is more pronounced in cities with larger initial economic scale, while spatial econometric results indicate positive spillovers to neighbouring cities. Discussion These findings suggest that formal regional coordination can help convert fragmented local regulation into more coherent environmental governance, providing evidence for urban agglomerations seeking cleaner and more efficient industrial development.

title: Risk Allocation in Public-Private Industrial Megaprojects: A Systematic Evidence Review and Implications for Saudi Automotive Development
source: BİLTÜRK Journal of Economics and Related Studies
summary: Risk allocation shapes the bankability, value for money, and long-term performance of public-private partnerships (PPPs), yet the evidence remains dispersed across infrastructure sectors and is rarely translated to industrial megaprojects.
content: Risk allocation shapes the bankability, value for money, and long-term performance of public-private partnerships (PPPs), yet the evidence remains dispersed across infrastructure sectors and is rarely translated to industrial megaprojects. This systematic evidence review synthesizes risk-allocation research and derives bounded implications for Saudi automotive development. Six OpenAlex searches were conducted on 22 July 2026 for peer-reviewed work published from 2000 to the search date. Crossref and source pages verified bibliographic data, while official Saudi and World Bank materials supplied policy context. Of 446 unique records screened, 75 underwent detailed eligibility assessment and 41 peer-reviewed studies were included. Framework-based synthesis identifies eight evidence domains: allocation principles; political and institutional risk; finance and demand; construction and technical delivery; operations and lifecycle performance; governance and renegotiation; private participation; and sustainability. The evidence rejects both maximal risk transfer and static allocation. Risks should be assigned to the party best able to influence probability or impact, absorb residual exposure at least cost, and exercise the required decision rights. Uncontrollable or policy-created risks may require sharing, relief events, guarantees, indexed payments, or contingent support. A lifecycle framework is developed for automotive industrial ecosystems covering enabling infrastructure, permitting, construction, technology, localization, demand, utilities, supply chains, workforce, environmental performance, and change in law.

title: Do firms conducting environmental projects funded by European Regional Development Funds perform better in Galicia (Spain)? The role of innovation
summary: This study assesses the effectiveness of regional business innovation policies in the field of environmental and technological development in Galicia (Spain) through the Conecta Peme programme. Financed by the European Regional Development
content: This study assesses the effectiveness of regional business innovation policies in the field of environmental and technological development in Galicia (Spain) through the Conecta Peme programme. Financed by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) under the regional operational framework, this initiative aimed to strengthen collaboration among SMEs, research centres, and technological partners to enhance innovation capacity and sustainable competitiveness in the Galician economy. The analysis examines the programme’s impact on key firm-level performance indicators, distinguishing between projects with explicit environmental and sustainability objectives and those without such goals. Employing a combined propensity score matching (PSM) and difference-in-differences (DiD) approach, complemented by robustness checks, the study assesses the effects of participation in Conecta Peme on firms’ innovation-related and economic performance indicators. The findings reveal heterogeneous effects across indicators, but no robust evidence of systematically positive impacts on firms’ short-term economic performance, suggesting both the potential and the constraints of regional innovation policies in promoting environmental transformation and economic resilience.

title: Exploring the main determinants of green and sustainable sukuk issuance: a neo-institutional perspective
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the main factors that influence the issuance of green and sustainable sukuk (GSS). Specifically, it investigates how institutional, environmental, and economic pressures shape GSS issuance across countries
content: Purpose This study aims to examine the main factors that influence the issuance of green and sustainable sukuk (GSS). Specifically, it investigates how institutional, environmental, and economic pressures shape GSS issuance across countries that have developed this market. Design/methodology/approach The study uses panel data from all 12 countries that issued GSS during the period 2017–2024. Drawing on neo-institutional theory, it examines five groups of determinants of GSS issuance: institutional quality, which represents coercive pressures; CO2 emissions and urbanization, which represent normative pressures; and foreign direct investment (FDI) and gross domestic product (GDP), which represent mimetic pressures. The empirical analysis employs the two-step System Generalized Method of Moments (System GMM) estimator to account for the dynamic nature of GSS issuance and potential endogeneity. The robustness of the results is further assessed using the Double Machine Learning (DML) approach. Findings The findings show that coercive pressures and some mimetic pressures are more relevant to GSS issuance than normative pressures. Institutional factors, including government effectiveness, regulatory quality, rule of law, and political stability, have positive and statistically significant effects on GSS issuance, which highlights the importance of a strong institutional framework for GSS market development. In contrast, normative pressures, measured by CO2 emissions and urbanization, are not statistically significant. This suggests that environmental and urbanization pressures alone do not directly stimulate GSS issuance. Among the mimetic pressures, FDI has a positive and robust effect on GSS issuance, whereas GDP has a positive but statistically insignificant effect. Practical implications The findings provide important implications for policymakers seeking to develop GSS markets. The results suggest that strong institutional and regulatory conditions are important for supporting GSS issuance. Policymakers should therefore strengthen government effectiveness, regulatory quality, the rule of law, and political stability to create a favorable institutional environment for GSS markets. Policies that attract foreign investment may also support GSS market development. By contrast, environmental pressures, such as CO2 emissions and urbanization, do not appear to be sufficient on their own to stimulate GSS issuance. These findings suggest that environmental objectives should be supported by appropriate institutional and regulatory frameworks. Originality/value The originality of this study lies in its cross-country analysis of the determinants of GSS issuance. To the best of our knowledge, it is one of the few empirical studies to jointly examine institutional quality, CO2 emissions, urbanization, FDI, GDP as potential determinants of GSS issuance within a neo-institutional framework.
