title: Techno-optimistic scientists take fewer climate actions
summary: Abstract Technological innovation is key to mitigating climate change, yet excessive faith in technology may undermine the wider societal transformations needed to address it. In their roles as knowledge producers and trusted public figures
content: Abstract Technological innovation is key to mitigating climate change, yet excessive faith in technology may undermine the wider societal transformations needed to address it. In their roles as knowledge producers and trusted public figures, scientists play an important part in shaping how societies understand and respond to climate change. We examine techno-optimism—here defined as the belief that technology will largely solve the problems caused by climate change—among scientists using survey data from N = 9199 scientists across 115 countries. Our findings show that techno-optimism is most prevalent among scientists in applied and natural sciences, and among those with right-leaning political views, but does not vary with the extent to which one’s research is related to climate change. Techno-optimistic scientists are substantially less likely to engage in civic climate action (23% lower) or make high-impact lifestyle changes (18% lower). We hope that our study can contribute to a critical discussion about how scientists’ own beliefs and worldviews shape their understanding of, and engagement in, climate action.

title: Planting subsidies or brand building? Policy thresholds and goal conflict in agribusiness-led contract farming
summary: Introduction Under yield uncertainty and agribusiness-led contract farming, government intervention is important for sustaining agricultural production and supporting farmer profit. Yet production-side planting subsidies and demand-side bra
content: Introduction Under yield uncertainty and agribusiness-led contract farming, government intervention is important for sustaining agricultural production and supporting farmer profit. Yet production-side planting subsidies and demand-side brand-building policies operate through different mechanisms, leaving their relative advantages and applicable conditions unclear. This study examines how the government should choose between the two policies and how firm social responsibility shapes their relative performance. Methods We develop a sequential game involving a government, an agribusiness firm, and a farmer under stochastic yield. The firm's objective incorporates concern for farmer profit. Equilibrium decisions are derived by backward induction, and the policies are compared in terms of social welfare and farmer profit. Numerical analysis illustrates the analytical results. Results The planting subsidy policy directly strengthens the farmer's production incentive, whereas the brand-building policy expands market demand and induces the firm to offer a higher procurement price. The benefits of brand building depend critically on its cost-effectiveness. We identify two endogenous thresholds: a social-welfare threshold and a farmer-profit threshold, with the former strictly lower than the latter. As brand-building cost-effectiveness increases, policy preference shifts through three regions: planting-subsidy dominance, goal conflict, and brand-building dominance. In the intermediate region, brand building generates higher social welfare, while the farmer remains better off under planting subsidies. Yield risk, price sensitivity, and planting costs widen the goal-conflict region, whereas higher expected yield and stronger firm social responsibility narrow it. Market size affects absolute outcomes but does not change the relative policy ranking. Discussion These findings extend the agricultural-policy literature from the design of production subsidies to the choice between production-side and demand-side interventions. They show that improvements in aggregate welfare do not necessarily translate into greater benefits for farmers.

title: Does diversity matter? Examining the association between board gender inclusion and greenwashing practices in ASEAN-5 countries
source: Journal of Asian Business and Economic Studies
summary: Purpose Although board gender inclusion has often been associated with greater engagement in sustainability initiatives, the rise of greenwashing raises questions about the authenticity of such commitments. Despite growing global attention,
content: Purpose Although board gender inclusion has often been associated with greater engagement in sustainability initiatives, the rise of greenwashing raises questions about the authenticity of such commitments. Despite growing global attention, empirical evidence on this issue remains limited in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) context. This study examines the association between board gender inclusion and greenwashing practices in ASEAN-5 countries (Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and the Philippines). Furthermore, it explores the moderating role of chief executive officer (CEO) duality, firm-level and institutional heterogeneity and critical mass dynamics in relation to greenwashing. Design/methodology/approach Our study uses an unbalanced panel of 322 nonfinancial listed companies across ASEAN-5 during 2016–2023. Data were obtained from Bloomberg, the London Stock Exchange Group and the World Bank. The analysis uses fixed-effect models with cluster-robust standard errors and a two-step generalized method of moments approach. Findings Board gender inclusion is associated with lower greenwashing. However, this association weakens when CEO duality is present. The analysis further indicates that board gender inclusion may mitigate greenwashing primarily among firms with high profitability, low leverage and small size, as well as in countries with stronger regulatory quality. In addition, the effect of board gender inclusion exhibits a critical mass threshold (approximately 20% of total board members), suggesting a meaningful level at which greenwashing may be reduced. Originality/value This study fills a critical gap in the literature on gender-diverse boards and greenwashing within the ASEAN context. By integrating the moderating role of CEO duality and examining critical mass theory, our study offers new empirical insight into how board gender inclusion may influence the integrity of corporate sustainability practices. Additionally, this study develops an alternative dummy-variable measure of greenwashing.

title: Effect of gentisic acid seed priming on growth, secondary metabolism, antioxidant defense, and nutrient acquisition in Zea mays L. under drought stress
summary: This work was performed to appraise the potential of gentisic acid seed priming (50, 150, and 200 mgL -1 ) for mitigating drought stress in maize plants.Drought stress resulted in high oxidative stress, as evident by high levels of hydrogen
content: This work was performed to appraise the potential of gentisic acid seed priming (50, 150, and 200 mgL -1 ) for mitigating drought stress in maize plants.Drought stress resulted in high oxidative stress, as evident by high levels of hydrogen peroxide, superoxide radicals, and malondialdehyde.Therefore, plants suffered a considerable reduction in growth parameters, chlorophyll contents, proteins, relative water contents, and plant nutrients.However, gentisic acid significantly improved plant growth, leaf pigments, and nutrient contents by regulating the antioxidant defense system and secondary metabolism.Moreover, gentisic acid conferred protection against drought induced oxidative stress by increasing signaling compounds (hydrogen sulfide and NO) that boosted the antioxidant system and mitigated oxidative damage.Seed priming with gentisic acid enhanced drought tolerance linked with antioxidants (non-enzymatic and enzymatic).Gentisic acid-mediated redox balance and osmoprotection helped mitigate drought effects, mainly in plants primed with 150 mgL -1 concentrations.The current work reveals gentisic acid priming as a potential approach to alleviate drought stress in maize plants.

title: From digital to real: The technology convergence and its impact on corporate employment expansion
summary: Promoting the deep integration of digital and real economy technologies and achieving high-quality full employment are important tasks in China’s high-quality economic development strategy. Based on panel data from Chinese A-share listed fi
content: Promoting the deep integration of digital and real economy technologies and achieving high-quality full employment are important tasks in China’s high-quality economic development strategy. Based on panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2014 to 2023, this paper measures technology convergence between digital and real economy industries (TCDR) from a micro perspective and empirically examines its employment effects. The results show that, first, TCDR significantly increases employment quantity and has a non-linear effect on employment quality, and the findings remain robust after endogeneity and robustness tests. Second, the mechanism analysis shows that TCDR promotes growth in employment quantity through production scale expansion, indicating a positive linear relationship in which the creation effect outweighs the inhibition effect. Meanwhile, TCDR has a non-linear effect on employment quality, initially suppressing and then improving it through productivity improvement, factor substitution, and enhanced market competitiveness. Finally, the heterogeneity analysis indicates that the employment effects of TCDR are shaped by internal firm characteristics, such as executives’ backgrounds and digital-technology bias; external conditions, such as government subsidies and digital infrastructure; and digital knowledge sources. Firms with a stronger digital-technology bias, as well as those that absorb more digital knowledge from the digital product services sector during the TCDR process, are more likely to achieve coordinated growth in employment quantity and employment quality.

title: Wastewater irrigation effects on contaminant fate soil quality nutritional traits and human health risks in rice agroecosystems with emphasis on microplastics
summary: Freshwater scarcity, rapid urbanization, and rising agricultural demand have increased interest in wastewater irrigation, especially in water-intensive rice systems. Wastewater reuse can support crop production through nutrient recycling an
content: Freshwater scarcity, rapid urbanization, and rising agricultural demand have increased interest in wastewater irrigation, especially in water-intensive rice systems. Wastewater reuse can support crop production through nutrient recycling and reduced fertilizer dependence, yet it also introduces a persistent mixture of contaminants into soil–plant systems. This review synthesizes evidence on contaminant fate, soil quality changes, nutritional effects, and human health risks associated with wastewater irrigation in rice agroecosystems, with particular emphasis on microplastics as an emerging pollutant. The reviewed literature shows that wastewater can improve soil fertility, increase nitrogen availability, and increase rice grain protein concentration and, in some systems, yield when wastewater supplies additional plant-available nutrients without excessive salinity or toxic-element loading. However, long-term use may also increase the accumulation of heavy metals, persistent organic pollutants, pathogens, salts, and microplastics. These contaminants can alter soil physical structure, nutrient cycling, and microbial activity, and may eventually enter edible rice tissues. Recent studies have detected microplastic particles in both raw and cooked rice and have identified polymers such as polyethylene (PE) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET), indicating that rice may represent a dietary exposure pathway; however, current evidence remains limited and does not yet establish the contribution of field irrigation relative to processing and packaging. This review adopts a global perspective while using Pakistan and other water-scarce regions as illustrative examples where wastewater irrigation is particularly relevant because of freshwater constraints, limited treatment infrastructure, and growing agricultural demand. The key challenge is not whether wastewater should be reused, but how to make its reuse safer through treatment, monitoring, and crop-specific management. The review concludes that sustainable wastewater irrigation requires stronger treatment infrastructure, standardized analytical methods, field-scale validation, and targeted risk assessment for both contaminants and nutritional benefits.

title: Is Europe a laggard? Comparing the EU and the US using an interdisciplinary well-being framework
summary: Well-being is increasingly recognized as a more meaningful measure of societal progress than economic output, yet most international comparisons continue to emphasize economic indicators. This focus has reinforced the perception that Europe
content: Well-being is increasingly recognized as a more meaningful measure of societal progress than economic output, yet most international comparisons continue to emphasize economic indicators. This focus has reinforced the perception that Europe is lagging behind the United States, with the productivity gap shaping the European Commission’s recent competitiveness agenda. Here, we compare European and American development from 1990–2023 using an interdisciplinary well-being framework that integrates five scientific schools of thought. We find that while the US increasingly outperformed the EU on productivity and income, the EU caught up in terms of various well-being indicators, including life satisfaction and education, while increasingly outperforming the US in life expectancy and safety. Europe also exhibits more equitable well-being outcomes and achieves them at lower environmental cost. However, in both regions, the conditions underpinning future well-being are under increasing pressure. These results challenge the dominance of economic metrics in evaluating progress and emphasize the need for inclusive development strategies that place sustainable well-being at their core.

title: Design hybrid renewable energy systems for electric vehicle charging stations at various sites in Pakistan
summary: The number of EVs is increasing rapidly globally, and that means the need for more sustainable and economical charging. A continuous supply of clean energy is required for the Highway EV charging stations that are crucial for intercity mobi
content: The number of EVs is increasing rapidly globally, and that means the need for more sustainable and economical charging. A continuous supply of clean energy is required for the Highway EV charging stations that are crucial for intercity mobility functions. One of the possible solutions is a hybrid renewable energy system technology, which has wind and solar photovoltaic (PV) energy. Most of the previous studies, though, are based on limited grid support and/or renewables penetration and system integration, limiting both sustainability and cost performance for high-demand applications. The authors suggest a solution for EV charging stations by proposing a hybrid wind-solar system grid-connected along the major motorway routes in Pakistan, namely, Bhera Motorway, Hakla Motorway, Karachi Northern Bypass, and Karakoram Highway. The novelty is the ability to achieve very near-grid-independent grid operation while still adhering to optimized renewable sizing, which helps minimize reliance on the conventional electricity grid and hence the amount of variability in the costs of grid energy. The system emphasizes the cost-optimized use of generation sizing with optimized grid interaction control whenever required and reduces battery investment, thus minimizing the system lifecycle cost. It can reduce energy costs, compared with fossil fuel transport energy (petrol and diesel), which makes it more sustainable in terms of the economy. Solar irradiance and wind speed data are solar-specific; EV load profiles are selected from the available ones in the EV automobile industry, and the grid characteristics of the exchange are run using the HOMER Grid software application to carry out the techno-economic analysis. One 250 kW wind turbine, one 400 kW solar PV array, and one 700 kW bidirectional DC–AC converter (modes: from DC to AC or from AC to DC) are built into each station, although the optimum sizing may differ depending on the location. The NPC of Bhera Motorway is around $15,929, LCOE is around $0.0225/kWh, and annual operating cost is around $11,643/yr. Combine the lowest cost configuration (Hakla Motorway ~ $7,893 with LCOE ~ $0.0214/kWh) to get the lowest cost overall. The NPC is the highest for Karachi Northern Bypass (ca. $78,214), and the highest LCOE for the four sites is at Karachi Northern Bypass (ca. $0.0286/kWh). It is found that the performance of the Karakoram Highway is similar to the Bhera site; the NPC is $15,951, and LCOE is $0.0225/kWh. Based on these conclusions, it can be seen that the deployment of a hybrid renewable system can offer affordable EV charging to achieve EV grid parity with low CAPEX and OPEX, which helps in transportation development in developing areas while being sustainable in nature.

title: Instability-Aware Digital Twin Control for Grid-Constrained Low-Carbon Smart Ports
summary: Modern smart ports combine terminal electrification, shore power, renewable generation, storage, and digital operational control under uncertain vessel traffic and time-varying grid limits. This study develops a simulation-based digital-twi
content: Modern smart ports combine terminal electrification, shore power, renewable generation, storage, and digital operational control under uncertain vessel traffic and time-varying grid limits. This study develops a simulation-based digital-twin control prototype that synchronizes vessel flow, berth occupancy, equipment activity, shore-power demand, renewable supply, battery state, grid import, and modelled emissions. A policy-weighted Instability Propagation Index (IPI) classifies lower-stress, critical-transition, and instability-dominated operating regimes and is embedded in an NSGA-II rolling-horizon controller for berth allocation, crane scheduling, vessel sequencing, shore-power timing, flexible loads, renewable curtailment, and battery dispatch. The confirmatory analysis uses a 720-h coupled congestion-and-grid-limit benchmark with 30 paired common-random-number replications, service-preservation controls, terminal-horizon accounting, optimizer-seed verification, and distribution-robust statistics. Relative to operation-focused, energy-focused, and decoupled policies, the proposed controller reduces operational energy by 8.9–21.2%, modelled grid-plus-queue emissions by 8.5–21.0%, peak grid import by 5.7–15.1%, and mean replication-level maximum IPI by 24.8–42.3%, while achieving the lowest composite vessel delay and highest berth-utilization efficiency. A 23 MW renewable portfolio with an 8 MW/16 MWh battery reduces net grid import from 14,510 to 8,370 MWh, peak import from 54.9 to 46.2 MW, modelled emissions from 8,040 to 4,847 tCO₂e, and mean maximum IPI from 0.82 to 0.68. The results demonstrate coordinated logistics–energy control within an externally grounded synthetic benchmark whose principal digital-twin, equipment, and shore-power operating scales are supported by published real-terminal evidence. Deployment at a specific port would nevertheless require local calibration of arrival, service, grid, emission, and control parameters.

title: QUANTITY SURVEYORS AS ENABLERS OF ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE INTEGRATION IN THE MALAYSIAN CONSTRUCTION INDUSTRY
summary: The increasing emphasis on sustainability in the Malaysian construction industry highlights the importance of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices as a structured approach to sustainable development. As a major contributor t
content: The increasing emphasis on sustainability in the Malaysian construction industry highlights the importance of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices as a structured approach to sustainable development. As a major contributor to Malaysia’s economic growth, the construction sector faces growing pressure to balance economic performance with ESG considerations. This study explores the evolving role of Quantity Surveyors (QSs) as enablers of ESG practices in the Malaysian construction industry. ESG indicators from the FTSE Russell ESG Scores published by Bursa Malaysia were used to examine the alignment between ESG principles and QS professional practices across construction stages. A qualitative approach was adopted through semi-structured interviews with six middle-management professionals from contractor firms. The findings reveal that QSs contribute significantly to ESG implementation through green procurement, occupational safety and health (OSH), and ethical governance. However, implementation is constrained by resistance to change, supply chain limitations, reporting challenges, project characteristics, and limited client support. The study highlights the need for stronger governance, digital solutions, incentives, standardized ESG reporting, and greater involvement of professional bodies.

title: Digital Green Bonds and ESG-Linked FinTech Platforms: Democratizing Sustainable Finance in Emerging Economies
source: Advanced International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research
summary: Convergence and digital finance and sustainability convergence has generated new institutional solutions, which comprise digital green bonds and ESG-linked FinTech solutions. They are not merely the financial products, but hypothetical cons
content: Convergence and digital finance and sustainability convergence has generated new institutional solutions, which comprise digital green bonds and ESG-linked FinTech solutions. They are not merely the financial products, but hypothetical constructions of the flow of financial resources, the democratization of the capital markets, the mechanisms of incorporating environmental and social governance into financial flows, and the restructuring of institutional standards in the emerging economies. This paper is devoted to building a theoretical perspective on these innovations, in the framework of the financial inclusion theory, the institutional innovation theory, and sustainability transition frameworks. It argues that digital green bonds and ESG-related platforms are transformational engines that increase participation, transparency, and bringing about systemic transitions towards low-carbon economies. The analysis puts these instruments into a wider argument of how these instruments are juxtaposed in the context of sustainable finance.

title: Optimizing sunflower performance through integrated irrigation and zeolite strategies in the north Nile Delta
summary: Abstract Two field studies were conducted at the Sakha Agricultural Research Station farm, Kafr El-Sheikh, Egypt, to evaluate zeolite and deficit irrigation through skipped irrigation events for sunflower. A split-plot statistical design wa
content: Abstract Two field studies were conducted at the Sakha Agricultural Research Station farm, Kafr El-Sheikh, Egypt, to evaluate zeolite and deficit irrigation through skipped irrigation events for sunflower. A split-plot statistical design was applied. Three irrigation regimes, i.e., irrigation every 12–15 days (I1, as a conventional irrigation), irrigation every 12–15 days but skipping the third irrigation event at 35 DAS (days after sowing) as I2, and skipping the sixth irrigation event at 65 DAS as I3. Three zeolite applications (i.e., no zeolite addition as a control, F1) and adding zeolite at a rate of 595 kg ha − 1 (F2) and 1190 kg ha − 1 (F3) for the subplot units. Results indicated that skipping irrigation events decreased leaf area by 9–13%, photosynthetic pigments by 9–16%, relative water content by 4–12%, seed yield by 10–14%, and seed oil percentage by 5–9%. All zeolite application rates significantly improved sunflower growth and productivity compared with no zeolite addition. The highest values of the studied traits were obtained under the conventional irrigation combined with zeolite application. Moreover, I1F2 treatment achieved the highest net return ($4,975.92 ha⁻¹) and economic water return (0.75 $ m − 3 ) compared with the other interaction treatments. Overall, zeolite application effectively enhanced sunflower growth and productivity under water-stress conditions.

title: Ethylene-Induced Growth Inhibition in Plants: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Mitigation Strategies
summary: In the role of plant growth regulation, ethylene emerges as a key indicator, exerting both stimulatory and inhibitory influences on various developmental processes.Ethylene biosynthesis is a consecutive catalytic process by the actions of 1
content: In the role of plant growth regulation, ethylene emerges as a key indicator, exerting both stimulatory and inhibitory influences on various developmental processes.Ethylene biosynthesis is a consecutive catalytic process by the actions of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid synthase (ACS) and ACC oxidase (ACO).Ethylene uses signal receptors for instance ethylene receptor protein1 (ETR 1 then gets to modulate transcription factors such as ethylene insensitive 1, 3 (EIN 1, 3) to ultimately, bring into play, genes that regulate growth.Such cellular changes morphologically manifested as growth retardation, shortening of stem and restricted leaf development in the plants treated with ethylene.Ethylene is involved in developmental processes and affects some milestones that include germination, root formation, and flowering.In this study, the impact of stress conditions mainly salinity, drought and pathogen attacks induce ethylene production which in turn religious defence mechanism but inhibits plant growth and development.Three genes that are involved in ethylene biosynthesis are known and ethylene receptors stand out as major control points in growth regulation.Alterations in these ethylene receptors through genetic and molecular means can enhance or diminish the inhibitory influence of ethylene and may provide ideal tools for modulating plant growth responses.These innovations in genetic engineering and targeted molecular interventions suggest the improvement of crop ethylene responses, growth and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses, in the context of sustainable farming.The role of novel regulators in ethylene biosynthesis may pave the way for eco-friendly strategies, ensuring in a new era of adaptive and efficient plant growth regulation.

title: Phthalates: the interplay between diet, obesity, diabetes, and gut microbiota
summary: Millions of tons of plastic are produced worldwide each year. Currently, it is almost impossible to avoid plastic and exposure to its effects. There are many chemical compounds that are used in its production. Some of them, classified as pl
content: Millions of tons of plastic are produced worldwide each year. Currently, it is almost impossible to avoid plastic and exposure to its effects. There are many chemical compounds that are used in its production. Some of them, classified as plasticizers, are phthalates, which are found in food packaging, toys, and many cosmetics. They give plastics durability, flexibility, and heat resistance. Humanity is exposed to these substances primarily through ingestion, i.e., processed food and its storage, and through inhalation of polluted air. Consequently, phthalates and their metabolites can be detected in the human body. Due to their ubiquity, they pose a global threat to human health. They contribute to overweight and obesity, insulin resistance, diabetes, and disorders of the nervous and endocrine systems. The purpose of this article was to review existing research on the impact of phthalates on diet, the development of obesity, and diabetes.

title: SOCIAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP AS A CATALYST FOR LOCAL ECONOMIC RESILIENCE: A PESTELE ANALYSIS OF A SCHOOL-BASED FARMING PROJECT
summary: This study aims to evaluate the socioeconomic viability and planning implications of a social entrepreneurship model through a rabbit farming project at SMITI Sains Bahrul Ulum, Penang, utilizing an analytical PESTELE diagnostic framework.
content: This study aims to evaluate the socioeconomic viability and planning implications of a social entrepreneurship model through a rabbit farming project at SMITI Sains Bahrul Ulum, Penang, utilizing an analytical PESTELE diagnostic framework. Employing a mixed-methods design, data were extracted from operational financial records, surveys involving 23 students and 14 school staff, and qualitative thematic analysis. The findings prove that the model is financially viable, generating a net profit of RM1,736.30 in its first cycle, which successfully triggered secondary economic spillover effects for the local community. From a social aspect, the acceptance level among educators was highly positive (mean 4.07); however, the students’ moderate practical skills (mean 3.64) necessitate the establishment of structured mentor-mentee workshops. Furthermore, spatial and operational analyses revealed that space constraints (40’ x 60’) and a low breeding rate (50%) restricted maximum profit, thus requiring smart technology interventions. Nevertheless, environmental sustainability was achieved through a circular economy system utilizing livestock waste. By implication, to ensure the replicability of this model, the study urges local authorities to formulate more flexible zoning policies to allow the integration of community economic activities within institutional zones.

title: Exploring Spitsbergen’s Potential for Sustainable Development and Geopark Creation
summary: There is growing evidence of environmental degradation in the Arctic, reflected in rising temperatures, ice melt, and more frequent extreme weather events. In this context, tourism development in Spitsbergen must be balanced with nature con
content: There is growing evidence of environmental degradation in the Arctic, reflected in rising temperatures, ice melt, and more frequent extreme weather events. In this context, tourism development in Spitsbergen must be balanced with nature conservation. This study aims to examine experiences of tourism and opinions on sustainable activities, as well as to explore the potential for establishing a geopark on Svalbard. The research is based on a literature review concerning sustainability and Spitsbergen as an Arctic destination, semi-structured interviews with local representatives (n = 12), and surveys conducted among residents and tourists in Spitsbergen (n = 104). The findings indicate that the geopark concept is generally viewed positively, with 75% of respondents recognising its environmental and heritage-related benefits. At the same time, 70% expressed concerns about commercialisation, 64% about overtourism, and 40% about environmental degradation. Responses to open-ended questions revealed both hopes for new jobs and greater environmental awareness, as well as frustration with the rising cost of living and increasing pressure on local infrastructure, particularly from cruise tourism.

title: Epoxidized ESBR as Functional Component in SSBR /Silica Nanocomposites for Potential Green Tire Tread Applications
summary: ABSTRACT Emulsion‐polymerized styrene‐butadiene rubber (ESBR) is the most widely used synthetic rubber globally, which is renowned for its broad molecular weight distribution and excellent processing properties. Solution‐polymerized styrene
content: ABSTRACT Emulsion‐polymerized styrene‐butadiene rubber (ESBR) is the most widely used synthetic rubber globally, which is renowned for its broad molecular weight distribution and excellent processing properties. Solution‐polymerized styrene‐butadiene rubber (SSBR) offers lower rolling resistance but is more expensive and more challenging to process. SSBR/ESBR blends filled with silica can combine the advantages of ESBR and SSBR. However, ESBR has weaker interaction with silica than SSBR. In this work, epoxidized ESBR (eESBR) with different epoxidation degrees was synthesized via an in situ epoxidation reaction to partially replace the SSBR matrix. The SSBR/eESBR/Silica nanocomposites were prepared, and the influence of eESBR with different epoxidation degrees on the structure‐properties relationship of SSBR/eESBR/Silica nanocomposites was explored. Compared to SSBR/Silica, SSBR/eESBR3.0/Silica nanocomposite shows better processability and performance, including a lower torque, longer scorch time, faster curing rate, 48.9% enhancement in modulus at 300% strain, a 4.7% decrease in tan δ at 7% strain, and comparable abrasion resistance, but a slight decline in tan δ at 0°C and elongation at break. This work proposes a new strategy for designing green tire treads.

title: Localized impact-resistant battery enclosures for electric vehicles: crashworthy lightweight design, mechanical–thermal safety, and validation pathways
summary: Electric-vehicle battery enclosures must reduce structural mass while preserving deformation clearance, sealing integrity, electrical isolation, and post-impact safety. These requirements are difficult under bottom strike and side-pole coll
content: Electric-vehicle battery enclosures must reduce structural mass while preserving deformation clearance, sealing integrity, electrical isolation, and post-impact safety. These requirements are difficult under bottom strike and side-pole collision because both load cases create localized intrusion near cells and modules, where only limited deformation space is available. This Mini Review synthesizes recent lightweight enclosure research through a scenario- and mechanism-based protection framework, rather than a conventional material-by-material catalogue, with specific emphasis on localized bottom strike and side-pole collision. The review links external impact loads to enclosure response, cell-level safety indicators, and post-crash thermal or electrical functions. Aluminum alloys, composite and hybrid structures, foam-filled members, sandwich panels, honeycomb cores, auxetic lattices, and bio-inspired absorbers are compared in terms of intrusion control, energy absorption, manufacturability, and coupled mechanical-thermal performance. The synthesis indicates that no single material family solves the design problem alone. Future enclosure design should combine local puncture resistance, progressive crush, load spreading, cell deformation limits, thermal propagation mitigation, repairability, and standards-based validation. Therefore, battery-enclosure lightweighting should be assessed through a staged protection chain: external localized loading, enclosure deformation, cell-level abuse indicators, and post-impact thermal/electrical safety.

title: Advances in plant electrostimulation: from cellular and molecular mechanisms to agricultural applications
summary: Electrical stimulation is an emerging physical strategy for agricultural regulation that applies electric fields or currents with defined parameters to modulate plant growth, development, and rhizosphere processes. Owing to its residue-free
content: Electrical stimulation is an emerging physical strategy for agricultural regulation that applies electric fields or currents with defined parameters to modulate plant growth, development, and rhizosphere processes. Owing to its residue-free nature, environmental compatibility, and high controllability, electrical stimulation has considerable potential to improve crop yield and quality while enhancing tolerance to abiotic and biotic stresses, making it increasingly relevant to sustainable agriculture. This review critically synthesizes the mechanisms and applications of electrical stimulation across cellular and molecular, physiological and metabolic, whole-plant, and field scales. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing continuous or quasi-continuous stimulation from high-voltage pulsed treatments, which differ in membrane-level mechanisms, reversibility, and safety profiles. Three interrelated factors are identified as central to its effectiveness: regulation of membrane potential and ion transport, root-targeted modulation of plant-soil interactions, and context-dependent matching of stimulation parameters with specific biological responses. We further highlight that translating laboratory-scale benefits into reliable field applications will require intelligent delivery systems capable of stable, scalable, energy-efficient, and feedback-controlled operation under variable environmental conditions. Future research should prioritize multiscale investigation of molecular mechanisms, standardized evaluation of stimulation parameters, development of smart and synergistic regulation platforms, and validation across diverse crops, soils, and production systems. These advances will facilitate the practical deployment of electrical stimulation technologies and support their integration into sustainable and precision agriculture.

title: A systematic assessment of environmental impacts and techno-economic benefits of solid digestate conversion to biochar: a case study of pig farm digestate in Taiwan
summary: Abstract Digestate, the solid by‑product of anaerobic digestion, can cause nutrient leaching, greenhouse‑gas release and heavy‑metal accumulation. Slow pyrolysis offers a promising route for upgrading digestate into biochar, yet its high en
content: Abstract Digestate, the solid by‑product of anaerobic digestion, can cause nutrient leaching, greenhouse‑gas release and heavy‑metal accumulation. Slow pyrolysis offers a promising route for upgrading digestate into biochar, yet its high energy demand and uncertain economics must be carefully weighed. This study evaluates the functional unit of 1 t solid digestate, the conversion of digestate to biochar at a pig farm in Pingtung, Taiwan, and compares the results with composting and incineration. Life‑Cycle Assessment and Techno‑Economic Assessment covered five scenarios: composting (S1); solid digestate pyrolysis at 500 °C (S2), 600 °C (S3) and 700 °C (S4); and incineration (S5). Because S2 required the least process energy, it yielded the lowest global-warming potential of 67.7 kg CO₂-eq t⁻¹. In contrast, S4 produced higher-value biochar and showed the strongest economic performance, with a positive Net Present Value of USD 371,480 and a payback period of 11 year under the scenario without carbon fees. Sensitivity tests (± 20% capital expenditure, operating expenditure and benefits) confirmed S4’s economic resilience, while S2–S3 were vulnerable to market shifts. A Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution multi-criterion ranking placed S4 first under the stakeholder-derived weighting scheme, mainly because of its stronger economic performance and product value. These results suggest that digestate-to-biochar conversion can improve digestate management, but the preferred pyrolysis temperature depends on the decision priority. In this case, 500 °C showed stronger environmental performance, whereas 700 °C provided greater economic potential when high-value biochar use and energy recovery were assumed.

title: Reduction of Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus titres in citrus seedlings via root-drenching application of bio-based nanoemulsions
summary: Huanglongbing (HLB) is one of the most devastating diseases of citrus nowadays. The etiological agent is a fastidious and non-culturable bacterium known as Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus ( C Las). C Las is a phloem-restricted pathogen, w
content: Huanglongbing (HLB) is one of the most devastating diseases of citrus nowadays. The etiological agent is a fastidious and non-culturable bacterium known as Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus ( C Las). C Las is a phloem-restricted pathogen, which makes the efficient delivery of antimicrobial compounds to control it a major challenge for citriculture. Therefore, the development of formulations capable of penetrating plant barriers and reducing the bacterial population within the phloem is critical for the control of HLB. Here we report on the development of a novel formulation loaded with oregano essential oil, hexyl gallate and eugenol, described in the literature as a transdermal permeation enhancer. The most effective formula was selected in vitro against bacterial surrogates ( Rhizobium tropici and Rhizobium phaseoli ), displaying bactericidal concentrations of 0.25 and 0.5% (v/v), respectively, of bactericidal concentration. The selected formulation was characterized as a near-Newtonian fluid, with 98.5% of particles measuring around 50 nm, a Polydispersity Index of 0.31, and zeta potential of -17.5 mV. Furthermore, Scanning electron microscopy revealed the presence of nanoparticles, alongside microscopic aggregates. The formulation maintained its bactericidal activity over 120-day storage period. During the root-drenching assays, the formulation significantly reduced overall C Las titres by 1.29 and 2.46 log 10 over a period of 300 days, in two independent experiments. Furthermore, ecotoxicological assessments revealed no acute toxicity in Tenebrio molitor or significant effects in the survival of Melipona scutellaris under the tested conditions. Our findings demonstrate the potential of this non-synthetic formulation as an effective and safe alternative for HLB management, without disrupting non-target organisms.

title: Global warming and the National Cattlemen’s Association 1986–1996
summary: In the mid-1980s, scientific studies first highlighted the role of anthropogenic methane in global warming and emissions from cows as an important source. This knowledge expanded views of responsibility for global warming beyond the fossil
content: In the mid-1980s, scientific studies first highlighted the role of anthropogenic methane in global warming and emissions from cows as an important source. This knowledge expanded views of responsibility for global warming beyond the fossil fuel sector. Using scientific studies, archival documents, media interviews, and various government reports, we analyzed how the National Cattlemen’s Association (NCA), a trade association for the U.S beef industry, reacted to news about its products’ impacts on global warming between 1986 and 1996. While previous studies have emphasized the role of trade associations in political lobbying, here we show that NCA responded mainly with strategic communications, including information gathering on civil society activities, commissioning academic experts to produce and share statistics that reframed scientific findings, and discursive tactics to influence politicians and the public. Despite scientific recommendations about opportunities to reduce methane emissions, we found no evidence that NCA researched or promoted any of these suggested changes to beef production. Instead, NCA treated global warming as a public relations concern that could affect consumer demand, rather than as a potentially serious consequence of beef production.

title: Selective Nitrate-to-Nitrite Electroreduction on Ag/Au Core-Shell Nanocubes
summary: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR) offers a promising route for the production of valuable fertilizers and nitrites (common food preservatives), yet the relevant active sites remain poorly defined. Here, we combine density f
content: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR) offers a promising route for the production of valuable fertilizers and nitrites (common food preservatives), yet the relevant active sites remain poorly defined. Here, we combine density functional theory (DFT) with operando electrochemical scanning tunneling microscopy (n-EC-STM) to analyze tunneling current noise and establish structure–activity relationships in Ag/Au(111) and Ag/Au(100) model systems. DFT calculations show that Ag overlayers strengthen nitrate adsorption relative to bare Au and facilitate the initial NO3* → NO2* step. The adsorption energetics depend on both the structure of the surface facet and adsorption geometry, with tridentate nitrate adsorption generally favored on Au(100)-based surfaces and more variable behavior on Au(111)-based surfaces. Experimentally, Ag-coated Au(111) and Au(100) exhibit strong coverage-dependent NO3RR activity, with maximum activity near completion of an Ag monolayer on both facets. AgML/Au(100) consistently outperforms AgML/Au(111). n-EC-STM identifies Ag(100)-like monolayer terraces as the dominant active sites for NO3RR, whereas adjacent Au sites remain inactive. The same design principle is reproduced in Au{100} nanocubes, where Ag5nm@Au43nm/C with a thinner Ag shell outperforms Ag11nm@Au43nm/C and Au43nm/C. Together, these results identify terrace-confined Ag monolayers on Au as the key active sites for the electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction and highlight the roles of strain, ligand presence, and electronic effects at the Ag/Au–electrolyte interface.

title: Rethinking leather and leather alternatives: comparative performance, sustainability trade-offs and future directions
summary: Leather and leather-like materials are evolving in response to environmental pressures, consumer preferences, animal welfare concerns and advancements in biofabrication, which influence novel material development. This review scrutinizes an
content: Leather and leather-like materials are evolving in response to environmental pressures, consumer preferences, animal welfare concerns and advancements in biofabrication, which influence novel material development. This review scrutinizes animal-derived leather, petroleum-based substitutes and emerging bio-based alternatives from material, performance and sustainability perspectives. The current narrative assessment of literature considers historical development, composition and processing, mechanical and functional performance, durability, carbon footprint and broader life-cycle implications, end-of-life behavior, commercial maturity, market trends alongwith industrial and policy constraints. The evidence suggests that no single material class is sustainable by all criteria. Traditional leather has superior durability and performance, but has debates about livestock allocation and intensive resources use in tanning process. Synthetic leather alternatives enable scalable and consistent properties but are largely dependent on fossil-derived polymers and present persistent end-of-life challenges. Although bio-based alternatives can reduce fossil feedstocks dependence, their benefits are affected by coatings, binders, textile backings, energy demand, production scale, durability and realistic disposal routes. Functional units, system boundaries, allocation methods, regional energy systems and service-life assumptions also affect comparative life-cycle conclusions. Besides stronger expectations for traceability, circularity and credible environmental claims, there is also market expansion in Europe, North America, India and Southeast Asia. Future progress will necessitate transparent formulations, standardized durability testing, commercial scale validation, harmonized and prospective life-cycle assessment, realistic end-of-life testing, techno-economic analysis and stronger social indicators. Sustainability must ultimately be measured by the delivered function and the service life relative to proven environmental and social burdens, not by labels like natural, vegan or bio-based.

title: Legitimizing nuclear power: Rhetoric, myth and symbols in South Korea's official nuclear communication, 1986–2016
summary: Understanding how nuclear power is justified matters for debates over energy security and climate change. Yet research has paid limited attention to how language, narratives, and images work together to sustain these justifications over tim
content: Understanding how nuclear power is justified matters for debates over energy security and climate change. Yet research has paid limited attention to how language, narratives, and images work together to sustain these justifications over time. This article examines South Korea's official nuclear communication from 1986 to 2016 through interpretive document analysis. It analyzes government and industry publications, educational materials, advertisements, sponsored journalism, and visual campaigns using rhetoric, myth, and symbol as analytical categories. Naming and euphemism downplayed risk in official accounts. Repeated narratives presented nuclear power as safe, affordable, indispensable, and environmentally responsible. Visual symbols associated it with scientific control and everyday life. These justifications persisted through adaptation. Major accidents were reframed as problems of technical management, while environmental claims were incorporated into established narratives of national development. Repeated circulation through education, advertising, and sponsored media formed a communication infrastructure that presented nuclear power as a normal and desirable national choice. The study examines the construction and circulation of these representations; it does not establish their causal effects on public acceptance or policy continuity. It advances energy communication research by showing how rhetorical adjustment, symbolic selection, and institutional repetition jointly renew justifications for contested technologies. The findings suggest that energy policy research should examine communication alongside the economic and institutional conditions sustaining energy systems.
