The analysis shows that optimal electrolyte performance in Na-O2 batteries arises from a balance between solvation stability, transport properties and interfacial chemistry rather than from maximizing isolated bulk parameters. Comparisons with sodium-ion batteries further emphasize the broader relevance of coordination chemistry and desolvation processes. Finally, this perspective argues for a redefinition of what constitutes a 'good solvent' in reactive battery systems, integrating molecular-level solvation, interfacial reactivity, safety and sustainability considerations. Such an approach is essential for advancing efficient, durable and environmentally responsible sodium-based energy storage technologies. This article is part of the theme issue 'Electrolytes within the domain of electrochemistry and electrochemical energy storage'.

title: Flexible Day-Ahead Scheduling of a Cascade Hydro-Wind-Solar-Thermal-Storage System Including Hybrid Pumped Storage
summary: To advance the modernization of power systems, the role of hydropower has transitioned from mere energy generation to serving as both a primary energy provider and a critical flexibility resource. However, conventional day-ahead scheduling
content: To advance the modernization of power systems, the role of hydropower has transitioned from mere energy generation to serving as both a primary energy provider and a critical flexibility resource. However, conventional day-ahead scheduling methodologies for cascaded hydropower often prove inadequate in mitigating the short-term power imbalances induced by renewable energy variability, primarily due to an oversimplification of operational constraints. To fully harness the regulatory potential of hydropower, this paper proposes an optimal day-ahead scheduling strategy for a cascade hydro-wind-solar-thermal-storage system incorporating hybrid pumped storage (HPS). First, leveraging the operational characteristics of HPS, this study evaluates its capacity for renewable energy accommodation and identifies key challenges in power balancing from the perspectives of water resource management and energy dispatch. Second, a collaborative optimization framework is established. By introducing the concept of an “allowable reservoir water level fluctuation range” within the day-ahead dispatch cycle, the framework constrains the deviation between the actual end-of-period water level and its predefined target, thereby ensuring strict adherence to medium-to-long-term operational boundaries. Finally, case studies conducted on a modified IEEE 33-node system demonstrate that the integration of HPS significantly enhances system regulation capabilities. The results confirm that the proposed strategy contributes to secure, economical, and low-carbon grid operation while maintaining reservoir sustainability.

title: The Dilated Cardiomyopathy E525K Mutation Stabilizes the Cardiac Myosin Interacting-Heads Motif While Activating the Isolated Motor Domain
summary: Mutations in β-cardiac myosin are a common cause of inherited cardiomyopathies. The dilated cardiomyopathy E525K mutation alters both thick filament regulation and motor activity, yet the structural basis for these effects has remained uncl
content: Mutations in β-cardiac myosin are a common cause of inherited cardiomyopathies. The dilated cardiomyopathy E525K mutation alters both thick filament regulation and motor activity, yet the structural basis for these effects has remained unclear. Here, we combined cryo-EM and MD simulations to determine how E525K affects the conformational landscape of cardiac myosin in both its autoinhibited interacting-heads motif (IHM) and isolated myosin head states. E525K-mutated myosin exclusively adopted a single S2 conformation in IHM, in contrast to the conformational heterogeneity observed in wild-type myosin. Structural and electrostatic analyses revealed that the mutation increased positive charge density at the blocked-head (BH) – S2 (subfragment-2) interface, strengthening interactions with negatively charged residues within S2. 3D variability analysis and MD simulations of the E525K IHM demonstrated reduced S2 mobility, consistent with strengthened BH – S2 interactions, and decreased conformational flexibility, providing a structural mechanism for stabilization of the IHM state. To investigate the isolated myosin head, we determined cryo-EM structures of wild-type and E525K subfragment-1 (S1). The mutation induced local conformational rearrangements in the activation-loop and Loop 3 region, the SH3-like domain, and the essential light chain of S1, revealing structural changes that support the enhanced motor activity previously reported for isolated E525K myosin motors. These findings show that E525K stabilizes the autoinhibited IHM through electrostatic stabilization of the BH – S2 interface while inducing structural changes consistent with activation of the isolated motor domain, providing structural insights into how a single DCM mutation differentially regulates cardiac myosin S1 and IHM structure and function.

title: Water incompatibility in carbonate reservoirs: mechanisms, mitigation, and emerging innovations for sustainable water injection
source: Journal of Petroleum Exploration and Production Technology
summary: Water incompatibility in carbonate reservoirs remains a major challenge affecting injectivity, production performance, and long-term reservoir sustainability during water injection operations. Interactions among injected brines, formation w
content: Water incompatibility in carbonate reservoirs remains a major challenge affecting injectivity, production performance, and long-term reservoir sustainability during water injection operations. Interactions among injected brines, formation water, and reactive carbonate minerals can trigger geochemical and flow-related problems, including mineral scaling, wettability alteration, fines migration, and reservoir souring. Unlike previous reviews that primarily focus on isolated mechanisms or individual mitigation methods, this study provides an integrated assessment linking fundamental geochemical processes, laboratory and field evidence, predictive modeling approaches, mitigation technologies, and emerging sustainability-oriented innovations within a unified framework for carbonate reservoirs. Particular emphasis is placed on the integration of reactive transport simulations, artificial intelligence-assisted prediction models, smart water injection, nanotechnology-based inhibitors, and digital monitoring systems for proactive incompatibility management. The review also critically examines current limitations associated with thermodynamic uncertainty, scale-up from laboratory to field conditions, and the insufficient understanding of coupled multi-ion interactions under dynamic reservoir environments. Emerging applications related to carbon capture, utilization, and storage and underground hydrogen storage are evaluated in the context of future low-carbon reservoir management strategies. Key conclusions highlight that conventional empirical scaling indices are insufficient, reactive transport simulators improve predictive capability but face field-scale limitations, nanotechnology and artificial intelligence offer transformative potential but require further validation, and sustainability-driven water management demands integrated approaches combining circular water use, green chemistry, and environmental, social, and governance compliance. Overall, this review emphasizes the transition from conventional reactive treatment approaches toward predictive, adaptive, and sustainability-driven water management frameworks for carbonate reservoirs.

title: Small extracellular vesicles as liquid biopsy targets and precision therapeutics for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
summary: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects over one-third of the global population, yet robust molecular biomarkers for early disease activity and treatment monitoring remain limited.Small extracellular vesicle
content: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects over one-third of the global population, yet robust molecular biomarkers for early disease activity and treatment monitoring remain limited.Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) carry nucleic acids, proteins, and lipids that reflect disease-associated intercellular signaling and are being investigated as liquid-biopsy analytes and therapeutic platforms.Candidate sEV miRNAs, proteins, and lipid signatures have shown potential for disease characterization, but evidence derives mainly from small, heterogeneous cohorts with limited external validation.No sEV-based assay is established for routine MASLD diagnosis, staging, or treatment monitoring.Mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEVs and engineered sEV platforms have shown therapeutic potential in preclinical MASLDrelated models through modulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, lipid metabolism, and targeted cargo delivery, although some engineering strategies remain supported primarily by non-MASLD proof-of-concept evidence.Key barriers to translation include heterogeneity in extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization, lipoprotein coisolation, prospective multicenter validation, and, for therapeutic products, manufacturing consistency, biodistribution, dosing, and safety.This narrative review integrates diagnostic and therapeutic evidence within an evidence-classified translational framework.

title: A chemically tuned La@MOF-808 adsorbent for simultaneous removal of Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), arsenic, and lead from aqueous solutions
summary: The pervasive co-contamination of water resources by per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), arsenic [As(V)], and lead (Pb 2+ ) presents a critical environmental challenge due to their high toxicity and distinct chemical behaviors. Con
content: The pervasive co-contamination of water resources by per - and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), arsenic [As(V)], and lead (Pb 2+ ) presents a critical environmental challenge due to their high toxicity and distinct chemical behaviors. Conventional adsorbents are often limited in their ability to address such complex multi-contaminant systems simultaneously. In this study, a lanthanum-modified metal-organic framework (La@MOF-808) was evaluated for the concurrent removal of PFAS, As(V), and Pb 2+ from aqueous solutions. Batch adsorption experiments showed substantial adsorption of the tested contaminants, with Langmuir-derived maximum adsorption capacities ( q max ) of 307.7 mg g -1 for As(V), 223.2 mg g -1 for Pb 2+ , and 254.4–267.7 mg g -1 for the grouped short- and long-chain PFAS mixtures, respectively. The presence of co-contaminants influenced PFAS adsorption, with As(V) and Pb 2+ increasing the removal of selected PFAS compounds, such as ADONA and PFDA, while competitive effects were observed for some ultra-short-chain PFAS. Thermodynamic analysis yielded negative ΔG° values and positive ΔH° values, indicating spontaneous and endothermic adsorption under the tested conditions. Kinetic analysis showed that both pseudo-first order and pseudo-second order models described the experimental data, with the pseudo-second-order model providing a slightly better overall fit. The observed adsorption trends suggest that electrostatic interactions contribute to contaminant uptake, while other surface interactions may also be involved. Overall, La@MOF-808 showed potential for simultaneous adsorption of PFAS, As(V), and Pb 2+ from multicomponent aqueous systems.

title: Protein acylation and heart failure: A review of novel lysine modifications in cardiac pathology
summary: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a primary contributor to heart failure (HF).Protein acylation, particularly acetylation, plays a crucial role in this process.Advances in mass spectrometry and proteomics have identified an increasing num
content: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a primary contributor to heart failure (HF).Protein acylation, particularly acetylation, plays a crucial role in this process.Advances in mass spectrometry and proteomics have identified an increasing number of novel lysine acylation modifications, including crotonylation, lactylation, succinylation, βhydroxybutyrylation, 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation, propionylation and malonylation.These novel acylations are implicated in key physiological processes and disease-related cellular functions, as they modify the physicochemical properties of proteins and closely link substrate metabolism to gene regulation.Research on these novel lysine acylations associated with cardiac hypertrophy and HF has been steadily increasing in recent years.This review aims to summarize the progress and significance of these novel lysine acylations in cardiac hypertrophy and HF, providing references for a deeper understanding of the pathogenesis of HF and development of innovative therapeutic strategies.

title: Full-field 3D scanning of warpage in carbon-fibre-reinforced FDM parts: Effects of print parameters and post-print annealing
summary: Most reported warpage data for carbon-fibre-reinforced (CF) fused deposition modelling (FDM) parts rely on sparse point measurements and single-replicate designs. This study uses full-field structured-light 3D scanning to quantify as-printe
content: Most reported warpage data for carbon-fibre-reinforced (CF) fused deposition modelling (FDM) parts rely on sparse point measurements and single-replicate designs. This study uses full-field structured-light 3D scanning to quantify as-printed warpage in three CF-FDM filaments (PLA-CF, PAHT-CF, PPA-CF) and test whether manufacturer annealing is dimensionally safe. Coupons were printed in a fully replicated design (n = 3/condition; 81 coupons, 162 scans), varying raster angle, infill density and chamber temperature. Baseline warpage differed significantly but modestly between materials (PPA-CF > PAHT-CF > PLA-CF; p < 0.001), although a dataset-level diagnostic reported below indicates this baseline ranking should not be treated as validated. Annealing significantly increased RMS warpage in PLA-CF and PAHT-CF (p < 0.001) but not PPA-CF (p = 0.310), although PPA-CF's shape changed significantly; RMS and point-based metrics disagreed in sign for 37-48% of specimens. These paired, within-specimen annealing findings are the manuscript's central result and are shown to be structurally independent of the baseline diagnostic above. Manufacturer schedules should not be assumed dimensionally safe without full-field checks. This dataset supersedes a preliminary single-replicate pilot (45 specimens); the pilot's different baseline values are addressed through a dedicated reproducibility analysis rather than simply disclosed as an unexamined limitation.

title: Residual Tree Damage During Forest Operations: a Comprehensive Review of Operational, Silvicultural, and Human-related Factors
summary: Minimizing residual tree damage during mechanized forest operations is vital for sustainable forest management since this damage can affect stand structure, timber quality, and long-term forest health. Although various studies have examined
content: Minimizing residual tree damage during mechanized forest operations is vital for sustainable forest management since this damage can affect stand structure, timber quality, and long-term forest health. Although various studies have examined tree damage factors, evidence remains fragmented across regions and systems. The review synthesizes the state of knowledge of residual tree damage during forest operations, identifying how operational, silvicultural, and human factors have been reported to influence damage characteristics and synthesize mitigation strategies. Of the 547 articles that were systematically screened, 76 were selected for synthesis. Reported damage frequency ranged from 0.7% to 68% across studies, reflecting substantial variation associated with differences in assessment methods, damage thresholds, and operational contexts. The reviewed literature associated residual tree damage with stand and site conditions, harvesting systems and methods, harvesting intensity, trail configuration, tree position, and operator-related factors. However, the direction and magnitude of these reported relationships varied across the studies suggesting substantial context dependence. Human-related factors received comparatively limited attention, and direct evidence relating to operator experience, mental workload, visibility, and related ergonomic conditions to residual tree damage remained limited. Residual tree damage cannot be consistently explained by any single factor, instead, reported patterns reflect interacting operational, silvicultural, and human influences. By categorizing the literature into these three factors, this review identifies an imbalance in the evidence base, with human-related influences receiving less direct examination in relation to residual tree damage than operational and silvicultural factors. This underrepresentation highlights the need for further research examining operator experience, workload, and visibility in relation to residual tree damage, and evaluating these factors jointly with operational and silvicultural factors. To support this integrated perspective, the review proposes a conceptual framework that organizes the reported factor categories, damage characteristics, and mitigation strategies.

title: Odd‐even effects in molecular junctions: A Solomonic resolution of conflicting reports on conductance trends, metal specificity, and microscopic origin
summary: Abstract Odd–even conductance alternation in alkanethiol (CnT, –12) self‐assembled monolayers has been debated for two decades, with conflicting reports on trends, metal dependence, and microscopic origin. Using conducting probe atomic forc
content: Abstract Odd–even conductance alternation in alkanethiol (CnT, –12) self‐assembled monolayers has been debated for two decades, with conflicting reports on trends, metal dependence, and microscopic origin. Using conducting probe atomic force microscopy (CP‐AFM) with Ag, Au, and Pt electrodes, we extract low‐bias conductance and effective molecule–electrode coupling via the off‐resonant single‐level model, combined with rigorous ‐score statistics (Welch's ‐test for unequal variances). We present a Solomonic resolution—meaning a balanced compromise that recognizes truth on both sides—to these long‐standing controversies. First, the odd–even effect has a dual origin, manifesting in both the contact conductance prefactor (, ) and the length‐decay constant (, ). Interface and bulk contributions are therefore not mutually exclusive. The assignment to interface versus bulk remains inferential from transport parameters; independent structural characterization would be desirable but faces substantial experimental challenges. Second, the relative conductance of odd versus even chains reverses with length: odd chains are more conductive at short lengths, while even chains become superior beyond a crossover. A point estimate near –13 emerges from the global fits, yet the limited experimental window (–12) and the small difference in decay constants produce a wide uncertainty interval; the precise location of the crossover therefore remains undetermined. The qualitative inversion itself (from to ), however, is a robust finding and offers a natural reconciliation of prior opposing claims. Third, the effect is observed in CP‐AFM junctions under the present experimental conditions. Earlier CP‐AFM analyses of CnT junctions did not report it because they employed parity‐agnostic fitting; once the data are deliberately split by parity the effect becomes statistically clear. Fourth, metal dependence follows parity‐insensitive work‐function scaling with . Paradoxically, although absolute odd–even differences are smallest on Ag (conductances ∼20 times lower than on Au), statistical confidence is highest for Ag ( %), owing to exceptional reproducibility of even‐chain data. This analysis demonstrates that “weaker” does not imply “absent” and highlights the necessity of variance‐aware statistics. Apparently contradictory literature findings arise from different regimes of a single underlying phenomenon.

title: TLD-Based Antiretroviral Therapy Compromises Ovarian Function and Reserve: Evidence from Experimental and Clinical Studies
summary: Combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) has improved human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) management, but long-term use is associated with reproductive dysfunction. This study investigated TLD (Tenofovir, Lamivudine and Dolutegravir)-based
content: Combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) has improved human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) management, but long-term use is associated with reproductive dysfunction. This study investigated TLD (Tenofovir, Lamivudine and Dolutegravir)-based cART effects on ovarian function using animal models and exploratory clinical investigations in women living with HIV. In the animal study, female Wistar rats were randomized into control, TLD-based cART (22 mg/kg), and dolutegravir alone (2.5 mg/kg) groups, administered orally for 28 days. Estrous cycle, histology, oxidative stress, reproductive hormones, and ova count were assessed. Both TLD-based cART and dolutegravir significantly prolonged diestrus (p = 0.0083 and p = 0.0007, respectively) and reduced metestrus (p = 0.0057 and p = 0.0083, respectively). Treated groups showed significantly reduced ova counts (p = 0.0002 and 0.0003, respectively). Histology revealed structural alterations of the ovary, including atretic follicles, distorted stroma, and sparse theca cells. Additionally, treated groups showed increased malondialdehyde (p = 0.0421) and decreased glutathione (p = 0.0046) and catalase activities (p = 0.0411), indicating oxidative stress. Serum follicle-stimulating and luteinizing hormones were significantly reduced in both treated groups (FSH: p < 0.0001 and p = 0.0002; LH: p < 0.0001 and p = 0.0108, respectively). In the clinical investigation, serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels were evaluated in HIV-positive women (n = 20) receiving TLD-based cART. Ten participants (50%) had AMH in low/very low categories ( < 1.0 ng/mL), while 11 (55%) had AMH below the normal reference range ( < 1.5 ng/mL). Menstrual interval and dysmenorrhea showed no significant changes. These preliminary findings suggest Dolutegravir and TLD-based cART may negatively affect female reproductive function by altering ovarian structure, hormonal balance, and ovarian reserve, potentially predisposing women living with HIV to fertility complications.

title: Green-function thimbles for internal conversion
summary: Oscillatory real-time integrals and the complete quadratic transformation between electronic-state normal modes are persistent obstacles in molecular internal-conversion calculations. We develop a finite-temperature Tyablikov–Moskalenko Gre
content: Oscillatory real-time integrals and the complete quadratic transformation between electronic-state normal modes are persistent obstacles in molecular internal-conversion calculations. We develop a finite-temperature Tyablikov–Moskalenko Green-function formulation that retains unequal frequencies, equilibrium displacement, Duschinsky rotation, the anomalous squeezing block, and a general first-order Herzberg–Teller nonadiabatic operator. The closed equations of motion reconstruct the vibronic correlation function by coupling-constant integration, while analytic continuation to complex time permits both a systematic saddle expansion and globally controlled integration on Lefschetz thimbles without numerical damping. For the 102-mode tetraoxa[8]circulene (4B) model at 300 K, the complete rate is 1.656× 10 7 s −1 at 18500 cm −1 . Herzberg–Teller coupling and Duschinsky rotation increase the rate by factors of approximately 2.45 and 2.06, respectively, while the squeezing contribution is about 46% in the mode-mixed calculation. The next-to-leading saddle result differs from the full thimble value by 0.66% at the molecular gap; one contributing thimble and no Stokes transition are found throughout 5000–35000 cm −1 . The same formalism gives aligned electric-and magnetic-field thresholds of 1.06 × 108 V m −1 and 41.6 T. The method therefore provides a fast, damping-free route to complete harmonic vibronic rates together with an explicit global test of the integration contour.

title: Point-of-care ultrasound in the acute abdomen and gastrointestinal emergencies: An evidence-based guide and the case for standardisation
summary: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is embedded in emergency assessment of acute abdominal pain, yet its evidence is scattered across emergency, surgical, anaesthetic and radiology journals.This structured narrative review synthesises four app
content: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is embedded in emergency assessment of acute abdominal pain, yet its evidence is scattered across emergency, surgical, anaesthetic and radiology journals.This structured narrative review synthesises four applications: (1) Small-bowel obstruction; (2) Gastric aspiration-risk assessment; (3) Non-traumatic free intraperitoneal fluid; and (4) Biliary disease including cholangitis.Sources came from a purposive search of PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science through August 2026, favouring the highest available evidence per application; it was English-language only, unregistered, and without review-level risk-of-bias appraisal or de novo pooling.We report thresholds, pooled sensitivities and specificities, likelihood ratios and, where retrievable, heterogeneity and risk-ofbias data.POCUS for small-bowel obstruction and cholecystitis is primarily a rule-in tool: A negative scan does not reliably exclude disease, and neither defines aetiology, ischaemia or perforation, for which computed tomography remains necessary.For non-traumatic free fluid the strongest rule-in evidence concerns suspected ectopic pregnancy; gastric POCUS stratifies aspiration risk against surrogate endpoints.We contribute an integrated, symptom-based, pretest-probability-driven algorithm with a competency precondition, a non-diagnostic exit and a defined action for every result; it is not prospectively validated.Dispersion across operators, thresholds and reference standards exceeds the margins bedside decisions turn on; we argue standardisation, not further accuracy estimation, is rate-limiting.

title: Molecular and environmental regulation of floral development, flowering, and sex differentiation in angiosperms
summary: Flowers, the reproductive organs of spermatophytes, are essential for fruit and seed formation and thus play a central role in plant reproductive success [ 1 ]. A typical angiosperm flower consists of four floral whorls: the calyx (sepals),
content: Flowers, the reproductive organs of spermatophytes, are essential for fruit and seed formation and thus play a central role in plant reproductive success [ 1 ]. A typical angiosperm flower consists of four floral whorls: the calyx (sepals), corolla (petals), androecium (stamens), and gynoecium (carpels). Ovules are borne within the ovary of the gynoecium and develop into seeds following fertilization. Considerable variation in floral structure occurs among species [ 2 , 3 ]. For example, Eucommia ulmoides and Salix babylonica produce unisexual flowers containing either stamens or pistils. Viburnum opulus produces flowers lacking reproductive organs, whereas Morus species often lack petals [ 2 , 4 ]. These variations highlight the diversity of floral structure and the complexity of developmental regulation. Floral organ development is governed by intricate genetic networks and influenced by both endogenous physiological signals and environmental cues [ 5 ]. The discovery of MADS-box transcription factors, including MCM1, AGAMOUS (AG), DEFICIENS (DEF), and serum response factor (SRF), established a foundation for understanding the molecular regulation of flower development [ 6 , 7 ]. The classical ABCDE model provides a framework for understanding floral organ identity through the combinatorial action of floral homeotic genes [ 8 ]. However, floral organogenesis involves additional transcription factors and regulatory genes that extend beyond this classical framework [ 8 , 9 , 10 ]. These regulatory networks integrate floral meristem identity, organ specification, developmental timing, and reproductive development.

title: Protic and aprotic bis(oxalato)borate based ionic liquids as electrolytes for electrical double layer capacitors
source: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
summary: In this study, we report about the synthesis of two fluorine-free ionic liquids (ILs), the protic 1-methylimidazolium bis(oxalato)borate (1-MimBOB) and the aprotic 1-butyl-2,3-dimethylimidazolium bis(oxalato)borate (BDMimBOB) and about thei
content: In this study, we report about the synthesis of two fluorine-free ionic liquids (ILs), the protic 1-methylimidazolium bis(oxalato)borate (1-MimBOB) and the aprotic 1-butyl-2,3-dimethylimidazolium bis(oxalato)borate (BDMimBOB) and about their use as electrolytes for electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs). We showed that the electrolytes 1.5 M 1-MimBOB in water and 1.5 M BDMimBOB in acetonitrile exhibited good solubility, high ionic conductivity and high thermal stability. EDLC containing protic IL can operate at 1.2 V, while those containing the organic electrolyte can operate at 2.9 V. EDLCs containing these electrolytes display ideal capacitive behaviour, excellent rate capability and promising capacitance retention after 200 hours of floating at their maximum operating voltage. The devices also achieved energy densities up to 23.3 Wh kg⁻¹, highlighting BOB-based ILs as sustainable, fluorine-free electrolytes for next-generation high-performance EDLCs. This article is part of the theme issue 'Electrolytes within the domain of electrochemistry and electrochemical energy storage'.

title: A multiscale assessment of general resilience capacity in China’s coastal social-ecological systems: a national baseline and nested diagnosis in Rongcheng
summary: Introduction Coastal social-ecological systems face climate change, resource exploitation, and fragmented governance. Hazard-specific assessments cannot fully represent their capacity to cope with uncertain disturbances, while connections b
content: Introduction Coastal social-ecological systems face climate change, resource exploitation, and fragmented governance. Hazard-specific assessments cannot fully represent their capacity to cope with uncertain disturbances, while connections between nationally consistent screening and fine-scale local diagnosis remain limited. Methods Drawing on general resilience theory, we developed a three-tier, ten-attribute framework linking a national baseline with a nested assessment in Rongcheng. Coastal land and marine subsystems were evaluated using a nominal 2025 temporal window that incorporated the closest reliable products for slowly updated variables. The analysis included indicator standardization, scale-specific weighting, composite assessment, Jenks natural breaks classification, and spatial autocorrelation analysis. Results The mean general resilience capacity indices were 0.359 for national coastal land and 0.470 for national coastal waters. Low and relatively low classes accounted for 39.75% of national coastal land, whereas moderate and relatively high classes accounted for 65.48% of national coastal waters. In Rongcheng, moderate and relatively low classes jointly represented 68.30% of coastal land. Relatively low and relatively high classes accounted for 56.33% of coastal waters, with a coefficient of variation of 0.282, indicating pronounced intra-bay heterogeneity. Discussion The national assessment provides a consistent baseline for broad-scale screening, whereas the Rongcheng assessment identifies bay- and shoreline-scale units for future field verification. Because the assessments differ in indicators, weights, and spatial supports, their results should be interpreted within their respective scales rather than compared directly. Scale-matched monitoring and governance feedback can connect national screening with local diagnosis.

title: Interfacial Resistance and Degradation Behavior of Uncoated Single-Crystal-like and Polycrystalline NCM523 in All-Solid-State Batteries Analyzed by Three-Electrode Cells
summary: Abstract All-solid-state batteries are promising as safe and high energy density power sources but often suffer from short cycle life due to insufficient solid|solid contact at the electrode|electrolyte interface. It has been reported that
content: Abstract All-solid-state batteries are promising as safe and high energy density power sources but often suffer from short cycle life due to insufficient solid|solid contact at the electrode|electrolyte interface. It has been reported that the conventional polycrystalline (PC) positive electrode materials need coating to suppress the interfacial reaction with sulfide-based solid electrolytes, while single-crystal-like (SC) materials can be cycled without coating. In this study, the behavior of uncoated SC and PC NCM523 electrodes was comparatively examined in sulfide-based all-solid-state cells using three-electrode cells to resolve the interfacial resistive components and relate them to cycling performance. By employing a chemically reduced Li4Ti5O12 reference electrode, four resistive components were separated, allowing the charge-transfer resistance and the interparticle contact-related resistance to be evaluated independently. The SC cell showed high cycling stability, whereas the capacity of the PC cell once decreased and partially recovered afterward, which was confirmed to be reproducible. With detailed impedance analysis, the capacity loss of the PC cell was chiefly assigned to an increase in the charge-transfer resistance, and the partial recovery was correlated with a contact-related resistance among the NCM523 particles. Both resistive components were kept low in the SC cell, leading to the higher cycling stability of the SC cell.

title: Berberine and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a global analysis of molecular mechanisms, translational challenges and research frontiers
summary: Objective Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide. Berberine (BBR), a bioactive monomer derived from traditional Chinese medicine, demonstrates remar
content: Objective Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide. Berberine (BBR), a bioactive monomer derived from traditional Chinese medicine, demonstrates remarkable multi-target pharmacological properties in regulating glucose and lipid metabolism, ameliorating insulin resistance, attenuating inflammation and oxidative stress, and modulating the gut–liver axis. This study aims to systematically delineate the research landscape, thematic hotspots, and evolutionary trends of BBR in the treatment of MASLD through bibliometric analysis, and to provide an in-depth review of its underlying molecular mechanisms and clinical translational potential, thereby offering a valuable reference for future investigations. Methods A dual-database literature search with cross-validation was conducted in the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus, utilizing refined retrieval strategies tailored to the research topic. Bibliometric analyses and network visualizations were performed using R (v4.5.1), VOSviewer (v1.6.19), and CiteSpace (v6.4.R1). Based on these scientometric findings, a comprehensive review of the identified mechanisms and clinical translational potential was subsequently undertaken. Results A total of 341 and 624 records were retrieved from WoSCC and Scopus, respectively. Thematic hotspots converged on four major directions: (1) BBR regulates hepatic glucose and lipid metabolism via the AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)/Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), Clock/Bmal1, and farnesoid X receptor (FXR)-Fibroblast Growth Factor 15 (FGF15) signaling pathways; (2) BBR attenuates MASLD progression through Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)/Antioxidant Response Element (ARE)-mediated antioxidant defense and suppression of nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation; (3) BBR reshapes gut microbiota architecture, restores mucosal barrier integrity, and modulates hepatic homeostasis via microbiota-derived metabolites along the gut–liver axis; and (4) the clinical efficacy of BBR in MASLD and the development of nano-delivery system-based formulations. Clinical evidence indicates that BBR ameliorates hepatic steatosis and improves metabolic profiles; however, its clinical translation remains constrained by poor oral bioavailability and substantial inter-patient variability in therapeutic response. Conclusion BBR demonstrates a distinct therapeutic profile in MASLD management through the concerted modulation of hepatic metabolism, inflammation, oxidative stress, and the gut–liver axis. Future research should focus on developing innovative drug delivery systems to overcome bioavailability constraints, conducting large-scale, long-term randomized controlled trials to establish long-term efficacy and safety, and implementing precision medicine approaches guided by metabolic phenotyping.

title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter SGLT2 Supports Metabolic Fitness and Ferroptosis Resistance in CAR-T Cells to Enhance Activity Against Solid Tumors
summary: Antitumor T-cell function is tightly coupled with cellular metabolism, which is severely compromised by glucose deprivation and elevated sodium chloride (NaCl) in the solid tumor microenvironment (TME). Here, we demonstrated that glucose re
content: Antitumor T-cell function is tightly coupled with cellular metabolism, which is severely compromised by glucose deprivation and elevated sodium chloride (NaCl) in the solid tumor microenvironment (TME). Here, we demonstrated that glucose restriction markedly impaired activation, cytotoxicity, and persistence of CAR-T cells while promoting exhaustion, whereas high NaCl partially reversed these defects. Overexpression of the sodium-glucose cotransporter SGLT2 in CAR-T cells to simultaneously enhance glucose and NaCl uptake led to stronger antitumor activity in multiple solid tumor xenograft models. Mechanistically, SGLT2 overexpression elevated glycolysis and mitochondrial fitness, inhibited ferroptosis, and activated the AKT-mTOR pathway. These findings establish a metabolic engineering strategy that boosts glucose utilization in CAR-T cells to overcome TME stress and enhance solid tumor control.

title: Two decades-long NDVI anomalies to understand Mediterranean forests ecosystem shifts
summary: Abstract Mediterranean forest ecosystems are increasingly exposed to climate change, land-use transformations and altered disturbance regimes. Understanding vegetation shifts across these complex landscapes requires scalable, high-resolutio
content: Abstract Mediterranean forest ecosystems are increasingly exposed to climate change, land-use transformations and altered disturbance regimes. Understanding vegetation shifts across these complex landscapes requires scalable, high-resolution tools. In this study, we analyzed a 24-year NDVI time series (2000–2023) from Landsat imagery over the Gargano National Park (Southern Italy) to identify anomalous vegetation dynamics and assess their potential drivers. We applied the Isolation Forest algorithm to detect extreme NDVI anomalies, followed by spatial cross-analysis with climate data, wildfire records, land cover change, and forest management information. Topographic variables (elevation, slope, aspect) were also included to evaluate their role in modulating anomaly occurrence. Results revealed that approximately 4% of the forested area exhibited significant anomalies, with the highest incidence observed in conifer and broadleaf plantations (up to 39%). Native forests such as beech and mixed oak stands accounted for the largest anomalous surfaces in absolute terms. Machine learning models (XGBoost, Random Forest) and SHAP analysis highlighted maximum temperature as the most influential climatic factor ( R 2 ≈ 0.37). A considerable portion of anomalies remained unexplained by the analyzed drivers, particularly in native forests, and is interpreted here as an exploratory hypothesis of vegetation changes not captured by the available attribution framework. Topographic analysis further revealed that anomalies tend to cluster on higher elevations, steeper slopes and south-facing aspects. Our findings underscore the value of combining remote sensing time series with machine learning and topographic analysis to support adaptive forest management under changing Mediterranean conditions.

title: Clarifying the roles of hydrogen and peroxyl radicals in the degradation of aromatic hydrocarbon polymer-based proton exchange membranes
summary: Abstract Chemical degradation by radicals limits the durability of aromatic hydrocarbon-based proton exchange membranes used in fuel cells and water electrolyzers. While hydroxyl radicals (HO • ) are recognized as important degradation init
content: Abstract Chemical degradation by radicals limits the durability of aromatic hydrocarbon-based proton exchange membranes used in fuel cells and water electrolyzers. While hydroxyl radicals (HO • ) are recognized as important degradation initiators, the roles of hydrogen (H • ) and peroxyl radicals (HOO • /ROO • ) remain poorly understood. Here, γ-radiolysis of water was used to selectively generate H • and HOO • /ROO • along with HO • under acidic conditions relevant to device operation. Two aromatic sulfonate model compounds representing structural motifs of hydrocarbon ionomers were exposed to radicals in N 2 saturated and O 2 containing solutions at pH 0 and 2. In the presence of HO • , degradation increased with radical dose and was enhanced by oxygen and increasing pH, consistent with established HO • -induced degradation pathways. Selective suppression of HO • using tert -butanol showed that H • radicals cause negligible degradation of the aromatic substrates, while HOO • and organic peroxyl radicals (ROO • ) exhibit only minor reactivity. These results indicate that HO • is the principal radical responsible for degradation of the investigated aromatic hydrocarbon model compounds, whereas H • and HOO • /ROO • contribute little to substrate loss. The findings improve the mechanistic understanding of radical-induced degradation and provide guidance for the development of more durable hydrocarbon membranes.

title: Running style and stability during uphill running are largely preserved with increasing shoe sole thickness
summary: Advanced footwear technology (AFT) shoes incorporate increased sole thickness and compliant midsole materials that may alter running biomechanics. While these effects have been widely studied during level running, little is known about how
content: Advanced footwear technology (AFT) shoes incorporate increased sole thickness and compliant midsole materials that may alter running biomechanics. While these effects have been widely studied during level running, little is known about how sole thickness influences running style and stability during uphill running. This study examined the effects of two AFT shoes differing in sole thickness (35 mm-AFT35; 50 mm-AFT50) and a traditional control shoe (27 mm-CON27) on running style and stability during uphill running. Seventeen experienced male runners performed treadmill running at a 10% incline at 6.5 and 10 km/h in three shoe conditions. Running style was assessed using duty factor, normalized step frequency, center-of-mass oscillation, vertical and leg stiffness, and lower-limb joint kinematics. Running stability was evaluated using local dynamic stability via the maximum Lyapunov exponent and detrended fluctuation analysis of stride time. Duty factor and normalized step frequency did not differ between shoes. However, AFT shoes showed greater center-of-mass oscillation (p = 0.004), and lower vertical stiffness (p = 0.022) compared to CON27. Joint kinematics revealed significant shoe effects at the ankle (p = 0.001), particularly increased dorsiflexion and eversion in AFT conditions. Running stability showed only minor changes. Local dynamic stability differed at the trunk (p = 0.027), with reduced stability in AFT50 compared with CON27 (p = 0.006), while global stability remained unchanged. No shoe × speed interactions were observed for any variable. Overall, uphill running style and stability remained largely preserved across shoe conditions, suggesting that sole thickness alone had limited influence.

title: Conformational Analysis of Methoxy- and Methylthio-Substituted Thiophenes by Broadband Rotational Spectroscopy and Computational Chemistry
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
summary: Abstract Functionalized aromatic heterocycles exhibit strong conformational preferences dependent on the identity of the heteroatom, substituent functional group, and substitution position. In this study, we investigated the conformational
content: Abstract Functionalized aromatic heterocycles exhibit strong conformational preferences dependent on the identity of the heteroatom, substituent functional group, and substitution position. In this study, we investigated the conformational landscapes of 2- and 3-substituted methoxy- and methylthio- thiophenes by chirped-pulse Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy. One lowest energy conformation for each molecule was identified due to efficient conformational cooling in the pulsed jet. For three of the four species, the conformational preference orients the substituent group syn to a double bond with all heavy atoms in the plane, while 2-(methylthio)thiophene uniquely adopts a skew conformation in which the barrier to methyl internal rotation is substantially reduced. Quantum chemical calculations, including natural bond orbital analysis, reveal that a balance of steric and stereoelectronic effects determines the lowest energy conformations of these species.

title: AI agent supervision of structural model building and refinement
summary: Structural model building and refinement need many decisions between different programs. These decisions often depend on an experienced researcher who knows how the programs work together and how to read experimental data. We used Claude Co
content: Structural model building and refinement need many decisions between different programs. These decisions often depend on an experienced researcher who knows how the programs work together and how to read experimental data. We used Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 to supervise this work for 24 cryo-EM and X-ray cases. The work finished in about 36 hours on one workstation. The agent prepared the inputs, ran established programs, read the validation results, compared candidate models and chose the next step. For 15 deposited cryo-EM models with weak starting geometry, the median MolProbity score improved from 2.62 to 1.76. For three crystal structures, the agent models came close to the published Rfree values. Chemical information such as ligands, ions and modifications must be provided by the researcher, in the same way as the sequence. With this information, the agent can place and check these components. These results show that agent supervision is acceptable when every decision can be inspected. The researcher makes the final scientific judgment. We suggest practical requirements for this kind of use. Future AI agents may help researchers obtain high quality and reliable structures of biological macromolecules.

title: TERRAS RARAS E TRANSIÇÃO ENERGÉTICA: SOBERANIA MINERAL E LIMITES SOCIOAMBIENTAIS DA LEI Nº 15.506/2026
summary: The extraction of rare earths for technologies associated with the energy transition requires industrial development and mineral sovereignty to be reconciled with the protection of producing territories. This study aims to analyze the socio
content: The extraction of rare earths for technologies associated with the energy transition requires industrial development and mineral sovereignty to be reconciled with the protection of producing territories. This study aims to analyze the socio-environmental limits governing the application of Brazilian Law No. 15,506/2026 to rare earth supply chains, considering its relationship with constitutional environmental protection duties. The research adopts a deductive method and a qualitative, exploratory and descriptive approach, based on bibliographic and documentary research. The analysis distinguishes geological availability, industrial capacity and socio-environmental admissibility, arguing that the strategic importance of these resources does not justify presuming the sustainability of mining projects. It also examines the scope of low-carbon certification and traceability, whose functions must remain coordinated with environmental licensing and regulatory oversight. As an analytical contribution, the study proposes three interpretive criteria: industrial additionality, ecological integrity and territorial legitimacy. It concludes that strengthening mineral sovereignty requires the development of domestic technological capabilities alongside impact assessment and the protection of affected people. Given the law’s recent enactment, the findings concern its normative design without attributing effects to instruments whose implementation has not been investigated.

title: Determinants of bacteriophage Qβ survival under ionizing radiation: roles of hydration, mineral matrices, and viral features
summary: Introduction Understanding how viruses persist under extreme physicochemical conditions is essential for both extreme microbiology and astrobiology. While the effects of a great variety of individual stressors have been explored, comparativ
content: Introduction Understanding how viruses persist under extreme physicochemical conditions is essential for both extreme microbiology and astrobiology. While the effects of a great variety of individual stressors have been explored, comparative analyses across different environmental and viral determinants remain limited. In particular, the respective contributions of radiation, hydration state, mineral matrices, and intrinsic viral properties to viral persistence remain largely unexplored. Methods We investigated the response of bacteriophage Qβ to increasing doses of ionizing radiation under different physicochemical conditions. Viral survival was quantified in liquid and desiccated systems, in the presence of Martian (MGS-1) and Lunar (LMS-1) regolith simulants, and at different initial viral concentrations. In addition, the susceptibility to ionizing radiation of a thermotolerant mutant was also evaluated. Dose-response relationships were analyzed using log-logistic or log-linear models depending on data structure. Results Analyses of the effect of initial viral concentration produced model-dependent results, indicating that any concentration-dependent effect on the radiation response should be interpreted with caution. In liquid medium, MGS-1 (12.5% w/v) modified the response of Qβ to ionizing radiation under the experimental conditions tested, producing a shift in the dose–response relationship and altering inactivation kinetics. However, at a fixed radiation dose of 750 Gy, increased survival was observed only at the highest MGS-1 concentration tested (100% w/v), whereas LMS-1 did not show evidence of a comparable effect under the same experimental conditions. Desiccation dramatically enhanced viral radiotolerance, increasing survival by several orders of magnitude. Finally, the thermotolerant mutant exhibited substantially higher survival under ionizing radiation, indicating that properties of the virion contribute to stress tolerance. Discussion Our results demonstrate that viral resistance to ionizing radiation depends on both intrinsic viral features and environmental factors. Among these, hydration state appears as the dominant determinant of survival, while the presence of mineral matrices may exert different effects. This integrative framework highlights the need to consider multiple variables when evaluating viral persistence in extreme environments.

title: Fischer Indole Synthesis Inspired De Novo and Modular Assembly of Indolines
summary: Abstract Herein, we report a modular and redox-neutral strategy for the de novo synthesis of structurally diverse indolines. While conventional approaches often rely on prefunctionalized arenes or require oxidative/reductive steps, our meth
content: Abstract Herein, we report a modular and redox-neutral strategy for the de novo synthesis of structurally diverse indolines. While conventional approaches often rely on prefunctionalized arenes or require oxidative/reductive steps, our method enables direct annulation from ortho-unsubstituted anilines and vinyldiazos. The sequence comprises a rhodium-catalyzed α-selective N–H insertion of vinyldiazoacetates, followed by TFA-promoted aza-Claisen rearrangement and intramolecular aza-Michael addition. This one-pot sequential protocol exhibits broad substrate generality and has been extended to an asymmetric version and intramolecular variant, allowing the synthesis of challenging seven-membered ring-fused indolines. DFT studies support a concerted mechanism via a chairlike transition state. With its operational simplicity and structural versatility, this methodology provides an efficient route to access privileged indoline scaffolds for pharmaceutical and synthetic applications.

title: Complexity-Informed Analysis in Data-Scarce Cities
source: Transactions of the Association of European Schools of Planning
summary: Urban change often unfolds in ways that are difficult to observe and explain, particularly in data-scarce cities. To address this, this paper presents a complexity-informed exploratory framework for spatial analysis using globally consisten
content: Urban change often unfolds in ways that are difficult to observe and explain, particularly in data-scarce cities. To address this, this paper presents a complexity-informed exploratory framework for spatial analysis using globally consistent Earth observation data. Here, data scarcity refers not to absence but to limitations in validation, temporal continuity, resolution, and proxy alignment. Guided by non-linearity, emergence, and distributed agency, the framework compares multiple indicators: built-up extent, density, vegetation, and land consumption across time and space, and examines their alignment and divergence. It applies explicit stopping rules to bound interpretation and treats ambiguity and non-detection as valid analytical outcomes; illustrated through an application to La Paz–El Alto. The framework establishes a disciplined basis for interpreting spatial evidence and supporting planning-relevant orientation under constrained observation.

title: Benthic foraminiferal turnover and the paleoenvironmental evolution of the Maikop Basin: From agglutinated to calcareous dominance (Kerch Peninsula, late Oligocene–Middle Miocene)
summary: Based on the revision of archival data by M.F. Kozyreva (1947–1949) and their modern reinterpretation, the paleoecological evolution of the Maikop Basin on the Kerch Peninsula sector during the Late Kerleutian–Tarkhanian (late Oligocene–Mid
content: Based on the revision of archival data by M.F. Kozyreva (1947–1949) and their modern reinterpretation, the paleoecological evolution of the Maikop Basin on the Kerch Peninsula sector during the Late Kerleutian–Tarkhanian (late Oligocene–Middle Miocene) was reconstructed using benthic foraminifera. Presence/absence data were analysed using Jaccard cluster analysis, taxa richness (S), and morphogroup analysis of agglutinated taxa, which allowed for the reconstruction of the temporal evolution of benthic foraminiferal assemblages, associated bottom-water environmental changes, and four successive phases of ecosystem transformation at local and basin-wide scales. The initial phase (Late Kerleutian–early Sakaraulian) was characterised by persistent agglutinated assemblages under relatively stable bathyal conditions, with recurrent Bathysiphon crises associated with reduced bottom-water circulation. The late Sakaraulian records the first calcareous inversion and local ecological restructuring within the existing bathyal basin. The Kotsakhurian records the regional ecological crisis, which is expressed by the widespread occurrence of monospecific Saccammina zuramakensis assemblages under hydrochemical instability. The Tarkhanian records a second calcareous inversion that is fundamentally different from the Sakaraulian event. It reflects basin shallowing toward outer sublittoral settings, increased marine connectivity, faunal renewal, and improved bottom-water oxygenation, while the characteristic Maikop-type of sedimentation was still maintained. These results demonstrate that, during the Late Kerleutian–Tarkhanian evolution of the Maikop Basin on the Kerch Peninsula sector, both local and regional environmental reorganisations elicited a recurrent pattern of benthic assemblage response, which is characterised by ecological crises followed by renewal.

title: Growth-state as a determinant of in vivo virulence of Mycoplasma pneumoniae
summary: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a leading cause of community acquired pneumonia and bronchitis in people, particularly children and young adults. Like many bacterial pathogens, M. pneumoniae can grow in biofilm towers on both biotic and abiotic su
content: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a leading cause of community acquired pneumonia and bronchitis in people, particularly children and young adults. Like many bacterial pathogens, M. pneumoniae can grow in biofilm towers on both biotic and abiotic surfaces. Current models indicate that planktonic M. pneumoniae are simply individual cells that are dispersed from biofilm towers due to physical shear forces, and do not represent a bona fide planktonic growth state. However recent data indicate that these fractions may be physiologically distinct and may differentially influence disease outcome. We observed that experimental infection of mice with inoculum containing both adherent and non-adherent fractions of M. pneumoniae produced more severe lung pathology than inoculum prepared from M. pneumoniae adherent biofilms alone. Direct comparison of experimental infection with titer matched non-adherent (P-Mp) and adherent (B-Mp) fractions revealed that P-Mp produces more severe lung pathology compared to infection with B-Mp. Furthermore, experimental infection with a lower dose of P-Mp resulted in similar lung pathology relative to B-Mp infected mice. This increase in pathology was not associated with differences in bacterial burden, bacterial dispersal during inoculum preparation, nor due to differences in the phenotype of host immune responses. Comparative proteomics revealed that certain known and putative virulence factors associated with immune evasion are upregulated in P-Mp, potentially explaining the difference in virulence between the two fractions. Furthermore, comparative proteomics revealed distinct metabolic phenotypes between the two fractions, consistent with distinct planktonic and biofilm growth states, indicating that P-Mp likely represents a bona fide planktonic growth state. Collectively, these data implicate the growth state of M. pneumoniae as a determinant of in vivo virulence for this atypical human pathogen.

title: Omics-Driven Design of Organic Nanomaterials for Sustainable Agriculture: Decoding Plant−Nanomaterial Interactions
summary: Abstract The application of nanomaterials in agriculture has emerged as a promising strategy to improve crop productivity, optimize agrochemical delivery, and support sustainable crop management. However, the development of agricultural nan
content: Abstract The application of nanomaterials in agriculture has emerged as a promising strategy to improve crop productivity, optimize agrochemical delivery, and support sustainable crop management. However, the development of agricultural nanoformulations remains largely empirical, particularly for biodegradable organic nanomaterials, owing to the limited mechanistic understanding of plant−nanomaterial interactions. Recent advances in omics and multiomics approaches are transforming this scenario by revealing how nanomaterials actively modulate molecular, metabolic, and physiological processes rather than acting solely as passive delivery systems. In this review, we examine how omics approaches are reshaping our understanding of plant responses to organic nanomaterials, highlighting emerging patterns of biological reprogramming, the influence of nanomaterial physicochemical properties on these responses, and current challenges in experimental standardization, multiomics integration, mechanistic interpretation, and field validation. The available evidence does not support a universally optimal nanomaterial, highlighting the need for biologically informed design strategies tailored to material properties, plant responses, and application conditions. Finally, we propose omics-guided design as a conceptual strategy in which biological information becomes an active engineering parameter for rationally developing next-generation organic nanomaterials. This perspective highlights how molecular information can support more targeted, biologically informed, and environmentally responsible nanoformulation strategies.

title: Comprehensive 4E evaluation of an integrated LNG and LH2 system from natural hydrogen well reservoirs
summary: The lack of a cost-competitive, low-carbon hydrogen supply pathway remains one of the most critical barriers to the global hydrogen economy. Natural hydrogen, a primary energy source occurring in geological formations, presents a compelling
content: The lack of a cost-competitive, low-carbon hydrogen supply pathway remains one of the most critical barriers to the global hydrogen economy. Natural hydrogen, a primary energy source occurring in geological formations, presents a compelling solution, yet engineering frameworks for its large-scale processing and utilization remain insufficiently developed. This study proposes an integrated process for simultaneous LNG and LH 2 co-production from a natural hydrogen well stream at 300 TPD, comparing LN 2 -based (Case 1) and SMR-based (Case 2) precooling configurations. Case 2 achieves 36.9% lower SEC and 54.1% less exergy destruction than Case 1, with 45–55% improvement over commercial plants. Techno-economic analysis yields an NPV of 404 million USD, IRR of 13%, and a production cost as low as 0.22 USD/kg at 3 MTPA scale. These results demonstrate that natural hydrogen can serve as a technically viable and economically transformative primary energy resource, potentially accelerating the transition toward a sustainable hydrogen economy.

title: Metabolic immune checkpoints (MICs) in cancer: from molecular mechanisms to challenges and opportunities in clinical translation
summary: Metabolic reprogramming is a core feature of tumor cells in adapting to microenvironmental stress and acquiring malignant phenotypes. It not only supports rapid proliferation but also mediates immune escape by reshaping the immune microenvi
content: Metabolic reprogramming is a core feature of tumor cells in adapting to microenvironmental stress and acquiring malignant phenotypes. It not only supports rapid proliferation but also mediates immune escape by reshaping the immune microenvironment. In recent years, the "metabolism-immune axis", serving as a central hub for the crosstalk between metabolic regulation and immune suppression, has provided a new perspective for understanding tumor immune evasion. This review systematically discusses how metabolic pathways, including glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism, along with mitochondrial function and other related processes, shape the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment by regulating immune cell function, immune checkpoint expression, and immune signaling networks, thereby promoting tumor immune escape. The concept of "metabolic immune checkpoints (MICs)" is innovatively proposed and classified into three categories based on their mechanisms of action: (1) MIC-I: metabolic modification-type immune checkpoints, exemplified by posttranslational modifications of immune checkpoint molecules such as PD-L1 lactylation, acetylation and glycosylation, etc.; (2) MIC-II: metabolic enzyme-dependent immune regulatory nodes, represented by enzymes such as indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 and others that directly influence immune cell function; and (3) MIC-III: microbial metabolite-coupled immune regulatory targets, including receptors for microbe-derived metabolites such as short-chain fatty acid receptors. By integrating molecular interaction networks of key targets such as lactate dehydrogenase A and ATP citrate lyase, this review explores synergistic therapeutic strategies that combine small-molecule inhibitors targeting MICs with immune checkpoint blockade. This highlights how metabolic intervention can restore immune cell function and reverse exhaustion. Current key challenges in clinical translation include limitations in metabolic dynamic monitoring technologies, lack of patient stratification biomarkers and insufficient specificity in microbiome regulation. Future directions will focus on personalized treatment guided by multiomics, integrating single-cell metabolic flux analysis, deep learning-driven target prediction, and synthetic microbiome engineering, driving tumor immunotherapy into the era of precision metabolic regulation. By integrating the fundamental mechanisms of MICs with translational medical research, this review not only provides a systematic paradigm but also establishes a foundation for the development of new-generation precision combination therapies.

title: Humidity‐driven shape morphing enhances fog harvesting in porous cactus spines
summary: Cacti develop spines instead of conventional leaves, which often serve as mechanical defence against herbivores. However, some cactus species grow porous and flexible spines, suggesting fundamentally different functions. Here we demonstrate
content: Cacti develop spines instead of conventional leaves, which often serve as mechanical defence against herbivores. However, some cactus species grow porous and flexible spines, suggesting fundamentally different functions. Here we demonstrate that the porous spines of Turbinicarpus alonsoi, a cactus native to central Mexico, function as hygro-morphing fog harvesters. Using experiments, we show that the spines are highly hygroscopic and straighten when exposed to fog, leading to increased fog-water collection rates. Numerical simulations confirm that straightening is driven by swelling-induced pressure in the cell walls of the spines. Swelling results from capillary imbibition of fog water and predominantly generates expansion in the transverse plane, which causes the pre-curved spines to straighten. Despite their porosity and hygroscopicity, the spines prevent direct absorption of fog water into the living cortex due to the presence of a suberin-rich tissue layer that instead promotes surface runoff towards the roots. Our work suggests that hygro-morphing emerges from distinct structural, biochemical and geometric adaptations of cactus spines and enables a fine modulation of the flow dynamics on the spine surface. The increasing plant water supply from fog by shape morphing provides a potential advantage for survival in a hot, semi-arid region with frequent fog formation.

title: Aligning Geological Storage, Industrial Decarbonisation, and Regional Planning for Post-Coal Sustainability: A Systems Perspective from Western Macedonia, Greece
summary: Coal-dependent regions face a multidimensional transition challenge that extends beyond energy substitution and requires coordinated transformation of industrial systems, landscapes, infrastructure, governance and local economies. Using a s
content: Coal-dependent regions face a multidimensional transition challenge that extends beyond energy substitution and requires coordinated transformation of industrial systems, landscapes, infrastructure, governance and local economies. Using a structured narrative review and framework-building approach, this paper develops a systems-based framework for sustainable post-lignite transition, using Western Macedonia as the main integrated case and Megalopolis as a comparative Greek lignite region. The proposed approach integrates four interrelated domains: subsurface and geological potential, industrial decarbonisation pathways, post-mining land and infrastructure reuse, and socio-economic and governance transition. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), low-carbon industrial technologies, renewable energy integration, energy-storage options, land rehabilitation, heritage valorisation and place-based development strategies. The analysis highlights that successful post-coal transition depends not only on the availability of individual technological solutions, but also on their spatial, environmental, economic and governance compatibility within the regional system. By aligning geological knowledge, engineering innovation, environmental management and just-transition planning, the paper proposes an integrated planning framework intended to structure the consideration of multiple forms of evidence in former lignite regions. The framework is broadly consistent with the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those related to clean energy, resilient infrastructure, sustainable communities, responsible land reuse, climate action and ecosystem restoration, and offers transferable insights for European coal regions seeking resilient, diversified and low-carbon development pathways.

title: Climate-adaptive amine sweetening optimization via the critical reversal temperature for seasonal mercaptan-accumulation and dehydration control
summary: Seasonal temperature variability can fundamentally alter the limiting mechanism in industrial amine gas sweetening, creating a trade-off between low-temperature methyl-mercaptan accumulation and high-temperature dehydration demand that cann
content: Seasonal temperature variability can fundamentally alter the limiting mechanism in industrial amine gas sweetening, creating a trade-off between low-temperature methyl-mercaptan accumulation and high-temperature dehydration demand that cannot be adequately addressed by a single annual operating point. Here, we develop a climate-adaptive, cost-aware optimization framework for an industrial methyl diethanolamine-piperazine (MDEA-PZ) sweetening system exposed to ambient temperatures from -4 to 46°C. A calibrated reduced-order model was constructed from eleven plant-validated seasonal operating states and evaluated using leave-one-season-out (LOSO) validation, yielding mean absolute percentage errors of 0.040% for reboiler duty, 2.34% for methyl mercaptan concentration, and 9.46% for sweet-gas water content. A polynomial Ridge surrogate trained over a 1400-point Latin hypercube design subsequently achieved a mean R² of 0.9782, a minimum R² of 0.9381 across all outputs, and a maximum MAPE of 2.05%. The central contribution is the identification of a Critical Reversal Temperature (CRT), defined here as the ambient temperature at which the dominant normalized operating burden switches from a methyl-mercaptan accumulation proxy to sweet-gas dehydration; it is not presented as a direct corrosion-rate threshold. For the nominal benchmark composition and solvent strength, the CRT was 19.61°C, and water-content, normalization-bound, and TOPSIS-weight sensitivity tests consistently retained the thermal-policy transition near 20°C. In contrast, exploratory off-design composition/solvent-strength scenarios shifted the modeled CRT over a wider 8.36-24.22°C range and are explicitly treated as scenario exploration rather than independently plant-validated predictions. Relative to the reference seasonal operation, the model-based CRT-adaptive screening strategy reduced annual OPEX from approximately 11.5 to 9.8 MUSD yr⁻¹, corresponding to about 1.8 MUSD yr⁻¹ in annual savings; the 15-year incremental NPV was approximately 16.2 MUSD with a simple payback of about 0.5 years. Because off-design circulation response is semi-empirical, the adaptive setpoints and associated economic outputs should be interpreted as screening predictions pending high-fidelity or plant re-validation. These results establish CRT as a physically interpretable regime-transition descriptor conditional on the benchmark model and provide a control-oriented framework for climate-responsive operation.

title: Quantifying Water Matrix Controls on PFAS Electrooxidation Degradation and Energy Efficiency
summary: Abstract Electrooxidation (EO) has been studied for PFAS treatment, but water matrix effects remain poorly understood. This study investigates how water matrix composition, PFAS concentration, and ionic conductivity govern EO performance an
content: Abstract Electrooxidation (EO) has been studied for PFAS treatment, but water matrix effects remain poorly understood. This study investigates how water matrix composition, PFAS concentration, and ionic conductivity govern EO performance and energy efficiency. Using a bench-scale EO reactor, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and response surface methodology (RSM), we evaluated PFAS degradation, electrical energy per order (EE/O), and short-chain transformation products. PFOS exhibited faster kinetics than PFOA (2.20 vs 0.25 h–1), achieving 99.5% removal at 1 ppm. Decreasing PFOS concentration to 0.01 ppm increased EE/O from 1.47 to 4.05 kWh m–3 order–1. Decreasing ionic conductivity from 50 to 1 mS cm–1 reduced 1-h PFOS removal from 98.4% to 73.5% and increased EE/O from 1.89 to 5.87 kWh m–3 order–1, consistent with increasing uncompensated resistance. Coexisting anions showed divergent effects: chloride enhanced PFOS degradation, nitrate inhibited it above 10 mM, and sulfate exhibited concentration-dependent behavior. The RSM-predicted optimal anion composition (30 mM SO42–, 0 mM NO3–, 10 mM Cl–) was experimentally validated (38.9% vs 40.8% predicted removal). Natural organic matter was the dominant inhibitor in complex matrices. These results quantify how water matrix composition governs EO performance and energy efficiency in PFAS-laden brines and regenerants.

title: Institutional determinants of sustainability awareness in higher education: advancing SDG 4.7 through curriculum integration, policy frameworks and campus engagement
source: International Journal of Sustainability in Higher Education
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of institutional mechanisms, including academic curriculum integration, policy frameworks and campus sustainability initiatives, on sustainability awareness among undergraduate students in highe
content: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of institutional mechanisms, including academic curriculum integration, policy frameworks and campus sustainability initiatives, on sustainability awareness among undergraduate students in higher education. Conducted within the context of Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) City Campus, this research contributes to global efforts in achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4.7 by promoting education for sustainable development through institutional innovation. It responds to calls for evidence-based practices in sustainability management within higher education institutions (HEIs), particularly in ASEAN contexts. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional, quantitative study was conducted using proportionate stratified random sampling among 311 undergraduate students from four faculties, which are the Faculty of Data Science and Computing, Faculty of Entrepreneurship and Business, Faculty of Hospitality, Tourism and Wellness and Faculty of Veterinary Medicine at UMK City Campus. Validated multi-item instruments were used to measure institutional determinants and sustainability awareness. Data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) to evaluate the measurement and structural models, with all significance tests conducted two-tailed. Findings The results show that academic curriculum integration, institutional policy frameworks and campus sustainability initiatives are each significantly associated with students’ sustainability awareness. Among these, curriculum integration recorded the largest coefficient. Peer and community influence did not reach conventional significance (β = 0.12, p = 0.060). The four institutional mechanisms together explained 61% of the variance in sustainability awareness (R² = 0.61), indicating that institutional design accounts for a substantial share of variation in students’ environmental consciousness, although the cross-sectional design does not permit causal inference. Research limitations/implications This study advances institutional theory by showing that the three institutional pillars are not equivalent in their capacity to shape individual cognition: regulative and normative mechanisms, expressed through policy and curriculum, showed clear micro-level penetration, whereas the cultural-cognitive mechanism represented by peer influence did not. Mapping these pillars onto the antecedents of the theory of planned behaviour (TPB) yields a boundary condition for TPB, namely, that the subjective-norm pathway is institutionally contingent rather than universal and should not be expected to operate where the cultural-cognitive pillar is not yet consolidated. This study is based on a single Malaysian university, so the model requires replication across institutions at different stages of sustainability institutionalisation, ideally using longitudinal designs capable of establishing temporal precedence. Practical implications The

title: Manganese scavenging is required for virulence of the cytosolic pathogen Listeria monocytogenes
summary: Metals are essential for all forms of life and are therefore the subject of tight competition at the host-pathogen interface. Manganese (Mn) is an important cofactor for enzymes involved in various processes in bacteria, including the respo
content: Metals are essential for all forms of life and are therefore the subject of tight competition at the host-pathogen interface. Manganese (Mn) is an important cofactor for enzymes involved in various processes in bacteria, including the response to oxidative stress, and the ability to scavenge Mn through the expression of high-affinity Mn transporters has been associated with virulence of many extracellular and vacuolar pathogens. While the cytosol has been established to be restrictive for growth of non-adapted pathogens, the extent to which metal limitation contributes to this is not well understood.
