summary: Developing countries face persistent constraints in producing transparent, consistent and nationally owned greenhouse-gas inventories for the land sector. Kenya responded through the System for Land-based Emissions Estimation in Kenya (SLEE
tags: Land use, land-use change and forestry
content: Developing countries face persistent constraints in producing transparent, consistent and nationally owned greenhouse-gas inventories for the land sector. Kenya responded through the System for Land-based Emissions Estimation in Kenya (SLEEK), a national programme designed to integrate activity data, country-specific parameters, spatial modelling, reporting tools and institutional capacity. This paper examines SLEEK’s contribution to emissions and removals accounting from Kenya’s land sector using documentary analysis of programme records, technical manuals, national reporting material and carbon-accounting spreadsheets for 1990-2015. The evidence shows that SLEEK supported complete land representation across six IPCC land-use classes, generated wall-to-wall land-cover and land-use change datasets for 17 epochs, enabled emission-factor development for forest strata and supplied land-sector activity data used in FOLU accounting. The accounting spreadsheets estimate cumulative net CO2 emissions of 858.66 Mt CO2 over 1990-2015, equivalent to an average of 34.35 Mt CO2 yr-1. Montane and Western rainforest strata accounted for 72.83% of cumulative forest-stratum emissions, while land converted to grassland and cropland were the dominant source categories. SLEEK’s major contribution was therefore both technical and institutional: it converted fragmented datasets into an auditable national accounting chain while building domestic expertise for transparency reporting.

title: Short-lived halogen sources and chemistry in the Community Earth System Model v2 (CESM2-SLH)
summary: Abstract. The implementation of short-lived halogen (SLH) sources and atmospheric chemistry in the Community Earth System Model v1 (CESM1), has extended the capabilities of this state-of-the-art model to study how SLH chemistry alters the o
content: Abstract. The implementation of short-lived halogen (SLH) sources and atmospheric chemistry in the Community Earth System Model v1 (CESM1), has extended the capabilities of this state-of-the-art model to study how SLH chemistry alters the oxidative capacity of the atmosphere and, consequently, the Earth’s climate. In this manuscript, we summarize 15 years of research and developments of SLH chemistry in CESM1 and present a complete revision of the porting of the original SLH implementation into the latest released version of CESM (v2), hereafter CESM2-SLH. This includes a detailed description of all offline and online sources of organic and inorganic SLH, as well as the gas-phase and heterogeneous recycling of chlorine, bromine and iodine in the troposphere and stratosphere, including their species-independent atmospheric sinks. In doing so, we provide a comprehensive evaluation of how changes in model parameters and coupled dynamics within the Community Atmosphere Model v6 (CAM6) affect SLH abundances and their implications. The new CESM2-SLH implementation offers various component sets (compsets) and resolutions, all of which result in equivalent global budgets and zonal distributions of organic and inorganic chlorine, bromine and iodine, which in turn, lead to SLH impacts on atmospheric composition that are consistent with previous CESM1 results. The released CESM2-SLH version includes specific namelist options, input files and technical notes detailing the most important SLH updates implemented over the CESM2/CAM6 routines. Our results show that the global tropospheric burden and tropical stratospheric injection of organic and inorganic chlorine, bromine and iodine species in CESM2-SLH are in agreement with observational assessments and previous modelling studies using CESM1, resulting in significant reductions in global ozone abundance (−21–28 % at the surface, −17–22 % in the troposphere and −2–3 % in the stratosphere) as well as in OH and NO2 (ranging between −2–9 % and −1–10 %, respectively), depending on the specific model configuration and resolution. Based on this, we encourage the wider CESM community to consider the released CESM2-SLH scheme to obtain a more realistic representation of the background influence of natural and anthropogenic short-lived halogen sources and chemistry in air quality and Earth’s climate studies.

title: Observational and model data from Planetary's TC26.1 Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement dosing period in Halifax, NS, Canada
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Submission Overview This submission contains data and documentation from Planetary's TC26.1 Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) dosing and crediting period. Dosing and monitoring occurred in Halifax Harbour between November 2025 and January
content: Submission Overview This submission contains data and documentation from Planetary's TC26.1 Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement (OAE) dosing and crediting period. Dosing and monitoring occurred in Halifax Harbour between November 2025 and January 2026, with carbon dioxide removal (CDR) occurring up to 13 March, 2026. These data are provided in support of the Carbon to Sea OAE Data Management Protocol (Long et al. 2025), and Planetary's TC26.1 credit issuance. Metadata and project information are also contained on the OAE data commons and Isometric registry, respectively. The current submission is in alignment with v.1.0.0 of the Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Data Management Protocol, v1.9 of the Isometric Standard, and v1.0 of the Isometric Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement from Coastal Outfalls protocol. Planetary's 2025 Community Engagement report is also archived here. The report provides significant context for the strong community collaboration and support that uphold much of the scientific findings and datasets in this submission. The data contained in this submission are provided under a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 International license. They are intended for non-commercial use only. Please use the following conventions when citing the reports or data contained herein: Reports: Planetary (2026). REPORT NAME. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20088388. Data: Planetary (2026). Observational and model data from Planetary's TC26.1 Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement dosing period in Halifax, NS, Canada. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20088388. Project description Planetary operates a continuous mineral OAE site out of the Nova Scotia Power Tufts Cove generation plant in Halifax, NS, Canada. At the plant, a high-solids feedstock slurry is produced using ambient seawater, and dosed into a cooling loop outfall, where it enters the receiving waters of Halifax Harbour and Bedford Basin. Partnering with Dalhousie University researchers, the biogeochemical and environmental impacts are monitored through continuous, in-pipe flow-through measurements and sample collection from boat surveys of various locations in the receiving environment. The resulting monitoring data, comprising pH and other carbon-system measurements, turbidity, total suspended solids, temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, and water and sediment metals fulfil Planetary’s regulatory and environmental monitoring compliance program, and R&D and MRV endeavours.Operational measurements are integrated with ocean modelling to quantify carbon sequestration. Gross removals are determined as the difference in cumulative air-sea CO2 flux between model simulations including the OAE intervention and a counterfactual simulation, which resolves the prevailing ocean state, including the natural background ocean uptake and/or outgassing of CO2 over the same domain and time period, but without the project’s alkalinity addition. title: The Strategic Importance of the Sea and the Protection of Its Natural Resources: Challenges and Opportunities in the Global Context from the Perspective of the Brazilian Navy
summary: Brazil is a maritime nation by nature: it is the largest nation in the South Atlantic; it possesses the most extensive coastline and topography conductive to establishing suitable ports; 80% of its population resides in coastal areas; 95% o
content: Brazil is a maritime nation by nature: it is the largest nation in the South Atlantic; it possesses the most extensive coastline and topography conductive to establishing suitable ports; 80% of its population resides in coastal areas; 95% of its foreign trade is carried out by sea; it is situated on the eastern salient of South America -specifically at the narrowest point of the Atlantic, closest to Africa (the Natal-Dakar route)- and possesses an immense economic potential (not yet fully quantified) regarding mineral and energy resources within its Exclusive Economic Zone. According to De Castro (1998: 44), “Brazil was born from the sea and in the sea, and its manifest destiny dictates that it must live from the sea; therefore, it cannot turn its back on it.” Thus, the most critical mission of the Brazilian navy remains “sea denial”, ensuring control and freedom of navigation, and promoting responsible maritime development (Silva & Moura, 2016). The Brazilian economy has a maritime dimension, if we focus on those sectors directly linked to the sea, as well as a range of activities related to the sea, that is, those indirectly influenced by the Atlantic Ocean. These activities generate economic linkages and multiplier effects, such as the marine manufacturing industry, marine biological and fishery resources, and maritime transport (cf. Carvalho, 2018). This text analyses the state policies supporting the tasks of the Brazilian Navy in protecting natural resources of a marine nature.

title: Layer-specific microbial community structures in the meromictic lake, Lake Suigetsu, unveiled by 16S rRNA gene amplicon and metagenomic analyses
summary: Meromictic lakes serve as natural laboratories for investigating microbially mediated biogeochemical cycling because their stable redox stratification supports diverse metabolic processes. Lake Suigetsu is a typical meromictic lake in Japan
content: Meromictic lakes serve as natural laboratories for investigating microbially mediated biogeochemical cycling because their stable redox stratification supports diverse metabolic processes. Lake Suigetsu is a typical meromictic lake in Japan characterized by a permanent oxycline separating the oxic brackish mixolimnion from the anoxic saline sulfidogenic monimolimnion. Recently, Lake Suigetsu's vertical bacterial composition, especially of autotrophs, sulfide oxidizers, and sulfate reducers, has gained significant attention. However, little is known about microbial communities particularly the abundant heterotrophs that contribute to the biogeochemical cycling by degrading organic matter. To characterize biogeochemical cycling in Lake Suigetsu, we investigated the microbial community structures under the amplicon sequencing variants that distinguish species and/or intraspecies populations in each layer of Lake Suigetsu by using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing analysis. We revealed the layer-specific microbial communities and there were abundant heterotrophs in each layer, in addition to the previously reported autotrophs. In the upper of monimolimnion sample, approximately 20% relative abundance was occupied by an uncultured Anaerolineaceae bacterium, that is probably an anaerobic heterotroph. In the mixolimnion, the most abundant one was SAR11 bacterium with approximately 6% relative abundance. In the oxycline, the most abundant, probably heterotrophic prokaryote was an uncultured Ectothiorhodospiraceae bacterium with approximately 5% relative abundance, while the four most abundant prokaryotes were comprised of autotrophic bacteria and occupied more than 43% relative abundance, apparently suggesting the primary production was predominant in the oxycline. This study provides insight into the layer-dependent, prokaryote-mediated biogeochemical cycling in Lake Suigetsu.

title: Evaluating Underground CO2 Storage Potential across Sedimentary Facies of the Michigan Basin
summary: Abstract Rising atmospheric CO2 concentrations demand scalable and geologically reliable carbon capture and storage solutions. The Michigan Basin, with its well-characterized Paleozoic sedimentary sequences and proximity to major industrial
content: Abstract Rising atmospheric CO2 concentrations demand scalable and geologically reliable carbon capture and storage solutions. The Michigan Basin, with its well-characterized Paleozoic sedimentary sequences and proximity to major industrial emission sources, represents a promising target for underground CO2 storage. This study systematically evaluates the CO2 storage potential of nine distinct sedimentary rock facies retrieved from the Consumers Brine Disposal 139 (BD-139) well, providing a facies-resolved framework for assessing subsurface sequestration capacity. High-pressure isochoric CO2 adsorption experiments were conducted across three temperature isotherms (25 °C, 35 °C, and 45 °C) and six pressure points (10–35 bar), complemented by comprehensive material characterization, including Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy equipped with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Based on their inferred mineralogical composition and thermal behavior, the nine facies were classified into three distinct groups: silicate-rich organic-bearing rocks (Group 1), siliciclastic assemblages with a subordinate carbonate component (Group 2), and carbonate-bearing dolomitic facies (Group 3). Facies 3 exhibited the highest apparent CO2 uptake, 855.7 mg/g at 35 bar and 25 °C, and all facies gave heats of sorption below 60 kJ/mol, consistent with predominantly physical interactions and with favorable reversibility for storage cycling. Because the measurements were performed on pulverized material, and because the apparent uptake of the highest-performing facies exceeds the volumetric capacity of its own pore system, these quantities are reported and interpreted throughout as apparent isochoric uptake determined under identical conditions. They provide a quantitative relative ranking of the facies rather than absolute in situ storage capacities, and the bounds governing their interpretation are set out in Section 3.5.3. Complementary CO2 absorption experiments in synthetic brine solutions yielded a solid precipitate on depressurization, indicating a potential mineral trapping pathway under high-pressure conditions. The findings establish a direct link between facies-level geological heterogeneity and CO2 storage performance, offering a practical screening framework for site selection and reservoir evaluation within the Michigan Basin and analogous sedimentary systems.

title: Climatological Horizontal Visibility Profile Over Indira Gandhi International Airport: A Twenty-Year Long-Term Assessment (2005–2024)
summary: Atmospheric horizontal visibility at Indira Gandhi International Airport (ICAO: VIDP; IATA: DEL), New Delhi, represents one of the most operationally restrictive meteorological phenomena affecting civil aviation in South Asia[cite: 1, 2]. T
content: Atmospheric horizontal visibility at Indira Gandhi International Airport (ICAO: VIDP; IATA: DEL), New Delhi, represents one of the most operationally restrictive meteorological phenomena affecting civil aviation in South Asia[cite: 1, 2]. This investigation presents a comprehensive, twenty-year climatological evaluation (2005–2024) of surface horizontal visibility profiles, examining the coupled interactions among regional topography, boundary layer thermodynamics, aerosol-cloud microphysics, and anthropogenic emissions[cite: 1, 2]. The observational record reveals a non-linear, U-shaped decadal trajectory in winter visibility, characterized by severe degradation during the 2005–2016 period, followed by stabilizing trends and modest recovery post-2017 attributable to targeted environmental policies and vehicular emissions standards[cite: 1, 2]. Mann-Kendall statistical trend analysis confirms a statistically significant negative trend during the first decadal epoch (ZMK = −2.92, p < 0.01), followed by a structural break and weak recovery in the subsequent epoch (ZMK = +1.15, p = 0.25)[cite: 2]. Thermodynamic analysis indicates that dense radiation fog routinely initiates at anomalously wide temperature–dew point spreads (≈ 3◦C), driven by the high concentration of hygroscopic chemical species acting as Cloud Condensation Nuclei (CCN)[cite: 1, 2]. In addition to monthly and intraseasonal transitions, this paper examines airport navigational infrastructure, flight disruption economics, and predictive operational frameworks[cite: 1, 2]. A dedicated mathematical appendix details the governing equations for aerosol extinction, boundary layer diffusion, inversion thermodynamics, statistical trend testing, and probabilistic visibility forecasting[cite: 1, 2].

title: Evaluating sediment color as a paleoceanographic proxy in Santos Basin continental slope sediments, SW Atlantic
summary: Abstract Sediment color is a valuable proxy in paleoceanography, reflecting chemical and mineralogical composition influenced by biogeochemical processes and depositional environments. This study investigates the relationship between sedime
content: Abstract Sediment color is a valuable proxy in paleoceanography, reflecting chemical and mineralogical composition influenced by biogeochemical processes and depositional environments. This study investigates the relationship between sediment color (RGB and CIE L*a*b*) and metals in three radiocarbon-dated sediment cores from the Santos Basin continental slope (SW Atlantic). The cores, located within the Upper Circumpolar Water domain, span different time intervals. Results show significant color variation, especially after the Bølling–Allerød event. Although we identified statistical correlations between metals and color parameters (e.g., positive for Ca, negative for Ti), multiple regression analyses indicated that, among the major constituents of these sediments, calcium content was the strongest statistical predictor of color variability across the cores. The statistical association between metals and color was not consistently robust, particularly with significant changes before and after the Bølling-Allerød transition, possibly due to early diagenetic processes. We argue that the relationship between sediment color and composition in samples from the Santos Basin is more complex than simple correlation coefficients, as observed at other continental margins.

title: How much saltmarsh dissolved organic carbon is mineralized before reaching the continental shelf?
summary: Tidal marsh “outwelling” of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is thought to stimulate downstream productivity and contribute to hypoxia, impacting coastal ecosystems and carbon cycling. However, quantifying the influence of marsh-derived DOC i
content: Tidal marsh “outwelling” of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is thought to stimulate downstream productivity and contribute to hypoxia, impacting coastal ecosystems and carbon cycling. However, quantifying the influence of marsh-derived DOC is challenging, as DOC is mineralized by photochemical and microbial processes as it travels along complex transport pathways to the continental shelf. Here, we combined laboratory incubations with hydrodynamic modeling to quantify how much saltmarsh DOC was mineralized within the estuary, during transport to the northern Gulf of Mexico continental shelf. Using a hydrodynamic model, we found that the average water residence time in a Louisiana marsh-estuary system was 28.5 days, spanning 3–100 days. Laboratory experiments on water from tidal marsh channels found that coupled solar irradiation enhanced microbial DOC mineralization by 215%. Combining these approaches, approximately 16% of saltmarsh DOC was mineralized during export, while a majority of saltmarsh DOC was delivered to the continental shelf. Plain Language Summary Many coastal scientists hypothesize that tidal marshes export nutrients and organic material to the ocean through a process called “outwelling”. However, it has been difficult to demonstrate that outwelling occurs and that it has a large influence on the coastal ocean, due to two primary difficulties: 1) Water in marshes moves through a network of channels and in different directions over large areas, so there is no single place to measure export, and 2) while organic matter is being transported, microorganisms and sunlight change its composition and convert some of its organic carbon into CO2 and other gases. We calculated how much of the dissolved organic carbon from a coastal marsh in Louisiana, USA was converted to CO2 and other gases before it reached the coastal ocean. We used a computer model to estimate how long organic material took to travel from different marshes to the ocean. We placed water from these marshes in bottles, where it was exposed to a powerful sun lamp and consumed by microorganisms, to understand how quickly organic carbon was removed. Combining these models and experiments, we calculated that about 16% of the dissolved organic carbon from marshes was removed while it was being exported.

title: Th-based Export Estimates Reveal Persistent Differences in Export Regimes Between Shelf and Basin Waters in the Arctic Ocean
summary: The rapidly changing Arctic Ocean remain poorly constrained with respect to particle dynamics and particulate organic carbon export. In cloudy and ice-covered polar regions, in-situ measurements are often the only means of assessing the bio
content: The rapidly changing Arctic Ocean remain poorly constrained with respect to particle dynamics and particulate organic carbon export. In cloudy and ice-covered polar regions, in-situ measurements are often the only means of assessing the biological carbon pump throughout most of the year. Here we synthesize high-resolution upper ocean observations of 234 Th (t ½ ~ 24 days) during an expansive GEOTRACES collaboration involving two 2015 expeditions spanning from the Bering Strait to the Barents Sea from late summer-fall 2015. This effort confirms that vertical surface export fluxes in the central Arctic basin (>1000 m water depth) continue to remain extremely low (range: 0–4 mmolC m -2 d -1 ). Conversely, the shelf-slope regions exhibited stronger and more variable Th deficits, with short (days to 2 weeks) residence times for dissolved 234 Th and an order of magnitude higher POC export, on average (range: 1–77 mmolC m -2 d -1 ). These shallow shelf fluxes reflect enhanced particle scavenging but may be biased by sediment resuspension, lateral advection and non-steady-state dynamics. This international effort provides an important baseline for the state of the Arctic biological pump as it is the last of only three campaigns (2005–2025) to report 234 Th-based export estimates from the central Arctic basin. Regular monitoring of Arctic Ocean is paramount as ice cover continues to decline, and more frequent episodic export events, large under ice blooms, and increased lateral transport from Arctic shelves have the potential to significantly impact the amount of particulate carbon buried in shelf sediments and reaching the deep Arctic.

title: Hybrid Writings on the Self and Ecological Dereliction
summary: How do hybrid writings—situated at the intersection of essay, autotheory, and autofiction—offer a form of "new narrative" for conceptualizing climate upheaval? Through a comparative study of Ben Lerner’s 10:04 (2014) and Maggie Nelson’s On
content: How do hybrid writings—situated at the intersection of essay, autotheory, and autofiction—offer a form of "new narrative" for conceptualizing climate upheaval? Through a comparative study of Ben Lerner’s 10:04 (2014) and Maggie Nelson’s On Freedom (2021), we will attempt to define modalities of first-person writing that investigate ecological dereliction. After discussing the distinctive nature of these texts, which reach beyond the boundaries of autotheory, we will focus on ecological mourning, expressed in a way that is both humble and original, that is, with lucidity, yet without fatalism.

title: Favorable habitats of endangered halophytes harbor unique soil properties and bacterial communities, with a dominant root-associated genus promoting host plant growth
summary: Understanding how edaphic factors and root-associated bacterial communities interact to shape plant growth is essential for effective conservation of halophytic species in coastal ecosystems. We investigated relationships among bulk soil, r
content: Understanding how edaphic factors and root-associated bacterial communities interact to shape plant growth is essential for effective conservation of halophytic species in coastal ecosystems. We investigated relationships among bulk soil, rhizosphere, and root bacterial microbiota; soil physicochemical properties; and Salicornia europaea growth spanning three distinct areas (Lakeside Park, Ubaranai and Misaki) within a brackish lake in Japan. Among the three study areas, S. europaea individuals from Lakeside Park exhibited the highest mean values for shoot length, fresh weight, dry weight, and number of primary branches, which were 1.9-, 11.2-, 12.1-, and 7.2-fold higher than those at Misaki in 2021, and 1.8-, 4.7-, 6.7-, and 4.7-fold higher than those at Misaki in 2022. Bacterial diversity and community composition associated with S. europaea varied in response to differences in plant growth and edaphic conditions. Soil texture, electrical conductivity, pH, total organic carbon, total nitrogen, C/N ratio, and water-soluble Ca 2+ were identified as key factors underlying microbial community structures. Based on heatmap and LEfse analyses, six bacterial genera, Bacteroidetes BD2-2, Candidatus Thiobios , SEEP-SRB1, Calditrichaceae , Bacteroidetes VC2.1 Bac22, and Luteibacter , were significantly enriched in areas where S. europaea exhibited vigorous growth. Among these, Luteibacter was consistently identified as the unique and dominant genus in root samples from the most favorable habitats. Inoculation experiments further demonstrated that L. aegosomatis and L. jiangsuensis significantly enhanced S. europaea growth, with shoot length, fresh weight, and dry weight being 1.4- and 1.2-, 2.1- and 1.6-, and 1.9- and 1.5-fold higher, respectively, than those of non-inoculated controls. These findings highlight that soil physicochemical conditions modulate root-associated bacterial assemblages and that a unique and dominant root-associated genus in favorable habitats may include strains capable of promoting S. europaea growth. Our results provide new ecological insights into plant–microbe–soil interactions and offer a promising framework for in situ conservation and restoration of rare halophytic species in brackish ecosystems.

title: Variations in Arctic aerosol iron solubility in relation to leaching methodology, air mass characteristics, and seasonality
summary: Abstract. Atmospheric deposition of the essential micronutrient, iron (Fe), can have an important influence on primary production and marine biogeochemistry. In the Arctic Ocean, the ongoing shift towards seasonal ice coverage means that su
content: Abstract. Atmospheric deposition of the essential micronutrient, iron (Fe), can have an important influence on primary production and marine biogeochemistry. In the Arctic Ocean, the ongoing shift towards seasonal ice coverage means that summertime atmospheric deposition increasingly takes place direct to the surface ocean, rather than onto sea ice. As a result, atmospheric deposition of material emitted from natural and anthropogenic sources may become a more relevant Fe input to the region. As part of the U.S. GEOTRACES GN01 section, aerosols and precipitation samples were collected to quantify the atmospheric delivery of Fe and other trace elements to the Arctic Ocean. Aerosol Fe solubility was assessed using three different leaching approaches. The readily soluble fraction, determined by rapid exposure leaches with ultrapure water (UPW) and filtered seawater (SW) was low throughout GN01, averaging 0.7 % and 1.4 %, respectively. Solubility determined using a more aggressive acetic acid (HAc) leach as an upper limit estimate of post-deposition aerosol Fe bioavailability averaged 44 %. Comparison to Fe UPW-solubility data from winter (median 6.5 %) and springtime (median 1.9 %) aerosol samples collected during the MOSAiC expedition suggests a strong seasonality to Arctic aerosol Fe solubility, potentially associated with winter/springtime Arctic haze. Iron stable isotope analysis of GN01 total Fe (d56FeTot = +0.10 ± 0.13 ‰) and UPW-soluble Fe (d56FeSol = −0.17 ± 0.33 ‰) indicate the low summertime total Fe loading was dominated by mineral aerosols, albeit with anthropogenic contributions to the small soluble Fe fraction in some samples. Bulk deposition fluxes, calculated using the beryllium-7 method, were estimated at 0.8 ± 1.2 nmol m-2 d-1 UPW-soluble Fe, 1.8 ± 1.9 nmol m-2 d-1 SW-soluble Fe, and 46 ± 48 nmol m-2 d-1 HAc-soluble Fe, with the UPW-soluble Fe flux around an order of magnitude lower than that measured during the winter months.

title: Microplastics in cloud cycles: Systematic review and the role of hybrid technology
summary: ABSTRACT Atmospheric microplastics (AMPs), defined here as plastic particles ranging from 1 μm to 5 mm, can remain airborne, undergo long-range transport, and reach remote environments. This review synthesises evidence on AMP occurrence, at
content: ABSTRACT Atmospheric microplastics (AMPs), defined here as plastic particles ranging from 1 μm to 5 mm, can remain airborne, undergo long-range transport, and reach remote environments. This review synthesises evidence on AMP occurrence, atmospheric cycling, cloud interactions, and emerging technological approaches for their management. A PRISMA-guided systematic search of Scopus and Google Scholar identified 62 studies published between 2015 and 2025, supplemented by 25 publications addressing emerging monitoring, capture, and remediation technologies. Fibres were the dominant morphology, while particles <100 μm represented the most frequently reported size category. Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) was the most frequently reported individual polymer, although mixed polymer assemblages were more common overall. Urban activities emerged as major emission sources, while atmospheric circulation, including monsoon systems and dust events, facilitates long-range transport. Atmospheric aging may enhance interactions with cloud droplets and ice, potentially enabling AMPs to act as cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) or ice nucleating particles (INP). However, direct field evidence of their atmospheric significance remains limited. Wet deposition represents a major removal pathway, while resuspension from terrestrial and marine surfaces may sustain continued atmosphere to surface cycling. Emerging hybrid sensing platforms and functional materials offer potential for AMPs monitoring, capture, and remediation, but their performance under realistic atmospheric conditions remains largely unvalidated. Effective AMPs management therefore requires both emission reduction at source and development of atmosphere specific technologies capable of monitoring and mitigating their atmospheric persistence.

title: Decoupled transport pathways and source materials of black carbon in the Pearl River Estuary and the North Yellow Sea
summary: Black carbon (BC) buried in marginal sea sediments represents a significant global carbon sink, yet the relative contributions of different transport pathways and source materials under varying climatic and emission regimes remain poorly co
content: Black carbon (BC) buried in marginal sea sediments represents a significant global carbon sink, yet the relative contributions of different transport pathways and source materials under varying climatic and emission regimes remain poorly constrained. In this study, we analyzed BC content, BC/TOC ratio, stable carbon isotopes (δ 13 C BC ), and sediment grain size in surface sediments from two contrasting Chinese marginal seas: the subtropical Pearl River Estuary (PRE) and the temperate North Yellow Sea (NYS). Using a Bayesian mixing model (MixSIAR), we apportioned BC sources along two dimensions: geographic transport pathway and specific source material. BC concentration ranges overlapped widely, yet PRE had a higher mean than NYS, with distinct controls. In the energetic PRE, grain size sorting drove a clear east-west zonation. In the muddy NYS, this sorting was regionally masked by atmospheric deposition of coal combustion BC at nearshore stations. Pathway apportionment revealed two distinct receiving modes: the open PRE was dominated by marine-proximal 13 C-enriched pathway (52.8%) against a uniform atmospheric background (27.2%), whereas the NYS acted as a steady-state sink dominated by terrestrial inputs (riverine: 34.5%; atmospheric: 38.4%). In contrast, source-material apportionment was highly consistent across both regions, following the order: fossil fuel combustion (∼45%) > biomass burning (∼35%) > rock weathering (∼20%). This decoupling, regionally divergent pathways but nationally convergent source materials, arises because BC transport is governed by local physical environments, while its composition reflects larger-scale emission patterns. Our findings clarify BC source–sink processes in Chinese marginal seas and provide scientific support for coordinated atmosphere–river–ocean pollution control.

title: VOLUMETRIC ESTIMATION OF CO2 STORAGE POTENTIAL IN ÁGUA GRANDE FIELD, RECÔNCAVO BASIN
source: Brazilian Journal of Petroleum and Gas
summary: Earth's climate has been increasingly affected by anthropogenic activities, primarily fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, which release greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (CO2). Geological carbon storage (CCS) stands out as a cri
content: Earth's climate has been increasingly affected by anthropogenic activities, primarily fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, which release greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide (CO2). Geological carbon storage (CCS) stands out as a critical mitigation strategy to curtail these emissions, though effective subsurface containment requires a clear understanding of trapping mechanisms. This study investigates the carbon storage potential of a depleted reservoir using real field data from Brazil. Applying the volumetric approximation method, which integrates geological and petrophysical parameters, we estimated the storage capacity of the Água Grande Field in the Recôncavo Basin. The results indicate a total storage potential of 65 MtCO_2 for the analyzed reservoir. Although of moderate magnitude, this capacity is highly suitable for a medium commercial-scale demonstration project, supporting injection rates between 1 and 5 million tons per year (Mtpa).

title: Heather management modifies climate sensitivity of surface peat moisture in UK upland peatlands
summary: Abstract. UK upland peatlands are important carbon stores, often dominated by heather, and are increasingly threatened by climate change, which promotes peat drying and wildfire risk. While water table depth (WTD) is often monitored to asse
content: Abstract. UK upland peatlands are important carbon stores, often dominated by heather, and are increasingly threatened by climate change, which promotes peat drying and wildfire risk. While water table depth (WTD) is often monitored to assess peatland hydrology, many key ecohydrological processes depend on surface peat moisture (SPM), which directly regulates surface carbon cycling, vegetation dynamics and peat fire risk, yet SPM remains poorly understood. We analysed seasonal SPM measurements under unmanaged, mown and burnt heather over 12 consecutive years post management from three replicated deep peat sites, together with measurements over five weeks of wet to dry conditions at a shallow peat site spanning three years post management. Across the deep peat sites, climate primarily controlled SPM, while heather management buffered moisture losses, particularly during warm and dry conditions. This buffering effect was strongest soon after management and weakened during vegetation recovery as heather height increased. After excluding low-rainfall events, SPM was strongly related to WTD, and the relationship remained relatively stable when the water table was within ~35 cm of the peat surface. At the shallow peat site, management substantially increased SPM during the first year after treatment relative to old heather, while mowing maintained higher SPM three years post-management, particularly under very dry conditions. Overall, heather management increased SPM across both peatland types, creating wetter near-surface conditions and reducing the sensitivity of surface-moisture to climatic drying. While mowing generally produced more consistent increases in SPM than burning, retained brash may increase wildfire risk under future climate change. The relative benefits of management types are likely to depend on site-specific conditions and time since management.

title: Selective radical pathways on defect-engineered electrophilic biochar for sustainable water purification
summary: Traditional advanced oxidation processes are frequently hindered by limited efficiency in complex wastewater, primarily due to the short lifetime and nonselective nature of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). While peracetic acid activation involves c
content: Traditional advanced oxidation processes are frequently hindered by limited efficiency in complex wastewater, primarily due to the short lifetime and nonselective nature of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). While peracetic acid activation involves competing nucleophilic and electrophilic pathways, selectively channeling this process toward the acetylperoxyl radical (CH3C(O)OO•)-mediated electrophilic route remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a universal nitrogen-removal strategy to engineer 5-14-5 vacancy-pentagon defects in nitrogen-containing agro-forestry biomass-derived biochar. These vacancy-based topological defects reconfigure the electronic landscape by downshifting the Fermi level and upshifting the p-band center. This electronic modulation transforms the carbon framework from a traditional electron donor into a potent electrophilic sink with a superior electron accepting capacity (EAC = 3.77 mmol·e−·g−1). This reconfiguration renders the electrophilic pathway thermodynamically favorable (ΔG = − 0.09 eV), achieving near-total selectivity (> 99%) for CH3C(O)OO• over •OH. More importantly, this system delivers a high normalized kinetic constant (409.82 min−1 M−1) and sustains high-flux radical production over 260 hours of continuous operation. Furthermore, life-cycle assessment validates its environmental sustainability, highlighting a net-negative carbon footprint. This study provides fundamental insights into defect-mediated radical chemistry and offers a scalable, sustainable paradigm for precision water decontamination. This study develops a defect-engineered biochar from nitrogenous agricultural waste that selectively activates peracetic acid into reactive acetylperoxyl radicals, offering an efficient and sustainable strategy for precision wastewater purification.

title: Timing Determines Fate: Temporal Dynamics of Jasmonate Signaling Distinguish Adaptive from Maladaptive Salt Stress Responses in Rice
summary: Abstract Plant encounters with saline conditions trigger a phase of osmotic stress, followed by ionic stress as salt accumulates in plant tissue. Jasmonate (JA) signalling plays a vital role in both phases, but its role for adaptation depen
content: Abstract Plant encounters with saline conditions trigger a phase of osmotic stress, followed by ionic stress as salt accumulates in plant tissue. Jasmonate (JA) signalling plays a vital role in both phases, but its role for adaptation depends on timing. Using wild-type rice ( Oryza sativa L. cv. Kitaake) and a JA-deficient allene oxide cyclase ( aoc ) mutant, we followed whole-plant physiology (growth, biomass, photosynthesis, ion distribution) with expression analysis for genes of jasmonate signalling, ion transporters and redox balance to separate adaptive from maladaptive JA effects. The aoc mutant sustained shoot and root growth more effectively than the wild type, maintaining cell expansion in the shoot and cell proliferation in the root under saline conditions. Likewise, stomatal conductance in the mutant was more persistent under salinity, accompanied by improved shoot K /Na homeostasis and reduced sodium in young leaves. In the wild-type, prolonged saline conditions were linked with induction of OsJAZ13 and OsNHX1 , stomatal closure and chlorophyll degradation. We discuss these findings in the context of a model, where the function of JA signalling does not merely depend on its accumulation, but on its temporal dynamics. Here, OsHAK16 emerges as a marker of early adaptive responses, whereas OsNHX1 and OsJAZ13 characterize later maladaptive stress states, emphasising the potential of modulating JA dynamics to improve salt resilience in rice breeding. Highlight Time-resolved physiology and transcript profiling show that jasmonate signalling promotes salt tolerance in rice when transient but drives ionic damage when sustained.

title: Influences of Seasonal Vegetation Dynamics and Morphological Change on Water Age and Connectivity in River Deltas
summary: River deltas are dynamic ecosystems in which seasonal vegetation dynamics mediate flow and sediment transport timescales and channel-network evolution, yet most delta models either omit vegetation or hold it static. We couple the Delft3D Fl
content: River deltas are dynamic ecosystems in which seasonal vegetation dynamics mediate flow and sediment transport timescales and channel-network evolution, yet most delta models either omit vegetation or hold it static. We couple the Delft3D Flexible Mesh (DFM) hydro-morphodynamic solver with the NBSDynamics vegetation module via the Basic Model Interface (BMI), using four representative freshwater vegetation types and three coupling scenarios to estimate the influence of seasonal vegetation dynamics and morphological development on water age and connectivity in an idealized river delta. We find that the vegetated deltas elongate, whereas unvegetated systems expand laterally. Channel water-age distributions are predominantly unimodal and tightly coupled to sedimentation, while island interiors exhibit multimodal distributions and a weaker water age–deposition coupling. System connectivity is largely discharge-driven in unvegetated deltas; however, in vegetated systems, connectivity control becomes state-dependent, shifting between hydrodynamic forcing during low biomass and vegetation dominance during peak canopy growth. Within this dynamic, seasonal vegetation emerges as a transitional regime between the static and no-vegetation endmembers across three network connectivity metrics. A Water-Age-Weighted Sedimentation Index (WAWSI) consolidates these signals into a seasonal fingerprint of vegetation-mediated connectivity, in which long-age and high-deposition zones form laterally in island interiors near the delta front. The results imply that the effectiveness of sediment diversions and marsh creation for sea-level-rise adaptation and land-loss mitigation depends on the phenological state of the vegetation species present and on antecedent morphological reworking, providing a process-based foundation for nature-based restoration in dynamic deltaic environments.

title: Size-resolved particle dry deposition velocities in a controlled spherical chamber: Effects of turbulence, surface complexity, and particle physicochemical properties
summary: Accurate quantification of size-resolved particle dry deposition velocities ( v d ) is essential for improving predictions of aerosol atmospheric lifetimes, surface contamination, and pollutant transport. Existing field measurement approach
content: Accurate quantification of size-resolved particle dry deposition velocities ( v d ) is essential for improving predictions of aerosol atmospheric lifetimes, surface contamination, and pollutant transport. Existing field measurement approaches such as eddy covariance and direct surface collection face fundamental limitations in resolving v d across the submicron size range. Here we report controlled laboratory experiments conducted in a spherical aluminum chamber (diameter 91.44 cm, volume ∼0.4 m 3 ) to systematically investigate how turbulence intensity, additional surface complexity, and particle physicochemical properties govern size-resolved v d . Deposition velocities were determined independently using two complementary methods: a chamber concentration decay method and a direct filter collection and re-atomization method. Experiments were conducted with three particle types chosen to span a range of morphological and hygroscopic properties: sodium chloride (NaCl), polystyrene latex (PSL) spheres, and black carbon (BC) aggregates. Conditions inside the sphere were maintained at low relative humidity (RH < 30%) and a fan was run at varying speeds from 0 to 1500 revolutions per minute (RPM). Key findings include: (1) turbulence exerts a strong, size-dependent influence on v d , with the viscous sublayer thickness governing the crossover between diffusion- and turbulence-controlled regimes; (2) flow-permeable objects (simulated vegetation) enhance normalized v d by a factor of 10-15 for particles smaller than 50 nm relative to the empty-chamber baseline, substantially exceeding predictions based on surface area addition alone; (3) particle morphology accounts for up to an order-of-magnitude spread in v d at a given mobility diameter, with BC fractal aggregates exhibiting morphology-driven deviations from spherical particle behavior. The filter and decay methods agree within a factor of 2 across the PSL size range tested, validating the filter collection approach as a quantitative tool. These results provide direct experimental constraints on dry deposition parameterizations used in regional and global aerosol models and motivate future deployment of analogous filter-based methods for in-situ determination of ambient particle deposition velocities.

title: Simulation of multispecies interactions and ecosystem functions based on functional–structural plant models: a review
source: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
summary: Under the dual pressures of sustained global population growth and climate change, food security and agricultural sustainability are facing unprecedented challenges. Agricultural ecosystems based on the principle of multispecies coexistence
content: Under the dual pressures of sustained global population growth and climate change, food security and agricultural sustainability are facing unprecedented challenges. Agricultural ecosystems based on the principle of multispecies coexistence have emerged as a key strategy for addressing these challenges, owing to their advantages in resource use efficiency and ecological sustainability. Functional-structural plant models (FSPMs) explicitly simulate plant growth and development through three-dimensional architectures and tightly couple these processes with the dynamic acquisition and allocation of environmental resources, such as light, water, and nutrients, thereby providing a powerful framework for elucidating the underlying mechanisms of interspecific interactions at the individual scale. This review systematically synthesizes recent advances in the application of FSPMs to multispecies systems, including aboveground light competition and canopy structural optimization, the adaptive significance of plant phenotypic plasticity in interspecific interactions, and belowground root interactions and resource acquisition strategies. It further identifies current limitations of FSPM-based studies, particularly in representing multispecies synergistic interactions and in the parameterization of belowground processes, and highlights future research directions toward the development of cross-scale, long-term, and multi-trophic integrated FSPMs. These insights provide a theoretical basis and strategic guidance for optimizing farmland management and advancing model-driven precision agriculture. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Multi-scale modelling of polymeric deposition for sustainable additive manufacturing: towards customised implant fabrication
source: AMS Dottorato Institutional Doctoral Theses Repository (University of Bologna)
summary: Droplet-based polymer additive manufacturing is increasingly considered viable for customised low-volume production, including patient-specific medical components. Industrial adoption is constrained by process variability and reliance on tr
content: Droplet-based polymer additive manufacturing is increasingly considered viable for customised low-volume production, including patient-specific medical components. Industrial adoption is constrained by process variability and reliance on trial-and-error tuning, which increases waste, energy use and lead time while undermining repeatability. This thesis addresses these challenges for Arburg Plastic Freeforming, a material-jetting process combining injection-moulding plasticisation with discrete droplet deposition of thermoplastic granules. The work develops modelling-informed tools and evidence-based insights to improve reliability across scales and support feed-forward understanding. A progressive model–material strategy is adopted, using amorphous and semi-crystalline thermoplastics. At the macro-scale, crystallisation-driven distortion in semi-crystalline polymers is examined. A modified polyamide 6 formulation shift the crystallisation peak from 184.6 °C to 161.2 °C and reduces warpage from 5.72 mm to 0.06 mm (–98.9%). Mechanical characterisation reveals marked anisotropy and conditioning sensitivity: moisture conditioning lowers elastic modulus by up to 70 – 76% and changes ductility with raster orientation. At the meso-scale, an analytical framework derived from mass conservation and deposition kinematics links droplet geometry to part density as a practical quality proxy. The model is verified via mass-balance closure and evaluated against Archimedes-based density measurements, with parity analysis and error metrics showing mean absolute errors of approximately ~0.01 g/cm3. The analysis explicitly accounts for machine-induced shutter-frequency drift at high deposition speeds. At the micro-scale, a computational fluid dynamics analysis resolves droplet spreading, coalescence, and interfacial evolution in polycarbonate. Extrusion temperature governs morphology and wetting, with droplet volume increasing from ~0.0123 mm3 to ~0.0159 mm3 between 285 °C and 305 °C. A William-Landel-Ferry equivalent-time metric shows that bulk-like bonding strength is reached within ~10-5 – 10-4 s, with the most balanced response at intermediate temperature conditions. Overall, the thesis provides a physically interpretable basis for improving process reliability through distortion-aware material strategies, feed-forward density screening and mechanistic interpretation of bonding.

title: Carbon cycle uncertainties and the role of land-use change emissions in ambitious mitigation pathways
summary: The carbon cycle and its sensitivity to different forcings is a major source of uncertainty in scenario assessments of Earth System Models (ESMs) on climate change. However, while the relevant carbon cycle uncertainties are often an importa
content: The carbon cycle and its sensitivity to different forcings is a major source of uncertainty in scenario assessments of Earth System Models (ESMs) on climate change. However, while the relevant carbon cycle uncertainties are often an important part of ESM assessments, they are currently poorly and inconsistently accounted for in the derivation of mitigation pathways using Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs). Here, we incorporate carbon cycle data from 9 different Dynamic Global Vegetation Models (DGVMs) into the REMIND-MAgPIE-MAGICC IAM framework, using the DGVM model diversity as the main source of uncertainty, and assess variations in scenario outcomes derived from them. We show that varying only assumptions about the carbon density potentials of vegetation types leads to important variations in the cost-effective deployment of land-based mitigation solutions. In scenarios where warming is limited to 1.7°C, cumulative landuse change emissions (2020-2050) vary from negative to substantially positive (-12 to 57 GtCO2), with a 30% variation in carbon prices, 100 Mha in forest area and a substantially different CDR mix. By calibrating the simple climate model MAGICC to reproduce the land carbon and nitrogen fluxes from these same DGVMs, we also consistently assess the uncertainty in the remaining carbon budget to limit warming to 1.7°C due to the varied responses of the carbon sink to environmental changes. We find that, although this budget effect in terms of cumulative emissions (a spread of 280 GtCO2) is much larger than the density effect, the two effects are not significantly correlated. The budget effect can therefore still be assessed with the climate emulator alone, as is current practice, whereas the density effect requires varying carbon densities in the IAM and adds to the budget effect. The results point to the need for a more consistent and systematic approach to the parametrization of carbon densities in IAM assessments.

title: Synthesis of the tethered balloon system and other TRACER campaign measurements elucidates aerosol property profiles
summary: Abstract. Coastal urban environments exhibit strong vertical and horizontal heterogeneity in aerosol properties, complicating process-level understanding of aerosol–cloud interactions. This study analyzes tethered balloon system (TBS) measu
content: Abstract. Coastal urban environments exhibit strong vertical and horizontal heterogeneity in aerosol properties, complicating process-level understanding of aerosol–cloud interactions. This study analyzes tethered balloon system (TBS) measurements from 149 flights during summer over the greater Houston, Texas, region as part of the DOE Atmospheric Radiation Measurement (ARM) Tracking Aerosol Convection interactions ExpeRiment (TRACER) campaign. We characterize the vertical structure of aerosol number concentrations, size distributions, and inferred cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) concentrations. Air mass history was classified using back-trajectory analysis and k-means clustering into three clusters: (1) marine-influenced, (2) mixed marine and urban emissions, and (3) urban/anthropogenic and long-range transported aerosols. CCN concentrations are estimated from observed size distributions using κ-Köhler theory. The resulting profiles show pronounced vertical variability across clusters, strongly modulated by boundary-layer depth and coastal circulations, leading to substantial variability in the aerosol population available for cloud activation. The marine cluster showed the lowest concentrations, with CCN at 0.8 % supersaturation below 1,000 cm⁻³, while urban and mixed clusters displayed higher concentrations and more complex layering. Profiles influenced by the mixed marine–urban cluster frequently exhibit decoupling between near-surface aerosol and elevated layers, including enhanced accumulation-mode number aloft, consistent with prior TBS-based compositional studies. A September 6–7, 2022 case study demonstrates that mesoscale transport can simultaneously transform both the thermodynamic environment and aerosol population, highlighting the importance of constraining boundary-layer dynamics and airmass origin before attributing cloud changes to aerosol effects in complex coastal environments.

title: An acetophenone carboxylase homolog from Rhodococcus aetherivorans initiates acetone rather than acetophenone catabolism
summary: Ketones such as acetone and acetophenone are chemically inert and must be activated prior to microbial degradation. In aerobic bacteria such as Rhodococcus , ketone activation is accomplished either by oxygenation or carboxylation reactions
content: Ketones such as acetone and acetophenone are chemically inert and must be activated prior to microbial degradation. In aerobic bacteria such as Rhodococcus , ketone activation is accomplished either by oxygenation or carboxylation reactions. Acetone and acetophenone carboxylases are homologous enzymes, but have different subunit compositions. While acetone carboxylases form heterohexameric complexes out of three distinct subunits, the acetophenone carboxylase core complex contains an additional duplicate of one of these subunits, resulting in a heterooctamer of four different subunits. Moreover, acetophenone carboxylase comprises a detachable fifth subunit ε, which is not present in acetone carboxylases. Here, we show that an apparent acetophenone carboxylase from Rhodococcus aetherivorans initiates acetone rather than acetophenone catabolism. The same strain of R. aetherivorans also degrades acetophenone, but as revealed by proteomics and enzyme activity measurements, this substrate is activated by an oxygenation reaction. In contrast to the canonical enzyme variant, which is restricted to acetone and butanone, the acetone carboxylase from R. aetherivorans apparently also accepts more aliphatic ketones with longer chain length. Furthermore, gene deletion studies confirmed the indispensability of the unique subunit ε for enzyme activity. In conclusion, we identified a novel type of acetone carboxylase with acetophenone carboxylase-like subunit composition and extended substrate spectrum. Phylogenetic analyses suggest that heterodecameric acetone carboxylases are particularly widespread across Actinomycetota and Pseudomonadota.

title: Codon-aware multi-scale feature fusion for metagenomic sequence classification
summary: Microorganisms exert profound influences on both natural ecosystems and human society. As the cornerstone of microbial research, metagenomics relies on the precise analysis of large-scale, multi-source genomic data. However, discriminating
content: Microorganisms exert profound influences on both natural ecosystems and human society. As the cornerstone of microbial research, metagenomics relies on the precise analysis of large-scale, multi-source genomic data. However, discriminating among diverse sequence types remains a formidable challenge. To address this, we present CamFi (Codon-aware Multi-scale Feature Fusion), a unified framework integrating overlapping nucleotide-triplet representations with multi-scale dilated convolutions for classifying prokaryotic chromosomes, eukaryotic chromosomes, plasmids, and viruses. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong mean F1 scores of 97.70% for eukaryotic chromosomes and 94.13% for plasmids. On the CAMI II marine dataset, CamFi achieved a weighted F1 of 82.65%, ranking second among six methods based on reported aggregate metrics. In a balanced four-class benchmark, CamFi attained a macro-F1 of 93.77%, compared with DeepMicroClass (90.03%) and the XGBoost stage of 4CAC (64.66%). These results establish CamFi as a competitive approach for unified metagenomic contig classification under the evaluated conditions.

title: Decoupled recovery of soil physicochemistry, microbiome and methane sink function during secondary forest succession in the Eastern Himalayas
summary: Abstract Secondary forests are increasingly important for biodiversity recovery and ecosystem functioning after disturbance. As vegetation regenerates, accompanying shifts in soil conditions and microbial communities regulate climate-releva
content: Abstract Secondary forests are increasingly important for biodiversity recovery and ecosystem functioning after disturbance. As vegetation regenerates, accompanying shifts in soil conditions and microbial communities regulate climate-relevant processes such as atmospheric methane (CH 4 ) uptake. Whether these belowground dimensions recover synchronously, however, remains unclear. Here we show that belowground recovery followed asynchronous trajectories across a forest chronosequence in Metok, Eastern Himalayas. Soil inorganic properties and microbial community composition converged progressively on the primary-forest state as soils acidified. By contrast, soil organic carbon, microbial diversity and abundance appeared to recover by 25 years but diverged again at 40 years. Co-occurrence network topology resembled the primary forest by 40 years, yet the keystone taxa underlying it were entirely stage specific. Atmospheric CH 4 uptake fluctuated: uptake recovered to primary-forest levels in 25-year stands but weakened in 40-year stands to rates comparable with the recently disturbed 5-year forest. Rather than canonical methane-cycling taxa, four amplicon sequence variants—three assigned to Mycobacterium —tracked CH 4 flux closely while acting as hubs or connectors in the co-occurrence networks, warranting genomic and experimental work to resolve their function. Apparent recovery within the first 25 years therefore did not persist, cautioning against inferring restoration success from early succession alone and highlighting the need for longer chronosequences and repeated observation to resolve the dynamics of secondary-forest recovery.

title: Paramanu Reclaimer: Plasma-Assisted Recovery and Mining of Atoms, Neutralizing Urban-Waste
source: International Journal Of Scientific Research In Engineering & Technology
summary: Every recycling system today follows one rule: sort first. The fine, mixed residue that sorting cannot handle, most of an old landfill, is capped, burned or buried again. The PARAMANU Reclaimer (Plasma-Assisted Recovery And Mining of Atoms,
content: Every recycling system today follows one rule: sort first. The fine, mixed residue that sorting cannot handle, most of an old landfill, is capped, burned or buried again. The PARAMANU Reclaimer (Plasma-Assisted Recovery And Mining of Atoms, Neutralizing Urban-waste) starts where sorting ends: a sealed, stack-free plasma reactor turns the residue fully into gas, and condensers at falling temperatures separate its elements band by band. We call this architecture Atomize-First. We derive eight design principles from established thermodynamics, with proofs, and test the design with an open simulation on NASA data, a 5,000-feed sweep and repeated rechecks of the computation. The results support it, placing valuable and toxic volatile metals in different bands, and correct it: the hot zone must last only tens of milliseconds, and mercury needs its own trap. Fume, fine particles that can carry metals past their condenser, is the largest open threat. Predictions registered before any experiment will judge a working plant. All code and data are public.

title: Evaluation of HNO 3 , SO 2 , and NH 3 in the Surface Tiled Aerosol and Gaseous Exchange (STAGE) option in the Community Multiscale Air Quality Model version 5.3.2 against field-scale, in situ and satellite observations
summary: Abstract. The Surface Tiled Aerosol and Gaseous Exchange (STAGE) model was developed for estimating dry deposition and bidirectional exchange for field-scale applications and use within the CMAQ v5.3.2 regional scale model. The model was ev
content: Abstract. The Surface Tiled Aerosol and Gaseous Exchange (STAGE) model was developed for estimating dry deposition and bidirectional exchange for field-scale applications and use within the CMAQ v5.3.2 regional scale model. The model was evaluated against micrometeorological flux measurements of NH3, HNO3, and SO2 at a managed grassland and NH3 in a cultivated corn (Zea Mays) field. When using field-scale observations for soil and vegetation NH3 compensation points, modelled fluxes for all species agreed well, within or near the reported measurement uncertainty. However, when using the CMAQ v5.3.2 values for NH3 emission potentials at the Duke Forest grassland site, the model estimated mean net deposition rate was 1.3 ng m-2 h-1 while the observed mean NH3 evasive flux was 8.4 ng m-2 h-1. Modelled NH3 concentration fields evaluated against Cross-Track Infrared Sounder (CrIS) satellite observations indicates a broad underestimation of NH3 concentrations by approximately 1 to 2 ppb in the U.S. Great Plains. The results from the grassland field data and indicates that there is likely an underestimation of the evasive NH3 flux in grassland sites due to the model's default tabular values of the vegetation/litter NH4+ concentrations. The STAGE's model sensitivity to soil and vegetation emission potentials indicates that regional scale model results for NH3 can be further improved with additional micrometeorological flux and vegetation and soil chemistry measurements over different land use types, soil types, and vegetation phenological stages.

title: TARSA v1.0: a lightweight Eulerian forward model for aerosol transport – description, verification, and observation-based evaluation
summary: Abstract. Atmospheric retrieval, inverse-modelling, and data-assimilation workflows require transparent transport models that can be evaluated repeatedly and provide consistent sensitivities. We present TARSA v1.0, a lightweight regional th
content: Abstract. Atmospheric retrieval, inverse-modelling, and data-assimilation workflows require transparent transport models that can be evaluated repeatedly and provide consistent sensitivities. We present TARSA v1.0, a lightweight regional three-dimensional Eulerian model for inert tracers and simplified aerosol applications under prescribed ERA5 meteorology. TARSA advances tracer mass mixing ratios with a conservative finite-volume core comprising monotonic advection, vertical turbulent diffusion, sedimentation, and parameterised dry and wet deposition. The default advection scheme uses a TVD-admissible, cubic-Hermite-regularised Koren limiter to reduce selected gradient-error roughness. Analytic, tangent-linear, discrete-adjoint, and automatic-differentiation gradients agree to single precision in a scalar emission-amplitude check. Numerical verification includes mass-conservation, analytical plume, and manufactured-solution tests. Independent evaluation against european and north-american regional experiments (ETEX-1, CAPTEX-1) shows agreement in plume timing and concentration amplitude, with performance broadly comparable to published transport-model results. A Saharan dust-column case during Fennec, driven by prescribed MERRA-2 emissions without externally prescribed dust initial or lateral boundary concentrations, shows moderate agreement with GRASP/POLDER coarse-dust column estimates. TARSA provides a reproducible forward operator for regional transport and observation-space studies, supporting future air-quality applications using satellite aerosol observations. Its prescribed process set and local sensitivity structure support future retrieval and inversion applications, while end-to-end inverse-modelling performance remains to be demonstrated.

title: Discovering new potential in a native fruit byproduct: An unprecedented evaluation of the composition and properties of cambucá seed (Plinia edulis (Vell.) Sobral)
summary: Cambucá seed is an unexploited native byproduct. To support complete fruit utilization, the nutritional, physicochemical, and technological properties and bioactive potential of cambucá seed were investigated. High carbohydrate content was
content: Cambucá seed is an unexploited native byproduct. To support complete fruit utilization, the nutritional, physicochemical, and technological properties and bioactive potential of cambucá seed were investigated. High carbohydrate content was found (56.28%), with starch predominating within this fraction (27.64%), while dietary fiber accounted for 36.68%, all on a dry basis. The seed showed high potassium content (4.88 mg.g −1 fresh seed), with potentially toxic metals below regulatory limits. Twenty-three volatile compounds and eight organic acids indicated sensory complexity, complemented by four anthocyanins responsible for purple coloration. The phenolic profile showed predominance of insoluble-bound compounds, with gallic acid as the major compound (3373.08 μg.g −1 fresh seed). These bioactive compounds contributed to high antioxidant capacity, especially in the ORAC assay (2643.74 μmo lTE.g −1 fresh seed). The seed composition resulted in high thermal stability and a specific paste-forming profile. Overall, cambucá seed is a sustainable coproduct with potential for developing high-value innovative products.

title: Variation in biomass and carbon storage in broadleaved and coniferous forests along altitudinal gradation and forest type
summary: Forest ecosystems play a crucial role as regulators of the global carbon cycle. Quantifying forest biomass and carbon storage is essential to evaluate their productivity and their potential to sequester carbon.. The study aimed to synthesiz
content: Forest ecosystems play a crucial role as regulators of the global carbon cycle. Quantifying forest biomass and carbon storage is essential to evaluate their productivity and their potential to sequester carbon.. The study aimed to synthesize and compare biomass and carbon stock across different forest types in the Northwestern Himalayas (NWH), covering Indian states of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Jammu & Kashmir, at varying altitudes. For the said exercise we conducted rapid literature review adopting ROSES protocol. We addressed the inconsistency in reported data of different forest types by harmonizing them to ensure comparability like standardizing/scaling them to a common unit (Mg ha 1 ) or normalizing them using standard conversion factor. Thereafter, we compared the forests based on their types, regions and altitudes in terms of their mean values and variability (standard deviation/standard error). Coniferous and broadleaf forests were two major forests in the region abundantly represented by retrieved data while, studies on mixed coniferous broadleaf forests were limited. We therefore, restricted our assessment to two dominant and well-documented forests. Oak-based broadleaved forests of Himachal Pradesh were quantified with highest biomass stock of 439.49–466.48 Mg ha -1 while, Chirpine the lowest showing statistical differences. Similarly, highest and lowest biomass carbon stock of 174.06 Mg ha -1 and 44.79 Mg ha -1 , was for Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir, respectively. On an average, 43.63 % more biomass carbon was stocked by Coniferous forests than other forest types while, among the states, Uttrakhand stocked 73.09 % more biomass carbon. Additionally, across the altitude, conifers on an average also stocked 44.60% more carbon than broadleaves, peaking at mid-elevations (1000–3000 m asl). Higher carbon stocks reported in these forests indicate their potential role as important carbon reservoirs. The present study compiles available information on forest biomass and carbon stocks across the North-Western Himalayan (NWH) region and provides a baseline dataset that may support forest managers and policymakers in developing altitude-, region-, and forest type-specific conservation and sustainable forest management approaches. Variations in carbon stocks observed among different forest types and locations highlight areas where further investigation may be useful. The study also identifies the need for additional long-term studies to monitor changes in forest carbon stocks and dynamics under changing climatic conditions. Such information could contribute to a better understanding of carbon dynamics in the NWH region and support future assessments of forest responses to climate change.

Tide-dominated deltas possess the highest sediment trapping efficiency, retaining ~70% of the fluvially-derived sediment 3. title: Global Ocean Urea Dynamics and Role in Nitrogen Cycling
summary: Urea is a widespread nitrogen and energy source for marine plankton. Many reports describe local urea distribution and utilization rates, but global-scale dynamics remain poorly constrained. Based on an extensive synthesis covering polar to
content: Urea is a widespread nitrogen and energy source for marine plankton. Many reports describe local urea distribution and utilization rates, but global-scale dynamics remain poorly constrained. Based on an extensive synthesis covering polar to tropical and from the surface to the deep ocean, we find that global urea distribution, to a first order, followed regenerated nitrogen. However, a high urea-to-ammonium ratio was observed in the oligotrophic surface and in the mesopelagic zone, whereas a low ratio was seen in polar regions. Urea uptake was highest in productive and lowest in polar regions. We observed a hierarchy of substrate preference with urea being quantitatively less desirable than ammonium but more desirable than nitrate. Despite being less desirable than ammonia, urea was the dominant N source in oligotrophic regions. We predict that urea is a key nitrogen source sustaining primary production in the oligotrophic ocean, but major gaps remain in our understanding of global ocean urea sources and sinks.

title: Moisture Constraints on Realized CO 2 -Associated Productivity Gains in Xinjiang Drylands
summary: Abstract. Rising atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) can enhance terrestrial productivity, but how CO₂-associated productivity responses are expressed across water-limited ecosystems remains uncertain. Here, we developed a model-based dual-pat
content: Abstract. Rising atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) can enhance terrestrial productivity, but how CO₂-associated productivity responses are expressed across water-limited ecosystems remains uncertain. Here, we developed a model-based dual-pathway framework comprising an explicit CO₂-associated productivity component and a water-use-efficiency (WUE)-related carbon–water response. Using paired standard CASA and CO₂-CASA simulations, seven-scenario attribution experiments, and complementary carbon–water diagnostics, we evaluated net primary productivity (NPP) changes across Xinjiang, China, during 2001–2020. Baseline CASA reproduced the major spatial and interannual variability of MOD17 NPP. Mean annual NPP in 2018–2020 exceeded that in 2001–2003 by 10.24 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹. Under the isolated-component framework, vegetation-state change contributed 9.41 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ (91.9 % of the total modeled change), whereas the analytically isolated explicit CO₂ component contributed 1.11 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ (10.8 %) and climate contributed −0.53 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ (−5.2 %). Long-term CO₂–WUE coupling was strongest under intermediate moisture conditions, with class-level associations strongest within 100–400 mm and a nonlinear fitted maximum near 200–300 mm. However, first-difference analysis showed little interannual CO₂–WUE association, while April–October precipitation was more closely associated with interannual NPP variability than annual precipitation. Positive productivity trends also persisted after excluding areas potentially influenced by persistent agriculture. Together, these results support a model-based dual-pathway interpretation of CO₂-associated productivity responses while identifying moisture context and temporal scale as key constraints on their expression and interpretation.

title: Decadal biogeochemical predictions for the changing bottom marine environment of the Gulf of Maine
summary: Abstract. The Gulf of Maine and the surrounding Northeast U.S. Continental Shelf are experiencing rapid marine environmental change arising from complex regional dynamics that challenge near-term (1–10 years) predictive capabilities for val
content: Abstract. The Gulf of Maine and the surrounding Northeast U.S. Continental Shelf are experiencing rapid marine environmental change arising from complex regional dynamics that challenge near-term (1–10 years) predictive capabilities for valuable living marine resources. Here, using a high-resolution regional ocean model, we demonstrate skilful decadal forecasts of ocean bottom habitat characteristics including bottom temperature, dissolved oxygen (O2), pH and aragonite saturation state (Ωar). Bottom temperature and pH predictions show substantial skill driven primarily by radiatively forced warming and carbon uptake trends, while bottom O2 and Ωar predictions benefit more from initialization due to stronger internal variability. Retrospective forecasts successfully predicted observed historical changes in water masses and environmental properties, including recent cooling/freshening transitions driven by replacement of Warm Slope Water with Labrador Slope Water. This water mass variability also modulates biogeochemical conditions and ocean acidification buffering capacity, with our recent forecasts indicating that benefits from the expected respite from rapid warming might be tempered by challenges posed by rapid acidification. The demonstrated predictability of coupled physical-biogeochemical processes supports developing integrated prediction systems for climate-informed marine resource management.

title: Efficient computation of global high-resolution Jacobian matrices for analytical inversions of satellite observations of greenhouse gases: Application to the Integrated Methane Inversion (IMI) version 2.3
summary: Abstract. Dense satellite observations of atmospheric composition call for global high-resolution inversions to infer surface fluxes from the observations, using a chemical transport model (CTM) as forward model to relate the fluxes to the
content: Abstract. Dense satellite observations of atmospheric composition call for global high-resolution inversions to infer surface fluxes from the observations, using a chemical transport model (CTM) as forward model to relate the fluxes to the observed concentrations. The inversion can be done analytically when the relationship of surface fluxes to the observable atmospheric concentrations is linear. The main cost of analytical inversions is the explicit construction of the Jacobian matrix describing the CTM sensitivity of atmospheric concentrations to the gridded surface fluxes (state vector elements) and requiring perturbation simulations for all individual state vector elements. This cost has so far limited global analytical inversions to coarse resolution (~200 km) despite the availability of fine-resolution (~10 km) satellite observations. Here we show how the stretched-grid capability of the high-performance GEOS-Chem CTM (GCHP) operating on a cubed-sphere grid can considerably reduce the computational and storage costs of global Jacobian construction by achieving high resolution in the near-field of the state vector elements (target face) while gradually relaxing to coarse resolution at the antipode. Application to a stretch factor of 10 on the C36 cubed-sphere GCHP grid (C36S10) enables generation of a compact global Jacobian archive at 25-km resolution with 100 times lower computational and storage costs than a regular-grid C360 GCHP with global quasi-uniform 25-km resolution. We have implemented this capability in the Integrated Methane Inversion (IMI) version 2.3.
