summary: Misinformation is widely recognised as a significant social risk, yet conceptual disagreement persists over how the problem should be defined, analysed and managed across disciplines. Within risk analysis, misinformation is typically approa
content: Misinformation is widely recognised as a significant social risk, yet conceptual disagreement persists over how the problem should be defined, analysed and managed across disciplines. Within risk analysis, misinformation is typically approached as a problem of encoding: a product of poor practice in risk assessment or risk communication, addressed through stronger scientific fundamentals and greater transparency. This article argues that such an approach, while necessary, is insufficient. Drawing on communication and systems theory, it advances an alternative account in which misinformation is significantly a decoding phenomenon, produced between senders and receivers and situated within cultural and media environments that risk analysts have limited power to influence. The argument is explored through the case of Australia's renewable energy transition, focusing on the contested offshore wind sector, where growing community opposition has become entangled with misinformation about environmental and social risks. The article identifies several features of the Australian public sphere, including concentrated media ownership, uneven institutional trust, the legacy of strict Covid-19 restrictions and historic ties between fossil fuel interests and media ownership that make it particularly susceptible to misinformation. The analysis suggests that even sound, evidence-based risk assessments can be relabelled as misinformation within such environments. The article concludes by considering the implications of this systemic, environmental view of misinformation for risk analysis practice, arguing for closer integration between risk science and communication science.

title: Sand Batteries for Thermal Energy Storage: A Review of Operating Principles, Technologies, Challenges and Future Perspectives
summary: Sand-based thermal energy storage (TES) has attracted increasing attention as a potential solution for storing renewable electricity and supplying heat over extended periods. This review examines operating principles, storage configurations
content: Sand-based thermal energy storage (TES) has attracted increasing attention as a potential solution for storing renewable electricity and supplying heat over extended periods. This review examines operating principles, storage configurations, materials, thermal performance, economic aspects, environmental considerations, safety, reliability, optimisation, and the potential integration of sand-based TES with renewable energy and wider energy systems. Particular attention is given to the relationships and trade-offs among these aspects and to current technological limitations. The reviewed studies indicate that sand-based TES can provide high-temperature heat storage using abundant, relatively low-cost storage media, while its performance depends strongly on system configuration, operating temperature, charging and discharging conditions, heat losses, and integration strategy. Reported economic and environmental results vary considerably according to electricity prices, utilisation, system lifetime, efficiency, system boundaries, and other methodological assumptions. Although sand-based TES shows potential for large-scale, long-duration thermal storage, comprehensive life-cycle assessments, long-term operational data, and system-level reliability and safety evaluations remain limited. Hybrid configurations, advanced optimisation, artificial intelligence, and integration with renewable energy systems represent promising areas for further investigation. Future research should therefore focus on long-term experimental validation, consistent techno-economic and environmental assessment, system-specific safety and reliability analysis, and the development of robust control and optimisation strategies to support practical deployment.

title: Janus-Structured Composites for Energy Harvesting, Thermal Management, and Superior Triboelectric Output Performance
summary: Abstract The intensifying global energy crisis and the steady advancement of the dual-carbon strategy have imposed increasingly stringent requirements on zero-energy temperature control technologies and renewable energy utilization systems
content: Abstract The intensifying global energy crisis and the steady advancement of the dual-carbon strategy have imposed increasingly stringent requirements on zero-energy temperature control technologies and renewable energy utilization systems across domains, such as building energy conservation, flexible electronics, and sensing. Herein, a multifunctional Janus-structured CA/PVDF/MXene (CPM) composite film was fabricated via electrospinning using a blended solution of cellulose acetate (CA) and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) as an electrospinning precursor. The composite achieves subambient cooling of approximately 7.0 °C outdoors, demonstrating excellent daytime radiative cooling performance. The CPM-based triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) exhibits outstanding electrical output, with an open-circuit voltage of 101.3 V, a short-circuit current of 3.9 μA, and a transferred charge of 34.9 nC. Moreover, the CPM-TENG shows excellent self-powered sensing capabilities, accurately detecting mechanical signals including human motion and handwriting traces, highlighting promising potential for applications in flexible wearable electronics. The composite possesses mechanical properties (200% enhancement in tensile strength), photothermal conversion capability (achieving a surface temperature of 64.6 °C under 0.8 W/cm2 irradiation), and Joule thermal response (reaching 156.4 °C at 6 V). This study provides a systematic design for multifunctional flexible electronic devices that integrate passive intelligent temperature regulation, mechanical energy harvesting, and high-sensitivity self-powered sensing.

title: Unlocking wind energy potential in data-scarce regions: a deep learning framework for strategic climate action in Vietnam’s Central Highlands
source: International Journal of Climate Change Strategies and Management
summary: Purpose As Vietnam accelerates its transition toward a sustainable energy future under ambitious national strategies like the Power Development Plan VIII (PDP8), a critical barrier persists: the lack of high-fidelity resource maps for strat
content: Purpose As Vietnam accelerates its transition toward a sustainable energy future under ambitious national strategies like the Power Development Plan VIII (PDP8), a critical barrier persists: the lack of high-fidelity resource maps for strategic planning. This is particularly acute in data-scarce regions with high potential, such as Vietnam’s Central Highlands. This study aims to address this strategic gap by developing and validating a robust deep learning framework to produce an enhanced and detailed high-resolution wind energy map for this region, providing a conservative proof-of-concept for regional energy planning. Design/methodology/approach The framework integrates coarse-resolution daily wind speed data from an ensemble of 11 global climate models with long-term observational records (1985–2023) from a sparse network of meteorological stations. To preserve synoptic extremes critical for wind power, the downscaling was conducted at a daily temporal resolution. A suite of advanced machine learning and deep learning models were systematically trained. To address the limitations of spatial interpolation in complex terrain, the downscaled 10 m wind speeds were extrapolated to a 149 m commercial hub-height using a terrain-aware power law, integrating high-resolution surface roughness data. A technical potential map (GWh/km²/year) was then generated by combining the turbine power curve (Enercon E-101) with a GIS-based availability index (AI), factoring in constraints such as elevation, slope, land cover and urban buffers. Findings Deep learning architectures, particularly the convolutional neural network and XGBoost, significantly outperformed traditional models, achieving R-Pearson correlation coefficients exceeding 0.85 on daily predictions. Validation against ERA5 reanalysis data demonstrated that our ML-downscaled outputs substantially reduced severe negative biases present in ERA5 over complex terrain. The framework generated one of the most detailed wind energy maps for the region, identifying specific “hotspots” capable of generating significant yields (>6.0 GWh/km²/year) while strictly masking physically constrained zones. Projections under future shared socioeconomic pathways indicate that this wind resource potential is expected to remain robust. Originality/value This study could provide a powerful, replicable methodological blueprint for de-risking renewable energy investment in data-scarce regions. By embedding high-resolution spatial covariates (DEM, roughness) into the vertical extrapolation rather than relying solely on 2D interpolation, it delivers an early, scientifically rigorous tool to guide national energy policy, optimize land-use planning and accelerate the sustainable expansion of wind energy for other regions in the country and abroad.

title: Assessment of Smallholder Farmers’ Knowledge, Adoption and Barriers to Agroecological Practices in the Western Highlands of Cameroon
source: Global research in environment and sustainability.
summary: Smallholder agriculture remains the backbone of rural livelihoods and food security in the Western Highlands of Cameroon. However, increasing climate variability, declining soil fertility, land degradation, and rising production costs conti
content: Smallholder agriculture remains the backbone of rural livelihoods and food security in the Western Highlands of Cameroon. However, increasing climate variability, declining soil fertility, land degradation, and rising production costs continue to threaten agricultural productivity and household resilience. Agroecological practices have emerged as sustainable alternatives capable of improving soil health, conserving biodiversity, enhancing climate resilience, and reducing dependence on external agricultural inputs. Despite these recognized benefits, the adoption of agroecological practices by smallholder farmers remains uneven, largely due to socioeconomic, institutional, and technical constraints. This study assessed farmers' knowledge, adoption, perceived benefits, and barriers to the implementation of agroecological practices in the West Region of Cameroon. A cross-sectional survey involving 200 smallholder farmers was conducted using structured questionnaires administered through digital data collection platforms. Descriptive statistical analyses were employed to evaluate farmers' awareness, adoption rates, perceived benefits, and major constraints affecting implementation. The results revealed that approximately 72% of respondents were familiar with at least one agroecological practice. Mixed cropping (78%), organic soil fertilization (65%), and water conservation techniques (55%) were the most widely adopted practices. Farmers identified improved soil fertility (74%), enhanced resilience to climate variability (68%), improved soil moisture retention (64%), and reduced dependence on synthetic fertilizers (58%) as the principal benefits of agroecological farming. However, inadequate technical knowledge (68%), limited access to organic inputs (54%), financial constraints (47%), labour shortages (39%), and insufficient agricultural extension services (41%) significantly constrained wider adoption. The findings demonstrate that although agroecological practices are increasingly recognized by farming communities, substantial institutional and technical barriers continue to limit their large-scale adoption. Strengthening farmer training programmes, improving extension services, facilitating access to organic inputs, promoting farmer-to-farmer learning networks, and integrating renewable energy technologies such as biogas slurry into nutrient management systems could significantly accelerate the transition towards sustainable agricultural production in Cameroon. The study provides valuable evidence to guide policymakers, development partners, and agricultural extension agencies in designing interventions that promote resilient, climate-smart, and environmentally sustainable farming systems.

title: Modification of Ni catalysts via La-induced Ce-O frustrated Lewis-pair sites on CeO2 for enhancing CO2 methanation
summary: Catalytic CO 2 methanation enables the conversion of captured CO 2 and renewable H 2 into synthetic methane, a crucial process for sustainable energy cycles. The Ni/La-CeO 2 catalyst was prepared by introducing La species into the CeO 2 sup
content: Catalytic CO 2 methanation enables the conversion of captured CO 2 and renewable H 2 into synthetic methane, a crucial process for sustainable energy cycles. The Ni/La-CeO 2 catalyst was prepared by introducing La species into the CeO 2 support via the coprecipitation-hydrothermal method followed by Ni loading. The catalytic performance in the CO 2 methanation reaction was investigated by experimental characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The results demonstrate that La species is dissolved in the CeO 2 matrix to form a La-Ce composite oxide solid solution. La 3+ substitution induces lattice distortion and charge-compensated oxygen-vacancy formation, constructing La-induced Ce-O frustrated Lewis-pair sites: under-coordinated Ce 3+ adjacent to oxygen vacancies acts as Lewis-acid site, while nearby intact lattice-oxygen serves as Lewis-base site. The Ce–O–La interactions in La-CeO 2 facilitate the formation of oxygen vacancies. These vacancies enhance the acid-base properties of Ce–O pairs adjacent to the La–Ov sites thus promoting the adsorption and activation of CO 2 , showing a large uphill thermodynamic energy change for the HCOO*-to-CHO* transformation, which suggests this step is kinetically challenging. The CO 2 reaction rate over Ni/La-CeO 2 is 8.69 × 10 –6 mol CO2 g –1 s –1 at 180°C, considerably higher than 4.93 × 10 –6 mol CO2 g –1 s –1 obtained over Ni/CeO 2 . The improved catalytic performance mainly originates from synergistic coupling between optimized Ni nanoparticles and FLP sites, providing a facile strategy for improving the catalytic activity of metal oxides in CO 2 methanation.

title: A distributed framework for coordination of green energy communities and renewable-rich distribution systems
summary: A collection of consumers, prosumers, homes or buildings may form an energy community. Optimal coordination between energy communities and distribution systems is of great importance. Although a lot of research effort has already targeted o
content: A collection of consumers, prosumers, homes or buildings may form an energy community. Optimal coordination between energy communities and distribution systems is of great importance. Although a lot of research effort has already targeted operational planning of energy communities, their coordination with local power grids has received comparatively limited attention in the literature. On the other hand, recently, the research on fully renewable energy systems has got considerable momentum; so, in this research, the main objective is to develop an efficient methodology for coordination of fully renewable/green energy communities and local active renewable-rich distribution systems. In a distributed optimisation framework, alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is used for optimal coordination of green, battery-integrated residential energy communities and renewable-rich distribution systems. In the proposed adaptive ADMM, in an iterative process, some penalty terms are added to the objectives of energy communities and active distribution system. In the developed model, energy communities are able to exchange both active and reactive power with distribution system; they also include capacitor banks as reactive power resources. The results show that the proposed ADMM efficiently coordinates energy communities and distribution system. The developed adaptive ADMM converges to an equilibrium, optimising the operation of distribution system and energy communities.

title: Bioenergy Potential of Spring Oat (Avena sativa L.) Cultivars and Gene Bank Accessions from Europe and the United States: Chemical Composition and Calorific Properties
summary: The physicochemical properties and energy potential of grain from 77 spring oat cultivars and gene bank accessions were evaluated using proximate and elemental analyses, as well as measurements of heat of combustion and higher heating value
content: The physicochemical properties and energy potential of grain from 77 spring oat cultivars and gene bank accessions were evaluated using proximate and elemental analyses, as well as measurements of heat of combustion and higher heating value (HHV). The samples exhibited high and relatively stable energy potential. Heat of combustion ranged from 19,262 to 20,429 kJ·kg−1, with a very low relative standard deviation (RSD) of 1.2%, indicating minimal variation in chemical energy content. The maximum HHV reached 17.69 MJ·kg−1 and also showed limited variability among cultivars and accessions. Hierarchical cluster analysis identified four distinct groups containing 8–30 cultivars and accessions each, based on 10 examined properties. Although significant differences in mean values were observed between clusters (except for carbon content), the overall variation among the samples analyzed remained low. Notably, all samples were characterized by very low chlorine concentrations (0.008–0.023% DM), which is advantageous for energy applications. The results confirm that oat biomass is a valuable renewable energy resource and that its calorific value is closely linked to chemical composition. However, the relatively small differences among cultivars and accessions suggest that identifying genotypes with exceptionally high energy potential may be difficult.

title: Aerobic ethanol oxidation by magnetic inductive heating of Pd NPs supported onto Ni foam
summary: Selective aerobic oxidation of ethanol to acetic acid is an attractive example of the conversion of biomass-derived alcohol value-added chemicals. In this context, conventional liquidphase processes often rely on harsh conditions, long reac
content: Selective aerobic oxidation of ethanol to acetic acid is an attractive example of the conversion of biomass-derived alcohol value-added chemicals. In this context, conventional liquidphase processes often rely on harsh conditions, long reaction times, inefficient external heating and limited catalyst recovery. Herein, a radically new strategy for acetic acid synthesis from ethanol is proposed and demonstrated. The catalyst used is designed not only as the active phase for chemical transformation, but also as the element responsible for local heat generation. Pd nanoparticles were immobilised onto magnetically-responsive Ni foam, affording a macroscopic, flow-compatible architecture that overcomes key limitations found for dispersed or powdered systems, including aggregation, active-phase loss and difficult reuse. Using a low amplitude alternating magnetic field of 9.2 mT, which corresponds to a lower magnetic flux density value than normally used for dispersed magnetic nanocatalyst, the Pd@Ni-foam system reached 90 % ethanol conversion after 8 h, while the acetic acid selectivity was >98 % already after 2 h reaction time. In analogous conditions, conventional heating was significantly less effective than magnetic induction, highlighting the advantage of delivering thermal energy directly at the Pd/liquid interface, thereby preserving ethanol availability at the active sites while limiting substrate evaporation. The structured catalyst showed direct reusability without regeneration, and analysis of the recovered catalyst revealed neither Pd NPs sintering, nor detectable Pd loss. By combining catalytic activity, lowfield magnetic responsiveness, stability, reduced bulk heating and continuous flow operation within a single tuneable material, a new approach to heterogeneous catalysis has been introduced, opening a modular route toward electrified, intensified and more efficient liquidphase transformations of renewable and volatile substrates, such as ethanol.

title: Power interplay among actors in the governance of Indonesian film and digital content censorship policy
summary: This study uses Indonesia as a case study to examine the complicated relationship between state and non-state actors in film and digital content censorship. As film, television, and digital content grow, censorship has become a crucial gove
content: This study uses Indonesia as a case study to examine the complicated relationship between state and non-state actors in film and digital content censorship. As film, television, and digital content grow, censorship has become a crucial governance instrument to manage cultural and moral standards. At the same time, creative industries and civic society are challenging restrictive rules to promote free speech. The research employs stakeholder analysis, grounded in Ackermann and Eden’s stakeholder identification theory, to explore actor configurations, interests, and influence within the policy process. Using qualitative methods—primarily in-depth interviews and FGD the study identified 18 stakeholder groups, including regulatory bodies, industry associations, civil society organisations, and community actors. Key findings show that the Indonesian Film Censorship Board (LSF) and Indonesian Broadcasting Commission (KPI) dominate film certification and broadcast content. LSF operations are also supervised by the Ministry of Culture. Government institutions have more power than industry and civil society, according to stakeholder mapping. The study found continuous contradictions between regulatory control and popular demand for creative space in Indonesia’s censorship environment. The stakeholder matrix adds a new empirical dimension to Southeast Asian media governance studies. It emphasizes the necessity for inclusive, transparent, and participatory censorship policymaking to balance stakeholder interests.

title: The Impact of Overlapping Phases in EPCC Projects on the Accuracy of 4D BIM (Time) and 5D BIM (Cost): A Literature Review
summary: Engineering, Procurement, Construction, and Commissioning (EPCC) projects often apply overlapping phases to accelerate project completion. This strategy allows procurement, construction, or commissioning to start before the preceding phase
content: Engineering, Procurement, Construction, and Commissioning (EPCC) projects often apply overlapping phases to accelerate project completion. This strategy allows procurement, construction, or commissioning to start before the preceding phase is fully completed. However, design, material, schedule, and cost information may continue to change and affect the accuracy of 4D and 5D Building Information Modeling (BIM). This study explains the effect of EPCC phase overlap on the time accuracy of 4D BIM and the cost accuracy of 5D BIM and describes the role of BIM in project control. A literature review was conducted using 38 journal articles covering fast-track construction, 4D BIM, 5D BIM, scheduling, procurement, quantity take-off, interoperability, and cost control. The findings show that overlap can reduce BIM accuracy when design changes, procurement status, field progress, and cost information are not updated promptly. The accuracy of 4D BIM is affected in work sequence, activity relationships, duration, progress, and completion time. The accuracy of 5D BIM is affected in quantities, prices, rework costs, scope changes, and final cost forecasts. Nevertheless, BIM remains important because it enables project teams to identify the time and cost consequences of changes more quickly. BIM accuracy can be maintained through regular model updates, consistent project data, integration of models with schedule and cost information, and coordination among EPCC phases.

title: Governance‑Driven Integration of Multi‑Source Renewable Energy Systems in South African Private Hospitals
source: International Journal of Business Ecosystem and Strategy (2687-2293)
summary: This study investigates how a major South African private hospital group adopts and scales multiple renewable energy sources (MRES) within a mission-critical healthcare environment characterised by chronic grid instability. Using a qualitat
content: This study investigates how a major South African private hospital group adopts and scales multiple renewable energy sources (MRES) within a mission-critical healthcare environment characterised by chronic grid instability. Using a qualitative single‑case study design, the research draws on semi-structured interviews with senior executives and technical managers, complemented by documentary analysis, to explore the barriers, enablers and governance mechanisms underpinning MRES adoption. The results reveal that financial and economic constraints, regulatory fragmentation, legacy infrastructure, and supply chain limitations constitute multidimensional barriers. In contrast, economic viability, executive leadership, risk-managed implementation, and energy-security imperatives serve as decisive enablers. The study demonstrates that effective adoption arises not from technology choices alone, but from an integrated organisational approach that combines diversified energy portfolios, phased implementation strategies, contractual procurement, and structured sustainability governance. The proposed Integrated MRES Adoption Framework synthesises these dimensions, offering a holistic model for energy transition in high-risk medical settings. The study concludes that hospitals can meaningfully advance renewable energy penetration when technical diversification is embedded within robust governance, financial feasibility assessments, and patient-safety-aligned risk management. Limitations include a single-case scope and senior-level perspectives; future research should compare public and private systems, evaluate long-term performance, and deepen inquiry into staff-level change processes.

title: DIGITAL MARKETING AND CONSUMER KNOWLEDGE : RESIDENTIAL SOLAR ENERGY ADOPTION INTENTION THROUGH PERCEIVED SUSTAINABLE PRODUCT INNOVATION
summary: This study examines the influence of digital marketing and consumer knowledge on residential solar energy adoption intention, with perceived sustainable product innovation serving as a mediating variable. A quantitative survey approach was
content: This study examines the influence of digital marketing and consumer knowledge on residential solar energy adoption intention, with perceived sustainable product innovation serving as a mediating variable. A quantitative survey approach was employed using data collected from 223 respondents in Indonesia and analyzed through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings demonstrate that digital marketing and consumer knowledge positively and significantly influence perceived sustainable product innovation and residential solar energy adoption intention. Perceived sustainable product innovation also significantly strengthens adoption intention and partially mediates the effects of both digital marketing and consumer knowledge. These findings indicate that consumers are more likely to consider adopting residential solar energy when they receive relevant and credible digital information, possess sufficient knowledge about solar technology, and perceive solar energy as an innovative and sustainable solution. The study contributes to the renewable energy adoption literature by integrating external marketing communication, internal consumer knowledge, and perceived sustainable innovation within a single consumer-level framework. It also highlights perceived sustainable product innovation as an important mechanism through which digital marketing and consumer knowledge translate into stronger adoption intentions. From a practical perspective, solar energy providers and related stakeholders should strengthen informative and credible digital communication, improve consumer understanding of solar technology, and emphasize its innovative and sustainability-related benefits. These efforts may help foster more favorable consumer perceptions and encourage greater intention to adopt residential solar energy.

title: Data and model code for: Water- versus air-based recovery of low-grade solar heat from asphalt pavements in a hot-arid climate (Doha, Qatar)
summary: Data and model code for the article "Water- versus air-based recovery of low-grade solar heat from asphalt pavements in a hot-arid climate: a thermodynamic characterisation for Doha, Qatar" (Case Studies in Thermal Engineering). The dataset
content: Data and model code for the article "Water- versus air-based recovery of low-grade solar heat from asphalt pavements in a hot-arid climate: a thermodynamic characterisation for Doha, Qatar" (Case Studies in Thermal Engineering). The dataset contains the inputs and results of an hourly steady-state model of a buried-pipe pavement heat-recovery collector (289 m2 road section in Doha) with water and with air as the carrier fluid, analysed with mass, energy, entropy and exergy balances. Files (comma-separated text; first line column names, second line units; temperatures in degrees Celsius; efficiencies as fractions): 01_climate_inputs_monthly.csv - monthly daily irradiation, derived peak irradiance, day length, mean daily maximum air temperature and seawater temperature (water inlet) for Doha. 02_july_diurnal_profiles.csv - typical July day at 15-minute steps: irradiance, air and surface temperature, recovered heat, outlet temperature and entropy generation for both collectors, blower power. 03_monthly_performance_water.csv and 04_monthly_performance_air.csv - monthly recovered energy, peak recovery, outlet temperature, equivalent peak hours, energy and exergy efficiencies, entropy generation and exergy destruction. 05a, 05b, 05c sweep files - recovered heat, outlet and surface temperature of the water collector against irradiance, air temperature and water mass flow at the July design point. 06_design_point_july.csv - complete state of the July design point for both collectors. 07_validation_cooled_cases_test_site.csv - reported and modelled peak surface and water outlet temperatures for nine test-site cases (three inlet temperatures, three water velocities). 08_validation_uncooled_surface_15_July_2015.csv - hourly reported and modelled surface temperature of the uncooled pavement. model_code/pavement_collector_model.m - MATLAB script of the model (requires CoolProp through MATLAB's Python interface); model_code/monthly_outputs.csv - its monthly output table. README.md maps each file to the figures and tables of the article. Third-party inputs, all cited and used as published values only: monthly irradiation from Bachour and Perez-Astudillo (2014), Renewable Energy 71, 32-36; air temperature from the World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal (CRU climatology, CC BY 4.0); seawater temperature from NOAA OISST v2.1 (US public domain); test-site temperatures read from the published curves of the HBKU pavement experiment cited in the article. No third-party raw dataset is redistributed.

title: Built‐In Electric Fields in Rechargeable Batteries: Formation Mechanisms, Functional Roles, and Design Principles
summary: Rechargeable batteries (lithium-ion, sodium-ion, zinc-ion) are core technologies for large-scale renewable energy storage, featuring high energy density, conversion efficiency, and application flexibility. However, their development remains
content: Rechargeable batteries (lithium-ion, sodium-ion, zinc-ion) are core technologies for large-scale renewable energy storage, featuring high energy density, conversion efficiency, and application flexibility. However, their development remains hindered by structural instability, sluggish ion/electron transport, and uncontrolled interfacial reactions during cycling. The built-in electric field (BIEF) is an intrinsic physical field that forms spontaneously without external bias, which could regulate the local potential distribution and guide the migration behavior of electrons and ions, showing significant potential for improving reaction kinetics and suppressing structural instability. Through the rational design of heterointerfaces, polarized structures, and composition or defect gradients, BIEFs effectively alleviate volume expansion, homogenize reaction fronts, accelerate carrier transport, and stabilize interfacial evolution. In this review, we provide a systematic overview of BIEF formation mechanisms, characterization methods, theoretical calculations, and functional roles in anodes, cathodes, and electrolytes. Recent progress in characterization techniques and theoretical calculations for clarifying BIEF mechanisms is summarized, along with key engineering strategies and design principles for BIEF construction. We hope that this review could provide useful guidance for the predictive design and practical implementation of BIEF in next-generation batteries with high energy density and long cycle life.

title: Green Chemistry and its Benefits
source: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
summary: Green chemistry is a preventive approach to chemistry that seeks to design chemical products and processes so that the use and generation of hazardous substances are minimized or eliminated. Rather than treating pollution after it has been
content: Green chemistry is a preventive approach to chemistry that seeks to design chemical products and processes so that the use and generation of hazardous substances are minimized or eliminated. Rather than treating pollution after it has been produced, green chemistry addresses pollution at the source through safer synthesis, efficient use of resources, renewable feedstocks, catalysis, safer solvents and reaction conditions, energy efficiency, and real-time process monitoring. This chapter introduces the concept and twelve principles of green chemistry and discusses their relevance to human health, environmental protection, resource conservation, industrial safety and sustainable chemical production. Examples of enabling approaches, including biocatalysts, biomass-derived feedstocks, ionic liquids, supercritical fluids, aqueous media, microwave-assisted synthesis and photocatalysis, are also outlined. The chapter highlights the multidisciplinary nature of green chemistry and its role in sustainable development.

title: Diffusion-Limited Solid-State Synthesis Selectivity in the Presence of Oxidation/Reduction Processes
summary: Abstract Solid-state synthesis outcomes arise from an interplay between thermodynamics and kinetics, with their relative importance governed by external control parameters such as temperature profiles and precursor selection. A recently int
content: Abstract Solid-state synthesis outcomes arise from an interplay between thermodynamics and kinetics, with their relative importance governed by external control parameters such as temperature profiles and precursor selection. A recently introduced framework, combining first-principles thermodynamics with machine-learning-enabled simulations of correlated ion transport, successfully captured this interplay in the Ba–Ti–O system by linking phase selectivity to ion mobility within “liquid-like”, amorphous interphases. Notably, in systems where valence states can change during synthesis, ion dynamics are strongly coupled to oxidation state. Here, we extend the framework to such mixed-valence systems and demonstrate its predictive power for the synthesis of ternary metal ferrites in the Ba–Fe–O and Y–Fe–O systems, benchmarked against in situ XRD experiments. Similar to the Ba–Ti–O system, we hypothesize that the rate-limiting transport of ionic species governing polymorph growth occurs through a “liquid-like,” noncrystalline interphase. To capture this behavior, we employ a charge-informed machine-learning potential (CHGNet) that enables modeling of correlated, redox-dependent transport. We find that the framework accurately predicts the sequence of phase formation and the time evolution of phase distributions in powder synthesis reactions, in agreement with experimental reports. These results show that diffusion-limited phase selectivity can be treated on a unified footing across mixed-valence oxides, further clearing a pathway toward rational, in silico synthesis design that simultaneously accounts for thermodynamic and kinetic factors.

title: Fungal Pretreatment-Assisted Methane Recovery from Food Waste: A Literature-Informed Simulation Framework
summary: Food waste is a heterogeneous, moisture-rich substrate with substantial potential for renewable methane recovery, but variability in composition, hydrolysis and reactor stability constrains reliable anaerobic-digestion performance. This stu
content: Food waste is a heterogeneous, moisture-rich substrate with substantial potential for renewable methane recovery, but variability in composition, hydrolysis and reactor stability constrains reliable anaerobic-digestion performance. This study presents a literature-informed computational scenario-screening framework that translates fungal pretreatment descriptors into model-ready variables for anaerobic digestion. Published experimental and modelling studies were used to parameterise food-waste composition, spent coffee grounds (SCG), enzyme-targeted pretreatment, anaerobic-digestion operating conditions, methane potential and heuristic risk indicators; no new experimental measurements were generated. The Python-based framework links fungal pretreatment severity with substrate solubilisation, hydrolysis, methane yield, raw-biogas CH4 fraction, gross methane energy recovery and operational-risk indicators. Under the specified model assumptions, heuristic stability-adjusted methane output methane screening output increased from 272.5 L CH4 kg−1 VS in the untreated control to 291.5 L CH4 kg−1 VS under high pretreatment and 295.5 L CH4 kg−1 VS under extended pretreatment, while increasing SCG inclusion and high organic loading reduced the corresponding screening outputs. These directional responses are partly imposed by the model structure and are therefore interpreted as comparative scenario outputs and experimentally testable hypotheses rather than independent quantitative predictions or process optima.

title: SF-FDO v5: Spherical Fuzzy Differential Optimization for Photovoltaic–Battery Energy Management — Real NSRDB Baku Dataset, DRL Surrogate, and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Learning Module (Simulation Code, Datasets, and Figures)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This repository provides the complete, reproducible implementation accompanying the manuscript "An Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Learning Framework for Throughput-Minimal Uncertainty-Aware Energy Management in Photovoltaic–Battery Systems" (ANF–SFDO
content: This repository provides the complete, reproducible implementation accompanying the manuscript "An Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Learning Framework for Throughput-Minimal Uncertainty-Aware Energy Management in Photovoltaic–Battery Systems" (ANF–SFDO / SF-FDO). Version 5 (this release) updates and extends the previous revision as follows: - Real-data integration: all reported results and figures are now driven by the real NSRDB Baku Typical-Meteorological-Year hourly irradiance record (N = 6,333 hours; exported from ADDNF_NSRDB_NASA_Datasets.xlsx), replacing the synthetic irradiance profile used in earlier revisions.- Bug fix: corrected a variable-reuse defect in the Lyapunov stability gradient (ΔV was previously always evaluated as zero), restoring the intended stability-constraint behaviour described in the manuscript.- DRL benchmark: replaced the placeholder deep-reinforcement-learning comparator with a genuinely trained lightweight neural policy (evolutionary-strategy optimization, train/deploy split), providing an honest, reproducible data-driven baseline.- Ablation study: implemented functional on/off toggles for the α-cut propagation mechanism and the Lyapunov stability term, enabling direct, real-data recomputation of these ablation conditions.- Adaptive neuro-fuzzy learning module (sf_fdo_adaptive.py): a faithful implementation of the online Gaussian-membership-function learning rule described in the manuscript (Eq. 19–24), with EMA-smoothed, L2-regularised gradient updates. This module is included as a transparent, exploratory supplementary analysis; the manuscript's headline "Full ANF–SFDO" results use fixed (non-adaptive) membership functions calibrated to the real operating range, and the online-adaptive variant's behaviour under real irradiance is documented in the manuscript's Limitations section.- Figures: all regenerated at 600 DPI with 18 pt text (titles, axis labels, legends, panel letters) throughout, matching journal figure-legibility requirements. Repository contents: core SF-FDO/ANF-SFDO controller (sf_fdo_core.py), adaptive-learning module (sf_fdo_adaptive.py), benchmark controllers and full simulation pipeline (simulation_main.py), hardware-in-the-loop / Edge AI deployment layer (hardware_daq.py), figure-generation scripts (generate_figures_v3.py, generate_figures_v4.py), the NSRDB Baku dataset export utility (export_nsrdb_from_xlsx.py) and the source workbook, and all regenerated manuscript figures. Keywords: photovoltaic–battery energy storage, spherical fuzzy differential optimization, adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference, generalized Hukuhara derivative, Lyapunov-stable control, deep reinforcement learning benchmark, NSRDB, Baku, Azerbaijan, renewable energy management, edge AI. License: MIT.

title: Photo-assisted supercapacitors: Working principles, electrode materials and prospects
summary: Unlike traditional supercapacitors, photo-assisted supercapacitors integrate photoactive materials into conventional supercapacitor structures, enabling the direct combination of renewable solar energy with energy storage devices. This inte
content: Unlike traditional supercapacitors, photo-assisted supercapacitors integrate photoactive materials into conventional supercapacitor structures, enabling the direct combination of renewable solar energy with energy storage devices. This integration effectively addresses the challenge of intermittency inherent in renewable energy sources. While considerable reviews have been devoted to photo-assisted rechargeable batteries and related photochemical energy storage systems, a comprehensive overview focusing specifically on the energy storage mechanisms and tailored electrode material design for photo-assisted supercapacitors remains scarce. In light of the growing importance of photo-assisted supercapacitors in modern industrial applications, this review systematically summarizes the development process, working principles, categorization, key components of photo-assisted supercapacitors, and research progess of photoactive electrode materials. The operational principles, including photo-charging and energy storage mechanisms, are introduced first, followed by a summary of the classification and constituent components of such devices. Given the critical role of electrode materials, existing photoactive electrode materials are categorized into three groups: metal oxides and oxide-based composites, metal sulfides and sulfide-based composites, and g-C 3 N 4 -based composites. The recent advance in these photoactive materials is emphasized, covering aspects of material design, performance enhancement, and the underlying light-enhanced mechanisms. Finally, current challenges and future prospects in the field of photo-assisted supercapacitors are outlined. It is expected that this review will provide valuable context, theoretical guidance, and practical design strategies for the development of novel photo-assisted supercapacitors.

title: USF-Net: a Unified Spatiotemporal Fusion Network for ground-based remote sensing cloud image sequence extrapolation
summary: Accurate extrapolation of ground-based cloud imagery is foundational to the stability of photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems. However, current methods rely on static kernels that neglect multi-scale cloud dynamics and lack robust tem
content: Accurate extrapolation of ground-based cloud imagery is foundational to the stability of photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems. However, current methods rely on static kernels that neglect multi-scale cloud dynamics and lack robust temporal guidance for long-range dependency modelling. Moreover, the quadratic computational cost of standard attention mechanisms increases the computational burden of high-resolution inference. To bridge these gaps, we propose the Unified Spatiotemporal Fusion Network (USF-Net), whose principal methodological contribution lies in a directional temporal-to-spatial conditioning and cross-stage temporal-state preservation architecture rather than in the individual convolution, attention, or gating operations. Specifically, USF-Net incorporates a unified spatiotemporal module (USTM), which comprises a spatial information branch equipped with a spatial selection module (SSM) for dynamic multi-scale context extraction and a temporal information branch featuring a temporal agent attention module (TAM). The TAM efficiently models long-range temporal dependencies, circumventing the computational bottlenecks of traditional attention. In the decoder, a dynamic update module (DUM) leverages initial temporal states to preserve motion signatures, thereby mitigating ghosting effects. Crucially, we introduce the ASI-Cloud Image Sequence (ASI-CIS) dataset, a large-scale, high-resolution benchmark designed to address current data limitations. Extensive experiments on ASI-CIS and the public Folsom benchmark demonstrate that USF-Net achieves competitive prediction performance across independent datasets. Additional zero-shot transfer from ASI-CIS to Folsom further indicates partial cross-dataset robustness, although performance degradation under domain shift remains evident. The dataset and source code will be available at https://github.com/she1110/ASI-CIS.

title: Research on microgrid power supply equipment system based on intelligent IoT remote monitoring and management
summary: The incorporation of renewable energy sources (RES) into grid-connected microgrids, especially in the manufacturing industry, has added significant complications to power generation forecasting, control, and management. As microgrids rely o
content: The incorporation of renewable energy sources (RES) into grid-connected microgrids, especially in the manufacturing industry, has added significant complications to power generation forecasting, control, and management. As microgrids rely on RES, such as solar and wind power, there is a crucial need for more accurate energy predictions and better management systems. Existing IoT-enabled microgrid monitoring systems still suffer from limited forecasting accuracy, inefficient hyperparameter optimization, and inadequate adaptation to dynamic renewable energy conditions in manufacturing environments.Research investigates the use of ML methods, particularly Adaptive tunicate swarm optimized random forests (ATSO-RF), to increase the efficacy and reliability of microgrid power systems in the manufacturing industry. It utilizes historical energy generation data, weather patterns, and dynamic grid conditions to create a sophisticated model for power generation prediction and management systems. Pre-processing with Z-score normalization and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) was used to reduce the number of topographies by decreasing variance across different energy states or microgrid conditions, thereby allowing for more accurate energy forecasting classification. The ATSO-RF algorithm outperforms traditional models by providing better predictive accuracy and improved energy management. The proposed method is implemented by using Python 3.10.1. In comparative evaluation against LGBM (R2 = 84%, MAE = 3.93, RMSE = 5.77) and RF (R2 = 95.2%, MAE = 22.8, RMSE = 31.7), the proposed ATSO-RF achieves R2 = 96.85%, MAE = 3.01, and RMSE = 4.81. The model also attains energy efficiency of 86%, fault detection rate of 93%, and system uptime of 94.5%, demonstrating practical potential for real-time adaptive energy management and cost-effective integration of renewable energy sources in manufacturing microgrids.The simulation results suggest potential for real-time adaptive energy management in manufacturing microgrids; hardware validation on a physical testbed is identified as a priority for future work.

title: Renewable Energy Output Uncertainty and Risk Transmission in Sustainable Power Supply Chains
summary: Uncertainty in renewable energy output changes how risk is allocated among generators and electricity retailers. We develop a mean–variance model with a thermal plant, a green plant, and a retailer under retailer-led Stackelberg and generat
content: Uncertainty in renewable energy output changes how risk is allocated among generators and electricity retailers. We develop a mean–variance model with a thermal plant, a green plant, and a retailer under retailer-led Stackelberg and generation-side Cournot arrangements. In the Stackelberg arrangement, greater retailer risk aversion raises the purchase price and both outputs by compressing the retailer’s unit-margin exposure. In the Cournot arrangement, greater thermal-plant risk aversion lowers thermal and total output but raises green output, the expected purchase price, and renewable share. At the baseline endpoints, green share falls from 55.9% to 51.6% in the former arrangement and rises from 54.8% to 74.1% in the latter. The green plant’s optimal mean output is independent of its own risk coefficient under additive zero-skewness, quadratic-profit, and decision-independent uncertainty conditions; a skewed-shock counterexample shows where this shielding can fail. Local, global, and distributional sensitivity checks and 5000 feasible parameter draws reproduce the analytical directions while showing that magnitudes are calibration dependent. Because renewable share can move opposite to absolute renewable generation, sustainability assessment should report generation levels, shares, procurement prices, and risk allocation together. The model does not estimate emissions, welfare, or reliability.

title: Exact variance of random return in distributional LQR and its application to mean–variance optimal control
summary: The classical linear quadratic regulator (LQR) minimizes the expected cumulative return but fails to account for performance variability, rendering it inadequate for risk-aware applications. To address this, we introduce the variance of the
content: The classical linear quadratic regulator (LQR) minimizes the expected cumulative return but fails to account for performance variability, rendering it inadequate for risk-aware applications. To address this, we introduce the variance of the cumulative return as a risk measure in LQR. We derive the first exact closed-form expression for the variance of the discounted in?finite horizon return within the discrete-time Distributional LQR framework, for i.i.d. disturbances with symmetric probability densities. For Gaussian disturbances, this expression elegantly simplifies to a form dependent only on the disturbance covariance. Leveraging these theoretical foundations, we formulate a mean-variance optimal control problem that explicitly manages the trade-off between expected return and performance variability. To address the resulting non-convex optimization problem, we propose a novel adjoint gradient descent algorithm for a penalized formulation of the original problem, and establish that all iterates remain stabilizing and converge to a stationary point of the penalized objective. The effectiveness of this framework and the inherent risk-performance trade-off? are demonstrated through numerical experiments.

title: Implementasi Deep Reinforcement Learning untuk Optimasi Energi Sistem Panel Surya pada Penghitung Ikan Otomatis
source: Mars Jurnal Teknik Mesin Industri Elektro Dan Ilmu Komputer
summary: Standalone battery-based photovoltaic systems can experience suboptimal energy utilization when energy-flow decisions rely on fixed control rules that do not adapt to changing operating conditions. This study implemented Deep Reinforcement
content: Standalone battery-based photovoltaic systems can experience suboptimal energy utilization when energy-flow decisions rely on fixed control rules that do not adapt to changing operating conditions. This study implemented Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) based on a Deep Q-Network (DQN) on an ESP32 as a system-level energy manager and evaluated its performance against conventional Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT). The experimental evaluation was conducted for six days, 21–26 June 2026, from 10:00 to 16:00 WIB, using the same prototype and a counterbalanced ABBA switching design. Data were sampled every 10 minutes, producing 444 valid observations consisting of 222 observations for MPPT and 222 for DRL. The evaluated parameters were panel output power, cumulative energy, and power stability. The DRL mode produced an average panel power of 46.75 W, compared with 45.08 W for MPPT, corresponding to a 3.70% increase. The final report summary also records cumulative energy of 1,693.93 Wh for DRL and 1,633.82 Wh for MPPT, while the coefficient of variation was 16.07% and 16.57%, respectively. DQN inference latency on ESP32 was 35–85 ms per decision. Daily-block inferential analysis reported a paired t-test of p < 0.001 and Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.031 (n = 6 days). The findings indicate that system-level DRL energy-flow management can improve the utilization of photovoltaic power while maintaining comparable or slightly better relative power stability under the tested conditions.

title: A Novel Edge Computing-Based System for Real-Time Neutral-to-Earth Voltage and Energy Monitoring in Distribution Networks
source: Istanbul University - Journal of Electrical & Electronics Engineering
summary: Neutral-to-earth voltage (NTEV) is a critical indicator of grounding integrity, insulation degradation, and electrical safety in distribution networks; however, it is often monitored only through centralized cloud-based systems, resulting i
content: Neutral-to-earth voltage (NTEV) is a critical indicator of grounding integrity, insulation degradation, and electrical safety in distribution networks; however, it is often monitored only through centralized cloud-based systems, resulting in high latency, limited visibility of time-dependent anomalies, and dependency on reliable communication infrastructure. This paper presents the design, implementation, and field validation of a Smart Energy Meter–Edge Gateway (SEM-EG) architecture that integrates continuous NTEV monitoring with edgebased analytics and cloud-supported supervision. The proposed system performs real-time measurement of NTEV together with voltage, current, and power-related parameters, enabling local anomaly detection and operational awareness at the field level while providing long-term data aggregation and visualization in the cloud. Long-term deployment in an operational distribution panel demonstrates that continuous edge-based monitoring detects time-dependent grounding-related faults that remain undetected by conventional measurements, and that corrective field interventions result in an approximately 80% reduction in night-time NTEV levels, quantitatively verifying maintenance effectiveness. In addition, a multi-parameter analysis framework combining NTEV, phase currents, phase voltages, and power metrics is used to assess indirect system impacts. The SEM-EG achieves a measurement precision of ±0.5% and reduces fault detection latency by 78% compared to cloud-only approaches. Results show that edge intelligence transforms NTEV from a passive diagnostic parameter into an active, real-time operational indicator, providing a scalable and practical solution for modern smart grids.

title: 5. Water underground
summary: Water underground can flow in unsaturated or saturated conditions. This chapter first explains how water infiltrates into unsaturated soils and redistributes through soil profiles. Moving to saturated conditions, the text presents mechanism
content: Water underground can flow in unsaturated or saturated conditions. This chapter first explains how water infiltrates into unsaturated soils and redistributes through soil profiles. Moving to saturated conditions, the text presents mechanisms of groundwater flow and describes where groundwater may re-emerge at the land surface. The chapter closes with a section on how groundwater has been used for water supplies. Technical sections cover techniques for measuring infiltration and groundwater levels, soil hydraulic properties, and groundwater equations. Sustainability sections introduce how soil sensors can be used to reduce irrigation water use, techniques to increase groundwater recharge, and a case study in Australia where groundwater management has helped water levels recover from previous depletion.

title: Sharia-Based Green Economy: A Philosophical Approach to Sustainable Natural Resource Management
summary: Excessive exploitation of natural resources has led to ecological damage and economic inequality. This calls for a variety of solutions, including those rooted in religious teachings. This study aims to identify strategies for implementing
content: Excessive exploitation of natural resources has led to ecological damage and economic inequality. This calls for a variety of solutions, including those rooted in religious teachings. This study aims to identify strategies for implementing sharia compliant green economy principles in the sustainable utilization of natural resources. This qualitative study employs a literature review approach by examining various scientific publications and regulations related to the green economy and Sharia-based economics. The findings indicate that Sharia principles, such as justice, balance, public interest, and human responsibility as stewards (khalifah) of the Earth, play an important role in implementing a sharia-based green economy. These principles can be manifested through the development of environmentally friendly investments, the utilization of renewable energy, the strengthening of the circular economy, and the management of natural resources that takes into account environmental sustainability and community welfare. This study contributes to the development of a green economy concept integrated with sharia principles as a solution for achieving sustainable development

title: BA3CAK(PO4)3:EU2+ PHOSPHOR TO ENHANCE GREEN LIGHT FOR WHITE LED APPLICATIONS
source: Journal of Science and Technology - IUH
summary: The Ba3CaK(PO4)3:Eu2+ (Eu-BCKPO) is synthesized with the high-temperature solid-state reacting route. The as-synthesized phosphor compound can result in cool white light with high quantum yield due to the site substitution of the Eu2+. To e
content: The Ba3CaK(PO4)3:Eu2+ (Eu-BCKPO) is synthesized with the high-temperature solid-state reacting route. The as-synthesized phosphor compound can result in cool white light with high quantum yield due to the site substitution of the Eu2+. To examine the effect of Eu-BCKPO phosphor on the green emission range and the total luminous flux of the conventional LED, different amounts of Eu-BCKPO are combined with blue chip (465 nm) and YAG:Ce3+ yellow phosphor. The increasing amount of Eu-BCKPO phosphor supports the stability of color temperature and improvement of luminosity of the examined LED. The green wavelength region in the total LED spectrum also increases with higher Eu-BCKPO doping amounts. However, the color rendering efficiency of LED white light goes downward as the concentration of Eu-BCKPO phosphor increases owing to the insufficient of the red component. Thus, the Eu-BCKPO can be utilized in green-LED fabrication or combine with blue and red luminescent materials for forming the multicolor/white LED devices.

title: EFEKTIVITAS KARBON AKTIF AMPAS KOPI TERHADAP PENURUNAN COD DAN TSS LIMBAH TAHU
source: PERISAI Jurnal Pendidikan dan Riset Ilmu Sains
summary: Limbah cair industri tahu merupakan salah satu sumber pencemar lingkungan yang mengandung bahan organik dan padatan tersuspensi tinggi sehingga memerlukan pengolahan sebelum dibuang ke badan air. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi efekti
content: Limbah cair industri tahu merupakan salah satu sumber pencemar lingkungan yang mengandung bahan organik dan padatan tersuspensi tinggi sehingga memerlukan pengolahan sebelum dibuang ke badan air. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi efektivitas karbon aktif berbasis ampas kopi sebagai adsorben dalam menurunkan kadar Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) dan Total Suspended Solids (TSS) pada limbah cair industri tahu. Karbon aktif dibuat melalui proses aktivasi kimia dan dikarakterisasi berdasarkan rendemen, kadar air, kadar abu, serta daya serap iodium. Proses adsorpsi dilakukan dengan variasi dosis adsorben 4, 6, dan; total suspended solids 8 gram serta waktu kontak 30, 40, dan 50 menit. Analisis COD dilakukan menggunakan metode spektrofotometri, sedangkan TSS menggunakan metode gravimetri. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa karbon aktif berbasis ampas kopi efektif menurunkan kadar COD hingga sekitar 90% dan TSS hingga sekitar 96%, dengan kondisi optimum pada dosis adsorben 6 gram dan waktu kontak 40 menit. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa karbon aktif berbasis ampas kopi berpotensi menjadi adsorben alternatif yang efektif, ekonomis, dan berkelanjutan untuk pengolahan limbah cair industri tahu.

title: Online transient stability assessment for AC/DC power systems based on clustering BCU and hybrid neural networks
summary: The widespread integration of power electronic devices including renewable energy sources and Line Commutated converter (LCC)-based High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) poses significant challenges to the transient stability of AC/DC power gr
content: The widespread integration of power electronic devices including renewable energy sources and Line Commutated converter (LCC)-based High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) poses significant challenges to the transient stability of AC/DC power grids. To realize the accurate and fast online transient stability assessment of AC/DC power systems, this paper firstly constructs terminal potential energy expressions through the integration of active power with respect to voltage phase angle and reactive power with respect to voltage magnitude. Subsequently, this paper proposes an online transient stability assessment method based on clustering Boundary of stability based Controlling Unstable-equilibrium-point (BCU) and hybrid neural networks to address the computational inefficiency issue of pure mechanism analytical approaches in critical energy determination. The clustering BCU method significantly reduces computational complexity when generating offline critical energy datasets by eliminating redundant calculations for different fault scenarios within the same coherent fault cluster. Besides, the convolutional neural networks-gate recurrent unit (CNN-GRU) based hybrid neural network is presented for real-time online transient stability assessment, which can quickly and accurately require the critical energy during system faults and compare it with the transient energy at fault clearing time to determine system stability. Compared with the multiple parallel CNN-GRU model, the proposed approach further provides physically interpretable indicators, including critical energy, critical clearing time, and stability margin, enabling more reliable evaluation of system stability boundaries. Finally, simulation results under different renewable penetration levels, transmission conditions, and fault scenarios demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high assessment accuracy, strong robustness, and improved computational efficiency for online transient stability assessment of renewable-integrated AC/DC hybrid power systems.

title: Quantifying interphase heat transport for analytical design of volumetric solar reactors: Exemplified by methane dry reforming
source: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
summary: To reduce carbon footprints, the field of thermochemical carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) conversion has recently focused on the electrified thermochemical system driven by Joule heating from renewable electricity ( e.g. , solar photovoltaics), where
content: To reduce carbon footprints, the field of thermochemical carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) conversion has recently focused on the electrified thermochemical system driven by Joule heating from renewable electricity ( e.g. , solar photovoltaics), where the overall solar-to-chemical (STC) energy conversion efficiency is limited. Thermochemical CO 2 conversion driven by direct solar thermal heating (especially volumetric solar heating), on the contrary, has been demonstrated to achieve higher STC efficiency. However, it has not yet been revealed how to quantitatively and analytically design the volumetric solar reactor to maximize STC efficiency. Here, we numerically identified local thermal non-equilibrium (LTNE) between gas (reactants) and solid (skeleton of the volumetric reactor) phases as the descriptor of STC efficiency by taking methane dry reforming as an example. A medium LTNE was found to simultaneously provide enough reaction driving force and reduce surface and volumetric thermal radiation losses; thus, it is beneficial to achieve high STC efficiency. We further theoretically derived an analytical criterion quantifying interphase heat transport to achieve a medium LTNE. Guided by this criterion, the volumetric solar reactor with the optimized bed parameters was experimentally demonstrated to achieve a near 40% STC efficiency, which is superior for nickel-based catalysts. Specifically, the optimized reactor in the medium LTNE regime (with the optimal pore size) achieved a relative enhancement of 23% in STC efficiency compared to the reactors in the high and low LTNE regimes.

title: A real-time validated improved voltage stabilizer with model predictive control–based hybrid energy storage optimization
summary: This work introduces an improved voltage stabilizer (IVS) architecture that combines a model predictive control (MPC)-based power system stabilizer (PSS) with a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) to increase voltage stability in microgrids
content: This work introduces an improved voltage stabilizer (IVS) architecture that combines a model predictive control (MPC)-based power system stabilizer (PSS) with a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) to increase voltage stability in microgrids. The proposed IVS–MPC architecture manages the active power support of batteries and super capacitors to efficiently reduce voltage fluctuations caused by renewable energy sources that aren’t always available and quickly changing loads. The stabilizer uses MPC’s ability to forecast future events to anticipate possible problems and change the HESS’s charging and discharging activities in real time, allowing for quick remedial control actions. This predictive and coordinated control system makes both steady-state voltage regulation and transient voltage recovery better.The battery unit mostly deals with long-term power imbalances, while the super capacitor makes up for short-term changes, thus the system can adapt quickly to changes over a range of time scales. The control method also has an optimization layer that figures out the best power contribution from each storage component. This makes better use of energy and cuts down on wasteful battery cycling.The OPAL-RT platform was used to test the proposed IVS–MPC method in real time, which showed that it worked. When compared to traditional PSS and voltage stabilizer designs, the suggested method shows better performance in terms of reducing voltage deviation, faster settling time, and better damping when the load changes. Both simulated and real-time experimental results show that the IVS-assisted HESS coordination greatly improves the microgrid’s ability to regulate voltage.

title: Development of Canva-Based Interactive Video to Enhance Environmental Literacy of Elementary School Students
summary: Students' low awareness of environmental conditions and the lack of learning activities that connect concepts with real-world contexts present key challenges in strengthening environmental literacy in elementary schools. This study aims to
content: Students' low awareness of environmental conditions and the lack of learning activities that connect concepts with real-world contexts present key challenges in strengthening environmental literacy in elementary schools. This study aims to develop and test the effectiveness of Canva-based interactive videos in supporting students' environmental literacy. The study utilized the ADDIE development model, involving fifth-grade students as the research subjects. Data were collected through tests, questionnaires, observations, and expert validations, and subsequently analyzed using quantitative descriptive techniques. The results indicated that the developed media achieved a valid category (76.44%) and a highly practical category (97.90%). The improvement in environmental literacy was observed in the cognitive aspect with an N-Gain score of 0.93 (high category), as well as in the affective (99.00%) and behavioral (100.00%) aspects, both falling into the excellent category. The uniqueness of this research lies in the implementation of the media within a local region facing challenges of environmental degradation and low ecological awareness, making the integration of local contexts a key factor in enhancing meaningful learning. Thus, contextually designed Canva-based interactive videos are proven effective in supporting the enhancement of environmental literacy among elementary school students

title: IMPLEMENTASI PROGRAM KREASEA TUMBUH DALAM PEMBERDAYAAN MASYARAKAT MELALUI BUDIDAYA PANGAN BERBASIS HIDROPONIK DI KELURAHAN LEBAKGEDE
summary: This study aims to analyse the implementation of the KreaSea Tumbuh Program regarding community empowerment, covering the program execution process, stakeholder involvement, community capacity building, and the resulting social, economic, a
content: This study aims to analyse the implementation of the KreaSea Tumbuh Program regarding community empowerment, covering the program execution process, stakeholder involvement, community capacity building, and the resulting social, economic, and environmental impacts. The research employs a qualitative method with a case study approach. Data were analysed using the interactive analysis model developed by Miles, Huberman, and Saldana, comprising data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing. The results indicate that the KreaSea Tumbuh Program was implemented in stages, ranging from social mapping and the institutionalisation of the Wahid Sapa Women Farmers Group (KWT) to capacity building through training and mentoring, the construction of hydroponic facilities, the utilisation of solar power (PLTS), and the strengthening of sustainability through knowledge transfer and the cultivation of local heroes. The program successfully enhanced community capacity in hydroponic cultivation, strengthened community institutions, created opportunities for increasing members' income, and promoted the use of clean energy and land in a more productive manner. The findings demonstrate that CSR program implementation based on multi-stakeholder collaboration can foster sustainable community empowerment by integrating hydroponic-based food cultivation with the use of renewable energy.

title: Energy Production and Economic Feasibility of a Tidal Barrage System in the Gulf of Khambhat
source: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
summary: Rising need for clean and reliable energy has raised tidal power system interest. The large tidal range in the Gulf of Khambhat has good potential for the extraction of tidal energy. To assess the feasibility of a proposed tidal barrage usi
content: Rising need for clean and reliable energy has raised tidal power system interest. The large tidal range in the Gulf of Khambhat has good potential for the extraction of tidal energy. To assess the feasibility of a proposed tidal barrage using harmonic tidal reconstruction and dynamic basin modelling techniques for the purposes of estimating the hydraulic head, turbine discharges and the power production. Annual energy production and capacity factor are calculated, and a simulation of key design parameters is performed as a sensitivity analysis. The findings show potential for a 500 km² basin to produce ~3.44 TWh per annum, and large-scale systems may be expected to produce 15-18 TWh per annum. Economic analysis using LCOE and Monte Carlo Simulation suggests that performance improves with scale. Overall, the study shows that the Gulf of Khambhat can be a promising site for predictable tidal energy generation with proper design optimization.

title: Magneto‐Ionic Devices With Polymer‐Based Electrolytes
summary: ABSTRACT Magneto‐ionics is a promising technology for unconventional magnetic data storage and energy‐efficient computing. In magneto‐ionic devices, voltage‐triggered ionic processes are exploited to control magnetic properties of an electr
content: ABSTRACT Magneto‐ionics is a promising technology for unconventional magnetic data storage and energy‐efficient computing. In magneto‐ionic devices, voltage‐triggered ionic processes are exploited to control magnetic properties of an electrode in an electrolyte. Liquid electrolytes typically generate magneto‐ionic effects at lower voltages compared to solid electrolytes, but complicate electronic integration, posing the risk of leakage. Here, we introduce polymer electrolytes for hydroxide‐ and hydrogen‐based magneto‐ionic devices, which enable magneto‐ionic effects at voltages of ∼2 V. For the hydroxide device, a polymer separator soaked in alkaline solution, a gel polymer electrolyte, and an anion exchange membrane are combined with Fe/FeO x nanofilm electrodes. In all three cases, a large voltage‐induced decrease in magnetic coercivity up to 66% is achieved. In the hydrogen device, a proton exchange membrane is utilized to load Co/Pd multilayer electrodes with hydrogen, leading to a coercivity increase. Direct comparison to corresponding liquid magneto‐ionic devices reveals a drastically improved reversibility for the hydrogen polymer device, while the hydroxide polymer devices exhibit an increased energy efficiency by up to a factor of four. Polymer‐based electrolytes could fully replace liquid electrolytes in magneto‐ionics and enable the design of energy‐efficient devices for magnetic data storage and spintronics.

title: Assessment of Waste Minimization Strategies in Urban Residential Building Construction Projects in Ede, Osun State, Nigeria
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
summary: Construction waste remains a major challenge in urban residential building projects, particularly in developing countries where weak regulatory enforcement, informal site management, and limited site space increase waste generation. This st
content: Construction waste remains a major challenge in urban residential building projects, particularly in developing countries where weak regulatory enforcement, informal site management, and limited site space increase waste generation. This study assessed waste minimisation strategies adopted in residential construction projects in Ede, Osun State, Nigeria, focusing on major waste types and sources, strategies employed at different project stages, their effectiveness, and factors influencing implementation. A qualitative approach was adopted using semi-structured interviews with fifteen stakeholders comprising five architects, three builders, three quantity surveyors, two site engineers, and two site supervisors. Data were analysed thematically. Findings revealed that construction waste in Ede is mainly associated with design modifications, inaccurate material estimation, procurement delays, poor material handling, and unskilled labour. Concrete remnants, timber off-cuts, mortar residues, and damaged blocks were the most frequently generated waste materials. Accurate quantity take-offs, modular design, and material standardisation were identified as effective minimisation strategies during design and procurement. However, implementation during construction was inconsistent due to financial constraints, limited technical expertise, inadequate storage space, and weak regulatory enforcement. The study concludes that effective waste minimisation requires improved project planning, stakeholder coordination, professional involvement in material estimation, worker training, and stronger institutional enforcement. The findings provide context-specific insights for improving sustainable residential construction and waste management practices in Nigeria.
