This study presents the design, implementation, and empirical evaluation of an ESP32- and Internet of Things (IoT)-based dual-axis solar tracking system engineered to maximize PV power generation. The experimental setup comprises a 10 Wp monocrystalline solar module, a light-sensing array of four Light Dependent Resistors (LDRs), dual MG996R servo actuators for azimuth and elevation adjustments, and an INA219 sensor for real-time electrical telemetry. System performance was benchmarked against a stationary PV panel across a five-day field trial during effective irradiance hours (08:00–16:00 WITA). Experimental results demonstrate that the dual-axis tracker achieved a mean daily energy yield of 55.0 Wh, exhibiting a 19.7% increase compared to the fixed baseline (46.1 Wh). Nevertheless, parasitic load analysis indicates that the control electronics and motor actuation consumed an average of 3.8 Wh/day, resulting in a net energy gain of 11.1%. These findings confirm the efficacy of dual-axis tracking in enhancing solar radiation capture, while underscoring the critical need for low-power management algorithms to optimize net energy efficiency in micro-scale PV applications.

title: Lithium-ion battery impedance identification in the time domain using fractional low frequency model
summary: This paper focuses on developing a low-frequency impedance model for Lithium-ion batteries, specifically designed for time-domain identification via Chronopotentiometry (CP). This model captures the restricted diffusion impedance characteri
content: This paper focuses on developing a low-frequency impedance model for Lithium-ion batteries, specifically designed for time-domain identification via Chronopotentiometry (CP). This model captures the restricted diffusion impedance characteristic of certain cell chemistries by coupling a DC resistance 𝑅 D C with a fractional diffusion impedance in series. While the diffusion impedance can only be simulated in the frequency domain, its fractional modeling approximation allows consistent simulation in both time and frequency domains. This diffusion fractional model design allows an accurate approximation of restricted diffusion, 𝑖 . 𝑒 . a capacitor behavior at lower frequencies, shifting smoothly toward a Warburg impedance 𝑍 W ⁡ ( 𝑠 ) = 1 / ( 𝑄 W ⁢ 𝑠 0 . 5 ) at higher frequencies. Identification is validated using simulation data generated by an independent simulator that differs from the identification model; the results demonstrate that the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm yields highly accurate ˆ 𝑅 D C and ˆ 𝑄 W estimates; specifically, when subjected to realistic noise levels, the bias remains under 1% and the 1-sigma uncertainty stays below 3.2%. Finally, the model is also validated experimentally through CP experiments performed on a cylindrical 18650 Li-ion NMC cell. Across various State of Charge (SoC) levels, the estimated ˆ 𝑅 D C and ˆ 𝑄 W values demonstrate strong consistency with reference parameters obtained from Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) in the frequency domain.

title: About other ends: climate change and the urgency of new futures
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This essay explores the idea of natural disaster and climate change as an imminent threat to humankind and to the planet Earth. It highlights the need to face the consequences that change the world and to understand the entities that interc
content: This essay explores the idea of natural disaster and climate change as an imminent threat to humankind and to the planet Earth. It highlights the need to face the consequences that change the world and to understand the entities that intercede those changes; instead of looking for unique answers, points out to the importance of questions to guide shared ethical and scientific actions. Over the essay, examples of science fiction stories, that portray futuristic worlds affected by human actions, are used to give a glimpse of our own future. The importance of taking urgent measures to face climate change is also highlighted, recognizing the interconnection between climate, social and political issues. Finally, the essay proposes a careful look to the possibilities of transformation and alliance in present and future time, emphasizing the value of collaboration and care with the planet and all living things; an appeal to environment awareness and the pursuit for alternatives to mitigate climate change and protect the future of humankind.

title: Morality and climate policy attitudes
summary: This paper studies the moral roots of climate policy attitudes. We fielded a survey with a representative sample in the US to study the predictive power of moral universalism in explaining heterogeneity in specific climate policy attitudes.
content: This paper studies the moral roots of climate policy attitudes. We fielded a survey with a representative sample in the US to study the predictive power of moral universalism in explaining heterogeneity in specific climate policy attitudes. Our results reveal that universalism is significantly related to support for various policy measures that prevail in current policy debates in most countries, including domestic policies such as a carbon tax and a green infrastructure program, as well as international policies such as international burden-sharing. Supporting evidence comes from simple bystander allocation decisions in which respondents are asked to decide “who should pay” to fight climate change or to mitigate the adverse consequences of global warming. Open-text elicitations further corroborate these results and identify moral universalism as a key aspect of how people reason about climate policies.

title: Sensitivity of municipal heatwave vulnerability assessment to population density: Urban-rural spatial shifts in South Korea
summary: As heatwaves become an increasingly recurrent hazard, accurate assessment of local heatwave vulnerability has become increasingly important. This study examined the sensitivity of the heatwave vulnerability index to the inclusion of populat
content: As heatwaves become an increasingly recurrent hazard, accurate assessment of local heatwave vulnerability has become increasingly important. This study examined the sensitivity of the heatwave vulnerability index to the inclusion of population density in terms of entropy weights, relative vulnerability rankings, and spatial clustering across 251 municipalities in South Korea in 2024. Candidate indicators were compiled within the exposure-sensitivity-adaptive capacity framework, and Spearman rank correlation analysis was used to examine their empirical associations with absolute counts of heat-related illness and inter-indicator redundancy. Sensitivity to the definition of the health outcome was also assessed using the crude rate of heat-related illness per 100,000 population. Comparison of HVI1, which included population density, with HVI2, in which population density was excluded and the remaining entropy weights were proportionally renormalized, showed that population density received the highest weight in HVI1(0.44293). Among municipalities classified into Jenks classes 8–10, 49 of 61 municipalities (80.33%) under HVI1 were located in special and metropolitan cities, compared with 32 of 70 municipalities (45.71%) under HVI2. LISA analysis also showed changes in High-High clusters, with some small and medium sized cities and rural municipalities included under HVI2. Because no independent external validation was performed, these findings should be interpreted as evidence of the sensitivity of vulnerability assessment results to index specification rather than as evidence that HVI2 is relatively more accurate. Accordingly, when heatwave vulnerability assessments are used to support policy, index-sensitivity checks and follow-up local assessments that account for urban and rural contexts should be considered. Practical implications Population-based information, such as population density and absolute population size, has long played an important role in assessing spatial variations in climate vulnerability and setting policy priorities for heatwave adaptation ( Cortekar et al., 2016 ). Although this approach may support the efficient allocation of limited resources, assigning high weights to population-based indicators such as population density can alter relative vulnerability assessments between high-density urban areas and low-density rural areas depending on the index specification ( Liang and Kosatsky, 2020 ). Using South Korea in 2024 as a case study, this study found that the inclusion or exclusion of population density can alter the weighting structure of the heatwave vulnerability index, relative municipal rankings, and the geographic composition of spatial clusters. These findings provide a diagnostic basis for examining the sensitivity of vulnerability assessments to urbanization proxy indicators such as population density. From a policy and decision-making perspective, sensitivity analysis of population-density inclusion can serve as

title: Are applications of a biostimulant based on Ascophyllum nodosum able to reduce lactofen phytotoxicity in soybean plants?
summary: Abstract The herbicide lactofen, a protoporphyrinogen oxidase (PPO) inhibitor, induces phytotoxicity in soybean ( Glycine max ), which is typically characterized by the accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and subsequent degradatio
content: Abstract The herbicide lactofen, a protoporphyrinogen oxidase (PPO) inhibitor, induces phytotoxicity in soybean ( Glycine max ), which is typically characterized by the accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and subsequent degradation of the photosynthetic apparatus. This study evaluated the potential of an Ascophyllum nodosum -based biostimulant to mitigate lactofen-induced phytotoxicity in soybean. A greenhouse-based pot trial using a completely randomized experimental design was employed with five treatments: control, biostimulant only, lactofen, lactofen + biostimulant (simultaneous), and lactofen followed by biostimulant application 6 days after herbicide application (6 DAA). Photosynthetic pigment content, gas exchange, chlorophyll a fluorescence, ascorbate peroxidase (APX) activity, and phytotoxicity were assessed at the V4 phenological stage, and grain yield was obtained at the R8 phenological stage. Simultaneous application of lactofen and the biostimulant minimized total chlorophyll loss by 61.45% and significantly enhanced the effective quantum yield of photosystem II ( ϕ PSII ) and carboxylation efficiency compared to the herbicide alone. The treatment led to a 26.76% reduction in H 2 O 2 concentration, driven by an upregulation of APX activity, which preserved leaf area and increased the 100-grain weight by 28.31%. These findings suggested that biostimulant stabilized photosynthetic complexes and improved redox homeostasis in treated leaves. Conversely, the delayed application of the biostimulant (6 DAA) proved ineffective, indicating that mitigation success was highly dependent on the application timing. Thus, simultaneous foliar application of A. nodosum -based biostimulant with lactofen serves as a robust strategy for mitigating chemical stress, ensuring metabolic resilience, and stabilizing productivity in soybean cultivation.

title: ZnO and SiO2 nanopriming enhancing seedling performance and changing volatile profiles of Melissa officinalis under drought and salinity stress
summary: Introduction Melissa officinalis L. is an important medicinal and aromatic plant whose germination, seedling establishment, and secondary metabolism can be adversely affected by drought and salinity. This study investigated whether ZnO and
content: Introduction Melissa officinalis L. is an important medicinal and aromatic plant whose germination, seedling establishment, and secondary metabolism can be adversely affected by drought and salinity. This study investigated whether ZnO and SiO 2 nanopriming could mitigate these effects and modify the volatile profile of M. officinalis . Methods Two independent factorial experiments were conducted under drought and salinity stress. Seeds were hydroprimed as the control or nanoprimed with ZnO or SiO 2 at 50 or 100 mg L −1 . Drought treatments were 0, −0.2, −0.4, and −0.6 MPa, while salinity treatments were 0, 4, 8, and 12 dS m −1 . Germination and early seedling traits were evaluated. Selected 50 mg L −1 treatments under moderate stress conditions were subsequently subjected to volatile profiling by GC/GC-MS. Results Nanopriming significantly improved several germination and early seedling traits, with the strongest responses generally observed at 50 mg L −1 . ZnO at 50 mg L −1 increased germination from 42% in the non-primed control to 56% under −0.4 MPa drought and from 36% to 52% under 8 dS m −1 salinity. Low-dose ZnO and SiO 2 also improved radicle and plumule growth and seedling vigour, although their effects declined under severe stress. Eleven volatile compounds were detected in all analyzed samples, with geranial and neral as the predominant constituents. Alloaromadendrene showed the largest descriptive change, increasing from 2.4% in the control to 6.3 -6.8% in selected treatments. Because volatile analysis was performed once per selected treatment (n = 1), these compositional differences were interpreted descriptively. Discussion Low-dose nanopriming, particularly ZnO at 50 mg L −1 , improved early-stage tolerance of M. officinalis to independently imposed drought and salinity stress and was associated with changes in its volatile profile. Replicated chemical analyses and greenhouse and field experiments are required to confirm the observed volatile responses and agronomic applicability.

title: Agaricia spp. recruitment failure and subsequent recovery in the wake of mass bleaching and disease outbreak on reefs of St. Thomas, US Virgin Islands
summary: Caribbean coral reefs have declined severely under cumulative stressors including hurricanes, thermal anomalies, disease outbreaks, and local anthropogenic impacts. In early 2019, stony coral tissue loss disease (SCTLD) emerged in the north
content: Caribbean coral reefs have declined severely under cumulative stressors including hurricanes, thermal anomalies, disease outbreaks, and local anthropogenic impacts. In early 2019, stony coral tissue loss disease (SCTLD) emerged in the northern U.S. Virgin Islands (USVI), followed later that year by anomalously high temperatures and mass bleaching across the territory, providing an opportunity to assess the resilience of recruitment to acute disturbance. This study quantified recruitment at three shallow reef sites (7–14 m) in St. Thomas from 2019–2022 and compared results with pre-disturbance data (2015–2017). Recruitment tiles (15 × 15 cm) were deployed across eight time periods and photographed to determine recruit density and taxonomic identity. Bleaching and disease prevalence were calculated from coral health assessments along six 10-m transects as part of the Territorial Coral Reef Monitoring Program. All recruits observed were Agaricia spp. Recruitment rates in 2019 and 2020, following these disturbances, declined by an order of magnitude relative to pre-disturbance surveys. Because the six environmental predictors vary to differing degrees among versus within sites, their correlations with recruitment were decomposed into between-site and within-site components. Coral cover and Agaricia spp. abundance varied predominantly among sites (86.9% and 51.9% of variance between sites, respectively); their apparent positive associations with recruitment reflected differences among three site means rather than temporal variation within sites, and neither persisted once site means were removed. In contrast, Degree Heating Weeks (DHW) and combined bleaching and paling prevalence varied almost entirely within sites (8.7% and 1.3% between-site variance), and both showed marginal negative within-site relationships with recruitment (DHW: r = -0.43, p = 0.054; bleaching/paling: r = -0.41, p = 0.064). Thermal stress was therefore the only environmental variable with a detectable within-site signal, consistent with the temporal concordance between the 2019 disturbance and recruitment collapse. By 2021–2022, recruitment rebounded toward pre-disturbance levels at most sites, indicating recovery of recruitment potential within approximately two years. These findings demonstrate the sensitivity of Agaricia spp. recruitment to disturbance and underscore monitoring recruitment as a key indicator of reef resilience, as continued thermal stress and persistent disease threaten the natural recovery capacity of Caribbean reefs.

title: Cumulative impact of climate change and adaptation measures on Venice and its lagoon
summary: Abstract Adaptation measures to climate change can generate unintended environmental consequences, particularly in vulnerable coastal systems. In the Venice Lagoon, the Mose mobile barrier system was designed to protect the city from sea-le
content: Abstract Adaptation measures to climate change can generate unintended environmental consequences, particularly in vulnerable coastal systems. In the Venice Lagoon, the Mose mobile barrier system was designed to protect the city from sea-level rise and storm surges, still ensuring the lagoon-sea exchange. However, under climate change the frequency and duration of Mose closures will increase and this might modify lagoon water renewal and affect ecosystem properties. Here, we apply a high-resolution hydrodynamic model forced by downscaled climate projections to analyse trade-offs of adaptation measures by projecting lagoon conditions under two emission scenarios (RCP-4.5 and RCP-8.5) at mid (2045–2049) and end-century (2095–2099), with and without Mose operation. Results show that Mose effectively limits sea-level rise inside the lagoon, but significantly increases water renewal time (WRT). Under RCP-8.5 closures would reach ~ 248 days/year and one-third of the lagoon would require more than 20 days to renew its water. Under this scenario, extreme warming would occur, with summer temperatures higher than 30 °C for over three months per year and frequent, long-lasting marine heatwaves. Under RCP-4.5 these impacts are about halved, highlighting the critical role of global mitigation. Our findings demonstrate that while Mose can safeguard Venice from flooding, it also intensifies hydrodynamic confinement, which would combine with temperature changes to produce a severe cumulative pressure on the lagoon system. These results highlight that only the combination of complementary local measures and effective greenhouse-gas mitigation can support viable long-term adaptation pathways for coastal systems.

title: From measurement to mitigation: a historical review of livestock emission research in the U.S. Southern and Central Great Plains
summary: As airborne emissions from agricultural operations began to receive more concentrated scrutiny, the federal Task Force on Agricultural Air Quality was established in the 1996 Farm Bill and began operations in 1997 to advance research and pr
content: As airborne emissions from agricultural operations began to receive more concentrated scrutiny, the federal Task Force on Agricultural Air Quality was established in the 1996 Farm Bill and began operations in 1997 to advance research and provide solutions for sustainable agricultural operations with primary focus on particulate matter, ozone, and odors. This historical review synthesizes research conducted by institutions serving the southern and central Great Plains from the early 2000s to mid-2010s across cattle, dairy, swine, and poultry production systems, identifying three interdependent research pillars: measurement technology, emission quantification, and abatement solutions. Research priorities varied by species, with cattle and dairy operations focusing primarily on particulate matter (PM), ammonia (NH 3 ), and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, while swine and poultry studies concentrated on odor and volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Measurement technology innovations proved foundational to reliable emission science. Quantification studies established baseline emission factors essential for regulatory compliance while revealing critical temporal dynamics and environmental drivers. However, persistent knowledge gaps emerged, particularly in transferring abatement solution effectiveness from controlled laboratory conditions to commercial settings, where performance declined substantially due to extreme spatial and environmental variability. Most importantly, the research field shifted from pursuing simple pollution reduction toward systematic approaches that monitor and manage multiple pollutants. We recommend that future research must develop frameworks that systematically assess pollutant trade-offs alongside economic feasibility to enable science-based mitigation strategies balancing environmental protection with agricultural sustainability.

title: Combining digital and green technologies in regions: How to close the gap with respect to the frontier?
summary: This paper focuses on the combination of green and digital technologies at the regional level. Using patent data, we put forward an original measurement of the regional speed of a new green-digital (i.e. twin) combination: the temporal dist
content: This paper focuses on the combination of green and digital technologies at the regional level. Using patent data, we put forward an original measurement of the regional speed of a new green-digital (i.e. twin) combination: the temporal distance between the time at which a combination is realised for the first time in the frontier region and the time at which this same combination is accomplished in the focal region. We proceed by investigating the drivers and the technological impact related to this speed. We find that the speed of combination is enhanced by dealing with broad twin technologies and by recombining more diverse prior knowledge to do that. The speed at which the gap is closed, also crucially depends on the interdependencies between green and digital local domains, captured by the overlap in their regional knowledge bases. Counterintuitively, the longer their combination paths, the faster regions combine green and digital technologies. Finally, we find that the earlier the first regional green-digital combinations happen, the greater is their impact on subsequent inventions, while the impact of all regional green-digital combinations is apparently lower. Overall, these results are discussed in terms of policy recommendations, given the high attention placed by policymakers on the twin transition.

title: Effects of body cooling on aerobic exercise capacity under combined heat stress and mental fatigue
source: Journal of Human Sport and Exercise
summary: This study examined the effects of body cooling on thermoregulatory and perceptual responses during exercise under combined heat stress and mental fatigue. Seven moderately trained males completed three randomized trials: thermoneutral (22°
content: This study examined the effects of body cooling on thermoregulatory and perceptual responses during exercise under combined heat stress and mental fatigue. Seven moderately trained males completed three randomized trials: thermoneutral (22°C, CON), hot (35°C, HOT), and hot with cooling (35°C, COOL). Participants performed a cognitive task during 45 min of cycling at 50% maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max), followed by exercise at 75% VO2max until exhaustion. In COOL, participants ingested ice slurry (1.25 g/kg body mass every 5 min for 30 min) and wore an ice vest starting 40 min before exercise. Absolute time to exhaustion was shorter in HOT (441 ± 83 s) than in CON (623 ± 153 s) and COOL (571 ± 198 s), although differences were not statistically significant. Exploratory analysis showed a smaller reduction in time to exhaustion relative to CON in COOL than in HOT (92.7 ± 22.9% vs. 73.9 ± 21.3%). The increase in rectal temperature from baseline to exercise onset was lower in COOL than HOT. Mental fatigue increased following the cognitive task in all trials, with no differences among trials, and objective cognitive performance was unchanged. These findings suggest that cooling reduced thermal strain but did not significantly improve absolute aerobic exercise capacity.

title: Shifting Patterns of Precipitation Extremes in the S outheast A tlantic Basin— B razil: From Observed Trends to Future Projections
summary: ABSTRACT Understanding the variability and evolution of precipitation extremes associated with climate change is essential to support adaptation strategies, risk management, and civil protection. In this context, this study investigates the
content: ABSTRACT Understanding the variability and evolution of precipitation extremes associated with climate change is essential to support adaptation strategies, risk management, and civil protection. In this context, this study investigates the climatology, observed trends, and future projections of precipitation extremes in the Southeast Atlantic Hydrographic Basin (SAHB), a region of great socioeconomic relevance in Brazil. Daily precipitation data from 244 pluviometric and meteorological stations of the National Water and Basic Sanitation Agency (ANA) and the National Institute of Meteorology (INMET) were used, covering the period from 1980 to 2023. Precipitation extremes were evaluated using standardized indices from the Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices (ETCCDI). Trend detection and assessment in the time series were performed using the non‐parametric Mann–Kendall test and Sen's slope estimator. For the evaluation of future conditions, simulations from the EC‐Earth3 Earth system model, part of CMIP6, were used, considering the SSP2‐4.5 and SSP5‐8.5 emission scenarios for the period 2030–2100. The results indicate a significant increase in the mean rainfall intensity and a longer duration of dry periods (+4 days/decade), suggesting greater irregularity in the regional precipitation regime. Extreme precipitation events over short periods exhibit spatially heterogeneous intensification, with greater intensity in coastal and mountainous regions. Future projections indicate intensified extreme rainfall (up to +41 mm/decade in precipitation above the 95th percentile) and longer dry spells, particularly under the high‐emission scenario, suggesting greater susceptibility to hydrometeorological disasters and significant impacts on water security and territorial planning across the basin.

title: Conservation of the Properties of Equilibrium Chemical Composition Under Temperature and Pressure Variations
source: match Communications in Mathematical and in Computer Chemistry
summary: A new method is developed, allowing control of chemical equilibrium in such a way that a criterion depending on the chemical composition is constant with temperature and pressure variations. The application of the implicit function theorem
content: A new method is developed, allowing control of chemical equilibrium in such a way that a criterion depending on the chemical composition is constant with temperature and pressure variations. The application of the implicit function theorem and Kuhn-Tucker conditions allows calculating the sensitivity of chemical composition with respect to internal parameters. The equations are derived that allow calculation of the dependence between temperature and pressure under a fixed value of a linear or non-linear function of chemical composition. Numerical calculations are conducted that confirm the theoretical results.

title: Fin whale movement patterns from the Mediterranean sea reveal summer habitat use in the North Atlantic and potential feeding behavior
summary: Abstract Understanding the movements of highly mobile marine species is essential for identifying critical habitats and developing effective conservation measures. Although occasional movements of fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) betwee
content: Abstract Understanding the movements of highly mobile marine species is essential for identifying critical habitats and developing effective conservation measures. Although occasional movements of fin whales ( Balaenoptera physalus ) between the Mediterranean Sea and the North Atlantic Ocean have been reported, the extent to which these movements represent a recurrent component of Mediterranean fin whale ecology remains unclear. Here, we present satellite telemetry tracks from seven fin whales (2022–2025) with five years of supporting evidence from systematic land-based observations (2021–2025) in the western Ibiza Channel to investigate movement patterns, behavior, and habitat use beyond the North-Western Mediterranean Sea. All tracked whales left the Mediterranean Sea passing through the Strait of Gibraltar and subsequently moved northward along the Atlantic coast of the Iberian Peninsula, providing direct evidence of cross-basin movements from the Mediterranean to the North Atlantic. Behavioral analyses using two independent movement-modeling approaches identified a common pattern of directed transit followed by area-restricted search (ARS) behavior—commonly associated with foraging—in several Atlantic areas, including waters off the Iberian Peninsula and the Bay of Biscay. The occurrence of prolonged ARS behavior in these areas is consistent with the use of Atlantic feeding habitats. The similarity of movement trajectories across individuals, years, tagging locations, and data streams indicates that seasonal use of Atlantic waters may represent a regular component of the movement ecology of at least some fin whales in the Mediterranean Sea. Given that these movements span multiple jurisdictions and areas of intense maritime activity, conservation measures should consider both important feeding habitats and the migratory routes that connect them.

title: FARCLIMATE_D5.1 NBS Guidelines for the Elaboration of Projects
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Task T5.1 focuses on promoting nature-based solutions (NbS), using the IUCN Global Standard for NbS, in the technical solutions that will be developed in the FARCLIMATE project case studies. This deliverable 5.1 presents guidelines for desi
content: Task T5.1 focuses on promoting nature-based solutions (NbS), using the IUCN Global Standard for NbS, in the technical solutions that will be developed in the FARCLIMATE project case studies. This deliverable 5.1 presents guidelines for designing, identifying and applying these nature-based solutions in the different technical solutions to be implemented in the various case studies. It is tailored to the scope of the project and target sectors. It also presents a preliminary review of the technical solutions already defined or foreseen, if applicable, in the living labs.

title: Pathways for Climate Investment in Iraq: Enlil Center's summary and assessment of the technical report behind Iraq's first Climate Investment Plan
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: An Enlil Center brief by Othman Kareem, Director of Research & Policy at Enlil Center, on Pathways for Climate Investment in Iraq — Technical Investment Report (Transitional Phase I, 2025–2030), published by the National Investment Commissi
content: An Enlil Center brief by Othman Kareem, Director of Research & Policy at Enlil Center, on Pathways for Climate Investment in Iraq — Technical Investment Report (Transitional Phase I, 2025–2030), published by the National Investment Commission and the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Iraq with support from UNDP (2025). Othman Kareem (Enlil Center), working as a consultant to UNDP, was a contributing author of the technical report. The brief summarises the report's estimate that Iraq needs about US$82.85 billion of climate investment by 2030 (US$36.85 billion in priority initiatives), its sector breakdown, its emissions baseline from Iraq's first Biennial Transparency Report, and its proposed funding streams, and gives Enlil's assessment of the plan's strengths and risks. It does not reproduce the report, which remains the work and property of its publishers. Web version: https://enlilcenter.org/research/pathways-for-climate-investment-in-iraq

title: Dietary quercetin and glucoraphanin supplementation improves growth performance and modulates ruminal microbiota in meat sheep
summary: Introduction This study investigated the effects of single or combined dietary supplementation with quercetin (QUE) and glucoraphanin (GRA) on growth performance, serum antioxidant capacity and biochemical parameters, rumen fermentation, an
content: Introduction This study investigated the effects of single or combined dietary supplementation with quercetin (QUE) and glucoraphanin (GRA) on growth performance, serum antioxidant capacity and biochemical parameters, rumen fermentation, and ruminal microbiota of meat sheep. Methods A total of 60 meat sheep (3–4 months old) with similar body weights were randomly divided into four groups, with three replicates per group and five sheep per replicate, and the feeding trial lasted for 35 days. Sheep in the control group (CON) were fed a basal diet. The TG1 group was supplemented with 300 mg/kg QUE; the TG2 group with 200 mg/kg GRA, and the TG3 group with 300 mg/kg QUE plus 200 mg/kg GRA. All additives were supplemented externally without altering the nutritional composition of the basal diet. Results and discussion The results showed that dietary supplementation with quercetin (QUE) and glucoraphanin (GRA) exerted a significant interactive effect on average daily feed intake (ADFI) of meat sheep ( p < 0.05). Serum biochemical analysis revealed a significant interaction between QUE and GRA for serum ALT levels ( p < 0.05). In addition, analysis of serum antioxidant indices indicated that QUE and GRA had a significant interactive effect on serum GSH-Px activity ( p < 0.05). Notably, significant interactive effects of QUE and GRA were also observed on the relative abundances of Succiniclasticum and Ruminococcus among ruminal microorganisms ( p < 0.05). In summary, dietary supplementation of QUE and GRA improved the antioxidant capacity of meat sheep. Changes in serum indicators suggested that they might exert potentially beneficial effects on liver function. Meanwhile, the co-supplementation could modulate the relative abundance of several ruminal bacterial genera and produce certain beneficial effects on partial growth-performance and meat quality indicators of meat sheep, which provides preliminary evidence for the combined application of QUE and GRA in meat sheep production.

title: Understanding Stakeholder Engagement in Coal Transportation Governance
summary: Coal transportation in Jambi Province created traffic congestion, road deterioration, traffic accidents, environmental degradation, and conflicts between economic interests and public welfare. This study examined stakeholder engagement in r
content: Coal transportation in Jambi Province created traffic congestion, road deterioration, traffic accidents, environmental degradation, and conflicts between economic interests and public welfare. This study examined stakeholder engagement in responding to these challenges and assessed how stakeholders addressed the impacts of coal transportation. A qualitative case study approach was employed using secondary data from 39 online news articles published by 14 national and local media outlets throughout 2023, complemented by reports from environmental organizations. Data were analyzed using QDA NVivo R1 through coding, classification, and stakeholder relationship mapping. The findings identified five major stakeholder groups: central government, local government, law enforcement agencies, civil society, and business actors. Stakeholder responses remained fragmented and predominantly reactive, with greater attention to traffic congestion, road damage, traffic accidents, and dedicated coal transportation roads, while environmental degradation, pollution, and community welfare receive comparatively limited attention. This study contributed to the stakeholder governance literature by demonstrating that stakeholder engagement was not determined solely by the presence or visibility of actors, but also by the balance, coordination, and integration of their responses across governance issues. Strengthening inter-stakeholder collaboration and integrated governance was essential to balance economic development, environmental sustainability, and public interests.

title: Soil carbon measurement
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Soil carbon measurement quantifies the amount of organic carbon stored in the soil. Accurate measurement of Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) is essential for evaluating soil health, fertility, agricultural productivity, and the ecosystem's capacit
content: Soil carbon measurement quantifies the amount of organic carbon stored in the soil. Accurate measurement of Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) is essential for evaluating soil health, fertility, agricultural productivity, and the ecosystem's capacity to sequester carbon for climate change mitigation.

title: MICROBIAL AND ENZYMATIC PLASTIC BIODEGRADATION: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF STUDIES FROM THE UNITED STATES, CHINA, AND BRAZIL
summary: The widespread use of plastics, combined with low recycling rates, has intensified concerns about the accumulation of plastic waste in the environment. This integrative review aimed to examine evidence on the microbial and enzymatic biodegr
content: The widespread use of plastics, combined with low recycling rates, has intensified concerns about the accumulation of plastic waste in the environment. This integrative review aimed to examine evidence on the microbial and enzymatic biodegradation of plastics in studies published between 2015 and 2023, focusing on the United States, China, and Brazil. Articles were searched in Scopus and Web of Science, and patents were searched in the Brazilian National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI) database. After the selection criteria were applied, 45 articles and four patents were included. The studies mainly addressed the action of bacteria, fungi, and their enzymes on polymers such as polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), and polystyrene (PS). The findings indicate potential for the biodegradation of these materials, but results vary according to the polymer, microorganism, experimental conditions, and indicators used to assess degradation. The evidence comes predominantly from laboratory studies conducted under controlled conditions and does not support general claims of complete mineralization or effectiveness at a large scale. Microbial and enzymatic biodegradation is a promising research area, although its application to plastic waste management still requires more consistent assessment methods and studies under conditions closer to real-world use.

title: Understanding out-of-home food waste among young Chinese adults: a photo-elicitation study
summary: Purpose This research examines how young Chinese adults understand and negotiate responsibility for food waste when dining out at the intersection of multiple cultural values. Design/methodology/approach This paper reports on a qualitative
content: Purpose This research examines how young Chinese adults understand and negotiate responsibility for food waste when dining out at the intersection of multiple cultural values. Design/methodology/approach This paper reports on a qualitative photo-elicitation study in which 20 young adults from China were asked to take photos when dining out. Follow-up interviews were conducted to explore the story behind photos. Data were analysed using an adaptive theory approach coupled with a moral economy lens to examine how cultural norms shape action. Findings Young Chinese adults' understandings and negotiation of responsibility for out-of-home food waste are embedded within intersecting normative narratives including relational harmony, market entitlement and personal standards. The data demonstrates that, even when moral concerns against food waste exist, responsibility is negotiated across social relationships. Market-based logic further legitimises this redistribution through economic values and market exchange. Together, these intersecting norms create a situation in which responsibility is negotiated and distributed rather than individually assumed. Originality/value This study spotlights a moral-economic “responsibilisation” dilemma faced by young Chinese adults from a cultural-normative perspective and highlights the need to develop new food waste avoidance norms grounded in existing and dominant Chinese cultural norms.

title: Оптимизация жизненного цикла попутного нефтяного газа с учетом климатических метрик: экономико-технологическое исследование
summary: Декарбонизация является одним из ключевых вызовов для глобальной энергетики. Многолетнее увеличение выбросов парниковых газов и вызванное им глобальное потепление формируют растущую обеспокоенность за перспективы планеты. В ответ на этот вы
content: Декарбонизация является одним из ключевых вызовов для глобальной энергетики. Многолетнее увеличение выбросов парниковых газов и вызванное им глобальное потепление формируют растущую обеспокоенность за перспективы планеты. В ответ на этот вызов энергетические корпорации во всем мире интегрируют принципы декарбонизации в свою систему менеджмента и устанавливают целевые ориентиры по достижению нулевого углеродного следа. Формирование плана по снижению выбросов представляет собой многоэтапную задачу с уникальной спецификой для каждого предприятия. Ее содержание определяется составом производственных мощностей, используемыми технологическими процессами, структурой капиталовложений, а также нормами национального законодательства. Эффективность этого перехода напрямую зависит от государственных механизмов стимулирования и трансграничной кооперации. Совместные усилия должны быть сосредоточены на создании прототипов и внедрении технологий с низким уровнем выбросов, а также на формировании благоприятного инвестиционного климата для развития альтернативной энергетики. Кроме того, стоит отметить, что важным направлением в борьбе с изменением климата является развитие технологий по улавливанию и хранению углекислого газа. Эти технологии могут сыграть важную роль в снижении углеродных выбросов от промышленных предприятий и теплоэнергетических установок. Для российского нефтегазового сектора, характеризующегося высокой долей выбросов парниковых газов, разработка эффективных механизмов снижения углеродного следа приобретает стратегическое значение. В статье рассмотрены различные пути снижения выбросов парниковых газов, как с точки зрения технологии, так и с точки зрения экономики. Результаты исследований могут быть использованы при разработке корпоративных стратегий декарбонизации, а также при формировании государственной политики в области климатического регулирования и налогового стимулирования низкоуглеродных технологий.

title: ESG and Profitability in the Palm Oil Industry: A Literature Review
source: Best Journal of Administration and Management
summary: Profitability is a key indicator of performance for oil palm plantation companies, but long-term profitability is increasingly influenced by their ability to manage environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks and opportunities. This a
content: Profitability is a key indicator of performance for oil palm plantation companies, but long-term profitability is increasingly influenced by their ability to manage environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks and opportunities. This article presents a narrative literature review to develop an ESG-based sustainability model and examine its relationship with profitability, primarily proxied by Return on Assets (ROA). The Environmental dimension covers emissions reduction, biodiversity protection, land management, waste and water management, and sustainable production. The Social dimension encompasses worker welfare, occupational safety, community relations, human rights, and smallholder inclusion. The Governance dimension includes board oversight, transparency, risk management, compliance, and stakeholder accountability. The synthesis indicates that sustainability standards and early adoption can influence palm oil company performance, although financial impacts vary because ESG implementation involves costs alongside benefits such as operational efficiency, market access, reputation, and risk reduction. The proposed model positions ESG as a multidimensional strategic capability that influences profitability through operational efficiency, risk reduction, legitimacy, market access, and stakeholder trust. This article provides a conceptual foundation for future empirical testing of oil palm plantation companies without claiming statistical results from company data.

title: Policy and institutional drivers of climate-smart agriculture transition in Sub-Saharan Africa: a review of governance, regulation, and institutional support with implications for South Africa
summary: Climate change continues to intensify agricultural vulnerability in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), threatening food security, rural livelihoods, and sustainable agrifood systems through increasing droughts, floods, land degradation, and erratic
content: Climate change continues to intensify agricultural vulnerability in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), threatening food security, rural livelihoods, and sustainable agrifood systems through increasing droughts, floods, land degradation, and erratic rainfall patterns. Although Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) has emerged as a strategic approach for improving agricultural productivity, resilience, and environmental sustainability, its implementation across SSA remains uneven and constrained by weak governance systems, fragmented policies, inadequate institutional support, and limited stakeholder coordination. Existing studies have largely focused on technological and agronomic dimensions of CSA, with insufficient attention given to the governance and institutional factors influencing CSA transition. This study, therefore, conducted a scoping review to examine the policy and institutional drivers of CSA transition in SSA, with emphasis on governance systems, regulatory frameworks, and institutional support mechanisms. The study adopted the PRISMA-ScR scoping review framework and systematically reviewed 21 eligible studies obtained from major academic databases and institutional repositories published between 2010 and 2026. Thematic content analysis was employed to synthesize evidence on governance systems, institutional arrangements, policy coherence, climate finance, extension services, and stakeholder partnerships influencing CSA implementation. The findings revealed that effective CSA transition depends significantly on coherent policies, institutional coordination, extension systems, climate financing, land governance, and inclusive multi-stakeholder partnerships. However, institutional fragmentation, weak policy integration, inadequate financing, poor extension services, and insecure land tenure systems remain major barriers constraining CSA adoption in SSA. The study recommends strengthening policy coherence, institutional capacity, decentralized governance systems, climate financing mechanisms, and participatory governance approaches to enhance climate-resilient agricultural transformation across Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: A review of natural fiber and agricultural waste fiber-based bio-composites used in building construction
summary: Bio-composites are emerging as viable alternatives to conventional building materials owing to their renewable origin, environmental benefits, and potential to reduce the carbon footprint of the construction sector. Comprising natural fiber
content: Bio-composites are emerging as viable alternatives to conventional building materials owing to their renewable origin, environmental benefits, and potential to reduce the carbon footprint of the construction sector. Comprising natural fibers embedded within polymer matrices, these materials have attracted considerable attention within the building industry for their capacity to mitigate environmental impact while offering functional alternatives to conventional synthetic materials. This review provides a comprehensive examination of the various classes of bio-composites, their applications in building construction, mechanical properties, manufacturing processes, associated advantages and limitations, and prospects for future development. Natural and agricultural fibers such as jute, hemp, flax, sisal, bamboo, rice husk, wheat straw, and coconut coir, combined with matrices including corn starch, arrowroot, polyethylene, polypropylene, polylactic acid, and bio-based epoxy resin, are evaluated in terms of their structural and functional performance. Particular attention is given to recent advances in bio-composite fabrication, including the incorporation of novel binder systems, hybrid fiber reinforcements, and chemical surface treatments aimed at enhancing mechanical and thermal performance. The environmental benefits of bio-composites are also discussed, including reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved energy efficiency, and minimized construction waste, all of which align with the objectives of green building standards and sustainable construction practices. Nevertheless, several challenges continue to impede widespread adoption, including moisture sensitivity, variability in raw material properties, insufficient long-term performance data, and the absence of standardized testing protocols. The significant potential of bio-composites to advance sustainable construction practices, offering a practical pathway toward reducing the environmental footprint of the built environment.

title: Plasma Engineering for Carbon Capture and Greenhouse Gas Reduction
summary: Plasma engineering has emerged as an advanced and sustainable technology for carbon capture and greenhouse gas reduction in response to increasing global climate change and environmental pollution challenges. While conventional carbon mitig
content: Plasma engineering has emerged as an advanced and sustainable technology for carbon capture and greenhouse gas reduction in response to increasing global climate change and environmental pollution challenges. While conventional carbon mitigation technologies are energy intensive, expensive catalysts and complex operational systems are used, plasma-based technologies can work as efficient, flexible alternatives under optimized conditions, although energy consumption remains a challenge. Future research in plasma-based technologies for carbon management will continue to advance towards hybrid plasma-catalytic systems, and it is a promising interdisciplinary area with great potential for advancing global efforts to reduce GHGs, optimize carbon neutral energy systems, and participate in solutions for global climate change.

title: Biofertilizantes como biossistemas dinâmicos: bases conceituais, modelagem e contribuições para a sustentabilidade agroambiental
summary: Biofertilizers have become established as strategic inputs for sustainable agriculture, promoting the reuse of organic waste, improving soil fertility, and reducing environmental impacts associated with intensive livestock farming. This cha
content: Biofertilizers have become established as strategic inputs for sustainable agriculture, promoting the reuse of organic waste, improving soil fertility, and reducing environmental impacts associated with intensive livestock farming. This chapter presents an integrative approach to biofertilizers, emphasizing their physicochemical and microbiological fundamentals, anaerobic biodigestion processes, and the implications of these systems for the modeling and simulation of biosystems. Based on a theoretical and analytical review of the scientific and normative literature, the mechanisms of organic matter decomposition, the microbial dynamics involved, and the formation of an agronomically stable and biologically active effluent are discussed. The state of the art shows significant advances in agronomic, environmental, and energy studies, highlighting the increasing incorporation of mathematical models and computational simulations for performance prediction, scenario evaluation, and optimization of biodigesters. This chapter analyzes the practical applications of biofertilizers in agriculture, their impacts on mitigating greenhouse gas emissions, generating renewable energy, and strengthening family farming. Additionally, it discusses the role of kinetic, energy, and quality modeling of biofertilizers as an essential tool for understanding dynamic, non-linear, and multivariate systems. It concludes that biofertilizers, combined with biosystem modeling and simulation, constitute a robust technological alternative for agroecological transition, contributing to more efficient, resilient, and environmentally responsible production systems.

title: Structuring High-Entropy Oxides at the Nanoscale: Ordered Mesoporous (CrMnFeCoNi)Ox Thin Films for High-Performance Oxygen Evolution Reaction Catalysis
summary: The synthesis of high-entropy oxides (HEOs) with nanoscale architectures is challenging, since both the peculiar crystalline structure with statistical element occupancy and the desired nanomorphology must be controlled. Here, ordered mesop
content: The synthesis of high-entropy oxides (HEOs) with nanoscale architectures is challenging, since both the peculiar crystalline structure with statistical element occupancy and the desired nanomorphology must be controlled. Here, ordered mesoporous (spinel) (CrMnFeCoNi)Ox HEO thin films were prepared via soft-templating and dip-coating under tailored synthesis conditions, and the influence of calcination temperature on their structural evolution and alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance was investigated. Electron microscopy revealed a temperature-dependent development of an ordered mesoporous architecture with 15–20 nm pores using polyisobutylene-block-poly(ethylene oxide) (PIB-b-PEO) as structure-directing agent. Energy-dispersive spectroscopy and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy demonstrated a near-equiatomic, spatially homogeneous distribution of all transition metals at the surface and in the bulk. Transmission electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction revealed a temperature-induced transition from an amorphous to nanocrystalline cubic spinel structure at 600 °C. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated a transformation from a high-valence, defective/hydroxylated surface composition rich in Cr6+, Mn3+, Co2+, and Ni2+ species at 300–400 °C to more low-valence surface states with increased lattice-oxygen contribution at 500–600 °C. The mesoporous HEO thin film annealed at 400 °C for 5 min exhibited one of the best OER performances ever reported (η10 = 273 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and Rct = 3.9 Ω at 1.5 V vs. RHE) in alkaline electrolyte. Overall, the structural evolution and OER performance of HEO thin films follow a temperature-dependent activity trend based on the balance and interplay of surface area, crystallinity, oxygen defects, and catalytically active species at the surface, highlighting the necessity of precise control of the synthesis conditions and formulation of structure-property relationships for improving the OER performance of compositionally complex catalysts.

title: Directional centroid trajectories reveal shifting fire activity across Brazilian biomes
summary: Abstract Understanding how fire activity reorganizes across space is key to interpreting long-term interactions among climate variability, land-use change, and integrated fire management in Brazil. Yet this reorganization is difficult to re
content: Abstract Understanding how fire activity reorganizes across space is key to interpreting long-term interactions among climate variability, land-use change, and integrated fire management in Brazil. Yet this reorganization is difficult to read directly: annual maps of millions of burn scars saturate the national territory, and year-to-year spatial shifts are visually indistinguishable at that scale. We examine this as a problem of legibility, using annual burned-area centroids as a compact, macro-scale summary of the burned-area distribution and its displacement over time. Analyzing MapBiomas Fire Collection 4 from 1985 to 2024, we distinguish fires in Natural Vegetation from those in Anthropogenic Land Use, quantify the spatial separation between these contexts, and decompose national centroid trajectories into biome contributions and two interannual mechanisms: biome reweighting (changes in each biome’s share of burned area) and within-biome migration (shifts in biome centroids). Across four decades, the two contexts form distinct centroid clouds separated by a mean of 308.2 km (95% CI 304.6–312.9; range 73–499 km); a within-year permutation test rejects spatial coincidence far beyond chance, and the contexts are strongly separable along the Cerrado–Amazon axis (AUC = 0.904, 95% CI 0.845–0.958). Biome decomposition uncovers a consistent structure dominated by the Cerrado–Amazon gradient, with the Cerrado anchoring the national centroid under Natural Vegetation and the Amazon dominating under Anthropogenic Land Use. Interannual shifts show contributions from reweighting and migration, which frequently partially cancel, and context separation projects largely, though not exclusively, onto the Cerrado–Amazon axis. By reducing millions of scars to interpretable trajectories with quantified uncertainty, this framework makes a persistent biome-scale organization, invisible in the raw distribution, legible, and links national fire patterns to conservation-relevant contrasts between fire-dependent and fire-sensitive systems.

title: Biochar amendments in a California salt marsh restoration reduced denitrification and supported distinct microbial community functions
summary: Accelerated sea level rise, combined with human-induced changes to hydrology and sediment transport, threatens the long-term persistence of coastal wetlands. Sediment addition is increasingly used to enhance wetland resilience to sea level
content: Accelerated sea level rise, combined with human-induced changes to hydrology and sediment transport, threatens the long-term persistence of coastal wetlands. Sediment addition is increasingly used to enhance wetland resilience to sea level rise, and incorporating biochar, a carbon-rich material produced through pyrolysis of organic matter, may enhance carbon storage, soil function, and vegetation recovery. We examined how biochar derived from Eucalyptus spp. feedstock influenced sediment properties, microbial communities, functional potential, and nitrate reduction pathways, with particular emphasis on differences between fresh and aged biochar and effects on nitrogen processing - a recognized data gap in biochar research. Fresh biochar had no influence on denitrification rates, but aged biochar was associated with substantially lower denitrification rates (by 88%); no detectable DNRA was observed. Biochar-amended sediments exhibited subtle differences in sediment properties and microbial communities, but had higher relative abundances of Cyanobacteria and Truepera (phylum Deinococcota) as well as greater sediment carbon content than restoration sediments. Inferred decomposition-related pathways differed significantly between biochar-amended and restoration sediments (F = 3.22, p = 0.026), with lower inferred sulfate reduction and greater inferred fermentation in biochar treatments. However, biochar amendments to low-organic-matter restoration sediments were also associated with reduced denitrification, indicating potential tradeoffs between carbon storage and nitrogen removal. Additional research is needed to determine the mechanisms underlying these responses and their implications for wetland restoration.

title: Perceived Influence of Indoor and Outdoor Air Quality on Active Sawmills in Port Harcourt Metropolis Rivers State
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: The present study examined Perceived Influence of Indoor and Outdoor Air Quality on Active Sawmills in Port Harcourt Metropolis Rivers State focusing on Air Quality Status, Human Health Risk and Seasonal variations. An experimental design w
content: The present study examined Perceived Influence of Indoor and Outdoor Air Quality on Active Sawmills in Port Harcourt Metropolis Rivers State focusing on Air Quality Status, Human Health Risk and Seasonal variations. An experimental design was used with cross-sectional observation, combining field measurements with lab analysis. The areas with different levels of sawmill activity and equipment are monitored at the four main sites and the units deployed are the Aeroqol, Kestrel and Air volume mini sampler. The collection of data was conducted over a period of one year including both wet and dry seasons, to address the temporal and seasonal variations. The pollutants measured were particulate matter fractions, gas pollutants and potentially toxic elements as well as meteorological parameters. The general meteorological conditions in the study areas were similar with low wind speed, high relative humidity, moderate to high temperature and prevailing north-western wind. The strong to very strong positive correlation of wind speed with temperature and moderate negative correlation of wind speed with relative humidity suggest that the meteorological conditions are crucial in the dispersion of pollutants. The Air Quality Index (AQI) evaluation showed that the air quality at all sites was very poor. Indoor AQI values at Illabuchi ranged from 124.25 to 50 km as 988.16 (Hazardous), mainly due to the extremely high levels of ozone and carbon monoxide. The same trends were found at Mile 3, Rumuosi and Marine Base sites where the indoor AQI were around 162.89 and the hazardous AQI were as high as 833.42 in the 50 km sites. Point B had consistently Very Unhealthy AQI (average of ~240.26) because of the combined effects of PM₂.₅ (115–126), PM₁₀ (95–96) and ozone. Overall, the study demonstrates that air quality around active sawmills in Port Harcourt is severely degraded, strongly influenced by meteorology and seasonality, dominated by particulate matter, ozone, and Pb–Cr contamination, and associated with significant non-carcinogenic health risks, particularly for children.
