title: Stacking ensemble learning and SHAP analysis for predicting CO2 solubility and guiding ionic liquid design
summary: Abstract Excessive CO2 emissions constitute a primary driver of global climate change, creating an urgent need for efficient CO2 capture technologies. Ionic liquids (ILs) are considered highly promising absorbents. However, their vast chemi
content: Abstract Excessive CO2 emissions constitute a primary driver of global climate change, creating an urgent need for efficient CO2 capture technologies. Ionic liquids (ILs) are considered highly promising absorbents. However, their vast chemical space poses significant challenges for experimental screening. In this study, Morgan fingerprint descriptors were combined with a stacking ensemble learning algorithm, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was employed to develop an accurate and interpretable framework for predicting CO2 solubility. The stacking ensemble model employs the light gradient boosting machine and the backpropagation neural network as base learners. The dung beetle optimizer and the grey wolf optimizer were used to determine optimal hyperparameter combinations for these learners, while linear regression was adopted as the meta-learner to produce the final CO2 solubility prediction. The results demonstrate that the stacking ensemble algorithm achieves the highest predictive accuracy, attaining a test-set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9888, a mean absolute error of 0.0149 and a mean squared error of 0.0006. SHAP analysis further reveals that the [Tf2N] (bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)amide) anion exerts the most significant influence, followed by the alkyl chain length of imidazolium cations. Accordingly, combining the [Tf2N] anion with imidazolium cations bearing longer alkyl chains represents a promising strategy for synthesizing ILs with high CO2 absorption efficiency.

title: Follow the e-riders: Travel behaviour change processes among e-bike adopters using a mixed-methods approach
summary: Electric-assisted bicycles (e-bikes) represent a key example of how emerging technologies can influence travel patterns and broader sustainability transitions. While existing studies have examined motivations, substitution patterns, and beh
content: Electric-assisted bicycles (e-bikes) represent a key example of how emerging technologies can influence travel patterns and broader sustainability transitions. While existing studies have examined motivations, substitution patterns, and behavioural impacts of e-bike adoption, limited evidence is available on the processes through which individuals adapt their travel behaviour after adoption. Moreover, the predominant reliance on either quantitative or qualitative approaches has constrained the ability to capture both statistical generalisation and context-specific behavioural mechanisms. This study addresses these gaps by employing a mixed-method approach to identifying the individual behaviour change process of e-bike adopters in Denmark. The analysis combines four waves of an online panel survey of 967 individuals intending to adopt an e-bike with before-and-after semi-structured interviews conducted with a subsample of 9 participants. Survey participants either adopted or did not adopt e-bikes, and their travel behaviour measures, motivational-attitudinal profiles, and interview narratives before and after potential adoption are used to understand how and why e‑bikes can support modal shifts and what conditions prevent behaviour change.

title: Optimizing Plant and Soil Response to Drought Conditions via Biochar, Fertilizer, and Chitosan Amendments: A Taguchi-Based Study
summary: Water availability can alter the effectiveness of soil amendments, yet responses to biochar, fertilizers, and biostimulants under water stress remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of biochar, chitosan oligosaccharide (
content: Water availability can alter the effectiveness of soil amendments, yet responses to biochar, fertilizers, and biostimulants under water stress remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of biochar, chitosan oligosaccharide (COS), and mineral fertilizer on substrate properties and kale growth under well-watered (WW) and water-stress (WS) conditions. A Taguchi L9 orthogonal array was implemented using sand as a simplified low-fertility substrate. Volumetric water content (VWC), pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and shoot dry biomass were evaluated. Biochar was the dominant factor affecting water retention under both irrigation regimes. Increasing biochar levels raised VWC from approximately 13% to > 95% under WW conditions and from 20% to 74% under WS conditions. Biochar also increased substrate pH from approximately 6.5 to 7.4 under WW conditions and from 6.7 to > 10 under WS conditions, indicating pronounced alkalinization at the highest application level. Fertilizer exerted the strongest influence on biomass under WW conditions and produced the largest increases in EC, whereas its effect on biomass was not significant under WS conditions. COS had comparatively smaller effects on water retention and biomass but significantly influenced substrate pH. Taguchi signal-to-noise analysis revealed shifts in factor hierarchy, with fertilizer ranking highest for biomass under WW conditions and biochar ranking highest for biomass and VWC under WS conditions. Overall, greater biochar-mediated water retention did not translate into greater biomass, emphasizing the need to balance hydrological benefits against changes in substrate chemistry when developing amendment strategies for water-limited, coarse-textured systems.

title: Effects of Straw Return and Soil Amendments on Methane Emissions During Early Anaerobic Incubation of Paddy Soil
source: RSF Conference Series Engineering and Technology
summary: Rice paddies are one of the largest global sources of anthropogenic methane (CH₄), and straw return can intensify emissions by supplying decomposable carbon and promoting reducing conditions. However, amendment-specific responses to rice st
content: Rice paddies are one of the largest global sources of anthropogenic methane (CH₄), and straw return can intensify emissions by supplying decomposable carbon and promoting reducing conditions. However, amendment-specific responses to rice straw-induced CH₄ emissions under anaerobic conditions remain insufficiently understood. A 15-day laboratory incubation experiment was conducted using 6 treatments: control (CK), straw only (S), straw combined with biochar (S+Bio), zeolite (S+Zo), CuSO₄ (S+Cu), and FeCl₃ (S+Fe), with three replicates. Flooded paddy soil was incubated at 25°C, and CH₄ flux, soil pH, electrical conductivity (EC), oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), dissolved H₂, and temperature were measured on days 0, 7, and 15. Results showed that straw return increased CH₄ emissions compared to CK, whereas amendment effects changed markedly over time. On day 7, S+Fe reduced CH₄ flux by 91.9% relative to S, the strongest early-stage suppression, but reversed by day 15 to the highest CH₄ flux among amended treatments. S+Bio and S+Zeo instead showed greater suppression at day 15 than at day 7, while S+Cu achieved the highest average suppression (45.2%) across the 15-day incubation. CH₄ was negatively correlated with ORP (r=-0.63, p<0.001) and positively correlated with dissolved H2 (r=0.69, p<0.001), confirming the central role of soil redox status in CH₄ production. These findings demonstrate that amendment effectiveness during post-harvest straw decomposition is strongly time-dependent, highlighting the need to evaluate mitigation performance across the full decomposition period rather than at a single time point.

title: Introductory Chapter: The Future of Boundary Layer Control Techniques
summary: The thin layer of fluid flow near the surface that contains the shearing forces is a crucial aspect of fluid dynamics and aerodynamic optimization. The manipulation of this layer results in a change in the overall behavior, such as the lift
content: The thin layer of fluid flow near the surface that contains the shearing forces is a crucial aspect of fluid dynamics and aerodynamic optimization. The manipulation of this layer results in a change in the overall behavior, such as the lift and drag forces. This control mechanism is critical in various engineering applications, from enhancing the lift on aircraft wings to reducing drag on high-speed vehicles. This chapter summarizes the latest control mechanisms at both lab-scale and engineering application scales. Beyond the theories, the chapter also considers socio-economic benefits and perspectives.

title: Water management and cropping pattern for rice cultivation in acid sulfate soils: A hydrological regimes and soil properties-based framework
summary: In tidal freshwater wetlands (TFW) dominated by acid sulfate soils (ASS), spatial variability in hydrological regimes and soil properties creates complex biogeochemical constraints that can reduce crop yield or lead to crop failure.Despite
content: In tidal freshwater wetlands (TFW) dominated by acid sulfate soils (ASS), spatial variability in hydrological regimes and soil properties creates complex biogeochemical constraints that can reduce crop yield or lead to crop failure.Despite this heterogeneity, water management practices are frequently applied uniformly across TFW landscapes, overlooking the combined effects of hydrological and soil variability on crop growth and productivity.This paper synthesizes the scientific basis to develop a site-specific framework for water management and cropping patterns of rice (Oryza sativa L.), explicitly considering spatial variability in both hydrological regimes and soil properties.Our synthesis reveals that water management should be tailored to hydrological regimes and soil properties to enable optimal implementation of rice cropping patterns.In frequent flooding areas, water management aims to control excess water and saline intrusion by low dike construction equipped with stoplogs.In areas that are flooded only during spring tides, water management aims to maintain water quality through regular flushing by low dike construction equipped with channel networks with a one-way flow system, flap gates, and stoplogs.In non-flooded areas, water management aims to create sustained flooding by retaining rainfall and runoff through the construction of low dikes and the installation of stoplogs.These water management systems are designed to improve soil properties while respecting inherent site conditions, thereby supporting double cropping with superior rice varieties for increased production.

title: Influence of an oregano-based essential oil on growth performance and carcass traits of beef steers
summary: Abstract The objective of this study was to determine the influence of an oregano-based essential oil on growth performance, health outcomes, and carcass characteristics of yearling beef steers finished in an all-natural program. Single-sou
content: Abstract The objective of this study was to determine the influence of an oregano-based essential oil on growth performance, health outcomes, and carcass characteristics of yearling beef steers finished in an all-natural program. Single-sourced yearling steers [N = 128; initial body weight (BW) = 335 ± 7.9 kg] were allotted to 16 pens (n = 8 pens/treatment with 8 steers/pen). Steers were blocked by pen location in a randomized complete block design (n = 8 blocks total). Treatment groups consisted of 1) control group fed no oregano-based essential oil product (CON) and 2) a group fed 4 g/steer daily of By-O-Reg+ Beef (Advanced Ag Products, Canton, SD; OEO). Steers were individually weighed on d 0 (arrival), d 38, d 66, d 108, and d 149 for growth performance measures. Steers were transitioned from a 70% concentrate diet to a 90% concentrate diet over the first 14 d and remained on the finishing diet until d 149. The finishing diet provided 1.37 Mcal/kg of NEg. Steers were evaluated daily for indications of disease or visible digestive disorders by a trained technician blinded to the treatments. Steers were harvested at a commercial packing facility when they reached a common compositional endpoint determined by visual assessment. Prior to carcass chilling, hot carcass weight and liver score was recorded for each carcass. Following chilling, ribeye area, 12th rib backfat thickness, marbling score, USDA Quality grade, USDA Yield grade, and instrumental color (L*, a*, b*) were recorded. Health outcomes were not influenced by dietary treatment (P ≥ 0.18). Inclusion of OEO did not influence (P ≥ 0.73) carcass-adjusted final BW, dry matter intake, average daily gain, gain:feed, observed dietary net energy for maintenance (NEm) or net energy for gain (NEg), observed-to-expected dietary NEm or NEg. No differences (P ≥ 0.30) were observed between treatment groups for carcass traits or the distribution of USDA Yield and Quality Grades (P = 0.94 and P = 0.79 respectively). Collectively, growth performance, health, and carcass traits of steers finished in an all-natural program in this experiment were not influenced by dietary inclusion of an oregano-based essential oil feed additive.

title: When perception meets reality: explaining measured food waste through consumer behavior in a university dining hall
source: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
summary: Food waste (FW) in university dining halls generates significant environmental and economic impacts, yet most studies rely on self-reported measures and rarely combine behavioral perceptions with objective waste data. This study investigate
content: Food waste (FW) in university dining halls generates significant environmental and economic impacts, yet most studies rely on self-reported measures and rarely combine behavioral perceptions with objective waste data. This study investigates the determinants of consumer FW by integrating individual plate-waste measurements with behavioral and dining-related factors in a university dining hall setting. Data were collected from 422 diners using a 31-item questionnaire, along with individual measurements of avoidable plate waste after meals. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Kruskal–Wallis tests were applied to examine behavioral relationships and differences across demographic and meal-related groups. Average plate waste reached 51.5 g per person, with higher waste levels observed during lunch and among female diners. Self-perceived waste behavior, intention to reduce FW, and sensory satisfaction were directly associated with the measured amount of discarded food. In contrast, consumer knowledge, portion size perception, and available eating time influenced only perceived waste behavior, revealing a disconnect between awareness and objectively measured PW. The findings highlight the importance of dining context and meal satisfaction in shaping consumer FW and demonstrate the value of integrating subjective perceptions with objective waste measurements. By combining behavioral evidence with direct waste quantification, this study advances methodological approaches to consumer FW research and provides insights for designing more effective waste reduction strategies in institutional food services.

title: Insights from co-design for relational policy-making: Farm animal health and welfare policy in the UK
summary: IMPACTThis article offers practical lessons for policy-makers working in contested, low-trust environments. It shows that co-design can build trust only when participation is supported by relational practices such as shared leadership, peer
content: IMPACTThis article offers practical lessons for policy-makers working in contested, low-trust environments. It shows that co-design can build trust only when participation is supported by relational practices such as shared leadership, peer challenge and clear principles of engagement. It also highlights a common risk in public administration: trust generated during the co-design process can quickly erode if delivery systems, fiscal rules and organizational structures are not aligned with what was agreed. The findings therefore suggest that governments should invest not only in co-design processes, but also in the institutional conditions to enable collaborative innovation needed to carry relational commitments into implementation and throughout the full policy cycle leading to a long-term sector transformation.

title: Chemical Speciation and Source Apportionment of PM 2.5 in Greek Urban and Suburban Areas: Insights from the PANACEA Initiative
summary: Abstract. This study, conducted under the PANhellenic infrastructure for Atmospheric Composition and climatE chAnge (PANACEA), examines PM₂.₅ chemical speciation and source apportionment across five Greek cities (Athens, Ioannina, Patras, V
content: Abstract. This study, conducted under the PANhellenic infrastructure for Atmospheric Composition and climatE chAnge (PANACEA), examines PM₂.₅ chemical speciation and source apportionment across five Greek cities (Athens, Ioannina, Patras, Volos, and Xanthi) representing urban background, urban, and rural environments. Sampling was conducted during summer (June to August 2019) and winter (December 2019 to February 2020), complemented by an earlier campaign at Athens Thissio (December 2018 to August 2019), yielding over 545 24-hour PM₂.₅ samples. Filters were analyzed for major and trace elements, water-soluble ions, organic carbon (OC), and elemental carbon (EC). Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) was applied separately for each site using a harmonized protocol. Seven source categories were identified across the network: biomass burning (16.2 % to 50.9 %), heavy oil combustion (2.5 % to 15.1 %), industrial emissions (3.3 % to 14.4 %), mineral dust (4.8 % to 16.4 %), sea salt (1.6 % to 11.7 %), secondary sulfates and organics (7.1 % to 33.0 %), and vehicular traffic (9.7 % to 27.6 %). Campaign-average PM₂.₅ concentrations in Ioannina and Volos remained above 25 μg m⁻³, pointing to severe air pollution burdens and a high risk of non-compliance with European standards. The high spatial and temporal variation in source contributions reveals that while regional background pollution strongly influences PM₂.₅ levels, localized anthropogenic activities, and particularly wintertime biomass burning for residential heating, remain a critical driver of urban air quality degradation in Greece.

title: Analysis of urban heat islands in the study of urban environmental problems based on remote sensing
summary: As global urbanization accelerates cities increasingly face ecological challenges, most notably the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. This study investigates the formation and spatial distribution of UHI’s in the cities of Mingachevir, Shirva
content: As global urbanization accelerates cities increasingly face ecological challenges, most notably the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. This study investigates the formation and spatial distribution of UHI’s in the cities of Mingachevir, Shirvan and Yevlakh, located in the central region of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Utilizing ArcGIS, the analysis processed Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS satellite imagery from August 2023. The analysis revealed that, despite their relatively small size, distinct urban heat islands have formed in the studied cities. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of satellite-based methods for identifying urban heat islands and can be used to support urban planning, environmental monitoring, and climate adaptation strategies in the region. The results indicate a strong correlation between urban urban density and thermal concentration, with LST values in urban cores reaching up to 42 °C, which is 2 °C higher than the surrounding rural landscapes. Analysis reveals that industrial zones and areas with low albedo surfaces (asphalt and concreate) are primary drivers of thermal intensity in these cities. To mitigate these effects, the study recommends the implementation of “cool roofs”, the expansion of urban green corridors, and the integration of permeable pavements into local zoning laws. These findings provide a quantiative framework for urban planners and environmental policymakers in Azerbaijan to develop targeted climate adaptation strategies and improve urban thermal comfort.

title: Intraoperative ventilation settings in Germany: an observational multicentre cross-sectional study
source: Canadian Journal of Anesthesia/Journal canadien d anesthésie
summary: Intraoperative lung protective ventilation and, in inhalational anesthesia, minimal fresh gas flow (FGF) are recommended. It remains unclear how these recommendations are transferred to clinical routine. We aimed to assess corresponding ane
content: Intraoperative lung protective ventilation and, in inhalational anesthesia, minimal fresh gas flow (FGF) are recommended. It remains unclear how these recommendations are transferred to clinical routine. We aimed to assess corresponding anesthesia practices in Germany and raise awareness of optimal ventilation settings. We performed a pragmatic prospective observational national cross-sectional assessment of intraoperative ventilation settings in Germany, followed by an educational intervention and follow-up assessment. The intervention consisted of a pocket card designed in a Delphi-process. The patient-centred primary endpoint was tidal volume (V T )·kg −1 ideal body weight (IBW), and the environment-centred primary endpoint was FGF in inhalational anesthesia. In a post hoc analysis, we grouped departments into quintiles of baseline V T and FGF, and explored changes after the intervention. Over 240 of 1,148 anesthesiology departments participated (21%). We collected data from 2,198 operating rooms in the first (preintervention) and 2,106 in the second (postintervention) assessment (96% response rate). The mean (standard deviation) V T ·kg −1 IBW was 7.4 (1.4) mL in the first assessment vs 7.3 (1.3) mL in the second assessment. The median [interquartile range (IQR)] FGFs were 0.60 [0.50–0.85] L·min −1 vs 0.50 [0.45–0.75] L·min −1 , respectively. Exploratory multilevel regression analysis did not show an effect of the intervention. In the anesthesiology departments whose baseline ventilation settings were in the highest quintile, the intervention was associated with improvements in both V T and FGF. This large-scale clinical study of intraoperative ventilation settings in Germany found that most anesthesiologists already followed current recommendations. Therefore, for the entire cohort, no major improvements were observed. The educational intervention might improve ventilation settings in anesthesiology departments whose baseline practice deviates strongly from current recommendations.

title: Transparent wood integrated with transparent solar photovoltaic panels for enhanced building energy performance and economic benefits
summary: In modern buildings located in cooling load-dominant climates, achieving low energy consumption while maintaining sufficient daylighting through skylights presents a significant challenge. This study focused on the novel attempts to integra
content: In modern buildings located in cooling load-dominant climates, achieving low energy consumption while maintaining sufficient daylighting through skylights presents a significant challenge. This study focused on the novel attempts to integrate Transparent Wood (TW) with Transparent Solar Photovoltaic Module (TSPV), which allows for both electricity generation and reduction in thermal loads while maintaining transparency. In this experimental study, heat gain and illumination levels were measured within a small-scale building model that consists of skylight openings. The skylight materials evaluated included TW from balsa, poplar, pine, and bamboo, each integrated with Transparent Solar Photovoltaic (TSPV) systems exhibiting different transmittance levels of 0%, 20%, 40%, and 60%. A total of 21 samples were tested for heat gain and illuminance. Additionally, theoretical calculations were used to determine operational costs, cost savings and CO 2 emission mitigations. Results show that TSPV 1 (TSPV using TW of Balsa) provided the highest illuminance in all the levels of transparency, whereas TSPV 4 (TSPV using TW of Bamboo) provided more cost savings among the investigated glazings in 60% transperancy levels. The lowest annual heat gain in 60% transparency of TSPV 4 was 371.78 kWh/m 2 , and the operating cost was 8.50 $/m 2 /year, which resulted in savings of 34.09 $/m 2 /year (with power generation) and reduced carbon emission by 0.058 tCO 2 /year. The results indicate that this solution would be a viable replacement for skylight glazings that would generate electricity and regulate the amount of heat gain.

title: Synergy and comprehensive evaluation of biochar-based biogas residue fertilizer for enhancing yield and quality of greenhouse cucumber
summary: The application of engineered organic amendments is crucial for advancing sustainable greenhouse vegetable production.This study evaluated the effects of a biochar-based biogas residue fertilizer (BRC) on cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) in a
content: The application of engineered organic amendments is crucial for advancing sustainable greenhouse vegetable production.This study evaluated the effects of a biochar-based biogas residue fertilizer (BRC) on cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) in a greenhouse system.Eight fertilization treatments were applied, including different N levels and combinations with chemical fertilizers.These included a control group with no fertilization (CK), conventional chemical fertilizer (CF), biogas residue from cow manure (BR), biochar-based biogas residue without chemical fertilizer (BRC), biogas residue mixed with chemical fertilizer (CB), and biochar-based biogas residue combined with chemical fertilizer (CBC).The results indicated that BRC significantly enhanced cucumber physiological performance: It increased the average growth rate by 21.95% compared to the unamended control and improved root activity by up to 46.34% relative to CF.Although the highest cucumber yield was achieved under sole high-rate biogas residue (BR-34), BRC treatments increased yield relative to conventional chemical fertilization (CF-34) and markedly improved N use efficiency by 109.27%.Notably, BRC improved fruit quality by elevating vitamin C and soluble protein contents while significantly reducing nitrate accumulation.A fuzzy mathematics-based comprehensive evaluation confirmed that CBC-34 (combined BRC and mineral fertilizer treatment) achieved the highest overall fruit quality score of 0.73.The synergistic effect between biochar and biogas residue likely moderated nutrient release and improved rhizosphere conditions.This work reveals that sole BRC application delivers outstanding N retention capacity, whereas CBC-34 balances nutrient supply, crop growth and fruit quality; thus CBC-34 is the optimal integrated fertilization regime for sustainable greenhouse cucumber production.

title: LOCC-GER - A georeferenced local climate policy database for Germany
summary: Local climate action has increased massively worldwide. Germany is a noteworthy case in this respect, as local measures have been strongly promoted by the federal system over the past two decades. However, studying policies, their determina
content: Local climate action has increased massively worldwide. Germany is a noteworthy case in this respect, as local measures have been strongly promoted by the federal system over the past two decades. However, studying policies, their determinants, and consequences at this scale has been difficult so far due to a lack of centralized data. This article introduces LOCC-GER, the largest existing dataset of georeferenced local climate policy-making in Germany. The dataset currently covers 26,142 measures from 5,033 municipalities, including detailed descriptions of employed measures, funding sum, and duration from 2008 to 2023. It is extended with important local context variables on public opinion and civil society activities, as well as detailed weather and climate indicators. We demonstrate how it can be used to map and analyze local governments' actions on climate change. Finally, we discuss how LOCC-GER may be extended by academics and other users through our proposed workflow for user-specific linking with additional covariates, offering high spatial and temporal flexibility.

title: Mangroves in Managing Microbial Infections and Resistance
summary: Mangroves are among the highly productive and ecologically crucial blue-carbon ecosystems, occurring along the coastal intertidal zones of the globe. These unique environments exert a huge impact in mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and m
content: Mangroves are among the highly productive and ecologically crucial blue-carbon ecosystems, occurring along the coastal intertidal zones of the globe. These unique environments exert a huge impact in mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and maintaining ecological equilibrium, particularly under the escalating challenges of climate change. These brackish ecosystems are rich in biodiversity and provide immense ecological and economic benefits, especially to coastal communities. Historically, mangrove plants were explored in traditional medicine for their antimicrobial features to treat infections, promote wound healing, and address various skin disorders. Key secondary metabolites isolated from mangroves and their endophytic bacteria and fungi include alkaloids, flavonoids, phenolic acids, terpenoids, and tannins. These compounds, as well as various extracts, exhibit promising antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral properties, including A. corniculatum, A. marina , B. gymnorhiza , C. tagal, R. mangle , S. alba, X. granatum , and other species. Research has demonstrated efficacy against E. coli , S. typhimurium , P. aeruginosa , V. cholerae , Staphylococcus spp ., Streptococcus spp ., Mycobacterium spp., and other species. Besides, antifungal as well as antiviral activities were also proven toward a panoply of fungi and viruses. The main underlying mechanisms of mangrove&s;s antimicrobial action include (i) impediment of cell wall synthesis, (ii) alteration of microbial membranes, and (iii) enzyme inhibition. Hence, with the rise of antibiotic resistance, exploring natural antimicrobial compounds derived from mangrove plants and their endophytic microorganisms has gained significant importance in drug development.

title: ASSESSING THE FACTORS INFLUENCING PRIVATE VEHICLE OWNERS’ INTENTION TO PAY PROPOSED CONGESTION FEES IN GEORGE TOWN, PENANG: A THEORY OF PLANNED BEHAVIOUR
summary: Penang was identified as the most congested city in Malaysia in 2024, primarily due to the influx of tourists in George Town, which contributed to high greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, the Penang State government proposed becoming the f
content: Penang was identified as the most congested city in Malaysia in 2024, primarily due to the influx of tourists in George Town, which contributed to high greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, the Penang State government proposed becoming the first state to implement a congestion fee. However, limited information was available regarding the stakeholders’ intentions towards congestion fees. Accordingly, the research aimed to determine the relationship between attitude, subjective norms (SN), perceived behavioural control (PBC), and intention to pay a congestion fee. Questionnaires were utilised to collect responses from 440 respondents through stratified sampling in George Town, involving residents of Penang and domestic tourists. The results of multiple regression analysis indicated that the constructs of the Theory of Planned Behaviour (Attitude, SN, and PBC) had significant and positive relationships. These findings provided valuable insights for the State Government and the Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department in designing effective congestion fee implementation strategies, which were aligned with the National Transport Policy 2021-2030 and SDG11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities).

title: Spatially uneven impacts of stratospheric aerosol injection on compound dry-heat wave events in the GeoMIP G6sulfur experiment
summary: Abstract. Compound dry-heat wave (CDHW) events, characterized by the joint occurrence of extreme heat and dry conditions for at least three consecutive days, pose substantial risks to ecosystems, agriculture, and human societies. However, t
content: Abstract. Compound dry-heat wave (CDHW) events, characterized by the joint occurrence of extreme heat and dry conditions for at least three consecutive days, pose substantial risks to ecosystems, agriculture, and human societies. However, the implications of stratospheric aerosol injection (SAI) for such compound extremes, particularly at regional scales, remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate changes in CDHW frequency, duration, and severity under the GeoMIP G6sulfur scenario relative to the high-emission SSP5-8.5 scenario using simulations from three Earth system models. We find that SAI substantially offsets the projected intensification of CDHWs over global land, with marked reductions in their frequency, duration, and severity. However, this mitigation is highly heterogeneous: Central Africa emerges as a prominent regional hotspot where CDHWs become more persistent in all three models and, while their frequency also increases under the percentile-based dry-day criterion, primarily in MPI-ESM1-2-LR. The enhancement is driven mainly by the dry side of the compound: dry spells lengthen in all three models (by 0.2–0.9 days per event) and the number of hot-and-dry days per summer rises, even though the total number of heat wave days falls in two of the three models, whereas the intensity of the individual compound events is reduced, consistent with the overall cooling. Comparison with SSP2-4.5 scenario, which has a global-mean radiative forcing comparable to that G6sulfur, indicates that the enhanced CDHW response over Central Africa is not driven by the greenhouse gas forcing component alone. The reduction in greenhouse gas forcing alone produces little change in CDHW exposure over Central Africa, whereas SAI reduces surface shortwave radiation and evaporation over tropical land, promoting mid-tropospheric subsidence and reductions in cloud cover, precipitation, and soil moisture over the region. The contrasting response over the Amazon Basin, where CDHWs decrease, is largely explained by the greenhouse gas component. Reduced greenhouse gas forcing substantially alleviates the projected drying over the Amazon but provides no comparable benefit over Central Africa, where aerosol-specific drying dominates. These hydroclimatic changes are further coupled with declining soil moisture and reduced latent heat flux, partly offsetting the SAI- induced cooling and favoring persistent heat extremes. Our results demonstrate that reducing global mean warming through SAI does not necessarily translate into uniform reductions in compound climate extremes, highlighting the importance of distinguishing the removal of greenhouse gas forcing from aerosol-specific effects, and of land-atmosphere interactions when assessing the climate risks and regional trade-offs of solar climate intervention.

title: A Highly Proton-Tolerant Multicenter Borane/Phosphazene Catalytic System for Efficient PO/CO2 Copolymerization toward CO2-Based Poly(carbonate-ether) Polyols
summary: Low-molecular-weight CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols from ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of propylene oxide (PO) with CO2 are highly desired as soft blocks to synthesize sustainable polyurethanes. However, such process remain
content: Low-molecular-weight CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols from ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of propylene oxide (PO) with CO2 are highly desired as soft blocks to synthesize sustainable polyurethanes. However, such process remains great challenges because of the demanding of highly proton-tolerant catalysts. Herein, we report a binary organocatalysis system based on a nanoscopic multicenter borane Lewis acid (POSS-B8) combined with various organobases for the tunable ROCOP of PO and CO2. The confined POSS-B8 framework not only endows excellent tolerance to proton but enables cooperative activation of PO and CO2, thereby facilitating PO/CO2 ROCOP while effectively suppressing the formation of cyclic propene carbonate (cPC). Remarkably, the binary system can tolerate high loadings of chain-transfer agents (up to 400 equivalents), affording low-molecular-weight polycarbonate polyols (0.6 kDa) with narrow dispersity (Ð = 1.16). By tuning POSS-B8 loading and CO2 pressure, both the carbonate content (19-64 mol%) and glass transition temperature (-58.6 to 4.7 °C) of resulting polymers can be modulated. This metal-free and tunable platform offers a versatile strategy for the preparation of CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols with controlled structure and strong potential for industrial applications.

title: Combining stated and revealed preferences to define smallholder cattle breeding objectives in northwest Ethiopia: Evidence for breeding program design
summary: Identifying high-priority traits is essential for designing effective breeding programs in smallholder systems. This study employed both stated and revealed preference methods to identify priority traits for cattle breeding objectives among
content: Identifying high-priority traits is essential for designing effective breeding programs in smallholder systems. This study employed both stated and revealed preference methods to identify priority traits for cattle breeding objectives among smallholders in northwest Ethiopia. Stated preferences were assessed using a discrete choice experiment (DCE), while revealed preferences were examined through a hedonic pricing approach. The two datasets were analyzed separately and their results compared to provide complementary insights. Data were collected between January and April 2024: 384 farmers participated in the choice survey across three districts (Farta = 91, Simada = 133, and Lay Gayint = 160), and 200 cattle transactions were recorded in three marketplaces-Debre Tabor, Simada, and Nefas Mewucha. Choice data were analyzed with a mixed logit model, and market data with a log-linear ordinary least squares regression. Results showed both convergence and divergence in trait preferences between methods. Farmers' strong preference for large body size in the DCE (p < 0.001) aligned with the significant positive effects of body condition and live body weight on market price (p < 0.001). However, traits not visually observable at sale-such as milk yield, docility, disease tolerance, libido, calving interval, and calf vigor-were highly valued in stated preferences but not captured in market prices due to observability constraints and information asymmetry. Conversely, the hedonic model revealed market structure effects not captured by the DCE, including higher prices paid by traders and premiums for slaughter animals. These findings demonstrate that employing both methods provides a more comprehensive evidence base for defining breeding objectives-capturing both invisible livelihood-critical traits valued by farmers and market dynamics that shape real-world prices. The identified priority traits provide a foundation for subsequent research to estimate genetic parameters and economic weights to design a breeding program.

title: Non-Excessive Natural Resource Use and Sustainable Development: The Indigenous Environmental Wisdom of Lubuk Larangan
summary: Sustainable development has guided global environmental governance for nearly four decades, yet continuing environmental degradation indicates persistent limitations in its implementation. This article examines whether clearer normative lim
content: Sustainable development has guided global environmental governance for nearly four decades, yet continuing environmental degradation indicates persistent limitations in its implementation. This article examines whether clearer normative limits on natural resource use can strengthen sustainable development. It explores the Indonesian customary institution of Lubuk Larangan and identifies the principles of non-excessive utilization, sufficiency, and simplicity embedded in its Indigenous environmental wisdom. Using a normative juridical method, the study analyzes legal instruments, scholarly literature, and published ethnographic research through historical, systematic, and sociological interpretation. It argues that sustainable development becomes more difficult to achieve when profit-driven production and non-essential consumption exceed reasonable human needs and ecological limits. The article proposes non-excessive utilization, sufficiency, and simplicity as general principles of environmental law, while distinguishing them from concrete legal obligations, policy directions, and ethical commitments. Non-excessive utilization requires natural resource use to remain within both reasonable human needs and the carrying and regenerative capacities of ecosystems. The complementary principles of sufficiency, simplicity, and sharing further connect sustainable consumption with environmental responsibility and social justice. Where these principles have not been recognized in positive law, they are presented as a normative framework for legal reform rather than as existing legal obligations. The article concludes that integrating these principles into environmental law and natural resource governance could strengthen sustainable development by aligning economic activity with ecological limits, intergenerational equity, and Indigenous environmental wisdom.

title: Green Sukuk and Climate Budget Tagging for Sustainable Infrastructure Development
summary: General Background: Sustainable finance and climate-responsive fiscal policy are central to Indonesia’s transition toward a green economy and the financing of environmentally oriented public projects. Specific Background: Green Sukuk provid
content: General Background: Sustainable finance and climate-responsive fiscal policy are central to Indonesia’s transition toward a green economy and the financing of environmentally oriented public projects. Specific Background: Green Sukuk provides thematic Islamic financing for environmentally sustainable projects, while Climate Budget Tagging (CBT) identifies and monitors state-budget allocations for climate change mitigation and adaptation. Knowledge Gap: Previous studies have addressed Green Sukuk and green budgeting, whereas their joint contribution within a single empirical framework for Indonesian public infrastructure requires further assessment. Aims: This study analyzes Green Sukuk and CBT in relation to sustainable infrastructure development in Indonesia. Results: Panel data from seven ministries during 2018–2024 were estimated using a Fixed Effect Model. Green Sukuk and CBT jointly explained 89.86% of variation in sustainable infrastructure development. Green Sukuk recorded a positive coefficient of 0.037332, while CBT produced a substantially larger positive coefficient of 1.005269. The ministry-specific intercepts were negative, indicating declining development in the absence of these financing and budgeting mechanisms. Novelty: The study integrates thematic Islamic finance and climate-specific fiscal allocation within one ministry-level panel model. Implications: The findings support coordinated use of Green Sukuk and CBT for green project financing, climate-budget planning, transparency, accountability, and climate-oriented public expenditure. Highlights: Fiscal allocation recorded the substantially larger regression coefficient. Thematic Islamic financing showed a positive association with public green projects. Seven ministries displayed negative intercepts without the two funding mechanisms. Keywords: Sustainable Finance, Green Sukuk, Fiscal Instrument, Climate Budget Tagging, Sustainable Development

title: Navigating the in-between: Contradictions in transitioning service ecosystems
summary: While research on change in service ecosystems has expanded considerably, one specific type of process—transitions—has received comparatively limited attention. This gap is consequential, as transitions are critical for addressing systemic
content: While research on change in service ecosystems has expanded considerably, one specific type of process—transitions—has received comparatively limited attention. This gap is consequential, as transitions are critical for addressing systemic problems, including sustainability challenges. More specifically, little is known about the nature of contradictions—coexisting yet opposing elements—within these processes. Addressing this gap, we conduct an abductive qualitative study of a transitioning energy service ecosystem, which surrounds a European utility firm. Our findings reveal the individual-level struggles that actors experience amid service ecosystem transitions, especially when the contradictions within transitions go unrecognized or unmanaged. We extend prior research on service ecosystem change in two ways: by conceptualizing contradictions as inherent to transition processes emerging from interactions between coexisting prevailing and emerging service ecosystem states, and by identifying four types of contradictions that further detail the systemic conditions actors must navigate amid transition processes.

title: Integrating the economic valuation of ecosystem services for sustainable futures: methodological variability, scale effects, and policy implications
summary: This study analyzed how valuation methods and spatial scale influence reported ecosystem service values. A systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines and the PICO approach screened 222 articles from the Scopus database (2016–2
content: This study analyzed how valuation methods and spatial scale influence reported ecosystem service values. A systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines and the PICO approach screened 222 articles from the Scopus database (2016–2025); after applying rigorous inclusion criteria, 38 studies were selected. Results reveal substantial methodological variability. Sum-based Total Economic Value (TEV) aggregation assigns 71.45% of total value to forests and vegetation; however, sensitivity analysis shows that this dominance is driven by a single macro-scale outlier. Median-based estimates are up to three orders of magnitude lower, indicating that robust central metrics are more appropriate than arithmetic sums for cross-study comparisons. Regulating services account for 19.47% of aggregated values, cultural services for 8.63%, and water resources for only 0.13% at local and regional scales. Cost-based methods yield the highest monetary estimates by capturing large-scale damage mitigation, whereas stated preference methods report substantially lower values ​​due to budget constraints. Regional estimates also vary by up to 23% because of differences in accessibility and beneficiary density. These findings have important policy implications. Ecosystem service valuations used in cost-benefit analyses, conservation prioritization, and environmental planning should avoid sum-based TEV aggregations because they can be dominated by extreme outliers and lead to biased resource allocation. Instead, policymakers should prioritize robust indicators such as medians and value ranges and explicitly account for spatial scale, beneficiary density, accessibility, and local socioeconomic conditions when evaluating green-blue infrastructure, ecosystem restoration, and conservation investments. Monetary valuation disparities reflect both methodological and contextual factors relevant to sustainable environmental decision-making.

title: Bioclimatic optimization for medium density housing in Jakarta transit oriented developments through microclimate simulation
summary: Rapid urbanization and the expansion of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) in tropical megacities often overlook the microclimatic experience of pedestrians, leading to severe Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects and thermal discomfort. This stu
content: Rapid urbanization and the expansion of Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) in tropical megacities often overlook the microclimatic experience of pedestrians, leading to severe Urban Heat Island (UHI) effects and thermal discomfort. This study introduces and computationally evaluates the Bioclimatic Transit-Infill Housing (BTIH) concept, a medium-density housing model with minimum parking, located at the Blok A Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station in Jakarta, Indonesia. By reallocating space from parking infrastructure to communal green areas and passive design, the proposed model seeks to improve thermal comfort for last-mile commuters. This study utilized Autodesk Forma to simulate critical microclimate parameters, including sun exposure, wind aerodynamics, and acoustic propagation, cross-referenced with calculated Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) and Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) metrics. Baseline analysis indicated extreme thermal stress (UTCI reaching 39 °C) and stagnant wind velocity (< 1 m/s). Conversely, predictive simulations of the BTIH suggest that subtractive geometric massing optimizes wind flow within the layout. Furthermore, the podium functions as an architectural shading facade, with theoretical WBGT values tracking near 29.45 °C, while acoustic strategies reduced rail noise to below the 55 dB residential threshold. This study, operating within the boundary assumptions and default settings of Autodesk Forma and its calculations, provides an early-stage simulation-based design evaluation rather than a field-validated environmental assessment. By acknowledging that these predictive results are not calibrated against on-site meteorological data or field measurements, this research demonstrates that integrating quantitative building physics into early-stage massing offers a comparative relative framework for localized microclimatic mitigation.

title: Coupling Redox-Active Prussian Blue Analogue Electrode with Membrane Bioelectrochemical System for Simultaneous Ammonium and Potassium Extraction from Wastewater
summary: Abstract Recovering ammonia and potassium from wastewater is important for sustainable nutrient management and pollution mitigation. Membrane bioelectrochemical systems (MBESs) offer a promising approach for simultaneous recovery of ammoniu
content: Abstract Recovering ammonia and potassium from wastewater is important for sustainable nutrient management and pollution mitigation. Membrane bioelectrochemical systems (MBESs) offer a promising approach for simultaneous recovery of ammonium (NH4+) and potassium (K+) from waste streams, although achieving distinct separation between these nutrient ions remains challenging. To address these limitations, this study aimed to improve reactor selectivity toward NH4+ and K+ to enhance nitrogen recovery while replacing the conventional oxygen reduction reaction with a solid-state electrode to reduce the aeration energy consumption. Here, we couple an ion-selective redox-active cathode based on Prussian blue analogues, potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate (KNiHCF), with a microbial fuel cell to evaluate ion intercalation behaviors and simultaneously recover NH4+ and K+ from synthetic wastewater. More electrons were produced to intercalate cations with the Na+-based catholyte than the Mg2+-based one. In most catholyte solutions, the electrode showed a preferential uptake of K+ and NH4+. The transport numbers indicated that the initial catholyte background cations (Na+ or Mg2+) played a critical role in facilitating transport of the target cations from the anolyte to the catholyte. When NH4+ was initially present in the catholyte, more than 60% of electrode occupancy corresponded to NH4+. These results demonstrate that catholyte composition strongly influences ion transport and selectivity in KNiHCF-coupled MBES systems.

title: Carbon-intensive development and undernourishment in Africa: the role of non-hydro renewable energy in the climate–food security nexus
summary: The study examines the relationship between carbon-intensive development, non-hydro renewable energy and undernourishment in 27 African countries between 2002 and 2021. The study focuses on whether non-hydro renewable electricity can reduce
content: The study examines the relationship between carbon-intensive development, non-hydro renewable energy and undernourishment in 27 African countries between 2002 and 2021. The study focuses on whether non-hydro renewable electricity can reduce the link between greenhouse gas emissions and food insecurity in Africa. The analysis follows several stages. First, descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, panel unit-root tests and cointegration tests were conducted to evaluate the distributional properties, relationships, stationarity and long-term behavior of the variables under study. Secondly, a two-step System Generalized Method of Moments estimator was applied to a balanced panel of 540 observations in order to address the persistence of undernourishment, potential endogeneity, reverse causality and unobserved country-specific effects. Model reliability is then evaluated using Arellano–Bond serial correlation tests, Hansen and Sargan overidentification tests, and difference-in-Hansen tests of instrument exogeneity. The findings generally indicate that undernourishment is persistent and strongly influenced by structural, energy-related, demographic, environmental and economic factors. Dependence on fossil fuel-based electricity and continued population growth was associated with deteriorating food security outcomes, whereas the adoption of renewable energy and economic growth show potential to improve food security. The interaction term results between greenhouse gas emissions and renewable energy suggested that high carbon intensity may limit the food security benefits of expanding renewable energy. These findings emphasize the importance of integrated policies that accelerate decentralized investment in renewable energy, reduce dependence on fossil fuels and greenhouse gas emissions while strengthening climate-resilient agriculture and improving rural energy access. Lastly, coordinating energy, agricultural, climate, and population policies is essential for achieving sustainable development goals 2 and 7 in Africa.

title: Insights Into Mg 2+ ‐Driven Lattice Stabilization and Na + Kinetics Regulation in O3‐Type NaMn 0.5 Fe 0.5 O 2 Cathodes for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as cost‐effective alternatives to lithium‐ion systems owing to the natural abundance of sodium. Among layered cathodes, O3‐type NaFe 0.5 Mn 0.5 O 2 exhibits high theoretical capacity and env
content: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) are emerging as cost‐effective alternatives to lithium‐ion systems owing to the natural abundance of sodium. Among layered cathodes, O3‐type NaFe 0.5 Mn 0.5 O 2 exhibits high theoretical capacity and environmental compatibility but suffers from structural degradation driven by O3→P3 transitions, volume variation, and transition‐metal migration during cycling. Herein, Mg 2+ is incorporated to regulate the lattice stability and electrochemical performance of NaFe 0.5 Mn 0.5 O 2 via grain boundaries/interface difustion at solid state. The sample Mg4‐NFM was synthesized via a solid‐state route and systematically characterized. The x‐ray diffraction combined with Williamson–Hall analysis reveals Mg‐induced lattice modulation, micro‐strain regulation, and crystallite‐size variation, while SEM, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, and BET measurements provide complementary insights into morphology, bonding, vibrational characteristics, and surface properties. Electrochemical evaluations demonstrate that the 0.48 At% Mg atoms in the hybrid sample deliver the optimal performance, achieving an initial discharge capacity of 83.3 mAh g − 1 with excellent capacity retention over 100 cycles at 0.1C and Coulombic efficiency exceeding 98.5%. Density functional theory calculations reveal that Mg incorporation enhances thermodynamic stability and increases the density of states near the Fermi level, indicating improved electronic conductivity. Furthermore, nudged elastic band calculations identify an ultralow Na + diffusion barrier of 0.113 eV, confirming favorable ion‐transport kinetics.

title: Assessment of Impact of Cement Industry on Surface and Ground Water Quality
source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
summary: This study aims to assess the impact of the cement industry on surface and groundwater quality. The research focuses on a specific cement plant location Athwajan Srinagar J&K and evaluates the physico-chemical parameters of water samples co
content: This study aims to assess the impact of the cement industry on surface and groundwater quality. The research focuses on a specific cement plant location Athwajan Srinagar J&K and evaluates the physico-chemical parameters of water samples collected from various points around the plant. Parameters such as pH, temperature, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, total dissolved solids, hardness, calcium, alkalinity, sulphate, nitrate, fluoride, chloride, and iron are analyzed to determine the extent of pollution. The study employs a combination of field surveys, laboratory analysis, and statistical methods to compare water quality between areas affected by cement industry emissions and control sites. The findings will highlight the adverse effects of cement industry activities on surface and groundwater quality, including potential health risks for local communities and ecological impacts. The objective is to provide a comprehensive understanding of the environmental implications of cement production and to identify strategies for mitigating these impacts. This research will contribute to the development of sustainable practices in the cement industry and inform policy decisions aimed at protecting water resources and public health.

title: Are economic diversification and bank-based financial development associated with CO2 emissions in Saudi Arabia? Evidence from a NARDL model
source: Arab Gulf Journal of Scientific Research
summary: Purpose This study examines asymmetric associations between economic diversification, bank-based financial development and per-capita CO2 emissions in Saudi Arabia, a hydrocarbon-dependent and electricity-intensive economy undergoing struct
content: Purpose This study examines asymmetric associations between economic diversification, bank-based financial development and per-capita CO2 emissions in Saudi Arabia, a hydrocarbon-dependent and electricity-intensive economy undergoing structural transformation under Vision 2030. Design/methodology/approach Using annual data for 1995–2020, converted to quarterly observations through quadratic-match average interpolation, the study estimates a nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) model. Economic diversification is measured by the Economic Complexity Index and bank-based financial development by private-sector bank credit. The model controls for electricity consumption, GDP per capita, industrial activity, urbanization and trade openness. Positive and negative changes in diversification and bank-based financial development are decomposed to estimate distinct short- and long-run associations with CO2 emissions. Findings Positive diversification changes are associated with lower CO2 emissions in the short run but higher emissions in the long run. Positive bank-based financial-development changes are associated with higher emissions across both horizons. Negative changes in both variables display distinct short- and long-run adjustment patterns. Electricity consumption and trade openness are positively associated with emissions, urbanization is negatively associated with emissions and GDP per capita and industrial activity are statistically insignificant. Originality/value The study jointly examines economic complexity and bank-based credit in a Saudi Arabian NARDL framework. As quarterly observations are interpolated from annual data, short-run estimates require cautious interpretation. The findings represent conditional asymmetric associations rather than causal effects or direct evidence of sectoral, technological, or policy mechanisms.

title: Agricultural blockchain readiness environment and carbon emission intensity in maize production: evidence from provincial panel data in major maize-producing areas of China
summary: China’s major maize-producing regions face the joint challenge of sustaining food production and reducing agricultural emissions. Existing research on digital agriculture often uses broad digitalization measures and therefore does not disti
content: China’s major maize-producing regions face the joint challenge of sustaining food production and reducing agricultural emissions. Existing research on digital agriculture often uses broad digitalization measures and therefore does not distinguish the regional conditions that may enable information management, traceability, and verification applications associated with blockchain. This study constructs an Agricultural Blockchain Readiness Environment Index (ABRE Index, block_index) using entropy weighting across digital infrastructure, the agricultural industrial base, and policy support. The index measures regional readiness and enabling conditions rather than realized blockchain adoption. Using 180 province-year observations for 12 major maize-producing provinces from 2010 to 2024, we estimate two-way fixed-effects models with province-clustered inference and conduct supplementary robustness analyses. The ABRE Index is negatively associated with carbon emissions per unit of maize-sown area, with the baseline coefficient statistically significant at the 10% level under conventional clustered inference and supported by supplementary inference procedures. The coefficient remains negative in all 12 leave-one-out specifications, is statistically significant at the 10% level or better in 10 specifications, and the wild cluster bootstrap test yields p = 0.0415. The index is positively correlated with blockchain-related patent activity ( r = 0.1883, p = 0.0114), although this correlation does not establish that the index measures realized adoption. The mechanism analysis is consistent with an organizational pathway through agricultural socialized services: the ABRE Index is positively associated with service_ratio (0.1099, p < 0.01), and agricultural socialized services are negatively associated with ce_area (−2.2765, p < 0.05). The interaction with the high-development indicator is negative but does not reach the conventional 10% significance threshold (−0.1499, p = 0.103). Overall, the evidence supports an associational relationship between blockchain-readiness conditions and maize-production carbon-emission intensity; it does not establish a strictly causal effect of blockchain adoption.

title: Carbon Balance in the Atmosphere through Forest Growth and the Utilization of Wood Products - By Comparing Scenarios with and without the Use of Forest Products
summary: This study evaluates the atmospheric CO2 balance of Cryptomeria japonica (Japanese cedar), plantations in Japan over a 200-year period, explicitly considering temporal carbon dynamics associated with forest growth, harvesting, decay, and th
content: This study evaluates the atmospheric CO2 balance of Cryptomeria japonica (Japanese cedar), plantations in Japan over a 200-year period, explicitly considering temporal carbon dynamics associated with forest growth, harvesting, decay, and the use of harvested wood products (HWPs). Two simplified systems were compared: (1) a forest utilization system, in which plantations are cyclically managed, harvested every 50 years, and the harvested wood is used for wooden buildings and wood fuel; and (2) a non-forest utilization system, in which forests are left unharvested while steel-frame buildings and fossil fuels substitute for HWPs. The results show that the forest utilization system performs substantially better in climate-change mitigation, with a 200-year atmospheric CO2 balance of 171.6 t-CO2eq./ha, compared with 2,552.5 t-CO2eq./ha for the non-forest utilization system. Sensitivity analysis further indicates that longer building lifetime enhance mitigation by delaying carbon release. The study concludes that cyclical plantation use and long-lived wooden buildings are important strategies for reducing atmospheric CO2 in Japan.

title: Hydrological Extremes Increase Water‐Resource Constraints Under Climate Change
summary: Abstract Hydrological extremes are projected to intensify under climate change, yet their implications for water scarcity remain poorly understood. We use a multi‐model ensemble to assess how changes in hydrological low and high extremes wi
content: Abstract Hydrological extremes are projected to intensify under climate change, yet their implications for water scarcity remain poorly understood. We use a multi‐model ensemble to assess how changes in hydrological low and high extremes will constrain renewable water for human use across 520 major river basins worldwide. We evaluate trends in two metrics of water availability: (a) annual lowest monthly runoff, and (b) annual accessible runoff, a conceptual indicator defined as total runoff excluding extreme high flows typically released rapidly for flood control. More than 40% of river basins are projected to experience declines in both metrics during 2015–2100. Mediterranean and several scattered basins are identified as hotspots where runoff reductions compound existing water scarcity. Scenario comparison shows that low emission mitigates, though do not fully eliminate, these declines, highlighting hydrological co‐benefits of climate mitigation. The novelty lies in explicitly incorporating hydrological extremes into water availability assessment.

title: Climate Patent Portfolios (% of all technologies)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

content: Climate patent portfolios as percentages of all technologies for 38 OECD countries, 2000 to 2022. Built from OECD ENV Tech data using fractional inventor country attribution. Seven mitigation dimensions: energy generation (CCMTPPG), grid regulation (CCMTREGTD), waste management and water treatment (CCMTRWTWM), carbon capture and storage (CSSDGG), buildings (CCMTRB), transport (CCMTRT), and ICT for energy management (CCMICT).

title: ปญหาวาดวยสทธทจะไมถกผลกดนกลบของผพลดถนขามพรมแดนในบรบทของการเปลยนแปลงสภาพภมอากาศ
summary: วิทยานิพนธ์เรื่อง “ปัญหาว่าด้วยสิทธิที่จะไม่ถูกผลักดันกลับของผู้พลัดถิ่นข้ามพรมแดนในบริบทของการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศ” มีวัตถุประสงค์ในการสำรวจความคุ้มครองระหว่างประเทศภายใต้หลักการห้ามการส่งกลับ (non-refoulement) โดยจะศึกษาถึงความเป็นไปไ
content: วิทยานิพนธ์เรื่อง “ปัญหาว่าด้วยสิทธิที่จะไม่ถูกผลักดันกลับของผู้พลัดถิ่นข้ามพรมแดนในบริบทของการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศ” มีวัตถุประสงค์ในการสำรวจความคุ้มครองระหว่างประเทศภายใต้หลักการห้ามการส่งกลับ (non-refoulement) โดยจะศึกษาถึงความเป็นไปได้ของการมีอยู่ของสิทธิที่จะไม่ถูกผลักดันกลับของผู้พลัดถิ่นข้ามพรมแดนอันเนื่องมาจากการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศบนพื้นฐานของสถานะผู้ลี้ภัย , บนพื้นฐานของหลักการห้ามการทรมาน และการปฏิบัติหรือการลงโทษที่โหดร้าย ไร้มนุษยธรรม หรือที่ย่ำยีศักดิ์ศรี และบนพื้นฐานของสิทธิในชีวิต เพื่อนำมาปรับใช้กับการให้ความคุ้มครองผู้พลัดถิ่นข้ามพรมแดนในบริบทของการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศ โดยจะศึกษาและวิเคราะห์หลักการห้ามการส่งกลับที่มีอยู่ในกฎหมายผู้ลี้ภัยระหว่างประเทศและกฎหมายสิทธิมนุษยชนระหว่างประเทศใน 3 ประเด็นดังนี้ 1. เพื่อศึกษาและวิเคราะห์ว่าผู้พลัดถิ่นข้ามพรมแดนอันเนื่องมาจากการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศถือเป็นผู้ที่มีคุณสมบัติในการได้รับสถานะเป็นผู้ลี้ภัย ตามข้อ 1A (2) ภายใต้อนุสัญญาว่าด้วยสถานภาพผู้ลี้ภัย ค.ศ. 1951 และภายใต้พิธีสารว่าด้วยสถานะของผู้ลี้ภัย ค.ศ.1967 หรือไม่ และรัฐมีหน้าที่ต้องให้ความคุ้มครองระหว่างประเทศแก่บุคคลดังกล่าวภายใต้หลักการห้ามการส่งกลับ ตามอนุสัญญาว่าด้วยสถานภาพผู้ลี้ภัย ค.ศ. 1951 และ พิธีสารว่าด้วยสถานะของผู้ลี้ภัย ค.ศ. 1967 หรือไม่จากการศึกษาพบว่า บุคคลที่จะได้รับความคุ้มครองภายใต้หลักการห้ามการส่งกลับบนพื้นฐานของสถานะผู้ลี้ภัยต้องเป็นบุคคลที่มีคุณสมบัติเป็นผู้ลี้ภัยตามข้อ 1 (A) (2) ของอนุสัญญาว่าด้วยสถานภาพผู้ลี้ภัย ค.ศ. 1951 กล่าวคือ จะต้องเป็นบุคคลที่มีความหวาดกลัวที่แท้จริงว่าหากต้องถูกส่งกลับไปยังประเทศต้นทางจะต้องถูกประหัตประหารด้วยสาเหตุทางเชื้อชาติ ศาสนา สัญชาติ ผู้พลัดถิ่นข้ามพรมแดนอันเนื่องมาจากการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศซึ่งชีวิตและสุขภาพตกอยู่ในอันตรายหรือความเสี่ยงอันเนื่องมาจากสถานการณ์ทางสิ่งแวดล้อมเพียงอย่างเดียว โดยไม่มีการกระทำที่เป็นการข่มเหงจากรัฐหรือบุคคลอื่นที่ไม่ใช่รัฐอันเนื่องมาจากสาเหตุทางเชื้อชาติ ศาสนา สัญชาติ สมาชิกภาพของกลุ่มทางสังคม หรือความคิดเห็นทางการเมืองร่วมอยู่ด้วย ดังนั้นจึงยังไม่มีความเป็นไปได้ของการมีอยู่ของสิทธิที่จะไม่ถูกผลักดันกลับของผู้พลัดถิ่นข้ามพรมแดนอันเนื่องมาจากของการเปลี่ยนแปลงสภาพภูมิอากาศบนพื้นฐานของสถานะผู้ลี้ภัย2. title: Investigating Key Technologies and Vulnerabilities for the Electricity System in the Yukon, Canada
summary: Abstract Planning electricity systems under conditions of deep uncertainty hinders the already challenging task of meeting growing electricity demands while aligning with sustainability objectives. In this work we use an ensemble of three a
content: Abstract Planning electricity systems under conditions of deep uncertainty hinders the already challenging task of meeting growing electricity demands while aligning with sustainability objectives. In this work we use an ensemble of three analyses (frequency of technology appearance across modelled scenarios, importance of uncertainty in affecting decisions, value of technology deployment options to adapt to uncertainty) to identify system vulnerabilities and identify prospective generators that support sustainability outcomes for a case study in the Yukon, Canada for a planning horizon of 2022 to 2050. Building upon a modelling framework we previously developed that couples Monte Carlo simulation with a form of myopic foresight to simulate cost-minimizing capacity expansion decisions, we assess how specific prospective generators and accompanying system uncertainties contribute to either robust or risky outcomes for key metrics including cost and socio-environmental indicators. Our findings suggest rising demand, higher peak loads, and early retirement of a hydroelectric dam are key risks to the Yukon’s electricity system. We find demand-side management programs and pumped hydro storage most frequently have potential to contribute to reducing costs and greenhouse gas emissions. Counterintuitively, the operational flexibility and small physical footprint of diesel generation enable it to be a frequent contributor to improve cost and social and ecological outcomes. Conversely, under the range of conditions modeled, the model indicates wind, solar, liquefied natural gas, and renewable thermal technologies are non-optimal in a large proportion of modeled futures. This study highlights specific vulnerabilities and generation assets that can assist electric utilities and system planners in making robust decisions for planning expansions to the Yukon’s electricity system.

title: Comparative Greenhouse Gas Implications of Wood Pallet Valorisation Pathways in Island Territories
summary: Island territories face structural constraints in waste management, including limited land availability, high dependence on imported goods, and restricted recycling infrastructure. In this context, waste wooden pallets represent a relevant
content: Island territories face structural constraints in waste management, including limited land availability, high dependence on imported goods, and restricted recycling infrastructure. In this context, waste wooden pallets represent a relevant but underexplored lignocellulosic stream, particularly in import-dependent economies. This study compares the greenhouse gas implications of two end-of-life routes for waste wooden pallets in La Réunion: slow pyrolysis for biochar production and incineration with energy recovery. The assessment adopts a functional unit of 1 t of pallets received for treatment and focuses exclusively on the end-of-life treatment stage, excluding collection and transport processes. The pyrolysis route was modelled using primary operational data from a local plant, whereas the incineration route was based on published inventory data normalized to the same functional unit and adapted to local energy conditions. Results indicate that both routes can provide net climate benefits, although through different mitigation mechanisms. Pyrolysis achieved a net climate balance of -527.64 kg CO2 eq t–1, mainly driven by stable carbon storage in biochar, while incineration reached -602.23 kg CO2 eq t–1 due to avoided emissions from recovered heat and electricity. These findings suggest that pallet pyrolysis may offer a promising end-of-life strategy for geographically constrained territories by combining waste treatment, carbon storage, and the production of a potentially useful material output. Future work should expand the assessment to a full life cycle perspective, including pallet production, reuse cycles, biochar application, substitution effects, and uncertainty related to biochar permanence and energy transition scenarios.

title: Landscape Architecture and Health: An Umbrella Review
source: Journal of Healthy Eating and Active Living
summary: Landscape architecture influences environmental conditions related to health, but evidence on how design features impact health is scattered across disciplines. The review aims to assess the evidence, identify pathways to health, and guide
content: Landscape architecture influences environmental conditions related to health, but evidence on how design features impact health is scattered across disciplines. The review aims to assess the evidence, identify pathways to health, and guide collaboration between landscape architects and public health professionals. Following PRISMA and JBI Umbrella Review guidelines, systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Academic Search Complete, and GreenFILE. Exposures included landscape design features, while outcomes captured pathways such as instoration, restoration, mitigation, adaptation, and direct health effects. The review is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251058826). Fifty-six systematic reviews and meta-analyses were included, covering 2,654 studies, most published from 2021 to 2025. Frequently, landscape types included parks, forests, recreational spaces, streetscapes, health gardens, and educational landscapes. Instoration pathways consistently increased physical activity and active transportation. Restoration pathways improved social inclusion, particularly in hospital gardens and green schoolyards. Mitigation pathways demonstrated reductions in heat and noise and improved thermal comfort. Adaptation pathways such as green roofs and other green infrastructure reduced heat stress and supported outdoor use. Reported health outcomes included improved psychological well-being, some cardiometabolic benefits, and reduced behavioral symptoms in clinical contexts; however, the quality of the evidence remains limited. Findings indicate that landscape architecture practice can improve health by encouraging physical activity and social cohesion, but climate mitigation and adaptation have been less studied. Despite standards that promote active living and climate resilience, systematic evaluation of health-focused landscape projects remains lacking. Collaboration between health and design is necessary to create evidence-based landscapes that enhance health and environmental quality.

title: Reducing Agricultural Emissions and Building Climate Resilience: Impact Case Study
summary: This report highlights the impacts of research to reduce agricultural greenhouse gas emissions and build climate resilience.Agriculture’s role in climate change is a priority issue for Aotearoa New Zealand. Agriculture accounts for about ha
content: This report highlights the impacts of research to reduce agricultural greenhouse gas emissions and build climate resilience.Agriculture’s role in climate change is a priority issue for Aotearoa New Zealand. Agriculture accounts for about half of our total greenhouse gas emissions, much more than the average contribution of around 10% in other developed countries. Climate change science is therefore a priority for the Bioeconomy Science Institute. Our science is focussed on the areas of most importance, and where we can make the most significant contribution, to our environment and the society and economy it supports.The Bioeconomy Science Institute leads science on climate change reduction, mitigation and adaptation for pastoral agriculture in Aotearoa New Zealand. Its long-term investment in greenhouse gas emissions research creates practical solutions with substantial benefits, reducing methane and nitrous oxide emissions, building climate resilience, and delivering environmental benefits, without compromising productivity or profitability. The combined economic benefits of just three of its research programmes are estimated at $2.4 billion, demonstrating the significant return on investment from greenhouse gas emissions research that addresses environmental challenges and presents economic opportunities for Aotearoa New Zealand’s agricultural sector.

title: Artificial Photoreforming Technology for Plastic Waste Valorization
summary: The escalating depletion of fossil fuels, rising greenhouse gas emissions, and pervasive plastic pollution pose unprecedented threats to the environment and human well-being, underscoring an urgent need for sustainable and clean resource re
content: The escalating depletion of fossil fuels, rising greenhouse gas emissions, and pervasive plastic pollution pose unprecedented threats to the environment and human well-being, underscoring an urgent need for sustainable and clean resource recycling technologies. Solar-driven photoreforming of plastic waste simultaneously generates value-added chemicals, fuels, and carbon materials. Conceptually, this process resembles an artificial photosynthesis system, wherein solar energy serves as the driving force, photocatalysts function as active media, and waste plastics act as the feedstocks. However, the practical efficacy of photoreforming is limited by the extent of plastic pretreatment, the activation ability of inert C─X bonds, and the selectivity toward desired products. This review focuses on the state-of-the-art in solar-driven photoreforming technologies for plastic conversion, offering a comprehensive analysis from fundamental reaction mechanisms to practical implementation. In particular, this review highlights the essential role of in situ characterization in uncovering reaction mechanisms and thereby guiding the construction of efficient reaction systems. Furthermore, key bottlenecks are identified, current mitigation strategies are assessed, and priority research directions are outlined for advancing the sustainable "photosynthesis" of plastic waste.

title: Modeling freshwater use for direct lithium extraction from geothermal brines in the Salton Sea
