Evidence on mineral-associated carbon clarifies mechanisms but does not convert unfilled stabilisation capacity into an immediately attainable mitigation budget. Apparent disagreement among studies frequently reflects differences in sampling depth, equivalent soil mass, controls, duration and the distinction between measured and modelled outcomes. Nitrous oxide, methane, displaced biomass uses and subsequent management reversals can materially change the climate balance. A defensible implementation strategy therefore separates soil restoration from offset certification, prioritises locally feasible management packages and combines repeated stock measurements with independently evaluated models. Long-term, multi-depth experiments that jointly measure carbon, greenhouse gases, yields and resource costs are the highest research priority. Soil carbon management is a conditional, finite and valuable complement to emissions reduction, not a substitute for it.

title: Plant Protein-Based Scaffolds for Cultivated Meat Production: A Review
summary: This review summarises recent progress in the development of plant protein-based scaffolds for cultivated meat production, with a particular focus on protein sources derived from major agricultural crops and their processing into functional
content: This review summarises recent progress in the development of plant protein-based scaffolds for cultivated meat production, with a particular focus on protein sources derived from major agricultural crops and their processing into functional biomaterials. We discuss how protein extraction strategies, as well as emerging technologies, influence protein purity, functionality and suitability for scaffold fabrication. Current fabrication approaches, such as extrusion, freeze-drying, electrospinning, hydrogels and composite polymer systems, are examined in relation to their ability to generate three-dimensional, food-grade scaffolds with appropriate mechanical properties, porosity and cell compatibility. Key challenges and future research directions are also addressed, including the optimisation of plant protein-based scaffolds to support muscle cell adhesion, proliferation and differentiation, as well as the need for improved reproducibility and practical scalability. Overall, this contribution highlights the strong potential of plant protein-based materials to enable scalable cultivated meat production while reducing environmental impacts and reliance on animal-derived components.

title: The Effect of Pre-oxidation on the Hydrogen Reduction of Magnetite Ores at 973 K: Role of Particle Size and Gangue Chemistry
summary: This study systematically investigates the effects of controlled pre-oxidation on hydrogen-based reduction of three industrial magnetite ores, distinguished by their gangue chemistries (CaO, negligible gangue, and MgO), and examines two par
content: This study systematically investigates the effects of controlled pre-oxidation on hydrogen-based reduction of three industrial magnetite ores, distinguished by their gangue chemistries (CaO, negligible gangue, and MgO), and examines two particle size fractions. Pre-oxidation behavior showed a strong particle size dependence, with particles of the fine fraction achieving the target oxidation degree significantly faster than the relatively coarse fraction. Pre-oxidation universally improved reducibility, with the enhancement magnitude inversely correlated to the residual magnetite content. Kinetic analysis using absolute and normalized reduction rates, along with novel kinetic descriptors, revealed that pre-oxidation fundamentally altered reduction pathways by broadening the active reduction window and delaying diffusion limitations of the later part of wüstite reduction. Microstructural characterization revealed that pre-oxidized magnetite samples developed a network of pores during reduction, which helps in decreasing effective diffusion lengths and reducing the formation of dense Fe shells that impede the reduction of raw magnetite ores. The effectiveness of pre-oxidation on reduction varied distinctly by ore type, where ore with minimal gangue content showed the highest improvement, MgO-containing ore exhibited moderate enhancement in coarse fraction, which amplified in finer fractions, and CaO-containing ore showed limited improvement due to inherently favorable reduction characteristics even in the raw magnetite state. These findings show that the effectiveness of pre-oxidation is governed by the coupled roles of particle size and gangue chemistry, which determine the extent to which ore-specific kinetic and microstructural limitations can be alleviated during subsequent hydrogen reduction.

title: Review and assessment of sensor-based disease detection in dairy cattle: conceptual and practical challenges
summary: Recent advances in sensor technologies and machine learning have increased expectations for actionable disease detection in dairy cattle, yet farm-level adoption remains limited. This conceptual review outlines an implementation trajectory
content: Recent advances in sensor technologies and machine learning have increased expectations for actionable disease detection in dairy cattle, yet farm-level adoption remains limited. This conceptual review outlines an implementation trajectory from proof of concept to deployment as follows: (i) case definitions and defensible reference standards for diseases such as mastitis, lameness and respiratory disease should be biologically based; (ii) model development should consider features that drive utility and address class imbalance, ensuring that algorithms can reliably detect diseases that occur infrequently within herds; (iii) external validation should occur at the herd level, across seasons and time, and should report prevalence-aware metrics (e.g., recall and precision [positive predictive value]) rather than relying solely on accuracy or receiver operating characteristic area under the curve; and (iv) interoperability and economic viability should be sufficient to support multi-sensor use and sustainable adoption. Economic factors such as hardware and software costs, follow-up time burden, usefulness and return on investment under realistic false-positive rates will primarily determine adoption. Ethical and welfare considerations include maintaining human oversight where possible, avoiding invasive sensing and preventing over-automation. In conclusion, sensor-based systems show promise but remain constrained by inconsistent case definitions, limited cross-herd validation, interoperability gaps and uncertain economics, and many tools still blur the line between detecting animals needing treatment and ancillary predictions. With regulatory and ethical safeguards, progress will depend on reliability-focused standard operating procedures and end-user-oriented design; until then, most systems remain closer to hype than independent clinical technologies.

title: Addressing the Interconnected Crises: Policy Integration for Climate and Biodiversity in Norway
summary: ABSTRACT The biodiversity and climate crises are interconnected through land use and land use change, posing significant threats to ecosystem integrity, human well‐being, food and water supply and climate resilience. To effectively address
content: ABSTRACT The biodiversity and climate crises are interconnected through land use and land use change, posing significant threats to ecosystem integrity, human well‐being, food and water supply and climate resilience. To effectively address these challenges, policies for climate change mitigation, climate change adaptation and biodiversity protection must be considered jointly. In this paper, we analyse Norwegian national policy documents related to these three areas within the land use sector. We assess the extent to which climate and biodiversity policies are integrated into these national policy documents and identify three approaches to integration. (1) an ambition for integration that applies ecosystem management as a guiding principle, (2) a tendency towards partial integration, which is inconsistently applied throughout the documents; and (3) a lack of ambition for integration, where only one issue is addressed or where the three issues are treated superficially. The latter approach is by far the most prevalent, highlighting an absence of comprehensive integration and revealing a fragmented bureaucracy that prioritises individual policy issues over interconnected strategies. We argue that successful integration may require not only strong cross‐sectoral leadership, but also structural reforms and the establishment of new decision‐making bodies to effectively address the intertwined challenges of climate change and biodiversity loss.

title: Enhancing renewable energy and electric mobility integration through strategic optimization planning of distributed energy resources in an agrifood farm
summary: The urgent need to mitigate climate change requires transformative approaches in sectors such as agriculture, which contribute significantly to global greenhouse gas emissions. This study examines the integration of renewable energy technol
content: The urgent need to mitigate climate change requires transformative approaches in sectors such as agriculture, which contribute significantly to global greenhouse gas emissions. This study examines the integration of renewable energy technologies into a selected agri-food farm to improve decarbonisation, energy resilience and economic performance. This work's novel contribution is the development of a custom algorithm that reconstructs hourly electricity consumption profiles from monthly Time-of-Use (ToU) tariff band data. This enables accurate energy system sizing in contexts where high-resolution smart meter data are unavailable. The algorithm was validated against measured hourly consumption data for two users characterized by different consumption levels and patterns, including a residential user and a non-residential facility. Validation was performed under both summer and winter conditions using normalized root mean squared error (nRMSE) and normalized mean absolute error (nMAE). The resulting nRMSE values ranged from 3% to 10%, while nMAE values ranged from 1% to 8%, indicating a reasonable reconstruction accuracy across the investigated cases. Implemented in MATLAB, the algorithm is adaptable to various ToU schemes and supports detailed energy simulations for renewable energy planning. The most advanced configuration achieved up to 75% energy self-sufficiency and avoided approximately 160 tCO 2 annually. However, the configuration including battery storage provided the greatest environmental benefits at a higher investment cost, whereas the configuration without storage achieved the best economic performance, with the lowest LCOSE (0.43 €/kWh). These results highlight the need to balance environmental performance and economic viability when selecting renewable energy configurations for agricultural systems.

title: The UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism
summary: The UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, operational from 1 January 2027, imposes a carbon tax administered by His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC) on selected carbon-intensive sectors: aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, and iro
content: The UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, operational from 1 January 2027, imposes a carbon tax administered by His Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC) on selected carbon-intensive sectors: aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, and iron and steel. The mechanism is designed to mirror the UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS), ensuring parity between domestic producers and importers.

title: Integrating photovoltaic water pumping within the water–energy Nexus: A systematic review and pvsyst-based assessment for rural applications
summary: Reliable access to water in rural and off-grid communities is fundamentally constrained by energy availability, positioning water supply technologies at the center of the water–energy–carbon nexus in sustainable development. This study eval
content: Reliable access to water in rural and off-grid communities is fundamentally constrained by energy availability, positioning water supply technologies at the center of the water–energy–carbon nexus in sustainable development. This study evaluates photovoltaic water pumping systems (PVWPS) as an integrated nexus intervention by combining a PRISMA-guided systematic review with a PVSyst-based techno-economic and environmental assessment in a rural Indonesian context. The systematic review, covering peer-reviewed literature published between January 2010 and January 2026, identifies dominant research trends, methodological patterns, and persistent gaps in the technical, economic, social, and environmental evidence base, and these review findings are used directly to parameterize and benchmark the simulation-based case study. The case study assesses water delivery reliability, lifecycle cost, and operational carbon mitigation for a 2.25 kWp system supplying a rural community in North Sulawesi, Indonesia. Results indicate that the proposed system reliably supplies approximately 30 m³/day of water with zero unmet demand on an annual basis, while avoiding about 2.96 tCO₂/year through diesel displacement, at an abatement cost of approximately 110 USD/tCO₂. Benchmarking against global case studies confirms the representativeness of the results and explains inter-study performance differences in terms of system sizing, efficiency definitions, and climatic context. Overall, the findings demonstrate that photovoltaic water pumping systems can provide reliable, cost-stable, and low-carbon water supply solutions for off-grid and underserved communities.

title: Global transportation impacts on wildlife mortality and emerging pathways for mitigation
summary: Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine transportation are fundamental to modern human life, but vehicle collisions with wildlife inadvertently kill hundreds of millions of animals across 2000 vertebrate and invertebrate species annually; howev
content: Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine transportation are fundamental to modern human life, but vehicle collisions with wildlife inadvertently kill hundreds of millions of animals across 2000 vertebrate and invertebrate species annually; however, a comprehensive framework to assess and mitigate these mortalities is missing. We identified and compared the most up-to-date information regarding the impacts of transportation on wildlife mortality to determine cross-cutting solutions to this challenging problem. For example, numerous strategies, such as under- or overpasses traversing roads and railways that increase wildlife-habitat connectivity, policies that enforce reduced speed in areas with active wildlife, and passive sensors that detect wildlife to alert nearby ships and vehicles and enable mandatory speed reductions, can reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions. We explored emerging technological advances that could help further reduce future wildlife-vehicle conflicts and provide a path forward for transportation systems. Specifically, we described how the combination of citizen science, artificial intelligence, targeted studies on wildlife demographic impacts, and cost-effective mitigation efforts will be powerful tools to inform needed future policies to decrease ship speed in areas with threatened whale species and reduce rates of wildlife mortality across ecosystems in a fast-moving world.

title: Potential of household food waste for compost production: A laboratory-scale evaluation of mixing formulations
summary: Household food waste (FW) is a major biodegradable fraction of municipal solid waste and represents a potential feedstock for decentralized compost production.This study evaluated the feasibility of converting household FW into compost thro
content: Household food waste (FW) is a major biodegradable fraction of municipal solid waste and represents a potential feedstock for decentralized compost production.This study evaluated the feasibility of converting household FW into compost through laboratory-scale composting and compared six mixing formulations to identify a promising formulation among the tested treatments for further development of decentralized household FW composting systems.Food waste was collected directly from 60 households in Binh Duong Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, over seven consecutive days to characterize its generation rate and composition and to obtain representative feedstock for subsequent composting experiments.Six composting formulations were evaluated under controlled laboratory conditions, with three replicates per treatment.Food waste accounted for 66% of household municipal solid waste, with average generation rates of 0.861 kg/household/day and 0.203 kg/person/day.Plant-based materials represented 61% of the collected FW, indicating a substantial biodegradable fraction suitable for composting.The composting process was conducted for 28 days under aerobic conditions, with periodic monitoring of temperature, moisture content, and pH.The quality of the final compost was evaluated based on total nitrogen, available P₂O₅, available K₂O, organic matter, humic acid, Mg, Pb, Escherichia coli (E.coli), and Salmonella.Among the six formulations, T5, consisting of 80% FW, 10% loam soil, and 10% cow manure, showed the most favorable overall performance in terms of compost quality, particularly for nitrogen, organic matter, humic acid, and magnesium contents, while meeting the assessed microbiological safety criteria.The results demonstrate the feasibility of converting household FW into compost under the tested laboratory-scale conditions and identify T5 as the most favorable formulation among those evaluated, providing a basis for further development and validation of decentralized household FW composting systems.

title: Modeling Livestock Greenhouse Gas Emissions through LCA Frameworks
summary: Livestock provides livelihood to vulnerable communities and ensures food and nutritional security, hence it is considered as an integral part of the agri-food system. Concurrently, livestock exerts significant pressure on the environment th
content: Livestock provides livelihood to vulnerable communities and ensures food and nutritional security, hence it is considered as an integral part of the agri-food system. Concurrently, livestock exerts significant pressure on the environment through the usage of natural resources and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. It is predicted that by 2050, the global population is going to reach 9.6 billion, thereby causing a significant increase in demand of livestock products like egg, meat and dairy products. Henceforth, meeting this increasing demand with climate and sustainability goals requires increase production by adoption of low-emission technology and appropriate policy measures. During the previous decade, global methane ( https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> CH 4 ) and nitrous oxide ( https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> N 2 O ) emissions from cattle have increased, even though up to 30% mitigation is claimed to be achievable. Nevertheless, robust quantification of livestock-associated GHG emissions is essential for designing and implementing such strategies. This chapter presents a comprehensive overview of global, national, and regional emission estimation frameworks, ranging from international inventory methodologies like the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and National Greenhouse Gas Inventories (NGHGI) to life cycle assessment (LCA)-based approaches and some important model-based simulations. It highlights on major databases and modelling methods for measuring emissions across whole production system and supply chains.

title: A review of the effectiveness of solutions to achieve the good environmental status of the marine environment
summary: Europe’s seas are at the nexus of a “triple crisis” of biodiversity and habitat loss, climate change, and pollution, increasingly eroding the ecosystems’ resilience and capacity to provide ecosystem services. Although essential, existing Eu
content: Europe’s seas are at the nexus of a “triple crisis” of biodiversity and habitat loss, climate change, and pollution, increasingly eroding the ecosystems’ resilience and capacity to provide ecosystem services. Although essential, existing European Union policies, especially the Marine Strategy Framework Directive (MSFD), proved insufficient. The objective of the MSFD to achieve Good Environmental Status (GES) in all EU marine waters by 2020 was not reached, due to gaps in GES definition, a lack of consideration of climate change, uneven ambition, insufficient measures, gaps in monitoring and data comparability, and inadequate integration with other key policies. The aim of this study was to review the management measures and solutions to address the pressures and ecosystem features covered by the 11 MSFD GES Descriptors, assessing their reported effectiveness, co-benefits and trade-offs, and implementation constraints. This review identifies a broad range of solutions contributing to GES, including ecological protection, passive and active restoration, nature-based solutions, pressure reduction, spatial protection and planning, sustainable resource management, and pollution prevention and mitigation. Their effectiveness is often context- and scale-dependent. Also, no single measure is sufficient, and outcomes are enhanced when these are integrated into a coherent framework, adapted to local conditions, and supported by long-term monitoring, stakeholder engagement, and coastal/marine spatial planning. Restoration measures should be preceded by effective pressure/stressor reduction, while pressure-reduction solutions can generate cascading benefits across multiple Descriptors, highlighting opportunities to prioritize interventions. While evidence is abundant for some Descriptors (e.g., non-indigenous species, commercial fish and shellfish, biodiversity, eutrophication), important knowledge gaps remain for food webs, seabed integrity, and hydrographic conditions, as well as on cumulative effects and interactions, cross-Descriptor effects, the status of emerging contaminants, the effectiveness of waste management/circular economy and of marine nature-based solutions against GES objectives, and on climate-change-related measures. Overall, achieving GES will require moving beyond isolated measures towards coordinated, adaptive, and ecosystem-scale management to effectively address the “triple crisis”.

title: Quantifying the microclimatic feedback of citywide rooftop photovoltaic deployment in Sendai, Japan
summary: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) deployment supports urban decarbonization, but its local microclimatic effects and interactions with urban morphology remain underexplored, particularly in coastal cities such as Sendai, Japan. The current study us
content: Rooftop photovoltaic (PV) deployment supports urban decarbonization, but its local microclimatic effects and interactions with urban morphology remain underexplored, particularly in coastal cities such as Sendai, Japan. The current study uses the weather research and forecasting (WRF) model with PV parameterization scheme and local climate zone (LCZ) data at 400 m resolution to conduct five experiments (exp_ctrl, exp_25, exp_50, exp_75, and exp_100) representing 0–100% citywide PV roof coverage during the hottest week of 2025. PV deployment produced a discernible, spatially heterogeneous cooling effect, with mean surface air temperature reductions of 0.03–0.06 °C by day and 0.07–0.14 °C at night, alongside minor localized warming (< 0.08 °C) during morning and evening transitions. Higher-coverage scenarios reduced specific humidity by 70.8% (exp_75) and 62% (exp_100) of the day. Ground and sensible heat fluxes declined by up to 11.8 and 21.7 W/m 2 as coverage increased, while latent heat flux changes remained minor, indicating that PV roofs cool mainly by reducing heat storage rather than by evapotranspiration. All scenarios lowered the mean boundary layer height by up to 79.4 m. Compact mid- and low-rise zones showed the strongest cooling and highest electricity yields, whereas compact high-rise zones warmed slightly under higher coverage. Mean electricity output rose linearly with coverage, reaching 151 Wh/m 2 per day and 66.5 g CO₂ m -2 per day savings at full deployment. These results indicate that moderate, LCZ-specific PV coverage, rather than full saturation, offers the best balance of cooling, energy generation, and climate resilience to guide effective PV deployment policy in cities.

title: EVDetect: a framework for orchestrated and AI-powered detection of cyber-attacks in EV charging networks
summary: E-mobility has gained significant attention in recent years due to its contribution to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and the technological advancements introduced by digital interfaces. However, these interfaces also expose the grid to
content: E-mobility has gained significant attention in recent years due to its contribution to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and the technological advancements introduced by digital interfaces. However, these interfaces also expose the grid to an expanded threat landscape, including attacks such as spoofing and Denial-of-Service. In this article, we propose EVDetect, a comprehensive intrusion-detection framework supporting exploratory unsupervised analysis and supervised Machine Learning (ML) for Electric Vehicle (EV) charging networks. Our methodology introduces a decoupled logging architecture that prevents logging noise and enables the retrospective use of historical models, supporting reproducible experimentation with tabular security data. Candidate models are evaluated using both functional (i.e., F1-macro) and non-functional (i.e., inference latency, CPU utilization, and model size) characteristics, with the latter providing relative computational comparisons on common reference hardware. The framework is evaluated on the CICEVSE2024 dataset. In the full-dataset binary experiment, the leading ensembles achieved F1-macro values of 0.87 - 0.88, with XGBoost providing the most favorable relative-efficiency profile. The full multiclass experiment achieved an F1-macro of approximately 0.66, highlighting the difficulty of distinguishing attack categories with overlapping power-consumption patterns. Overall, EVDetect supports reproducible comparison of functional and computational model characteristics, while deployment performance on EVSE-class hardware remains to be validated.

title: Regeneration After Severe Wildfire: Hotter Microclimates Exceed Hydraulic and Thermal Tolerances in Sierra Nevada Conifer Seedlings
summary: ABSTRACT Tree seedling regeneration after wildfire will determine the long‐term trajectory of forests under climate change, yet increasing drought and heat extremes can suppress regeneration and result in forest type conversion. We combined
content: ABSTRACT Tree seedling regeneration after wildfire will determine the long‐term trajectory of forests under climate change, yet increasing drought and heat extremes can suppress regeneration and result in forest type conversion. We combined field observations and a controlled drought‐heat growth chamber experiment to investigate how these stressors independently and jointly affect drought‐ and heat‐tolerance physiology in seedlings of montane conifer species from drought‐ and wildfire‐prone regions in the southern Sierra Nevada. In both the field and growth chamber experiment, we found that exposure to elevated leaf temperatures in post fire‐like environments dwarfed the effect of physiological adjustments in heat tolerance (temperatures causing initial impairment (T crit ) or 50% loss (T 50 ) of photosystem II capacity) and drought tolerance (turgor loss point). In the field, this resulted in narrower thermal safety margins across five conifer species in burn scars with no remaining canopy, while in the growth chamber experiment three species showed narrower or even negative thermal and hydraulic safety margins. In the growth chamber experiment, leaf temperatures were also frequently decoupled from air temperature, highlighting that biophysical feedbacks between leaf temperature and transpiration may amplify seedling water loss even under stomatal closure. For both the field and growth chamber experiment, we found no evidence of a trade‐off between drought and heat tolerance within or among species. Among species, seedlings of the range‐restricted Sequioadendron giganteum (giant sequoia) were observed to be the most vulnerable to combined drought and heat stress in the growth chamber experiment. Our results highlight that direct thermal stress may strongly constrain post‐fire conifer regeneration and underscore the need to integrate seedling energy balance and microclimate into predictions of post‐fire recovery and management strategies, especially for vulnerable species such as giant sequoia.

title: Where should straw return be promoted? Spatial zoning of management suitability based on C/N ratio optimization in Northeast China
summary: CONTEXT Straw return is widely promoted as a key conservation practice in the black soil region of Northeast China, yet its effects on crop yield, soil nutrients, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are highly variable across locations and m
content: CONTEXT Straw return is widely promoted as a key conservation practice in the black soil region of Northeast China, yet its effects on crop yield, soil nutrients, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are highly variable across locations and management contexts. This heterogeneity has hindered the transition from uniform promotion to spatially targeted management strategies. OBJECTIVE This study aims to quantify the overall effects of straw return on soil–crop–emission indicators, identify the key drivers and causal pathways governing yield and GHG responses, determine the optimal soil C/N ratio window for synergistic yield gain and GHG mitigation, and translate this window into spatially explicit management suitability zones under future climate scenarios. METHODS An integrated framework was developed, coupling meta-analysis of 180 paired field observations, random forest, structural equation modeling (SEM), NSGA-II multi-objective optimization, and remote sensing–GIS spatial mapping. Three complementary nonlinear detection methods with bootstrap uncertainty quantification were employed to delineate C/N ratio thresholds. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS Meta-analysis revealed that straw return significantly increased available phosphorus (17.7%), available potassium (12.9%), total nitrogen (4.4%), soil organic carbon (9.5%), and crop yield (6.5%). GHG emission responses were highly heterogeneous: N₂O showed a non-significant increase, while CH₄ increased substantially (64.8%, p < 0.001), with both indicators exhibiting high spatial variability across provinces. Total nitrogen was the dominant driver of yield response, whereas soil organic carbon was the dominant driver of GHG response; management practices exerted stronger control on GHG emissions than on yield. SEM identified a cascading pathway from climate through soil carbon and nitrogen pools and C/N ratio to yield response, with C/N ratio as the key mediator. Three complementary threshold detection methods consistently delineated an optimal C/N management range of 12.53–14.65. NSGA-II optimization yielded a knee-point management strategy (N at approximately 205.35 kg ha −1 , straw at approximately 9838 kg ha −1 ). Spatial zoning revealed 46.7% of cropland in Heilongjiang Province as a structural-optimization priority zone, and optimized strategies in southern low-latitude areas remained robust under SSP1–2.6, SSP2–4.5, and SSP5–8.5 scenarios. SIGNIFICANCE These findings demonstrate that spatially differentiated straw management guided by C/N ratio optimization can balance food security and GHG mitigation goals more effectively than uniform recommendations. The framework provides a quantitative scientific basis and a spatially explicit decision-support tool for transitioning straw return policy from uniform promotion to precision management tailored to local soil stoichiometric conditions.

title: A socially informed optimization framework for rural electrification planning across alternative electricity demand scenarios: A case study in Bolivia
source: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development
summary: Achieving universal electricity access remains a global challenge, particularly in remote rural areas where grid extension is technically or economically unfeasible. Existing approaches provide cost-optimal and technically feasible solution
content: Achieving universal electricity access remains a global challenge, particularly in remote rural areas where grid extension is technically or economically unfeasible. Existing approaches provide cost-optimal and technically feasible solutions for decentralized energy system design, but often fall short in delivering context-sensitive electrification strategies that combine microgrids and stand-alone systems while accounting for social and operational constraints. This paper proposes a socially informed optimisation framework for rural electrification planning, capable of generating alternative system configurations across different electricity consumption scenarios. The framework integrates solar PV generation, battery energy storage, and diesel backup, and incorporates hourly demand profiles together with socially informed constraints to enhance system manageability and reflect the electricity adoption process in rural areas. Methodologically, the proposed planning framework is built around a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) optimization model, integrated within a heuristic procedure to efficiently generate near-optimal electrification layouts and system designs under different social and operational preferences. The approach is applied to the rural community of Molle Orcko in Raqaypampa, Bolivia. Results demonstrate the framework's ability to adapt electrification strategies to varying community priorities and highlight the importance of jointly considering technical and social dimensions in decentralized energy planning.

title: Comparison of virtual energy sharing schemes for renewable energy communities under European regulations: A mixed-use case study in Italy
summary: The Renewable Energy Directive (RED II) introduced Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) as a mechanism to empower local actors in the energy transition through collective renewable energy sharing. European Member States have transposed RED I
content: The Renewable Energy Directive (RED II) introduced Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) as a mechanism to empower local actors in the energy transition through collective renewable energy sharing. European Member States have transposed RED II into diverse regulatory frameworks and incentive schemes, leading to different approaches to electricity sharing. This study analyses the techno-economic performance of a mixed-use REC composed of a university campus and a residential district, using City Energy Analyst to simulate six scenarios combining two virtual energy sharing schemes, Virtual Self-Consumption (VSC) and Virtual Net Metering (VNM), and three ownership configurations, ranging from a centralized external producer to a distribution of prosumers. Sensitivity analyses on PV sizing and electricity market prices are also performed. Results show that VSC schemes achieve higher energy performance than static VNM schemes due to more effective matching between generation and demand, while economic outcomes remain comparable across schemes. Compared to the baseline, energy sharing increases self-consumption by up to 35% in VSC schemes and up to 25% in VNM schemes, with revenue increases of up to 20% under both schemes. Configurations involving non-residential prosumers improve self-consumption and enable higher PV penetration without a proportional loss in economic viability. At the same time, economic performance is largely driven by accounting rules, including incentive tariffs and market price structures, which can offset differences in energy performance between sharing schemes. These findings suggest that REC design should prioritise the integration of non-residential prosumers, while regulatory frameworks should align economic incentives with energy efficiency objectives.

title: The Global Forestation Network: Orchestrating the Financing and Development of Tree Planting Programs
summary: ABSTRACT This study introduces the ‘global forestation network’ (GFN)—an arrangement of actors that shape afforestation, reforestation, and forest restoration activities worldwide. These activities typically involve planting trees, and are
content: ABSTRACT This study introduces the ‘global forestation network’ (GFN)—an arrangement of actors that shape afforestation, reforestation, and forest restoration activities worldwide. These activities typically involve planting trees, and are motivated by supporting biodiversity, local communities, and climate change mitigation. At the GFN's core sit the ‘orchestrators’—the world's largest non‐governmental tree planting organisations—that collectively influence how forestation is financed and implemented. Here, interviews with 23 actors reveal how orchestrators attempt to strategically and sustainably connect financiers and local planting organisations—developing portfolios of geographically and ecologically diverse projects. Yet, interviewees perceived mismatches between the funding sizes and project sizes available: while smaller and larger funds are often accessible, there exists a ‘missing middle’ ranging from USD 0.1–1 million that is difficult to source but what many planting organisations require. Orchestrators use an array of strategies to abate this challenge whilst balancing preferences of other actors within the GFN.

title: National-Scale Screening of Enhanced Rock Weathering in Ghana: Environmental Suitability and Geological Prospectivity
summary: Abstract Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) deployment requires locations where favourable soil and climatic conditions coincide with suitable silicate resources. This study developed a national spatial framework for Ghana that integrates topso
content: Abstract Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) deployment requires locations where favourable soil and climatic conditions coincide with suitable silicate resources. This study developed a national spatial framework for Ghana that integrates topsoil pH and cation exchange capacity, mean annual temperature and precipitation, and mapped lithological prospectivity to identify where these conditions converge. Soil and climate data from SoilGrids 2.0 and WorldClim 2.1 were combined with the Geological Survey of Ghana 1:1,000,000 map within a multi-criteria index evaluated across 216 districts. Four alternative weighting scenarios were used to test the stability of national rankings. ERW-SI values ranged from 42.0 to 75.8, with strong agreement among scenario rankings (Spearman’s ρ = 0.88–0.99). Forty districts covering 26,707 km² remained in the top quartile under all four scenarios, forming a spatially coherent candidate set concentrated mainly in the Deciduous Forest. These districts combine moderate soil acidity, comparatively high cation-retention capacity, adequate rainfall, and proximity to prospective mafic lithologies. Breakpoint and CEC-response perturbations produced little change in the national ranking, indicating that the identified spatial pattern is not strongly dependent on the reference parameterization. Area-based scenarios for the robust candidate set correspond to 1.8–4.4 Mt CO₂ yr⁻¹, although stoichiometric analysis shows that the upper end requires high first-year weathering efficiency. The framework establishes a reproducible basis for directing feedstock characterization, field trials, and ERW measurement campaigns toward the parts of Ghana where environmental and geological opportunities most strongly coincide.

title: Climate Change Projections for Mexico in the 21st Century
summary: ABSTRACT Climate change projections for Mexico remain subject to substantial regional and inter‐model uncertainty, particularly for precipitation. Here, we assess 21st‐century changes in temperature and precipitation over Mexico using 36 CM
content: ABSTRACT Climate change projections for Mexico remain subject to substantial regional and inter‐model uncertainty, particularly for precipitation. Here, we assess 21st‐century changes in temperature and precipitation over Mexico using 36 CMIP6 models under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1‐2.6, SSP2‐4.5, SSP3‐7.0 and SSP5‐8.5). Model performance was evaluated against CRU and ERA5 for 1981–2000 using the Taylor Skill Score, and the five best‐performing models were selected to construct a primary multimodel ensemble. Projections from this selected ensemble were compared with those from the complete 36‐model ensemble to evaluate the influence of historical model performance on projected climate signals and uncertainty. Results show robust warming across Mexico under all scenarios, with national mean temperature increases reaching approximately 1.7°C under SSP1‐2.6 and 4.9°C under SSP5‐8.5 by 2081–2100. Warming intensifies with radiative forcing, is generally stronger over northern Mexico, and exhibits high inter‐model consistency. In contrast, precipitation shows greater temporal, spatial and inter‐model variability. National precipitation remains comparatively stable under SSP1‐2.6 but progressively declines under higher‐forcing scenarios, with widespread drying projected across southern and southeastern Mexico. Seasonal analysis indicates that this annual drying signal is primarily associated with reductions during the wet season, whereas dry‐season changes remain comparatively small and heterogeneous. The selected and complete ensembles produce similar large‐scale temperature and precipitation patterns, but historical model selection reduces inter‐model spread and areas of low agreement, particularly for precipitation. Overall, our results show that future climate change in Mexico will be characterized by robust and spatially coherent warming, together with a more uncertain but progressively stronger drying tendency, particularly during the wet season.

title: Can the U.S. Endangered Species Act protect biodiversity from climate change effects? Post-Weyerhaeuser unoccupied critical habitat designations
summary: Unoccupied critical habitat designation is often highlighted as a beneficial U.S. Endangered Species Act provision for conserving biodiversity in the face of climate change. However, the effectiveness of this legal mechanism may be at risk
content: Unoccupied critical habitat designation is often highlighted as a beneficial U.S. Endangered Species Act provision for conserving biodiversity in the face of climate change. However, the effectiveness of this legal mechanism may be at risk due to the U.S. Supreme Court’s 2018 ruling in Weyerhaeuser Co. v. the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) and resulting shifts in federal rules regulating unoccupied critical habitat designations. This project examines how the FWS navigated the first Trump administration’s regulatory changes following Weyerhaeuser in proposed rules for three South Florida reptile taxa threatened by climate change effects. The FWS proposed designating unoccupied critical habitat for the Florida Keys mole skink ( Eumeces egregius egregius ) and the rim rock crowned snake ( Tantilla oolitica ). However, they determined that unoccupied critical habitat was not essential for the conservation of the Key ring-necked snake ( Diadophis punctatus acricus ) despite its entire occupied habitat being vulnerable to sea level rise. The FWS contended that these proposed critical habitat designations would have been the same whether finalised under the Trump administration’s post-Weyerhaeuser regulations or prior regulations. Textual evidence demonstrates that the FWS likely drew on the Trump administration’s more stringent language and criteria for proposing unoccupied critical habitat units even when finalising analyses under less stringent regulations. Along with drawing broader lessons about how conservation law might adapt to the climate crisis, the study cautiously advocates for designating unoccupied critical habitat for the Key ring-necked snake for future assisted migrations provided the potential risk of hybridisation is considered.

title: N-LAS-IAM: Climate change in a balance-of-payments framework
summary: Climate change is becoming a macro-financial development problem for peripheral economies, yet integrated assessment models remain poorly equipped to analyse climate vulnerability in externally constrained developing countries. Existing het
content: Climate change is becoming a macro-financial development problem for peripheral economies, yet integrated assessment models remain poorly equipped to analyse climate vulnerability in externally constrained developing countries. Existing heterodox models are mostly closed or global, while balance-of-payments-constrained growth models treat climate in reduced form and incompletely formalise the financial channel. This paper introduces the N-LAS-IAM, a recursive framework coupling a Thirlwall–Hussain growth core with endogenous green structural change, capital flows under financial fragility, sovereign risk, and a climate module mapping global emissions into damages that feed back into profitability and sovereign fragility. Green structural change is endogenised through logistic diffusion equations governing trade income elasticities as functions of green R&D and the real exchange rate. The model is explored via Monte Carlo experiments in which damage intensity and climate-to-risk transmission vary while emissions, policy, and structural-change parameters remain fixed. Three results emerge. First, higher damage produces a more fragile debt regime with elevated spreads, tighter financing, and prolonged deleveraging. Second, damages widen the elasticity gap between exports and imports, slowing green upgrading and locking the economy into lower-sophistication trade patterns. Third, the damage-to-fragility relationship is nonlinear: below a threshold the economy absorbs shocks, but above it a self-reinforcing regime emerges where lower productivity, higher spreads, weaker inflows, and structural regression feed on one another. These findings suggest that physical damages erode policy capabilities by raising external finance costs when green investment is most needed, and that early mitigation may yield convex macroeconomic returns for peripheral economies under balance-of-payments constraints.

title: Advances and Novel Approaches in Enteric Methane Mitigation in Ruminant Livestock
summary: Ruminant livestock systems occupy a strategic position at the cross-section of food security, environmental sustainability, and climate change mitigation. Ruminants serve a crucial role in global food systems as they convert inedible fibrou
content: Ruminant livestock systems occupy a strategic position at the cross-section of food security, environmental sustainability, and climate change mitigation. Ruminants serve a crucial role in global food systems as they convert inedible fibrous biomass into nutrient-dense animal products; however, they are also an important biological source of enteric methane, a key greenhouse gas (GHG) generated as a result of normal ruminal fermentation ( Beauchemin et al., 2020 ). The proportion of enteric methane emissions is approximately 30%–40% of the total agricultural GHG emissions on Earth, and cattle represent the largest contribution to this total due to their number, increased feed consumption, and increased ruminal capacity ( Morsy et al., 2025 ; Roques et al., 2024 ). Methane is a short-lived climate pollutant, having an atmospheric lifetime of approximately 12 years and a warming potential that is approximately 28 times more than that of carbon dioxide in a 100-year time period ( IPCC, 2021 ). As a result, enteric methane mitigation has emerged as a priority for near-term climate action, as highlighted by global initiatives such as the Global Methane Pledge ( Hristov et al., 2015 ; Roques et al., 2024 ). In addition to its environmental impact, methane production is also a huge energetic waste in ruminant systems, as it consumes about 6%–12% of gross dietary energy intake and directly impacts negatively on feed-utilization efficiency and productive performance ( Beauchemin et al., 2020 ; Malyugina et al., 2025 ).

title: Implementing sustainable procurement through category management and ESG-based supplier evaluation: an EPC case study supported by the Operational Ethical Dilemma
summary: Sustainable procurement has become a strategic organizational priority as companies increasingly seek to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles into procurement decision-making while maintaining operational efficie
content: Sustainable procurement has become a strategic organizational priority as companies increasingly seek to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles into procurement decision-making while maintaining operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness. Despite the growing body of literature on sustainable procurement, limited research has examined its practical implementation within complex project-based industries. This study addresses this gap by presenting the implementation of a sustainable procurement framework within an international Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) contractor through the integration of Category Management, ESG-based supplier evaluation, and structured executive decision-making. The research adopts an implementation-oriented qualitative case study approach. A structured ESG assessment questionnaire, developed by the author and informed by internationally recognized sustainability principles, was applied annually to the organization’s twenty-five most strategically important suppliers based on procurement expenditure. Rather than conducting statistical analyses, the study focused on the individual evaluation of suppliers to support executive procurement decisions within a real organizational environment. The findings demonstrate that integrating ESG criteria into Category Management enables organizations to embed sustainability within existing procurement processes without fundamentally altering established procurement practices. The study further shows that while ESG assessments produce valuable operational evidence, final procurement decisions require executive judgement that balances operational findings with organizational strategy, stakeholder expectations, commercial priorities, and ethical responsibilities. To facilitate this process, the Operational Ethical Dilemma (OED) was applied as a managerial decision-support framework linking operational assessment with executive decision-making. The study contributes to both theory and practice by demonstrating a practical approach to implementing sustainable procurement in a complex EPC environment. It provides procurement professionals with an implementation framework that integrates Category Management, ESG-based supplier evaluation, and executive decision-making while supporting responsible procurement governance and long-term organizational sustainability.

title: SEQUESTRO DE CARBONO NO SOLO PELOS SISTEMAS AGRÍCOLAS INTEGRADOS NO BRASIL – AG4C
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Este relatório técnico apresenta os resultados finais do projeto Ag4C – Sequestro de Carbono no Solo pelos Sistemas Agrícolas Integrados no Brasil, desenvolvido no âmbito do Research Centre for Greenhouse Gas Innovation (RCGI) e voltado à a
content: Este relatório técnico apresenta os resultados finais do projeto Ag4C – Sequestro de Carbono no Solo pelos Sistemas Agrícolas Integrados no Brasil, desenvolvido no âmbito do Research Centre for Greenhouse Gas Innovation (RCGI) e voltado à avaliação do potencial dos Sistemas Agrícolas Integrados (SAIs) como solução baseada na natureza para mitigação das mudanças climáticas e intensificação sustentável da agropecuária brasileira. O projeto integrou gestão e disseminação científica, revisões sistemáticas e meta-análises, bases de dados georreferenciadas, experimentação de campo e laboratório e modelagem espacial e de cenários. Os resultados mostram que o desempenho dos SAIs varia conforme solo, clima, histórico de uso, composição e manejo do sistema, mas evidenciam potencial relevante para recuperação e estabilização dos estoques de carbono, melhoria da saúde do solo, aumento da eficiência produtiva e mitigação de gases de efeito estufa. Em escala nacional, sistemas integrados apresentaram, em média, estoques de carbono do solo 12,5% superiores aos monocultivos, com ganhos de até 15,3% no Cerrado. O projeto também consolidou evidências sobre mecanismos de estabilização do carbono, papel das gramíneas e raízes, atividade microbiana, agregação do solo, emissões de CO₂, CH₄ e N₂O e trade-offs associados a diferentes sistemas de manejo. A modelagem demonstrou que não existe uma taxa única de sequestro de carbono aplicável ao território brasileiro e que as respostas dependem de fatores edafoclimáticos, uso da terra e práticas de manejo. Foram utilizadas abordagens complementares, incluindo DayCent, CENTURY, InVEST, espectroscopia, aprendizado de máquina e geoestatística, com aplicações em diferentes regiões e escalas. Como legado, o Ag4C gerou bases de dados, mapas, modelos, metodologias, artigos científicos, formação de recursos humanos e recomendações com potencial de aplicação em inventários de gases de efeito estufa, sistemas de Monitoramento, Relato e Verificação (MRV), fatores Tier 2 e Tier 3, políticas de agricultura de baixo carbono, financiamento climático e estratégias de descarbonização das cadeias de bioenergia e biocombustíveis.

title: Innovative Extension Approaches for Climate-Smart Smallholder Livestock System in Developing Countries
summary: Smallholder livestock production systems in the developing countries are recognised as pathways to address poverty, hunger and gender equity. More than 68% of rural households depend on smallholder livestock, and this farming generates subs
content: Smallholder livestock production systems in the developing countries are recognised as pathways to address poverty, hunger and gender equity. More than 68% of rural households depend on smallholder livestock, and this farming generates substantial income and employment opportunities for them. At the same time, smallholder livestock faces immense challenges due to climate change, resulting in increased disease outbreak incidence, production losses and animal welfare issues. Furthermore, it contributes 12% of GHG emissions to the atmosphere. With existing smallholder livestock’s social importance, adverse effects of climate change on it and its contribution to climate change, there is a demand for access to mitigation and adaption technologies/practices. This necessitates a strong livestock extension advisory system capable of addressing complex challenges. Taking this scenario into account, this chapter presents emerging insights from research and field experiences on current livestock extension system(s) and their approaches, identifies gaps and proposes approaches to address them. This chapter will comprise the following sections. The first section details the context of climate change and smallholder livestock production in developing courtiers, followed by the rationale for climate-smart livestock farming practices and the role of livestock extension advisory services and their limitations. The next sections broadly encompass approaches to strengthening extension organisations with co-designing of technologies, leveraging ICT tools and facilitating farmer’s behaviour towards adoption by mainstreaming gender and social inclusion. The final section details about strengthening livestock extension advisory systems to promote climate-smart smallholder livestock system.

title: CO2 and CH4 fluxes from monomictic volcanic lakes in a remote oceanic island: Flores island case study (Azores)
summary: Abstract Flores Island, situated in the Azores archipelago, is a volcanic island formed by overlapping stratovolcanoes. The island hosts several volcanic freshwater bodies, some of them present poor ecological state. Flores Island maar crat
content: Abstract Flores Island, situated in the Azores archipelago, is a volcanic island formed by overlapping stratovolcanoes. The island hosts several volcanic freshwater bodies, some of them present poor ecological state. Flores Island maar craters lakes were studied to assess greenhouse gas emissions, through investigation of temporal and spatial variations of the diffuse CO 2 (ΦCO 2 ) and CH 4 (ΦCH 4 ) flux. Comprida, Negra, and Funda lakes were the selected study cases, with four field surveys combining geochemical and microbial analyses. Water composition varies between Na-HCO 3 , Na-HCO 3 -Cl, and Na-Cl-HCO 3 , showing low variation across surveys. The total CO 2 flux (calculated by Graphical Statistical Approach) shows higher emissions at Funda Lake (1.06 ± 0.26 and 1.02 ± 0.36 t d − 1 ), as the other lakes present values as high as 0.39 ± 0.08 t d − 1 . All of them showed lower ΦCO 2 during the second survey (August), as high temperatures enhance photosynthetic activity. ΦCH 4 values range between 0.64 and 6.28 kg d − 1 , with higher emissions at Funda Lake, although bellow worldwide lake averages. ΦCO 2 values were 2 to 3 orders of magnitude higher than ΦCH 4 . Microbial communities and their diversity varied between lakes, with Negra and Funda lakes depicting stronger seasonal shifts. During winter mixing of the water column appears to favor anaerobic processes, enhancing microbial respiration and potential CO 2 release from sediments, and enrichment in syntrophic taxa and potential CH 4 oxidizers (e.g. Syntrophaceae , Methylomonadaceae ). Results indicate that ΦCO 2 and ΦCH 4 emissions are mainly controlled by biogeochemical processes, and show that the trophic state of a lake ecosystem can enhance the greenhouse gases emissions.

title: Balancing power generation with ecological impact: hydraulic and biological performance of a modernized adjustable-blade Kaplan turbine assessed using Sensor Fish technology
summary: Hydropower remains a major source of affordable, clean, and reliable energy; however, aging infrastructure must be modernized to meet evolving environmental and operational requirements. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) operates 90
content: Hydropower remains a major source of affordable, clean, and reliable energy; however, aging infrastructure must be modernized to meet evolving environmental and operational requirements. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) operates 90 large Kaplan turbines within the Federal Columbia River Power System, many approaching the end of their service life. At Ice Harbor Dam in Washington State, an adjustable-blade turbine was installed at Unit 3 (U3AB) and evaluated using autonomous Sensor Fish (SF) technology to assess hydraulic conditions relevant to fish passage. Unlike conventional fixed-blade turbine designs, the adjustable-blade configuration allows modification of blade positioning to mitigate adverse hydraulic conditions associated with fish injury. SF data showed that U3AB improved hydraulic conditions for fish passage relative to the baseline turbine. The highest combined median value of the nadir pressure occurred during the lowest (Lower 1%) operation (144.8 kPa), while the lowest occurred during the Generator Limit (Upper 1%) operation (120.0 kPa), indicating reduced barotrauma risk. Across operations, ≤1.0% of SF releases experienced nadir pressures below 64.1 kPa, and modeled barotrauma-related mortal injury probabilities remained low (0.78–2.26%). U3AB demonstrated lower percentages of severe acceleration events (≥95 g) in its runner region (5.2–9.9%) compared to the baseline turbine. Strike metrics and SF measurements further indicated high estimated 48-h fish survival rates of 96.1–98.7% across turbine operations based on the velocity-based strike metric ( M V ), consistent with live-fish survival estimates. These results demonstrate that U3AB met its design goals for improved fish passage while maintaining operational efficiency and support modernization of aging hydropower infrastructure with reduced ecological impacts.

title: Modulation of Root Exudate–Microbe Interactions for Sustainable Rhizosphere Function and Soil Health
summary: The rhizosphere is a highly dynamic and biologically complex ecosystem where plants, fungi, bacteria, and other microorganisms interact through integrated chemical signaling, molecular recognition, metabolic cooperation, and competition tha
content: The rhizosphere is a highly dynamic and biologically complex ecosystem where plants, fungi, bacteria, and other microorganisms interact through integrated chemical signaling, molecular recognition, metabolic cooperation, and competition that collectively regulate plant growth, nutrient cycling, stress resilience, and ecosystem stability. Root exudates act as the primary driver of microbial assembly by releasing spatially and temporally regulated metabolites that mediate chemotaxis, nutrient mobilization, microbial recruitment, immune modulation, and pathogen suppression. Microbial communication via quorum sensing, volatile organic compounds, and interkingdom signaling coordinates biofilm formation, antimicrobial production, and plant physiological responses, while pattern recognition receptors and microbial-associated molecular patterns enable selective immune activation or symbiotic accommodation. Within this network, microbial communities enhance plant performance through phytohormone production (auxins, cytokinins, gibberellins), 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase-mediated stress reduction, and cooperative processes such as metabolic cross-feeding and siderophore-mediated nutrient acquisition. Beneficial microorganisms like Bacillus, Pseudomonas, Streptomyces, Trichoderma, inhibit pathogens through antibiosis, mycoparasitism, biofilm formation, and induced systemic resistance (signaling through jasmonic acid and ethylene). Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) and helper bacteria increase nutrient uptake (P and N), mineralization of organic matter, and symbiotic efficiency. Niche exclusion and resource partitioning are affected by microbial competition for C, N, P, and Fe. These mechanisms collectively create a holistic rhizosphere network that promotes sustainable productivity, stress tolerance, and ecosystem stability.

title: Real Options Analysis for Adaptable Buildings: A Cost and Carbon Analysis
summary: Abstract There is increasing interest in adaptable building design as spatial needs, market conditions, and performance expectations evolve over time. Uncertainty in future demand requires designers to assess not only the financial implicat
content: Abstract There is increasing interest in adaptable building design as spatial needs, market conditions, and performance expectations evolve over time. Uncertainty in future demand requires designers to assess not only the financial implications of expansion strategies, but also their associated carbon impacts from an early stage. This study applies Real Options Analysis (ROA) to evaluate the value of incorporating adaptability into building design and to support decision-making under uncertainty and fluctuations of future demands. A case study of a commercial building in Singapore is used to compare three alternatives: Fixed (a base case retaining the existing building without expansion), Demolish-and-Rebuild (D&R), and Flex (embedding adaptability to permit future expansion at five-year decision intervals). Historical vacancy rate data from 2011 to 2023 were used to estimate demand trends and forecast future occupancy through year 2065. The alternatives were assessed using three metrics: Cost of Construction (CC), Net Present Value (NPV), and Embodied Carbon (EC). Results show positive mean NPV for all alternatives, with Flex achieving the highest mean NPV at approximately SGD 654 million. D&R resulted in the highest mean construction cost (SGD 78.6 million), the highest embodied carbon (8,180 metric tons CO₂e), and the lowest mean NPV (SGD 233 million). While Fixed offered the lowest immediate cost and carbon impact, it underperformed in capturing future growth. Overall, the findings highlight a clear trade-off between short-term certainty and long-term adaptability, emphasizing that embedding adaptability can improve financial performance while reducing the likelihood of future demolition and rebuilding. The study demonstrates the value of ROA methodology as a decision-support tool to navigate this trade-off between immediate cost certainty, long-term value creation, and environmental responsibility in building design.

title: Adsorption of heavy metals using fruit peels biochar: a review
summary: Heavy metals (HMs) are a significant class of pollutants in aquatic environments, posing serious risks to both ecosystems and human health. Concurrently, managing agricultural residues, such as fruit peels, has become increasingly challengi
content: Heavy metals (HMs) are a significant class of pollutants in aquatic environments, posing serious risks to both ecosystems and human health. Concurrently, managing agricultural residues, such as fruit peels, has become increasingly challenging due to their abundance and limited disposal options. Transforming these wastes into engineered adsorbents offers a sustainable and cost-effective solution for wastewater treatment. This review provides a comprehensive examination of fruit peel biochar (FPB) as an adsorbent for HM removal via adsorption. It highlights the synthesis processes, structural and chemical characteristics, including morphology, composition, functional groups, crystallinity, and thermogravimetric features, and their influence on adsorption performance. The mechanisms governing HM adsorption are elucidated, with emphasis on the interactions between metal ions and biochar surfaces. Furthermore, the effects of operational parameters, including pH, initial concentration, and adsorbent dosage, on removal efficiency are systematically discussed. Recent advances in biochar regeneration and reuse are also explored, underscoring strategies to improve recovery, extend life cycles, and enhance treatment durability. By promoting the valorisation of fruit peels, this review advances circular economy principles while addressing pressing challenges in wastewater remediation.

title: Introduction to Resilience and Sustainability in Livestock Systems under a Changing Climate
summary: Globally, livestock production systems play a pivotal role in strengthening food systems through their contributions to food security and nutrition by supplying high-quality animal protein. It contributes significantly to the world’s supply
content: Globally, livestock production systems play a pivotal role in strengthening food systems through their contributions to food security and nutrition by supplying high-quality animal protein. It contributes significantly to the world’s supply of calories, protein and vital micronutrients like calcium, iron and vitamin B12 through a range of products including meat, milk and eggs. They contribute to around 33% of protein and 17% of calories consumed worldwide ( FAO, 2017 ). In addition to this, the livestock sector’s economic impact extends beyond its direct role in food production and is closely linked to ensuring the livelihood security of billions of people across the globe. It is particularly important in developing countries like Africa and Asia where a major proportion of the small-scale and poor farmers depend primarily on the livestock sector for their source of income and livelihood. It forms the backbone of agricultural economies in these developing countries contributing substantially to around 40% of total agricultural output ( FAO, 2024 ). It provides regular income by selling milk, eggs, animals and other animal products, which in turn helps reduce poverty and maintain financial stability. Additionally, livestock are an important asset for rural communities, offering a range of crucial services like finance, savings and protection against natural disasters and other emergencies. Beyond this, the livestock also assists in agricultural activities by providing draught power essential for routine farm operations. It is said that the draught power animals such as cattle, camels, horses and donkeys contribute up to 81% of farm power in Northern Africa ( FAO, 2017 ).

title: Resilient skies: developing sustainable key performance indicators for airport operation and maintenance under public–private partnership frameworks in Egypt
summary: The Egyptian airport sector has faced an 18% gap in operation and maintenance (O&M) efficiency relative to Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) benchmarks. This gap has driven a strategic shift toward Public-Private
content: The Egyptian airport sector has faced an 18% gap in operation and maintenance (O&M) efficiency relative to Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) benchmarks. This gap has driven a strategic shift toward Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) to improve efficiency and attract private investment. This study develops sustainable key performance indicators (KPIs) for O&M agreements at Egyptian airports. A mixed-methods approach identified 41 KPI and categorized them into the environmental, economic, social, and urban dimensions. These indicators were evaluated through a questionnaire distributed to 40 academic and professional experts. Scale reliability was confirmed (overall Cronbach’s α = 0.892). Results were analyzed using means and standard deviations and the Mann-Whitney U test to compare the two independent expert groups. Statistical analysis revealed no significant perceptual divergence between academic and professional experts across all indicators (P > 0.05), indicating similar evaluation patterns across stakeholder groups. Consequently, 25 priority KPIs were identified, achieving a rating (mean > 3.4). Notably, the urban dimension exhibited the highest density of priority KPIs (70%), led by spatial efficiency (U1) and circulation efficiency/permeability (U10). No rank difference between the two groups (P=1.000) was obtained for service quality (Ec1), confirming a value-driven model. Integrating these KPIs into a conceptual managerial logic model (Interdependent Value Chain) transforms airports from transit points into dynamic urban gateways, enhancing operational efficiency and long-term asset resilience. In practice, the framework provides policymakers, airport authorities, and private operators with an expert-assessed benchmark for designing and monitoring future O&M concessions in Egypt and similar emerging markets.

title: Evolution of mechanical properties of recycled rubber aggregate alkali‐activated slag concrete subjected to freeze–thaw cycling
summary: Abstract To investigate the evolution of mechanical properties of recycled rubber aggregate alkali‐activated slag concrete (RA‐AASC) under freeze–thaw cycles, cube compressive strength tests, splitting tensile strength tests, and SEM examin
content: Abstract To investigate the evolution of mechanical properties of recycled rubber aggregate alkali‐activated slag concrete (RA‐AASC) under freeze–thaw cycles, cube compressive strength tests, splitting tensile strength tests, and SEM examination were conducted by considering the number of freeze–thaw cycles, coarse rubber aggregate (CRR), and fine rubber aggregate (FRR) as variables. The results indicate that both the cube compressive strength and splitting tensile strength of RA‐AASC decrease at an accelerated rate with increasing freeze–thaw cycles, and the tensile performance is more sensitive to freeze–thaw damage. A 50% replacement ratio of FRR can inhibit strength loss within a certain number of freeze–thaw cycles, whereas an excessive replacement ratio accelerates deterioration. CRR has a significantly greater adverse effect on the mechanical properties of RA‐AASC than FRR, and the combined incorporation of CRR and FRR offsets the beneficial effect on freeze–thaw damage resistance. Microscopic analysis shows that fine rubber particles can fill pores and buffer frost‐heaving stress, while CRR weakens the aggregate skeleton and intensifies interfacial debonding, which are the main microscopic mechanisms responsible for the differences in mechanical performance.

title: Fully automatic trace gas plume detection
summary: Abstract Future imaging spectrometers will expand contemporary data volumes by orders of magnitude, requiring automated methods to upscale labor-intensive detection of trace gas point sources. Here we present a fully-automated approach that
content: Abstract Future imaging spectrometers will expand contemporary data volumes by orders of magnitude, requiring automated methods to upscale labor-intensive detection of trace gas point sources. Here we present a fully-automated approach that achieves operational performance for plume detection and labelling without human participation. Our method combines machine learning (ML)-based morphological analysis with physics-based spectroscopic model fitting. We deploy it on data from the EMIT imaging spectrometer, operating in two modes. First, we present a “daily digest” that runs automatically on all downlinked data, flagging the largest events for immediate response. The daily digest demonstrates that a significant fraction of the largest plumes can be detected automatically with negligible false positives. This represents a significant new high-water mark in plume detection accuracy. Second, we use it for retrospective analysis to find plumes that were missed by the existing human review process. We observe that at least 25% of large plumes may have been passed over in the existing workflow due to confirmation bias and ambiguity in the visual cues used by human reviewers. Finally, we extend detection to three understudied trace gases: NH $$_{3}$$ , NO $$_{2}$$ and the first observations of carbon monoxide (CO) plume in EMIT imagery.

title: Does rural land transfer promote high-quality agriculture development? Empirical evidence from 30 provinces in China
summary: As a fundamental pathway toward agricultural-scale operations, rural land transfer (RLT) has emerged as an important institutional mechanism for promoting high-quality agricultural development (HQAD). However, how to effectively unleash the
content: As a fundamental pathway toward agricultural-scale operations, rural land transfer (RLT) has emerged as an important institutional mechanism for promoting high-quality agricultural development (HQAD). However, how to effectively unleash the productive potential of land resources and align RLT with the objectives of high-quality development remains an important research question. Treating the 2010 national regulatory intensification of rural land transfer as a common policy milestone, this study employs a continuous difference-in-differences (DID) model and a mediating effect model to examine the relationship between RLT intensity and HQAD and to explore the potential transmission role of new agricultural business entities (NABE). The results show that the overall level of HQAD in China has steadily improved, although substantial spatial and temporal disparities remain, with HQAD generally decreasing from the eastern to the central and western regions. The continuous DID estimates indicate a significant positive association between RLT intensity and HQAD after the 2010 national regulatory-intensification milestone, and this relationship remains stable across the reported robustness checks. The mediation analysis provides evidence consistent with a potential transmission pathway through new agricultural business entities (NABE). Furthermore, the estimated association between RLT intensity and HQAD is stronger in the central region and in non-major grain-producing areas.

title: Contrasting short- and medium-term effects of N-enriched biochar on greenhouse gas emissions and nutrient use efficiency in a maize-wheat rotation
summary: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are a key contributor to climate change, and biochar has been proposed as an amendment to reduce GHG emissions while improving soil properties and crop yield. However, the impact of N-enriched biochar (NB) on
content: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are a key contributor to climate change, and biochar has been proposed as an amendment to reduce GHG emissions while improving soil properties and crop yield. However, the impact of N-enriched biochar (NB) on GHG emissions, global warming potential (GWP), and GHG intensity (GHGI) remains poorly understood in rainfed maize-wheat cropping systems. We evaluated the performance of two types of NB (NB1 and NB2) produced from pristine biochar (PB) with a two-year field trial. Four amendment treatments [without biochar (CK), PB, NB1, and NB2] were applied at two N fertilizer levels: 100% (N100) and 70% (N70) of the recommended rate, resulting in eight treatment combinations. Our results indicated that NB significantly increased nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions, GWP, and GHGI during the maize 2023 growing season, indicating an initial spike, alongside a non-significant rise in methane (CH 4 ) emissions. NB2 had higher GHG emissions and lower mitigation efficiency than NB1. However, in the subsequent cropping seasons (wheat 2023, maize 2024, and wheat 2024), NB1-N70 consistently and significantly reduced CH 4 emissions (24.8%-40.9%), N 2 O emissions (2.8%-16.5%), GWP (7.4%-21.1%), and GHGI (18.9%-33.2%) as compared to CK-N70. Compared with CK-N70, NB1-N70 also remarkably increased the uptake and partial factor productivity of N and P, as well as crop yield, which were associated with improved soil properties. Furthermore, NB1-N70, as compared with CK-N70, enhanced net economic profit by 16.4%-28.7% except for the first crop (maize 2023), reflecting higher returns relative to treatment costs. Overall, NB1-N70 exhibited the most favorable balance between GHG mitigation and crop productivity, although the initial increase in N₂O emissions highlights a short-term trade-off that should be considered when estimating its climate gains.

title: Il ruolo delle riserve naturali integrali nella mitigazione degli eff etti del cambiamento climatico
summary: Le foreste svolgono un ruolo cruciale nella mitigazione e nell’adattamento ai cambiamenti climatici grazie alla loro capacità di regolare il microclima, ridurre le temperature estreme e aumentare la resilienza degli ecosistemi. In questo co
content: Le foreste svolgono un ruolo cruciale nella mitigazione e nell’adattamento ai cambiamenti climatici grazie alla loro capacità di regolare il microclima, ridurre le temperature estreme e aumentare la resilienza degli ecosistemi.
