title: ESG disclosure intensity and firm performance: Empirical evidence from ASEAN listed firms
summary: This study examines the association between ESG disclosure scores and firm financial performance. Firms are categorized into low- and high-ESG disclosure groups, and the study also examines the association of these categories with financial
content: This study examines the association between ESG disclosure scores and firm financial performance. Firms are categorized into low- and high-ESG disclosure groups, and the study also examines the association of these categories with financial performance. The study’s independent variables are the ESG disclosure score and level groups, while the dependent variable, financial performance, is measured using Return on Assets (ROA) and Tobin’s Q. This study analyses 4,220 firm-year observations from ASEAN-listed firms using a panel fixed-effect regression. The results show that the ESG disclosure score is negatively associated with both ROA and Tobin’s Q. High-disclosure firms exhibit lower financial performance, whereas low-disclosure firms exhibit higher ROA relative to the reference group. Robustness tests using an alternative performance measure, lagged disclosure, and dynamic-panel GMM are conducted. The dynamic-panel GMM supports the negative associations with Tobin’s Q. However, the associations are no longer statistically significant when year fixed effects are included, indicating that the findings are sensitive to this specification. The negative associations appear to operate through regional temporal patterns rather than firm-level differences in disclosure. Furthermore, the study does not establish causality, and further research could examine the causal relationship between ESG disclosure and financial performance.

title: Community Monitoring and Project Resilience under Funding Uncertainty in Community-Based Projects in Kajiado County, Kenya.
source: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
summary: Community-based projects are critical in advancing socio-economic development in marginalized regions of Kenya, contributing to improved access to water, healthcare, education and livelihood opportunities. In Kajiado County, which hosts abo
content: Community-based projects are critical in advancing socio-economic development in marginalized regions of Kenya, contributing to improved access to water, healthcare, education and livelihood opportunities. In Kajiado County, which hosts about 255 community-based projects and 53 youth groups supported by government agencies, NGOs and international development partners, nearly 40–45% of projects experience delays or interruptions owing to funding inconsistencies and up to 65% struggle after donor withdrawal. Community monitoring has emerged as a key mechanism for enhancing accountability, transparency and resilience, yet its influence on project sustainability under financial instability remains inadequately understood. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the effect of community monitoring on project resilience under funding uncertainty in community-based projects in Kajiado County, Kenya. It specifically assessed the influence of frequency of tracking, citizen feedback mechanisms, data literacy levels and inclusivity of monitoring committees on project resilience. The study was anchored on the Participatory Development Theory, Stakeholder Theory, Adaptive Management Theory and Human Capital Theory. A descriptive and explanatory research design was adopted, targeting 32 major donor-funded community-based projects and 648 stakeholders comprising project committee members, beneficiaries, NGO representatives, local administrators and youth group leaders. A sample of 87 respondents was determined using Nassiuma's formula and selected through stratified random sampling. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire, and both descriptive and inferential statistical methods, namely Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis, were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four dimensions of community monitoring jointly explained 45.6% of the variation in project resilience. Citizen feedback mechanisms had the strongest positive and significant effect on project resilience, followed by data literacy levels and frequency of tracking, while inclusivity of monitoring committees had a positive and significant but comparatively weaker effect. The study, therefore, recommends that community-based projects should standardize monitoring and reporting schedules, ensure timely processing of community feedback, build stakeholders' capacity in data analysis and digital monitoring tools, and promote meaningful participation of marginalized groups in monitoring committees so as to strengthen project resilience under funding uncertainty in Kajiado County.

title: A Study of Artificial Intelligence and Green Finance: Building A Sustainable Economy
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Green Finance have emerged as two of the most important forces that have the potential to drive the world towards a sustainable economy. The current paper attempts to explore the role of AI and Gre
content: Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Green Finance have emerged as two of the most important forces that have the potential to drive the world towards a sustainable economy. The current paper attempts to explore the role of AI and Green Finance in promoting and supporting a sustainable economy with reference to building a Viksit Bharat 2047. A survey was conducted among 160 respondents, with the results analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation, regression, and an independent-samples t-test. The results demonstrated that the population studied had a generally positive perception about how AI can support Green Finance and lead the economy towards sustainability. The analysis identified strong awareness about AI as the biggest predictor of increased perception of the integration of AI and Green Finance (r = 0.78, p < .001). Additionally, participants who were aware of Green Finance had significantly higher scores for the perceived level of integration than those who were not (t = 2.65, p = .009). As such, there is reason to reject the null hypothesis, which claimed that there is no connection between the two concepts. Finally, the paper provides recommendations that financial institutions, regulators, and educators can consider in order to promote and support responsible and AI-enabled Green Finance.

title: AQRAR SAHƏDƏ İNNOVASİYANIN İNKİŞAFININ MALİYYƏ TƏMİNATINDA BEYNƏLXALQ TƏCRÜBƏ VƏ AZƏRBAYCAN ÜÇÜN TƏTBİQ İMKANLARI

content: A S Ə Tədqiqatın məqsədi -aqrar sahədə innovasiyaların maliyyə təminatının beynəlxalq modellər əsasında analitik qiymətləndirilməsi və bu təcrübənin Azərbaycan üçün tətbiq imkanlarının müəyyən edilməsidir.Tədqiqatın metodologiyası -tədqiqatda müqayisəli təhlil, struktur-funksional yanaşma, statistik məlumatların analizi və elmi ədəbiyyatın sistemləşdirilməsi metodlarından istifadə edilmişdir.Tədqiqatın tətbiqi əhəmiyyəti -əldə olunan nəticələr aqrar innovasiyaların maliyyələşdirilməsi sahəsində dövlət proqramlarının təkmilləşdirilməsi, subsidiya və güzəştli kredit mexanizmlərinin optimallaşdırılması, eləcə də strateji iqtisadi qərarların qəbulunda istifadə oluna bilər.Tədqiqatın nəticələri -müəyyən edilmişdir ki, Azərbaycanda aqrar innovasiyaların maliyyə təminatında dövlət maliyyə resursları üstünlük təşkil edir, lakin uzunmüddətli və dayanıqlı innovativ inkişaf üçün özəl investisiyaların və bazaryönümlü maliyyə alətlərinin payının artırılması zəruridir.Tədqiqatın orijinallığı və elmi yeniliyi -məqalədə aqrar innovasiyaların maliyyələşdirilməsi beynəlxalq təcrübə əsasında sistemli müqayisəli təhlil edilmiş, Azərbaycan üçün adaptasiya edilə bilən innovasiyayönümlü maliyyə mexanizmləri elmi əsaslarla təklif olunmuşdur.Açar sözlər: aqrar

title: Why do millennials still hesitate to go cashless? Determinants of continued mobile payment use in Sri Lanka
summary: This study investigates the factors influencing Sri Lankan millennials’ intention to continue using mobile payment systems by extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) with privacy and security considerations
content: This study investigates the factors influencing Sri Lankan millennials’ intention to continue using mobile payment systems by extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) with privacy and security considerations while examining the moderating role of gender. This research makes use of an explanatory sequential mixed-method design where both quantitative and qualitative methods are combined to provide a holistic understanding of the continuous usage of mobile payment technology in the context of a growing digital economy. Quantitative data was gathered from 401 young adults in Sri Lanka using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using PLS-SEM. Qualitative data was obtained from 16 semi-structured interviews and was subjected to thematic analysis. Convenience sampling was used for the quantitative stage while purposive sampling was used for the qualitative stage. The results showed significant positive relationships between performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, privacy and security, and continued-use intention. Gender significantly moderates only the relationship between privacy and security and continued-use intention. The qualitative findings identified additional barriers beyond those captured by UTAUT, including digital literacy limitations, infrastructure constraints, merchant resistance, language barriers, and continued reliance on cash. The research extends the UTAUT model by including privacy and security, which is the most important factor that affects the adoption of mobile payment systems in the future.

title: Multi-currency Cash-Flow Risk Management
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: A U.S. automobile manufacturer that earns Mexican-peso revenue and pays Canadian-dollar costs at a common horizon faces two jointly random exchange-rate exposures that combine into a single net operating cash flow measured in U.S. dollars.
content: A U.S. automobile manufacturer that earns Mexican-peso revenue and pays Canadian-dollar costs at a common horizon faces two jointly random exchange-rate exposures that combine into a single net operating cash flow measured in U.S. dollars. This paper asks which instrument most suitably hedges that net exposure: a forward, a futures contract, a portfolio of vanilla Foreign Exchange (FX) options, or an exchange option. Within a two-factor Garman–Kohlhagen model featuring correlated Brownian motions, FX forward prices are derived via risk-neutral zero-value and cash-and-carry logic. Closed-form valuation is solved for portfolios consisting of vanilla FX puts and calls, while exchange options are priced through a numéraire shift to the MXN risk-neutral measure, yielding a Margrabe-style formula relying solely on relative volatility as its volatility input. A calibrated numerical experiment, cross-checked by Monte Carlo, confirms the theory: at the baseline parameters, the exchange option costs about 27% less than the vanilla portfolio while still flooring the firm's net loss at zero, and its premium declines monotonically in ρ. The forward remains best for locking a deterministic cash flow, whereas the exchange option is the most efficient instrument when management targets net operating loss rather than each currency leg separately.

title: Peace: Still a Sideshow
summary: The 2023 judicial reform protests highlighted how far the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the question of peace had faded from Israeli political debate. While the 7 October Hamas attack and the war in Gaza renewed focus on the conflict, th
content: The 2023 judicial reform protests highlighted how far the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and the question of peace had faded from Israeli political debate. While the 7 October Hamas attack and the war in Gaza renewed focus on the conflict, this is not the same as renewed focus on peace. The trauma of 7 October renders a Palestinian state, a core minimum Palestinians demand for peace, an unacceptable risk for an even larger number of Israelis than before. Ripeness theory identifies hurting stalemates and enticing opportunities cultivated by third parties as vehicles for peace negotiations. This chapter argues that neither exists in the current context, with the Trump administration unwilling to impose sufficient costs on Israel. Although a Palestinian state remains key to a broader regional peace with countries like Saudi Arabia, even for centrist Israelis, this incentive will likely remain insufficient compared to the perceived risk.

title: INVESTMENT ATTRACTIVENESS OF THE COMMUNICATIONS SECTOR OF UKRAINE AS THE BASIS OF ITS SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT
summary: The article examines the investment attractiveness of Ukraine’s communications (electronic communications) sector as a key prerequisite for ensuring its sustainable development under martial law and post-war recovery conditions. Special att
content: The article examines the investment attractiveness of Ukraine’s communications (electronic communications) sector as a key prerequisite for ensuring its sustainable development under martial law and post-war recovery conditions. Special attention is paid to the analysis of the dynamics and structure of capital investments in the sector, factors of the investment climate and the relationship between investment activity and the sustainable development of the industry. Based on data from the National Commission for the State Regulation of Electronic Communications (NCEC) and surveys of the European Business Association, it has been established that in 2022–2025 capital investments in electronic communications increased from UAH 12.6 to 33.9 billion. The main barriers and incentives for investment activity have been identified. Directions for increasing the investment attractiveness of the industry are proposed, taking into account the goals of sustainable development and European integration processes. The study reveals that despite significant security risks and infrastructure damage caused by the full-scale war, the telecommunications sector of Ukraine has shown remarkable resilience. Capital expenditures increased by more than 30% annually in 2024–2025, reflecting operators’ commitment to network restoration, resilience enhancement (backup power solutions), and preparation for 5G deployment. The investment climate index of Ukraine improved to 2.70 points in 2025 according to the EBA survey, approaching pre-war levels. Positive factors include European integration progress, digitalization of public services, and preferential trade regimes. Key challenges remain related to security risks, regulatory uncertainty, energy supply instability, and the need for large-scale reconstruction of damaged infrastructure. The article substantiates that increasing investment attractiveness of the communications sector is a fundamental condition for achieving sustainable development goals, ensuring digital inclusion, supporting economic recovery, and strengthening national resilience. Practical recommendations include improvement of the regulatory framework, development of public-private partnership mechanisms, stimulation of foreign direct investment through risk insurance instruments, acceleration of 5G spectrum allocation, and integration of ESG principles into investment strategies of telecom operators. The research also highlights the critical role of telecommunications infrastructure in supporting Ukraine’s digital transformation agenda and the country’s integration into the European Digital Single Market.

title: Diagnosing governance and data gaps in urban groundwater management with a transferable workflow based methodology evidenced in Munich
summary: Abstract Urban groundwater management is emerging as a critical sustainability challenge in European cities under accelerating pressures of climate change and urbanization. Despite substantial investment in monitoring infrastructure and tec
content: Abstract Urban groundwater management is emerging as a critical sustainability challenge in European cities under accelerating pressures of climate change and urbanization. Despite substantial investment in monitoring infrastructure and technical expertise, effective groundwater management remains constrained by institutional fragmentation across multiple departments and authorities with dispersed responsibilities, disconnected data systems, and limited coordination. In the two Munich processes examined, the main barrier lay not in technical knowledge, but in institutional governance. The objective of this paper is to develop and demonstrate a methodology that improves the institutional governance of urban groundwater management. The paper applies a four-step Data-Governance Diagnostic combining stakeholder engagement, data assessment, governance workflow analysis, and prioritization of critical gaps, illustrated through two Munich application cases: rainwater infiltration under the Sponge City strategy and thermal groundwater use under the Municipal Heating Plan. Findings show that recurring problems, fragmented data infrastructures, limited digitalization, and data-sharing restrictions, are symptoms of deeper governance weaknesses. Groundwater data can only deliver practical value when embedded in governance systems that enable coordination, accessibility, and effective use in decision-making. The novelty is threefold: a practitioner-friendly step-by-step diagnostic applicable directly by municipalities; a structured output making principal data and governance gaps explicit and actionable; and the demonstration that these gaps are mutually reinforcing and must be addressed simultaneously. Future research should validate the methodology across cities of varying size, institutional capacity, and stage of urban development outside the Alpine context. An interactive workshop-based tool is currently under development to support application in observer cities. A key open scientific question emerging from the Munich cases is whether rainwater infiltration measures produce measurable effects on groundwater recharge at city scale, it remains unclear both how much these measures actually contribute to recharge and whether this contribution is large enough to be relevant for groundwater management. Resolving this requires dedicated city-scale monitoring and quantitative assessment.

title: Keynes’ Clearing Union, the Dollar Standard, and the Perils of Globalization
source: Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal
summary: The 1944 Bretton Woods agreement provided an international green light for the dollar standard. H. D. White, the lead US negotiator, saw to it that the ability of other countries to obtain commitments from the US (via the soon-to-be Interna
content: The 1944 Bretton Woods agreement provided an international green light for the dollar standard. H. D. White, the lead US negotiator, saw to it that the ability of other countries to obtain commitments from the US (via the soon-to-be International Monetary Fund) for loans or approval for currency devaluations would be limited. J. M. Keynes, representing Britain, in contrast proposed an International Clearing Union that would issue its own currency (“bancor”), intended to reduce systemic dependence on the dollar or on gold. The ICU would be a bank for the world’s central banks, which would allow debtor nations to borrow. In contrast to White’s plan, ICU creditors would be expected to reduce their balances by expanding domestic credit or other means. Insights from Keynes’ plan help to understand subsequent monetary history. An ICU premise was that international reserves should be pooled, and centralized. The Bretton Woods gold-dollar standard was jeopardized during the 1960s – the Triffin dilemma -- when European creditor countries demanded gold reserves from the US. An intermediate-run monetary truce, proposed by R. Mundell, would have included joint US-European action to agree on a US inflation target and to adjust gold-to-dollar ratios in European reserves. Monetary cooperation could thereby have created de facto international reserves. Instead, the Bretton Woods exchange rate apparatus collapsed by 1973, leaving major currencies to float. Against expectation, international demand for reserves soared. Relentless demand for US securities has contributed to soaring debt and malign distributional consequences. And exchange rate depreciation has done little to correct account imbalances. Clearing Union concepts help to understand the euro experiment – why it nearly failed, and how it recovered. An international currency can succeed only if 1) both creditor and surplus countries are required to adjust; and 2) member countries agree on inflation targets. Demands on China to revalue have been misguided. From the perspective of 2026, correction of account imbalances will not happen without the assent of the world’s now largest creditor, – China – which for domestic political reasons is likely to resist. Perils of globalization under the existing dollar standard are likely to continue.

title: When women take all: Direct election and female leadership
summary: This paper investigates how direct election regimes ( à la presidential democracy) affect the gender composition of political leaders compared to indirect appointment regimes ( à la parliamentary democracy). I study a 1993 reform that repla
content: This paper investigates how direct election regimes ( à la presidential democracy) affect the gender composition of political leaders compared to indirect appointment regimes ( à la parliamentary democracy). I study a 1993 reform that replaced mayoral appointment by councilors with direct election of mayors by popular vote in Italian municipalities. Exploiting the staggered adoption of the reform across municipalities between 1993 and 1997, I find that direct election raises the probability that a municipality is led by a woman by about 2.5 percentage points, from a pre-reform baseline of 3.5 percent to approximately 6 percent. The effect is stronger in municipalities with a greater pre-reform female representation in municipal councils and is driven by more educated officials replacing less-educated incumbents.

title: CETICISMO VERDE, GREENWASHING E CONFIANÇA NO CONSUMO SUSTENTÁVEL: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA E UMA AGENDA DE PESQUISA SOB A LENTE DA CONFIANÇA INSTITUCIONAL
summary: O consumo sustentável tornou-se meta explícita da Agenda 2030, mas a distância entre atitudes ambientais favoráveis e a compra efetiva permanece um problema central do campo. Este artigo mapeia e sintetiza a produção científica sobre cetici
content: O consumo sustentável tornou-se meta explícita da Agenda 2030, mas a distância entre atitudes ambientais favoráveis e a compra efetiva permanece um problema central do campo. Este artigo mapeia e sintetiza a produção científica sobre ceticismo verde, greenwashing e confiança no consumo sustentável, verifica em que medida a confiança institucional foi incorporada como antecedente desses construtos e propõe um modelo integrativo com uma agenda de pesquisa. Adotou-se revisão integrativa da literatura, de natureza qualitativa, organizada em torno de cinco questões e três eixos: o hiato atitude-comportamento, o par ceticismo verde e greenwashing e a confiança institucional. A análise indica que atitudes pró-ambientais são necessárias, porém insuficientes, porque preço, disponibilidade, hábito e desconfiança moderam a conversão da intenção em compra. O greenwashing eleva a confusão e o risco percebido e corrói a confiança verde, ao passo que o ceticismo opera como mediador e como moderador do hiato. A confiança institucional aparece como antecedente negligenciado nos modelos de consumo, embora a qualidade do governo condicione o comportamento pró-ambiental. Formulam-se quatro proposições teóricas e uma agenda voltada a mercados emergentes, com atenção ao Brasil, caso de baixa confiança institucional e alta incidência de alegações ambientais enganosas. Conclui-se pela necessidade de integrar a confiança institucional aos modelos e de segmentar consumidores por comportamento efetivo.

title: The winding road toward a wholesale digital euro: geoeconomics and bureaucratic politics
summary: Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) have become a prominent topic in International Political Economy (IPE). Of particular interest are wholesale CBDCs, given their implications for payment infrastructures, both domestic and cross-border
content: Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) have become a prominent topic in International Political Economy (IPE). Of particular interest are wholesale CBDCs, given their implications for payment infrastructures, both domestic and cross-border. The European Union (EU), one of the ‘great (financial) powers’, has been working on the development of a wholesale digital CBDC, yet progress has been uneven, characterized by sudden accelerations followed by periods of stasis. What accounts for this winding road toward the wholesale digital euro? Theoretically, we combine two approaches that are rarely deployed in tandem: geoeconomics and bureaucratic politics. Empirically, we show that a geoeconomic rationale, particularly concerns about the vulnerability of critical financial infrastructures in Europe and the desire to strengthen the international role of the euro, helps explain the drive toward a wholesale digital euro. At the same time, bureaucratic politics, understood as competing models sponsored by the main EU national central banks, accounts for the ECB’s cautious approach. In doing so, the paper contributes to the literatures on the weaponisation of finance, the geoeconomics of money, as well as the role of central banks as simultaneously geoeconomic and bureaucratic actors.

title: Central and Local Taxes: Which Plays a Greater Role in Improving the Human Development Index in Indonesian Regencies and Cities?
source: Ilomata International Journal of Tax and Accounting
summary: Taxation plays a fundamental role in financing public services and promoting human development through fiscal decentralization. However, empirical evidence comparing the contributions of central and local taxes to human development remains
content: Taxation plays a fundamental role in financing public services and promoting human development through fiscal decentralization. However, empirical evidence comparing the contributions of central and local taxes to human development remains limited. This study examines whether central tax revenue sharing (DBH) or locally generated tax revenues (LTR) play a greater role in improving the Human Development Index (HDI) across Indonesian regencies and municipalities. Using balanced panel data from 486 regencies and municipalities during 2018–2022, panel data regression is employed to estimate the effects of tax-based fiscal resources on HDI, controlling for gross regional domestic product (GRDP), government expenditure, population, and unemployment. The results show that both DBH and LTR have positive and statistically significant effects on HDI, indicating that taxation supports human development through fiscal equalization and local fiscal autonomy. The larger coefficient of LTR suggests a stronger marginal association with HDI than DBH. GRDP positively affects HDI, while government expenditure is negatively associated with HDI, highlighting the importance of expenditure quality rather than magnitude. Population is not statistically significant, whereas unemployment has a relatively small effect. These findings extend the fiscal decentralization literature by demonstrating the complementary roles of central and local taxation: DBH strengthens local fiscal capacity through revenue redistribution, while LTR enhances fiscal autonomy and responsiveness to local priorities. Improving human development therefore requires effective revenue sharing, stronger local revenue mobilization, and more efficient public expenditure, particularly for education, healthcare, and human capital development.

title: Uncertainty and global common volatility: an explainable artificial intelligence approach
summary: Global financial markets are increasingly exposed to shocks that propagate rapidly across countries, sectors, and asset classes, generating synchronized volatility that reflects the systemic dimension of financial risk. While prior research
content: Global financial markets are increasingly exposed to shocks that propagate rapidly across countries, sectors, and asset classes, generating synchronized volatility that reflects the systemic dimension of financial risk. While prior research documents the emergence of global volatility shocks, less attention has been paid to the factors associated with volatility synchronization. This paper investigates the uncertainty proxies associated with global common volatility (COVOL), combining SHAP values, Accumulated Local Effects (ALE), and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) within a machine learning framework to capture potentially nonlinear relationships. The results show that COVOL is most strongly associated with uncertainty proxies linked to oil market volatility, broad equity market volatility, technology-sector volatility, and global investor risk aversion, with nonlinear and time-varying contributions across these predictors. These findings carry direct practical implications. Because oil market uncertainty (OVX) and equity market uncertainty (VIX and VXN) emerge as the proxies most strongly associated with global common volatility, monitoring these specific indicators can serve as an early-warning signal for the build-up of synchronized volatility across markets. This is particularly relevant for risk managers calibrating hedging strategies against systemic volatility, for investors managing global portfolio exposure, and for policymakers tracking financial-stability risks.

title: The dual role of ungulates in the post-ingestion seed fate of an invasive forest tree
summary: Acacia species are widespread invasive plants in Mediterranean ecosystems, including in central Portugal, where they promote significant negative impacts. These species exhibit vigorous regeneration strategies, with seed germination being f
content: Acacia species are widespread invasive plants in Mediterranean ecosystems, including in central Portugal, where they promote significant negative impacts. These species exhibit vigorous regeneration strategies, with seed germination being facilitated by scarification, which may be achieved with high temperatures during fires, and passage through animals’ digestive tracts. We conducted feeding trials with captive domestic goats ( Capra hircus ), red deer ( Cervus elaphus ) and wild boar ( Sus scrofa ) to evaluate the potential of these ungulates to disperse or predate Acacia seeds. Acacia dealbata seeds were fed to animals to examine post-digestion fate. Results were compared with manually scarified and control seeds. Fragmented and intact seeds were detected in the faeces of all animal species. Seed recovery rate differed between domestic goat (very low) and wild ungulate (higher and similar for red deer and wild boar) species. Seed germination, seed destruction, and T 50 (time required for 50% of seeds to germinate) were similar among the animal species. Germination did not differ from the control, whereas seed destruction was higher and T 50 was lower than in the control treatment. Manual scarification increased germination and reduced T 50 . Our results show that domestic goat, red deer and wild boar can act as both dispersers through endozoochory and predators of Acacia seeds. Despite this pathway likely being a minor contributor to the overall spread of Acacia trees compared to other vectors, management should prioritize the control of Acacia in areas frequently used by ungulates. Overall, contrary to initial expectation, seed fate was largely consistent across ungulate species, despite differences in body size and digestive strategies.

title: From Temporary to Timeless
source: Transactions of the Association of European Schools of Planning
summary: World Expos take place in cities worldwide. They offer visions of the future and act as catalysts for urban transformation. Despite their ambitions, these events remain inherently temporary, lasting only three to four months. This paper ask
content: World Expos take place in cities worldwide. They offer visions of the future and act as catalysts for urban transformation. Despite their ambitions, these events remain inherently temporary, lasting only three to four months. This paper asks how the Expo format engages with urban dynamics through temporary intervention strategies. It explores the relationship that exists between ephemerality and permanence by examining how temporal complexity shapes urban space at World Expos. It does so with a focus on Expo ’92 in Seville. Using a critical comparative analysis of theoretical understanding of time, the paper evaluates their effects at the urban scale. The temporal distance since 1992 allows an assessment of the long-term urban legacy of a shortterm global event.

title: VENÇUR KAPİTAL VƏ BİZNES MƏLƏKLƏRİ MEXANİZMLƏRİNİN AZƏRBAYCAN KOS-LARININ MALİYYƏLƏŞDİRİLMƏSİNƏ TƏSİRİ
source: Journal of Science and Innovative Technologies
summary: Tədqiqatın məqsədi vençur kapital və biznes mələkləri mexanizmlərinin Azərbaycan kiçik və orta sahibkarlıq subyektlərinin (KOS) maliyyələşdirilməsində rolunu və təsir imkanlarını qiymətləndirməkdir.Tədqiqatın metodologiyası -tədqiqat çərçiv
content: Tədqiqatın məqsədi vençur kapital və biznes mələkləri mexanizmlərinin Azərbaycan kiçik və orta sahibkarlıq subyektlərinin (KOS) maliyyələşdirilməsində rolunu və təsir imkanlarını qiymətləndirməkdir.Tədqiqatın metodologiyası -tədqiqat çərçivəsində institusional və müqayisəli təhlil metodlarından, eləcə də beynəlxalq təcrübənin öyrənilməsindən istifadə olunmuşdur.Araşdırmada Azərbaycan maliyyə ekosisteminin mövcud vəziyyəti təhlil edilmiş, vençur kapital və biznes mələklərinin KOS-ların innovasiya potensialına, rəqabət qabiliyyətinə və davamlı inkişafına təsiri qiymətləndirilmişdir.Tədqiqatın tətbiqi əhəmiyyəti ondan ibarətdir ki, əldə edilən nəticələr KOS-ların maliyyələşdirilməsi sahəsində siyasət formalaşdıran qurumlar, startap ekosistemi iştirakçıları və investorlar üçün praktik tövsiyələr təqdim edir.Tədqiqatın nəticələri -göstərir ki, alternativ maliyyələşmə mexanizmlərinin inkişafı KOS-ların maliyyə resurslarına çıxışını əhəmiyyətli dərəcədə genişləndirə bilər.Tədqiqatın orijinallığı və elmi yeniliyi -tədqiqatın orijinallığı Azərbaycan şəraitində vençur kapital və biznes mələkləri mexanizmlərinin kompleks şəkildə təhlil edilməsində, elmi yeniliyi isə bu mexanizmlərin KOS-ların inkişafında sistemli rolunun konseptual əsaslarla müəyyənləşdirilməsindədir.

title: Implementing computer‑aided detection for TB active case finding: A qualitative study of feasibility and acceptability in Tondo, Manila
summary: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent, with over 1.23 million deaths globally in 2024. Despite available treatment and prevention strategies, timely and accurate detection remains challenging, p
content: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent, with over 1.23 million deaths globally in 2024. Despite available treatment and prevention strategies, timely and accurate detection remains challenging, particularly in high-burden settings such as the Philippines, which accounted for 6.8% of the global burden of TB in 2024. Computer-aided detection (CAD) software integrated with digital chest X-ray offers enhanced screening capacity, but its success depends on feasibility and acceptability within local health systems. This qualitative study explored perceptions and experiences of CAD integration during a Médecins Sans Frontières community-based TB active case finding campaign (ACF) in Tondo, Manila. In-depth interviews, focus group discussions, and direct observations were conducted with MSF staff, health center physicians, TB program personnel, ACF participants, and community leaders between January and April 2023. Thematic analysis identified four main themes: (1) Operational functionality and efficiency: Staff reported CAD increased screening capacity, supported clinical decision-making, and streamlined workloads; ACF participants reported a convenient process. (2) Human resources and role adaptation: Staff perceived role redistribution as initially challenging, highlighting the need for adequate capacity building and technical support; (3) Technical feasibility and system design: project managers and staff emphasized understanding CAD's capabilities and limitations to plan infrastructure, set thresholds, and compensate for inherent limitations. (4) Community acceptability and ethical considerations: community participants expressed mixed views on the reliability of novel "high-tech" tools and stressed the importance of aligning with local healthcare needs. This study demonstrates that implementing CAD in TB ACF is both feasible and acceptable when supported by careful planning and adaptation to local contexts. Sustainable implementation hinges on technical support and the meaningful involvement of healthcare workers and communities, whose insights help ensure ethical and effective digital health innovation. The experience in Tondo offers lessons on deploying CAD in high-burden, resource-constrained settings.

title: Cigarette leachates: a neglected threat to the growth of Salvinia auriculata Aublet
summary: Abstract Every year, trillions of cigarette butts are discarded in public areas and may enter aquatic ecosystems. In this context, the research assessed the impact of leachates from smoked (SB) and unsmoked cigarette butts (USB) and filters
content: Abstract Every year, trillions of cigarette butts are discarded in public areas and may enter aquatic ecosystems. In this context, the research assessed the impact of leachates from smoked (SB) and unsmoked cigarette butts (USB) and filters (SF; USF) on the growth of Salvinia auriculata Aublet at four concentrations: 1.0, 1.75, 2.5, and 5.0 cigarette butts/filters per liter, with ten replicates per treatment ( n = 10). S. auriculata growth was monitored weekly over 9 weeks, under controlled temperature (25 °C), through photographic records, and leaf area was quantified using ImageJ software. The growth coefficient (μ) and doubling time were obtained by fitting leaf area data to a logistic model. Cigarette leachate reduced S. auriculata mean leaf area by up to 72%, growth coefficient by up to 86%, and increased the doubling time by up to 8.5 times. These results highlight that leachates from both cigarette butts and filters induce severe phytotoxicity in S. auriculata , triggering physiological and morphological changes that can lead to plant mortality. This evidence underscores the urgent need for improved public awareness campaigns and management strategies targeting the proper disposal of cigarette waste.

title: Informal Communication and Employee Productivity: A Comparative Study of Guaranty Trust Bank and Zenith Bank, Port Harcourt
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE AND COMMUNICATION STUDIES
summary: This study examined the role of informal communication in influencing employee productivity in Guaranty Trust Bank (GTB) and Zenith Bank, Port Harcourt. Using a mixed-methods approach, data were collected through surveys and interviews with
content: This study examined the role of informal communication in influencing employee productivity in Guaranty Trust Bank (GTB) and Zenith Bank, Port Harcourt. Using a mixed-methods approach, data were collected through surveys and interviews with 384 employees and 2 management staff. The study explored the nature and forms of informal communication, its impact on productivity, the factors influencing its effectiveness, and its potential benefits and drawbacks on team dynamics and the work environment. Findings revealed that informal communication in both banks predominantly occurred through face-to-face conversations, instant messaging, and casual phone calls. This communication fostered collaboration, reduced delays, and boosted morale, leading to enhanced productivity. Factors such as organizational culture, trust levels among employees, and the accessibility of digital communication tools significantly influenced the effectiveness of informal communication. While informal communication offered benefits like improved collaboration and innovation, challenges such as misinformation and distractions were also identified. Based on these findings, the study recommends fostering a supportive organizational culture that values open communication, enhancing the accessibility and training for digital communication tools, and implementing policies to manage the potential drawbacks of informal communication. These measures aim to maximize the benefits of informal communication while mitigating its challenges, ultimately driving higher employee productivity in the banking sector. This study contributes to the understanding of how informal communication operates in a developing country’s banking sector, offering insights into improving workplace communication dynamics and productivity.

title: Beyond the factory floor: analyzing job-switching attitudes among executives in Bangladesh’s garment industry
summary: Abstract Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector is central to the national economy, yet it faces persistent turnover among its executives. Although labor-level attrition has been widely studied, executive mobility and its implications
content: Abstract Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector is central to the national economy, yet it faces persistent turnover among its executives. Although labor-level attrition has been widely studied, executive mobility and its implications for organizational stability remain under-examined. Guided by Herzberg’s two-factor theory and job embeddedness theory, this study identifies the drivers of executive job-switching and examines their association with job satisfaction and intentions to leave the sector. Data from a cross-sectional online survey of 300 RMG executives were analyzed using descriptive statistics, one-sample Z-tests, correlation and regression analysis, individual-level logit and probit models with controls, and probability analysis. Insufficient compensation (52.7%) was the most frequently cited reason for switching jobs, followed by improper supervisor behavior (41.3%) and a lack of new responsibilities (34%). About 44.7% of respondents were considering leaving the RMG sector (approximately 19% definitely and 26% possibly), mainly because of concerns about social status and job security. Higher salaries were associated with higher job satisfaction and more favorable organizational ratings, whereas longer tenure was associated with lower salary-increment expectations and weaker exit intentions. Most executives regarded 3–5 years as the ideal interval for switching jobs, and the 95% confidence interval for the mean monthly salary of mid-level executives was BDT 57,312–66,838. The study provides new empirical evidence on executive turnover in the RMG sector and suggests that retention can be improved through inflation-adjusted compensation, supervisor training, structured career pathways, and benefits such as provident funds.

title: Stakeholders’ experiences during the resumption of in-person classes: A qualitative study in public schools in Bulacan, Philippines
source: International Journal of Education Learning and Pedagogical Sciences (INJELPS)
summary: Aim: This study explored the experiences of head teachers, teachers, students, and parents during the transition from distance learning to in-person classes in public schools in the post-pandemic era.It specifically sought to provide a basi
content: Aim: This study explored the experiences of head teachers, teachers, students, and parents during the transition from distance learning to in-person classes in public schools in the post-pandemic era.It specifically sought to provide a basis for strengthening learning delivery, school readiness, and strategic planning for in-person education.Methodology: An exploratory qualitative research design was employed.In-depth interviews were conducted with 44 participants, comprising 11 head teachers, teachers, students, and parents, respectively, from public schools in District VI of Bulacan, Philippines.Participants were selected through purposive sampling.Results: Three major themes emerged: transitional experiences, challenges encountered, and coping strategies.Participants described both positive and challenging experiences during the return to in-person classes.Major challenges included health and safety concerns, poor student behavior, unmet academic requirements, and lack of resources.Participants also identified coping strategies such as advanced planning and preparation, classroom preparation, coordination with parents and local government units, adjustment to schedules and rules, and psychosocial support. Conclusion:The transition to in-person classes required substantial adjustment among school stakeholders and was influenced by school readiness, resource availability, health and safety conditions, and stakeholders' capacity to adapt.The findings underscore the importance of collaborative learning continuity planning, adequate resources, responsive teaching practices, psychosocial support, and stakeholder engagement.Schools may use these findings as a basis for strategic initiatives that strengthen in-person learning, address learning gaps, and promote educational resilience.

title: Analisis Hukum Ekonomi Syariah terhadap Akad Jual Beli Borongan Petani Kopi di Kampung Palintang Desa Cipanjalu Kabupaten Bandung
summary: This research aims to explore the practice of bulk coffee buying and selling in Kampung Palintang and measure its compliance with Sharia Economic Law provisions. The research background departs from the reality that the wholesale system oft
content: This research aims to explore the practice of bulk coffee buying and selling in Kampung Palintang and measure its compliance with Sharia Economic Law provisions. The research background departs from the reality that the wholesale system often places farmers in a weak bargaining position, with prices determined unilaterally or based on rough estimates without accurate measurement. This study employs a qualitative descriptive approach through direct observation, structured interviews with 10 farmers and 3 collectors, and document review. The results show that although transactions are conducted orally and traditionally, this practice formally fulfills the pillars of sale. However, there is a sharia defect in the form of gharar (uncertainty) because the object (coffee cherries) is not yet ready for harvest and its quantity cannot be precisely measured when the contract is agreed. Additionally, there are indications of price injustice that disadvantage farmers due to economic pressures requiring them to accept down payments. Within the Maqasid Syariah framework, this activity is classified as mubah (permissible), but requires intervention in the form of cooperative assistance and the use of written contracts to create public welfare and avoid exploitative practices. This research recommends strengthening sharia economic literacy among farmers and developing more transparent contract standards.

title: Words build worlds: corporate communication, brand politicization, and sustainability rollback
summary: Purpose This commentary aims to examine corporate communication as a mechanism through which sustainability rollback is constructed, amplified and normalized. It argues that firms are not merely affected by these developments but may active
content: Purpose This commentary aims to examine corporate communication as a mechanism through which sustainability rollback is constructed, amplified and normalized. It argues that firms are not merely affected by these developments but may actively shape them through communication practices, brand positioning and stakeholder engagement. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a conceptual commentary approach and develops a critical perspective on the communicative dimensions of sustainability rollback. Findings Sustainability rollback is not only a political phenomenon but also mediated through consumer-facing narratives. Consumers and other stakeholders interpret corporate actions through political and identity-based lenses. Corporate communication practices, including misinformation, disinformation, propaganda, greenwashing, greenhushing and brand politicization, contribute to the normalization of sustainability rollback by reshaping perceptions of what constitutes legitimate corporate conduct. Rather than serving as neutral communication channels, firms may inadvertently reinforce broader political dynamics that undermine sustainability commitments. Research limitations/implications Future research should examine how corporate communication strategies influence the legitimacy of sustainability norms across different political and cultural contexts. Practical implications Managers should critically assess the broader societal consequences of their communication strategies. They need tools that help identify how corporate narratives may unintentionally reinforce polarization, misinformation and the erosion of sustainability commitments. Social implications By normalizing sustainability rollback, communication practices can have significant consequences for environmental protection, social equity, human rights and public well-being. Originality/value A marketing and consumer behavior perspective to emerging debates on sustainability rollback identifies corporate communication as a strategic battleground where sustainability norms are either reinforced or undermined. It proposes futures literacy as a means of strengthening reflexivity, enabling firms to recognize blind spots, challenge dominant narratives and evaluate the long-term social value implications of their communication and strategic choices.

title: Viabilidad de un programa de gestión ambiental en escuelas secundarias rurales y costeras periurbanas de Yucatán, México
summary: [Introduction]: Environmental management in schools in Latin America faces obstacles such as the absence of policies, inadequate waste management, and limited teacher training. International and Latin American backgrounds show progress, alt
content: [Introduction]: Environmental management in schools in Latin America faces obstacles such as the absence of policies, inadequate waste management, and limited teacher training. International and Latin American backgrounds show progress, although with limitations in continuity and curricular integration. In response, this study proposes a flexible Environmental Management Program based on ISO 14001 in two secondary schools with contrasting social and economic contexts in the state of Yucatán, Mexico. [Objective]: To evaluate the feasibility of an Environmental Management Program in two secondary schools with contrasting contexts: one located in a rural area with a strong Mayan identity and the other in a coastal peri-urban area affected by tourism. [Methodology]: A qualitative, descriptive, and cross-sectional study was conducted involving 54 members of the leadership, administrative, and teaching staff, utilizing field observation, interviews, an ISO 14001-based checklist, SWOT analysis, and a risk matrix. [Results]: Challenges identified at the coastal peri-urban school included environmental awareness, waste accumulation, and the vulnerability of the immediate mangrove and wetland environment. The rural school faced limitations regarding infrastructure, water and energy use, and waste management. Both institutions lacked formalized environmental policies, systematic recycling programs, and mechanisms for evaluating environmental performance. [Conclusions]: The findings indicate that implementing an EMP requires context-specific strategies: in the rural school, priorities include strengthening basic infrastructure and improving resource management; in the peri-urban coastal school, priorities include environmental awareness, waste management, and coordination with external stakeholders. The study provides context-specific recommendations to guide the implementation of environmental management programs in schools with similar conditions.

title: The Kadro Movement: A Search for National Socialism After the Great Depression
summary: This study aims to analyze the political practice of the Kadro movement in the context of the early Republican period in Türkiye. Examining the problematic relationship of the Kadro movement with segments of the Turkish bourgeoisie and land
content: This study aims to analyze the political practice of the Kadro movement in the context of the early Republican period in Türkiye. Examining the problematic relationship of the Kadro movement with segments of the Turkish bourgeoisie and landowners, this study attempts to show how the Kadro group tried to realize its statist projects through strategic articulations and conflicts. In this context, the ideological, economic, and political theses developed by the Kadro journal, their organizational forms, and the oscillation of these theses between nationalism and socialism are investigated in depth, and this movement is evaluated as an alternative version of the national socialist constructions that emerged after the 1929 World Economic Depression.

title: Anchoring in the Storm: How Does Digital Intelligence Technology Foster Green Innovation Resilience?
summary: Abstract In an era characterized by dual transformations and climate-induced turbulence, manufacturing firms are compelled to shift their strategic paradigm from static "green growth" to dynamic "green survival." Based on data from Chinese
content: Abstract In an era characterized by dual transformations and climate-induced turbulence, manufacturing firms are compelled to shift their strategic paradigm from static "green growth" to dynamic "green survival." Based on data from Chinese A-share manufacturing listed companies from 2012 to 2023, this study empirically examines the impact mechanisms and boundary conditions of digital intelligence technology on green innovation resilience. The findings indicate that: (1) Digital intelligence technology significantly enhances the green innovation resilience of manufacturing firms. (2) Mechanism tests reveal that digital intelligence technology empowers green innovation resilience through a dual pathway of alleviating financing constraints and improving managerial efficiency. (3) Climate risk attention plays a critical moderating role in this process; specifically, it significantly enhances the marginal contributions of financing constraint alleviation and managerial efficiency improvement to green innovation resilience. (4) Heterogeneity analysis shows that the empowering effect is more pronounced in non-high-tech, non-heavy-polluting, and high-competition industries, as well as in Eastern-based, non-labor-intensive, and upstream firms. This study reveals that only by achieving strategic alignment between digital capabilities and subjective risk perception can firms effectively coordinate resources to maintain green innovation resilience.

title: Explainable AI and ESG analytics for sustainable investment decision: the roles of ESG forecast credibility and trust in AI-generated information
summary: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming sustainable investing, yet limited evidence explains how AI capabilities influence investors stated preferences and willingness toward sustainable investment. Methods This study deve
content: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming sustainable investing, yet limited evidence explains how AI capabilities influence investors stated preferences and willingness toward sustainable investment. Methods This study develops and empirically tests a sequential behavioural framework explaining how AI-related characteristics influence investors stated sustainable investment preferences through perceived ESG forecast credibility and trust in AI-generated ESG information, using survey data from 566 middle-income retail investors across four Indian metropolitan cities. Results The findings reveal that explainable AI and ESG analytics capability significantly enhance perceived ESG forecast credibility, which sequentially strengthens trust in AI-generated ESG information and is associated with stronger stated preferences and willingness toward sustainable investment. Perceived Greenwashing Risk weakens the positive relationship between Perceived ESG Forecast Credibility and Trust in AI-generated ESG Information, while the interaction between Human-AI Interaction Competency and Trust in AI-generated ESG Information is statistically significant but negligible in practical magnitude (f 2 = 0.012) in relation to Sustainable Investment Decision. Discussion The study provides actionable guidance for AI developers, financial institutions, and policymakers to enhance transparency, credibility, investor trust, and responsible AI-enabled sustainable finance.

title: Can compassion drive firm innovativeness through organizational trust?
summary: Purpose This paper addresses the escalating issue of suffering within organizations, emphasizing the pivotal role of compassion in mitigating the detrimental impacts of workplace suffering and enhancing the mental well-being of employees. C
content: Purpose This paper addresses the escalating issue of suffering within organizations, emphasizing the pivotal role of compassion in mitigating the detrimental impacts of workplace suffering and enhancing the mental well-being of employees. Contrary to existing literature that has primarily focused on individual well-being, we propose to explore the broader organizational implications of compassion, specifically its influence on innovativeness. Design/methodology/approach To investigate the intricate relationship between organizational compassion and firm innovativeness, we employ a structural equation model. Our study encompasses a sample of Spanish companies spanning various sectors. A key element in our analysis is the inclusion of organizational trust as a mediator, aiming to elucidate how compassion at work might impact firm innovativeness through this intermediary variable. Findings The results of our study demonstrate a positive correlation between compassion at work and firm innovativeness. Moreover, we reveal that the influence of organizational compassion on innovativeness is mediated by organizational trust. This indirect pathway underscores the significance of trust in translating compassionate workplace practices into enhanced firm innovativeness. Originality/value This research contributes to the existing literature by offering a novel perspective on how organizational compassion drives innovation. Specifically, it demonstrates that compassion enhances firm innovativeness both directly and indirectly through the mediating role of organizational trust. By doing so, the study bridges emotional and strategic dimensions within organizational processes – an integration rarely addressed in prior research. While previous studies have primarily focused on the benefits of compassion for individual well-being, this paper shifts the focus to its broader organizational implications, particularly its impact on innovation outcomes. This expanded lens advances the academic discourse on compassionate practices by emphasizing their relevance not only for employee care, but also for enhancing strategic performance.

title: Systematic benchmarking of oversampling, undersampling, and hybrid sampling techniques using SMOTE-CCU+ with statistical validation and ablation analysis
summary: Abstract The persistent challenge of class imbalance continues to hinder predictive accuracy and fairness in Educational Data Mining (EDM), particularly in modelling academic performance and student behaviour. In this study, we present a co
content: Abstract The persistent challenge of class imbalance continues to hinder predictive accuracy and fairness in Educational Data Mining (EDM), particularly in modelling academic performance and student behaviour. In this study, we present a comprehensive benchmark of resampling strategies encompassing oversampling, undersampling, and hybrid approaches to evaluate their effectiveness in improving classification performance across diverse educational contexts. We trained and evaluated five machine learning classifiers (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Support Vector Classifier) on two complementary datasets: a structured academic performance dataset and a publicly available heterogeneous behavioral dataset. To address imbalance-induced bias, we propose a novel hybrid resampling technique, SMOTE-CCU + (Synthetic Minority Oversampling and Cluster Centroid Undersampling Plus), which integrates DBSCAN-based minority filtering, distance-weighted synthetic sample generation, adaptive centroid undersampling (CCU), and Tomek Link boundary refinement. This multi-stage pipeline enhances minority representation while preserving decision-boundary integrity, thereby improving model generalisation. Our experimental results demonstrate that SMOTE-CCU + consistently outperformed established methods (SMOTE, ADASYN, ENN, and CCU) across all evaluation metrics, particularly in the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), the most reliable indicator of discriminative performance under imbalance. Notably, while tree-based models achieved near-perfect performance even without resampling due to their inherent robustness to class imbalance, SVC’s MCC improved dramatically from 0.000 to 0.986 when paired with SMOTE-CCU + , demonstrating its critical role for classifiers sensitive to imbalance. To ensure rigorous statistical validation, we applied three complementary frameworks: the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test with effect size estimation ( $$r = Z/\sqrt{N}$$ ), the Friedman test for multi-group comparison, and Nemenyi post-hoc analysis with critical difference diagrams. The Friedman test confirmed statistically significant differences among sampling strategies on both datasets (primary: $$\chi ^2 = 11.50$$ , $$p = 0.042$$ ; secondary: $$\chi ^2 = 14.07$$ , $$p = 0.015$$ ), while 24 out of 25 pairwise Wilcoxon comparisons yielded large effect sizes ( $$r \ge 0.50$$ ), confirming practical superiority independent of sample size constraints. Our ablation study revealed that DBSCAN filtering is the critical differentiator of the pipeline, while CCU and Tomek Links provide structural refinement most pronounced under noisy, heterogeneous conditions. Computational time analysis further confirmed that SMOTE-CCU + is the most efficient resampling method evaluated (0.036s on the secondary dataset training partition), faster than SMOTE, ENN, ADASYN, and CCU, confirming its suitability for practical deployment.
