title: The evolution of spatial organisation of state constructed apartment buildings in Hungary 1945-1989
summary: The devastation of World War II and the decline in housing construction led to a housing shortage across Europe. The situation was exacerbated by the number of rural folks and political refugees moving to the cities as a result of industria
content: The devastation of World War II and the decline in housing construction led to a housing shortage across Europe. The situation was exacerbated by the number of rural folks and political refugees moving to the cities as a result of industrialisation. Industrialisation also led to the development of towns and cities organised around new factories. In Eastern Europe, the construction of housing estates became a dominant feature in the four decades following the Second World War, not only as a method of alleviating housing shortages but also as a way of expressing the socialist ideal of the state, which emphasised social welfare as propaganda, and of expressing the capacity to perform. This led to significant changes in regional settlement patterns, contributing to urbanisation, which not only resulted in densification but also in expansionary growth. The focus of construction has been on both the rehabilitation of urban cores and the emergence of intensive new urban structures in expanding peripheral areas - both processes have led to the creation of urbanising residential areas that provided better living conditions for millions of people. In our study, we examine the housing stock of sub-central systems in empty urban peripheral areas that have implemented modern urban planning principles without constraints - tracing the evolution of typologised housing quality through the development of the basic tenets of urban planning. The article is based on contemporary literature on housing estates built under state socialism, supplemented with archival records and recent publications.

title: A ‘brain-first’ mouse model of progressive alpha-synuclein pathology via intranasal rotenone administration
summary: The precise etiology of Parkinson’s disease (PD) is still poorly understood, but it is thought to arise due to an intricate relationship between genes and the environment. Our study takes a unique approach to understanding the effect of env
content: The precise etiology of Parkinson’s disease (PD) is still poorly understood, but it is thought to arise due to an intricate relationship between genes and the environment. Our study takes a unique approach to understanding the effect of environmental factors on the onset and progression of α-synuclein (aSyn) pathology, a key feature of PD, from the olfactory bulb (OB) to other brain regions. In the present study, we evaluated the time-dependent progression of PD-like pathology by administering rotenone intranasally for 5.5 months in C57BL/6 male mice. We performed olfactory and motor tests and examined aSyn accumulation, glial cell activation, and dopaminergic (DAergic) neurodegeneration after 3, 4, and 5.5 months of rotenone exposure by immunoblotting and immunofluorescence techniques. We observed a time-dependent progression of aSyn accumulation from the OB to other brain regions, including the mid-brain and cortex. Consistently, we observed a time-dependent behavioral impairment, OB atrophy, progression of aSyn pathology, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration. Our findings also established a link between distinct astrocyte activation and DAergic activity. In conclusion, this chronic and progressive mouse model mimics the brain-first type of progression of PD-like pathology in some PD patients, opening the possibility for testing potential disease-modifying interventions.

title: Waste(d) commons, transversal toxicity, and environmental (in)justice in Eastern Europe case studies from Câmpulung and Băicoi
summary: This article examines environmental injustice and waste economies in post-socialist Eastern Europe through case studies of Câmpulung and Băicoi, Romania. Drawing on environmental justice, anthropology, post-socialist studies, and 44 semi-st
content: This article examines environmental injustice and waste economies in post-socialist Eastern Europe through case studies of Câmpulung and Băicoi, Romania. Drawing on environmental justice, anthropology, post-socialist studies, and 44 semi-structured interviews, we analyze how toxic waste accumulation, weak regulation, post-industrial decline, global waste flows, and class dynamics intersect. We develop the concept of the “double communality of waste.” First, we argue that waste functions as a “negative commons,” as its harmful effects are collectively shared despite fragmented responsibility. Second, we argue that post-socialist transformations have “wasted” former industrial and social commons through privatization, deindustrialization, and the erosion of collective infrastructures and values. Our analysis makes three key observations. First , waste invites waste: initial dumping, enabled by weak governance and uneven development, generates self-reinforcing cycles attracting further accumulation and integration into transnational waste networks. In short, where there is waste—where public infrastructure, nature, or human lives are “wasted”—more waste is created. Second , repeated cycles of contamination and limited resistance normalize environmental harm, rendering waste an ordinary condition of everyday life. Third , we conceptualize these dynamics as “transversal toxicity,” where material pollution converges with neglect, corruption, anticommunist discourses, and an economy reproducing dependency and inequality: the dumping of toxic materials is enabled by “toxic” corruption and political carelessness, unnuanced anticommunism and the indictment of any retrospective gaze, ultimately encouraged by a “toxic” economic model that lays waste to human lives and formerly thriving industrial communities.

title: Otra vuelta a la tuerca sobre la vivienda contemporánea
There is no ‘grid’: Configuring everyday sanitation in Tamale, Ghana
summary: This paper interrogates the growing use of the term “off-grid sanitation” in describing service provision in southern cities. While the “off-grid” imaginary originates in northern infrastructural contexts (particularly energy and electricit
content: This paper interrogates the growing use of the term “off-grid sanitation” in describing service provision in southern cities. While the “off-grid” imaginary originates in northern infrastructural contexts (particularly energy and electricity) it has become a widely used descriptor for sanitation systems that lack sewerage connections in southern cities. Drawing on interviews, group discussions and observations in Tamale, Ghana (a city that never had gridded or networked sanitation and where people do not aspire to one), we seek to re-situate their sanitation practices as infrastructural configurations guided by labour, spatiality and negotiation rather than an absence of a ‘grid’. Theoretically, we draw upon and add to the broader discourse on infrastructural labour, adding attention to the ideas of spatiality and negotiation in sustaining everyday management of sanitation in Tamale. In doing so, we show that sanitation in Tamale is not captured by a binary of connection or disconnection to a ‘grid’, rather that access falls unevenly across gender, age, mobility, and class, producing differentiated negotiations, that ‘off-grid’ framings obscure. This framing decentres northern imaginaries, instead it offers a more explicit, grounded analytic of the labour intensive, spatially contingent and daily negotiated sanitation realities, for a more situated understanding of sanitation infrastructural configurations in southern cities.

title: AI empowerment and supervisory board effectiveness: Evidence from an information processing framework
summary: In the context of rapid digitalization and intelligent governance, artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly embedded in organizational supervision and decision-making processes, fundamentally reshaping how supervisory boar
content: In the context of rapid digitalization and intelligent governance, artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are increasingly embedded in organizational supervision and decision-making processes, fundamentally reshaping how supervisory boards process information and perform monitoring tasks. Drawing on information processing theory, this study develops a moderated mediation model to examine how AI empowerment is associated with supervisory board effectiveness through information transparency, and how this process is contingent upon organizational learning capability. Using survey data collected from 382 supervisory board members and senior managers across multiple industries, this study adopts an organizational-level perspective and employs hierarchical regression and bootstrap analyses to test the proposed hypotheses. The results show that AI empowerment significantly associated with both information transparency and supervisory board effectiveness. Information transparency partially mediates the relationship between AI empowerment and supervisory effectiveness, indicating that AI is positively associated with supervisory performance by optimizing organizational information-processing mechanisms. Moreover, organizational learning capability positively moderates the relationship between AI empowerment and information transparency. However, the moderated mediation effect is not statistically significant, indicating that the indirect effect of AI empowerment on supervisory effectiveness through information transparency remains relatively stable across different levels of organizational learning capability. These findings suggest that organizational learning capability shapes the relationship between AI empowerment and information transparency, but does not significantly alter the overall indirect pathway to supervisory effectiveness.

title: Subterranean Effects of the Termite Constrictotermes cyphergaster on Soil Fungal Abundance in the Brazilian Caatinga
summary: Termites are key ecosystem engineers whose nesting activities influence soil structure, nutrient dynamics, and microbial communities, particularly in resource-limited environments. In semiarid ecosystems, where soils are typically low in or
content: Termites are key ecosystem engineers whose nesting activities influence soil structure, nutrient dynamics, and microbial communities, particularly in resource-limited environments. In semiarid ecosystems, where soils are typically low in organic carbon, termite-induced modifications may help sustain belowground biological activity. Constrictotermes cyphergaster is a widespread arboreal termite in the Brazilian Caatinga whose nests maintain consistent subterranean connections with the soil, yet the microbial implications of these structures remain poorly understood. In this study, we assessed fungal abundance in soils associated with the nesting system of C. cyphergaster at two semiarid sites with contrasting precipitation regimes and soil classes. Soil samples were collected from beneath arboreal nests, from termite-built hypogeous constructions, and from surrounding soils, and fungal density was quantified using colony-forming units. Fungal abundance differed significantly among sampling points at both sites, with higher densities consistently observed in soils influenced by termite structures compared to surrounding soils. These results suggest that the nesting system of C. cyphergaster creates localized conditions that favor fungal proliferation. Our findings highlight the ecological importance of arboreal termites with subterranean connections in structuring soil microbial communities and emphasize their potential role in maintaining soil functioning in semiarid landscapes.

title: From credibility to purchase: an S-O-R perspective on influencer marketing and social media participation in the online beauty market
summary: Cosmetics and skincare products are among the product categories strongly influenced by social media. This study applies the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework to examine influencer credibility and social media participation as tw
content: Cosmetics and skincare products are among the product categories strongly influenced by social media. This study applies the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework to examine influencer credibility and social media participation as two external stimuli associated with consumer attitude and purchase intention in the online beauty market. Data were collected through an online questionnaire from 300 Thai Generation Z consumers aged 18–24 who followed beauty influencers and had previously purchased cosmetics or skincare products online. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results showed that influencer credibility and social media participation were positively associated with consumer attitude, which was positively associated with purchase intention. Both stimuli also had significant direct relationships with purchase intention and significant indirect relationships through consumer attitude, with influencer credibility showing the stronger overall relationship. This study extends the application of the S-O-R framework in the online beauty market by examining credibility- and participation-based stimuli together. It also identifies consumer attitude as a shared psychological mechanism linking both stimuli to purchase intention. The findings provide practical guidance for cosmetics and skincare businesses in selecting influencers, developing credible content, and designing strategies to encourage consumer participation on social media.

title: The Spatial Journey: A Visual Narrative of the Keffi to Makurdi Field Trip
summary: Background: Field-based education is a critical academic component in geographical studies, designed to bridge theoretical knowledge with empirical observation. This paper reports on the development of a visual and interactive geospatial na
content: Background: Field-based education is a critical academic component in geographical studies, designed to bridge theoretical knowledge with empirical observation. This paper reports on the development of a visual and interactive geospatial narrative based on a five-day geography educational field trip from Keffi to Makurdi, Nigeria, from the 26th to the 30th of August 2024. Objective: The primary aim is to create an accessible web map utilizing collected field trip datasets. Specific objectives for this study include (i) geospatial capturing of significant features and points of interest along the route; (ii) documenting and structuring the resulting spatial, non-spatial, and multimedia datasets; and (iii) producing an animated web-based visualization and web mapping. Methodology: The study used a GPS-enabled smartphone, a handwritten field book, and a digital camera to capture 102 geotagged waypoints (latitude, longitude, altitude, and timestamp) along the route. The waypoints, together with digitized local-government and ward boundaries produced in QGIS version 3.42.2-Münster, were published as a freely accessible, layer-controlled interactive web map. Leveraging the principles of Web Cartography and Visualization (WCV), these processed layers were then integrated into an interactive web-based map hosted on a web page at: www.UmarYusuf.com/nsuk/fieldtripmap. The same field programme included structured site visits to the Benue Geographic Information Service (BENGIS), the Benue State Urban Development Board (BUDB) and the Oracle Business Limited (OBL), during which the institutional workflow for issuing a digital Certificate of Occupancy (C of O) and the use of a river-gauge station for flood early-warning were documented. Result: Results show that a low-cost smartphone-and-web-GIS pipeline can produce a citable, reproducible spatial dataset from routine fieldwork, and that the recorded geographical features were spatially distributed across nine Local Government Areas (seven in Nasarawa State and two in Benue State) and thirty-two political wards (twenty-six and six in Nasarawa and Benue states respectively). Conclusion: This study successfully demonstrates the practical application of geospatial technology in creating a robust experiential learning tool, underscoring the vital educational significance of mandatory student field excursions for fostering academic learning and recommending their continued, essential integration into the curriculum.

title: A qualitative evidence synthesis on perinatal screening for sickle cell disease in high-burden countries
summary: BACKGROUND: Sickle cell disease (SCD) screening can improve lives and reduce mortality through prevention and targeted treatment, but screening programmes are not universally available in the settings which could most benefit from them. We
content: BACKGROUND: Sickle cell disease (SCD) screening can improve lives and reduce mortality through prevention and targeted treatment, but screening programmes are not universally available in the settings which could most benefit from them. We aimed to understand the implementation considerations for prenatal and newborn SCD screening programmes in countries with a high livebirth prevalence of SCD using the socioecological model of health. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of qualitative evidence relating to prenatal and newborn screening programmes for SCD in the thirty countries with the highest SCD case to livebirth ratio. We included 18 papers published between 2004 and 2024 that covered nine countries and performed the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme Qualitative Studies Checklist on each. Through recursive interaction with our data, we interpretively developed four themes using reflexive thematic analysis and used the GRADE-CERqual method to appraise our key findings. RESULTS: We framed our results using the socioecological model of health which organizes influences on health into individual, community, and systems levels. From macro to micro levels, our themes are (1) sustainable SCD screening programmes require financial and political support from government and integration into existing healthcare infrastructure, (2) experiences of and knowledge-sharing about SCD fosters further acceptance and opportunity for newborn screening, (3), the decision to conduct a SCD test has extensive ramifications for both child and family, and (4) prenatal and newborn screening modalities offer parents of affected children different options for action. Our policy suggestions focus on planning for programme sustainability at the outset, leveraging existing community knowledge, alleviating stigma, and providing different testing options for families. CONCLUSIONS: We identified the need for more qualitative inquiry on systems-level implementation of SCD screening programmes and impact of external funding. We call for decreased stigmatization by supporting knowledge-sharing programmes grounded in local modes of understanding and recognize SCD screening decisions as both consequential to families and shaped by parents' experiences over time.

title: Employee Perceptions of Organizational Sustainability: A Systematic Review and Integrative Multilevel Framework
summary: ABSTRACT Employee perceptions are central to whether organizational sustainability initiatives become embedded in workplace practice or remain symbolic. This study reviews 123 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2000 and 2024 to clarif
content: ABSTRACT Employee perceptions are central to whether organizational sustainability initiatives become embedded in workplace practice or remain symbolic. This study reviews 123 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2000 and 2024 to clarify how employees interpret organizational sustainability and how these interpretations are associated with workplace outcomes. The findings show that perceptions are linked to individual values and capabilities, leadership signals, green HRM practices, sustainability communication, perceived authenticity, and wider stakeholder pressures. Favorable perceptions are associated with engagement, pro‐environmental behavior, creativity, and organizational citizenship for the environment, whereas perceived greenwashing or corporate hypocrisy is associated with weaker trust and commitment. Drawing on Social Exchange Theory, the Resource‐Based View, and Signaling Theory, the study proposes an association‐based multilevel framework that positions employee perceptions as the interpretive link between sustainability drivers and individual, organizational, and external outcomes.

title: Do SAE levels reflect real-world capability? A supplemental environmental-situational-capability taxonomy for L3–L4 automated driving
source: Journal of Intelligent and Connected Vehicles
summary: Abstract The widely adopted SAE (Society of Automotive Engineers) taxonomy categorizes driving automation primarily based on the division of operational responsibilities between the human driver and the system. This has worked well for seve
content: Abstract The widely adopted SAE (Society of Automotive Engineers) taxonomy categorizes driving automation primarily based on the division of operational responsibilities between the human driver and the system. This has worked well for several applications. However, it fails to distinguish the requisite versatility of autonomous vehicle (AV) performance across diverse operational environments. This structural limitation has spawned critical challenges, including safety risks, commercialization barriers, regulation challenges, and inadequate Operational Design Domain (ODD) development guidelines toward Level 5 autonomy. To address these gaps, this paper proposes a supplemental taxonomy for SAE Levels 3 and 4 using an Environmental-Situational Capability (ESC) evaluation framework across three core dimensions: the built environment, natural environment, and ambient traffic conditions. Using a two-stage hierarchical classification strategy, the ESC framework maps expert evaluations of a specific automated driving system (ADS) to corresponding levels of the proposed taxonomy. This novel classification bridges the ADS level and the ODD by correlating environmental complexity with the minimum capabilities required for safe autonomous operation. Operating orthogonally to SAE standards, this taxonomy categorizes systems based on their actual operational capabilities rather than driving automation task responsibility alone. Consequently, it establishes a crucial alignment across researchers, manufacturers, regulators, and consumers, providing a practical reference for product benchmarking, safety validation, and policymaking.

title: Boys’ Love Media Scholarship, 2000–2026: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric-Thematic Synthesis
summary: Originating in Japanese manga traditions depicting romantic relationships between men, Boys’ Love (BL) has developed into a transnational media phenomenon. Scholarship has expanded accordingly but remains fragmented across disciplines, nati
content: Originating in Japanese manga traditions depicting romantic relationships between men, Boys’ Love (BL) has developed into a transnational media phenomenon. Scholarship has expanded accordingly but remains fragmented across disciplines, national contexts, media forms, and methods. This systematic review examines 134 English-language, peer-reviewed, Scopus-indexed journal articles published between January 2000 and June 2026. Combining bibliometric mapping with a PRISMA-guided thematic synthesis, it maps geographic, temporal, thematic, and methodological patterns in the internationally indexed literature. Publication growth accelerates after 2020, accompanied by increased attention to Thai and Chinese screen media alongside continued work on Japanese manga. Four bibliometric clusters are interpreted through eight analytical themes: fandom and audiences; state, censorship, and regulation; representation and narrative; gender, sexuality, and feminist critique; industry, political economy, and soft power; transnational circulation and localization; genre history and aesthetics; and affect, emotion, and intimacy. Qualitative approaches dominate the corpus, whereas quantitative and mixed-method designs remain comparatively uncommon. Country-related patterns are treated as descriptive author-affiliation tendencies rather than statistical country-theme relationships. The review identifies four priorities: deeper production and political-economy analysis, stronger examination of multidirectional transnational circulation, broader geographic and linguistic coverage, and greater methodological diversity. It further argues that intercultural BL scholarship would benefit from moving beyond nation-bounded localization models toward transcultural and counter-flow perspectives.

title: Counting the cost: The impact of five years of high inflation on living standards
summary: This briefing note takes stock of five years of successive cost of living crises, examining how the surge in prices since 2021 has hit household incomes, finances and living standards across the income distribution. It also assesses how a n
content: This briefing note takes stock of five years of successive cost of living crises, examining how the surge in prices since 2021 has hit household incomes, finances and living standards across the income distribution. It also assesses how a new energy shock, triggered by the war with Iran, will add to that damage. It argues that the Government should focus fresh support tightly on the poorest households, starting with help on energy bills.

title: Trends and developments in individual financial fraud research: a bibliometric study
summary: Purpose Financial fraud targeting individuals has received considerably less scholarly attention than business or organizational fraud. The current study addresses this gap by presenting a simple classification scheme for individual financi
content: Purpose Financial fraud targeting individuals has received considerably less scholarly attention than business or organizational fraud. The current study addresses this gap by presenting a simple classification scheme for individual financial fraud (IFF) and systematically examining the evolution of research in this domain. Design/methodology/approach This study analyzes 248 articles from the Scopus database published between 1972 and 2024. The study employs a bibliometric approach and uses tools such as R Biblioshiny and VOSviewer to conduct performance analysis and science mapping. Findings The analysis identifies Marcus Antanas Butavicius as the most prolific contributor to the IFF literature and Rui Chen as the most cited author. Bibliographic coupling reveals three key clusters in the literature: investment fraud, phishing scams and deceptive advertising. A focused content analysis of the clusters highlights victimization patterns associated with the fraud types and identifies gaps for future research. Research limitations/implications The current study is limited to English-language articles indexed in Scopus. Practical implications The findings identify key types of fraud, supporting targeted fraud prevention and awareness efforts for researchers, policymakers and practitioners. Social implications This study fosters consumer awareness and endeavors to protect individuals from financial harm. Originality/value This study offers a comprehensive bibliometric overview of the field and aims to position IFF within mainstream academic research, facilitating a deeper understanding and classification of this emerging domain.

title: Impacting Green Finance on Sustainable Agricultural Development: Evidence from Vietnam
summary: The transition toward sustainable agriculture requires substantial financial resources aligned with environmental and social objectives. Green finance has emerged as a critical instrument for mobilizing such resources; however, the mechanis
content: The transition toward sustainable agriculture requires substantial financial resources aligned with environmental and social objectives. Green finance has emerged as a critical instrument for mobilizing such resources; however, the mechanisms by which institutional, technological, and market forces shape green finance and translate into sustainable agricultural development remain underexplored, particularly in emerging economies. This study investigates the determinants of green finance and its role in promoting sustainable agricultural development in Vietnam. Using a mixed-methods approach, qualitative interviews with 45 experts in green farm economics and agrarian project financing were conducted first to develop context-specific measurement scales. Subsequently, a large-scale survey of 900 respondents from farm cooperatives, agricultural enterprises, green project participants, and green supply chain actors was conducted. The proposed research model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that environmental regulation pressure is the most influential driver of green finance, followed by stakeholder and market ESG pressure and digital financial inclusion. Green finance significantly promotes sustainable agricultural development and serves as a key transmission mechanism linking institutional, technological, and market factors to sustainability outcomes. Moreover, green supply chain requirements and ESG governance and transparency significantly strengthen the effectiveness of green finance and policy instruments. This study contributes to the literature by integrating green finance, ESG governance, and supply chain perspectives into a unified framework and provides important policy implications for promoting sustainable agriculture in emerging economies.

title: Sense and Sensibility: Sensible Quality Control and Data Decision-Making in Passive Sensing Data for Adolescent Substance Use Risk Prediction
summary: Background: Passively collected smartphone and wearable data, combined with genomic information, may enable scalable early identification of youth who are at risk for substance use disorder. However, heterogeneous data collected in naturali
content: Background: Passively collected smartphone and wearable data, combined with genomic information, may enable scalable early identification of youth who are at risk for substance use disorder. However, heterogeneous data collected in naturalistic settings limit researcher control over data quality, requiring substantial preprocessing. Data cleaning and feature engineering decisions can meaningfully influence analytic outcomes yet are often minimally described or omitted in published work. Objectives: We provide rationales and recommendations for common preprocessing challenges in passive sensing research, including establishing inclusion criteria when "outliers" may reflect true behavioral variability, analyzing differences across smartphone operating systems, handling observations collected outside protocol windows, and engineering features for machine learning applications. Methods: We illustrate principled approaches to these challenges using smartphone and Fitbit data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (ABCD). The sample was drawn from the available half of the year-4 follow-up (data release 5.1; N = 4,754; ages 13-14). Results: Extreme outlying observations were concentrated among low-engagement participants with few observed days. Smartphone usage among Apple users appeared under-recorded relative to Android users when compared with self-report measures. Fitbit-derived behavior differed systematically between observations collected within versus outside protocol windows. We also identified potential errors in the study's default preprocessing pipeline. Conclusion: We recommend prioritizing person-level inclusion criteria that preserve meaningful behavioral variability, examining temporal distributions rather than assuming observations are exchangeable, and thoroughly investigating and reporting data quality issues. Although illustrated using the ABCD Study, these principles broadly apply to research using smartphones, wearables, and other digital data sources.

title: An Explainable Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM with Attention for Phishing Email Detection
source: Journal of Applied Science and Technology Trends
summary: Phishing emails are one of the most serious cybersecurity threats, using evolving social engineering techniques to steal sensitive information and cause financial losses. In this study, a hybrid deep learning framework is proposed to classi
content: Phishing emails are one of the most serious cybersecurity threats, using evolving social engineering techniques to steal sensitive information and cause financial losses. In this study, a hybrid deep learning framework is proposed to classify phishing emails in binary and multiclass settings. It combines a CNN-BiLSTM architecture with multi-head self-attention and handcrafted features specifically designed for phishing detection. The study combined different sources of public emails into a single multi-source dataset with a wide variety of examples, including legitimate, phishing, spam and fraud emails. This incorporation makes an important contribution to the research. The proposed framework integrates contextual linguistic representations with domain-specific features. These features are extracted from various elements, including the URL, sender-receiver interactions, email header, temporal data, keywords, and formatting characteristics, all processed through parallel branches. The framework was tested using both binary and multiclass classification settings. It was also compared to traditional deep learning models and Transformer-based baseline models. The proposed model attained an accuracy of 99.41% and a ROC-AUC of 99.97% in binary classification. In multiclass, it achieved 98.79% accuracy and a ROC-AUC of 99.90%. In addition, the model achieved macro-F1 and weighted-F1 scores of 98.55% and 98.79%, respectively. The ablation analysis validated the roles of multi-head attention and handcrafted features. To improve model interpretability, we used LIME and SHAP to quantitatively evaluate the impact of features on prediction confidence. The results show consistent, and robust performance in the experimental and validation settings and indicate the proposed frameworks potential applicability to practical phishing email detection.

title: What are the configuration paths for improving the business performance of land trusteeship enterprises?
summary: To promote the growth of agricultural enterprises and enhance their ability to collaborate with and benefit farmers, improving the business performance of land trusteeship enterprises has become an urgent issue. Drawing on the perspective o
content: To promote the growth of agricultural enterprises and enhance their ability to collaborate with and benefit farmers, improving the business performance of land trusteeship enterprises has become an urgent issue. Drawing on the perspective of interest linkage mechanism and employing fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis method, this paper explores pathways for enhancing the business performance of land trusteeship enterprises, then conducting a series of heterogeneity analyses and robustness tests. The main findings are as follows. No component is individually necessary. Two configurations are sufficient for high performance: cooperative trust combined with resource sharing, and cooperative trust combined with mutual benefit. The configurations associated with low performance are structurally distinct from the negation of these pathways, confirming causal asymmetry. Sub-sample analyses show that the sufficient configuration shifts systematically with governance architecture and service breadth: mutual benefit is pivotal where enterprises contract with households directly, resource sharing becomes pivotal once a cooperative or village collective mediates the relationship, and full-item providers require all three components jointly. These findings can provide guidance for improving the operational performance of land trusteeship enterprises. Unlike the regression only to analyze the net effect of individual influencing factors, this study based on perspective of interest linkage mechanism to examine the coupled effects of multiple influencing factors.

title: The Belt and Road Initiative and its competitors: a comparison between BRI and Global Gateway
summary: Purpose The paper presents a comparison of China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and the EU’ Global Gateway (GG). Design/methodology/approach The paper undertakes an economic and institutional comparison of China's BRI and EU's GG to asses
content: Purpose The paper presents a comparison of China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and the EU’ Global Gateway (GG). Design/methodology/approach The paper undertakes an economic and institutional comparison of China's BRI and EU's GG to assess their differences and similarities and their effect on developing countries. Findings China's strategy was successful, but with time it met with some economic and political difficulties. So far GG was unable to really compete with BRI, although it may offer an interesting complement to developing countries and feeble chances of cooperation between the two initiatives. Originality/value The comparison between BRI and GG concentrates on facts and achievements, including the accuracy of criticism and prize for each of the two initiatives, but avoids political and partisan judgements.

title: Strategic Brand Management
summary: The book comprehensively covers the subject of brand management in a fiercely competitive market environment. In an age in which brand is the most valuable asset in a business, the book discusses, with illustrations, the process of building
content: The book comprehensively covers the subject of brand management in a fiercely competitive market environment. In an age in which brand is the most valuable asset in a business, the book discusses, with illustrations, the process of building and protecting brands, what it takes for a popular name to become a brand, and then, a power brand. With relevant case studies and examples, particularly of fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), this volume provides strategic directions and lessons for creating and developing brands that can stand test of the time. It also expounds on building brand equity in challenging times, brand extension, brand strategy as well brand accounting and valuation. The book also covers strategies for building service brands -- marketing strategies and processes have changed over time with technology and brands now must be built through social media and digital marketing, which is discussed comprehensively with cases in this title. The book will be useful to students and teachers of Marketing, Advertising and Brand Management, Business Studies, Business Communication, Media and Journalism and Public Relations. It will also be an invaluable resource for brand marketers and practitioners.
