title: Davlat-xususiy sheriklik asosida ijtimoiy soha infratuzilmasini rivojlantirishda "value for money" (VfM) baholash mexanizmini takomillashtirish
summary: This article investigates the theoretical, methodological, and practical dimensions of the 'Value for Money' (VfM) assessment methodology in delivering social infrastructure (education, healthcare, public utilities) through Public-Private P
content: This article investigates the theoretical, methodological, and practical dimensions of the 'Value for Money' (VfM) assessment methodology in delivering social infrastructure (education, healthcare, public utilities) through Public-Private Partnerships (PPP). Comparing standard procurement models via the Public Sector Comparator (PSC) benchmark against PPP alternatives represents a cornerstone in ensuring fiscal prudence and optimizing lifecycle expenditure. Drawing on recent social infrastructure modernization initiatives in Uzbekistan, the paper evaluates current qualitative and quantitative VfM practices. Furthermore, based on international best practices, comprehensive policy recommendations are provided to enhance project selection, standardize appraisal frameworks, and elevate public service quality.

title: Does Pay Drive Performance? A PLS-SEM Analysis of Compensation and Employee Outcomes in Nepal
source: Quest Journal of Management and Social Sciences
summary: Background: Compensation is an important human resource management practice that influences employees’ motivation, job satisfaction, and performance. In Nepal’s private sector, organizations need effective compensation systems to attract, r
content: Background: Compensation is an important human resource management practice that influences employees’ motivation, job satisfaction, and performance. In Nepal’s private sector, organizations need effective compensation systems to attract, retain, and motivate employees. Understanding the relationship between financial and non-financial compensation and employee performance can support organizations in developing effective employee management practices. Purpose: The purpose of the study is to identify the impact of compensation on employee performance for private sector in Nepal. Specifically, the study tries to identify the current status of compensation package on employee performance, to examine the impact of compensation status on employee performance and to assess the mediating role of job satisfaction and motivation in relationship between compensation and employee performance. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopted an explanatory research design. Equity theory is used for major study because it gives comprehensive insight about compensation model. The primary data for this study was collected from 405 respondents, using a non-probability convenience sampling method. Structured questions were administered through the KOBO toolbox to gather the necessary information. The collected data was then analyzed using descriptive and inferential analysis using MS Excel and Smart PLS 4.0. Findings: The relationship between employee performance, job satisfaction, and motivation is well-established. This study concludes that financial compensation, non-financial compensation, employee motivation and job satisfaction have a positive and significant relationship with employee performance Conclusion: Compensation plays a crucial role in enhancing employee motivation, which in turn influences job satisfaction. When employees feel fairly compensated, they are more likely to be motivated, leading to improved job satisfaction and ultimately better performance. Therefore, adequate compensation can act as a powerful driver for motivating employees and enhancing their overall work output. Keywords: Compensation, job satisfaction, employee motivation, employee performance, financial compensation, non- financial compensation.

title: The development finance regime complex and crisis response: a comparative perspective of multilateral development banks’ response to COVID-19
source: Journal of International Relations and Development
summary: Abstract This article explains variation in multilateral development banks’ (MDBs) crisis-response policies during the COVID-19 crisis. Drawing on a focused, structured comparison of 22 MDBs, this study analyzes five crisis-response policie
content: Abstract This article explains variation in multilateral development banks’ (MDBs) crisis-response policies during the COVID-19 crisis. Drawing on a focused, structured comparison of 22 MDBs, this study analyzes five crisis-response policies: investment scale-ups and resource repurposing; institutional restructuring; fast-track facilities and procedures; policy and scope expansions; and inter-institutional collaboration and orchestration. It argues that MDBs’ crisis responses were shaped not only by institutional capacity but also by competitive pressures and hierarchical positioning within the development finance regime complex. MDBs occupying higher positions in the hierarchy demonstrated greater flexibility and were more likely to scale up lending, introduce expedited procedures, and expand operational scope, while lower-positioned MDBs adopted more cautious strategies and relied more heavily on cooperation with established MDBs. The analysis shows that some of this variation takes the form of patterned convergence in policy choices within hierarchical tiers and benchmarking practices across them, suggesting that hierarchy conditions both competition and coordination among MDBs during fast-moving crises and helps explain variation in countercyclical responses.

title: Retaining the Next Generation: A PLS-SEM Study of Factors Influencing Gen Z Employee Retention in Nepal's Corporate Sector
source: Quest Journal of Management and Social Sciences
summary: Background: Employee retention is increasingly challenging as Generation Z enters the corporate workforce with distinct expectations regarding career growth, compensation, supervisory support, organizational culture, and work–life balance.
content: Background: Employee retention is increasingly challenging as Generation Z enters the corporate workforce with distinct expectations regarding career growth, compensation, supervisory support, organizational culture, and work–life balance. Understanding these factors is essential for organizations seeking to retain young employees and strengthen workforce stability. Purpose: The purpose of the study is to identify employee retention among Gen Z employees in the corporate sector of Nepal. The research also includes specific objectives and they are to identify the factors affecting the employee retention, to identify the effectiveness of retention strategies implied by the companies to retain the Gen Z employee and to access the challenges faced by employee to retain the corporate sector for a longer period in Nepal. Design/methodology/approach: This study adopted an explanatory research design. Social Exchange Theory (SET) is used for the study as it explains the relationships between employers and employees as a series of exchanges where both parties seek to maximize benefits and minimize costs. Primary data was collected from 404 respondents, using a non-probability purposive sampling method. Structured questionnaire was administered through KOBO toolbox to gather the necessary information, and the collected data was then analyzed using descriptive and inferential analysis using MS Excel and Smart PLS 4.0. Findings: The study reveals that corporate sectors in Nepal lack proper implementation of retention strategies and those which implement retention strategies are not focusing on core challenges the employees are facing. The main challenge preventing young employees from staying with the company is the lack of career development and growth opportunities. Conclusion: This study tested four hypotheses on the relationship between organization culture, pay, supervisor support, work life balance and Gen Z employee retention in the corporate sector and concludes that pay, supervisor support and work life balance have a significant relationship with Gen Z employee retention whereas organization culture has no significant impact on the retention of the employees.

title: JUDICIAL REVIEW AND CIVIL APPEALS: COMMON GROUNDS
summary: Abstract A civil appeal from a judicial decision is different from a judicial review of an administrative decision. But how are they different, exactly? One common view is that the grounds of appeal are more extensive than the common law gr
content: Abstract A civil appeal from a judicial decision is different from a judicial review of an administrative decision. But how are they different, exactly? One common view is that the grounds of appeal are more extensive than the common law grounds of judicial review. Specifically, appeal concerns the merits of a decision whereas review concerns only its legality. I argue that this common view is false. All the grounds of appeal are, in fact, also grounds of review. The implication is that review concerns the merits of a decision at least as much as appeal does.

title: Just-In-Time Practices and the Operational Performance of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises in Taraba State, Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: This study examines the effects of Just-in-Time (JIT) purchasing, production, and selling on cost reduction, product quality, and responsiveness among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Taraba State, Nigeria. Grounded in the Re
content: This study examines the effects of Just-in-Time (JIT) purchasing, production, and selling on cost reduction, product quality, and responsiveness among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Taraba State, Nigeria. Grounded in the Resource-Based View, the study addresses two gaps in the JIT literature: the near-absence of MSME-focused evidence and the tendency to treat JIT and firm performance as aggregate rather than disaggregated constructs. Using a quantitative survey design, structured questionnaires were administered to 400 MSME employees across five Local Government Areas selected through stratified systematic sampling; 380 valid responses (95% response rate) were analysed using descriptive statistics and simple linear regression in SPSS 25. JIT purchasing had a strong, statistically and practically significant positive effect on cost reduction (β = 0.653, R² = 0.426, p < .001). JIT selling had a moderate positive effect on responsiveness (β = 0.387, R² = 0.150, p < .001). JIT production had a statistically significant but practically negligible effect on product quality (β = 0.173, R² = 0.030, p = .001). Limited financial resources (33%) and adverse economic/policy conditions (30%) were the most frequently cited implementation barriers. The findings indicate that relational JIT capabilities (purchasing and selling) generate stronger performance advantages than internal production capabilities among resource-constrained MSMEs, extending the boundary conditions of the Resource-Based View to a developing economy MSME context. The study recommends that MSMEs prioritise supplier relationships and demand-responsive selling, while policymakers target financing and infrastructure constraints that limit the returns to JIT production investment.

title: Unlocking Employee Performance Through Internal Marketing: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Organizational Commitment in Nepal's Service Industry
source: Quest Journal of Management and Social Sciences
summary: Background: Employee performance is critical to service organizations, where employee attitudes and organizational support can directly shape service delivery. Internal marketing practices such as empowerment, rewards, supportive supervisor
content: Background: Employee performance is critical to service organizations, where employee attitudes and organizational support can directly shape service delivery. Internal marketing practices such as empowerment, rewards, supportive supervisor relationships, and career opportunities can strengthen organizational commitment and enhance employee performance. However, limited evidence exists on these relationships in Nepal’s service industry, particularly regarding the mediating role of organizational commitment. Purpose: This study investigates the impact of internal marketing practices on job performance, incorporating organizational commitment as a mediating variable. Specifically, it aims to examine the factors of internal marketing influencing job performance in the service industry, identify the challenges faced by employees, and assess managerial solutions to address these challenges. Design/methodology/approach: Grounded in Social Exchange Theory, an explanatory research design was used to collect data from 391 respondents in Kathmandu Valley's service industry through purposive sampling, and the data were analyzed using PLS-SEM in Smart PLS 4.0. Findings: Results show that empowerment (β = 0.247, p = 0.000), reward (β = 0.225, p = 0.001), relationship with supervisors (β = 0.275, p = 0.000), and internal promotion (β = 0.144, p = 0.005) significantly predict organizational commitment, which in turn strongly predicts job performance (β = 0.730, p = 0.000), collectively explaining 72.9% of the variance in organizational commitment. Working environment did not significantly predict organizational commitment (β = 0.065, p = 0.253). Conclusions: The study concludes that internal promotion, empowerment, relationship with supervisors, and reward play a crucial role in shaping organizational commitment, which subsequently drives job performance. Key challenges identified include work-life balance issues, communication gaps, unclear roles and responsibilities, lack of recognition and appreciation, and ineffective performance management, with regular communication, flexibility, and clearly defined roles emerging as the most favored solutions.

title: Pengaruh Keuangan Berkelanjutan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan dengan Profitabilitas Sebagai Variabel Mediasi pada Sektor Perbankan di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) 2020-2024
summary: Sustainable finance has become an important part of the banking sector's strategy as attention to environmental, social, and governance aspects increases in creating long-term corporate value. This study aims to analyze the influence of sus
content: Sustainable finance has become an important part of the banking sector's strategy as attention to environmental, social, and governance aspects increases in creating long-term corporate value. This study aims to analyze the influence of sustainable finance, as proxied by Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), on firm value, analyze the influence of ESG on profitability and profitability on firm value, and examine the role of profitability as a mediating variable. The study uses a quantitative approach with secondary data sourced from annual reports, sustainability reports, and stock price data of banking companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2020–2024 period. The sample was determined using a purposive sampling technique, resulting in 10 companies with 50 observations. ESG disclosure was measured using content analysis based on 15 indicators adapted from the 2021 GRI Standards. Profitability was proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), while firm value was proxied by Price to Book Value (PBV). The analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4. The results showed that ESG has a positive and significant effect on firm value, but not a significant effect on profitability. Profitability has a positive and significant effect on firm value, but does not significantly mediate the relationship between ESG and firm value. These findings suggest that sustainable finance is associated with increased firm value primarily through the direct influence of ESG on market valuation, not through increased profitability.

title: Monsters of finance
summary: Abstract An anthropology of horror can serve as a vernacular critique of financial speculation. Drawing on fieldwork in San Pedro, Paraguay, I track horror across three registers: pombero tricksters; plata yvyguy (buried money) as a foundin
content: Abstract An anthropology of horror can serve as a vernacular critique of financial speculation. Drawing on fieldwork in San Pedro, Paraguay, I track horror across three registers: pombero tricksters; plata yvyguy (buried money) as a founding myth of postwar finance; and obligations binding sesame farmers to monsters, patrones , and creditors. Horror—a critical ontology and distinctive wonder—arises when obligation becomes undecidable: when one cannot tell whether the forces manipulating time and the future are persons who stand in relation, or how far the liability extends. Paraguay has produced this condition twice, first under the Stroessner dictatorship (1954–89), with its network of civilian informants, and later under climate finance running through the same clientelist orders. As Martha Blache's 1982 study of Guarani folklore helps us understand, finance bears rather than subsumes the moral arrangements of prestation, and horror is a native theorization of speculation rather than a response to an external capitalist threat.

title: Light stimuli attenuates inflammatory activation in primary bone marrow-derived macrophages
summary: Abstract Bone repair depends on a regulated macrophage-driven inflammatory response. Non-activated macrophages (M0) differentiate into pro-inflammatory (M1) or anti-inflammatory (M2) phenotypes in response to microenvironmental signals. Thi
content: Abstract Bone repair depends on a regulated macrophage-driven inflammatory response. Non-activated macrophages (M0) differentiate into pro-inflammatory (M1) or anti-inflammatory (M2) phenotypes in response to microenvironmental signals. This study evaluated, in vitro, the effects of photobiomodulation (PBM) on bone marrow-derived macrophage polarisation. Monocytes were isolated, differentiated into macrophages (M0), and induced to acquire M1- or M2-associated characteristics. Cells were irradiated using a PBM protocol for bone regeneration (equivalent dose of 2.1 E). Cells were analysed according to morphology, expression of M1 ( iNOS , Tnf-α ) or M2 markers ( Arg1 , Cd206 ), protein expression (iNOS and ARG1), and nitric oxide (NO) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. Data were analysed using 1-way analysis of variance or Student’s t -test ( p ≤ 0.05). PBM promoted selective and transient modulation of inflammatory and metabolic markers in M0, M1, and M2 macrophages. Compared to non-PBM-treated cells, M1 PBM cells had reduced NO levels, increased early ROS levels, and decreased gene and protein expression. In M2 PBM cells, transient changes in NO and ROS production were detected, with reduced Cd206 expression and similar Arg1 expression, although increased ARG1 protein expression was detected compared to non-irradiated controls. In M0 PBM cells, NO levels remained unchanged, while early ROS levels increased, accompanied by reduced iNos and Arg-1 , and increased Cd206 expression. Under the selected parameters, PBM modulated macrophage inflammatory behaviour, but was insufficient to induce classical macrophage polarisation towards a specific phenotype. These findings suggest that modulation of macrophage-mediated inflammatory responses may contribute to the effects of this PBM protocol during bone repair.
