title: Unpacking Service Quality and Student Satisfaction in Nepal's Private Higher Education: A PLS-SEM Analysis of the SERVQUAL Dimensions in Pokhara University Affiliated Colleges
source: Quest Journal of Management and Social Sciences
summary: Background: Student satisfaction is an important indicator of educational service quality and can influence students’ perceptions of institutional performance, engagement, and continued affiliation with an institution. In an increasingly co
content: Background: Student satisfaction is an important indicator of educational service quality and can influence students’ perceptions of institutional performance, engagement, and continued affiliation with an institution. In an increasingly competitive higher education environment, private colleges must understand which dimensions of service quality most strongly shape students’ experiences. Although the SERVQUAL framework provides a widely used approach for assessing service quality, evidence on the relative importance of its dimensions in private higher education institutions in Nepal remains limited. Purpose: This study examines the impact of service quality on student satisfaction among undergraduate students in private colleges affiliated with Pokhara University in Kathmandu Valley. It further seeks to identify the challenges students face in these institutions and to propose potential solutions for addressing them. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopted an explanatory research design, guided by Expectation Confirmation Theory (ECT), given that the SERVQUAL model is grounded in the expectancy-disconfirmation paradigm. Primary data were collected from 401 respondents using a non-probability convenience sampling technique, with structured questionnaires administered through the KOBO Toolbox. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical methods, employing Microsoft Excel and SmartPLS 4.0. Findings: The results indicate that tangibility (β = 0.247, p < 0.001) and empathy (β = 0.310, p < 0.001) have a positive and statistically significant influence on student satisfaction in private colleges affiliated with Pokhara University, with empathy emerging as the strongest predictor. In contrast, reliability (β = 0.068, p = 0.238), responsiveness (β = 0.085, p = 0.154), and assurance (β = -0.024, p = 0.617) did not show a statistically significant relationship with student satisfaction. Conclusion: The study concludes that students place greater value on the physical appearance of their institution and on individualized, empathetic support than on reliability, responsiveness, or assurance. This suggests that the latter dimensions may already be adequately addressed within these institutions and are therefore not primary drivers of differentiation in student satisfaction, whereas tangibility and empathy warrant continued institutional attention and investment.

title: A Privacy-Preserving Data Sharing Framework Driven by Blockchain for Smart Childcare Subsidy Systems
source: ICST Transactions on Scalable Information Systems
summary: With the continuing development of digital government and public childcare-assistance programs, cross-departmental subsidy services must jointly address sensitive-data minimization, dynamic authorization, fraudulent-application identificati
content: With the continuing development of digital government and public childcare-assistance programs, cross-departmental subsidy services must jointly address sensitive-data minimization, dynamic authorization, fraudulent-application identification, and accountable auditing. This paper proposes a blockchain-driven privacy-preserving data-sharing framework that combines a consortium blockchain, on-chain evidence with off-chain ciphertext storage, zero-knowledge eligibility proofs, attribute-based encryption, proxy re-encryption, secure aggregation, federated learning, and smart-contract auditing. The contribution is a scenario-specific system integration and governance design rather than a new cryptographic primitive. In addition to the original Hyperledger Fabric feasibility test, the revision adds literature-grounded validation against peer-reviewed studies of childcare-subsidy administration and administrative-data evaluation, component implementation-status disclosure, a 2048-bit proof-of-knowledge precomputation microbenchmark, non-IID federated-learning tests, and colluding-node poisoning tests. The original prototype reaches 718 TPS and 236 ms average latency at 400 concurrent requests, 91.8% federated-learning accuracy, and 138 ms on-chain index retrieval for 20,000 audit records. In the added five-run tests, strong non-IID data retain an F1 score of 82.69% +/- 0.09%; adaptive clipping and robust aggregation retain F1 scores of 84.04% and 84.14% under one and two colluding sign-flip clients, respectively. Offline commitment precomputation reduces the online arithmetic time for four eligibility subproofs from 8.03 +/- 0.34 ms to 0.06 +/- 0.01 ms. These results support the feasibility of the integrated framework while clarifying that production deployment still requires authorized local data, audited cryptographic libraries, and multi-orderer field validation.

title: DEVELOPING A COMMUNITY-BASED WATER RESOURCE SECURITY FRAMEWORK FOR RURAL MALAYSIA: INTEGRATING GREEN TECHNOLOGY AND SOCIAL CAPITAL PERSPECTIVES
summary: Access to safe and reliable water remains a persistent challenge for rural communities in Malaysia, where infrastructural limitations, spatial constraints, and governance fragmentation continue to undermine water security. While technologic
content: Access to safe and reliable water remains a persistent challenge for rural communities in Malaysia, where infrastructural limitations, spatial constraints, and governance fragmentation continue to undermine water security. While technological solutions have been widely promoted, their long-term effectiveness in rural contexts is often constrained by limited community ownership and weak institutional coordination. This paper develops a Community-Based Water Resource Security Framework (CBWSF) that integrates social capital, place-responsive green technology, and institutional coordination. This study used a structured integrative synthesis of peer-reviewed scholarship, Malaysian planning evidence, and national policy documents to derive and connect five dimensions: institutional governance, social capital, green technology, spatial and environmental context, and sustainability monitoring. The framework distinguishes four recurring terrain-settlement configurations (interior highland, riverine floodplain, coastal peat-lowland, and island or stilt settlement) and links each to source, technology, and governance choices. It also translates the National Water Resources Policy and Rural Development Policy 2030 into operational community-level planning actions. The paper contributes a policy-connected implementation logic for rural water planning rather than an empirically validated causal model. Its propositions should therefore be tested through comparative case studies and longitudinal performance assessment.

title: Quantifying local mechanical work at the nanoscale in optically driven piezoelectric membranes
summary: Quantifying mechanical work generation in active micro- and nanoscale systems requires measuring both displacement and force under controlled loading conditions, yet most approaches probe these quantities separately. Here, we present an ato
content: Quantifying mechanical work generation in active micro- and nanoscale systems requires measuring both displacement and force under controlled loading conditions, yet most approaches probe these quantities separately. Here, we present an atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based method to determine nanometer-scale displacement, local force response, and mechanical work in optically actuated piezoelectric photodiode membranes. Suspended membranes with diameters from 1 to 8 mm were driven by modulated optical excitation and probed using AFM cantilevers with different spring constants to impose controlled mechanical loads. By alternating between constant-force and constant-height operation modes, displacement and force amplitudes were independently extracted, and the local mechanical work was calculated from their product. The optomechanical response depends strongly on membrane size and probe loading. Radial measurements reveal non-uniform deformation, including off-center displacement maxima in smaller devices and a radial sign change in large membranes. The results further indicate that probe–membrane coupling plays an important role when the cantilever stiffness becomes comparable to the effective membrane stiffness. This approach provides a practical framework for evaluating load-dependent mechanical work in active materials and for optimizing micro- and nanoscale actuators and energy-converting devices.

title: MEASURING EFFICIENCY IN MALAYSIAN REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUSTS
summary: This paper highlights the necessity of evaluating the efficiency of Malaysian Real Estate Investment Trusts (M-REITs) across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic phases. While the sector holds significant strategic value, there is
content: This paper highlights the necessity of evaluating the efficiency of Malaysian Real Estate Investment Trusts (M-REITs) across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic phases. While the sector holds significant strategic value, there is a lack of empirical research focusing on the technical, managerial, and scale efficiencies of M-REITs. To address this gap, the study analyses M-REITs efficiency between 2015 and 2024 by applying a non-parametric Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) methodology. Specifically, the input-oriented Variable Return to Scale (VRS-DEA) model was employed to determine the efficiency scores for M-REITs. The findings indicate the average technical efficiency score is 0.633, indicating moderate overall performance. Pure technical efficiency is relatively high at 0.801, while scale efficiency averages 0.783. This suggests that M-REITs demonstrate strong relative resource-conversion capabilities under managerial control, but efficiency losses are partly due to operating at a non-optimal scale. Ultimately, this study highlights the importance of better resource utilisation and appropriate scale adjustments to improve performance.

title: Observation of relativistic bond weakening in seaborgium hexacarbonyl
summary: Abstract The seventh row of the periodic table of the elements has been completed with the discovery of the five heaviest elements from flerovium (Fl, Z = 114) through oganesson (Og, Z = 118) 1 . Chemical properties of the superheavy elemen
content: Abstract The seventh row of the periodic table of the elements has been completed with the discovery of the five heaviest elements from flerovium (Fl, Z = 114) through oganesson (Og, Z = 118) 1 . Chemical properties of the superheavy elements (SHE, Z ≥ 104) are unique owing to the strong influence of relativistic effects on their valence electron shells 2 . The stability of the metal–ligand bonding in carbonyl complexes is a property that is predicted to be affected by such effects 3,4 . Here we present an experimental gas chromatography study on the stability of the Sg(CO) 6 complex. The measured formation yields of Sg(CO) 6 and W(CO) 6 enabled determining the first bond dissociation energy (FBDE) of Sg(CO) 6 , which is 4(2) kJ mol −1 lower than that of W(CO) 6 and corresponds to a value of 188(9) kJ mol −1 . Thus, the trend of increasing FBDE values of hexacarbonyls within group 6 of the periodic table is reversed from W to Sg. Our result agrees with state-of-the-art theoretical calculations, which predict a decrease in the FBDE from W(CO) 6 to Sg(CO) 6 owing to the relativistic destabilization of the 6d atomic orbitals (AOs) in Sg (ref. 4 ). Also, the adsorption enthalpy value of Sg(CO) 6 on gold of $${45}_{-6}^{+4}\,{\rm{kJ}}\,{{\rm{mol}}}^{-1}$$ 45 − 6 + 4 kJ mol − 1 is reported.

title: Drivers of Employee Engagement in Nepal's Private Sector: A PLS-SEM Analysis of Recruitment, Training, Performance Appraisal, and Compensation Practices in Kathmandu Valley
source: Quest Journal of Management and Social Sciences
summary: Background: Employee engagement is a key driver of a company's competitive advantage and performance. Employee engagement creates opportunities for employees to connect with their managers, employees, and organizations through the human res
content: Background: Employee engagement is a key driver of a company's competitive advantage and performance. Employee engagement creates opportunities for employees to connect with their managers, employees, and organizations through the human resource management practices. Purpose: The objective of this research is to study the impact of human resource management practices on employee engagement in private sector of Kathmandu valley. Design/methodology/approach: The explanatory research design was used in this study. A purposive sampling method was used to collect data from 400 private sector’s employees in Kathmandu Valley. Social Exchange Theory and Work Engagement Theory is utilized. To analyze the data, both descriptive and inferential statistics were used. SEM was used to analyze the data. Findings: The study's findings showed that almost all respondents had sufficient understanding of creating efficient HR practices as the primary factor influencing employee engagement within the company. The major findings of the study indicate that there exists a positive impact of human resource practices such as recruitment and selection, training and development, performance appraisal, and compensation and reward on employee engagement. The main challenges faced regarding employee engagement in organization are lack of training and development effectiveness and HR department are responsible for addressing these challenges, by offering more training and development programs problems can be solved. Conclusion: The findings revealed that effective HRM practices such as recruitment and selection, training and development, performance appraisal, and compensation and reward are crucial for effective employee engagement in private sector.

title: Oracle integrity under predatory attack: a calibrated jump-diffusion model with public-data evidence and a positivity-preserving numerical scheme
summary: Introduction Oracle-dependent DeFi protocols execute collateral valuations, liquidations, and settlements based on reported data. Methods We model oracle integrity and attack pressure as coupled positive states in a controlled jump-diffusio
content: Introduction Oracle-dependent DeFi protocols execute collateral valuations, liquidations, and settlements based on reported data. Methods We model oracle integrity and attack pressure as coupled positive states in a controlled jump-diffusion. Multiplicative shocks preserve the integrity state space while separating continuous variation from discrete attack windows. Scenario inputs are anchored to 24 documented oracle-related incidents, an oracle-consumer exposure panel, and Chainlink metadata covering 1,669 feeds across 29 networks. A positivity-preserving log-Euler scheme simulates Baseline, Stress, and Controlled configurations. Results The corresponding 10-year collapse probabilities are 10.1%, 93.0%, and 0% across 4,000 paths, with a one-sided 95% upper bound of 0.09% for the Controlled configuration. Within the sampled parameter ranges, pressure decay has the strongest rank association with simulated collapse probability. Discussion These results are scenario diagnostics, not causal estimates of protocol controls.

title: REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT DECISION-MAKING CHALLENGES AMONG GOVERNMENT-LINKED INVESTMENT COMPANIES IN MALAYSIA
summary: Institutional real estate investment decisions in emerging economies remain underexplored, particularly among government-linked entities that must balance commercial returns with broader national development mandates. Although Malaysia gove
content: Institutional real estate investment decisions in emerging economies remain underexplored, particularly among government-linked entities that must balance commercial returns with broader national development mandates. Although Malaysia government-linked investment companies (GLICs) are among the country’s dominant institutional investors in the commercial real estate market, the challenges influencing their real estate investment decisions remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the challenges that influence real estate investment decisions among Malaysian GLICs. A qualitative study design was adopted, drawing on semi-structured interviews with 15 key informants directly involved in real estate investment decision-making. Thematic analysis identified challenges across two broad dimensions, namely internal and external. Internal challenges include organisational and structural constraints, behavioural biases such as herding and home bias, and social and sustainable challenges, including environmental, social, and governance (ESG) pressure and ambitious development. External challenges comprise political and geopolitical risk, macroeconomic challenges, real estate market constraints, and regulatory and legal requirements. These findings reveal a dual mandate tension between achieving risk-adjusted returns and fulfilling socio-political obligations. This study contributes to the limited literature on institutional real estate investment challenges in emerging economies and offers practical implications for fund managers, policymakers, and regulators seeking to enhance institutional real estate investment practices in Malaysia.

title: Conceptualizing an athlete support ecosystem for women in professional team sport
source: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
summary: The expanse of women’s professional team sports has burgeoned in the last ten years. The inroads made by women’s leagues have raised questions about how to equitably and sustainably support, finance, and manage and foster the growth and dev
content: The expanse of women’s professional team sports has burgeoned in the last ten years. The inroads made by women’s leagues have raised questions about how to equitably and sustainably support, finance, and manage and foster the growth and development of women athletes. Women’s leagues have unique characteristics that warrant recognition and positioning which are different from their counterpart men’s leagues and enable gender specific value creation. However, the development of many women’s leagues, both stand alone and those that share league governing bodies with the men’s leagues, have positioned women in precarious and unsustainable employment condition with little consideration of gender relevant work conditions, culture and safety, career pathways and representation. We argue that an alternative framework for women’s leagues, that attends to the gendered needs of women athletes, can foster equitable approaches that support sustainable practice and better employment outcomes. In this paper we propose a gendered conceptual framework, termed a Women Athlete Support Ecosystem, as a holistic way to enhance professional team athlete support and development for women. Drawing on literature and framework analysis we re-frame a socio-ecological model to consider a feminist intersectional approach proposing four key areas: individual and sustainable care; interdependence of athlete wellbeing; organizational practices; and community connection. Our approach to athlete support and development incorporates sport as community, and concepts embodied in sustainability, flourishing, wellbeing, and care.

title: Sri Lankan ethnic cuisine on YouTube: a computational netnographic study of food-neophobic and food-neophilic audience reactions and the digital transmission of culinary heritage
summary: Abstract Sri Lankan cuisine is a layered ethnic food heritage shaped by tropical agriculture and by centuries of Arab, Portuguese, Dutch, and British contact atop a South Indian rice-and-curry foundation, and it is increasingly encountered
content: Abstract Sri Lankan cuisine is a layered ethnic food heritage shaped by tropical agriculture and by centuries of Arab, Portuguese, Dutch, and British contact atop a South Indian rice-and-curry foundation, and it is increasingly encountered by global audiences not at the destination but on digital platforms. This paper analyses 21,984 predominantly English-language comments posted on 45 YouTube videos about Sri Lankan ethnic cuisine, using VADER sentiment analysis, LDA topic modelling, and a purpose-built keyword lexicon for phobic and philic markers. The findings challenge two conventions of the survey literature. First, philic markers outnumber phobic markers by about seven to one (13.1 vs 1.9%), and where both appear in the same comment (1.5% of the sample) the sentiment reads positive, not negative; because the unit of analysis is the comment rather than the commenter, this co-occurrence is reported as a discursive rather than a dispositional phenomenon. Second, phobic response is not concentrated in a single kind of content but spreads across every one of the eight topics recovered by the LDA. The strongest interpretive contribution of the analysis is the identification of peer-to-peer cultural translation as a discursive mechanism associated with the mitigation of neophobic framing: commenters writing from insider-like discursive positions routinely convert unfamiliar Sri Lankan dishes into familiar reference points for outsider viewers, performing what this paper argues is a contemporary form of oral tradition through which Sri Lankan ethnic food heritage is transmitted to global audiences. Long-form videos polarise audience response more sharply than Shorts do. Implications for ethnic food heritage preservation, cross-cuisine transmission, and destination practice follow.

title: TOWARDS SHARIA COMPLIANT MARKET SOUNDING PRACTICES IN PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIPS: EVIDENCE FROM INDONESIA
summary: This study examines whether Sharia principles emphasising transparency and full disclosure can be operationalised within market sounding practices in Public-Private Partnership (PPP) schemes. The study adopts a qualitative research design b
content: This study examines whether Sharia principles emphasising transparency and full disclosure can be operationalised within market sounding practices in Public-Private Partnership (PPP) schemes. The study adopts a qualitative research design based on semi-structured interviews with 21 expert stakeholders from government institutions, financial organisations, private investors, advisory bodies, and Sharia authorities. Data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns and to develop a conceptual framework. The findings reveal a strong convergence among stakeholders that transparency and full disclosure are fundamental requirements under Sharia and are consistent with principles of good governance in PPPs. However, practical limitations, including limited project readiness, institutional capacity constraints, and the need to preserve competitive innovation, restrict the feasibility of full disclosure at early stages. The study is limited to the Indonesian context and expert perspectives. Future research may incorporate comparative studies across jurisdictions and quantitative validation of impacts on investor participation. This study contributes to the emerging discourse on Sharia PPPs by proposing market sounding based on transparency and full disclosure as a foundational mechanism bridging Sharia principles and conventional PPP practices.

title: Bridging the gaps in circular economy adoption: Conceptualizing a framework for Ghana’s manufacturing sector
summary: Industrial decarbonization and resource efficiency have driven Circular Economy (CE) to the top of manufacturing discussions, yet putting it into practice depends on technological and digital capabilities, which remain uneven across develop
content: Industrial decarbonization and resource efficiency have driven Circular Economy (CE) to the top of manufacturing discussions, yet putting it into practice depends on technological and digital capabilities, which remain uneven across developing economies. This exploratory study develops a preliminary CE framework for Ghana's manufacturing sector, integrating formal industries, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), informal manufacturers, and third-party waste actors. Drawing on the Multi-Level Perspective and Modified 8Ms frameworks, it employs a mixed-methods design, combining survey data from 50 purposively sampled enterprises with policy document analysis. Results from the sampled enterprises indicate predominantly linear practices, constrained by financial, institutional, infrastructural, and digital-readiness barriers. Formal manufacturers show partial CE awareness (60%) but limited strategic and technological integration, while informal enterprises exhibit adaptive reuse behaviours (72%) driven by resource scarcity rather than policy. Inferential analysis confirmed significant associations between formality status and CE awareness (χ² = 8.33, p = 0.004), waste tracking (Fisher's Exact p < 0.001), and demand for financial incentives (Fisher's Exact p = 0.016). The framework places Industrial Symbiosis at the operational centre, connecting all actors through material, financial, knowledge, and digital flows, and specifies governance and monitoring arrangements. Policy actions recommended include improved coordination, circular financing mechanisms, digital waste-exchange and monitoring platforms, and formalized partnerships with informal recyclers. Given the exploratory sample (n = 50), findings are indicative. The study offers a context-sensitive, empirically informed model to advance inclusive, technology-enabled circular manufacturing transitions in Africa.

title: Green Strategic Management and Organizational Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Cross River State, Nigeria
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: This study examined the effect of green strategic management on the organizational performance of manufacturing firms in Cross River State, with particular reference to Flour Mills Nigeria PLC, Calabar. Specifically, it investigated the eff
content: This study examined the effect of green strategic management on the organizational performance of manufacturing firms in Cross River State, with particular reference to Flour Mills Nigeria PLC, Calabar. Specifically, it investigated the effects of green innovation, green supply chain management and green human resource management on organizational performance. A descriptive survey research design was adopted. The population comprised 396 employees, from whom 196 respondents were selected through simple random sampling. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire validated by experts in business management and research methodology. The instrument recorded an overall Cronbach’s alpha coefficient of 0.887, confirming its reliability. Of the 196 questionnaires administered, 184 were completed and returned, representing a response rate of 93.9 per cent. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis with SPSS version 27 at the 5 per cent significance level. The findings showed that green innovation had a positive and significant effect on organizational performance (β = 0.341, t = 5.679, p < 0.001). Green supply chain management also had a positive and significant effect (β = 0.377, t = 6.103, p < 0.001), while green human resource management exerted a positive and significant effect (β = 0.296, t = 4.754, p < 0.001). Collectively, the variables explained 69.1 per cent of the variation in organizational performance. The study concluded that integrating environmental considerations into innovation, supply chain activities and human resource practices significantly improves overall organizational performance. It recommended cleaner technologies, environmentally responsible sourcing and regular employee environmental training.

title: From Uncertainty to Risk: How Firms Respond in Circular Economy Transitions
summary: ABSTRACT The transition to a circular economy exposes firms to multiple sources of uncertainty, yet existing research largely treats these challenges as barriers rather than drivers of firm behavior. This paper develops a conceptual underst
content: ABSTRACT The transition to a circular economy exposes firms to multiple sources of uncertainty, yet existing research largely treats these challenges as barriers rather than drivers of firm behavior. This paper develops a conceptual understanding of how uncertainty is translated into risk and how this shapes firm responses in circular economy contexts. It proposes that firms translate uncertainty into perceived risk through identifiable organizational processes, and this translation varies systematically with firms' prior experience and resource flexibility in CE ‐related activity rather than being inferred only from firms' eventual responses. Building on this perspective, the paper extends the behavioral theory of the firm by showing that in circular economy settings, risk perception is shaped across networks of interdependent firms rather than within a single firm, and that anticipated and realized risk can push firms in opposite directions. It further specifies when perceived risk leads to defensive versus proactive firm responses, based on firm experience and resource flexibility. By positioning risk as a central mechanism linking uncertainty to firm behavior, the paper offers an integrated explanation of circular economy transitions with theoretical, managerial, and policy implications.

title: Integrasi Tanggung Jawab Sosial dan Akuntansi Lingkungan bagi Kemaslahatan Pemangku Kepentingan
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis integrasi tanggung jawab sosial perusahaan dan akuntansi lingkungan di PT Amerta Indah Otsuka, mengidentifikasi manfaat yang diterima oleh pemangku kepentingan, dan memetakan praktik perusahaan me
content: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis integrasi tanggung jawab sosial perusahaan dan akuntansi lingkungan di PT Amerta Indah Otsuka, mengidentifikasi manfaat yang diterima oleh pemangku kepentingan, dan memetakan praktik perusahaan melalui kerangka syariah maqashid. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain studi kasus kualitatif deskriptif yang menganalisis 26 sumber, yang terdiri dari dokumen perusahaan, pemerintah, standar, dan akademis. Data disaring, diekstraksi, dikodekan, dibandingkan, ditriangulasi, dan dipetakan ke dimensi maqashid. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa integrasi CSR dan akuntansi lingkungan terjadi secara bertingkat, dengan bukti terkuat ditemukan dalam manajemen lingkungan dan kinerja fisik, termasuk energi terbarukan, efisiensi energi, penggunaan kembali air, bahan daur ulang, pengelolaan sampah masyarakat, dan pendidikan lingkungan, sementara dokumen publik belum secara sistematis mengungkapkan biaya lingkungan, investasi, kewajiban, penghematan, dan manfaat di tingkat entitas. Praktik-praktik tersebut terbukti mendukung perlindungan kehidupan, akal budi, generasi penerus, dan kekayaan, sementara perlindungan agama tampak hanya secara tidak langsung melalui kepatuhan, kepercayaan, dan integritas. Studi ini menyimpulkan bahwa akuntabilitas lingkungan yang lebih kuat memerlukan pelaporan di tingkat entitas, catatan biaya lingkungan, indikator hasil, partisipasi pemangku kepentingan, dan jaminan independen.

title: INTEGRATING WAQF MU’AQQAT AND EQUITY CROWDFUNDING FOR THE SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF IDLE WAQF LAND
summary: In Malaysia, it was reported that an estimated 17% of waqf lands remains undeveloped in 2024 due to financial and managerial constraints. Agricultural use of idle waqf land could generate up to RM18,000 per hectare annually, reflecting sign
content: In Malaysia, it was reported that an estimated 17% of waqf lands remains undeveloped in 2024 due to financial and managerial constraints. Agricultural use of idle waqf land could generate up to RM18,000 per hectare annually, reflecting significant unrealised economic value. Hence, it results in substantial opportunity costs, including lost financial sustainability and socio-developmental capacity of waqf institutions. In this context, developing idle waqf land for sustainable agriculture strengthens food security and socio-economic outcomes. It also can support local economic development by creating employment across the agricultural value chain. Overall, productive waqf land utilisation promotes income generation, rural livelihoods, and inclusive development. Therefore, this study aims to develop a sustainable financing model using equity crowdfunding to support the development of idle waqf land through sustainable agricultural initiatives. To achieve these objectives, this study adopts a qualitative research approach through a comprehensive analysis of relevant literature and semi-structured interviews with selected experts and practitioners from State Islamic Religious Councils (SIRCs), agricultural agencies, and land-related authorities. It was found that an alternative financing is crucially needed for waqf land development. Thus, equity crowdfunding can be proposed as a means of sustainable financing. However, to adapt into waqf land, it is suggested equity crowdfunding is integrated with waqf muaqqat (temporary waqf). This study contributes to the country economy agenda by developing idle land and providing venture capital for the agriculture sector business. At the same time, it aligns with Financial Sector Blueprint 2022-2026 in terms of advancing digitalisation of the financial sector and value-based finance through Islamic finance leadership Islamic finance. Finally, this model support Capital Market Masterplan 2026-2030 by encouraging development of innovative Islamic social finance products and frameworks, including waqf-linked investment for social and climate objectives.

title: Eco-innovar a pesar del sistema: colaboración y obstáculos en las empresas latinoamericanas
summary: In Latin America only 23% of the Sustainable Development Goal targets are on track, and eco-innovation operates within fragmented national innovation systems marked by weak regulation and drivers dominated by cost efficiency. Drawing on mic
content: In Latin America only 23% of the Sustainable Development Goal targets are on track, and eco-innovation operates within fragmented national innovation systems marked by weak regulation and drivers dominated by cost efficiency. Drawing on microdata from the Inter-American Development Bank’s Harmonized Latin American Innovation Surveys (LAIS) —30 surveys conducted between 2007 and 2017 across ten countries, with some 72,000 observations of potentially innovative firms—, the article examines whether intensive collaboration buffers the obstacles to eco-innovation. The results reveal a differentiated pattern: collaboration attenuates knowledge obstacles and partially reverses market obstacles, but does not alter financial constraints and even aggravates the effect of regulatory and institutional barriers. Latin American firms are eco-innovating despite the system, yet this strategy is not sustainable without green financing and stable regulatory frameworks.

title: Communicating EU External Action: What Role for Strategic Narratives in the Commission's Promotion of the Global Gateway?
source: JCMS Journal of Common Market Studies
summary: Abstract When the European Union promotes its external policies, it usually goes largely unnoticed. This was different for the EU's flagship initiative for external investments, the Global Gateway, which quickly created a public discussion
content: Abstract When the European Union promotes its external policies, it usually goes largely unnoticed. This was different for the EU's flagship initiative for external investments, the Global Gateway, which quickly created a public discussion amongst European pundits about what it means for the EU as a geopolitical actor. Yet, this EU‐centric debate omits those audiences for whom the policy is intended. This contribution starts from the assumption that communication can be a form of soft power through the use of strategic narratives. Building on insights from a perceptual approach to the EU's external relations, the contribution asks how the EU uses strategic narratives in the promotion of the Global Gateway and how this speaks to third countries' perceptions of the EU with the aim of improving partners' engagement. To shed light on the underlying strategic narratives, the contribution analyses the Commission's public communication on the Global Gateway in the early phase following the initiative's launch between December 2021 and July 2023. Whilst the public focus was on the geopolitical narrative turn, we show that the Commission's narratives highlighted development and the importance of values, representing a degree of continuity that speaks to accusations of the EU's hypocrisy and lack of willingness to consider external perceptions of partners seriously.

title: Creativity Under Pressure: A Case Study of Drug Cartel Innovation
summary: ABSTRACT This article examines drug cartels as creative, innovation‐driven organizations rather than solely violent criminal enterprises. Building on creativity research applied to terrorist groups, we use a qualitative case study approach—
content: ABSTRACT This article examines drug cartels as creative, innovation‐driven organizations rather than solely violent criminal enterprises. Building on creativity research applied to terrorist groups, we use a qualitative case study approach—drawing from news reports, official documents, open‐source materials, and academic work—to analyze 10 cases of cartel innovation across tactical, strategic, and organizational domains. The cases show that cartel innovation is a systematic, adaptive process shaped by constraints, competition, and environmental pressures. Cartel problem‐solving aligns with core phases of the creative process, from identifying problems to generating, testing, and refining solutions. Innovation is further enabled by organizational learning, the recruitment of external talent (such as engineers or trained soldiers), the repurposing of everyday technologies, and diversification into new markets. Enforcement constraints often act as creative catalysts, pushing groups toward more sophisticated adaptations. Integrating creativity and innovation theory into the study of organized crime offers both explanatory and practical value. Viewing cartel tactics as outputs of an underlying innovation system highlights opportunities to disrupt creative processes in the initial stages rather than only reacting to their outcomes. The article concludes by outlining implications for anticipating criminal innovation and suggesting directions for future empirical research on creativity within criminal organizations.

title: Determinants of Vietnamese SMEs’ decision to start exporting
source: Journal of International Economics and Management
summary: Purpose Understanding the determinants of international market entry is critical for the growth and survival of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in emerging economies. This research examines the key internal and external factors dr
content: Purpose Understanding the determinants of international market entry is critical for the growth and survival of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in emerging economies. This research examines the key internal and external factors driving the export entry decisions of Vietnamese SMEs. Design/methodology/approach To evaluate these dynamics, this research analyzes a three-wave longitudinal panel dataset comprising 7,502 observations from 2,500 Vietnamese SMEs across survey years 2011, 2013 and 2015, complemented by an independent post-COVID cross-sectional dataset from 2023 (N = 599) as a robustness check. The study employs advanced econometric techniques, specifically linear probability models (LPM), logit and probit models incorporating random effects models, to rigorously account for unobserved firm heterogeneity. Findings Government support and internationally recognized quality certifications are significantly and positively associated with SMEs’ entry into foreign markets. Furthermore, global integration – achieved through importing materials, securing foreign ownership and serving as foreign subcontractors – exhibits a strong correlation with export participation. Internally, export decisions are strongly predicted by having a license to operate overseas and a higher proportion of professional and female employees. Originality/value These results imply that Vietnamese SMEs can strategically enhance their global competitiveness by diversifying their workforce, pursuing international certifications and proactively embedding themselves within global supply chains.

title: An Experimental and Computational Investigation of the Kinetics of Branched Butyl Radicals 2-Methylpropan-1-yl and 2-Methylpropan-2-yl with Molecular Oxygen
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
summary: Abstract We have measured the rate coefficient for the reaction between the 2-methylpropan-1-yl radical and molecular oxygen as a function of temperature and pressure in both He and N2 bath gases using photoionization mass spectrometry. Sim
content: Abstract We have measured the rate coefficient for the reaction between the 2-methylpropan-1-yl radical and molecular oxygen as a function of temperature and pressure in both He and N2 bath gases using photoionization mass spectrometry. Similar measurements were performed for the 2-methylpropan-2-yl radical. It was found that 2-methylpropan-1-yl reacts much slower with O2 than 2-methylpropan-2-yl both in the falloff region and near the high-pressure limit. We complemented the experimental work by constructing master-equation models for both reaction systems to simulate their kinetics under conditions not covered by experiments. By optimizing the value of few key parameters against measured data, the models were able to reproduce the observed temperature and pressure dependencies of both rate coefficients. To facilitate the use of present results in modeling, PLOG and Chebyshev rate-coefficient parametrizations are provided. Although 2-methylpropan-1-yl reacts much slower with O2 than 2-methylpropan-2-yl, the former reaction generates more products that lead to chain-propagation and -branching than the latter, which almost exclusively forms 2-methylpropene and hydroperoxyl and is thus chain-terminating.

title: Twinning living heritage: human-centered digital twins coupling CADA and HUL for arid cities
summary: The integration of urban digital twins and artificial intelligence is changing city management by introducing innovative methods for simulations, observations, and control. However, their application is primarily technical and spatially res
content: The integration of urban digital twins and artificial intelligence is changing city management by introducing innovative methods for simulations, observations, and control. However, their application is primarily technical and spatially restricted to certain regions. Urban digital twins (UDT) have shown efficacy in infrastructure, energy, and hydrological modeling; however, they infrequently incorporate cultural significance or distribution considerations. This omission is significant in hot-arid cities, where escalating heat stress, rapid urban development, and vulnerable historical public spaces intersect. However, no existing framework links heritage values, outdoor thermal comfort, and spatial equity within a single decision-making instrument. This study couples the Convergent Appreciation/Divergent Activation (CADA) design model with the UNESCO Historic Urban Landscape (HUL) approach, using a human-centered digital twin as the operational intermediary to link design epistemology with values-based heritage management. CADA provides a structured approach to shared place appreciation and varied generative design outcomes, whereas HUL presents a values-based, layered reading of heritage values—the significance that communities and experts attribute to places—beyond isolated monuments. The framework incorporates a CADA–HUL crosswalk, a five-tier twin architecture (sensing, representation, reasoning, negotiation, and intervention), and a mechanism to transform statements of importance into computable and contestable twin layers. Six testable propositions were specified with disconfirmation criteria and matched empirical methods. Although specified for hot-arid heritage public spaces, the architecture is relevant to other climatic and heritage contexts, which is a testable claim. The framework does not automatically resolve cultural and climatic trade-offs; instead, it makes them explicit, contestable, and available for human deliberation, repositioning the UDT from a technical benchmark to a culturally informed, climate-sensitive, and equity-aware instrument. A parameterized analysis of a space left over after planning (SLOAP) in Doha attributed three interventions with midday mean radiant temperature (MRT) reductions of approximately 18, 14, and 11 °C. The thermal-only ranking favored the solid canopy, but activating the significance layer flagged a sightline conflict and reordered the ranking toward the mashrabiya re-enclosure; these are illustrative inputs, not simulation results.​

title: THE IMPACT OF RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT COSTS ON THE OPERATIONAL PROFITS OF JORDANIAN COMPANIES
summary: Research and development drive competitive advantage but requires substantial investments that can constrain profitability. This study examines the impact of R&D costs on the operating profits of Jordanian pharmaceutical companies listed in
content: Research and development drive competitive advantage but requires substantial investments that can constrain profitability. This study examines the impact of R&D costs on the operating profits of Jordanian pharmaceutical companies listed in ASE from 2015-2022. Financial data across five major players is analysed using multiple regression techniques using EViews. The results reveal a statistically significant positive relationship whereby a 1% increase in R&D spending as a proportion of revenue enhances the profit margin by 0.17%. However, when controlled for company size, the R&D impact becomes insignificant, indicating scale-based barriers. But incorporating age and sales growth factors restores significance, suggesting life cycle contingent effects. However, R&D displays a contingent profitable influence depending on organizational context. Thus, for further research can support optimal resource allocation towards differentiated research initiatives across market segments. Quantifying input-output mechanisms and delineating cost thresholds promises to nurture the pharmaceutical innovation ecosystem. This paper offers specific insights for pharmaceutical leaders to optimize innovation planning based on companyspecific factors to elevate financial sustainability. This paper highlights the need for evidence-based allocation decisions catering to life cycle stage, growth objectives and market positioning. Based on the study's findings, companies should create collaborative partnerships with universities and research institutions. The collaborative partnerships will help them cover service gaps, reduce costs, and, most importantly, reduce the uncertainties that come with innovation. Managers should consider the size, age, and growth levels of the firm while developing research and development strategies. On the other hand , policymakers should pay special attention to innovative strategies, especially in the pharmaceutical industry. This should be done by introducing appropriate rewards, financing, and initiatives to support R&D.

title: Effect of carbon quantum dots on the UV-curing behavior and properties of waterborne polyurethane acrylate coatings
summary: Photoactive carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are promising modifiers for waterborne polyurethane acrylate (WPUA) coatings, but their effect on UV-curing kinetics depends on how they interact with the photopolymerizable matrix. This study evaluate
content: Photoactive carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are promising modifiers for waterborne polyurethane acrylate (WPUA) coatings, but their effect on UV-curing kinetics depends on how they interact with the photopolymerizable matrix. This study evaluates the influence of CQDs surface chemistry, photoluminescence quantum yield (QY), and incorporation route on curing behavior and final coating properties. Two CQDs with distinct QY values (≈23% and ≈62%) but similar surface functional groups were incorporated into WPUA dispersions via aqueous-phase addition and acetone pre-dispersion. Photo-DSC analysis revealed that CQDs broadened curing profiles, increased peak time from 4.2 s to 13.7–44.5 s, and reduced C=C conversion from 92.8% to 50.8–77.9%. A semi-quantitative analysis indicated that curing retardation arises from combined competitive UV absorption and route-dependent mobility restrictions induced by CQDs–WPUA interactions. Despite reduced conversion and gel content (97.8% to 83–93%), CQDs improved coating performance, increasing tensile strength from 4.3 MPa to 6.1–6.6 MPa (≈40–53%), and thermal stability (T 10% ) from 298.2 °C to 309.1 °C. The incorporation route affected curing and properties in a CQDs-dependent manner, while QY differences produced only minor kinetic effects, indicating that surface chemistry and matrix interactions govern the response more strongly than photoluminescence. Under air, selected formulations suggested an apparent attenuation of oxygen inhibition, consistent with auxiliary CQDs photoactivity. Hansen solubility parameter analysis further revealed a contraction of the solubility sphere, indicating a more constrained network with improved solvent resistance. CQDs act as multifunctional modifiers that tune curing efficiency and coating performance through surface functionality and incorporation route.

title: Magnetic Electrospun Polycaprolactone (PCL) Fibers Modified with Oleic Acid-Coated Iron Oxide Nanoparticles
summary: Abstract Magnetic polycaprolactone (PCL) fibers containing oleic acid-coated iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs/OA) were produced by electrospinning. First, a systematic study was carried out to determine the optimal processing parameters, est
content: Abstract Magnetic polycaprolactone (PCL) fibers containing oleic acid-coated iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs/OA) were produced by electrospinning. First, a systematic study was carried out to determine the optimal processing parameters, establishing a 20% (w/v) PCL concentration, an applied voltage of 20 kV, a needle-to-collector distance of 22 cm, and a flow rate of 2 mL/h as the most suitable parameters. Homogeneous neat PCL fibers with an average diameter of 543 ± 88 nm were obtained under these conditions. Subsequently, different IONPs/OA concentrations (5, 10, and 20 wt %) were incorporated, leading to a progressive increase in fiber diameter, with a maximum of 961 ± 201 nm for the 20 wt % formulation. Magnetic measurements confirmed superparamagnetic behavior at room temperature for all composite fiber samples, with a maximum saturation magnetization (Ms) of 6.1 ± 0.1 emu/g for the 20 wt % formulation. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed that the incorporation of IONPs/OA into the fibers decreased the degradation temperature by approximately 63 °C compared to neat PCL. Finally, water contact angle (WCA) measurements revealed a progressive increase in fiber hydrophobicity, reaching a maximum WCA of 135°. These results indicate that the produced fibers exhibited promising morphological, compositional, thermal and magnetic properties for potential future biomedical applications, such as drug delivery and magnetic hyperthermia.

title: AI and promote carbon reduction: exploring an optimal deep learning model to predict CO2 emissions under technological innovations and green finance
summary: Accurate prediction of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions is essential for effective carbon management and evidence-based climate policy. However, emission dynamics are inherently nonlinear and arise from complex interactions among technologica
content: Accurate prediction of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions is essential for effective carbon management and evidence-based climate policy. However, emission dynamics are inherently nonlinear and arise from complex interactions among technological, financial, energy, economic and demographic factors. This study develops an interpretable artificial-intelligence framework to predict CO₂ emissions across 15 Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) economies during 2000–2024. Annual data were converted to quarterly frequency and decomposed using Improved Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise. Fifteen neural-network and deep-learning architectures were evaluated using mean absolute error, mean squared error, root mean squared error, and training time. The Radial Basis Function network achieved the strongest overall performance, with MAE of 0.028, MSE of 0.002, RMSE of 0.040, and a training time of 00:01:12. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis and three-dimensional representation showed heterogeneous contributions from technological innovation, green finance for renewable energy, nonrenewable energy consumption, financial development, economic growth and population aging. Patent activity and R&D expenditure were predominantly associated with lower predicted CO₂ emissions, whereas green finance showed context-dependent predictive contributions. The findings demonstrate that a comparatively parsimonious RBF network can provide accurate and computationally efficient CO₂ prediction. By integrating signal decomposition, multi-model benchmarking and explainable AI, the proposed framework provides an interpretable decision-support tool for identifying emission patterns and informing targeted carbon-management and climate-mitigation strategies across RCEP economies.

title: A universal musical minimum: capability, universal design and body percussion in Spanish primary music education
summary: Music is affirmed as an entitlement across the European Union, yet what children receive varies with the resources their schools and regions can command. This paper applies Universal Design for Learning at a level where it is rarely employe
content: Music is affirmed as an entitlement across the European Union, yet what children receive varies with the resources their schools and regions can command. This paper applies Universal Design for Learning at a level where it is rarely employed: not the individual lesson, but the statutory curricular minimum itself. Taking Spain as a case study, it examines what minimum of musical participation a state could guarantee in a form from which no school and no learner could be excluded. Joining universal design with the capability approach, the article argues that such a minimum must be defined as a capability rather than as a resource and specified in competencies rather than materials or gestures. It proposes an instrument-independent curricular floor: a legally protected minimum of rhythmic, ensemble-based and improvisatory participation achievable with the body and voice alone, complementary to instrumental provision and never a substitute for it. Body percussion serves as the analytical test case rather than as the content of the entitlement. The article presents a normative and doctrinal analysis, not an empirical evaluation. It advances a central hypothesis and four derived propositions, states the observations that would confirm or disconfirm each, and specifies the research programme required to test them. Its principal claim is conditional and structural: the current architecture permits variation in what children receive, an entitlement defined in capability terms would remove one mechanism through which that variation operates, and whether it does so in practice is a question for empirical evaluation rather than for theoretical argument.

title: Can fiscal and financial synergy promote the development of the recycled water industry? — Based on the dynamic analysis of evolutionary games and empirical research using staggered DID
summary: China’s recycled water industry faces a financing dilemma: private capital is deterred by high risks, yet fiscal funds alone are insufficient to bridge the gap. As a fiscal-financial policy, the “Water-Saving Loan” launched in 22 provinces
content: China’s recycled water industry faces a financing dilemma: private capital is deterred by high risks, yet fiscal funds alone are insufficient to bridge the gap. As a fiscal-financial policy, the “Water-Saving Loan” launched in 22 provinces since 2019 attempts to resolve this deadlock. This paper investigates whether and how such synergy works. We develop a four-party evolutionary game model incorporating banks as strategic actors, revealing a two-stage transmission chain: government subsidies first reshape enterprises’ financing expectations, which then signal project quality to banks, reducing their risk perception and triggering credit supply. Simulation analysis shows this chain operates only when subsidy rates exceed a calculable threshold. Using staggered DID on provincial panel data, we find that the policy significantly increases recycled water utilization, driven by expanded green credit and infrastructure investment. Heterogeneity analysis indicates that the effect of the water-saving loan policy is significant only in regions with high financial development levels and high urbanization rates. These findings suggest that fiscal-financial tools can amplify but cannot substitute basic infrastructure investment, and that regionally differentiated subsidy thresholds are essential for policy design.

title: Do Performance Appraisals Really Drive Performance? A PLS-SEM Analysis of Feedback, Self-Assessment, and Rewards in Nepal's Organizations
source: Quest Journal of Management and Social Sciences
summary: Background: Employee performance is essential to organizational success, and performance appraisal systems can enhance performance by providing feedback, recognizing contributions, and identifying development opportunities. However, concern
content: Background: Employee performance is essential to organizational success, and performance appraisal systems can enhance performance by providing feedback, recognizing contributions, and identifying development opportunities. However, concerns regarding fairness, transparency, and effectiveness remain, highlighting the need to examine their influence on employee performance. Purpose: The objective of this study is to examine the impact of performance appraisal systems on employee performance. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study adopted a descriptive and explanatory research design. Data were collected from 387 employees using a structured questionnaire through non-probability sampling. The questionnaire was administered using KoboToolbox, and the collected data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistical techniques. The study was grounded in Equity Theory to explain the relationship between performance appraisal practices and employee performance. Findings: The findings indicate that performance appraisal systems, timely feedback, constructive criticism, and self-evaluation significantly improve employee performance. However, financial rewards and employee involvement in goal setting did not have statistically significant effects on employee performance. The findings further indicate that perceived bias, lack of transparency, and delayed feedback can hinder the effectiveness of performance appraisal practices. In contrast, transparent evaluation procedures, employee recognition initiatives, and regular feedback mechanisms were identified as important practices for improving employee performance. Conclusion: Effective performance appraisal practices can contribute significantly to employee performance and organizational success. Appraisal systems that emphasize fairness, transparency, constructive feedback, recognition, and employee development can support employee motivation, job satisfaction, and productivity.

title: Reimagining Species Relations
summary: The year 2022 marked the 10th anniversary of the course Critical Animal Studies: Animals in Society, Culture and the Media at the Department of Communication and Media at Lund University. As the first initiative of its kind in Sweden, the c
content: The year 2022 marked the 10th anniversary of the course Critical Animal Studies: Animals in Society, Culture and the Media at the Department of Communication and Media at Lund University. As the first initiative of its kind in Sweden, the course explores the shifting roles and positions of non-human animals in today’s complex societies. It aims to equip students with analytical tools to critically assess norms and structures that organise human-animal relations, along with their ethical, cultural, and social consequences. What started as a one-course offering driven by an idea has evolved into a decade-long project of education and emancipation for non- human animals. This anthology stands as a testament to the course’s impact, aiming to extend the rich discussions, debates, and insights cultivated beyond the classroom walls. This celebratory collection assembles writings from former students, instructors, and guest lecturers, delving into themes ranging from critical media analysis over activist strategies to pedagogical reflections. The anthology’s scope not only reflects the diverse facets of the course but also unveils the myriad, often subtle intersections between human-centered society and the lives of non-human animals.
