title: FATORES CONTINGENCIAIS E ECONOMIA CIRCULAR: REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA DA LITERATURA E AGENDA DE PESQUISA
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A transição para uma Economia Circular (EC) é influenciada por contingências que podem inibir a flexibilidade desse processo.A influência dos fatores contingenciais na adoção da circularidade é determinante para o sucesso dessa transição.Di
content: A transição para uma Economia Circular (EC) é influenciada por contingências que podem inibir a flexibilidade desse processo.A influência dos fatores contingenciais na adoção da circularidade é determinante para o sucesso dessa transição.Diante disso, o objetivo deste artigo é analisar os fatores contingenciais que influenciam na adoção da circularidade por meio de uma Revisão Sistemática da Literatura (RSL).Especificamente pretende-se: (i) apresentar uma visão geral das pesquisas; (ii) identificar fatores contingenciais que influenciam na EC; e (iii) indicar uma agenda de pesquisa.O método aplicado foi o protocolo PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses), cujas etapas de identificação, triagem e inclusão permitiram chegar a uma amostra de 64 artigos.Os resultados mostram que existem lacunas geográficas, setoriais e organizacionais que explorem a influência dessas contingências na circularidade.Os principais fatores contingenciais identificados foram: institucionais e regulatórios; recursos e capacidades organizacionais; inovação e maturidade tecnológica.A agenda de pesquisa foi proposta considerando os seguintes aspectos: interação entre os fatores contingenciais, práticas circulares e os níveis de circularidade; contexto geográfico, institucional e setorial; contexto organizacional; intersecção teórica e metodológica; e interação entre os fatores.Por fim, os resultados evidenciam que o sucesso da EC é contingente a uma série de fatores, demonstrando que não há uma "única e melhor maneira" de implementar a EC.

title: War-Affected Soils and the Imitation of Knowledge: A Critical Analysis of O. A. Gordienko’s “Impact of War on Soils” in Eurasian Soil Science
summary: This protocol documents a critical case analysis of Gordienko’s 2025 review Impact of War on Soils. The principal conclusion is that a low-quality compilation can acquire the institutional status of knowledge by reproducing the external for
content: This protocol documents a critical case analysis of Gordienko’s 2025 review Impact of War on Soils. The principal conclusion is that a low-quality compilation can acquire the institutional status of knowledge by reproducing the external form of a scientific publication while failing to perform the verification, differentiation, comparison and synthesis required of its declared genre. The initial question is how the publication system recognizes and disseminates such an imitation as a contribution to knowledge. A figure of 121,406 km² and 0.024 percent of Earth is examined against a source about the United States Department of Defense’s real-estate portfolio. Arithmetic reconstruction shows that converting 30 million acres produces the published area, but does not validate its reinterpretation as global war-affected soil. The complete dossier examines soil definitions, named soil categories, Ukraine’s representation, bibliographic selection, contemporary Russian territory, synthesis, genre, scholarly certification, translation, and AI disclosure. The protocol records competing explanations and distinguishes public evidence from interpretations and earlier audit findings requiring reproducible confirmation. It treats narrative reviews as a legitimate genre and does not equate the absence of a systematic-review checklist with invalidity. The full pattern supports the analytical classification of this text as imitation of review knowledge and identifies successful publication of that imitation as the main institutional problem. The citation error is evidence within the case, not its whole conclusion. This classification does not imply proof of deliberate deception or establish private reviewer conduct or prevalence across publishing.

title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO2 by the stick-to-culture strategy
summary: The accelerating global energy demand, coupled with diminishing fossil fuel reserves and growing carbon emissions, underscores the urgent need for sustainable energy solutions. Autotrophic microalgae are promising cell factories for convert
content: The accelerating global energy demand, coupled with diminishing fossil fuel reserves and growing carbon emissions, underscores the urgent need for sustainable energy solutions. Autotrophic microalgae are promising cell factories for converting CO2 into renewable biofuels. However, conventional microalgal biofuels typically depend on energy-intensive or nutrient-deficient regimes that suppress microalgal proliferation, resulting in a critical trade-off between biomass growth and lipid biosynthesis. Here, we report a separable living interface with microalgae (SLIM) platform that employs extracellular-matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds to spatially organize microalgae and dynamically reconfigure their microenvironment, enabling spatiotemporal switching between biomass accumulation or lipid induction. The SLIM platform supports high-density growth of microalgae while facilitating precision substrate-driven metabolic regulation, enabling low-carbon operation and improved lipid production (8.89 g L−1). This work establishes an engineered living material that overcomes essential bottlenecks in microalgal biofuel production and offers a generalizable blueprint for biohybrid systems in advanced biomanufacturing. Balancing biomass growth and lipid accumulation remains a challenge in microalgal biofuel production. Here the authors report extracellular matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds that dynamically reconfigure the microenvironment of spatially organized microalgae, allowing controlled switching between the two states.

title: Co-Benefit Analysis from the Implementation of the REDD+ Program in West Kalimantan, Indonesia
source: Jurnal Pengelolaan Sumberdaya Alam dan Lingkungan (Journal of Natural Resources and Environmental Management)
summary: Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (REDD+) remains a key mechanism to mitigate climate change in developing nations. However, forest degradation in Indonesia often stems from local livelihoods that depend on forest
tags: Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation
content: Reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (REDD+) remains a key mechanism to mitigate climate change in developing nations. However, forest degradation in Indonesia often stems from local livelihoods that depend on forest resources. Standard REDD+ implementations frequently fail when they overlook livelihood co-benefits for local villagers. This study analyzes how stakeholders in West Kalimantan recognize and generate co-benefits through the REDD+ program. Structural critical discourse analysis (CDA) is employed to examine the entanglement of micro-level community practices and macro-level forest governance policies, particularly following the implementation of Law 23/2014. Field data were collected between 2018 and 2023 through focus group discussions (FGDs) and key informant interviews across intervention villages. The results demonstrate that aligning emission reduction targets with community socio-economic welfare—specifically through non-timber forest product (NTFP) development and silvofishery—enabled the program to achieve 293,142 tCO2e in emission reductions (representing 97.71% of the planned minimum target). Furthermore, the welfare performance, evaluated qualitatively through the IDM’s assessment, shows that the status of a very underdeveloped village, which was attributed to the intervened villages, has been reduced to none. Also, villages transitioning from "Developing" to “Developed” to "Independent" village status experienced reductions in village welfare. These all indicate > 80% improvement in villagers' livelihoods. I conclude that securing tangible local co-benefits is essential for sustaining long-term carbon mitigation outcomes in tropical forest landscapes.

title: SERVITIZAÇÃO NO SETOR ENERGÉTICO: UMA ANÁLISE BIBLIOMÉTRICA DAS TENDÊNCIAS GLOBAIS

summary: A servitização tem ganhado destaque no setor energético em função da digitalização, da busca por eficiência e das exigências da transição energética.Apesar da crescente adoção de modelos baseados em serviços, ainda são limitadas as revisões
content: A servitização tem ganhado destaque no setor energético em função da digitalização, da busca por eficiência e das exigências da transição energética.Apesar da crescente adoção de modelos baseados em serviços, ainda são limitadas as revisões sistemáticas focadas especificamente nesse setor.Assim, este estudo tem como objetivo mapear o estado da arte, identificando sua evolução, principais contribuições e tendências emergentes.Para tanto, realizouse uma revisão sistemática na base Scopus, com termos relacionados à servitização, Product-Service Systems e modelos as-a-service, resultando em 2. 588 documentos analisados por bibliometria com apoio do VOSviewer.Os resultados indicam que China, Estados Unidos e Índia lideram a produção científica na área.A análise de coocorrência identificou quatro eixos centrais: (i) computação em nuvem e eficiência energética; (ii) armazenamento e integração de fontes renováveis; (iii) economia circular e modelos de negócio sustentáveis; e (iv) digitalização baseada em IoT e plataformas de serviço.Conclui-se que a servitização no setor energético constitui um campo interdisciplinar em expansão, impulsionado por avanços tecnológicos e agendas de sustentabilidade, abrindo oportunidades de pesquisa, especialmente no contexto brasileiro.

title: Gérer les forêts suisses pour optimiser l'utilisation du bois
summary: La Suisse s’est fixé l’objectif ambitieux d’atteindre la neutralité carbone d’ici 2050. Le secteur de la construction, en particulier, recèle d’un immense potentiel en remplaçant les matériaux fortement émetteurs de CO2 (tels que le béton e
content: La Suisse s’est fixé l’objectif ambitieux d’atteindre la neutralité carbone d’ici 2050. Le secteur de la construction, en particulier, recèle d’un immense potentiel en remplaçant les matériaux fortement émetteurs de CO2 (tels que le béton et l’acier) par des biomatériaux comme le bois. Toutefois, pour évaluer la faisabilité de cette transition, il est nécessaire d’estimer la quantité future de biomasse forestière locale disponible ainsi que la composition en essences forestières et les impacts sur la biodiversité. Dans le cadre du projet multidisciplinaire MainWood, nous simulons l’évolution future des forêts suisses selon des scénarios climatiques anticipés et pour différentes stratégies de gestion développées en collaboration avec les parties prenantes. Nous avons sélectionné cinq régions d’étude représentant chacune des zones biogéographiques suisses. Pour évaluer l’adéquation climatique des essences forestières et leur dynamique de croissance, nous avons utilisé le modèle ForClim à l’échelle du peuplement. Nos simulations s’appuient sur différents scénarios de gestion forestière: un scénario «Business-as-usual» (sylviculture proche de la nature et polyvalente) et des scénarios alternatifs élaborés en concertation avec les parties prenantes, incluant des approches de gestion différenciées (par exemple, des plantations de conifères à rotation courte) pour répondre à la demande future attendue en bois de construction. Nous évaluons également l’impact de ces différents scénarios de gestion forestière sur la biodiversité, ce qui permet de trouver un équilibre entre l’exploitation du bois et les mesures liées à la biodiversité. Dans certaines régions, nous avons constaté une augmentation de la productivité forestière aux altitudes plus élevées. Cependant, ces gains de biomasse ne pourront pas nécessairement être exploités en raison de la difficulté et du coût des opérations d’exploitation dans les régions montagneuses. A plus basse altitude, la productivité forestière devrait diminuer, parfois assez drastiquement dans certaines régions. Le rajeunissement artificiel pourrait, dans certains cas, pallier partiellement cette perte de productivité forestière en favorisant une évolution vers une proportion plus élevée d’essences feuillues. Cela nécessitera toutefois une adaptation de la filière forêt-bois, incluant le développement de nouvelles technologies capables de mettre en œuvre des processus de construction rentables utilisant de nouveaux produits d’ingénierie du bois à base d’un mélange d’essences résineuses et feuillues.

title: Evaluation of performance and emissions of a diesel engine using dual aqueous ammonia -diesel fuel
summary: Abstract The carbon footprint of fossil fuel application is a crucial indicator of the overall quantity of greenhouse gases discharged into the atmosphere. Sustainable replacements, such as aqueous ammonia, are viewed as a good approach to
content: Abstract The carbon footprint of fossil fuel application is a crucial indicator of the overall quantity of greenhouse gases discharged into the atmosphere. Sustainable replacements, such as aqueous ammonia, are viewed as a good approach to solve the shortage of conventional fuel, low-carbon fuels and address climate change. Emissions and performance of diesel engine running on dual fuel of diesel and aqueous ammonia were investigated. Ammonia and water were combined in volumetric amounts of 5, 10, and 15% to get around these adverse effects. Adding aqueous ammonia of 5, 10 and 15% to diesel boosted brake specific fuel consumption by 4, 7, and 13% at 75% of engine output power. Thermal efficiency of diesel and aqueous ammonia were decreased by 4, 7 and 13% when aqueous ammonia was added by 5, 10 and 15%. Aqueous ammonia of 5%, 10% and 15% demonstrated increases of 17, 32 and 42% in CO emissions about diesel, whereas the decreases in nitrogen oxides were 5, 10 and 15% in relation to diesel, respectively. At 100% of output power, increases in hydrocarbon emissions for 5%, 10%, and 15% aqueous ammonia were 10, 23, and 31% but carbon dioxide values were decreased by 6, 12, and 17% for diesel with aqueous ammonia compared to diesel oil. Increases of oxygen concentrations for 5%, 10% and 15% aqueous ammonia were 6, 8 and 10%, respectively at 75% of output power. Engine performance penalties and emissions issues limit the use of aqueous ammonia, despite its potential as a carbon-reducing supplemental fuel.

title: A comparative TEA–LCA study of biomethane production through anaerobic digestion and five upgrading technologies: Amine scrubbing, water scrubbing, membrane separation, PSA, and cryogenic separation
summary: Producing grid-quality biomethane from sewage-sludge biogas is promising, yet selecting an upgrading route remains uncertain because mature technologies differ in energy use, cost, methane losses in off-gas or vent streams, and the fate of
content: Producing grid-quality biomethane from sewage-sludge biogas is promising, yet selecting an upgrading route remains uncertain because mature technologies differ in energy use, cost, methane losses in off-gas or vent streams, and the fate of biogenic CO 2 . This study evaluates anaerobic digestion integrated with five commercial upgrading technologies: amine scrubbing, water scrubbing (WS), membrane separation (MEM), pressure swing adsorption (PSA), and cryogenic separation (CRYO), modelled for a municipal wastewater treatment plant. All configurations deliver grid-quality biomethane, while separated CO 2 is compressed and liquefied where feasible; venting is assumed for the dilute CO 2 stream from WS. Aspen Plus simulations were coupled with techno-economic analysis (TEA) and consequential life cycle assessment (LCA). The results show clear trade-offs. Amine scrubbing has the highest thermal demand (1207 kW), whereas CRYO and MEM have the highest upgrading-unit electricity demands (257 and 201 kW, respectively). Economically, without an additional emission charge, WS is the most attractive option, with the lowest levelized cost of biomethane (LCOM) of 436 €/t, while amine scrubbing is the most expensive (652 €/t). Hypothetical charges on vented biogenic CO 2 and CH 4 progressively increase the LCOM of WS above those of MEM, CRYO, PSA, and amine scrubbing at approximately 36.5, 37.7, 43.2, and 120.4 €/t CO 2 -eq, respectively. From an environmental perspective, consequential LCA shows that PSA, MEM, and CRYO outperform solvent-based routes in human health, ecosystem, and climate performance due to efficient CO 2 liquefaction and avoidance of upgrading-stage venting. In the deterministic base case, PSA delivers the highest net human-health savings and the largest net GHG reduction, whereas WS shows the weakest climate performance. The economic preference for WS depends on emission-pricing assumptions, while PSA, MEM, and CRYO are more suitable for carbon-circular biorefineries.

title: Continuous Low-Temperature Photothermal CO2 Desorption Enables Scalable Solar-Driven Direct Air Capture
summary: Direct air capture (DAC) is increasingly recognized as an indispensable negative-emission technology for achieving carbon neutrality. However, its practical deployment is severely constrained by energy-intensive CO 2 desorption, high desorp
content: Direct air capture (DAC) is increasingly recognized as an indispensable negative-emission technology for achieving carbon neutrality. However, its practical deployment is severely constrained by energy-intensive CO 2 desorption, high desorption temperature, poor stability, and complex batch operations. Here, we present a continuous low-temperature photothermal CO 2 desorption strategy that enables scalable solar-driven DAC. Photothermal polyethyleneimine–polyethylene glycol (PEI–PEG) functionalized pellets suitable for scalable applications are developed, which simultaneously demonstrate high broadband solar absorptance of 87.4%, good CO 2 adsorption capacity of 1.2 mmol·g −1 , and ultralow desorption temperature of 66 °C. The underlying mechanism is attributed to hydrogen bond cross-linking network of PEI and PEG, stabilizing the anime active sites and reducing the steric hindrance for internal CO 2 diffusion. Building on these materials, a kilogram-scale continuous photothermal CO 2 desorption system is established for the first time via integrating PEI–PEG adsorbent pellets with hourglass inspired self-rolling reactors. Remarkable solar-chemical efficiency of 24.8%, in stark contrast to only 11.5% for discontinuous batch reactor system, is demonstrated due to high pellet solar absorptance, low desorption temperature, and dynamic balance between pellets flow and incident photoenergy. This work establishes a promising pathway toward scalable, efficient, and low-carbon-footprint DAC through continuous low-temperature photothermal CO 2 desorption.

title: Pathways to Enhance Direct Carbon Sequestration and Indirect Carbon-Saving Benefits in Urban Parks: A Joint Analysis of Landscape and Morphological Spatial Patterns
summary: The carbon mitigation benefits of urban parks are expanding beyond traditional biological carbon sequestration to encompass the regulation of urban energy demand. Direct carbon sequestration capacity (DCSC), resulting from vegetation carbon
content: The carbon mitigation benefits of urban parks are expanding beyond traditional biological carbon sequestration to encompass the regulation of urban energy demand. Direct carbon sequestration capacity (DCSC), resulting from vegetation carbon fixation, and indirect carbon-saving capacity (ICSC), arising from reductions in building cooling energy consumption induced by summer cooling effects, represent two important pathways for carbon mitigation by urban parks. However, how landscape patterns and morphological spatial patterns jointly regulate DCSC and ICSC, and what nonlinear responses and interactions exist among different spatial indicators remain to be further investigated. Focusing on urban parks in the main urban area of Harbin, this study quantified DCSC and ICSC using multisource remote sensing data and revealed the spatial differences between these two carbon mitigation functions. By developing an analytical framework integrating explainable machine learning and nonlinear response modeling, this study identified the key indicators affecting DCSC and ICSC, the directions of their contributions, and their interactions. It further characterized the nonlinear responses of key indicator combinations and identified favorable ranges for the synergistic enhancement in both carbon benefits. The results showed that: (1) DCSC ranged from 0.96 to 946.75 kg C·day−1, while ICSC ranged from 0.10 to 9,828.50 kg C·day−1. Total ICSC across all parks was approximately 16 times the total DCSC, and both DCSC and ICSC were generally lower in urban parks located within the inner ring. (2) The relative contributions of landscape metrics and MSPA classes to the two carbon benefits differed markedly: landscape metrics made a greater explanatory contribution to ICSC, whereas MSPA classes made a relatively greater explanatory contribution to DCSC. Mean shape index (SHAPE_MN), patch density (PD), and Perforation were identified as key indicators with the potential to enhance both DCSC and ICSC. (3) From a synergistic perspective, interactions involving SHAPE_MN were prominent, with SHAPE_MN × PD ranking among the strongest for both responses, highlighting the importance of boundary complexity and spatial fragmentation. In addition, coordinating green space coverage, spatial continuity, boundary morphology, and the integrity of core spaces can effectively promote the synergistic enhancement in both carbon benefits. These findings provide a new planning basis for optimizing urban park structures in cold-region cities under spatial constraints and advancing the goal of urban carbon neutrality.

title: Green is Queen: Do Female CEOs Promote Substantive Green Innovation or Tactical Green Innovation?
summary: ABSTRACT Green innovation serves as a pivotal strategy for firms to achieve sustainable development. Given the steadily increasing demand for female leadership in the firms, understanding how female CEOs impact green innovation has emerged
content: ABSTRACT Green innovation serves as a pivotal strategy for firms to achieve sustainable development. Given the steadily increasing demand for female leadership in the firms, understanding how female CEOs impact green innovation has emerged as a critical area of inquiry. This study utilizes panel data from Chinese listed companies from 2012 to 2025 to empirically investigate how female CEOs impact different types of green innovation. The research findings indicate that female CEOs play a significant role in promoting substantive green innovation while simultaneously inhibiting tactical green innovation. From the perspective of time attention allocation, female CEOs exert differentiated impacts on green innovation by suppressing the senior executives' current attention and promoting their future attention. Furthermore, media environmental protection coverage exerts distinct moderation effects on the impact of female CEOs on the green innovation. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the impact of female CEOs on the two types of green innovation is more significant in state-owned enterprises, heavy-polluting industries, northern regions, and firms with longer female CEO tenure. This study contributes to the advancement of cross-theoretical research on leadership and corporate governance.

title: Policy Coherence for Industrial Sustainability Under SDG 9: A Systematic Literature Review and Integrative Framework for Emerging Economies
summary: ABSTRACT Implementing SDG 9 in emerging economies faces persistent policy incoherence, which existing studies often examine as isolated administrative issues. To address this gap, this study uses an abductive design combining a systematic l
content: ABSTRACT Implementing SDG 9 in emerging economies faces persistent policy incoherence, which existing studies often examine as isolated administrative issues. To address this gap, this study uses an abductive design combining a systematic literature review (2015–2025) with a literature‐driven comparative synthesis of India, Indonesia, and Thailand under a Most‐Different Systems Design. We conceptualize a cascading fragmentation mechanism, proposing how institutional disconnects may sequentially generate capability, knowledge, and transition gaps that contribute to policy incoherence as an emergent outcome. Based on these insights, we introduce the Multi‐level Sustainability Governance Framework (MSGF). The MSGF contributes to policy coherence scholarship by framing incoherence as a dynamic sequence and offers planning agencies a diagnostic logic to identify operational bottlenecks in emerging contexts.

title: From Labor to Land: Rethinking the Objective of Agricultural Mechanization in China
source: China Journal of Agricultural Economics & Development
summary: : Agricultural mechanization has long been valued primarily for its capacity to substitute for labor. However, with increasingly binding constraints on arable land and raising yields per unit of land becoming central to safeguarding nationa
content: : Agricultural mechanization has long been valued primarily for its capacity to substitute for labor. However, with increasingly binding constraints on arable land and raising yields per unit of land becoming central to safeguarding national food security, the developmental objective of mechanization must evolve accordingly. This study argues that mechanization should move from a predominantly labor-substituting orientation toward a dual labor–land substitution objective, focusing on strengthening its land-substituting capacity. Drawing on the theory of induced technical change, it identifies two broadly established evolutionary phases of agricultural mechanization’s substitution effects since 1978 in China: draft-animal substitution followed by labor substitution. It further identifies an emerging post-2023 tendency for mechanization to acquire a land-substituting dimension. In this emerging technological context, the increasingly intensive application of artificial intelligence and digital technologies is reshaping the functional role of agricultural mechanization. Through precision sowing, optimized plant density, and low-loss harvesting, mechanization improves operational precision and reduces production losses, thereby providing an increasingly important technological and material foundation for raising grain yields. Taken together, these developments suggest a reorientation toward dual labor–land substitution. Against this technological backdrop, the study outlines policy directions for strengthening the land-substituting and yield-enhancing capacities of agricultural mechanization.

title: Chitosan-Based miR-675 Nanocarriers Immobilized on Polycaprolactone/Silk Fibroin Nanofibers for Enhanced Odontogenic Differentiation
summary: Enhancing odontogenic differentiation of dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) is a crucial aspect of regenerative endodontic treatments. Herein, miR-675-loaded chitosan nanoparticles were engineered to obtain ultra-small, positively charged compl
content: Enhancing odontogenic differentiation of dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) is a crucial aspect of regenerative endodontic treatments. Herein, miR-675-loaded chitosan nanoparticles were engineered to obtain ultra-small, positively charged complexes (~60 nm, zeta potential > +15 mV) with high colloidal stability, biocompatibility, and 70% cellular uptake. These nanocarriers were immobilized onto polydopamine-modified PCL/silk fibroin nanofibers, using pH-controlled deposition to tune chitosan protonation, nanoparticle aggregation, and surface coverage without disrupting the three-dimensional fibrous architecture. This approach produced a uniform miR-675/CSNPs-loaded PD-modified PCL/SF scaffold with increased hydrophilicity and preserved interconnected porosity, thereby enhancing DPSC adhesion, proliferation, and cytoskeletal organization compared with bare scaffolds. Moreover, alkaline phosphatase activity, extracellular matrix mineralization, and Western blot analysis revealed marked upregulation of odontogenic markers, including RUNX2, ALP, COL-I, DSPP, and DMP-1. Collectively, these findings demonstrate a synergistic effect between sustained miR-675 delivery via CSNPs and the biomimetic PCL/SF architecture, establishing a promising platform for odontogenic differentiation of DPSCs and dentin-pulp complex regeneration.

title: Exploring the Digital Economy and Green Logistics Nexus in China: Evidence from 120 Logistics Hub Cities
summary: The integration of the digital economy (DE) and green logistics (GL) is increasingly recognized as a critical pathway for modernizing logistics systems and achieving carbon neutrality. However, their spatiotemporal synergy remains underexpl
content: The integration of the digital economy (DE) and green logistics (GL) is increasingly recognized as a critical pathway for modernizing logistics systems and achieving carbon neutrality. However, their spatiotemporal synergy remains underexplored. Utilizing panel data from 120 logistics hub cities (LHC) in China from 2013 to 2022, this study constructs a comprehensive framework to evaluate the coupling coordination degree (CCD) between DE and GL. We employ the Dagum Gini coefficient to dissect spatial disparities and integrate the CatBoost algorithm with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to unravel the driving mechanisms of this coordination. The results reveal that: (1) The overall CCD in Chinese LHC exhibits a consistent upward trajectory, yet spatial development remains highly uneven, forming a distinct hierarchical spatial pattern. (2) Spatial disparities in the integration level have widened over time, with transvariation density constituting the primary source of overall inequality. (3) The CatBoost-SHAP analysis identifies urban economic density, urbanization level, advanced industrial structure, and human capital level as the paramount drivers. These findings enrich existing literature by providing nuanced, data-driven insights for policymakers to leverage digitalization, formulate spatially differentiated strategies, and foster sustainable logistics networks.

title: Biosynthesis of selenium nanoparticles with orange peel waste in microwave: characterization, and spectral properties
summary: Abstract The objective of this study was to reuse agroindustrial waste from orange peels to obtain an orange peel aqueous extract (OPEa), used in the biosynthesis and characterization of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs). The OPEa acted as a r
content: Abstract The objective of this study was to reuse agroindustrial waste from orange peels to obtain an orange peel aqueous extract (OPEa), used in the biosynthesis and characterization of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs). The OPEa acted as a reducing and stabilizing agent in the synthesis of SeNPs, due to its polyphenolic compounds, such as flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, and coumarins, identified by UHPLC-HRMS/MS. The synthesis of SeNPs was conducted in a microwave reactor, at 120 °C and 150 °C, for 30 min, using different volumetric proportions/concentrations between OPEa and sodium selenite (Na₂SeO₃) (5 and 10 mM), in ratios of 1:4, 2:3, 1:1, 3:2, and 4:1 (OPEa (mL) :Na 2 SeO 3(mL) ). The SeNPs were characterized by visual inspection, UV/Vis, DLS, pH, TEM, SEM, and EDX. The results showed that SeNPs were successfully biosynthesized under all conditions, exhibiting distinct characteristics depending on the synthesis conditions. The formation of SeNPs was confirmed by the chromatic transition from greenish tones to light yellow to intense red and by UV/Vis spectrometry, with absorption peaks in the range of 250–340 nm. The SeNPs exhibited a hydrodynamic diameter (HD) of 213.6–1296 nm, with mono- and polydispersity characteristics (PdI: 0.033–0.885) and Zeta potential (ZP) between − 24.2 to -54.9 mV. Among the conditions tested, SeNPs with the best characteristics presented more homogeneous UV/Vis bands, lower HD (273.2–282.8 nm), and PdI (0.089–0.231), high ZP (-34.4 to -36.5 mV), stable pH (6), clear, translucent, and pellet-free colloidal solution, spherical morphology, and selenium accounted for 20.17% of its elemental composition.

title: Reparative soil science: Soil, colonialism, and environmental justice between scientific knowledge and local cultures
summary: Soil is a repository for historical accounts of power, dispossession, and cultural continuity. This paper proposes the development of “reparative soil science,” a new paradigm that combines soil remediation with theories of environmental ju
content: Soil is a repository for historical accounts of power, dispossession, and cultural continuity. This paper proposes the development of “reparative soil science,” a new paradigm that combines soil remediation with theories of environmental justice, decolonization, and multi-knowledge systems. We define it as an orientation within soil science that treats the discipline’s own concepts, classifications, and survey conventions as historical products, and that couples the biophysical repair of degraded soils with repair of the rights, relations, and forms of knowledge that colonial land regimes displaced. By analyzing examples from around the world, the paper shows how colonialism and postcolonial land governance have resulted in the devaluation of local epistemologies and the transformation of socioecological systems. Results indicate that successful integration of scientific and Indigenous knowledge requires mutual legitimacy, long-term trust-building, and equitable sharing of decision-making authority and benefits. It is argued that reparative soil science should extend beyond the purely technical rehabilitation of degraded soils to challenge existing structural inequalities and help restore cultural and ecological relationships between humans and the land. Soil is our entry point, but the same reasoning extends to land, territory, and natural resources more broadly. The perspective positions soil science within global agreements such as the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, the Sustainable Development Goals, and Land Degradation Neutrality, and argues for a pluralistic, participatory, and politically aware practice serving both ecological resilience and social repair.

title: Effects of carbonization temperature on the performance of bamboo fiber-reinforced cementitious composites and their potential applications in deicing pavement
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates the effects of carbonization temperature and fiber dosage on the mechanical properties, thermal conductivity, and rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) response of bamboo fiber-reinforced C40 concrete. Bamb
content: ABSTRACT This study investigates the effects of carbonization temperature and fiber dosage on the mechanical properties, thermal conductivity, and rapid chloride penetration test (RCPT) response of bamboo fiber-reinforced C40 concrete. Bamboo fibers were incorporated at dosages of 1.5%–4.5% and used in three states: uncarbonized, carbonized at 300 °C, and carbonized at 800 °C. Compressive strength, splitting tensile strength, thermal conductivity, RCPT charge passed before and after dry-wet cycling, and microstructural characteristics were evaluated. Uncarbonized fibers improved tensile resistance but reduced thermal conductivity because of their porous and insulating structure. In contrast, the 800 °C carbonized bamboo-derived material enhanced thermal conductivity and exhibited lower RCPT charge-passed values, accompanied by a carbon-rich structure and a denser fiber–matrix interface. At 3.5% fiber content, the 800 °C carbonized mixture showed a 19% increase in thermal conductivity relative to the reference mixture under the reduced-aggregate testing conditions. Scenario-based finite element analysis showed that lowering the ambient temperature from −3 to −8 °C increased the predicted heating time from 2.6 to 3.4 h. The study identifies a mechanical–thermal trade-off associated with carbonization and examines its implications for a layered pavement concept.

title: When does hydrogen become competitive? Cost and efficiency thresholds for storage in a pan-European renewable energy system
summary: Abstract This paper examines the integration of hydrogen storage in renewable-intensive energy systems through the application of stochastic optimization processes, followed by a comprehensive sensitivity analysis. Our findings indicate tha
content: Abstract This paper examines the integration of hydrogen storage in renewable-intensive energy systems through the application of stochastic optimization processes, followed by a comprehensive sensitivity analysis. Our findings indicate that while current hydrogen storage technology is costly and inefficient, reducing hydrogen costs to 12.5% of current levels and increasing round-trip efficiency to 70% could make it competitive. These requirements are challenging but feasible, given positive predictions on cost reduction and efficiency attainability currently. Furthermore , we find that assuming the hydrogen’s competitiveness, including hydrogen storage can reduce total energy system costs by partly replacing lithium batteries to lower storage costs, and increasing grid flexibility to lower transmission costs. Additionally, integrating hydrogen can decrease the share of nuclear and fossil fuels in the generation mix, thereby reducing generation costs. Italy and Germany are identified as primary targets for hydrogen expansion in Europe. Lastly, in the scenario of limited lithium battery expansion due to the expected lithium shortage in Europe by 2030, hydrogen will need to be introduced into the energy system earlier than anticipated to compensate for increasing system storage demand.

title: Steering directional charge migration via ordered self-assembled molecular layers for efficient BiVO4-silicon artificial leaf
summary: Abstract The BiVO 4 -silicon artificial leaf represents a promising unbiased photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting device, yet its efficiency remains limited by sluggish charge transport in the BiVO 4 photoanode. To overcome these limi
content: Abstract The BiVO 4 -silicon artificial leaf represents a promising unbiased photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting device, yet its efficiency remains limited by sluggish charge transport in the BiVO 4 photoanode. To overcome these limitations, we propose a self-assembled molecular-bridge strategy to establish ordered and fast pathways for efficient charge transport between BiVO 4 and NiFeCoO x oxygen evolution cocatalysts (OECs). To clarify the role of dipole strength, we compare two self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) with distinct dipole moments: [4-(9H-carbazol-9-yl)ethyl]phosphonic acid (4PACZ ~ 1.83 Debye) and (4-(7H-dibenzo[c,g]carbazol-7-yl)butyl)phosphonic acid (4PADCB ~ 2.54 Debye). The larger dipole of 4PADCB generates a stronger interfacial electric field (IEF), which drives directional hole extraction and suppresses recombination. Consequently, the optimized BiVO 4 /4PADCB/NiFeCoO x photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.35 mA cm⁻ 2 at 1.23 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode (V RHE ), ranking among the best BiVO 4 -based systems modified with organic interfacial layers. Furthermore, by integrating the photoanode with a silicon solar cell, a standalone artificial leaf (1.5 cm 2 area) was constructed, achieving a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 8.75% and stable operation for over 15 hours. This work establishes a clear link between molecular dipole strength and interfacial charge separation, providing a generalizable design principle for molecular interface engineering in PEC water splitting.

title: Do government debt, trade openness, and oil prices affect inflation rates in GCC countries?
summary: Abstract This paper investigates whether the effects of government debt, trade openness, and oil prices on inflation in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries during the period 1980–2024 are symmetric or asymmetric, and if these relat
content: Abstract This paper investigates whether the effects of government debt, trade openness, and oil prices on inflation in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries during the period 1980–2024 are symmetric or asymmetric, and if these relationships are influenced by play external shocks in shaping inflation dynamics. The study utilizes Panel Autoregressive Distributed Lag (PARDL) and Panel Nonlinear ARDL (PNARDL) models to examine both short-run and long-run dynamics accompanied by stationarity and co-integration test to confirm the robustness of estimations, while IS bootstrap causality test is applied to detect the direction and crisis-sensitivity of the nexus among variables. The findings indicate that government debt, trade openness and oil prices have statistically and economically significant and asymmetric impact on inflation, where positive shocks in trade openness induce higher inflationary pressures than negative shocks. The error correction term indicates the presence of a stable long-run equilibrium, suggesting a convergence in transitory deviations. Moreover, bidirectional and crisis-sensitive linkages are indicated from causality results, especially in the major global perturbations like the financial crisis of 2007–2008 and the COVID-19 pandemic. Although the analysis is confined to the GCC countries and this may limit the applicability of the results, it offers useful policy implications by signaling the necessity of having fiscal and monetary regimes that consider asymmetries and external vulnerabilities. In addition, they signal the relevance of tackling structural imbalances and shielding households from non-uniform inflationary consequences linked with debt accumulation, trade openness and oil price volatility, in shaping macroeconomic policies that are more robust and better able to adapt. JEL classification: E62, E31, E32, C33

title: Study on properties, mechanism and carbon benefit of cementing tailings backfill with full solid waste binder
summary: The synergistic effects of full solid waste binder (FWB) on the performance of cemented tailings backfill (CTB) require in-depth investigation. In this study, the performance, mechanism and carbon emission benefit of FWB CTB are systematica
content: The synergistic effects of full solid waste binder (FWB) on the performance of cemented tailings backfill (CTB) require in-depth investigation. In this study, the performance, mechanism and carbon emission benefit of FWB CTB are systematically investigated. Experimental results revealed that slurry fluidity is significantly reduced with increasing content of alkaline slag in FWB. Notably, ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) exhibited a more pronounced fluidity-reducing effect compared to steel slag. The compressive strength of CTB is gradually decreased as the FWB-to-tailings ratio decreases. Remarkably, at a 1:10 FWB-to-tailings ratio, the A4 CTB achieved 116% higher compressive strength than conventional cement CTB. Field trials confirmed the practical viability of FWB CTB, with engineering strength reaching 2.3 MPa, which exceeding the 1.8 MPa of design requirement. A4 CTB at a 1:6 FWB-to-tailings ratio demonstrated a 49% reduction in 14d drying shrinkage relative to cement CTB. More ettringite (AFt) was generated in A4 CTB, coupled with a substantial porosity reduction of 5.5%. A larger number of pores and unreacted particles was found in A7. The superior performance of FWB CTB is attributed to three synergistic mechanisms: (1) development of a denser CTB micro-structure, (2) increased formation of hydration, and (3) inherent shrinkage compensation capabilities. FWB exhibit a reduction of over 95% in carbon emission compared with Portland cement. A decrease in the FWB-to-tailings ratio, by contrast, results in a unexpected rise in carbon emission normalized to unit compressive strength.

title: Multistage Thermally Responsive Aerogel for Full‐Cycle Thermal Protection in Battery Modules to Prevent Thermal Runaway Propagation
summary: ABSTRACT Thermal runaway propagation (TRP) remains a critical safety challenge for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, traditional thermal protection materials cannot address the coupled hazards of heat, flames, and explosion‐induced mec
content: ABSTRACT Thermal runaway propagation (TRP) remains a critical safety challenge for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, traditional thermal protection materials cannot address the coupled hazards of heat, flames, and explosion‐induced mechanical impact during TR. Herein, a multistage thermal response aerogel strategy for full‐cycle TR protection was designed. During the controllable stage, the aerogel releases water vapor, which not only reduces the theoretical oxygen mole fraction to 4.07% but also enables early warning through changes in local humidity. During the uncontrollable stage, Co‐BDC‐assisted decomposition sustains the evolution of flame‐retardant gases, enabling prolonged flame suppression. Meanwhile, an in situ ceramization reaction is triggered, generating a dense ceramic layer on the aerogel surface. Together with sustained gas‐phase flame suppression, this condensed‐phase ceramic barrier effectively suppresses flame propagation. The sandwich‐like porous structure of the aerogel creates a tortuous heat‐transfer pathway, suppressing heat transfer. Furthermore, in situ ceramization enhances the compressive strength of the aerogel from 1.25 to 4.5 MPa, enabling resistance against explosion‐induced mechanical impact during TR. TRP experiments conducted on different battery modules confirmed that the aerogel effectively suppresses TRP. This study demonstrates a strategy for thermal protection materials that is tailored to the stages of TR, ensuring the operational safety of battery modules.

title: Bridging Micro and Macro Sustainability: How Sustainable Finance Connects Corporate esg to Sustainable Development Goals
summary: ABSTRACT Sustainable finance (SF) has increasingly been conceptualized in the literature as a mechanism linking firm‐level ESG practices to broader sustainable development outcomes. However, the field remains theoretically fragmented, with
content: ABSTRACT Sustainable finance (SF) has increasingly been conceptualized in the literature as a mechanism linking firm‐level ESG practices to broader sustainable development outcomes. However, the field remains theoretically fragmented, with limited integrated mapping of micro–SF–macro linkages. Using scientometric and bibliometric techniques, this study analyzes 1,024 Scopus‐indexed publications (2004–2025) through performance analysis, keyword co‐occurrence, text mining, and bibliographic coupling. Thirteen keyword clusters reveal the intellectual structure of the field, spanning green finance, ESG performance, governance, climate policy, and energy transition. Bibliographic coupling identifies six thematic clusters that suggest how sustainable finance is theorized to link firm‐level actions with macro‐level sustainability transformations. Despite rapid post–Paris Agreement growth, theoretical and methodological coherence remains limited. The study outlines future research directions, emphasizing disclosure harmonization, causal identification, innovation–policy alignment, and multi‐level approaches. Accordingly, the findings capture patterns in the literature rather than empirically verified causal relationships.

title: Centralized versus conventional anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge: An environmental and economic assessment
summary: High-solid anaerobic digestion (HSAD), in which dewatered sewage sludge from several small wastewater treatment plants is treated centrally, is an alternative to conventional low-solid anaerobic digestion (LSAD) for sludge stabilization and
content: High-solid anaerobic digestion (HSAD), in which dewatered sewage sludge from several small wastewater treatment plants is treated centrally, is an alternative to conventional low-solid anaerobic digestion (LSAD) for sludge stabilization and energy recovery from biogas. This work develops a modelling framework to compare centralized HSAD and decentralized LSAD through a coupled life cycle assessment (LCA) and economic analysis approach, supporting case-specific decision-making for sludge management under defined local boundary conditions. Four different sub-scenarios were modeled for both HSAD (S1.1-S1.4) and LSAD (S2.1-S2.4), forecasting different biogas uses, alternative sludge transportation routes, digestate valorization pathways, and ammonia extraction. The sub-scenarios were compared with the respective baselines (S1.0 for HSAD and S2.0 for LSAD), corresponding to full-scale Italian plant configurations. Under the investigated full-scale conditions, HSAD showed lower environmental impacts than conventional LSAD when transport distances were limited, due to higher credits generated by biogas and the avoided mineral fertilizer use in agriculture. However, input sludge/digestate transportation is a dominant driver of both environmental and economic impacts. Moreover, biogas upgrading to biomethane is environmentally preferable to electricity generation, but economically unfavourable at current market conditions. Overall, centralized HSAD can represent a favorable solution under regional-scale planning when logistics, digestate valorization, and gate-fee conditions are suitable, whereas optimized LSAD with dynamic sludge thickening can achieve comparable performance. Although the specific results are related to an Italian case study, this work provides a useful tool for decision-making among alternative sludge management solutions when local boundary conditions (sludge characteristics, transportation distances, HSAD/LSAD plant availability) are specified.

title: ACCOUNTING, ANALYTICAL, AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH AMIDST DEMOGRAPHIC DECLINE
source: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
summary: The study clarifies the essence of the theoretical and methodological regulation of the analytical, accounting, financial, and social aspects of supporting stable economic growth amidst a demographic decline. It specifies that a shrinking t
content: The study clarifies the essence of the theoretical and methodological regulation of the analytical, accounting, financial, and social aspects of supporting stable economic growth amidst a demographic decline. It specifies that a shrinking total population and rising unemployment necessitate a revision of the traditional economic growth model one that incorporates the need to sustain labor productivity and investment, mobilize financial resources, and comprehensively retrain personnel. A methodology is detailed for ranking factors that allow for the analysis of how demographic variables, workforce efficiency, and production output influence the integrated performance indicator of a business entity. The study defines the nature and significance of demographic growth, which fundamentally shapes the future trajectories of the national economy's sustainable socio-economic development. It establishes critical thresholds for a demographic crisis; exceeding these limits indicates the state's inability to offset demographic losses and signals a sustained decline in productivity across specific economic sectors. The proposed thresholds are conceptual and methodological in nature and require further empirical justification on the basis of statistical data. The methodology for the financial and accounting assessment of costs associated with maintaining demographic resources, specifically through the mobilization of additional capital required to sustain employment levels, is elaborated in detail. The concept of compensating for demographic costs is further developed, offering a means to mitigate negative demographic trends within society. Three scenarios are proposed, demonstrating the extent to which demographic costs can be offset by labor productivity without causing economic imbalances. It is noted that an increase in labor productivity should not automatically be viewed as a sign of improved economic efficiency.Therefore, it is appropriate to distinguish between overall growth in labor productivity and the surplus productivity gain that remains after the requirements for demographic compensation have been met. Ultimately, the proposed methodology establishes the necessary foundation for implementing effective financial-analytical management aimed at curbing demographic decline while creating the conditions for demographic compensation.

title: Unravelling the non-linear Impact of Energy Diversification on CO2 Emissions: Evidence from Emerging Economies
source: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Social Science
summary: Global warming is a global issue. Goal 13 of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the United Nations (UN) emphasizes the reduction of carbon emissions. Fossil fuel energy is a major source of carbon emissions. A transition to a clean
content: Global warming is a global issue. Goal 13 of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the United Nations (UN) emphasizes the reduction of carbon emissions. Fossil fuel energy is a major source of carbon emissions. A transition to a cleaner energy mix can be helpful, however, this dynamic is less explored. Therefore, this study assesses the nonlinear effect of energy diversification on carbon emissions in case of emerging economies including Brazil, India, Russia, Turkiye, China, Mexico and Indonesia. These countries are among the highest polluters. Results suggest that a significant U-shaped relation prevails between carbon emissions and energy diversification. An initial increase in energy diversification lowers the carbon 443emissions. This relation reverses at very high levels of energy diversification. After a certain threshold point, further increase in energy diversification increases the carbon emissions. Growth, trade openness and urbanization are among the other significant contributing factors. Dataset spanning from 1991-2023 is used for estimation. Results of the study suggest a careful selection of energy mix to optimally handle the issue of carbon emissions.

title: Scalable crosslinking-regulated membranes with ultra-high Li+/Mg2+ selectivity for lithium recovery from brines
summary: Abstract Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In
content: Abstract Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In this work, we demonstrate that regulation of the crosslinking degree during membrane formation enables subnanometer pore size control within the narrow window required for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Under electrodialysis conditions, the membrane achieved a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor of up to 6454 at an Mg/Li mass ratio of 140, outperforming previously reported membranes for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Importantly, the membrane maintained a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor above 1200 in untreated natural salt-lake brine, despite the high Mg/Li mass ratio (Mg/Li = 87) and the presence of multiple competing ions. Fabrication of a 25 cm × 35 cm membrane and stable performance over 15 days of repeated operation further supported the practical viability of this approach. The practical membrane design strategy reported in this work can inspire the development of ion-selective membranes with precisely regulated subnanometer pores for a wide range of sustainable separation processes.

title: When carbon counts differ: the complexities of biogenic carbon accounting in BECCUS and why accounting choices matter
summary: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (BECCUS) is an important pathway towards net-zero and net-negative emissions. Its mitigation potential depends on net atmospheric CO2 removal into durable storage after accounting for s
content: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (BECCUS) is an important pathway towards net-zero and net-negative emissions. Its mitigation potential depends on net atmospheric CO2 removal into durable storage after accounting for system-wide emissions and removals. However, lifecycle assessment, national greenhouse gas inventories and carbon-market frameworks apply differing accounting approaches, producing divergent mitigation estimates. This study identifies key sources of variability and examines their influence on reported outcomes through a systematic literature review and illustrative calculations for a hypothetical BECCUS system. Depending on the accounting approach, the net system outcome ranges from +422 kt CO2 (net-emitting) to −2,084 kt CO2 (net-reducing), while reported carbon removal ranges from 0 to −1,688 kt CO2. These deviations arise from four interconnected sources: (1) goals and framing, including definitions of concepts, terms and carbon flows; (2) methodological and analytical choices; (3) scope and system boundaries; and (4) baselines and counterfactuals. Governance, monitoring, reporting and verification, and crediting frameworks further shape these sources. Reported outcomes therefore vary primarily because of accounting choices rather than technical performance. The study calls for better alignment of existing methodologies and frameworks so that BECCUS accounting reflects atmospheric outcomes and supports credible climate mitigation.

title: Multi-scale haplotype signatures distinguish among evolutionary processes
summary: Natural selection embeds distinct genomic signatures as populations adapt to environmental pressures. Machine learning approaches, particularly deep neural networks, have emerged as powerful tools to detect adaptive signatures from genomic
content: Natural selection embeds distinct genomic signatures as populations adapt to environmental pressures. Machine learning approaches, particularly deep neural networks, have emerged as powerful tools to detect adaptive signatures from genomic data. While machine learning has dramatically improved our ability to extract these signals from sequence variation, distinguishing among multiple evolutionary processes remains challenging. We introduce SHADES, a deep learning framework that employs information about sequence differences and their frequencies at various spatial resolutions to capture evolutionary signatures at different genomic scales. We found that SHADES has the capacity to distinguish among neutrality, selective sweeps, balancing selection, and adaptive introgression and outperformed several contemporary methods evaluated for both classification accuracy and power. In addition, SHADES remained robust to a number of confounding factors, with only modest changes in classification performance. Furthermore, application of SHADES to empirical haplotypic variation from European humans recovered previously reported signals for selective sweeps, balancing selection, and adaptive introgression, while also identifying novel genes broadly involved in immune defense, inflammatory regulation, and epithelial barrier biology.

title: Spatial and vertical variability of soil physico‐hydraulic properties and subsurface lithology in the Upper Indus Plain of Pakistan
summary: Abstract Accurate characterization of soil physico‐hydraulic properties is critical for irrigation and drainage design, solute transport, soil–water–plant, and rainfall–runoff relationships. However, spatially representative datasets for th
content: Abstract Accurate characterization of soil physico‐hydraulic properties is critical for irrigation and drainage design, solute transport, soil–water–plant, and rainfall–runoff relationships. However, spatially representative datasets for these properties remain limited for the Indus Basin of Pakistan, where hydrological studies often rely on generalized parameters derived from other regions, introducing uncertainties in model‐based assessments. This study presents a basin‐scale integrated assessment of soil texture, bulk density, infiltration behavior, and soil moisture retention characteristics covering the Upper Indus Plain of Pakistan. Field‐based in situ measurements were conducted at 66 spatially distributed sites across four doabs (area between the two rivers) at surface, 0.5‐m, and 1.0‐m depths. An integrated methodological framework was employed, combining hydrometer analysis for soil texture, improved double‐ring infiltrometer tests for infiltration, pressure‐plate extractor for soil water retention, oven‐dried weight for bulk density, and resistivity survey for subsurface lithological assessment. Infiltration datasets were analyzed using the Horton and Philip cumulative infiltration models, while soil water retention behavior was quantified using hanging water column and pressure plate methods and parameterized using the van Genuchten model. Results indicate that the Horton infiltration model outperformed the Philip model for estimation of cumulative infiltration. Silty clay loam, sandy loam, and silt loam are the dominant texture classes. The soil with infiltration rates up to 30 mm/h remain predominant across the study area. This study provides robust and accurate baseline datasets along with an integrated methodological framework to support basin‐scale improved hydrological modeling, flood simulations, recharge estimation, and effective water resource management.

title: Erosion carbon dynamics extend beyond carbon accounting to ecological significance
summary: Abstract For decades, the debate over whether erosion acts as a carbon source or sink has advanced our understanding of carbon redistribution across stocks and fluxes. Yet, this quantitative perspective alone does not capture the full ecolo
content: Abstract For decades, the debate over whether erosion acts as a carbon source or sink has advanced our understanding of carbon redistribution across stocks and fluxes. Yet, this quantitative perspective alone does not capture the full ecological significance of carbon along these pathways. Carbon value lies not only in how much is stored, but also in how it functions within ecosystems. Erosion is not merely a switch governing land–atmosphere carbon exchange, but also a driver redistributing carbon among ecological states. Here, a framework is developed that interprets erosion as a reorganization of the soil functional layer, linking carbon redistribution to changes in stability and functionality across landscape contexts. This perspective helps explain the paradox in erosion management, whereby processes that reduce carbon burial may simultaneously enhance ecosystem functioning. It reframes carbon redistribution from changes in carbon stocks to shifts in ecological states, with implications for carbon accounting and ecosystem management.

title: Water‐Heat Synergistic Regulation to Optimize Water State and Enhance Thermal Effect in Solar Interfacial Evaporation
summary: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to the global freshwater shortage. However, current evaporation systems typically suffer from low water management efficiency and poor interfacial thermal effects. This w
content: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to the global freshwater shortage. However, current evaporation systems typically suffer from low water management efficiency and poor interfacial thermal effects. This work proposes a strategy to synergistically enhance the heat and mass transport of solar interfacial evaporators by balancing water transport capacity and water activity and reverse heat compensation. A higher proportion of loosely bound intermediate water (IW) with low enthalpy of vaporization is induced by in situ construction of a hydrophilic micron‐to‐submicron hierarchical pore structure within the wood‐based biomass framework, while maintaining its water pumping capacity. Simultaneously, a biomimetic thermal compensation mechanism significantly enhances the thermal effect of the wood‐based biomass evaporation interface (temperature up to 50.7°C). This synergistic design enables a record evaporation rate of 5.12 kg m −2 h −1 in wood‐based evaporators. Furthermore, the vertically distributed hierarchical pore structure and surface polar groups endow it with excellent salt repellency and antifouling capabilities. This reported water‐heat management strategy provides a scalable, low‐cost, and environmentally friendly approach to highly efficient solar interfacial evaporation.

title: How sustainable finance initiatives and forums address environmental issues, including climate change, and the challenges they face
summary: Abstract An increasing number of transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums are focusing on shifting and mobilizing private finance. Consequently, it has become more difficult to grasp the big picture concerning their roles an
content: Abstract An increasing number of transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums are focusing on shifting and mobilizing private finance. Consequently, it has become more difficult to grasp the big picture concerning their roles and effects, including how they overlap and synergize. This study examined how transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums contribute to scaling up private finance and investment and encourage private sector participation. It also explored the challenges that they face in achieving climate-related and other environmental goals. To assess the effectiveness and legitimacy of transnational governance, the institutional and actor-related dimensions and impacts of five major United Nations-related transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums were analyzed using an analytical framework that included the following elements: transparency, accountability, participation, environmental and other societal impacts, and academic and practical literature. This study showed that each of these initiatives and forums differed in its governing structure and approaches, as well as in its relationship with United Nations-related institutions and actors. Furthermore, overlapping institutions and actors were involved across initiatives and forums, with areas of collaboration between them. While each initiative successfully engaged diverse actors, common challenges emerged, including difficulty in evaluating and enhancing the effectiveness of transnational initiatives and forums, the need for effective links among transnational initiatives and other governance systems (e.g., effective institutional and actor interplay between these voluntary initiatives and compulsory interventions), and the need to include diverse actors. This study showed that more research is required to explore ways of evaluating and enhancing transnational governance of voluntary multistakeholder initiatives and to address the above challenges.

title: Transformational Research on the Existing Traditional Manufacturing OEM Enterprises' Transformation Path under Excess Capacity: Quantitative Empirical Research Based on the Textile Printing and Dyeing Industry
summary: China's state-owned enterprise (OEM) enterprises in textile printing and dyeing industry face persistent overcapacity and tightened environment protection regulation, and various small and middle OEMs are trapped in a dilemma of price taker
content: China's state-owned enterprise (OEM) enterprises in textile printing and dyeing industry face persistent overcapacity and tightened environment protection regulation, and various small and middle OEMs are trapped in a dilemma of price taker (e.g. low bargaining power, narrow margins and lack of transformation momentum). The study collects data (for the years of 2010–2023) from China Industry Statistical Yearbook, China Environmental Statistical Yearbook, Wind database, constructs a panel and uses descriptive statistic, group comparison, correlation analysis and fixed-effects regression to check the logic of dropping the price competition game and entering the value competition game. The results demonstrate: (1) capacity utilization is highly and positively correlated with the profit rate, and overcapacity is a main factor for the drop in profit; (2)R&D intensity has a positive and significant effect on the company profit rate, but with a "transformation threshold effect", such as R&D transforming into profit only if the capacity utilization is more than about 0.70; (3) too large concentration of the customers decreases bargaining force and inhibits transformation; (4)moderate environmental regulation encourages upgrading and is consistent with Porter hypothesis. From the results above, the paper proposes a three-dimensional path for equipment iteration and process upgrade, customer structure optimization and migration toward value competition, which provides evidence for OEM enterprises' escape from "dilemma lock-in" and to regulators' designing policies based on issues, respectively.

title: Biotechnologies and Bioeconomics: How to Increase Resource Efficiency, Reduce Emissions, and Strengthen Energy Security (Comparing the United States, China, and the EU)
summary: The objective of the research is the national models of bioeconomics development in the three largest economies of the world. The subject of the study is the quantitative relationship between the level of biotechnology development, resource
content: The objective of the research is the national models of bioeconomics development in the three largest economies of the world. The subject of the study is the quantitative relationship between the level of biotechnology development, resource efficiency, dynamics of greenhouse gas emissions reduction, and the degree of energy independence of regions. The aim of this study is an empirical assessment of progress in the development of bioeconomics over the period 2020-2030 and the identification of regional leaders for each of the key indicators. However, bioengineering has become not only a technical field but also one of the key drivers of sustainable technological progress, with which we move towards a bio- circular economy. Microorganisms and genetically modified bacteria have reshaped and revolutionized the modern energy sector. Some key features of bioengineering make it even more valuable for the traditional energy sector: it is available now, applicable in all energy sectors (electricity, direct heat, transport), readily integrated with existing infrastructure, storable, and can support the expansion of intermittent renewables. One of the most important features is that it is capable of delivering negative emissions when linked to Carbon Capture & Storage (CCS). The methodological basis of the study is economic modeling based on OECD data presented in the Bioeconomy to 2030 report through the construction of three-dimensional regression surfaces, radar diagrams, and change matrices. China demonstrated the highest growth rates of all indicators of the bioeconomy (resource efficiency +86.2%, investment +125.8%, and bioenergy +204.2% over the decade). The United States remains the leader in terms of absolute resource efficiency−3.83% of GDP and investments −36.47 billion dollars. The European Union is the undisputed leader in environmental efficiency, with emissions of 2.90 billion tons, a 25.7% reduction, and a 14.0% share of bioenergy in the energy mix. In this study, we aimed to examine bioengineering technologies, their contribution to the transformation of global energy systems and development of a sustainable economy, and the economic and political barriers, using a multidisciplinary approach that integrates biological sciences, bioengineering, and economics.

title: An explainable graph learning framework for carbon footprint prediction: Integrating SHAP-based policy insights and country similarity networks
summary: Accurate prediction of carbon footprint dynamics is essential for climate policy design and sustainable development planning, yet complex nonlinear interactions among energy systems, environmental factors, and socioeconomic activities make
content: Accurate prediction of carbon footprint dynamics is essential for climate policy design and sustainable development planning, yet complex nonlinear interactions among energy systems, environmental factors, and socioeconomic activities make estimation challenging. To address this gap, this study proposes an integrated framework combining machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and graph neural networks to predict carbon footprints across 27 European countries from 2015 to 2023. Evaluating several algorithms revealed that tree-based models substantially outperformed linear approaches, with LightGBM achieving the highest machine learning performance. SHAP analyses identified fossil fuel dependency, municipal waste generation, environmental impacts, protection capacity, and climate initiatives as the primary predictive determinants. Furthermore, incorporating a country similarity network into Graph Neural Network architectures improved predictive accuracy, with the Graph Attention Network (GAT) delivering the overall best predictive performance. Robustness checks confirmed model stability across various configurations, demonstrating that carbon footprint formation is driven by both national indicators and structural cross-country relationships. Ultimately, this framework bridges a methodological gap in environmental forecasting, offering robust predictive tools for policymakers and actionable, feature-level insights for targeted climate mitigation strategies.

title: ENERGY RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN THE STRATEGIC PLANNING OF REGIONS IN SLOVAKIA: WIND ENERGY DIMENSION
source: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
summary: The transition towards a low-carbon and energy-secure economy makes effective energy resource management an increasingly important component of strategic regional planning. In this context, the development of renewable energy sources, inclu
content: The transition towards a low-carbon and energy-secure economy makes effective energy resource management an increasingly important component of strategic regional planning. In this context, the development of renewable energy sources, including wind energy, can contribute not only to decarbonisation but also to the sustainable economic development, energy security, and competitiveness of regions. This issue is particularly relevant for Slovakia, where the potential of wind energy remains largely underutilised despite the country’s commitments to increase the share of renewable energy sources and achieve climate neutrality by 2050. The slow development of wind energy is associated with administrative and permitting procedures, regulatory and institutional constraints, spatial planning challenges, environmental and social considerations, and insufficient integration of renewable energy development into regional strategic planning. The aim of the study is to assess the role of wind energy resource management in the strategic planning and sustainable development of regions in Slovakia, identify the main barriers limiting its effective integration into regional energy systems, and formulate recommendations for improving regional and national approaches to wind energy development. The study analyses relevant strategic and policy documents concerning the Slovak electricity sector and renewable energy development, examines the current state of wind energy development, and considers the planned trajectories for increasing wind power capacity towards 2030 and the longer-term decarbonisation objectives. The results indicate that the limited development of wind energy in Slovakia cannot be explained solely by the availability of technical potential. Institutional fragmentation, lengthy permitting procedures, spatial and environmental constraints, limited regional coordination, and insufficient integration of energy considerations into regional development planning represent significant barriers. The study also demonstrates that more effective management of wind energy resources can support regional energy security, diversification of energy supplies, local economic development, and progress towards decarbonisation. The study concludes that accelerating wind energy development in Slovakia requires closer integration of energy resource management with regional strategic planning. Strengthening institutional coordination, simplifying permitting procedures, improving spatial planning mechanisms, and establishing clearer regional and national development frameworks could facilitate the sustainable utilisation of wind energy potential and contribute to the long-term development of Slovak regions.

title: Anti‐Dissolution Tungsten Alloying Stabilizes Highly Active Platinum for Industrial‐Grade Hydrogen Evolution
summary: ABSTRACT Platinum‐based alloys remain the most promising electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet suffer from activity‐stability trade‐offs, particularly in alkaline media where Pt‐Ni alloys undergo continuous dissolu
content: ABSTRACT Platinum‐based alloys remain the most promising electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet suffer from activity‐stability trade‐offs, particularly in alkaline media where Pt‐Ni alloys undergo continuous dissolution. Herein, we report the rational design of intermetallic Pt 2 W alloy nanoparticles uniformly anchored on N‐doped carbon nanomeshes (N‐CM), leveraging tungsten's exceptional thermodynamic stability and corrosion resistance to address this dilemma. Systematic compositional optimization reveals that Pt 2 W/N‐CM delivers superior alkaline HER performance, achieving an ultralow overpotential of 7 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and outperforming both Pt‐Ni analogues and commercial Pt/C. Critically, the catalyst exhibits unprecedented long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for 200 h at an industrial‐grade high current density of 800 mA cm −2 . Combined theoretical and experimental analyses elucidate that W fulfills a cooperative trifunction whereby oxophilic sites markedly lower the kinetic barrier for water dissociation while directional electron transfer downshifts the Pt d ‐band center to optimize hydrogen adsorption. Simultaneously, the intrinsic anti‐dissolution property of W fundamentally suppresses active site degradation under harsh HER conditions, establishing a structural self‐stabilization mechanism. This work demonstrates that leveraging corrosion‐resistant tungsten enables a structurally self‐stabilizing and highly active Pt 2 W electrocatalyst for industrial alkaline water electrolysis.

title: Do Investors Price Different Types of Climate Risk Disclosure? Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
source: International Journal of Economics and Finance
