summary: With the transition toward global carbon neutrality and a circular economy, remanufacturing technologies for high-value industrial components have gained significant attention. Additive cladding processes such as laser cladding, directed en
content: With the transition toward global carbon neutrality and a circular economy, remanufacturing technologies for high-value industrial components have gained significant attention. Additive cladding processes such as laser cladding, directed energy deposition (DED), wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), and plasma transferred arc (PTA) are key solutions for localized structural restoration. However, dynamic melt pool instability and complex thermal histories often induce defects like porosity and microcracks, degrading product reliability. Recently, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multi-sensor monitoring and closed-loop control systems have been introduced to enhance process stability and repeatability. This review comprehensively categorizes additive cladding processes for remanufacturing and explores recent advancements in AI-driven sensing, deep-learning-based defect prediction, adaptive feedback control, and digital twin integration. Finally, critical technical challenges and future perspectives for industrial deployment are discussed.

title: Remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries using a causal STL-based multiscale CNN-BiLSTM-attention network
summary: Abstract As a key energy storage component in high-reliability power systems, such as electric transportation and spacecraft, lithium-ion batteries necessitate precise remaining useful life (RUL) estimation to guarantee safe operation and f
content: Abstract As a key energy storage component in high-reliability power systems, such as electric transportation and spacecraft, lithium-ion batteries necessitate precise remaining useful life (RUL) estimation to guarantee safe operation and facilitate early fault detection. However, battery capacity degradation is jointly affected by complex electrochemical mechanisms, external environmental disturbances, and cell-to-cell variability. As a result, it is highly nonlinear, shows pronounced local fluctuations, and remains difficult to generalize across different batteries. This paper presents an STL- convolutional neural network (CNN)-bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM)-Attention framework for lithium-ion battery RUL estimation, leveraging recursive multi-step capacity trajectory prediction. First, at each prediction point, rolling STL decomposition is performed using only the historical capacity sequence. The resulting trend, seasonal, and residual components are then integrated with multidimensional features, including cycle number, capacity, state of health, internal resistance, and charging-process parameters, to prevent information leakage from future data. Second, a sliding-window approach is employed to construct time-series samples, enabling the network to simultaneously identify short-term variations and extended degradation trends. Furthermore, a difference-based label learning strategy is introduced to convert absolute capacity prediction into capacity-change prediction, thereby improving the representation of local degradation variations and short-term capacity prediction. By combining the local feature extraction ability of CNN, the temporal dependency modeling ability of BiLSTM, and the attention mechanism’s ability to weight key degradation information, the proposed model enables more accurate prediction of complex nonlinear capacity fading. The proposed framework differs from conventional one-step capacity prediction approaches by performing recursive multi-step capacity trajectory prediction from a predefined starting point, where the RUL is determined as the first cycle at which the predicted capacity reaches the failure threshold. The experimental findings demonstrate that the STL-CNN-BiLSTM-Attention model achieves better performance than CNN, BiLSTM, CNN-BiLSTM, and other decomposition-based models across root mean square error, mean absolute error, and R 2 metrics. The model effectively reduces prediction errors and improves the accuracy and robustness of RUL prediction for unseen batteries, demonstrating its practical potential in complex degradation scenarios.

title: From Metro to Multimodal Mobility Hub: Transforming Thessaloniki’s West Centre for Climate Neutrality
summary: Abstract Following the goal of achieving climate neutrality and accelerating the transition of European cities through innovation and digitization, Thessaloniki was awarded with the relevant EU Mission label. As part of its commitment to th
content: Abstract Following the goal of achieving climate neutrality and accelerating the transition of European cities through innovation and digitization, Thessaloniki was awarded with the relevant EU Mission label. As part of its commitment to the NetZeroCities Pilot Programme, the ReGenWesT project builds on one of the Climate City Contract’s emblematic interventions for the creation of climate neutral districts. This paper focuses on pilot actions designed to enhance sustainable urban mobility in the city’s West Centre. The recent metro launch presents a unique opportunity to improve the safety and accessibility of mobility nodes, reduce pollution, and promote sustainable travel, core objectives of the European Green Deal. The methodology outlines how to create secure walking and cycling routes for diverse user groups through GIS mapping, participatory co-design, and on-site pilots. These actions aim to demonstrate the validity of the proposed design and establish a community based, data-driven plan for climate-neutral urban renewal.

title: Mandates and Penalties: The Impact of Policy Implementation on Biofuel Markets – A Comparative Study on Road and Aviation Transport Fuel Prices in Different EU Countries
summary: Abstract To achieve the EU’s 2050 climate neutrality goal, biofuel use in domestic transport is necessary which has mostly been promoted by biofuel blending mandates. By 2022, all EU Member States had implemented such mandates for road tran
content: Abstract To achieve the EU’s 2050 climate neutrality goal, biofuel use in domestic transport is necessary which has mostly been promoted by biofuel blending mandates. By 2022, all EU Member States had implemented such mandates for road transport fuels, while only two had applied them to aviation fuel. The mandates vary in design, criteria and penalties for non-compliance, resulting in varying impacts on the blended fuel market. This study maps penalties for non-compliance with blending mandates in the road and aviation sectors and assesses their impact on fuel prices and mandate fulfilment. Based on penalty levels, it was estimated how much fuel suppliers are willing to pay for biofuels and the calculated maximum prices on blended fuel were compared to actual consumer prices. While no clear correlation between penalty levels and mandate fulfilment could be found, findings highlight the need for a balanced combination of penalty levels, blending mandates, and policy measures to increase the biofuel share in transport fuels without disrupting fuel markets.

title: Intermediate‐Phase Blocking as a Kinetic Lever for High Ionic Conductivity of Wet‐Synthesized Cl‐Rich Li Argyrodite for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Achieving high ionic conductivity of wet‐synthesized sulfide solid electrolytes remains a critical challenge for enabling scalable all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs). In Cl‐rich Li‐argyrodites, Li + transport is strongly governed by
content: ABSTRACT Achieving high ionic conductivity of wet‐synthesized sulfide solid electrolytes remains a critical challenge for enabling scalable all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs). In Cl‐rich Li‐argyrodites, Li + transport is strongly governed by the Cl occupancy at the 4d Wyckoff site, yet conventional wet syntheses fail to control this local structure due to the spontaneous formation of unfavorable intermediate phases. Here, we uncover that the formation of the PS 3 Cl 2− moiety during intermediate heat‐treatment stages suppresses 4d‐site Cl incorporation, thereby limiting ionic conductivity. By introducing controlled amounts of S 8 as a reaction‐kinetic modulator, we show that S–S‐containing precursor environments kinetically hinder PS 3 Cl 2− formation during heat treatment. Multimodal structural analyses (solid‐state NMR, XRD Rietveld refinement, DSC) confirm that increasing S 8 systematically increases 4d‐site Cl occupancy while suppressing the undesired intermediate. This kinetic steering enables the Li 5.5 PS 4.5 Cl 1.5 (LPSCl 1.5 ) electrolyte to reach a high ionic conductivity of 6.06 ± 0.29 mS cm −1 at 25°C without additional specialized processing such as rapid thermal annealing or spark plasma sintering. ASSB half‐cells incorporating this electrolyte exhibit excellent rate capability and 77.8% capacity retention over 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes a mechanistic framework for intermediate‐phase engineering in wet synthesis and presents a high‐performance wet‐synthesis route with potential for scale‐up.

title: Scaling up retrofit: regional challenges and opportunities for MMC
summary: Increasing energy retrofit rates is considered essential for reducing housing-related greenhouse gas emissions, particularly in Central and Northern Europe. In Germany, despite ambitious and costly policies, annual retrofit rates have remai
content: Increasing energy retrofit rates is considered essential for reducing housing-related greenhouse gas emissions, particularly in Central and Northern Europe. In Germany, despite ambitious and costly policies, annual retrofit rates have remained largely stagnant at around 1% of the housing stock. The current trend of modern methods of construction (MMC) and digitisation have renewed hope that serial retrofit and service platforms could enable the scaling up of energy retrofits by reducing costs, disruptions and management burdens, especially for non-professional property owners. While a growing literature explores this potential, empirical research on the region-specific conditions to scale up serial retrofit remains limited. To address this gap, this study interviewed intermediaries and professionals who organise retrofits in the Freiburg region in south-west Germany. Their views were sought on the challenges and opportunities for serial (prefabricated) retrofit facilitated by digitised planning, platform thinking, and collaboration among trades and other partners. Applying the challenge-oriented regional innovation systems (CORIS) framework revealed an early-stage reorientation pathway in the region, providing entry points for scaling up MMC. PRACTICE RELEVANCE There is leeway for practitioners to deepen existing and create new networks across sectors and trades, and to experiment with collaborative methods, working towards serial approaches. The early adoption of innovative methods and the use of regional and renewable resources is recommended to strengthen both ecological sustainability and the regional economy. As for governance, the provision of digital tools and legal bases for data collection is essential to promote a transformation pathway for MMC and platforms. Institutional innovations such as publicly funded one-stop shops and database can contribute to a comprehensive housing transition.

title: Thermal Decomposition Pathways for Hydrogen Production: Selection and Efficiency Enhancement
summary: The dual-carbon target has driven the low-carbon transformation of hydrogen energy. Thermal decomposition for hydrogen production, which can be coupled with high-temperature heat sources such as solar energy, nuclear energy, and industrial
content: The dual-carbon target has driven the low-carbon transformation of hydrogen energy. Thermal decomposition for hydrogen production, which can be coupled with high-temperature heat sources such as solar energy, nuclear energy, and industrial waste heat, has emerged as an important direction for green hydrogen production. This paper systematically reviews four core pathways: direct hydrothermal decomposition of water, pyrolysis of hydrocarbons, ammonia thermal decomposition, and thermochemical cycle water splitting. It compares their reaction mechanisms, process conditions, technical advantages and disadvantages, as well as applicable scenarios. Direct hydrothermal decomposition uses clean raw materials but requires ultra-high temperatures and remains at the fundamental research stage. Hydrocarbon pyrolysis technology is mature and serves as a transitional solution for the shift from fossil energy to hydrogen energy. Ammonia thermal decomposition features mild reaction conditions and is well-suited for distributed hydrogen supply scenarios. Thermochemical cycle water splitting reduces the required reaction temperature and represents the core technology for future large-scale zero-carbon hydrogen production. The study indicates that pathway selection must comprehensively consider factors including raw materials, heat sources, carbon emissions, application scenarios, and economic viability. In the future, thermal decomposition for hydrogen production will develop toward low-temperature and high-efficiency processes, coupling with clean energy sources, and system integration. These advancements will provide strong support for the industrialization of hydrogen energy and the low-carbon transformation of the energy sector.

title: 2030 and 2050 Foresight Scenarios for Zero Emissions Waterborne Transport Deployment
summary: Abstract Europe is facing an existential transformation as it strives to meet climate neutrality by 2050, with shipping as a cornerstone in achieving climate objectives while ensuring Europe’s security and competitiveness. Clear and compreh
content: Abstract Europe is facing an existential transformation as it strives to meet climate neutrality by 2050, with shipping as a cornerstone in achieving climate objectives while ensuring Europe’s security and competitiveness. Clear and comprehensive foresight scenarios in which ZEWT (Zero Emission Waterborne Transport) will be deployed are essential to provide ZEWT decision makers and indirect stakeholders at policy, investment, industry, technology and operational level with the necessary comprehensive and reasoned set of knowledge and recommendations. The clarity of positive and negative externalities of a future system, the limited uncertainties on factors shaping and quantifying the demand and type of future services, and the capability to progress under an ecosystemic approach towards novel business models and technologies are crucial to overcome resistance to change and leverage efficient investments, under regulatory pressures. The paper will provide an overview of the most possibly realistic picture of boundaries, uncertainties, and dependencies resulting from socio-cultural, political, technological, and economic trends that will determine the context in which surveyed technologies and concepts will be allegedly incorporated in the 2030 and 2050 target time horizons.

title: Super Living Labs for Integrated Peri-Urban Areas in the Transition Towards Climate Neutrality
summary: Abstract Peri-urban areas face a series of complex challenges that hinder their transition towards climate neutrality. One of the primary obstacles is the strong dependence on city-led strategies, which are often shaped by current administr
content: Abstract Peri-urban areas face a series of complex challenges that hinder their transition towards climate neutrality. One of the primary obstacles is the strong dependence on city-led strategies, which are often shaped by current administrative structures, budgetary constraints, and fluctuating political agendas. Through a multi-level governance, the Transition Super Living Lab (TSLL) approach is implemented in five peri-urban areas in Antwerp-Rotterdam, Milan metropolitan region, Alicante- Elche Functional Area, Epirus-Ioannina region and Lisbon metropolitan region, providing a new cross-sectoral model to support them on achieving the change towards climate neutrality through innovation and digitalization. The TSLLs implement targeted interventions addressing four key innovation axes: sustainable mobility, decarbonized energy systems, zero-pollution industry, and cross-sectoral governance. To support this systemic transformation, a set of cutting-edge and data-driven innovations such as AI-driven and CO2 led traffic corridors management system, real time demand management system, Energy Community EV sharing platform, Demand-Response energy management system for industry and peri-urban PT decision support tool are implemented. These data-driven solutions will optimize transportation networks, decarbonize energy grids, enhance governance structures, and improve industrial sustainability of peri-urban areas positioning them as key drivers of systemic change in Europe’s climate-neutral future.

title: Operational Monitoring of Brine-Based Lithium Production Facilities Using Sentinel-2 Time-Series Imagery and Assessment of Potential Supply-Chain Applications: A Case Study of the Olaroz and Cauchari Salars, Argentina
summary: Lithium demand is increasing with the expansion of electric vehicles and energy storage systems, making the operational status of production facilities and supply-chain stability increasingly important.Detailed operational information on pr
content: Lithium demand is increasing with the expansion of electric vehicles and energy storage systems, making the operational status of production facilities and supply-chain stability increasingly important.Detailed operational information on production facilities is generally not disclosed, whereas large evaporation ponds used in brine-based lithium production remain exposed at the surface, enabling continuous observation using satellite imagery.This study analyzed changes in the operational states of final lithium evaporation ponds in the Olaroz and Cauchari areas of Argentina using Sentinel-2 time-series imagery.Time-series Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) was applied to identify brine filling, concentration, depletion, and re-filling, revealing pond-specific operational characteristics and repetitive cycles.Distinct depletion states were observed at Olaroz in March 2023 and February 2024, and brine refilling after depletion was identified in RGB imagery.A comparison of operational-state changes with publicly available production and shipment records indicated cases in which depletion was observed before reported production records.These findings suggest that satellite imagery can provide baseline information for interpreting operational status, production readiness, and lithium supply-chain monitoring.

title: The Role of EU Funding Instruments and IPCEIs in Enabling Maritime Decarbonisation
summary: Abstract For the EU, decarbonising the maritime industry represents a fundamental test of its capacity to enhance industrial competitiveness in a contested global market. This paper examines the relationship between EU funding mechanisms, i
content: Abstract For the EU, decarbonising the maritime industry represents a fundamental test of its capacity to enhance industrial competitiveness in a contested global market. This paper examines the relationship between EU funding mechanisms, industrial policy, and the drive for breakthrough innovation, focusing specifically on the adoption of hydrogen technologies. The analysis charts the EU’s current funding architecture, assessing how instruments like Horizon Europe, the Innovation Fund, and the Connecting Europe Facility support different stages of the innovation lifecycle. This paper argues that the Important Projects of Common European Interest function as unique, ecosystem-building tools, capable of tackling the systemic market failures in “hard-to-abate” sectors. The strategic construction of the hydrogen value chain through four IPCEI “waves” is examined, with Fincantieri’s “Wave 2 the Future” project as an example of this integrated policy’s real-world impact on maritime innovation. The paper situates the debate within the EU’s strategic evolution from a “Green Deal” to a “Clean Deal” where competitiveness is the central pillar. The vision for a consolidated post-2027 framework, exemplified by the proposed European Competitiveness Fund, aims to rectify current systemic fragmentation. A strategic, streamlined, and market-focused funding ecosystem positions Europe’s maritime industry as a leader in the global green transition.

title: Green digital transformation and clean energy management in fashion companies: Circular economy and green innovation as pathways to sustainable performance
source: European Journal of Sustainable Development Research
summary: The purpose of the present study is to analyze the capacity of green digital transformation and clean energy management to achieve sustainable performance in textile and fashion firms, considering circular economy and green innovation. Draw
content: The purpose of the present study is to analyze the capacity of green digital transformation and clean energy management to achieve sustainable performance in textile and fashion firms, considering circular economy and green innovation. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the resource-based view, the study argues that green capabilities do not automatically improve sustainable performance; rather, they require internal organizational mechanisms that make them tangible. Based on a survey administered to 283 business managers in Colombia, the proposed theoretical relationships were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results showed that green digital transformation capability and clean energy readiness were positively associated with circular economy practices and green innovation capability, which were, in turn, positively associated with sustainable performance. The study identifies two internal organizational pathways consistent with corporate sustainability in a resource-intensive industry.

title: Green Energy Policies in Promoting Sustainable Development: A Literature Review
summary: Green energy policies have become essential instruments for addressing climate change, environmental degradation, energy insecurity, and sustainable development challenges. This study aims to examine the role of green energy policies in pro
content: Green energy policies have become essential instruments for addressing climate change, environmental degradation, energy insecurity, and sustainable development challenges. This study aims to examine the role of green energy policies in promoting sustainable development by analyzing policy frameworks, implementation strategies, environmental and socioeconomic contributions, institutional challenges, and policy innovations. The study employed a literature review approach with a qualitative descriptive and analytical orientation. Relevant academic publications were identified through Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar, prioritizing peer-reviewed articles published between 2021 and 2026. Literature selection was guided by predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, while data were examined using qualitative thematic analysis and narrative synthesis. The findings indicate that renewable energy regulations, financial incentives, carbon pricing mechanisms, and investment policies contribute to emission reductions, economic development, employment opportunities, and improved energy accessibility. However, their effectiveness varies according to institutional capacity, regulatory consistency, financial accessibility, technological readiness, and stakeholder participation. Major implementation challenges include fragmented governance, inadequate financing, infrastructure limitations, technological disparities, and unequal distribution of transition benefits. Policy innovations involving green financing, smart energy technologies, collaborative governance, and international cooperation offer opportunities to strengthen renewable energy transitions. The review highlights the importance of integrating environmental objectives with economic resilience, social equity, and institutional accountability. It concludes that coherent policy frameworks, technological modernization, inclusive governance, and coordinated investment strategies are critical for accelerating sustainable energy transitions and advancing long-term sustainable development across diverse national and institutional contexts.

title: Addressing global environmental degradation: examining the role of financialization and trade globalization on reducing carbon emissions
summary: The pressing challenge of achieving environmental sustainability hinges on financialization and trade globalization. These dynamics are central to strategies aimed at mitigating ecological degradation. Effective financial and policy decisio
content: The pressing challenge of achieving environmental sustainability hinges on financialization and trade globalization. These dynamics are central to strategies aimed at mitigating ecological degradation. Effective financial and policy decisions are crucial in managing the interplay between finance, trade, and environmental outcomes. This study investigates the relationship between financialization and ecological degradation by employing three dimensions of financialization financial development, financial markets, and financial institutions within the framework of the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC). Using a two-step system generalized method of moments (GMM) on a balanced panel of 129 developed and developing countries covering the period 2000 to 2022, the analysis provides robust evidence on the heterogeneous roles of financialization. The findings reveal that trade and financial development are associated with higher emissions in both developed and emerging economies, while financial markets significantly reduce emissions. Financial institutions also demonstrate a negative association with emissions, underscoring their role in supporting sustainable investment. The squared term of trade openness indicates significant emission reductions, consistent with the EKC’s inverted U-shaped hypothesis. However, the interaction effects of financialization and trade on emissions are essentially insignificant, suggesting weak synergies between these forces. Overall, the study highlights that financial development and trade can initially exacerbate ecological pressures. Still, financial markets and institutions, when supported by regulatory and governance frameworks, play a critical role in advancing sustainability. These results offer theoretical contributions to the finance–environment nexus and provide policy insights for aligning financial systems and trade with the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Global potential of decentralized waste biomass to solid carbon for scalable carbon removal
summary: Livestock manure and crop residues are abundant agricultural by-products whose mismanagement releases ~1.56 Gt CO2-eq yr-1, about 22% of agricultural greenhouse gas emissions. Here, we propose a circular bioeconomy system to recover their e
content: Livestock manure and crop residues are abundant agricultural by-products whose mismanagement releases ~1.56 Gt CO2-eq yr-1, about 22% of agricultural greenhouse gas emissions. Here, we propose a circular bioeconomy system to recover their energy, nutrients, and carbon. The proposed solar-powered, farm-scale system integrates anaerobic digestion, biomethanation, and methane pyrolysis to convert these residues into stable solid carbon, recycling hydrogen internally and returning nutrients to the soil as digestate. We apply a coupled mass, energy, and cost model globally using spatially explicit biomass and solar datasets. We estimate a sequestration potential of ~596 Mt C yr-1 (~2.2 Gt CO2-eq yr-1, ~6% of global fossil CO2 emissions), with a median levelized cost of 926 USD t-1 C for crop residue (5th–95th percentile: 904–980 USD t-1 C), and 1,534 USD t-1 C for manure (5th–95th percentile: 1,510–1,589 USD t-1 C), assuming no revenue from the carbon product. Capital expenditure dominates (~89% of cost, led by anaerobic digestion) while solar electricity contributes only ~11%. Under tailored process conditions, the product can be recovered as carbon black, graphite, carbon nanofibers, graphene, or nanotubes; both its market prices and carbon-credit prices could exceed the sequestration cost, making distributed carbon removal a potential source of farm income.

title: eRoadMontBlanc: A Large-Scale Demonstrator of Ground-Level Power Supply for Electric Heavy Trucks
summary: Abstract To reduce greenhouse gas emissions from heavy trucks, the development of a network of electric roads is an economically viable solution that reduces the strain on natural resources for batteries. Major investment in the development
content: Abstract To reduce greenhouse gas emissions from heavy trucks, the development of a network of electric roads is an economically viable solution that reduces the strain on natural resources for batteries. Major investment in the development of this network can only be made once the relevance of electrification technologies has been proven on demonstrators. The ground-level power supply technology using conductive segments on the surface of the pavement can deliver high power with excellent efficiency and is compatible with different types of vehicles, from cars to heavy trucks. A 420 m long demonstrator of this technology was built in late 2024 on the Transpolis site in France. This French test centre is a closed site dedicated to innovation and the development of safe, sustainable vehicles and infrastructure. The aim of this demonstrator is to transfer power of up to 500 kW to light commercial vehicles, coaches and heavy trucks. It was built by Eiffage in collaboration with Alstom and under the management of Université Gustave Eiffel as part of the eRoadMontBlanc research project funded by the French government and the European Union. Several innovative processes were implemented for the construction of the demonstrator and for the monitoring of its operation.

title: MUSSI Working Paper Series No – 33 Forestry: Policy Review Analysis of how climate policy shapes Ireland’s forest landscape
source: Maynooth University ePrints and eTheses Archive (Maynooth University)
summary: This policy review examines forestry in the context of climate-goals-related land interventions that reorganise the use and, as the report aims to show, the value and ownership of rural land in Ireland. The key policies start with the EU’s
content: This policy review examines forestry in the context of climate-goals-related land interventions that reorganise the use and, as the report aims to show, the value and ownership of rural land in Ireland. The key policies start with the EU’s Land Use, Land-Use Change and Forestry (LULUCF) framework, which, by accounting for forests as carbon removals towards member states’ binding climate targets, creates national demand for forest carbon sinks and reorganises rural land around its measurable climate value. That quantified climate value is subsequently translated into monetary investment value, which, in Ireland, takes the form of state subsidies through the Climate Action Plan and Forestry Programme, turning this accounting demand into afforestation targets stimulated by grants and premiums.

title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
summary: Abstract Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures s
content: Abstract Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures supported by robust metal-carbon bonds remains underdeveloped, largely because kinetic persistence limits the reversible structural correction required for conventional self-assembly. Herein, we employ binuclear palladacycles as intrinsically neutral and geometrically preorganized building blocks and develop a hierarchical assembly strategy that temporally separates geometric programming, scaffold editing, and topology locking. Through a polymerization-cleavage-assembly process, cyclopalladated polymers are converted into discrete binuclear precursors while retaining their programmed geometrical information. Subsequent trans-effect-directed N -heterocyclic carbene ligation affords a series of size-tunable, kinetically robust, and neutral organometallic rectangles. The resulting architectures are fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and single crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Moreover, single crystal X-ray diffraction identifies guest-mediated breathing-like geometric deformations in the solid state, driven by exo-wall π-π stacking and charge-transfer interactions with both electron-rich and electron-deficient planar guests. This work establishes a hierarchical construction principle for accessing discrete neutral organometallic architectures by separating geometric programming from the final locking of the topology through strong bond formation, while demonstrating that local geometric adaptation can occur without disrupting the framework connectivity established by Pd-C bonds.

title: Electric‐Field‐Coupled Heterointerface Engineering via Li/F Co‐Doping for Enhanced Rate Capability and Interfacial Stability of Fe/Mn‐Based Layered Sodium Cathodes
summary: ABSTRACT P2‐type Fe/Mn‐based layered oxide materials have long been plagued by structural degradation, air sensitivity, and interfacial instability, which severely restrict their application in sodium‐ion batteries. Herein, we propose an in
content: ABSTRACT P2‐type Fe/Mn‐based layered oxide materials have long been plagued by structural degradation, air sensitivity, and interfacial instability, which severely restrict their application in sodium‐ion batteries. Herein, we propose an in situ modification strategy integrating bulk Li/F co‐doping with a surface heterojunction coating and successfully synthesize Na 0.67 Fe 0.35 Mn 0.5 Li 0.15 O 1.93 F 0.07 (LMO@NFMLOF). IDPC‐STEM reveals the heterogeneous structure comprising distinct inner and outer regions. DFT calculations confirm the presence of a built‐in electric field at the heterointerface. The experimental results demonstrate that bulk Li/F co‐doping enhances crystal stability, while the built‐in electric field generated by the surface heterojunction accelerates Na + kinetic processes, and the coating further improves air and interfacial stability. Consequently, the LMO@NFMLOF cathode delivers a discharge capacity of 110 mAh g − 1 after 200 cycles at 2C. Remarkably, it maintains a discharge capacity of 85.6 mAh g − 1 after 300 cycles at 5C, demonstrating outstanding rate capability and cycling stability. This synergistic bulk‐surface optimization provides a new approach for designing high‐rate layered oxide cathodes.

title: Sulfuric acid activated water hyacinth root biosorbent for hexavalent chromium removal from synthetic aqueous solutions
summary: Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] discharged from tannery effluents poses severe environmental and human health risks. This study evaluates sulfuric-acid-treated water hyacinth root powder (TWHRP) as a low-cost biosorbent for Cr(VI) removal and
content: Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] discharged from tannery effluents poses severe environmental and human health risks. This study evaluates sulfuric-acid-treated water hyacinth root powder (TWHRP) as a low-cost biosorbent for Cr(VI) removal and recovery, using synthetic Cr(VI) solutions representative of the polishing/tertiary-treatment stage of tannery effluent. The biosorbent was characterised by proximate analysis, BET, point of zero charge, FTIR, and SEM before and after modification and adsorption. Batch experiments varying pH, contact time, adsorbent dosage, and initial Cr(VI) concentration yielded removal efficiencies of 16.98–97.11%. Response surface methodology with a face-centred central composite design identified the optimum as pH 2.01, dosage 0.59 g/100 mL, contact time 62.77 min, and 10.12 mg/L Cr(VI), giving 98.08% predicted removal (experimentally validated at 97.39 ± 0.14%). Equilibrium data fitted both Langmuir and Freundlich isotherms, and the pseudo-second-order model best described the rate data; the underlying mechanism is presented as proposed rather than experimentally demonstrated. Desorption with 0.5 M NaOH (30 mL) recovered 91.27% of the Cr(VI); subsequent reaction with BaCl 2 ·2H 2 O yielded a yellow precipitate consistent with, but not confirmed as, BaCrO 4 , pending XRD and SEM–EDS characterisation.

title: Marine ranching policy and inclusive green growth in coastal cities: evidence from China’s national marine ranching demonstration zone program
summary: Introduction Marine development programs often pursue resource conservation and production objectives simultaneously, yet their broader implications for sustainable coastal development remain insufficiently understood. This study examines w
content: Introduction Marine development programs often pursue resource conservation and production objectives simultaneously, yet their broader implications for sustainable coastal development remain insufficiently understood. This study examines whether China’s National Marine Ranching Demonstration Zone (NMRDZ) program improves inclusive green growth (IGG) in coastal cities. Methods IGG is measured using an entropy-weighted composite index covering economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability. Treating staggered NMRDZ designation as a quasi-natural experiment, this study applies a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) model to panel data for 37 Chinese coastal cities from 2011 to 2024. The analysis examines the program’s overall effect, transmission mechanisms, heterogeneity, and moderating conditions. Results The results show that: (1) the program increases IGG by approximately 0.174 standard deviations, and the finding remains robust; (2) it increases mariculture output per unit area, generating a positive transmission effect, but reduces marine capture production, creating an offsetting effect; (3) it significantly promotes IGG both within and outside the Northern Marine Economic Circle and across initial and subsequent designation batches, while its gains are statistically evident in larger-population cities but not in smaller-population cities; and (4) the estimated program effect is larger in cities with higher levels of green technological innovation or a more advanced industrial structure. Discussion These findings reveal a dual production dynamic in marine ranching development: higher mariculture output per unit area reinforces IGG, whereas contraction in marine capture production partially offsets the overall improvement. By evaluating marine ranching through an integrated economic, social, and environmental framework, this study moves beyond separate ecological or economic outcomes and provides evidence for refining the NMRDZ program, guiding fisheries production restructuring, and advancing inclusive and sustainable development in coastal cities.

title: Optimization of Arch Rib Inclination on Arch Bridges (Case Study: Kali Kuto Bridge)
summary: Optimizing the geometric parameters of arch bridges is essential for achieving material efficiency and indirectly minimizing negative environmental impacts. This study quantitatively evaluates the effect of arch rib inclination on structura
content: Optimizing the geometric parameters of arch bridges is essential for achieving material efficiency and indirectly minimizing negative environmental impacts. This study quantitatively evaluates the effect of arch rib inclination on structural performance to determine the optimal design configuration in accordance with SNI 1729:2020. A parametric Finite Element Method was utilized to analyze seven bridge models with arch rib inclinations of 0°, 5°, 10°, 15°, 20°, 25°, and 30°. The evaluation focused on internal forces, steel capacity ratio, deflection, structural weight, and structural performance. The analysis results indicate that an arch rib inclination of 20° is the optimal configuration, achieving the highest structural performance index of 0.987. At this optimum angle, the structural weight is reduced by 5.9%, and the deflection reaches a minimum of 63.3 mm, indicating superior vertical and lateral stiffness. Mechanically, this geometric modification activates a spatial frame mechanism that efficiently redistributes flexural demands into axial forces. Consequently, the combined internal forces on the cross beam arches remain highly efficient, utilizing a maximum of only 11.8% of their nominal capacity. It also minimizes the tensile force on the hangers, thereby lowering localized working stress and providing a larger safety reserve. Ultimately, this study validates that proper geometric optimization can significantly improve material efficiency, which indirectly aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by minimizing the overall environmental footprint.

title: Explainable and Uncertainty‐Aware Neural Modeling of Industrial CO 2 Emissions With Economic, Energy, and Institutional Interaction Dynamics
summary: ABSTRACT This study develops an explainable and uncertainty‐aware neural framework for forecasting industrial carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions in a heterogeneous global panel. The analytical panel integrates EDGAR, WDI, and V‐Dem data for 5
content: ABSTRACT This study develops an explainable and uncertainty‐aware neural framework for forecasting industrial carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions in a heterogeneous global panel. The analytical panel integrates EDGAR, WDI, and V‐Dem data for 5138 country–year observations from 165 countries during 1990–2024. The proposed dual‐input neural network combines standardized economic, energy, and institutional interaction and lagged features with a learned country embedding to represent persistent cross‐national heterogeneity. The framework is formulated as conditional (covariate‐assisted) forecasting. The target enters only through its 1‐year lag, whereas economic, energy, and institutional covariates are taken for the forecast year. The target is log‐transformed industrial CO 2 emissions, and evaluation uses an expanding‐window rolling‐origin design in addition to time‐blocked fivefold cross‐validation, a strictly temporal hold‐out, benchmark comparison, ablation analysis, and uncertainty calibration. The full model achieved a mean cross‐validation R 2 of 0.9649 (SD = 0.0034), root mean squared error (RMSE) of 0.4069 (SD = 0.0176), and MAE of 0.3272 (SD = 0.0275). In rolling‐origin evaluation for 2010–2024, it retained a mean R 2 of 0.9446 and a mean RMSE of 0.4798. It also outperformed other benchmarks, including XGBoost, random forest, long short‐term memory, linear regression, ridge, persistence, and autoregressive distributed lag, on the reported temporal test set. The ablation results indicate that governance features and country embeddings enhance the model's predictive ability, while the institutional interaction terms alone do not necessarily reduce RMSE. Overall, the model achieves a 53.80% reduction in RMSE compared with the baseline specification. Lagged industrial emissions are always the most important predictive factor for all four methods of SHAP, LIME, PFI, and IG, and the other factors, in order of importance, are income, renewable energy, and governance‐conditioned interactions. Initial interval diagnostics indicated that 0.801 empirical coverage was achieved for nominal 0.90 intervals. The chronological split‐conformal recalibration resulted in 0.873 empirical coverage, which remains below the nominal level, and the intervals should be used as preliminary before high‐stakes use, such as policy deployment. The model was trained and tested only on the countries of interest. The framework offers a clear and transparent predictive tool for analyzing industrial‐emissions pathways and makes a clear distinction between predictive association and causal effect.

title: Interactive Comparators – Life-Cycle Assessment of Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Passenger Cars and Heavy-Duty Vehicles
summary: Abstract This paper summarises detailed studies across various powertrain technology and energy options to create two interactive life-cycle assessment comparator tools for passenger cars and heavy-duty vehicles. This enables a comparison o
content: Abstract This paper summarises detailed studies across various powertrain technology and energy options to create two interactive life-cycle assessment comparator tools for passenger cars and heavy-duty vehicles. This enables a comparison of the CO 2 emission intensity of various transport technology pathways to determine the best decarbonisation options for a range of vehicle categories and use cases. Understanding the merits of each solution from a life-cycle perspective for a given use case is difficult, hence these comparators aim to improve this understanding and assist in decision-making. The tools combine a wide range of parameters to compare specific options of transportation pathways: Powertrains and their efficiencies: ICEV; HEV; PHEV; FCEV; BEV and CEV. Energy carriers: Diesel or diesel-like renewable fuels, Gasoline or gasoline-like renewable fuels, gaseous fuels, hydrogen, and electricity (with variations in carbon intensity). Vehicle categories: D-segment passenger car, long-haul truck (Class 5), delivery truck (Class 2), city bus, coach, and refuse truck. Sensitivities around battery, fuel cell capacity and hydrogen tank production emissions. Number of battery packs used. Use cases (payload, trip profile, charging frequency). All of this provides the user with a comprehensive yet simple tool, based on sound scientific studies, to make direct comparisons on a free-to-use platform via the Concawe website.

title: Comparing the role of ‘security’ in EU energy and agri‐food law
source: Review of European Comparative & International Environmental Law
summary: Abstract In EU energy and agri‐food law, ‘security’ is constantly invoked to justify legal action and to guide the adoption and interpretation of law. This article compares the concepts of energy security and food security, focusing on thei
content: Abstract In EU energy and agri‐food law, ‘security’ is constantly invoked to justify legal action and to guide the adoption and interpretation of law. This article compares the concepts of energy security and food security, focusing on their relationship to sustainability, and asks whether invoking security enables or obstructs each sector's environmental transformation. It argues that EU energy law has integrated sustainability into the concept of energy security itself, whereas agri‐food law treats sustainability as separate from—and, in times of crisis, in tension with—food security. Two case studies illustrate the implications: in the wake of Russia's war against Ukraine since February 2022, invoking security accelerated the clean energy transition but triggered a backlash against agri‐environmental measures; the 2026 US–Israeli war against Iran largely reproduced this divergence, although the EU's response to the resulting fertiliser crisis shows early signs of convergence between food security and sustainability. Four structural elements explain these profoundly divergent effects of a seemingly similar concept: the sectors' factual situations and historical evolutions, their regulatory rationales, the temporal dimension of security and agricultural exceptionalism. The article concludes that long‐term food security requires integrating sustainability into the legal concept of food security itself.

title: Selective responsibility: Environmental, social and governance frameworks and the containment of environmental and social harm in urban real estate
summary: As environmental, social and governance (ESG) frameworks become increasingly institutionalised within real-estate investment, questions of corporate responsibility for urban social and environmental challenges become more evident. Drawing o
content: As environmental, social and governance (ESG) frameworks become increasingly institutionalised within real-estate investment, questions of corporate responsibility for urban social and environmental challenges become more evident. Drawing on the case of Zurich and applying Young’s Social Connection Model of responsibility, this paper examines how ESG shapes the ways in which real-estate investors identify, articulate and act upon their responsibilities towards urban environments and communities. I argue that rather than constituting a meaningful framework for addressing structural housing inequality and environmental harm, ESG operates primarily as a risk-management tool that translatesc heterogeneous societal concerns into discrete, auditable categories. Environmental metrics dominate due to their compatibility with existing valuation practices, while social dimensions stagnate and governance is reduced to documentation. The result is a form of selective, depoliticised responsibility that acknowledges corporate implication in urban processes while simultaneously containing and neutralising its scope. Nevertheless, ESG’s ambiguity creates organisational openings through which individual actors can advance more ambitious environmental and social agendas. The paper concludes that ESG enables incremental progress while leaving the structural drivers of housing inequality and environmental harm fundamentally unchallenged.

title: OECD ÜLKELERİNDE MALİYE POLİTİKASI ARAÇLARININ KARBON AYAK İZİ ÜZERİNDEKİ ETKİSİ: PANEL VERİ ANALİZİ
source: Cumhuriyet Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Dergisi
summary: İklim değişikliği ve çevre kirliliği, günümüzde küresel gündemin en öncelikli sorunları arasında yer almaktadır. Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi kapsamında imzalanan Paris Anlaşması ve 2030 Sürdürülebilir Kalkınma H
content: İklim değişikliği ve çevre kirliliği, günümüzde küresel gündemin en öncelikli sorunları arasında yer almaktadır. Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi kapsamında imzalanan Paris Anlaşması ve 2030 Sürdürülebilir Kalkınma Hedefleri, çevre politikasını üye ülkeler açısından bağlayıcı bir zorunluluk haline getirmiştir. Bu uluslararası yükümlülükler çerçevesinde, karbon emisyonlarını azaltmaya yönelik etkili politika araçlarının belirlenmesi hem akademik hem de politika yapımı açısından kritik önem taşımaktadır. Bu çalışma, 1995-2022 döneminde 19 OECD ülkesinde enerji vergisi, çevre koruma harcamaları ve ekonomik büyümenin karbon ayak izi üzerindeki uzun dönemli etkisini ampirik olarak incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır. Bunun yanı sıra söz konusu ülkelerde Çevresel Kuznets Eğrisi (ÇKE) hipotezinin geçerliliği de sınanmaktadır. Ampirik bulgular, politika etkilerinin ülkeden ülkeye belirgin biçimde farklılaştığını ortaya koymaktadır. Bu bulgular dört başlık altında özetlenebilir: (i) Enerji vergisi, Hollanda’da karbon ayak izini istatistiksel olarak anlamlı biçimde artırmaktadır. (ii) Çevre koruma harcamaları, İspanya’da karbon ayak izini anlamlı ölçüde azaltmaktadır. (iii) Ekonomik büyüme, Belçika'da karbon ayak izini artırıcı yönde etki yapmaktadır. Ancak büyümenin, Macaristan ve Polonya’da ise negatif etkisi bulunmaktadır. (iv) Belçika’da ters U şeklindeki Çevresel Kuznets Eğrisi geçerlidir. Elde edilen bulgular çerçevesinde, üç somut politika çıkarımı öne çıkmaktadır. Birincisi, enerji vergisinin Hollanda’da karbon ayak izini artırdığı bulgusu, mevcut vergi yapısının emisyon azaltımı amacına hizmet etmediğine işaret etmektedir. Bu ülkelerde enerji vergisi gelirlerinin doğrudan temiz enerji araştırma-geliştirme faaliyetlerine ve enerji verimliliği sübvansiyonlarına yönlendirilmesi, vergilerin çevresel etkinliğini artırmaya katkı sağlayabilir. İkincisi, İspanya’da çevre koruma harcamalarının karbon ayak izini azaltıcı etkisi dikkate alındığında, bu harcamaların bütçedeki payının artırılması ve söz konusu kaynakların özellikle karbonsuzlaştırma teknolojileri ile yenilenebilir enerji altyapısı gibi daha yüksek çevresel getiri sağlayan alanlara yönlendirilmesi önerilmektedir. Üçüncüsü, Belçika'da ekonomik büyümenin karbon ayak izini artırması, bu ülkelerin büyüme süreçlerinin hâlâ fosil yakıt bağımlılığından tam anlamıyla kopamadığını göstermektedir. Bu çerçevede söz konusu ülkelerin sürdürülebilir büyüme politikalarını güçlendirmesi ve yeşil dönüşüm araçlarını daha etkin biçimde uygulamaya koyması gerekmektedir.

title: Bridging Policy and Practice: Enabling Robust GHG Emission Accounting Across Transport Services
summary: Abstract Reliable and harmonised GHG emission factors are essential for enabling fair and transparent climate impact comparisons across transport services. However, current methodologies are fragmented, with limited treatment of emerging fu
content: Abstract Reliable and harmonised GHG emission factors are essential for enabling fair and transparent climate impact comparisons across transport services. However, current methodologies are fragmented, with limited treatment of emerging fuels, inconsistent data handling, and poor integration of upstream energy carrier pathways. This paper presents the scientific and methodological basis of the CLEVER framework, a new EU supported standard to calculate lifecycle based GHG emission factors for transport fuels and energy carriers. Designed in alignment with ISO 14083 and as a core component of the upcoming CountEmissionsEU regulation, CLEVER introduces a modular, attributional LCA based approach that integrates upstream well to tank and operational tank to wheel emissions. The framework improves on existing approaches by clarifying system boundaries, harmonising modelling rules, and incorporating additional climate relevant sources such as indirect land use change, methane slip, black carbon, and hydrogen leakage. It supports both default factors and operator specific data, enabling comparability while also rewarding more accurate, fuel pathway specific assessments. CLEVER advances best practice in data quality scoring, certification linkage, and reporting granularity, creating a credible foundation for industry wide decarbonisation tracking and digital emissions integration in transport.

title: Introducing Circularity in Public Transport for Greater Sustainability: From Strategy to Action
summary: Abstract Public transport (PT) systems are vital to society, providing access to goods, services, and opportunities. However, the construction, maintenance, and decommissioning of PT assets contribute to carbon emissions, resource depletion
content: Abstract Public transport (PT) systems are vital to society, providing access to goods, services, and opportunities. However, the construction, maintenance, and decommissioning of PT assets contribute to carbon emissions, resource depletion, and ecological disruption. The CE4CE (Circular Economy for Central Europe) project addresses this by promoting a shift from a linear to a circular model using the “Avoid-Extend-Transform-Enable” life-cycle framework. This framework has been applied to develop three strategies focused on rolling stock, infrastructure, and energy, based on consultations with public transport operators (PTOs) from Central Europe and beyond. These three strategies serve as the foundation for localized, stakeholder-aligned action plans in Leipzig, Bergamo, Gdynia, and Maribor. This paper provides a concise overview of these strategies, covering: 1) the application of the life-cycle thinking framework to each pillar; 2) a status quo analysis of circularity integration in PT systems; 3) a catalogue of practical cases for implementing circularity; and 4) a set of tailored indicators for monitoring and measuring impact. The paper also discusses how these strategies have been adapted into action plans, supporting the transition from isolated initiatives to more strategic, life-cycle-oriented approach in PT, with a greater focus on resource efficiency and a significant reduction in ecological impacts.

title: CUL3-mediated NRF2 dysregulation in TP53-driven non-small cell lung cancer: neddylation-associated structural perturbations
summary: CUL3 encodes Cullin-3, the scaffold of Cullin-RING Ligase 3 (CRL3), which mediates proteasomal degradation of NRF2 through KEAP1-dependent ubiquitination. While canonical NRF2 alterations such as KEAP1 or NFE2L2 mutations are well character
content: CUL3 encodes Cullin-3, the scaffold of Cullin-RING Ligase 3 (CRL3), which mediates proteasomal degradation of NRF2 through KEAP1-dependent ubiquitination. While canonical NRF2 alterations such as KEAP1 or NFE2L2 mutations are well characterised in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the role of CUL3 mutations remains poorly defined. We hypothesised that CUL3 missense variants are conditionally enriched in TP53-altered NSCLC, with the EGFR-oncogenic subset as a defined disease background rather than a synergistic requirement. A multi-cohort NSCLC dataset (n = 47,862; 10,228 with oncogenic EGFR mutations and confirmed CUL3 coverage) was interrogated using two-layer Fisher’s exact testing and logistic regression with an EGFR × TP53 interaction term, and validated transcriptomically in TCGA LUAD/LUSC. CUL3 mutations showed conditional enrichment in the TP53-mutant EGFR background (OR = 2.92, p = 4.68 × 10 −29 ); the non-significant EGFR × TP53 interaction (OR = 0.86, p = 0.547) confirmed that enrichment is driven by TP53 loss rather than EGFR synergy. CUL3-mutant tumours showed elevated NRF2 activation across three independent signatures, with increased proliferative signalling and altered drug metabolism. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations of wild-type, L321F, G402E and M711I CUL3:KEAP1 complexes in inactive and neddylation-active states revealed variant-specific conformational behaviour. L321F drove the neddylated complex into a conformationally restricted state with reduced backbone flexibility, decreased radius of gyration, and a shifted free energy minimum, whereas G402E showed progressive destabilisation and M711I remained comparable to wild-type. Free energy landscape analysis confirmed a shifted conformational energy minimum in L321F + NEDD8 relative to wild-type, indicating impaired catalytic flexibility despite intact complex formation. These findings define CUL3 as a TP53-associated modifier of NRF2 regulation within EGFR-driven NSCLC, operating through allosteric rigidification of the neddylation-active CRL3 complex.

title: Reel Efektif Döviz Kuru Teknolojik Kapasitenin Çevresel Etkilerini Koşullandırıyor mu? OECD Ülkeleri Üzerine Kanıtlar
source: Iğdır Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
summary: Teknolojik kapasitenin çevresel etkileri, ülkelerin ekonomik ve rekabetçi yapısına bağlı olarak farklılaşabilmektedir. Ancak bu farklılaşmada reel efektif döviz kurunun oynadığı rol henüz yeterince açıklığa kavuşturulamamıştır. Bu kapsamda
content: Teknolojik kapasitenin çevresel etkileri, ülkelerin ekonomik ve rekabetçi yapısına bağlı olarak farklılaşabilmektedir. Ancak bu farklılaşmada reel efektif döviz kurunun oynadığı rol henüz yeterince açıklığa kavuşturulamamıştır. Bu kapsamda çalışmada, teknolojik kapasitenin karbon emisyonları üzerindeki etkisini ve reel efektif döviz kuru düzeyinin bu ilişki üzerindeki koşullandırıcı rolünü incelemektedir. Analizde, 2007–2023 döneminde 20 OECD ülkesine ait panel veriler kullanılmıştır. Teknolojik kapasiteyi temsil etmek amacıyla, yüksek teknoloji ihracatı, Ar-Ge yoğunluğu ve teknoloji temelli patent göstergelerinden yararlanılarak, Temel Bileşenler Analizi (PCA) yöntemiyle bir bütünleşik teknolojik kapasite endeksi (BTKE) oluşturulmuştur. Değişkenler arasındaki dinamik ilişkiler ise iki aşamalı Sistem GMM yöntemiyle tahmin edilmiştir. Ayrıca, teknolojik kapasitenin farklı reel efektif döviz kuru düzeylerindeki etkisi koşullu marjinal etki analizi kullanılarak değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, teknolojik kapasitenin karbon emisyonları üzerindeki etkisinin doğrusal olmadığını göstermektedir. Reel efektif döviz kurunun düşük olduğu seviyelerde teknolojik kapasite karbon emisyonlarını artırırken, reel efektif döviz kuru yükseldikçe bu etki zayıflamakta ve belirli bir seviyeden sonra emisyonu azaltıcı hale gelmektedir. Sonuçlar, teknolojik gelişmelerin çevresel etkilerinin ülkelerin rekabet yapısı ve makroekonomik koşulları tarafından şekillendirildiğini ortaya koymaktadır.

title: Policy-Driven Good Practices for Sustainable Intermodal Transport in Rural and Urban Areas
summary: Abstract In Europe, rural and peri-urban regions face challenges in accessing integrated transport systems, digital connectivity for improving travel experience and flexible mobility services, which make the use of private vehicles predomin
content: Abstract In Europe, rural and peri-urban regions face challenges in accessing integrated transport systems, digital connectivity for improving travel experience and flexible mobility services, which make the use of private vehicles predominant. EMBRACER is a region-driven project where seven underserved regions have committed to integrating public transport with informal modes (cycling, ride-hailing, car/bike/scooter sharing, on-demand transport, and autonomous shuttles) to enhance the interconnection with urban areas and achieve seamless, intelligent, climate-resilient regional and local intermodal mobility. The focus is to build capacity based on interregional learning through a structured cooperation process that fosters a multi-stakeholder co-creation approach to the identification of innovative intermodal mobility solutions, which is further enriched by a pilot testing the viability of an autonomous shuttle service to interconnect with public transport and enhance travel in remote areas.

title: Corn straw fiber-modified asphalt for high-RAP recycled PAC-13 mixtures: preparation, rheology, and pavement performance
summary: Introduction Open burning of corn stalks causes environmental pollution, while recycled asphalt mixtures with high reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) content require adequate binder performance to maintain pavement durability. This study eval
content: Introduction Open burning of corn stalks causes environmental pollution, while recycled asphalt mixtures with high reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) content require adequate binder performance to maintain pavement durability. This study evaluated corn stalk fibers as bio-based modifiers for high-RAP recycled PAC-13 mixtures. Methods Corn stalk fibers were prepared using physical-mechanical and chemical alkali treatments, and treatment conditions were evaluated using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and thermogravimetric analysis. Asphalt binders containing 0.4%–2.0% fiber were tested using a dynamic shear rheometer and a bending beam rheometer. The selected binder was used to prepare recycled PAC-13 mixtures containing 20%–60% RAP, and their pavement performance was assessed. Results Chemical alkali treatment with 3% NaOH for 50 min produced fibers with superior thermal stability and oil absorption capacity. The optimal fiber content was 1.2%, improving the binder’s high-temperature shear resistance and low-temperature stress relaxation. As RAP content increased, optimum binder content, Marshall stability, dynamic stability, moisture resistance, and low-temperature crack resistance declined, while air void content increased. At approximately 40% RAP, all key performance indicators met the relevant technical specifications. Discussion Under the materials and experimental conditions investigated, approximately 40% RAP is the recommended upper limit for corn stalk fiber-modified recycled PAC-13 mixtures.

title: Waste, Resources, and Regulation: Assessing Environmental Sustainability in the European Union
summary: ABSTRACT Waste generated by economic activities has reached serious levels and threatens ecological sustainability. These activities not only prevent the economic use of natural resources but also leave behind waste that is difficult to man
content: ABSTRACT Waste generated by economic activities has reached serious levels and threatens ecological sustainability. These activities not only prevent the economic use of natural resources but also leave behind waste that is difficult to manage for the environment. Policymakers are seeking to meet some of their energy demand in a clean way while reducing the pressure on the ecology through waste management. The effectiveness of waste management may vary depending on environmental policy stringency. However, globalization affects society by changing consumption patterns and policymakers with different application examples. These factors, which drive one another, have the potential to seriously affect ecological sustainability. In this study, the impact of waste management expenditures, natural resource depletion, globalization, and environmental policy stringency on load capacity factor in selected European Union (EU) countries is investigated from 1995 to 2020. The results of the study reveal that while natural resource depletion, waste management expenditures, and globalization negatively affect environmental sustainability in France, environmental policy stringency affects it positively. Waste management expenditures in Spain and environmental policy stringency in Ireland increase environmental sustainability. To improve environmental quality in EU countries, it is recommended that environmental policies and standards be further harmonized between countries and that cooperation be increased to achieve common environmental goals.

title: Co‐Producing Environmental Resilience: Integrating Stakeholder, Legitimacy, and Co‐Production Theories to Explain Firms' Responses to Environmental Risk
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental risks challenge firms. While prior research assumes environmental resilience stems from communication or internal capability, this study reconceptualizes resilience as a relational capability co‐produced through firm‐
content: ABSTRACT Environmental risks challenge firms. While prior research assumes environmental resilience stems from communication or internal capability, this study reconceptualizes resilience as a relational capability co‐produced through firm‐stakeholder interactions. Integrating Stakeholder Theory, Legitimacy Theory, and Co‐production Theory, we test our framework using a two‐study design: Study 1 analyzes 93 multinational firms across 26 countries via hierarchical OLS, while Study 2 provides complementary evidence by tracking a matched sample of 139 Japanese firms using cross‐temporal lagged specifications. Our results indicate that stakeholder engagement alone does not mitigate environmental risk; resilience requires aligning external engagement with internal organizational readiness. Moreover, while substantive adaptation incurs immediate operational costs, our temporal evidence indicates that its financial implications are primarily contemporaneous and suggestive of temporal persistence, rather than demonstrating definitive long‐term financial causality. This study extends Co‐production Theory to corporate sustainability, reframing resilience as a strategic relational investment rather than a short‐term financial performance metric.

title: Self-organization of alternating acetate- and carbonate-based interlayer spaces in bimetallic CoZn layered hydroxide salts
summary: Layered hydroxide salts (LHS) are versatile functional materials whose properties can be tailored by the composition of metal hydroxide layers and interlayer anions. Here, a novel cobalt–zinc layered hydroxide salt (Co–Zn–LHS) containing di
content: Layered hydroxide salts (LHS) are versatile functional materials whose properties can be tailored by the composition of metal hydroxide layers and interlayer anions. Here, a novel cobalt–zinc layered hydroxide salt (Co–Zn–LHS) containing distinct intercalated layers of acetate and carbonate anions was reported. A comprehensive combination of indirect experimental data, compiled using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, Raman scattering, ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy, and thermal analysis, strongly indicated the formation of a single ordered phase with alternating mixed Co Zn hydroxide layers separated by acetate and carbonate interlayer spaces. The structure exhibited a basal periodicity of about 19.9 Å, close to the sum of typical carbonate- and acetate-LHS spacings, and showed up to twelve basal reflections with a coherent scattering domain size of approximately 500 Å, evidencing long-range ordering along the stacking direction. Anion-exchange experiments demonstrated the selective replacement of acetate FTIR bands, while carbonate bands remained essentially unchanged, which was consistent with the spatial separation of the two anionic interlayer spaces. The highest degree of ordering was achieved at near-equimolar Co/Zn ratios, where Zn preferentially stabilized tetrahedral sites and Co occupied octahedral positions. Thermal analysis revealed a sharp collapse of the layered structure at 240–300 °C, followed by transformation into a mixed Zn–Co–O oxide phase. Electrodes prepared from the optimized Co–Zn–LHS showed a specific capacity of 40 mAh g −1 (equivalent to a specific capacitance of 314 F g −1 ), with 61% capacity retention at 10 A g −1 . These results demonstrated a new route toward mixed-anion LHS materials with long-range ordered interlayer architectures.

title: A study on the four-party evolutionary game of collaborative carbon emission reduction in the petrochemical industry
summary: Against the dual backdrop of domestic green transformation and international carbon emission reduction constraints, this paper addresses the challenge of synergistic carbon governance in the petrochemical industry. Grounded in the industry’
content: Against the dual backdrop of domestic green transformation and international carbon emission reduction constraints, this paper addresses the challenge of synergistic carbon governance in the petrochemical industry. Grounded in the industry’s characteristics of long facility service life, high transformation costs, and strong policy dependence, it focuses on the interest conflicts among four parties—the central government, local governments, petrochemical enterprises, and third-party regulatory agencies—and develops a four-party evolutionary game model. Through local stability analysis and numerical simulation, the stability conditions and evolutionary trends of the four parties’ strategy choices are systematically examined. The results indicate that: (1) Raising the central government’s penalty intensity significantly shortens the decision-making time of the central government, petrochemical enterprises, and third-party agencies, yet prolongs the strategy evolution time of local governments; (2) As the central government’s subsidy coefficient increases, the central government’s strategy exhibits persistent fluctuation within the 0–1 interval and fails to converge to a steady state, while the decision-making time of petrochemical enterprises is markedly shortened, with the evolutionary trajectories of local governments and third-party agencies showing no significant change; (3) Strengthening local governments’ penalty intensity effectively accelerates the decision-making of local governments and petrochemical enterprises, whereas the evolutionary trajectories of the central government and third-party agencies remain largely unaffected; (4) Increasing local governments’ subsidy coefficient slows the evolution of local governments toward the proactive emission-reduction governance strategy, but effectively drives petrochemical enterprises to actively evolve toward proactive carbon reduction strategies. These findings offer theoretical support and practical implications for improving the multi-agent collaborative governance mechanism of carbon reduction in the petrochemical industry, assisting governments at all levels in formulating differentiated carbon regulation policies with precision, and promoting the green and low-carbon transformation of the petrochemical sector.

title: Recyclable Lignin‐Based Thermadapt Shape Memory Polymers With Near‐Infrared Light Response
summary: ABSTRACT Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) have been designed to address the recycling challenges associated with thermosets, while preserving their mechanical properties. However, producing biobased CANs with intelligent response capabili
content: ABSTRACT Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) have been designed to address the recycling challenges associated with thermosets, while preserving their mechanical properties. However, producing biobased CANs with intelligent response capabilities remains challenging. We report the preparation of lignin‐polypentadecalactone‐based CANs with a high biomass content (86.2–96.4 wt%). In lignin‐PPDL CANs, acetoacetate‐modified lignin serves dual roles as the hard segment and crosslinker, while the polypentadecalactone (PPDL) soft segment exhibits a semi‐crystalline nature. Crosslinking between the soft PPDL and hard lignin segments is achieved via vinylogous urethane chemistry, resulting in CANs with markedly enhanced mechanical properties and recyclability. When applied to shape memory systems, the semi‐crystalline polymer domains act as reversible molecular switches, while dynamic bond exchange enables topological rearrangement, allowing reconfiguration of the permanent shape, characteristic of thermadapt shape memory polymers. Leveraging the photothermal conversion capability of lignin, we successfully developed near‐infrared (NIR) light‐responsive shape memory CANs. These innovative materials hold promising prospects for applications in intelligent materials, given their unique combination of mechanical strength, shape memory capabilities, and responsiveness to NIR light. Furthermore, the approach of tailoring the new material based on the specific properties of the raw material in this study offers a novel avenue for designing high‐performance multifunctional CANs.

title: Predicted soil loss and the contribution of soil map units in a tropical protected forest: Revised universal soil loss equation assessment of Ir. H. Djuanda Forest Park, Indonesia
summary: Soil erosion degrades soil and water resources in tropical protected areas.We mapped RUSLE-predicted soil loss in Ir.H. Djuanda Forest Park, West Java, Indonesia, and quantified the contribution of soil map units (SMUs) to spatial variation
content: Soil erosion degrades soil and water resources in tropical protected areas.We mapped RUSLE-predicted soil loss in Ir.H. Djuanda Forest Park, West Java, Indonesia, and quantified the contribution of soil map units (SMUs) to spatial variation in model inputs.Rainfall erosivity was derived from 2016-2025 CHIRPS precipitation using the modified Fournier index and Arnoldus relation, giving a period-mean R of 13,825.61MJ mm•ha -1 •h -1 •yr -1 .Soil erodibility was derived from a 1:50,000 soil map and SoilGrids organic carbon, the topographic factor from the DEMNAS grid using the Desmet-Govers formulation, and cover from SPOT-6 imagery (overall accuracy 82.5%, kappa 0.77).Cells with at least 300 contributing cells were treated as concentrated-flow cells and excluded from the hillslope calculation.The baseline RUSLE × SMU intersection contained 493.32 ha of valid estimates, with 93.36% below 385.14 t•ha -1 •yr -1 and a maximum predicted soil loss of 8,184.15t•ha -1 •yr -1 .SMU-4 contained 97.0% of the 32.74 ha above 385.14t•ha -1 •yr -1 .The area-weighted variance of ln(K) was 0.16% of that of ln(C), indicating substantially greater spatial contrast from land cover than from SMU-based K classes.Sensitivity testing showed that concentrated-flow treatment strongly affected the upper tail, whereas median LS changed by less than 10% between the unmasked and 75-cell scenarios.Without independent erosion measurements, the results are interpreted as modelled soil-loss potential and spatial screening information rather than measured erosion rates.

title: KÜRESEL EMİSYON TİCARET SİSTEMLERİNİN ÇEVRESEL VE EKONOMİK ETKİLERİNİN PRISMA YÖNTEMİ İLE ANALİZİ
source: Uluslararası İktisadi ve İdari İncelemeler Dergisi
summary: Emisyon Ticaret Sistemleri (ETS), iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede maliyet etkin emisyon azaltımı sağlayan önemli bir piyasa temelli politika aracı olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Bu çalışma, ETS’nin ekonomik ve çevresel etkilerini bütüncül bir pers
content: Emisyon Ticaret Sistemleri (ETS), iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede maliyet etkin emisyon azaltımı sağlayan önemli bir piyasa temelli politika aracı olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Bu çalışma, ETS’nin ekonomik ve çevresel etkilerini bütüncül bir perspektifle değerlendirmeyi amaçlamaktadır. Bu doğrultuda, PRISMA yöntemi kullanılarak Web of Science ve Scopus veri tabanlarında tarama gerçekleştirilmiş, eleme süreci sonucunda 76 makale araştırmaya dahil edilmiştir. Bulgular, ETS’nin çevresel performansın yanı sıra enerji tüketim yapısı, endüstriyel dönüşüm, yeşil teknoloji inovasyonu, doğrudan yabancı yatırımlar ve yeşil finansman üzerinde de önemli etkiler oluşturduğunu göstermiştir. Ayrıca, kısa vadede karbon yoğun sektörlerde maliyet baskısı oluştursa da uzun vadede düşük karbonlu üretimi teşvik ederek sürdürülebilir ekonomik büyümeyi desteklediği belirlenmiştir. Araştırma sonucunda, ETS’nin çevresel hedefler ile ekonomik performans arasında denge kurabildiği ve etkinliğinin politika tasarımı ile tamamlayıcı düzenlemelere bağlı olduğu ortaya konulmuştur.

title: Implementing the 2ZERO Technology in Vehicle Parc Models: The Impact of Research and Innovation in Long-Term Outlooks for the EU
summary: Abstract The European Commission has set ambitious CO 2 reduction targets for the transport sector as part of its broader carbon neutrality strategy for 2050 (Fit for 55). In response, the 2ZERO Partnership seeks to accelerate the transitio
content: Abstract The European Commission has set ambitious CO 2 reduction targets for the transport sector as part of its broader carbon neutrality strategy for 2050 (Fit for 55). In response, the 2ZERO Partnership seeks to accelerate the transition toward zero tailpipe emission mobility focusing on affordable, user-centric technologies and services and supporting their widespread adoption. 2ZERO also supports progress in life-cycle analysis methods, the deployment of efficient charging infrastructure, and the mitigation of non-powertrain emissions and road transport-related noise within a circular economy context. LeMesurier is a Horizon Europe Coordination and Support Action that developed a framework for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of the 2ZERO Partnership in achieving its goals. It assesses progress against Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) outlined in the Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda (SRIA) of the Partnership.
