title: Marine ranching for carbon-neutral fisheries in China: Carbon sink evidence, policy instruments, and transition pathways
source: Asian Journal of Water Environment and Pollution
summary: Marine-ranching carbon sink (MRCS) is defined as an additional, verifiable net climate benefit attributable to a bounded ranching intervention after considering baseline conditions, carbon fate, life-cycle emissions, and uncertainty. Marine
content: Marine-ranching carbon sink (MRCS) is defined as an additional, verifiable net climate benefit attributable to a bounded ranching intervention after considering baseline conditions, carbon fate, life-cycle emissions, and uncertainty. Marine ranching is increasingly discussed in China as a means to align fisheries with the national carbon-neutrality agenda. However, terms such as additional biomass, harvested carbon, long-lived storage, avoided emissions, and offset credits refer to different outcomes. This review examines when a marine ranch can deliver a defensible net climate benefit. It combines research on fishery emissions and sequestration, Chinese policy and technical standards, empirical pilot practices, and international work on blue-carbon accounting. The evidence is analyzed through 4 key dimensions: carbon pool alterations, ultimate carbon destination, emissions within the project boundary, and the additionality and verifiability of the claimed change. Chinese estimates demonstrate substantial biological uptake by shellfish and macroalgae, but they vary widely with species coverage, carbon coefficients, treatment of dissolved and particulate carbon, ecological carrying capacity, and deduction of production emissions. Although policy has advanced from demonstration zones to measurement standards and voluntary-market rules, no generally accepted method yet covers an entire ranching system. Therefore, this review interprets marine ranching as a managed area in which restoration, low-input mariculture, operational decarbonization, and monitoring can be combined and tested against a baseline. Credible MRCS claims require carbon-fate evidence, life-cycle inventories, long-term observation, conservative uncertainty treatment, and transparent allocation of benefits.

title: The Role of Carboxymethyl Cellulose (CMC) from Banana (Musa paradisiaca) Peels and Corn (Zea mays L.) Cobs as Ice Cream Stabilizers
summary: Background: The growing demand for natural food additives has spurred theexploration of agricultural waste, such as banana peels and corn cobs, as alternativesources of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC). CMC functions as a stabilizer in foodpro
content: Background: The growing demand for natural food additives has spurred theexploration of agricultural waste, such as banana peels and corn cobs, as alternativesources of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC). CMC functions as a stabilizer in foodproducts, including ice cream, improving its texture and shelf life. Objectives: This study aimed to produce and analyze CMC from two types of agriculturalwaste, Musa paradisiaca peels and Zea mays L. cobs, and evaluate its application in icecream formulations. Methods: The methods used include delignification, alkalization, carboxymethylation,purification and neutralization. The CMC was synthesized through alkalization andetherification using NaOH and sodium monochloroacetate. The extracted CMC wasapplied as a stabilizer in ice cream formulations. The physicochemical properties of CMC(pH and yield) and the quality of ice cream (melting rate, overrun, and texture) wereanalyzed using descriptive and comparative methods. Results: The yield of CMC from Musa paradisiaca peels (29.5%) was higher than Zeamays L. cobs (26.9%). CMC from Musa paradisiaca peels and Zea mays L. cobs showedpH stability. Ice cream stabilized with Musa paradisiaca peel CMC demonstrated highermelting rates and better overrun than ice cream stabilized with CMC from Zea mays L.cobs. Conclusions: Musa paradisiaca peels and Zea mays L. cobs can be utilized as alternativeraw materials for CMC production. Among the two, Musa paradisiaca peel-derived CMCexhibited superior stabilizing properties in ice cream, offering a sustainable and effectivesubstitute for natural stabilizers.

title: Quantifying and attributing CO emissions over Central Asia using TROPOMI and explicit observational uncertainty
summary: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric constituent influencing both air quality and climate. Using TROPOMI CO and HCHO column retrievals within the Model-Free Inversion Estimation Framework (MFIEF), this study quantified da
content: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric constituent influencing both air quality and climate. Using TROPOMI CO and HCHO column retrievals within the Model-Free Inversion Estimation Framework (MFIEF), this study quantified daily, gridded CO emissions in Central Asia (Xinjiang-China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan) for 2019–2024. Results reveal a marked interannual decline of ~ 38 % in mean emissions, accompanied by a weakening of emission hotspots. Seasonal peaks in winter and early spring highlight the roles of heating and industrial demand. Importantly, explicit perturbation-based uncertainty analysis showed that ~ 69 % of grid-level estimates are unreliable if observational uncertainties are ignored or using an overly simplified emissions estimation approach, underscoring the nonlinear propagation of retrieval errors. By integrating coal consumption data, we confirm the consistency between satellite-inferred emissions and bottom-up activity estimates, while also identifying missing sources such as underground coal fires. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of MFIEF in data-scarce regions, provides actionable insights for inventory improvement and mitigation strategies, and highlights the framework's potential extension to CH4 and CO2 retrieval-based emission estimation.

title: Synthesis of greenhouse gas emission factors for forest organic soils in the Köppen–Geiger Dfb climate zone
summary: Abstract. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from organic soils are a key component of land-use-related emissions, particularly in countries with large areas of organic soils. Temperate-zone forest soils remain less studied in GHG research than
content: Abstract. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from organic soils are a key component of land-use-related emissions, particularly in countries with large areas of organic soils. Temperate-zone forest soils remain less studied in GHG research than boreal soils. However, recent work has expanded coverage in the northeastern temperate region, which, under the Köppen–Geiger climate classification, shares key climatic characteristics with the southern boreal region (Dfb). This study synthesised updated GHG flux data to evaluate carbon balance and emissions from forest organic soils in the Dfb zone, stratified by drainage status, nutrient availability, and dominant tree species. Such stratification revealed CO2 source-sink patterns, which encourage the ecological relevance of using these categories for data aggregation. The dominant tree species reflected nutrient status: drained coniferous and deciduous stands have been reported as CO2 sources, emitting 0.03 ± 0.55 and 0.47 ± 0.29 t CO2‑C ha−1 year−1, respectively, though soils tended to shift toward CO2 sinks in stands older than 25 years. In contrast, undrained soils have generally been observed to function as CO2 sinks, although not necessarily in all sites. However, this stratification was less informative for CH4 and N2O. CH4 fluxes were primarily determined by water table level rather than by other site variables, whereas N2O showed a tendency toward elevated emissions in deciduous stands, irrespective of drainage status.

title: Selection of optimal HHP conditions for processing of Tenebrio molitor paste based on a comprehensive evaluation of quality indicators
summary: This study aimed to understand the effects of different operational parameters and define the best conditions for applying high hydrostatic pressure to Tenebrio molitor paste, aiming to maximise benefits while minimising undesired effects o
content: This study aimed to understand the effects of different operational parameters and define the best conditions for applying high hydrostatic pressure to Tenebrio molitor paste, aiming to maximise benefits while minimising undesired effects on the quality of the final product. Three pressure levels (200, 400, 600 MPa) were applied to fresh mealworm paste for dwell times of 0- (control), 5-, 15-, 30-, 45- and 60-min. Microbial investigation of the studied pastes revealed a significant reduction in total viable count at pressures of 600 and 400 MPa, whereas no microbial reduction was observed at 200 MPa. A slight increase in titratable acidity was observed at every pressure, with the highest acidity measured for paste treated at 400MPa for 60 min. Complete absence of lipid oxidation was measured at every pressure, with the peroxide value showing no significant differences. Similar behaviour was also observed for TBARs at 600 MPa. An increase in TBARs from short to long dwell time was observed at 400 and 200 MPa. The total phenolic content and antioxidant activity increased notably after the HHP treatment, with the highest values recorded at 400 MPa, regardless of the treatment time. A reduction in lipase activity was also observed at every pressure level, with a clear linear effect over treatment time. The process optimisation study revealed that 510 MPa applied for 31 min is the best treatment for maximising positive effects while minimising adverse effects. However, further studies should be conducted to validate and confirm the transferability of this observation.

title: Socio-techno-ecological imaginaries: A framework for understanding future-making for and with ecology
summary: This article proposes socio-techno-ecological imaginaries (STEI) as a conceptual extension of sociotechnical imaginaries (STI). While STI has been valuable for showing how social order and technological change co-produce “desirable futures,
content: This article proposes socio-techno-ecological imaginaries (STEI) as a conceptual extension of sociotechnical imaginaries (STI). While STI has been valuable for showing how social order and technological change co-produce “desirable futures,” we argue it tends to leave implicit how visions of ecology – beliefs about what nature is and acts, how it is valued, and how humans ought to relate to it – are entangled in this process. This implicitness risks limiting STI’s explanatory power, its capacity to evaluate the desirability of imagined futures amid socio-ecological crises, and its own imaginative horizon in futures work. Drawing on literatures on socio-ecological imagination, eco-social imaginaries, and environmental and nature imaginaries, we define STEIs as institutionally embedded and publicly performed visions of desirable futures, animated by specific understandings and valuations of society, technology and ecology. STEI rests on three premises: (1) imaginaries are co-produced across social, technical, and ecological dimensions; (2) each dimension carries specific assumptions and normative valuations that condition what futures are deemed plausible and desirable; and (3) alignment or misalignment across these assumptions and valuations can be sites of conflict, lock-in, and transformation. We demonstrate the framework’s analytical value through an empirical study of the STEIs that guide the development and use expectations of sensor technologies in the Dutch agricultural sector. The study combines interviews with a corpus of public web texts to identify two STEIs, showing how divergent visions of society, technology, and ecology co-produce distinct farming futures. STEI, we conclude, strengthens critical futures research by enabling more explicit, plural, and ecologically attuned evaluations of future-making.

title: Mechanism model for long-term degradation failure of PEM water electrolyzers
summary: Abstract One of the bottlenecks restricting the large-scale commercialization of proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers lies in their poor durability. Due to numerous degradation categories and complex degradation mechanisms within el
content: Abstract One of the bottlenecks restricting the large-scale commercialization of proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers lies in their poor durability. Due to numerous degradation categories and complex degradation mechanisms within electrolyzers, it is still difficult to quantify the ratio of one single mechanism on the overall degradation through experiments, making it impossible to fully understand the degradation characteristics. A mechanistic model for simulating the degradation process in PEM electrolyzers is proposed in this study. It describes three dominant degradation processes, including ionomer degradation, IrO 2 dissolution, and titanium passivation and corrosion. Then, these three degradation sub-models are coupled into a three-dimensional full-electrolyzer model to reveal the mechanism of long-term operation failure of electrolyzers. It captures the coupling mechanism between degradation and internal heat and mass transfer process, revealing the rapid electrolyzer degradation in the early stage is mainly caused by titanium and ionomer degradation. Increasing the temperature and current density accelerate degradation, that is, temperature primarily accelerates IrO 2 and ionomer degradation, while current density mainly accelerates IrO 2 and Ti degradation. Under low-temperature and low-current-density conditions, electrolyzer failure is mainly due to the voltage reaching the failure criterion; in contrast, electrolyzer failure is more likely caused by IrO 2 dissolution under high-temperature and high-current-density conditions. The developed model provides a foundation for understanding the mechanism of PEM water electrolyzer’s degradation and enhancing the application durability.

title: Quantitative in vitro PET/MRI and kinetic modelling of imaging agent release from a thermoreversible intranasal sol-gel
source: European Journal of Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics
summary: Intranasal phase-transforming thermoresponsive gels can prolong nasal residence and enable controlled release of diagnostic or therapeutic payloads. However, quantitative real-time release characterisation of multimodal imaging probes remai
content: Intranasal phase-transforming thermoresponsive gels can prolong nasal residence and enable controlled release of diagnostic or therapeutic payloads. However, quantitative real-time release characterisation of multimodal imaging probes remains limited. Here, we developed a poloxamer-based sol–gel and established a hybrid PET/MRI framework to quantify the release of PET tracers and an activatable MnO 2 nanoflower into simulated nasal fluid. The formulations transformed from solution-to-gel at ∼ 28–29 °C with a storage modulus of 8.2−9.5 kPa attained at typical nasal cavity temperature (34 °C), while maintaining a nasal-compatible pH. PET imaging with an extended time window demonstrated diffusion-dominated release with clear size dependence: ionic [ 64 Cu]Cu 2+ reached 30.0 ± 3.0 % cumulative release at ∼42 h, whereas [ 64 Cu]Cu-Sar-OP showed 15.6 ± 3.1 % cumulative release under the same simulated conditions. PEGylated MnO 2 nanoflowers exhibited negligible apparent release in simulated nasal fluid without reductant due to the absence of redox-triggered MnO 2 dissolution to soluble Mn 2+ and electrolyte-induced nanoparticle aggregation trapping, which restricts diffusion out of the gel; but with GSH-supplementation, quantitative T1/T2 mapping enabled relaxivity-calibrated tracking of apparent Mn-equivalent accumulation, reaching 13.9 ± 0.7 % of the nominal loaded Mn (T1-based) at ∼24 h. The cytocompatibility of MnO 2 NFs–PEG was also evaluated in an RPMI 2650 human nasal epithelial cell model following 24-h exposure. Kinetic modelling (Higuchi and Korsmeyer − Peppas) supported diffusion-dominated transfer of the PET tracers, whereas the MnO 2 profile reflected coupled redox and transport processes under limited-GSH conditions. Overall, our integrated PET/MRI approach provides a quantitative framework for comparing in vitro depot release kinetics and informing intranasal PET/MRI formulation design; however, the findings should not be interpreted as direct evidence of mucosal retention or in vivo nose-to-brain transport.

title: Restored but Still Emitting: High CO 2 Fluxes From a Mediterranean Wetland Challenge Inundation‐Based Restoration Strategies
summary: Abstract Mediterranean wetlands significantly influence terrestrial carbon storage but lack comprehensive, long‐term carbon flux measurements, particularly those that distinguish fluxes between vegetated and open‐water surfaces. Inundation‐
content: Abstract Mediterranean wetlands significantly influence terrestrial carbon storage but lack comprehensive, long‐term carbon flux measurements, particularly those that distinguish fluxes between vegetated and open‐water surfaces. Inundation‐based restoration primarily aims to arrest drainage‐driven soil‐carbon loss; whether a re‐flooded wetland also becomes a net CO 2 sink is not guaranteed and depends on recovery time, wetland design, and vegetation establishment. We conducted a 3‐year (2021–2024) eddy covariance study using dual towers over a restored Mediterranean wetland (Agmon Hula, Israel) to partition CO 2 fluxes between these surfaces. Results show that the restored wetland acted as a persistent net source of CO 2 , emitting 3.8 ± 7.2 g C m −2 day −1 (∼14 t C ha −1 yr −1 ), with open water (∼80% area) as a major source (5.0 ± 8.6 g C m −2 day −1 ; ∼18.3 t C ha −1 yr −1 ), especially during summer nights driven by water‐to‐air temperature gradients and atmospheric instability, while vegetated zones acted as a net sink (−1.0 ± 11.3 g C m −2 day −1 ; ∼−3.7 t C ha −1 yr −1 ). When placed in the context of reported Mediterranean wetland fluxes, the Hula wetland exhibits the highest CO 2 emission rate observed for the region. Our findings indicate that commonly used functional relationships linking CO 2 to hydrological conditions should explicitly account for surface heterogeneity and nocturnal atmospheric coupling. Furthermore, enhancing vegetation cover may be critical for shifting open‐water‐dominated Mediterranean wetlands toward net carbon sinks under changing climatic conditions.

title: Data-driven valorization of mixed olefins byproducts via self-stabilized precipitation polymerization
summary: The transition of fossil fuels from energy sources to chemical feedstocks has generated huge amount of mixed olefins byproducts, whose efficient valorization remains an important challenge in chemical engineering. Self-stabilized precipitat
content: The transition of fossil fuels from energy sources to chemical feedstocks has generated huge amount of mixed olefins byproducts, whose efficient valorization remains an important challenge in chemical engineering. Self-stabilized precipitation (2SP) polymerization offers a promising route to directly convert these under-utilized olefins into polymer products without costly separation or other pre-treatments. However, the multi-factor nature of 2SP leaves its mechanism largely speculative, and the reaction feasibility currently relies on time-consuming trial-and-error experimentation. Here, we developed a machine learning predictor, 2SP-MLP, trained on 844 experimental data points to enable rapid and accurate prediction of 2SP outcomes. Following Bayesian optimization with 5-fold cross-validation, the XGBoost classifier achieved the best performance (ACC = 0.90, AUC = 0.96). Interpretability analysis identified the monomer-solvent solubility parameter difference (2.4-11.3 MPa1/2) as the key factor governing 2SP feasibility. Beyond solubility parameter, molecular shape, flexibility and charge distribution were found to significantly influence polymer precipitation and microparticle formation. Regression models for precipitate yield and olefin conversion both performed best with XGBoost (R2 = 0.73 and 0.89, respectively). Experimental validation under 10 newly designed conditions confirmed the model’s generalizability with 70% prediction accuracy. Overall, this work provides a data-driven tool that accelerates process design and reduces experimental cost for 2SP-based valorization of mixed olefins, demonstrating the potential of ML to advance sustainable chemical manufacturing.

title: Sawdust biochar as a dual cement and sand substitute for strength‐optimized and low‐carbon mortar with life‐cycle benefits
summary: The building industry is a major contributor to global CO 2 emissions, highlighting the need to develop low-carbon cement-based products. Biochar emerges as a promising additive for cementitious composites, owing primarily to its inherent c
content: The building industry is a major contributor to global CO 2 emissions, highlighting the need to develop low-carbon cement-based products. Biochar emerges as a promising additive for cementitious composites, owing primarily to its inherent capacity for long-term carbon sequestration, chemical stability, and sustainability benefits. In this study, biochar prepared from wood sawdust at 400 °C in a low-technology pit kiln was incorporated into mortar through two distinct series: (i) partial cement replacement at 1-5% by volume to evaluate microstructural development and mechanical performance, and (ii) 5-25% sand replacement by volume, which permits far higher biochar contents and therefore greater carbon sequestration while also reducing demand for natural sand. Owing to its irregular surface, porous structure, and low feedstock uniformity, biochar promoted hydration, potentially through internal curing and nucleation effects, resulting in greater formation of hydration products. This enhanced the strength and microstructure of biochar-modified mortar, which was compared with a cement-only control mortar. Thermogravimetric analysis of the corresponding pastes showed greater water-related mass loss, consistent with a greater extent of hydration. The maximum improvement in compressive strength, 17.3%, was achieved with a 4% cement replacement. Life cycle assessment (LCA) confirmed a 9.6% decrease in global warming potential (GWP) at this dosage with no strength penalty, rising to 22.9% when normalized per unit compressive strength. Notably, a 25% sand replacement approached carbon neutrality, with a GWP of -8.3 kg CO₂-eq/m³ under the base-case carbon permanence assumption, highlighting the potential of biochar to produce high-performance, low-carbon cementitious materials for specific application requirements.

title: Power system expansion in Ecuador: A stakeholder driven sustainability assessment of generation technologies
summary: Ecuador experienced severe power shortages in 2024, with blackouts lasting up to 14 h a day, exposing the vulnerability of an electricity system that relies heavily on hydroelectric plants, is affected by drought, and has seen limited inves
content: Ecuador experienced severe power shortages in 2024, with blackouts lasting up to 14 h a day, exposing the vulnerability of an electricity system that relies heavily on hydroelectric plants, is affected by drought, and has seen limited investment in new capacity since 2018. In this context, the central government has begun promoting nuclear energy as a medium- and long-term option, despite the country’s lack of experience with this technology and the Electricity Master Plan’s identification of substantial renewable potential. This study provides a sustainability assessment of eight generation technologies for Ecuador’s future energy mix: PV-US, geothermal, onshore wind, biomass, combined-cycle gas turbines, mini hydropower, small modular nuclear reactors, and conventional nuclear fission. The analysis is supported by Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis methods using ELECTRE III and HELDA (Helmholtz MCDA Tool), based on a performance matrix with 15 static baseline sustainability criteria grouped into environmental, technical, economic, and social categories, and weightings derived from a 35-stakeholder survey across the public, private, and academic sectors. Results show that stakeholders rank the availability of domestic resources as the most important criterion, followed by the levelized cost of electricity, risk to human health, and investment costs. When technologies are ranked using these weighted criteria, four renewable options (mini hydropower, onshore wind, PV-US, and geothermal) are preferred, followed by combined-cycle gas turbines and biomass, while both nuclear options are consistently ranked at the bottom. These results recommend that energy policy decisions in Ecuador should be based on transparent, stakeholder-driven assessments of technological options, rather than unilateral decisions detached from stakeholder preferences and system realities.

title: Coupling compliance and voluntary carbon markets: a system dynamics assessment in China
summary: The strategic coupling of compliance and voluntary carbon markets is emerging as a pivotal path for achieving cost-effective decarbonization. However, existing literature seldom captures the dynamic feedback loops, cross-sectoral heterogene
content: The strategic coupling of compliance and voluntary carbon markets is emerging as a pivotal path for achieving cost-effective decarbonization. However, existing literature seldom captures the dynamic feedback loops, cross-sectoral heterogeneities, and environmental economic benefits inherent in dual-market architectures. To fill this gap, this study develops a sector-specific system dynamics model to evaluate the integrated impacts of coupling China’s Emissions Trading System (ETS) and the China Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) scheme. Three distinct scenarios are modeled: no carbon trading market (BAU), Single Market (ETS-only), and Dual Market (ETS + CCER). Results indicate that the Dual Market scenario achieves emission reductions (40.3%) and energy savings (39.7%) comparable to the Single Market scenario, while the unit abatement cost advantage widens from CNY 0.02 to 0.41 per ton of CO2, and cumulative employment losses are reduced by around 0.19 million. Sectoral analysis reveals the power sector is the predominant buyer in the CCER market, accounting for 59.5% of the total transaction volume, while the cement sector acts primarily as a net seller of carbon allowances in 2030. Sensitivity analyses further confirm the robustness and advantages of coupling markets. Policy implications include gradually reducing the free allocation rate from 95% to 90%, dynamically adjusting the CCER offset rate within 5%-10% under strengthened oversight, and establishing coordinated price mechanisms. These findings provide robust evidence for optimizing dual-market architectures to advance both climate targets and a just, resilient low-carbon transition.

title: Influence of Geopolitical Risk on Energy Transition and Climate Change
summary: ABSTRACT Geopolitical tensions can influence energy transition, which, in turn, can impact climate change. Thus, we construct a framework that integrates these processes, analyzing 17 economies from 1990 to 2020 using a GVAR model. We hypot
content: ABSTRACT Geopolitical tensions can influence energy transition, which, in turn, can impact climate change. Thus, we construct a framework that integrates these processes, analyzing 17 economies from 1990 to 2020 using a GVAR model. We hypothesize that geopolitical risk shocks affect economies through domestic financial markets. The results demonstrate that geopolitical risk shocks (i) hinder national energy transitions and contribute to increased carbon emissions; (ii) induce fluctuations in financial markets; (iii) have a minor direct impact on energy transition, except in Scandinavia and the United States; (iv) indirectly influence economies through financial markets (particularly stock markets); and (v) generate spillover effects and heterogeneities. We corroborate our findings through shock identification, treating financial markets as conduits for the geopolitical risk shock. Additionally, we conduct a battery of robustness checks addressing structural breaks, time‐varying bilateral trade, and bilateral financial flows (instead of bilateral trade), all of which confirm the consistency of our results. We conclude by discussing fiscal policies aimed at counterbalancing the negative effects of geopolitical risk on energy transition and climate change, emphasizing the importance of international cooperation for the effectiveness of these policies.

title: Analysis of Beijing’s Energy Intensity Changes Based on an Input–Output Structural Decomposition Model from 2007 to 2020
summary: As China’s capital and a global megacity, Beijing has experienced sustained and rigid growth in energy demand driven by rapid population and economic expansion, rendering the analysis of energy intensity critically imperative for optimizing
content: As China’s capital and a global megacity, Beijing has experienced sustained and rigid growth in energy demand driven by rapid population and economic expansion, rendering the analysis of energy intensity critically imperative for optimizing its energy system, alleviating resource and environmental pressures, and advancing toward carbon neutrality. By constructing a long-term comparable-price series, this study applies multi-period comparative structural decomposition analysis (SDA) across five benchmark years, spanning major policy cycles. It disaggregates changes in energy intensity into energy technology, production technology, and final demand structure effects across six sectors and five energy categories. The principal findings are threefold. First, Beijing’s aggregate energy intensity exhibited a consistent downward trajectory, declining from 0.33699 tons of standard coal equivalent (tce) per 10,000 yuan in 2007 to 0.16393 tce per 10,000 yuan in 2020 (at constant 2012 prices). Second, the direct, indirect, and total energy consumption coefficients for all six sectors exhibited a broadly downward trend, with the largest reduction in the freight and postal sector, followed by industry. Third, energy technology change was the predominant driver of the decline in both aggregate energy intensity and consumption intensity across the five energy categories. Production technology and final demand structure changes exhibited heterogeneous effects across sectors and sub-periods. These findings provide policy-relevant insights for optimizing Beijing’s energy structure, and several targeted recommendations are proposed.

title: Sustainable Biochar Sorbents for Elemental Mercury Capture From Flue Gas: Review and Prospects
summary: ABSTRACT Elemental mercury (Hg 0 ), as the most dominant form of airborne mercury, is extremely hard to be captured because of its high volatility, aqueous insolubility, and thermal stability. Hg° capture from coal combustion, metallurgical
content: ABSTRACT Elemental mercury (Hg 0 ), as the most dominant form of airborne mercury, is extremely hard to be captured because of its high volatility, aqueous insolubility, and thermal stability. Hg° capture from coal combustion, metallurgical, and incineration flue gases is still challenging due to lack of cost‐efficient sorbents. Recently, biochar, as a sustainable and cost‐effective sorbent, has been extensively employed for Hg° capture due to its low price, natural abundance, renewability, carbon neutrality, and variety diversity. This review outlines the recent progress of Hg° capture by biochars in terms of biochar production, chemical activation, surface modification, and reaction mechanisms. Pristine biochar holds a lower Hg 0 adsorption activity. Chemical activation and surface modification can effectively reinforce the performance of the biochar due to improved porosity and augmented active species. Generally, the optimal mass ratio of activators to biomass is 2:1. Molten salt activation combined with sulfide modification or H 2 S plasma treatment is proposed as a prospective pathway to prepare high‐performance biochars. Mercury capture mechanisms of the biochars could likely be unraveled using theoretical calculation based on density functional theory (DFT).

title: Sanitizing the stain: a critical integrative review of sportswashing discourse
source: Qualitative Market Research An International Journal
summary: Purpose This paper aims to develop a marketing-oriented understanding of sportswashing by synthesizing its burgeoning, fragmented and cross-disciplinary scholarship through Mary Douglas’s anthropology of purity and pollution, explaining how
content: Purpose This paper aims to develop a marketing-oriented understanding of sportswashing by synthesizing its burgeoning, fragmented and cross-disciplinary scholarship through Mary Douglas’s anthropology of purity and pollution, explaining how sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a critical integrative review of 45 peer-reviewed articles, identified through systematic searches of major academic databases. After two-stage screening, the corpus was analyzed qualitatively from an interpretive stance, using thematic synthesis followed by abductive theorization. Findings This study first maps the sportswashing ecosystem − stains, actors, motivations, mechanisms, phases and outcomes − revealing complexity and tensions pervading the literature. Building on this synthesis, it identifies five cleansing logics through which sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process: separation, dilution, displacement, containment and sanctification. Each logic illuminates how sportswashing operates as a contest over cultural classification through association without explicit claims. Research limitations/implications This synthesis advances a research agenda for interpretive marketing and consumer research, highlighting what qualitative inquiry could reveal about sportswashing across consumer resistance, platformization of consumer culture, CSR-washing, macromarketing, branding and reputation, marketing communications, market systems and critical and postcolonial marketing. Originality/value This paper theorizes sportswashing as a symbolic purification process, extending the CSR-washing literature from deception to associative classificatory work. Its five cleansing logics connect marketing scholarship on sponsorship, reputation, meaning transfer and brand activism; show how fan meaning-making and consumer resistance become embroiled in cultural-political reputation management; and reframe sportswashing as a contest over cultural classification, resolving persistent conceptual tensions.

title: Impacts of Ground Deformation on Annual Vegetation Carbon Sequestration in an Underground Mining Area Based on Scenario Simulation via a CA Model
summary: Impacts of mining-induced ground deformation on annual vegetation carbon sequestration have seldom been detected considering long-term plant succession after subsidence. To address this, a subsidence in the semi-arid underground mine of Chi
content: Impacts of mining-induced ground deformation on annual vegetation carbon sequestration have seldom been detected considering long-term plant succession after subsidence. To address this, a subsidence in the semi-arid underground mine of China was selected, and dynamics of annual vegetation carbon sequestration under deformation and baseline scenarios were simulated via a developed plant community succession model based on cellular automata. Results showed that ground deformation constrained tree growth, leading to a gradual transition from the original arbor forest to mixed forest under the deformation scenario. Annual vegetation carbon sequestration increased under both the deformation and baseline scenarios, but remained consistently lower under the deformation scenario. Moreover, the difference in annual vegetation carbon sequestration between the two scenarios gradually increased with spontaneous succession, from 30.56 Mg C yr−1 after 5 years to 44.53 Mg C yr−1 after 30 years. Compared with the baseline scenario, the annual vegetation carbon sequestration under the deformation scenario in the study area decreased by 6.59% to 67.36%, and showed the highest decrease (56.85–67.36%) in the area with 1–2 m’ subsidence. With the increase in succession years, the decline degree of the annual vegetation carbon sequestration in the deeper subsidence area decreased, while that in the shallower subsidence area gradually increased. In general, ground deformation affects the natural growth and community succession of vegetation, leading to the gradual degradation of tree vegetation and the decline in annual vegetation carbon sequestration. This study provides a method for quantifying impacts of ground deformation on the annual vegetation carbon sequestration, and provides theoretical guidance for the construction of green mining under the “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals”.

title: Prioritizing transport decarbonization strategies in Nigeria: An intuitionistic fuzzy decision framework for energy transition policy
summary: Nigeria's transport sector is a major and growing source of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, largely because mobility remains heavily dependent on petroleum products. Efforts to shift toward low-carbon transport are hindered by economic, ins
content: Nigeria's transport sector is a major and growing source of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, largely because mobility remains heavily dependent on petroleum products. Efforts to shift toward low-carbon transport are hindered by economic, institutional, infrastructural, and technological constraints. This study develops an integrated decision framework for prioritizing these challenges and identifying suitable policy responses within Nigeria's wider energy transition. Drawing on the literature, national policy documents, and the judgments of six experts from academia, government, transport, and energy, the study evaluates eight decarbonization challenges and five policy alternatives. It proposes an Intuitionistic Fuzzy (IF) extension of the RANking COMparison method (IF-RANCOM) to determine the relative importance of the challenges while considering uncertainty and hesitation in expert judgments. The resulting weights are incorporated into an Intuitionistic Fuzzy Additive Ratio Assessment (IF-ARAS) model to evaluate the policy alternatives. Compromise Fuzzy Ranking (CFR) is then used to reconcile differences among expert assessments and produce a collective ranking. The findings identify Nigeria's economic dependence on petroleum as the most important barrier, followed by weak policy frameworks and planning, inadequate infrastructure and technological capacity, and the high cost of zero-emission vehicles. Promoting mass transit is ranked as the most suitable policy response. Comparative and sensitivity analyses reveal that the main rankings remain stable under different methodological assumptions and parameter settings. The findings demonstrate the need for coordinated investment in mass transit, integrated transport and land use planning, sustainable financing, infrastructure modernization, and institutional reform. The proposed framework may also support other fossil-fuel-dependent developing economies in aligning transport priorities with energy security, social inclusion, and long-term decarbonization goals.

title: Tuning Coordination Chemistry and Composition of Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient Hydrogen Production
summary: ABSTRACT Improving the cost and efficiency of hydrogen production via water splitting is a long‐standing research challenge in support of carbon neutrality goals. Optimising the structural composition and coordination chemistry of metal−org
content: ABSTRACT Improving the cost and efficiency of hydrogen production via water splitting is a long‐standing research challenge in support of carbon neutrality goals. Optimising the structural composition and coordination chemistry of metal−organic frameworks (MOFs) can yield suitable catalysts or supports that enhance hydrogen production efficiency. MOFs offer precise control over porosity, metal nodes and linker chemistry that is unattainable with conventional catalysts. This review provides a critical, cross‐cutting assessment of MOF‐based catalysis across electrochemical (EC) and photo(electro)chemical (PC and PEC) water‐splitting technologies. We systematically analyse how key structural features (ultrahigh porosity, surface area and compositional changes) and coordination chemistry (tunable metal active sites and functionalised linkers) govern catalytic activity and stability. For electrochemical systems, we critically examine the multifunctionality of pristine MOFs, their conductive carbon‐based derivatives and the synergistic performance of MOF/carbon and MOF/metal hybrids. For MOF‐driven PC and PEC water splitting, we examine MOF selectivity and the mechanisms of light absorption, charge separation and interfacial electron transfer that enable MOFs to serve as integrated platforms bridging light harvesting and redox catalysis. Notably, we devote dedicated sections to limitations in charge‐carrier dynamics and defect engineering, significant bottlenecks that are often overlooked yet key to future performance breakthroughs. A machine‐learning perspective is briefly included, with case studies presented as an emerging design tool for predicting hydrogen adsorption capacity and optimising hydrogen production activity via MOF‐based catalysts. Finally, the review concludes with targeted future directions aimed at accelerating the transition from laboratory discovery to practical, sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Wellhead stability during drilling in weakly consolidated marine hydrate-bearing sediments
summary: Natural gas hydrates are undoubtedly an important clean energy source in the future. However, its temperature sensitivity poses a significant challenge to the stability of the wellhead and wellbore during the drilling process of hydrate-bea
content: Natural gas hydrates are undoubtedly an important clean energy source in the future. However, its temperature sensitivity poses a significant challenge to the stability of the wellhead and wellbore during the drilling process of hydrate-bearing sediments. In this study, the evolution characteristics of key parameters, including hydrate dissociation, bearing capacity and wellhead displacement, were analyzed using a thermo-hydro-mechanical-chemical coupled model. The results show that hydrate dissociation leads to a ∼40% reduction in bearing capacity, resulting in a final wellhead displacement of 4.1 cm under the base case. Meanwhile, the effects of factors such as hydrate saturation and drilling fluid temperature on wellhead stability were then analyzed. It was found that higher hydrate saturation in sediment and lower drilling fluid temperature significantly enhances wellhead stability. Specifically, increasing hydrate saturation from 20% to 60% reduces the final wellhead displacement from 5.4 cm to 1.7 cm, while raising drilling fluid temperature from 15 °C to 30 °C increases displacement from <0.2 cm to 7.5 cm. Furthermore, the effectiveness of vacuum insulation casing in maintaining wellbore stability was numerically evaluated through numerical simulation. The simulation results indicate that, hydrate dissociation is almost completely suppressed, bearing capacity remains stable, and wellhead displacement is nearly 0 cm when vacuum insulation casing is employed. This study provides valuable guidance for ensuring the safe and efficient drilling operation in hydrate-bearing sediment.

title: EL-RAKHAWI UNIFIED FRAMEWORK FOR AI-OPTIMIZED MANGANESE METAMATERIALS IN DYNAMIC CARBON CAPTURE AND PHOTOCATALYTIC FUEL SYNTHESIS
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The El-Rakhawi Unified Framework for AI-Optimized Manganese Metamaterials solves the climate and energy crises. It replaces expensive rare-metal catalysts with earth-abundant manganese-based Metal-Organic Frameworks (Mn-MOFs). This system a
content: The El-Rakhawi Unified Framework for AI-Optimized Manganese Metamaterials solves the climate and energy crises. It replaces expensive rare-metal catalysts with earth-abundant manganese-based Metal-Organic Frameworks (Mn-MOFs). This system achieves dynamic carbon capture and photocatalytic fuel synthesis via four pillars: (1) Redox-active Mn-MOFs utilizing multi-valent Mn states for direct CO2-to-methanol conversion; (2) Dynamic spin-state modulation via pulsed electromagnetic fields to reconfigure d-orbital geometry and prevent catalyst poisoning; (3) Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) performing real-time, quantum-constrained optimization of light and field parameters; and (4) A closed-loop carbon-to-fuel cycle achieving >90% carbon utilization. By harmonizing quantum physics, materials, and AI, this framework proves manganese can achieve superior turnover frequencies and lifetimes exceeding five years, establishing a scalable, highly efficient, low-cost pathway to quantum-intelligent carbon neutrality.

title: Yield and energy efficiency tradeoffs in sweet sorghum under different nitrogen management strategies: Mineral vs. recycled organic fertilization
summary: Sweet sorghum [ Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] biomass production is a promising component of the bioeconomy that combines high productivity with the potential use of local resources and by-products from bioenergy processes. The aim of this s
content: Sweet sorghum [ Sorghum bicolor (L.) Moench] biomass production is a promising component of the bioeconomy that combines high productivity with the potential use of local resources and by-products from bioenergy processes. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of nitrogen (N) fertilization strategy and N rate on biomass yield and the energy balance of sweet sorghum grown for energy purposes. A field experiment was conducted in northeastern Poland in 2023–2025. Nitrogen was applied at six rates (0, 40, 80, 120, 160, and 200 kg N ha −1 ) either as a mineral fertilizer (MF, ammonium nitrate) or a recycled organic fertilizer (digestate, DG). Production performance was assessed based on dry matter yield (DMY), total energy inputs (E-IN), energy output (E-OUT), energy gain (E-GAIN), and the energy efficiency ratio (E-ER). An increase in N rates led to a significant increase in DMY, although the effective response range was differentiated by the type of fertilizer. In the MF-based system, DMY increased significantly up to 160 kg N ha −1 , whereas in the DG-based production technology, DMY increased up to 120 kg N ha −1 . Mineral fertilization resulted in higher DMY as well as higher E-OUT and E-GAIN across all N rates, and the maximum E-GAIN was achieved at 160 kg N ha −1 . The replacement of MF with DG reduced DMY (by 15–33%, depending on the N rate), but also significantly decreased total E-IN (by 40–44%). Consequently, E-ER was markedly higher (by 29–34%) in the DG-based production technology than in the MF-based system. The highest E-ER values were obtained at low to moderate N rates applied as DG (40–80 kg N ha −1 ). The study demonstrated that the choice of N fertilization strategy should be determined by the production objective: maximizing biomass yield and E-GAIN or improving energy efficiency and the overall sustainability of the production system.

title: Innovation frameworks for energy‑efficient building renovation in Spain: an integrated perspective on energy, materials and people
summary: This paper develops an integrated framework for innovation in large‑scale building renovation in Spain, grounded in a national study commissioned by the Ministry of Housing. Innovation is articulated across three interdependent domains—ener
content: This paper develops an integrated framework for innovation in large‑scale building renovation in Spain, grounded in a national study commissioned by the Ministry of Housing. Innovation is articulated across three interdependent domains—energy, materials and people—so as to move beyond technology‑centric views of energy efficiency. Methodologically, the study combines a transversal review of 16 strategic and regulatory documents (2020–2024), climatic modelling based on Spanish Building Code (CTE) zones and IPCC scenarios (SSP2‑4.5/SSP5‑8.5) for five representative cities (Almería, Las Palmas, Valencia, Madrid, Burgos), life‑cycle and circularity criteria for materials, and a people‑centered lens addressing habitability, adaptive comfort and vulnerability. Results show a generalized reduction in heating needs and a sharp increase in cooling demand towards mid‑century, underscoring the priority of climate‑adaptive passive measures and hybrid strategies. As operational emissions decline, embodied carbon becomes a decisive frontier—calling for reversible construction (ISO 20887), modularity, reuse, and material passports. Social dimensions are central to effective renovation: around one fifth of Spanish households experience energy poverty, so user agency, equitable processes and accessible information are necessary conditions for performance persistence. Building on these insights, the research assembles a technical catalogue of 75 solutions classified by scale, maturity, environmental performance and climatic suitability. The framework thus provides a method to prioritize context‑specific packages that jointly address demand reduction, circular material flows and people‑centered outcomes, and it offers actionable principles for Spain’s forthcoming National Building Renovation Plan (PNRE 2026)..

title: An Introduction to Methods to Quantify Carbon Dynamics in Rangeland Ecosystems
summary: ABSTRACT Rangeland ecosystems store substantial terrestrial carbon and contribute to climate mitigation, yet their spatial heterogeneity, dynamic disturbance regimes, and multiple carbon pools make accurate quantification challenging. This
content: ABSTRACT Rangeland ecosystems store substantial terrestrial carbon and contribute to climate mitigation, yet their spatial heterogeneity, dynamic disturbance regimes, and multiple carbon pools make accurate quantification challenging. This introduction outlines and compares methodological approaches for measuring aboveground biomass, soil organic carbon, and fire-derived pyrogenic carbon across rangelands, with emphasis on how sampling design, sensor platforms, modeling frameworks, and accounting tools scale across ecological gradients. We outline field-based protocols, remote sensing technologies, process-based simulators, and machine learning upscaling strategies, highlighting trade-offs in resolution, cost, uncertainty, and spatial-temporal coverage. Particular attention is given to how these methods complement one another across spatial and temporal scales, including the conversion factors and sampling assumptions used to translate biomass estimates into carbon stocks. We then compare practical considerations across spatial and temporal scales to guide method selection, and connect them to rangeland carbon accounting, monitoring, and management by showing how method selection influences assessment reliability and outcomes. By integrating ecological insight, technological innovation, and standardized measurement, this overview provides a practical foundation for designing robust monitoring programs and reducing uncertainty in rangeland carbon assessments.

title: Dedicated Hybrid Engines: Pathways from Otto Cycle to beyond 50% BTE
summary: Dedicated Hybrid Engines (DHEs) represent a paradigm shift: engine’s purpose designed to operate within electrified powertrains, enabling them to achieve brake thermal efficiencies (BTE) of 45% and beyond – a level once considered unattaina
content: Dedicated Hybrid Engines (DHEs) represent a paradigm shift: engine’s purpose designed to operate within electrified powertrains, enabling them to achieve brake thermal efficiencies (BTE) of 45% and beyond – a level once considered unattainable for spark ignition (SI) engines. This chapter traces the technological evolution from the classic Otto cycle to today’s highly optimized DHEs. It explains how the Atkinson/Miller cycle, combined with advanced combustion strategies such as lean burn, cooled exhaust gas recirculation, and prechamber ignition, synergize with hybrid electrification to dramatically improve efficiency. Key enabling technologies – including high compression ratio, friction reduction, thermal management, and novel ignition systems – are examined through industrial case studies. It discusses the compatibility of DHEs with carbon neutral fuels (ethanol, synthetic fuels, hydrogen, etc.), positioning them as a cornerstone of sustainable mobility well into the future. Furthermore, data oriented approach for controls is explored to tackle uncertain dynamics through physics informed neural network (PINN) to further raise the engine performance. This chapter directly addresses the book’s core themes: Internal combustion engine design – focusing on DHEs optimized for hybrid operations; combustion technologies – covering prechamber ignition, advanced ignition systems, and controls; low carbon and alternative fuels – discussing ethanol, and hydrogen; engine controls with application of PINN. The chapter builds on the authors’ industrial and academic expertise, integrates recent research, and provides a forward looking perspective that will be valuable for researchers, engineers, and policymakers.

title: China’s Socialist Market Economy with Chinese Characteristics: A PESTEL Analysis
summary: This chapter applies the PESTEL framework political, economic, social, technological, environmental, and legal factors to China’s contemporary business environment, written for international executives, founders, and investors. It argues th
content: This chapter applies the PESTEL framework political, economic, social, technological, environmental, and legal factors to China’s contemporary business environment, written for international executives, founders, and investors. It argues that China operates as a hybrid system in which Party authority, industrial policy, and an increasingly assertive regulatory state jointly structure commercial life, so that law and politics cannot be read in isolation. The discussion situates market opportunity within this institutional setting: political signals shape market access; social structures, including the hukou system and the Social Credit System, shape labor and compliance; technological policy drives innovation and data governance; environmental codification reframes compliance as industrial policy; and a fast-moving, state-centric legal regime turns regulatory fluency into strategic advantage. Rather than treating these dimensions as separate risks, the chapter presents them as interconnected conditions of operating in China, providing the practical context for the more detailed legal and regulatory analysis developed in subsequent chapters.

title: Optimising Cold Chain Warehousing Through Autonomous Robotics, IoT Monitoring and Intelligent Inventory Management in Saudi Arabia's Food Distribution Sector
summary: Cold-chain warehouses are expected to preserve food safety while meeting increasingly variable distribution demand. Yet robotics, environmental monitoring and inventory software are often assessed independently, leaving the mechanisms throu
content: Cold-chain warehouses are expected to preserve food safety while meeting increasingly variable distribution demand. Yet robotics, environmental monitoring and inventory software are often assessed independently, leaving the mechanisms through which their integration affects product quality insufficiently explained. This critical integrative review synthesises 30 DOI-identifiable publications from 2020–2025 and interprets their relevance to Saudi Arabian food distribution. Its aim is to develop a safety-led operating model linking autonomous material handling, connected temperature evidence, remaining shelf-life estimation and stock allocation. The review distinguishes demonstrated findings from proposed applications, compares technical and organisational constraints, and identifies measurable implementation requirements. The synthesis indicates that robotic throughput is valuable only when product release decisions remain governed by validated temperature histories, traceability and quality rules. A proposed layered architecture connects sensors, warehouse systems, predictive models and supervised robotic execution. An associated performance framework balances temperature excursions, expiry losses, service reliability, worker safety and refrigeration energy. Saudi deployment priorities include heat-resilient infrastructure, segregated food categories, reliable connectivity, verifiable data governance and staged piloting. Evidence for integrated implementations in Saudi facilities remains limited; consequently, claims of productivity or waste reduction require local field validation rather than extrapolation from unrelated warehouses.

title: Diastereoselective Synthesis of Indane Scaffolds via Acid‐Mediated Cascade Cyclization
summary: Indanes are privileged bicyclic architectures in bioactive molecules and are ubiquitous in many pharmaceuticals and natural products. A simple, efficient acid‐mediated domino reaction between o ‐cinnamylated chalcones and 2,6‐diisopropylphe
content: Indanes are privileged bicyclic architectures in bioactive molecules and are ubiquitous in many pharmaceuticals and natural products. A simple, efficient acid‐mediated domino reaction between o ‐cinnamylated chalcones and 2,6‐diisopropylphenol leading to indanes is reported. The reaction proceeds stereoselectively to furnish a highly diastereoselective indane possessing three consecutive stereocenters in good to excellent yields (up to 91%). This approach applies to a wide range of chalcones and is easy to operate. An initial intramolecular cyclization triggered by the nucleophilic double bond of o‐cinnamyl group onto β‐position of enone part of chalcone moiety followed by an intermolecular Friedel–Crafts reaction of 2,6‐diisopropylphenol with incipient carbocation furnished the final product. The remarkable diastereocontrol may be attributed to steric factors.

title: NBD-Net: A structured degradation memory and local-global bridging network for lithium-ion battery remaining useful life prediction
summary: Abstract Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of lithium-ion batteries from measured capacity is a core function of battery management, but public datasets contain few cells, a predictor must generalize to unseen cells, and training cells
content: Abstract Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of lithium-ion batteries from measured capacity is a core function of battery management, but public datasets contain few cells, a predictor must generalize to unseen cells, and training cells often miss the late-life regime. This paper proposes NBD-Net, a Nonstationary-Bridged Degradation Network for next-cycle capacity prediction, and examines which elements make it reliable on unseen cells. NBD-Net normalizes each input window (RevIN), encodes it with a local stabilization branch, a causal detrending followed by learned causal convolutions, in parallel with a recurrent trend encoder, and couples the two branches through an attention memory (SDMC) and a bidirectional cross-attention bridge (LGBI). Under a leave-one-battery-out protocol covering all eleven cells of the CALCE, NASA, and TJU datasets, NBD-Net has the lowest capacity RMSE of nine models on every unseen cell, 9%–27% below the strongest baseline of each dataset, also after nested tuning of all models. When the training cells cover only the first half of life, it remains the most accurate model on every cell, and its error grows by 29% where that of PatchTST and TCN grows by 160% and 222%. Controlled experiments attribute these two results to different elements: with complete training data the per-window normalization carries the advantage, lowering the error by 22%–34% on every cell, so that a normalized recurrent predictor reaches comparable accuracy; with incomplete training data the local stabilization branch provides 84% of the gain over the recurrent backbone, whereas SDMC and LGBI add smaller gains at regeneration events and in late life. The results hold for next-cycle prediction under one cycling condition per dataset; its RUL relative error statistically matches that of the baselines, and its accuracy gain holds while input noise stays comparable to the scatter of the training data. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/luxing-just/NBDNet_open_source.

title: MICROPLASTIC WASTE TO FUNCTIONAL CARBON MATERIALS
source: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
summary: Microplastic pollution is a persistent environmental challenge due to the widespread distribution, chemical stability, and continuous generation of polymeric particles smaller than 5 mm.Instead of relying only on separation, filtration, or
content: Microplastic pollution is a persistent environmental challenge due to the widespread distribution, chemical stability, and continuous generation of polymeric particles smaller than 5 mm.Instead of relying only on separation, filtration, or destruction, microplastics can be considered carbon-rich secondary feedstocks for producing functional carbon materials, linking plastic-waste management with green chemistry and circular-economy principles.Technologies such as pyrolysis, hydrothermal carbonization, catalytic carbonization, microwave processing, flash Joule heating, and plasma conversion can transform polymeric waste into porous carbons, activated carbons, graphene-like materials, carbon nanotubes, and carbon dots for applications in adsorption, photocatalysis, advanced oxidation, CO₂ capture, and electrochemical treatment.However, feedstock heterogeneity, additives, halogen-containing polymers, energy demand, chemical activation, contaminant transfer, and material safety remain important challenges.This review critically examines microplastic-to-carbon conversion, polymer-carbon property relationships, environmental applications, regeneration, end-of-life management, and life-cycle assessment.A future framework integrating selective recovery, low-energy conversion, safer activation, multifunctional remediation, AI-assisted materials design, and circular life-cycle assessment is proposed to shift microplastic management from a linear "capture-and-dispose" model toward a circular "recover-convert-remediate-regenerate" strategy.

title: Uncovering the Structural Drivers of Carbon Emissions in Malaysia: Energy Demand vs. Macroeconomic Determinants
summary: Rapid industrialization and urbanization in Malaysia have driven substantial economic expansion alongside a sharp escalation in carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, creating a major policy tension regarding its commitment to reduce carbon intens
content: Rapid industrialization and urbanization in Malaysia have driven substantial economic expansion alongside a sharp escalation in carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions, creating a major policy tension regarding its commitment to reduce carbon intensity by 45% by 2030. This study examines the symmetric and asymmetric long-term relationships, cointegration, and dynamic causality among GDP, energy consumption, renewable energy, urbanization, industrialization, and CO2 emissions within a unified dynamic framework. Empirical results reveal that energy consumption is the sole statistically significant driver of Malaysia's long-run carbon emissions, whereas GDP, renewable energy, urbanization, and industrialization exert no statistically significant direct impact. Crucially, the statistical insignificance of GDP refutes the applicability of the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis in Malaysia, demonstrating that higher income levels will not automatically induce environmental recovery past a specific development threshold. Therefore, policymakers cannot rely on passive economic growth to achieve sustainability. To effectively decouple economic progress from carbon output, national frameworks must move beyond income-driven assumptions and implement targeted interventions focused on direct energy demand management, fossil fuel subsidy reforms, and aggressive clean-energy substitution.

title: Nadir Toprak Element Potansiyeli Açısından Jeotermal Kaynaklar
summary: "Global carbon neutrality targets, the pressure of digitalization, and the green energy transition are rapidly increasing the demand for Rare Earth Elements (REEs), which are indispensable inputs for advanced technology and the defense indu
content: "Global carbon neutrality targets, the pressure of digitalization, and the green energy transition are rapidly increasing the demand for Rare Earth Elements (REEs), which are indispensable inputs for advanced technology and the defense industry. This situation has triggered the search for alternative raw materials to break geographical monopolies in the supply chain, making geothermal fluids, enriched with certain elements through water-rock interaction under high temperature and pressure conditions, strategic resources. The concentration of REEs in geothermal fluids develops under the control of environmental factors such as fluid pH, reservoir temperature, salinity (chloride/sulfate complexes), and the geochemical composition of the interacting reservoir rock. Industrialscale licensing and pilot production projects for the recovery of critical metals such as lithium (Li) and europium (Eu) from geothermal fluids are being carried out in areas such as Salton Sea (USA), Upper Rhine Graben (France-Germany), and Hellisheidi (Iceland). Türkiye, situated on the Alpine-Himalayan tectonic belt, has approximately 1000 natural geothermal resources in various regions. With an installed electricity generation capacity of 1797 MWe by 2025, Türkiye ranks 4th in the world in geothermal electricity production. Despite the creation of high added value through integrated applications ranging from residential/greenhouse heating to industrial liquid CO2 production across the country, no commercially viable REE has yet been encountered in the studies conducted in the operational fields. This study examines the formation mechanisms of REE in geothermal systems and global extraction technologies, and evaluates target geothermal fields in Türkiye that possess economic REE potential. It is shown that future REE exploration strategies in geothermal fields should focus on deep-circulating fluid-rock interaction areas in the Central Anatolian Crystalline Complex, where alkaline magmatism extends, and in the alkaline volcanics of the Kula and Selendi regions in Western Anatolia, as well as in the granitic intrusions of the Çanakkale-Kestanbol region. Geothermal legal regulation is crucial for utilization of geothermal resources as extraction of precious metal as well as renewable energy."

title: Power-reduction detection and classification in photovoltaic modules using clustering of parametric deviations
summary: Power reduction in photovoltaic modules may be caused by environmental conditions, faults, and degradation mechanisms, whose correct identification is essential to improve the reliability, safety, and energy yield of photovoltaic systems. T
content: Power reduction in photovoltaic modules may be caused by environmental conditions, faults, and degradation mechanisms, whose correct identification is essential to improve the reliability, safety, and energy yield of photovoltaic systems. This article proposes a classification approach for power-reduction scenarios based on parametric deviations extracted from a Global Nonlinear Model (GNLM) derived from the Single-Diode Model (SDM). The methodology starts with the construction of a GNLM representative of a healthy reference photovoltaic module, capable of describing its electrical behavior under different irradiance and temperature conditions. For each evaluated experimental current–voltage ( I–V ) curve, selected SDM parameters associated with this healthy reference model are adjusted to approximate the electrical behavior of the analyzed module. The deviations required for this adjustment, calculated with respect to the healthy reference condition, are used as diagnostic markers for clustering-based classification. Different power-reduction conditions were evaluated, including soiling, short-circuited bypass diodes, open-diode conditions under different shading levels, front-glass breakage, and partial shading (PS). To reduce the overlap between scenarios with distinct electrical behaviors, the samples were initially separated according to the number of maxima in the power–voltage ( P–V ) curve, denoted by N peak , distinguishing cases with N peak = 1 from those with N peak > 1 . Based on these diagnostic markers, two strategies are investigated according to the set of SDM parameters used in the classification process. Strategy 1 uses deviations in the diode ideality factor ( n ) and photogenerated current ( I p h ), achieving the best performance, with an overall accuracy of 99.6%. Strategy 2 uses deviations in the n , series resistance ( R s ), and shunt resistance ( R s h ), achieving an overall accuracy of 98.3%.

title: Multiscale Interfacial Engineering Enables Robust Reconstituted Wood
summary: ABSTRACT Development of sustainable, high‐performance structural materials capable of replacing traditional engineering plastics and lightweight alloys is critical to achieving carbon neutrality. However, engineering renewable wood into str
content: ABSTRACT Development of sustainable, high‐performance structural materials capable of replacing traditional engineering plastics and lightweight alloys is critical to achieving carbon neutrality. However, engineering renewable wood into structural materials intrinsically relies on reconstitution and bonding, during which traditional polymer adhesives introduce compositionally and mechanically heterogeneous interfaces. These discontinuities produce stress concentrations under water‐induced swelling and shrinkage, undermining long‐term stability. Herein, we proposed a synergistic strategy integrating interfacial reconstruction and water‐induced regeneration to reconstruct heterogeneous interfaces into homogeneous ones with compositional and structural continuity. This approach enabled lap joints to achieve a high dry shear strength of 6.2 MPa, exceeding that of natural wood. Notably, this strategy utilized water to facilitate the regeneration and performance retention of the interface, allowing the material to retain 97% of its strength even after two boiling water cycles. Furthermore, the mechanical properties were optimized through pressure control, thereby yielding specific flexural strength (276.2 MPa cm 3 g −1 ) and specific flexural modulus (24 000 MPa cm 3 g −1 ) that were comparable or even superior to those of certain metals, construction materials, and engineering plastics. This work provides useful insights into the design of high‐performance, sustainable wood‐based structural materials suitable for outdoor environments.

title: Electrolyte Solvation Chemistry and Systemic Safety in Potassium‐Ion Batteries
summary: Potassium‐ion batteries (KIBs) are a leading candidate for low‐cost energy storage, yet their commercial viability hinges on full cell stability and thermal safety rather than the half cell metrics that dominate the literature. Both are gov
content: Potassium‐ion batteries (KIBs) are a leading candidate for low‐cost energy storage, yet their commercial viability hinges on full cell stability and thermal safety rather than the half cell metrics that dominate the literature. Both are governed by the electrolyte. This review examines recent KIB progress through electrolyte solvation chemistry and its control over the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), showing how salt and solvent selection dictate sheath composition and whether an anion‐ or solvent‐derived interphase forms. Studies are sorted by whether the solvation structure was characterized, separating electrolytes that are adopted, formulated for a bulk property, or engineered at the sheath. The division is sharpest among the anodes: every solvation‐engineered study uses unmodified commercial graphite, while adopted‐electrolyte studies reach for modified carbons and conversion anodes, placing their engineering on opposite sides of the interface. Thermal safety proves interfacial rather than a bulk‐solvent problem, as nonflammable electrolytes still drive a low‐temperature anode‐initiated exotherm that interphase stabilization delays more effectively than nonflammability alone. That conclusion rests on a narrow base, since all available calorimetry uses potassiated graphite. We identify the half cell‐to‐full cell gap and interphase‐mediated capacity loss as the central obstacles to practical KIBs.

title: Regulating Platinum Utilization and Intrinsic Hydrogen Evolution Activity via Carbon Pore Architecture
summary: Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a key process for sustainable hydrogen production. However, its practical implementation remains limited by the high cost and inefficient utilization of platinum (Pt). Here, we investigated the influence
content: Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a key process for sustainable hydrogen production. However, its practical implementation remains limited by the high cost and inefficient utilization of platinum (Pt). Here, we investigated the influence of carbon pore architecture on Pt dispersion and intrinsic catalytic activity using a series of porous carbons spanning narrow mesoporous (MH and MH‐18; 2–5 nm), wider mesoporous (MJ010 and MJ030; 10–40 nm), and macroporous (MJ150; ~110 nm) frameworks. Pt nanoparticles formed via microwave‐assisted polyol reduction showed uniform nucleation. Macroporous MJ150 stabilizes ~2.3 nm Pt nanoparticles while preserving porosity, whereas narrow mesoporous carbons promote confinement and pore blockage, with XRD/Raman confirming higher crystallinity. XPS further shows a dominant metallic Pt 0 state with minimal Pt–O interactions on the macroporous support. Electrochemical measurements reveal that Pt/MJ150 exhibits superior HER performance, delivering an overpotential of 20 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , and higher mass activity than commercial Pt/C. C dl , ECSA, ICP‐OES, durability, post‐HER XRD and XPS measurements confirm improved active‐site accessibility and Pt utilization, through mass transport. Overall, this study shows a clear structural–property–performance relationship, where macroporous carbon supports enable efficient Pt utilization at low loading provide a scalable strategy for HER.

title: When Is POME a Residue? Definitional Boundaries, Carbon Accounting and Policy Integrity in Sustainable Aviation Fuel
source: Journal of Business Research and Reports
summary: This qualitative literature review examines the definitional controversy surrounding palm oil mill effluent (POME) and its recovered oil as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) feedstocks. Drawing on 52 cited peer-reviewed journal articles from
content: This qualitative literature review examines the definitional controversy surrounding palm oil mill effluent (POME) and its recovered oil as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) feedstocks. Drawing on 52 cited peer-reviewed journal articles from 2020–2026 and official ICAO and certification documents, it distinguishes unavoidable wastewater, genuinely recovered residual lipids and deliberately diverted primary palm oil. The review interprets the CORSIA POME-HEFA default core lifecycle value of 18.1 g CO₂e/MJ, derived from two modelling estimates, without conflating its assigned indirect land-use change treatment with measured system-wide climate effects. Five thematic findings concern classification boundaries, model-dependent emissions, wastewater methane interactions, plausible recovered-oil supplies and an auditable chain of custody. An origin-and-function framework is proposed to preserve legitimate feedstock eligibility while preventing inappropriate relabelling, duplicate emissions claims and undocumented changes in oil flows. The discussion differentiates official fuel lifecycle accounting from supplementary assessment of methane management and displaced product markets. It recommends mill-level mass balances, independent verification, measured conversion inputs and an adaptive Indonesian policy roadmap. Definitional precision is necessary for regulatory credibility, but cannot substitute for reliable environmental performance or certified fuel production

title: Enabling Shared Mobility Through Policy Innovation: A Scalable Approach for European Cities
summary: Abstract Shared mobility is central to sustainable urban transport, but its adoption across Europe requires strong policy support. This paper draws on recommendations from the GEMINI project, which supports eight cities in deploying New Mob
content: Abstract Shared mobility is central to sustainable urban transport, but its adoption across Europe requires strong policy support. This paper draws on recommendations from the GEMINI project, which supports eight cities in deploying New Mobility Services (NMS). Based on shared learning sessions, co-creation workshops, and structured partner engagement, we identify key themes shaping the implementation and scaling of NMS. First, we examine policy drivers and barriers influencing car-, bike−/e-scooter-sharing and Mobility as a Commons (MaaC) across local, national, and EU levels. Second, we investigate how NMS can be more effectively embedded into Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans (SUMPs), proposing updates to planning processes and document structures. Third, we assess technological and data-related challenges, focusing on how improved data sharing can strengthen shared services. Finally, we highlight enablers for adoption, including capacity-building, communication, behaviour change, and citizen engagement. Findings show that success relies not only on infrastructure and technology but equally on behavioural change and local adaptation to ensure accessibility and equity. Aligning shared mobility with public transport, SUMPs, and effective data coordination is critical. Insights will inform policy roadmaps and a practical handbook to help cities design and manage shared mobility tailored to local contexts.

title: The integrated environmental zoning-based regulation further enhances sustainable development in China
summary: Ecological degradation and environmental pollution have posed persistent obstacles to sustainable development. To address those rising challenges, the Chinese government initiated an integrated environmental zoning-based regulation (EZR) in
content: Ecological degradation and environmental pollution have posed persistent obstacles to sustainable development. To address those rising challenges, the Chinese government initiated an integrated environmental zoning-based regulation (EZR) in 2017.
