title: UPLOTS: A Unified Pretrained Language Model for Constrained Time-series Generation
source: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
summary: In time-series generation, existing approaches typically handcraft ortrain a separate model for each dataset, which hinders their scalability and fails to leverage shared temporal structures across domains. To address this fragmentation, we
content: In time-series generation, existing approaches typically handcraft ortrain a separate model for each dataset, which hinders their scalability and fails to leverage shared temporal structures across domains. To address this fragmentation, we propose UPLOTS, a Unified, Prompt-guided Language model framework fOr constrained Time-Series Generation across diverse domains. Instead of building task-specific models, UPLOTS leverages a single pre-trained transformer backbone guided by learned constraint prompts, enabling on-demand generation with precise pattern control. One key innovation is our dynamic multi-dataset loss re-weighting and prompt-to-pattern mapping, which allows UPLOTS to internalize diverse temporal structures during training and conditionally generate them at inference. We evaluate UPLOTS on four real-world benchmarks and multiple constraint settings, including peak-period, calendar, load-level, and volatility patterns. Additional held-out constraint-combination and downstream forecasting experiments further demonstrate that UPLOTS generalizes beyond the original peak-pattern setting and improves data augmentation under scarce real-data regimes. Our code and baselines are available at github repo: https://github.com/cruiseresearchgroup/UPLOTS.

title: LithoFormer: A Robust Framework for Stratigraphic Inference via Geology-Informed Multi-Task Transformers
source: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
summary: Accurate geological characterization of subsurface reservoirs from well log data is essential to support projects such as carbon capture and storage (CCS), geothermal development, and extraction of natural resources. Existing automated tech
content: Accurate geological characterization of subsurface reservoirs from well log data is essential to support projects such as carbon capture and storage (CCS), geothermal development, and extraction of natural resources. Existing automated techniques for geological characterization primarily use sliding-window classification, which limits their ability to understand broader geological contexts, often leading to misaligned formation layers. To overcome these limitations, we introduce LithoFormer, a robust framework for stratigraphic inference using a Seq2Seq transformer model that ingests entire multivariate well logs in a single pass. The framework utilizes a channel-independent PatchTST backbone enhanced with rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) to capture long-range geological dependencies across entire multivariate well logs. A decoupled multi-task head is employed to jointly predict geological zonation and precise boundary probabilities, while a geology-informed loss function enforces physical constraints such as the Law of Superposition. Validated and deployed on three real-world datasets, LithoFormer demonstrates a 90% reduction in median boundary error and eliminates stratigraphic order violations compared to traditional sliding-window baselines. It also achieves a 80% reduction in manual expert labor and eliminates stratigraphic inconsistencies, providing a scalable and reliable solution for large-scale subsurface modeling.

title: Continuous harvesting of intermittent and continuous heats by a mixed ion/electron thermoelectric generator using an ionogel blended with carbon nanotubes
summary: Abstract Ionic thermoelectric (TE) materials have drawn considerable interest because their thermopower can far exceed that of conventional electronic TE materials. They are typically implemented in ionic thermoelectric capacitors (ITECs) f
content: Abstract Ionic thermoelectric (TE) materials have drawn considerable interest because their thermopower can far exceed that of conventional electronic TE materials. They are typically implemented in ionic thermoelectric capacitors (ITECs) for heat harvesting. However, ITECs can harvest only intermittent heat, and there is no electricity generation under steady temperature. Here, we demonstrate a mixed ion/electron thermoelectric generator (MTEG) that can continuously harvest both intermittent and continuous heats into electricity. The active layer is an ionogel blended with single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs), forming a mixed conductor in which the ionic liquid enables ion transport while the SWNT network provides electronically conductive pathways. Under a constant temperature gradient, the MTEG delivers a stable output voltage to an external load, closely resembling the behavior of conventional thermoelectric generators. The thermopower exceeds 11.3 mV·K − 1 , which is 1–2 orders of magnitude higher than the Seebeck coefficient of the best electronic TE materials. This operation is attributed to synergistic effects: hole tunneling across the SWNT network coupled with the large ionic thermopower arising from the Soret effect.

title: When Persona Simulations Are Informative: Graph-Structured Signals for Pluralistic Opinion Sensing
source: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
summary: Persona-conditioned large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate survey responses across diverse domains. However, apparent response variation can reflect unconditioned model priors or token sampling noise rather than syst
content: Persona-conditioned large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate survey responses across diverse domains. However, apparent response variation can reflect unconditioned model priors or token sampling noise rather than systematic persona conditioning. We argue that persona-conditioned variation is informative when semantically similar personas exhibit concordant response shifts. To operationalize this principle, we introduce Persona-Conditioned Informativeness (PCI), an unsupervised diagnostic metric that measures whether semantically similar personas deviate in concordant directions relative to item-level sample baselines. By modeling personas as a similarity graph, PCI uses Local Moran's I to quantify local spatial coherence and extract compact persona subsets without using construct labels. To evaluate PCI without external human benchmarks, we test its ability to recover established latent value structure using the 57-item Portrait Values Questionnaire-Revised (PVQ-RR). Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) shows that a PCI-selected 10% subset substantially improves overall construct recovery relative to response-stability and random selection. These findings support PCI as a principled internal diagnostic for screening synthetic respondents in survey pipelines.

title: Differential methanogenic archaea-induced TLR8-dependent signaling engages gene classes regulated by NF-κB p65 and STAT1/2
summary: Abstract Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared imm
content: Abstract Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. Conserved early-upregulated genes separated into Class I genes, preferentially induced by M. stadtmanae , and Class II genes, similarly induced by both. M. stadtmanae showed greater early uptake, while responses to both archaea were broadly TLR8-dependent. ChIP-qPCR linked the stronger Class I gene activation induced by M. stadtmanae to greater NF-κB p65 binding at Class I promoters, whereas STAT1/2 binding at Class II promoters occurred with both stimuli. Dose-response analyses with archaeal RNA inputs supported distinct activation thresholds, with Class II genes at lower input and Class I genes requiring higher input. Together, these findings support an input-tuned TLR8-dependent mechanism shaping differential immune programs towards archaea.

title: Real-time dual-telescope normalization for improved density estimation in absorption muography
summary: Absorption muography infers path-averaged density from the attenuation of atmospheric muons. Transient flux variations driven by weather, solar activity, and geomagnetism bias sequential measurements that rely on a non-simultaneous backgrou
content: Absorption muography infers path-averaged density from the attenuation of atmospheric muons. Transient flux variations driven by weather, solar activity, and geomagnetism bias sequential measurements that rely on a non-simultaneous background. Here we show a real-time dual-telescope normalization in which two identical plastic-scintillator telescopes operate in parallel, one viewing open sky as a reference and one viewing the target. Their count-rate ratio cancels common-mode flux changes and tracks detector drift. A 140-h no-target run yields a stable calibration, and stacked acrylic slabs give an empirical transmission–thickness curve. Applied to blind targets, the dual-telescope workflow recovers the densities of 20-cm aluminum and 10-cm stainless-steel blocks within uncertainties, whereas a single-telescope workflow shows systematic biases of +18.95% and −22.82%. A vertical stack of the two telescopes further improves common-mode rejection, reducing calibration ratio scatter from 7.6% to 3.3%. The method is model-independent, removes systematic density biases in any campaign where a simultaneous flux reference is feasible, and is directly applicable to field deployments.

title: Uncovering the unseen: a multi-scalar scoping review of short-term rentals and urban transformation
summary: Abstract This critical scoping review examines how short-term rentals (STRs) have transformed urban tourism research and proposes an integrated sustainability framework bridging economic, social, spatial, and governance dimensions. Building
content: Abstract This critical scoping review examines how short-term rentals (STRs) have transformed urban tourism research and proposes an integrated sustainability framework bridging economic, social, spatial, and governance dimensions. Building on PRISMA-ScR guidelines, it systematically maps 161 studies published between 2009 and 2025, identifying key patterns in the economic, environmental, spatial, and regulatory analysis of STRs. The findings reveal that while STRs foster tourism growth and local development, they also exacerbate housing unaffordability, gentrification, and overtourism. The literature remains dominated by data-driven methods, spatial analysis, econometric modelling, and machine learning yet exhibits strong geographic biases and limited integration across disciplines. Results highlight the growing professionalisation of hosts, the role of digital technologies in reshaping governance, and the urgent need for adaptive, sustainability-oriented regulation. By consolidating fragmented debates, this review offers a multidimensional synthesis that informs smart city planning, digital governance, and the pursuit of the Sustainable Development Goals in contemporary tourism destinations.

title: Borrelia burgdorferi binds serum amyloid A and modulates subcutaneous adipose tissue immune signaling
summary: ABSTRACT Following a tick bite, Borrelia burgdorferi spirochetes replicate in human skin and disseminate through tissues, including subcutaneous adipose tissue. Adipose is a complex organ containing both immune and non-immune cells that pla
content: ABSTRACT Following a tick bite, Borrelia burgdorferi spirochetes replicate in human skin and disseminate through tissues, including subcutaneous adipose tissue. Adipose is a complex organ containing both immune and non-immune cells that play a significant role in the immune response, yet little is known about adipose-specific immune signaling after B. burgdorferi infection. We investigated the landscape of immune signaling within adipose tissue-resident cells during B. burgdorferi infection in human tissue (skin and adipose tissue) ex vivo . Single-cell sequencing pathway analysis revealed upregulation of inflammatory pathways in skin, yet overall downregulation of immune pathways in adipose tissue cells during B. burgdorferi infection. Adipose-resident myeloid cells and adipose stem/progenitor cells (ASPCs) displayed an inflammatory profile characterized by the increased expression of IL-1β, TNF, and NFKB1. CellChat, a cellular communication comparative analysis, showed increased cell-to-cell communication across adipose-resident cell populations. ASPCs demonstrated the strongest outgoing signals, positioning them as key hubs of intercellular communication in adipose tissue. Interestingly, we observed adipose-specific downregulation of serum amyloid A (SAA), an inflammatory serum marker known to have antimicrobial properties and typically elevated in Lyme disease patients during acute infection. Therefore, we further evaluated the interaction between SAA and B. burgdorferi . Here, we show that human recombinant SAA protein directly binds B. burgdorferi spirochetes, reduces spirochete viability in a dose-dependent manner in vitro, and enhances phagocytosis. Taken together, these findings show that adipose tissue is a site of active immune signaling in the setting of infection and identify SAA as a host defense factor against B. burgdorferi . IMPORTANCE Borrelia burgdorferi is the bacterium that is transmitted by ticks and causes Lyme disease. These bacteria replicate in the skin to cause the localized skin rash erythema migrans, then disseminate to cause symptoms in other organs, including the joints and heart. Adipose tissue, or fat, is adjacent to skin, joints, and heart—all target organs of infection. In this study, we set out to understand how adipose tissue/fat plays a role in Lyme disease. We discovered that B. burgdorferi infection leads to an immune response in adipose tissue cells with specific downregulation of a gene called serum amyloid A (SAA). Our work shows that B. burgdorferi bacteria bind serum amyloid A (SAA), leading to decreased viability in vitro and enhanced uptake of B. burgdorferi by white blood cells. These findings highlight the dynamic role our fat can play during B. burgdorferi infection and can lead to the identification of new treatments for Lyme disease.

title: MLAWind: a monthly sea surface wind dataset derived from an interpretable machine learning approach integrating in-situ observations and satellite data
summary: A gridded sea surface wind dataset with long temporal coverage is crucial for understanding atmospheric circulation changes and air–sea interactions at different time scales. This study employs an interpretable machine learning model based
content: A gridded sea surface wind dataset with long temporal coverage is crucial for understanding atmospheric circulation changes and air–sea interactions at different time scales. This study employs an interpretable machine learning model based on random forest algorithm to generate a 1° × 1° monthly sea surface wind dataset (MLAWind) from 1950 to 2023, covering the near-global ocean within 60° S–60° N. The data reconstruction model integrates the Cross-Calibrated Multi-Platform (CCMP) satellite data and the spatially sparse long-term International Comprehensive Ocean-Atmosphere Data Set (ICOADS), exhibiting robust interpretability and generalization capability. Quantitative validations against satellite and in-situ data indicate that MLAWind achieves better consistency with observations than most reanalysis datasets, maintaining robust performance during both training (1993–2022) and testing periods (2023). The performance of MLAWind since 1950 is assessed across multiple time scales. Its characteristics in climatology, annual cycle, and inter-annual variability are comparable to those of reanalysis datasets, even during the non-satellite period prior to 1993. Independent coral records from 1950–1982 are employed as proxy indicators to evaluate long-term sea surface wind trends. The trend derived from MLAWind is corroborated by these proxies, exhibiting significantly higher temporal correlation than those obtained from reanalysis products. MLAWind demonstrates a more reliable reconstruction of long-term sea surface wind variability during historical periods since 1950. The results indicate that MLAWind serves as a robust data resource for global climate change research. The reconstructed MLAWind dataset is publicly accessible at https://doi.org/10.12157/IOCAS.20250707.001 (Guo et al., 2025c).

title: Tensor-network methodology for real-space super-moiré excitons
summary: Computing excitonic spectra in quasicrystal and super-moiré systems constitutes a formidable challenge due to the exceptional size of the excitonic Hilbert space. Here, we demonstrate a tensor-network method for the real-space Bethe-Salpete
content: Computing excitonic spectra in quasicrystal and super-moiré systems constitutes a formidable challenge due to the exceptional size of the excitonic Hilbert space. Here, we demonstrate a tensor-network method for the real-space Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian, allowing us to access the spectra of an excitonic 10^{18} 10 18 -dimensional Hamiltonian, and enabling the direct computation of bound-exciton spectral functions for systems exceeding one billion lattice sites, several orders of magnitude beyond the capabilities of conventional approaches. Our method combines a tensor-network encoding of the real-space Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian with a Chebyshev tensor network algorithm. This strategy bypasses explicit storage of the Hamiltonian while preserving full real-space resolution across widely different length scales. We demonstrate our methodology for one- and two-dimensional super-moiré systems, achieving the simultaneous resolution of atomistic and mesoscopic structures in the excitonic spectra in billion-size systems, showing exciton miniband formation and moiré-induced spatial confinement. Our results establish a real-space methodology enabling the simulation of excitonic physics in large-scale quasicrystal and super-moiré quantum matter.

title: Harvesting Indoor Light for Electricity Recovery Using Semitransparent CdTe Solar Cells for Energy Efficient Buildings
source: Journal of Energy and Power Technology
summary: Abstract This study presents a preliminary proof-of-concept demonstration exploring how indoor artificial lighting - specifically LED systems - can serve a dual function: providing illumination while enabling electricity generation through
content: Abstract This study presents a preliminary proof-of-concept demonstration exploring how indoor artificial lighting - specifically LED systems - can serve a dual function: providing illumination while enabling electricity generation through integration with semitransparent photovoltaic (PV) panels. Using cadmium telluride (CdTe) PV cells with varying visible light transmittance levels, we show that diffused indoor LED lighting can generate meaningful electrical output, even under relatively low light power densities. A multi-layer panel configuration further enhances power output, underscoring the system's potential scalability. While detailed PV performance data are provided, the broader objective is to initiate discussion on integrating energy-harvesting systems within interior spaces - walls, ceilings, and floors - as a pathway toward energy-neutral buildings. From a cost-benefit perspective, if 15% efficient PV panels were installed on just 30% of the Willis Tower’s surface area, the projected annual electricity savings would be approximately $0.81 mil-lion/year. These findings highlight an untapped opportunity to transform indoor lighting into a sustainable energy asset, supporting long-term building efficiency and environ-mental goals.

title: Synergistic antibiotic activity and integrated genomic–metabolomic profiling of patch- and plaque-derived Staphylococcus aureus in mycosis fungoides
summary: ABSTRACT Mycosis fungoides (MF), the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, is frequently associated with skin dysbiosis, and advanced lesions are often dominated by multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus . To characterize microb
content: ABSTRACT Mycosis fungoides (MF), the most common form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, is frequently associated with skin dysbiosis, and advanced lesions are often dominated by multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus . To characterize microbiologically relevant properties of MF-associated S. aureus , we evaluated synergistic antibiotic combinations and performed integrated phenotypic, genomic, and metabolomic profiling. Several antibiotic combinations, most notably carbenicillin combined with either gentamicin or levofloxacin, exhibited pronounced synergistic activity and restored in vitro antimicrobial activity against highly resistant isolates. Comparative genomic analyses revealed substantial variability between isolates in resistomes and virulence repertoires, including enterotoxins, immune-evasion, and stress-response factors. Metabolomic profiling further revealed isolate-specific extracellular signatures, including putrescine and urocanic acid. In summary, this study identifies promising antibiotic combinations against multidrug-resistant S. aureus strains. Furthermore, this exploratory investigation demonstrates phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity among MF-associated S. aureus isolates, warranting further evaluation in larger longitudinal studies. IMPORTANCE Despite its predominance in advanced mycosis fungoides (MF) lesions, the role of multidrug‑resistant Staphylococcus aureus in adverse clinical outcomes remains poorly understood. Bridging the gap between clinical observations and microbiological mechanisms is essential to clarify how S. aureus persists in MF skin and to identify therapeutic alternatives for S. aureus ‑positive patients, for whom treatment options remain limited. This study addresses two major clinical needs: the lack of effective antibiotic strategies and the limited understanding of bacterial factors that may contribute to worsened clinical outcomes. By integrating synergistic antibiotic testing with genomic, phenotypic, and metabolomic profiling, our work highlights clinically relevant heterogeneity among MF-associated S. aureus isolates. These findings identify promising therapeutic directions and establish a framework for future large-scale longitudinal studies to better understand the role of diverse S. aureus strains in MF pathogenesis.

title: Fabrication of Fluorine Doped Ti/SnO2-Sb/α-PbO2/F-doped β-PbO2 Electrode and Optimized Treatment of Dye Wastewater Using Response Surface Methodology in Plate and Frame Electrolytic Cell
summary: Abstract Metal-oxide electrode with high catalytic performance and good corrosion resistance is the core of electrochemical oxidation. PbO 2 electrodes have a long service life, excellent electrocatalytic stability and electrochemical corro
content: Abstract Metal-oxide electrode with high catalytic performance and good corrosion resistance is the core of electrochemical oxidation. PbO 2 electrodes have a long service life, excellent electrocatalytic stability and electrochemical corrosion resistance. Electrochemical treatment of dyeing wastewater has many advantages, but its practical application is restricted by high energy consumption. In this paper, by optimizing the NaF doping concentration, the β-PbO 2 electrode with the best decolorization performance for methylene blue wastewater was prepared, and the prepared electrode has the highest oxygen evolution potential of 1.81V and the longest accelerated life of 32 h. The optimized PbO 2 electrode was used in a plate frame electrolytic cell to treat methylene blue wastewater, and the electrolytic conditions were optimized to reduce energy consumption. The quadratic multivariate fitting model of electrolytic conditions on decolorization rate and energy consumption was established by the response surface method. The experimental results show that the fitting effects of the two models were good, and the adjusted R 2 square was greater than 0.99. The Pareto solution set was obtained by the NSGA-Ⅲ algorithm. The optimized operation condition with the lowest energy consumption was investigated and listed as follows: current density is 9.37 mA/cm 2 , electrolyte concentration is 0.025 M, pH value is 6.37 and electrolytic time is 10 min. The optimized energy consumption per ton of wastewater treatment is 4.60 kWh.

title: Assessment of Sub-50 nm Nanopipette Emitters for Native Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry
source: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry
summary: Abstract Native mass spectrometry (nMS) is well established for measuring protein masses and stoichiometries using nano-electrospray ionization (nESI), yet salt adduction and source activation energies can limit routine measurements. In thi
content: Abstract Native mass spectrometry (nMS) is well established for measuring protein masses and stoichiometries using nano-electrospray ionization (nESI), yet salt adduction and source activation energies can limit routine measurements. In this study, we benchmark submicron quartz nanopipette nESI emitters (<50 nm internal diameter) across three mass spectrometry platforms (quadrupole-time-of-flight, quadrupole-Orbitrap, and tribrid-Orbitrap platforms) and a wide protein range (14.5-800 kDa). We analysed the intrinsically disordered protein alpha synuclein (αS; 14.5 kDa) and holo-myoglobin (17 kDa) over a range of concentrations (10 μM-1 nM) and capillary voltages to determine limits of detection and define a gentle operating regime. We additionally observed reduced Na⁺ adduction and preservation of the Zn²⁺-bound metalloproteoform of carbonic anhydrase II (29 kDa). Proteins and protein complexes spanning the mid-to-high mass range including ovalbumin (∼44 kDa), malate dehydrogenase (∼70 kDa), transferrin (80 kDa), glutamate dehydrogenase (∼350 kDa), β-galactosidase (∼465 kDa), and GroEL (∼800 kDa), were readily detected using nanopipette emitters. Compared with conventional 1-2 μm internal diameter borosilicate emitters, quartz nanopipettes provided higher signal-to-noise ratios and fewer adducts. Finally, direct analysis of clarified bacterial lysate expressing α-synuclein yielded a clear monomeric charge-state distribution, demonstrating compatibility with complex biological matrices. Collectively, these results establish quartz nanopipette nESI as an instrument-portable, salt-tolerant approach suitable for routine nMS analysis across a broad range of protein molecular weights and sample complexities.

title: Assessing greenhouse gas measurement consistency and traceability in the UK and Ireland atmospheric monitoring network using whole and synthetic air reference materials
summary: Abstract. Atmospheric greenhouse gas (GHG) measurements are essential for assessing climate change and verifying national emission inventories. As global networks rely on high-precision observations of potent GHGs such as carbon dioxide (CO
content: Abstract. Atmospheric greenhouse gas (GHG) measurements are essential for assessing climate change and verifying national emission inventories. As global networks rely on high-precision observations of potent GHGs such as carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄) and nitrous oxide (N₂O), ensuring accuracy between observation stations is essential. Maintaining accuracy within a network requires the use of whole air reference materials (RMs) with well-defined calibration scales, such as those maintained by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) for the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO). With the global expansion of atmospheric monitoring networks there is a growing need for readily available RMs, stimulating the development of complementary alternatives such as synthetic air RMs traceable to the International System of Units (SI). In the United Kingdom (UK) and Ireland, the atmospheric GHG monitoring network, comprising long-term atmospheric monitoring stations, is equipped with high precision in situ GHG analysers. These observations are used to verify bottom-up assessments of national emissions. Here, a case study is presented which provides the first direct, network‑wide evaluation of whole air versus synthetic air RMs under routine field conditions, allowing an assessment of the implications of SI‑traceable RMs within an active national atmospheric monitoring system. We assess the UK and Ireland’s network accuracy using WMO-NOAA scale-traceable whole air RMs and SI-traceable synthetic air RMs, through a blind multi-site round-robin intercomparison. Between 2021 and 2022, measurements were made of CO2, CH4 and N2O in whole and synthetic air RMs at six sites using a range of instruments and the results were used to assess biases between sites. The measured mole fractions for each cylinder, at each site were then compared with the assigned value on the WMO-NOAA scale and the SI-traceable values for the whole air and synthetic air RMs, respectively. Weighted residual analysis reveals that whole air RMs generally meet the WMO/Global Atmospheric Watch (GAW) compatibility goals for CO₂ and CH₄, while N₂O remains more difficult due to its small atmospheric variability and instrument performance. Synthetic SI-traceable RMs have associated absolute uncertainties on their assigned values for CH4 that are comparable to the extended WMO compatibility goals. However, absolute uncertainties for CO2 and N2O remain significantly larger than both the compatibility and extended compatibility goals, which is consistent with previous studies. Overall, these results indicate that while scale-traceable whole air RMs remain essential for achieving the highest level of network compatibility required for atmospheric monitoring, SI-traceable synthetic RMs could play a valuable complementary role, particularly for CH4. title: Genetic architecture of the murine serum metabolome reveals carboxyl esterases as master regulators of circulating fatty acid metabolism
summary: ABSTRACT Background The systemic biochemical diversity of circulating metabolites and lipids reflects the integrated effects of genetic variation and environmental exposure. Metabolite quantitative trait locus (mQTL) studies in humans have
content: ABSTRACT Background The systemic biochemical diversity of circulating metabolites and lipids reflects the integrated effects of genetic variation and environmental exposure. Metabolite quantitative trait locus (mQTL) studies in humans have established gene-metabolite associations, but genetic contributions can be obscured by sex, diet, age, medication use, and environmental exposures. Genetically diverse model systems offer a powerful complementary strategy to isolate genetic contributions to the biochemical diversity of the circulating metabolome. Methodology/Principal Findings We applied mass spectrometry profiling to serum samples in 541 mice from the Diversity Outbred (DO) population and identified 1,933 mQTL across 240 metabolites, 561 lipids, 43 oxylipins, and 4,465 MS/MS features. Co-mapping QTL, i.e., QTL hotspots, on chromosomes 8 and 17 implicated carboxyl esterase gene clusters ( Ces1 and Ces2 ) as major regulators of circulating lipid remodeling and demonstrated genetic control of circulating protein/peptide-like features at the major histocompatibility complex and complement C3 loci. QTL hotspots on chromosomes 9 and 10 revealed previously unknown genetic drivers of lipid and amino acid metabolism. Comparisons with matched red blood cell mQTL revealed widespread compartment-specific genetic control. Conclusions/Significance Collectively, these findings provide a high-resolution map of the genetic regulation of the circulating metabolome, offering mechanistic insights that complement and extend human metabolic genetics.

title: Decoupled regression rate and stability characteristics of carbon-black and aluminum-doped paraffin fuels for hybrid rocket engines
summary: Abstract Hybrid rocket engines offer inherent safety and throttling by separating fuel and oxidizer, yet their wider use is hindered by low fuel regression rates and by combustion instabilities that frequently accompany performance-enhancin
content: Abstract Hybrid rocket engines offer inherent safety and throttling by separating fuel and oxidizer, yet their wider use is hindered by low fuel regression rates and by combustion instabilities that frequently accompany performance-enhancing additives. In this paper, an experimental and analytical framework is presented that decouples these two issues. Instability mechanisms are classified into low-frequency (LFI), intermediate-frequency (IFI), and feed-system coupled modes. A systematic experimental campaign of 31 firings was conducted on paraffin-based fuels doped with carbon black (PC, 1 wt\%), conventional micron-aluminum (PA, 14 wt\%), and activated nano-aluminum (PAA, 14 wt\%), all burned with gaseous oxygen. A two one‑sided test (TOST) equivalence procedure with a $\pm10\%$ margin confirmed that the regression rates of the three fuels are practically equivalent. In contrast, the stability signatures differ fundamentally: PC burns in a stable manner; PA exhibits coupled LFI‑bulk mode instability with a secondary peak at 254 Hz; PAA shows LFI and a bulk mode together with a decoupled higher‑frequency peak at 414 Hz. The physical mechanism for this shift remains unclear and warrants further study. A data‑driven classification framework using an ensemble classifier, trained and cross‑validated on the present dataset, achieved 90\% accuracy across instability categories, though independent validation is needed. The results quantify the performance–stability trade-off and demonstrate the utility of the proposed analysis approach.

title: Coupled Geophysical and Technoeconomic Industrial Growth Constraints on Geological Carbon Storage Scale-Up: Application to UK Offshore Resources
summary: Abstract Geological carbon dioxide storage is central to meeting many national climate change commitments, but large-scale deployment may be limited by both techno-economic rates of growth and physics-based processes imposed by subsurface g
content: Abstract Geological carbon dioxide storage is central to meeting many national climate change commitments, but large-scale deployment may be limited by both techno-economic rates of growth and physics-based processes imposed by subsurface geology. We develop a modeling framework for the assessment of feasible CO2 storage scale-up trajectories that unifies constraints arising from industrial rates of growth, dynamic injection rate limits from reservoir pressurization, and static maximum cumulative storage resource. We employ logistic and Gompertz models to represent policy-compliant deployment trajectories, parametrized by the total cumulative storage resource. We then use a simplified physics model to estimate the resulting regional subsurface pressurization along these trajectories. Growth curves where reservoir pressurization exceeds safe limits are updated by reducing the static storage resource until residing in the safe deployment range. The result is both a growth trajectory and static storage resource achievable subject to injectivity limits. Applying the framework to the United Kingdom (UK), we find that offshore storage resources are sufficient to accommodate all government midcentury deployment rate scenarios up to 175 Mt yr–1. Cumulative storage of up to 78 Gt, representing a reference estimate of the UK storage resource base used in national planning, can be achieved under Gompertz growth trajectories. The more aggressive logistic trajectories are constrained by reservoir pressure, limiting the achievable resource base to 69 Gt. The framework is transferable to other regions to assess the feasibility of policy-driven CO2 storage pathways under coupled industrial growth and geophysical constraints, informing national decarbonization planning and global integrated assessment models.

title: Two-Photon Excitation Microscopy of Individual Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Two-photon fluorescence imaging achieves deep-tissue penetration through long excitation wavelengths and nonlinear excitation confinement. The NIR-IIb transparency window is particularly attractive, as it optimally balances tissue
content: Abstract Two-photon fluorescence imaging achieves deep-tissue penetration through long excitation wavelengths and nonlinear excitation confinement. The NIR-IIb transparency window is particularly attractive, as it optimally balances tissue scattering and absorption. However, efficient fluorophores for two-photon excitation in this window remain limited. Moreover, the weak near-infrared emission of individual emitters and the low photon detection efficiency have so far precluded single-particle imaging. Here, we characterize the two-photon excitation properties of chirality-sorted pristine and quantum color center-functionalized single-walled carbon nanotubes under 1630–1700 nm excitation. By measuring and comparing their two-photon action cross sections, we identify quantum color center-functionalized (6,5) nanotubes emitting at 1140 nm as the most promising emitter, with an exceptionally large cross section of (17.1 ± 0.6) × 103 GM/nm. Leveraging these favorable photophysical properties, we image individual nanotubes in the NIR-IIb window, which to our knowledge is the first demonstration of single-particle imaging in this spectral window. These results establish quantum color center-functionalized (6,5) nanotubes as a strong candidate for long-wavelength two-photon imaging and pave the way toward single-particle imaging in scattering tissues.

title: Randomized trial of pressure controlled versus volume controlled ventilation during robot assisted urological surgery in the clasp knife position
summary: Abstract Background The combination of CO₂ pneumoperitoneum and clasp-knife position imposes substantial respiratory and hemodynamic challenges in Da Vinci robot-assisted urological surgery. Although volume-controlled ventilation (VCV) and
content: Abstract Background The combination of CO₂ pneumoperitoneum and clasp-knife position imposes substantial respiratory and hemodynamic challenges in Da Vinci robot-assisted urological surgery. Although volume-controlled ventilation (VCV) and pressure-controlled ventilation (PCV) are widely used, their comparative effects under these specific surgical conditions remain unclear. We hypothesized that PCV could reduce peak inspiratory pressure (Ppeak) and improve dynamic lung compliance (Cdyn) without compromising hemodynamic stability. Method Sixty ASA I–II patients undergoing Da Vinci robot-assisted laparoscopic urological surgery in the clasp-knife position were randomized to receive VCV or PCV. Ventilatory parameters, hemodynamic variables, and arterial blood gas values were recorded at five time points: T1 (15 min after induction), T2 (15 min after clasp-knife positioning), T3 (30 min after CO₂ pneumoperitoneum), T4 (60 min after CO₂ pneumoperitoneum), and T5 (15 min after pneumoperitoneum removal). Result Ppeak was significantly lower in the PCV group compared with the VCV group at T2 (P = 0.0076), T3–T4 (P < 0.0001), and T5 (P = 0.0059). Cdyn was significantly higher in the PCV group at T2 (P = 0.0154), and T5 (P = 0.0038). Patients in the PCV group had higher blood pH levels than those in the VCV group (T1, P = 0.0079; T2, P = 0.0132; T3, P = 0.0072; T4, P = 0.0015; T5, P = 0.0258). No severe postoperative complications were observed. Conclusion PCV reduces Ppeak and improves Cdyn compared with VCV during Da Vinci robot-assisted laparoscopic urological surgery in the clasp-knife position, without adversely affecting hemodynamic stability. Therefore, PCV may represent a preferable ventilation strategy in this surgical context.

title: Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry B
summary: Abstract Thermally induced solid-state polymorphic transitions in an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor (NDI-C6) are investigated using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. NDI-C6 exhibits two stable
content: Abstract Thermally induced solid-state polymorphic transitions in an n-hexyl-functionalized naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor (NDI-C6) are investigated using atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. NDI-C6 exhibits two stable polymorphs: the α phase at room temperature and the γ phase at higher temperatures. The MD simulations reproduce the structural stability of both phases and provide a refined description of their unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations, which have been only partially resolved experimentally. The α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted two-step mechanism. An initial fast (subnanosecond) process involves the collective rearrangement of the NDI cores, followed by a slow process (several ns) characterized by side-chain extension. These results provide an atomistic picture of polymorphism in NDI-C6 and establish a robust computational protocol for investigating labile phase transitions in the broader class of NDI-based n-type soft organic semiconductors.

title: Record-Breaking Elemental Superconductivity in Tetralayer Kagome Borophene
summary: Abstract Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature remains rare in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where strong covalent bonding often yields high phonon frequencies but insufficient electron–phonon coupling. Here, using f
content: Abstract Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature remains rare in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where strong covalent bonding often yields high phonon frequencies but insufficient electron–phonon coupling. Here, using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal–Eliashberg theory, we predict tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) stabilized by ABAB covalent stacking, as a liquid-nitrogen-temperature elemental superconductor. With a predicted critical temperature of ∼100–113 K, TKB sets a record-high value among previously reported elemental superconductors. Unlike known high-Tc boron-based superconductors dominated by in-plane σ-bonding states and high-frequency in-plane B–B stretching modes, TKB realizes an out-of-plane s–pz-bonding-mediated pairing mechanism, in which interlayer s–pz bonding states at the Fermi level are strongly coupled to low-frequency out-of-plane vibrations of boron atoms. These results reveal a distinct out-of-plane pairing channel in multilayer borophene and establish covalent stacking engineering as a potential route for high-Tc superconductivity in two-dimensional materials.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance pulmonary artery peak flow velocity as a marker of pulmonary vascular resistance in fibrotic interstitial lung disease
summary: Abstract Background. Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a common and severe complication of interstitial lung disease (ILD), yet early diagnosis remains challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) offers non-invasive assessment of pulm
content: Abstract Background. Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a common and severe complication of interstitial lung disease (ILD), yet early diagnosis remains challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) offers non-invasive assessment of pulmonary vascular hemodynamics, but evidence in PH associated with ILD is limited. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between CMR-derived parameters and invasive hemodynamics in patients with fibrotic ILD. Methods. In this prospective observational study, 41 patients with fibrotic ILD underwent pulmonary function testing, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, transthoracic echocardiography, and CMR. Twenty patients additionally underwent RHC. CMR-derived measurements included ventricular function parameters, heart chamber and great vessel dimensions, and pulmonary artery flow hemodynamic metrics. Associations between CMR parameters, invasive hemodynamics, exercise capacity and symptom burden were assessed using correlation, regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. Results. Among 20 patients who underwent RHC, PH was confirmed in all cases, including 15 with isolated precapillary PH and 5 with combined PH. Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) of over 5 Wood units defined severe PH in 6 patients who met the criteria. Pulmonary artery peak flow velocity (PA-Vmax) measured on CMR was significantly higher in the non-severe PH group (81.15 ± 19.27 cm/s vs. 52.33 ± 5.13 cm/s, p < 0.001) and demonstrated promising discriminatory performance for identifying severe PH (AUC 0.923, 95% CI 0.778-1.000, p = 0.004), with a threshold of < 62.5 cm/s yielding 100% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity. An inverse-transformed PA-Vmax model demonstrated a strong association with invasive PVR (R 2 = 0.651, F = 31.65, p < 0.001). Higher PA-Vmax correlated with greater exercise capacity, including higher anaerobic threshold (r = 0.419, p = 0.015) and maximal workload (r = 0.329, p = 0.050). Lower CMR-derived TAPSE was independently associated with greater dyspnea severity (β=-0.426, p = 0.025), while CMR-TAPSE/RHC-mPAP ratio demonstrated an even stronger association with symptom burden (r s =-0.570, p = 0.021). Conclusions. In patients with fibrotic ILD, CMR-derived PA-Vmax was significantly associated with PVR measured by RHC and demonstrated promising discrimination for severe PH in this exploratory cohort. CMR measurements of right ventricular adaptation were associated with functional capacity and dyspnea severity. These findings support further evaluation of CMR as a promising non-invasive modality for pulmonary vascular assessment in fibrotic ILD patients undergoing evaluation for suspected PH.

title: A Cyanopolyyne-rich but Complex-organic-molecule-poor Massive Protostar: The First Hot Carbon-chain Chemistry Source G28.28-0.36
summary: Abstract We present molecular emission line data from the massive young stellar object (MYSO) G28.28-0.36 (G28.28) obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Band 3. Cyanopolyynes (HC 3 N and HC 5 N) and three complex or
content: Abstract We present molecular emission line data from the massive young stellar object (MYSO) G28.28-0.36 (G28.28) obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Band 3. Cyanopolyynes (HC 3 N and HC 5 N) and three complex organic molecules (COMs; CH 3 OH, CH 3 CN, and CH 3 CHO) are detected from the MYSO G28.28. In addition, strong emission regions of cyanopolyynes are identified between G28.28 and a nearby ultracompact H ii region. The HC 5 N emission is coincident with the dust continuum peak, where an excitation temperature of 100 K is derived from CH 3 CN. These results suggest that the hot carbon-chain chemistry (HCCC) mechanism produces cyanopolyynes in the hot region around G28.28. We find that G28.28 exhibits a unique chemical feature: cyanopolyynes are abundant, but COMs are deficient, unlike the other MYSOs studied previously. These results imply that G28.28 is a counterpart of the warm carbon-chain chemistry (WCCC) low-mass source L1527. G28.28 is the first HCCC source identified so far.

title: Field Demonstration of Enhanced Cellulose Triacetate Membranes for CO2 Separation Under High Pressure, High Temperature and High CO2 Partial Pressure Conditions
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Membrane technology has become an increasingly important solution for carbon dioxide (CO2) removal from natural gas due to its operational simplicity, modular design, and ability to accommodate varying feed-gas compositions. However, reliab
content: Membrane technology has become an increasingly important solution for carbon dioxide (CO2) removal from natural gas due to its operational simplicity, modular design, and ability to accommodate varying feed-gas compositions. However, reliable membrane operation under high-temperature, high-pressure (HTHP) conditions remain a significant challenge. Elevated operating temperatures can reduce membrane selectivity and increase hydrocarbon permeation, making it more difficult to achieve product gas specifications without compromising methane recovery. Simultaneously, high feed pressures increase separation duty and permeate compression requirements, creating additional constraints on plant throughput, energy consumption, and overall operating costs. A membrane replacement project was undertaken at a natural gas processing plant operating in an arid climate characterized by prolonged periods of extreme summer heat. The gas plant was originally designed to process feed gas containing approximately 7.5–10.5 mol% CO2 and produce up to 310 MMSCFD of sales gas with a CO2 specification of ≤3 mol%. As feed-gas availability increased, operational flexibility was introduced, allowing the sales-gas CO2 specification to be relaxed to 4.2 mol% to accommodate higher throughput while maintaining applicable regulatory and commercial requirements. During peak summer conditions, ambient temperatures frequently exceeded 45°C and could approach 50°C during the hottest periods of the year. The elevated ambient temperatures reduced the effectiveness of cooling equipment, resulting in higher process temperatures throughout the membrane system. Combined with feed pressures exceeding 57 barg and limited permeate compressor capacity, these conditions created a challenging operating environment for membrane-based CO2 removal. At high throughput rates, the incumbent membrane technology consequently faced increased difficulty in maintaining sales-gas CO2 specifications and hydrocarbon recovery. To address these challenges, the incumbent membranes were replaced with enhanced CTA hollow-fiber membranes.

title: Aerothermal Hypersonic Reentry Simulation at Mach 15: Non-Linear PICA-X Thermal Shield Diffusion at 2,564 GB/s on NVIDIA Blackwell
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Predicting localized aerothermal heat flux and thermal degradation in hypersonic vehicles during atmospheric re-entry (Mach 15+) requires resolving non-linear diffusion, radiative boundary conditions, and material pyrolysis across millions
content: Predicting localized aerothermal heat flux and thermal degradation in hypersonic vehicles during atmospheric re-entry (Mach 15+) requires resolving non-linear diffusion, radiative boundary conditions, and material pyrolysis across millions of composite volumetric cells. Classical computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and material response codes (e.g., FIAT, CHAR) are bottlenecked by memory latency and distributed message-passing overheads, restricting real-time on-board trajectory adaptation. In this paper, we present an ultra-fast, register-fused non-linear thermal diffusion operator implemented in OpenAI Triton to simulate aerothermal response in Phenolic-Impregnated Carbon Ablator (PICA-X) heat shields. Tested across 10,800,000 spatial finite volumes on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU (94.97 GB VRAM, 188 SMs, sm_120), the engine computes complete non-linear temperature progression, peak thermal shock localization, and regularized adjoint thermal state inversion in 0.0505 milliseconds (50.5 microseconds). This delivers an unprecedented sustained memory throughput of 2,564.91 GB/s.

title: Advancing remote sensing of carbon fractions in coastal waters: retrieval algorithms and optical proxies for Sentinel-2 MSI and Sentinel-3 OLCI
summary: A thorough understanding of the global carbon pools and cycle is essential for understanding and predicting the effects of climate change. Coastal waters play a key role in the global carbon cycle but remain poorly understood due to their o
content: A thorough understanding of the global carbon pools and cycle is essential for understanding and predicting the effects of climate change. Coastal waters play a key role in the global carbon cycle but remain poorly understood due to their optical complexity, high spatial variability, and sensitivity to climate change. Satellite remote sensing data can provide high spatial and temporal resolution for carbon monitoring at local, regional, and global scales. This study estimates the potential of Sentinel-2 MSI (S2) and Sentinel-3 OLCI (S3) for mapping carbon fractions in coastal waters. In situ hyperspectral reflectance measurements and concentrations of different carbon fractions, namely Total Organic Carbon (TOC), Dissolved Organic Carbon (DOC), Particulate Organic Carbon (POC), and Dissolved Inorganic Carbon (DIC), were used. Bio-optical and physical water parameters, as well as carbon fractions, were measured in the coastal areas of the eastern Baltic Sea from 2023 to 2024. In situ reflectance spectra were recalculated to S2 and S3 band reflectance using their respective spectral response functions. Regression models, including linear regression and machine learning methods, were developed and validated against in situ data to estimate carbon fractions. For S2, the combinations of green and red or red-edge bands achieved the best performance in carbon retrieval, with R 2 values of 0.67, 0.64, and 0.56 for TOC, DOC, and DIC, respectively. The corresponding MAPE values ranged from 14% to 18%, and biases were close to zero. Slightly higher accuracies were obtained with S3 simulations. The S3 models that used reflectance at 490, 620, and 665 nm produced the most accurate estimates for both TOC ( R 2 = 0.71) and DOC ( R 2 = 0.67). For DIC, the best predictive model combined information from 510, 665, and 709 nm bands, achieving R 2 of 0.62. Among the tested optical proxies, CDOM absorption at 443 nm showed the most consistent relationship with TOC, DOC, and DIC ( R 2 = 0.56–0.30). The study represents a significant step forward in the remote sensing of coastal waters, and if adopted, the proposed carbon-fraction products could enable substantial progress across various fields, from carbon-cycle research to monitoring and policymaking.

title: Optimization of N, P, and K Fertilizer Rates for ‘IPB 13S’ Rice
summary: Fertilizer recommendations for newly released rice varieties need to be optimized because nutrient requirements may vary among varieties and growing environments. ‘IPB 13S’ is a newly released rice variety developed by IPB University, and i
content: Fertilizer recommendations for newly released rice varieties need to be optimized because nutrient requirements may vary among varieties and growing environments. ‘IPB 13S’ is a newly released rice variety developed by IPB University, and information regarding its optimal nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P2O5), and potassium (K2O) requirements is still limited. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the optimal rates of N, P2O5, and K2O fertilizers for ‘IPB 13S’ rice. The study was conducted from May to September 2024 at the Sawah Baru Experimental Farm, Dramaga, Bogor, Indonesia. Three fertilizer experiments (N, P2O5, and K2O) were arranged in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with five fertilizer levels (0%, 50%, 100%, 150%, and 200% of the regional recommended rate) and three replications. Growth parameters, yield components, grain yield, and nutrient use efficiency were evaluated. Data were analyzed using analysis of variance, orthogonal polynomial analysis, and quadratic regression. The results showed that N, P2O5, and K2O applications significantly affected plant growth, yield components, grain yield, and nutrient use efficiency. Quadratic regression analysis identified optimal fertilizer rates of 170 kg N/ha, 53 kg P2O5/ha, and 71 kg K2O/ha, resulting in the highest predicted grain yield. These findings indicate that variety-specific fertilizer recommendations are needed to optimize grain yield and nutrient use efficiency in the ‘IPB 13S’ rice variety.

title: Efectos de las prácticas de remoción de arbustos en sistemas ganaderos del Chaco Árido, Argentina
summary: 1. El aumento de la abundancia de arbustos nativos, impulsado por factores como la tala intensiva y el sobrepastoreo, afecta a bosques y pastizales. En el Chaco Árido, este proceso reduce el forraje. Para compensar, se remueven los arbustos
content: 1. El aumento de la abundancia de arbustos nativos, impulsado por factores como la tala intensiva y el sobrepastoreo, afecta a bosques y pastizales. En el Chaco Árido, este proceso reduce el forraje. Para compensar, se remueven los arbustos y se siembran pastos exóticos. Sin embargo, se conocen poco los efectos de estas prácticas sobre la estructura de la vegetación y la relación entre pastos y leñosas. 2. Evaluamos los efectos del rolado y del desarbustado manual sobre la cobertura de árboles, arbustos y pastos, la estructura poblacional de las leñosas y la relación entre su densidad y la cobertura de pastos. Consideramos cuatro tipos de cobertura del suelo: bosque de referencia, arbustal degradado, rolado y desarbustado manual (los dos últimos, sembrados con Cenchrus ciliaris L.).3. El rolado y el desarbustado manual presentaron menor cobertura arbórea que el bosque de referencia y difirieron entre sí en arbustos y pastos. El desarbustado manual presentó menor cobertura arbustiva y mayor cobertura de pastos. El rolado presentó valores intermedios de pastos y cobertura arbustiva similar al bosque de referencia y al arbustal degradado. El bosque de referencia mostró mayor densidad de plántulas arbóreas y, junto con el arbustal degradado, mayor densidad de árboles adultos. Respecto de los arbustos, los adultos presentaron menor densidad bajo el desarbustado manual.4. La cobertura de pastos disminuyó al aumentar la densidad de leñosas, que explicó el 61% de su variación. El modelo segmentado identificó un cambio de pendiente en 1527±314 individuos leñosos/ha, disminuyendo marcadamente por debajo de este valor. La relación fue más fuerte con los arbustos adultos (R²=0.59) que con los árboles (R²=0.30).5. Implicancias. El desarbustado manual favorece los pastos, pero simplifica la vegetación leñosa. El rolado permite una mayor coexistencia entre ambos estratos, aunque sin recuperar el componente arbóreo.

title: A Comparison of Tensile Testing Techniques and Predictive Correlations
summary: Abstract The engineering properties of a rock foundation are key parameters in the analysis of dams as they inform an understanding of how a structure will perform under a loading condition of interest. One important, but difficult to accur
content: Abstract The engineering properties of a rock foundation are key parameters in the analysis of dams as they inform an understanding of how a structure will perform under a loading condition of interest. One important, but difficult to accurately evaluate, engineering property is the tensile strength of rock. As the direct tensile strength (DTS) testing of intact rock is non-trivial and expensive, the tensile strength is typically inferred from more common indirect methods, such as the Brazilian tensile strength (BTS) test, akin to the splitting tensile strength test performed on concrete, or using correlations to other mechanical properties, such as the crack initiation (CI) strength, m i parameter from the Generalized Hoek-Brown failure criterion, or the Mode I fracture toughness. This research leverages a robust laboratory testing program utilizing a state-of-the-art digital image correlation (DIC) system to understand how the different platen shapes and the use of a soft cushion affect BTS results, improve the understanding about the relationship between DTS and BTS tests (with a specific focus on optimizing the test arrangement), and explores correlations between other laboratory-measured properties (e.g., CI and m i ) and the DTS. The DTS was difficult to measure directly, but was found to be closely related to the BTS when testing was performed using curved platens, with or without a cushion; this testing arrangement also resulted in a failure mechanism that aligns with the underlying assumptions from Hondros (1959); ISRM (1978); and ASTM (2016). When analyzing the BTS data from different platen arrangements, it is important to use a relationship that incorporates the loading arc angle to ensure data are comparable as the BTS is a function of the loading arc angle in the full stress solution. The use of CI or m i to estimate the DTS was found to be unreliable with the BTS providing the closest approximation

title: Source-dependent structural and pH-responsive swelling properties of bentonite/cellulose/alginate hydrogel beads derived from agricultural biomass residues
summary: Agricultural biomass residues are abundant and renewable feedstocks for the development of cellulose-based functional biomaterials. However, direct comparisons of cellulose-rich fractions derived from multiple agricultural biomass sources w
content: Agricultural biomass residues are abundant and renewable feedstocks for the development of cellulose-based functional biomaterials. However, direct comparisons of cellulose-rich fractions derived from multiple agricultural biomass sources within the same hydrogel formulation and under identical fabrication conditions remain limited. This study investigated the structural and swelling properties of bentonite/cellulose/alginate (BT/CL/ALG) hydrogel beads prepared from eight agricultural residues: coffee pulp, mango leaf, corn cob, corn leaf, corn husk, corn stalk, sugarcane leaf, and bagasse. The biomass residues were subjected to combined alkaline hydrogen peroxide (AHP) pretreatment to obtain cellulose-rich fractions, which were subsequently incorporated into a sodium alginate matrix with bentonite clay and crosslinked with Ca²⁺. The resulting materials were characterized by compositional analysis, FTIR, XRD, SEM, and TGA/DTG. AHP pretreatment resulted in substantial cellulose enrichment, with the highest cellulose contents observed in corn stalk (76.0%) and bagasse (70.4%). FTIR and XRD analyses indicated changes in the chemical structure and relative crystalline organization of the biomass following pretreatment, while SEM revealed source-dependent morphological changes. The resulting hydrogel beads exhibited differences in swelling behavior, with swelling capacities measured at 144 h ranging from 218.57% to 419.83% in deionized water. Under PBS conditions, all hydrogel beads exhibited pH-responsive swelling, with greater swelling at pH 9 than at pH 3. The highest swelling capacity was observed for the corn-leaf-derived hydrogel at pH 9 (2245.85%). Overall, the findings demonstrate that agricultural biomass residues can provide cellulose-rich feedstocks for the preparation of BT/CL/ALG hydrogel beads with source-dependent structural and swelling characteristics.

title: Anthropogenic atmospheric heavy metal emission inventories in China: Theoretical frameworks, methodological evolution, and future perspectives
summary: Heavy metals (HMs) pollution is a global environmental and public health concern due to its persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity. Reliable atmospheric HM emission inventories (AHMEI) are essential for identifying source characteristic
content: Heavy metals (HMs) pollution is a global environmental and public health concern due to its persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity. Reliable atmospheric HM emission inventories (AHMEI) are essential for identifying source characteristics and supporting air pollution mitigation policies. This study summarizes the historical evolution and methodological advances in AHMEI quantification, including both top-down and bottom-up approaches. In China, coal combustion and non-ferrous metal smelting remained major HM sources around 2010. Peak emission intensities were concentrated in central-eastern and southern China, especially in economically developed provinces. Stringent regulations and improved control technologies have promoted integrated multi-pollutant strategies, leading to 17% to 84% decreases in Pb, Hg, Cd, As, and Cr emissions from 2015 to 2020. The total HM emissions from major industrial point sources showed declining trends during this period, whereas Hg emissions remained challenging, fluctuating between 300 and 500 t. Despite progress using dynamic emission factor models, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and high-resolution spatial modeling, developing countries still face barriers to high-resolution AHMEI because of limited source data and model uncertainty. In addition, complex industrial structures and regional disparities hinder robust interpretation and sustained reduction. Future AHMEI should advance toward dynamic, multi-pollution, high-resolution frameworks integrating cross-media transfer and species transformation. Emission control policies should align with China’s Green Industrial Restructuring, the Beautiful China Initiative, and the Dual-Carbon Goals to support sustainable development.

title: Autonomous Green Hubs: Reimagining Shore Power as a Maritime Energy Ecosystem
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract Conventional shore power is often treated as a cable-and- transformer project serving one vessel at one berth. That narrow approach can transfer emissions from ship to grid, cerate a new port demand peak, strand capacity between ve
content: Abstract Conventional shore power is often treated as a cable-and- transformer project serving one vessel at one berth. That narrow approach can transfer emissions from ship to grid, cerate a new port demand peak, strand capacity between vessel calls, and fail to accommodate mixed voltage offshore fleets. This paper develops an autonomous green hub: a standard- based, multi- berth maritime microgrid that coordinates utility supply, solar photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, shore-to-ship converters, yard charging, and vessel schedules through a safety- bound energy- management system. The contribution is a benefit- led engineering and verification framework rather than a vendor specific proposal. A non- confidential reference case comprises six berths, four simultaneously connected offshore vessels at an average 350kw hotel and auxiliary load, 18 connected hours per day, 2mwp solar generation, a 4- MW/8-MWh battery, and an 11-kV grid interface. The hub delivers 9,198 MWh/y to vessel. Relative to onboard auxiliary generation, a 215 g/kWh, it avoids approximately 1,978 t/y diesel consumption, 6,340 t/y tank-to-wake CO2,92t/y indicative NOX, and 26,280 generation operating hours. After 7% shore-system losses, a 30% renewable share, and a residual-grid factor of 0.35 kg CO2/kWh, net operational CO2 reduction remains approximately 3,917 t/y, or 62% of the berth-generation baseline. A modeled dispatch day limits grid imports to about 3.2 MW against a 4.8- MW unmanaged peak, while the battery absorbs solar surplus and supplies the evening berth peak. Additional benefits include reduced noise and vibration at berth, lower generator maintenance, improved power quality, black- start support for nonessential port loads, auditable energy allocation, and a modular path to vessel charging and low-carbon fuels. The paper defines electrical architecture, interoperability, protection, cyber- security, operating logic, measurement and verification, staged implementation, and decision gates. All numerical results are simulations and planning assumptions; they are not NMDC Energy performance or an approved investment case.

title: Hybrid resorbable anchors/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers for enhanced pedicle screw fixation
summary: Pedicle screw loosening remains a challenge for surgeons and patients. We propose using hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers to enhance the bone fixation of pedicle screws. Polylactide (PLA) anchors with various
content: Pedicle screw loosening remains a challenge for surgeons and patients. We propose using hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers to enhance the bone fixation of pedicle screws. Polylactide (PLA) anchors with various designs were fabricated using additive manufacturing, while simvastatin- and bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanofibers were prepared through coaxial electrospinning. The effects of PLA anchors and drug/biomolecule-loaded PLGA nanofibrous membranes on improving the pullout strength of pedicle screws from artificial bones were investigated. The in vitro release characteristics of simvastatin and BMP-2 from the nanofibers were evaluated using high-performance liquid chromatography and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, while the in vivo elution of simvastatin was assessed in a rabbit model with histological examinations. The results demonstrate that electrospun drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers, when wrapped around pedicle screws, enhance the screws’ pullout strength. Additionally, the nanofiber/screw system provides a sustained release of simvastatin and BMP-2 for over 30 days in vitro and 4 weeks in vivo. Histological analysis also confirmed the biocompatibility of nanofibrous anchors. Hybrid resorbable anchors and drug/biomolecule-eluting nanofibers show potential for improving screw fixation and serving as a platform for extended drug delivery.

title: Ocean-sourced CO2 Boosts Radiolytic Oxidants at Europa’s Chaos
summary: Abstract James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of Europa’s leading hemisphere reveal enhanced CO 2 abundances over equatorial chaos terrains where the subsurface ocean is thought to have breached the ice shell. Hydrogen peroxide, s
content: Abstract James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations of Europa’s leading hemisphere reveal enhanced CO 2 abundances over equatorial chaos terrains where the subsurface ocean is thought to have breached the ice shell. Hydrogen peroxide, synthesized radiolytically by Jovian magnetospheric charged particles impinging on Europa’s ice, is also elevated in these geologically active regions, spatially coinciding with CO 2 . This correlation implicates CO 2 in H 2 O 2 synthesis, consistent with laboratory experiments showing increased radiolytic peroxide yields in carbon-bearing ices. Our radiolysis model – which incorporates charged-particle precipitation through electromagnetic fields accounting for Europa’s interaction with Jupiter’s magnetosphere – predicts enhanced H 2 O 2 on the leading hemisphere equatorial regions. The relative dearth of energetic electrons in this region shields peroxide from destruction, leaving a notably higher abundance towards the leading apex compared to the mid-latitude regions or the trailing side. Integrating the inferred CO 2 abundance and the associated boost in peroxide yield, we show that ocean-derived CO 2 acts as a multiplier, further elevating H 2 O 2 concentrations within the fractured surfaces of Tara and Powys Regiones. Together, these results imply that geologic resurfacing at Europa’s chaos terrains and precipitating radiation conspire to contribute to the excess peroxide observed by JWST, with endogenic CO 2 amplifying oxidant production in these potentially ocean-linked regions.

title: A review of phase-change display: materials, architectures, driving, and applications
summary: The rapid advancement of next-generation display technologies has driven an increasing demand for devices that simultaneously offer ultrahigh resolution, high refresh rates, and ultralow power consumption. Phase-change materials (PCMs) unde
content: The rapid advancement of next-generation display technologies has driven an increasing demand for devices that simultaneously offer ultrahigh resolution, high refresh rates, and ultralow power consumption. Phase-change materials (PCMs) undergo reversible structural transitions between amorphous and crystalline states, accompanied by pronounced changes in optical constants. This process is inherently nonvolatile and requires no sustaining bias, resulting in near-zero static power consumption. These properties have established PCMs as a highly competitive platform for next-generation display technologies. However, several critical challenges remain, including limited color gamut coverage, insufficient cycling endurance, and difficulties in pixel-level addressing, all of which continue to hinder the practical deployment of PCM-based displays. This review provides a systematic overview of phase-change display technologies, organized along four interconnected dimensions: materials, device architectures, driving schemes, and applications. The microscopic mechanisms and optimization strategies governing switching speed, energy consumption, and cycling stability are first summarized. The optical modulation principles of thin-film interference structures, subwavelength metasurfaces, and multimodal hybrid devices are then reviewed. The multilevel grayscale control strategies of electrothermal and laser-based driving schemes are subsequently compared. Representative applications, including reflective, transmissive, and holographic displays, are also surveyed. This review aims to establish a coherent framework spanning from material fundamentals to device architectures and application development, providing a structured reference for advancing PCM-based displays toward high-performance and practical implementation.

title: All-optical 2D perovskite photodetector arrays for pixelated long-wave infrared imaging
summary: Abstract Infrared detection and imaging are important for applications including thermal monitoring, night vision, environmental sensing, and molecular identification. All-optical mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) detec
content: Abstract Infrared detection and imaging are important for applications including thermal monitoring, night vision, environmental sensing, and molecular identification. All-optical mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) detection offers a compelling alternative to conventional infrared detectors by enabling non-contact photothermal sensing without needing electronic readout circuitry. Here, we demonstrate pixelated LWIR imaging using solution-processed two-dimensional metal-halide perovskites (2D-MHPs), whose strong electron-phonon interaction produces a large temperature coefficient of reflectance in the visible wavelength range. By integrating (PEA) 2 PbI 4 films with LWIR-absorbing SiNₓ membranes, we realize centimeter-scale imagers capable of detecting 9.5-µm LWIR light with sensitivity down to ~20 pW·µm⁻². To mitigate lateral thermal diffusion that limits spatial fidelity, we introduce a structured-probe illumination scheme, and we further develop a fully pixelated imager with thermally isolated membrane-disc arrays. This design effectively eliminates pixel-to-pixel crosstalk and enables high-resolution optical readout using a silicon-based CMOS camera. These advances establish 2D-MHP-based all-optical thermal imaging as a scalable, low-cost platform for LWIR sensing, with strong potential for extension to far-infrared and terahertz detection.

title: Hylocereus undatus peel extract and ZnO nanoparticles suppress cancer through apoptosis and Wnt/β-catenin inhibition
summary: Abstract Cancer treatment faces the challenge of multidrug resistance and systemic cytotoxicity. This study explores the anticancer potential of Hylocereus undatus peel extracts and their biogenically synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (Z
content: Abstract Cancer treatment faces the challenge of multidrug resistance and systemic cytotoxicity. This study explores the anticancer potential of Hylocereus undatus peel extracts and their biogenically synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). Total phenolics, flavonoids and GC–MS profiles of the extracts were determined. Then, ZnO NPs were synthesized by using aqueous and n-hexane extracts and characterized by FTIR, Zeta Potential, XRD, SEM, EDX, and TEM. Among all tested formulations, ZnO NPs-AE (derived from the aqueous extract) showed the strongest antitumor activity, both in cell culture (Caco‑2 and HepG2) and in the Ehrlich ascites carcinoma mouse model. In MTT assays, ZnO NPs-AE was highly cytotoxic to Caco‑2 and HepG2 cells (IC₅₀ = 9.22 and 12.93 µg/mL, respectively) and performed on the same level as doxorubicin ( p < 0.05). It also showed a more favourable selectivity profile, being less toxic to normal colon fibroblasts (CCD‑18Co; IC₅₀ = 32.35 µg/mL) than to Caco‑2 cells (IC₅₀ = 9.22 µg/mL), which was better than doxorubicin. Consistent with this, ZnO NPs-AE reduced the proportion of cells in G2/M phase (7.39% compared with 12.65% in untreated cells) and increased total apoptosis to 25.98% in Caco‑2 cells. Molecularly, it up-regulated caspase-3 (6.15-fold), down-regulated topoisomerase II (0.33-fold) and suppressed the Wnt/β catenin axis. Consistently, ELISA quantification of Axin2 and Cyclin D1 in Caco‑2 cells confirmed down‑regulation of these Wnt/β‑catenin targets in parallel with the decrease in β‑catenin protein. In vivo, ZnO NPs-AE (5 mg/kg) reduced EAC volume to 89.36%, normalized hepatic/renal biomarkers, improved lipid profiles, and alleviated oxidative stress by elevating GSH, CAT, and SOD levels, while reducing MDA, alongside histopathological improvements. Overall, ZnO NPs-AE represents a promising, well tolerated biogenic nanoplatform for targeted cancer therapy.

title: Overshoot and the Cryosphere: Averting Global Meltdown
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The Implications of Temperature Overshoot, Peak and Decline for the Cryosphere Exceeding the 1.5°C Paris Agreement target will bring large and in many cases irreversible impacts from the Earth’s melting ice sheets, permafrost, glaciers, sea
content: The Implications of Temperature Overshoot, Peak and Decline for the Cryosphere Exceeding the 1.5°C Paris Agreement target will bring large and in many cases irreversible impacts from the Earth’s melting ice sheets, permafrost, glaciers, sea ice and polar oceans. These losses can still be limited if overshoot is kept to a minimum by deep emissions reductions followed by scaled-up carbon drawdown. Overshoot and the Cryosphere: Averting Global Meltdown sets out the global impacts of ice loss with overshoot, exploring which ones are locked in – and how more urgent climate action can still stop or slow the worst of this damage, delivering vital evidence ahead of COP31 in Türkiye. The report lays out out actionable solutions to bring temperatures back down from overshoot. Renewable energy and battery technologies are booming, reliance on coal and oil is slowing, and climate policies have cut emissions in many places. Successful policies now need to be scaled up to reduce emissions by at least 5% per year, starting now, reaching net zero greenhouse gas emissions by mid-century.
