The resulting peptide is inert to modification with iodoacetamide. Consistent with the assignment, TqqB also cross-links Thr30Ala variant of TqqA, which lacks a side chain hydroxyl, forming a Cys25–Gln31 cross-link. Using a Gln31Ala TqqA that had been isotopically enriched with deuterium at Ala 31, we show that the α-carbon deuterium at position 31 is lost upon cross-link formation. NMR analysis of 13C-labeled Gln31Ala variant revealed a 13C chemical shift for the attachment site that is consistent with a thioether and not an ether. Finally, TqqB can form the analogous cross-link in a TqqA peptide spanning residues 22–37, revealing significant tolerance for truncated substrates.

title: Diffusion Monte Carlo Study of Methane-to-Methanol Conversion on Fe– and Mn–MOF Catalysts
summary: Abstract The direct partial oxidation of methane to methanol is an important catalytic challenge, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with open transition-metal sites have emerged as promising candidates for this reaction. However, the comp
content: Abstract The direct partial oxidation of methane to methanol is an important catalytic challenge, and metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with open transition-metal sites have emerged as promising candidates for this reaction. However, the complex electronic structure of their reactive intermediates often limits the reliability of standard density functional theory (DFT) predictions. In this work, we use fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo (FNDMC) to establish accurate reaction energetics for the complete methane-to-methanol conversion pathway using two representative cluster models, Fe2–BTC(Mg) and Mn2–HTPA(Mg). These models represent an Fe-based MOF constructed from 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylate (BTC) linkers and an Mn-based MOF constructed from tris((4-carboxyl)phenylduryl)amine (HTPA) linkers, respectively. FNDMC predicts mildly endothermic O atom adsorption on both systems, with adsorption energies of 0.66(5) and 0.71(4) eV for Fe2–BTC(Mg) and Mn2–HTPA(Mg), respectively. For Fe2–BTC(Mg), FNDMC identifies a septet ground state for the oxygen-bound intermediate, consistent with Fe(III)–oxyl character, whereas all tested DFT functionals favor a quintet state. FNDMC predicts that the C–H activation step is more exothermic for Fe2–BTC(Mg), with a reaction energy of −0.51(6) eV, than for Mn2–HTPA(Mg), for which it is only slightly exothermic at −0.16(6) eV. Methanol desorption is 0.97(7) eV more endothermic on Mn2–HTPA(Mg) than on Fe2–BTC(Mg), indicating stronger product retention despite their similar O atom adsorption energies. These results show that FNDMC captures differences in reaction energetics and electronic structure that standard DFT may miss, providing a robust reference for reactive MOF intermediates.

title: A Novel Phenolic From the Heartwood of Cotinus coggygria Scop. With Potential Neuroprotective Effects: In Silico and In Vitro Studies
summary: ABSTRACT Seven known phenolic compounds ( 2 – 8 ) along with one new phenolic compound ( 1 ) were isolated from the heartwood of Cotinus coggygria Scop. (Anacardiaceae). Among them, compounds 3 – 5 are reported from the genus Cotinus for th
content: ABSTRACT Seven known phenolic compounds ( 2 – 8 ) along with one new phenolic compound ( 1 ) were isolated from the heartwood of Cotinus coggygria Scop. (Anacardiaceae). Among them, compounds 3 – 5 are reported from the genus Cotinus for the first time, while compounds 2 and 6 – 8 are reported from the family Anacardiaceae for the first time. The structure of the new compound was elucidated by detailed spectroscopic analysis, including HR‐ESI‐MS, 1D, and 2D NMR experiments. In vitro assays showed that compound 1 attenuated glutamate‐induced oxidative injury in HT22 cells (EC 50 = 3.852 µM, MTS assay) and inhibited TNF‐α‐induced NF‑κB activation in 293T luciferase reporter cells. Molecular docking suggested that compound 1 may bind to IKKβ, consistent with the observed NF‑κB inhibition. Preliminary structure‐activity relationship trend analysis indicated that compounds possessing a 6″‐ O ‐rhamnose‐containing disaccharide moiety ( 6 – 8 ) showed stronger apparent protective activity than the 6″‐ O ‐galloyl derivatives ( 1 – 5 ) under the present assay conditions. These preliminary findings suggest that cotinusin A ( 1 ) may warrant further investigation for its potential against glutamate‐induced oxidative neuronal injury. However, whether the observed NF‑κB inhibitory activity translates into anti‐neuroinflammatory effects in relevant models remains to be determined, and further mechanistic and in vivo studies are needed to establish its therapeutic potential.

title: Analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution of agricultural production efficiency and its determinants in China
summary: China faces regional disparities in agricultural development. Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution of agricultural production efficiency and its driving factors is essential for advancing sustainable agricultural development. Using pa
content: China faces regional disparities in agricultural development. Understanding the spatiotemporal evolution of agricultural production efficiency and its driving factors is essential for advancing sustainable agricultural development. Using panel data from China’s 31 provinces from 2013 to 2023, we constructed an input–output indicator system and applied the super-efficiency slacks-based measure (SBM) model to evaluate agricultural production efficiency. The results indicate that the evolution of agricultural production efficiency went through three stages. The period from 2013 to 2016 was characterized by fluctuations; the period from 2016 to 2021 was characterized by an overall upward trend; the period from 2021 to 2023 was characterized by a downward trend. The number of provinces with an agricultural production efficiency score of ≥1 increased from 8 to 11. Temporal kernel density analysis revealed that polarization between high- and low-efficiency provinces weakened from 2013 to 2022 but intensified in 2023. Spatial kernel density analysis showed a decline in the spatial clustering of agricultural production efficiency, with high-density zones gradually expanding from coastal areas to inland regions. Geographic detector analysis identifies socioeconomic factors (per capita education expenditure, farmer income, agricultural development level) and agricultural structure (pesticide input, planting structure) as key determinants, with rankings showing moderate sensitivity to temporal aggregation and discretization method but substantive policy priorities remaining consistent. Region-specific issues, including the low comparative returns from agriculture in the eastern region and low production efficiency in the central grain-producing region, underscore the need for countermeasures tailored to regional patterns of agricultural production efficiency across different regions. Such measures could include increased investment in human capital and optimization of crop structures. These findings provide empirical support for region-specific strategies aimed at improving agricultural production efficiency and promoting sustainable agricultural development.

title: An integrated bio- and chemostratigraphic framework for the Triassic–Jurassic boundary interval and its potential for global correlations
summary: The Triassic/Jurassic boundary (TJB) interval records one of the major Phanerozoic mass extinctions, commonly linked to the effects of volcanism of the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province. However, uncertainties persist regarding the age, du
content: The Triassic/Jurassic boundary (TJB) interval records one of the major Phanerozoic mass extinctions, commonly linked to the effects of volcanism of the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province. However, uncertainties persist regarding the age, duration and synchroneity of events across the boundary, largely because of ambiguities in stratigraphic correlations, even among reference TJB sections. Stratigraphic correlations across the TJB have traditionally been based on the δ 13 C record of the sedimentary organic carbon (δ 13 C org ), while the carbonate carbon-isotope record (δ 13 C carb ) has been long considered unreliable. Here, we reassess inorganic carbon-isotope stratigraphy across the TJB using well-preserved skeletal and bulk carbonate δ 13 C records from reference sections of the Northern Calcareous Alps (Austria) and the Laurasian Seaway (UK). These records are used to build a new δ 13 C carb framework that is anchored to ammonite biostratigraphy and complemented with the sequence of negative δ 13 C org excursions adopted in previous studies. We document reproducible δ 13 C carb patterns consisting of: (1) a prominent negative excursion, corresponding to the initial carbon-isotope excursion of the δ 13 C org record in the topmost Marshi Chronozone and characterised by the minimum point “a”, (2) a positive excursion encompassing the TJB herein named “Triassic/Jurassic Boundary Event” and culminating in the positive peak “b” in the top Tilmanni Chronozone, (3) a negative trend to pre-excursion values with the minimum point “c” documented in the Angulata Chronozone and (4) a second positive excursion encompassing the Hettangian/Sinemurian Boundary and culminating in the positive peak “d” in the Semicostatum Chronozone. These δ 13 C carb patterns appear globally reproducible across deep-sea to shallow-water sections and are potentially extended to the δ 13 C carb signature of pedogenic carbonates in continental records, offering a powerful new tool for global basin-to-land correlations and for understanding carbon-cycle perturbations associated with CAMP volcanism.

title: Inverse Model Inferred Time Series of Photosynthesis Parameters From Three Decades of Primary Production Measurements
summary: Abstract Understanding how phytoplankton photosynthetic physiology varies over seasonal to multi‐decadal time scales is important for assessing changes in ocean productivity and its role in the carbon cycle. Here we show that, at the Bermud
content: Abstract Understanding how phytoplankton photosynthetic physiology varies over seasonal to multi‐decadal time scales is important for assessing changes in ocean productivity and its role in the carbon cycle. Here we show that, at the Bermuda Atlantic Time‐series Study and Hawaii Ocean Time‐series stations, photosynthesis parameters exhibit pronounced seasonal and shorter‐term variability but no statistically significant multi‐decadal trends over more than three decades of observations. To investigate these temporal patterns, we use in situ chlorophyll and primary production profiles together with an inverse model to reconstruct long‐term time series of photosynthesis parameters. The two time series stations have surpassed the 30‐year mark, making data collected there suitable for climatological research. A shifted Gaussian is used as a model for the chlorophyll profile and an exactly solvable model of the production profile is used to infer photosynthesis parameters from measured production profiles. The models yielded high coefficients of determination, which enabled the construction of thirty‐year‐long time series of photosynthesis parameters. The seasonal cycle and long‐term changes in the parameters were analyzed. No statistically significant long‐term trends were detected in the estimated photosynthesis parameters, while substantial variability was observed on shorter time scales. The results highlight the importance of accounting for temporal variability in photosynthesis parameters when modeling ocean primary production.

title: Molecular MRI of Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's Disease using a Folate-targeted Nanoprobe
summary: Background: Neuroinflammation, driven by activated microglia, plays a central role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Non-invasive imaging of neuroinflammation holds promise for advancing our understanding of disease mechanism
content: Background: Neuroinflammation, driven by activated microglia, plays a central role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Non-invasive imaging of neuroinflammation holds promise for advancing our understanding of disease mechanisms and evaluating anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategies. The folate receptor (FR), specifically its β isoform, has been identified as a marker of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells in peripheral inflammatory diseases; however, its association with AD neuroinflammation remains unknown. In this work, we first determined FR expression in microglia in mouse models of AD and subsequently evaluated molecular MRI (mMRI) using a folate-targeted nanoprobe for in vivo imaging of the folate receptor expression. Methods and results: Microglial activation and FR expression in APP/PS1 and P301S transgenic mouse models of AD was measured using flow cytometry. A FR-targeted nanoprobe for mMRI was prepared by functionalizing high T1-relaxivity liposomal gadolinium nanoparticle with folic acid. Following intravenous injection, localization of the nanoprobe in the brains of aged transgenic and wild-type mice was measured using T1-weighted MRI. Post-mortem microscopy measured nanoprobe localization relative to microglia and amyloid pathology. In both mouse models, FRβ was significantly (p < 0.05) upregulated in pro-inflammatory microglia expressing TNF and IL-1β. The folate-targeted nanoprobe demonstrated MR signal enhancement in the cortical and hippocampal regions of transgenic mice but not in wild type mice; non-targeted nanoprobe control did not demonstrate signal enhancement in brain of transgenic mice. Microscopy confirmed colocalization of FR-targeted nanoprobe with IBA1-positive microglia/macrophages and amyloid plaques. Conclusions: Pro-inflammatory microglia exhibit elevated levels of FR, and its measurement by non-invasive mMRI is a promising marker of neuroinflammation in AD.

title: Preoperative cardiopulmonary variability assessment for predicting postoperative adverse events following thoracic surgery: A systematic review
summary: Abstract Objectives: Postoperative adverse events (AEs) remain a major source of morbidity and mortality following thoracic surgery. Current preoperative risk assessment tools have limited ability to predict individual postoperative complic
content: Abstract Objectives: Postoperative adverse events (AEs) remain a major source of morbidity and mortality following thoracic surgery. Current preoperative risk assessment tools have limited ability to predict individual postoperative complications. Cardiopulmonary variability assessment (CPVA), including heart rate variability (HRV) and respiratory rate variability (RRV), has emerged as a potential biomarker of autonomic function and physiologic reserve. This systematic review evaluated the role of preoperative CPVA in predicting postoperative AEs following thoracic surgery. Methods: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. MEDLINE and Embase were searched from inception to identify studies evaluating preoperative HRV and/or RRV as predictors of postoperative AEs in adults undergoing thoracic surgery. Eligible study designs included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, case-control studies, and diagnostic accuracy studies. Study characteristics, CPVA methodology, comparator assessments, postoperative outcomes, and risk of bias were extracted and evaluated using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale and QUADAS-2. Results: Five cohort studies comprising 693 patients met the inclusion criteria. Four studies evaluated pulmonary resection for non-small cell lung cancer and one evaluated esophagectomy. Three studies assessed HRV directly, while two evaluated functional measures of cardiopulmonary reserve. Reduced preoperative HRV, particularly lower root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) and high-frequency power (HFP), was associated with postoperative pneumonia, atrial fibrillation, and delirium. Lower RMSSD (OR 0.812, 95% CI 0.720–0.912) and HFP (OR 0.990, 95% CI 0.983–0.996) independently predicted postoperative pneumonia, with good discrimination (AUC 0.867). Risk of bias was low to moderate. Conclusions: Preoperative CPVA, particularly HRV, is a promising non-invasive biomarker for predicting postoperative AEs following thoracic surgery. Reduced HRV was consistently associated with pulmonary, cardiac, and neurologic complications. Larger prospective multicentre studies using standardized acquisition and analysis protocols are required to establish the incremental value of CPVA beyond current preoperative risk assessment tools.

title: Water- and Alkali-Stable Cellulose Nanocrystal Films via Synergistic Citric Acid Cross-Linking and Poly(vinyl alcohol) Incorporation for Hydroxide-Conducting Membranes
summary: Abstract Cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) are promising reinforcing materials for biopolymer films, but their poor stability in water and alkaline environments limits their application in alkaline energy-conversion systems. In this study, CNC-b
content: Abstract Cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) are promising reinforcing materials for biopolymer films, but their poor stability in water and alkaline environments limits their application in alkaline energy-conversion systems. In this study, CNC-based composite films (CNC/CP) were fabricated through a simple aqueous suspension-casting method using citric acid (CA) as a green cross-linker and poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA, 10 wt%) as a secondary polymer. The cross-linking degree was controlled by varying the CA content from 10 to 30 wt% relative to CNC, followed by heat treatment to promote esterification. The combined effect of CA cross-linking and PVA incorporation greatly improved the film performance. The CNC/CP films showed excellent water stability, with low swelling values of ∼6.66% and 20% after 960 h at room temperature and 80 °C. Mechanical performance was also improved, with the optimized CNC/CP film showing a 109.9% increase in tensile strength and a 590.3% increase in toughness compared with the pristine CNC film. The hydroxide-ion conductivities of CNC/CP films reached up to 122.64 mS cm–1 at 25 °C and 157.99 mS cm–1 at 80 °C in 1 M KOH. Moreover, the CNC/CP films showed good alkaline stability, retaining hydroxide-ion conductivities of 29.32–48.25 mS cm–1 after soaking in 1 M KOH for 720 h. These results show that citric acid cross-linking combined with PVA incorporation is an effective strategy to produce stable, mechanically robust, and conductive CNC-based films for further alkaline energy-conversion applications.

title: Synthesis of Sulfate Chitosan using a Sulfuric-Acid Method Based on Chitosan Obtained from Non-Commercial Artemia parthenogenetica Cysts from the Aral Sea
source: Journal of the Turkish Chemical Society Section A Chemistry
summary: The study reports the synthesis and physicochemical characterization of sulfated chitosan (SCh) obtained from chitosan isolated from non-commercial Artemia parthenogenetica cysts of the Aral Sea using a sulfuric acid-mediated sulfation meth
content: The study reports the synthesis and physicochemical characterization of sulfated chitosan (SCh) obtained from chitosan isolated from non-commercial Artemia parthenogenetica cysts of the Aral Sea using a sulfuric acid-mediated sulfation method. The obtained SCh was a dark-brown powder containing 9.21% sulfur and exhibiting a degree of substitution of 22.0%. Elemental analysis and FTIR spectroscopy confirmed the incorporation of sulfate groups into the chitosan structure. Characteristic sulfate-related absorption bands were observed at 1032 and 1385 cm⁻¹, corresponding to O–S–O and sulfate-group stretching vibrations, respectively. Size-exclusion chromatography revealed that the obtained SCh consisted predominantly of low-molecular-weight fractions of approximately 1.0 and 3.0 kDa, indicating partial degradation of the chitosan chains under the acidic conditions of the sulfation process. The obtained results demonstrate the feasibility of producing low-molecular-weight SCh from non-commercial Artemia parthenogenetica cysts of the Aral Sea.

title: Phytogenic Synthesis of Platinum Nanoparticles: Characterization and In Vitro Biological Evaluation of Antioxidant, Antimicrobial, and Anticancer Activities
summary: ABSTRACT This study presents the eco‐friendly synthesis of platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs) utilizing Coleus barbatus leaf extract as both a reducing and stabilizing agent. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) identified key biomole
content: ABSTRACT This study presents the eco‐friendly synthesis of platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs) utilizing Coleus barbatus leaf extract as both a reducing and stabilizing agent. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) identified key biomolecules, including ascorbic acid, terpenoids, amino acids, and hydrocarbons, responsible for reducing platinum ions. X‐ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed a face‐centered cubic (FCC) crystal structure with a crystallite size of 62 nm. Zeta potential measurements, ranging from 9.4 to 11.8 mV, indicated moderate colloidal stability. Morphological characterization via scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and high‐resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) revealed spherical PtNPs with diameters between 42 and 65 nm. The biological efficacy of the synthesized PtNPs was assessed through antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anticancer assays. The NPs demonstrated significant antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli (Gram‐negative) and Staphylococcus aureus (Gram‐positive), effectively inhibiting bacterial growth. Antioxidant evaluation showed strong free radical scavenging capabilities, particularly against superoxide ions and hydroxyl radicals. Furthermore, cytotoxicity tests on the MCF‐7 breast cancer cell line revealed potent anticancer properties, yielding an IC 50 value of 2.28. These findings underscore the potential of C. barbatus ‐mediated PtNPs as effective agents for antimicrobial treatments, antioxidant applications, and cancer therapy, highlighting the promise of green chemistry in nanomedicine.

title: A deacetylase governs thermotolerance and pathogenicity by regulating host amino-acid utilization in Cryptococcus neoformans
summary: Thermotolerance is critical for fungal survival in vivo , yet how metabolic remodeling enables pathogenic fungi such as Cryptococcus neoformans to withstand heat stress remains unclear. Here, we identify the protein deacetylase Dac6 as a th
content: Thermotolerance is critical for fungal survival in vivo , yet how metabolic remodeling enables pathogenic fungi such as Cryptococcus neoformans to withstand heat stress remains unclear. Here, we identify the protein deacetylase Dac6 as a thermotolerance regulator in C. neoformans functioning independently of the yeast deacetylase Rpd3 and mirroring the heat-resistant phenotype of clinical isolates. Integrated multi-omics analyses reveal that Dac6 remodels histone acetylation and gene expression to reprogram amino acid metabolism under heat stress, thereby enhancing lysine and threonine utilization. Lysine and threonine are also among the most markedly altered metabolites in the host during cryptococcal infection, and Dac6 deletion impairs fungal utilization of these amino acids under heat stress in vitro and in vivo . Consequently, Dac6 deficiency leads to reduced lung and brain colonization and attenuated virulence in mice. Thus, Dac6 couples nutrient utilization to thermal adaptation, revealing a chromatin-guided metabolic strategy that supports fungal survival in the host.

title: D-Cysteine preserves postharvest quality of fresh-cut button mushrooms by regulating antioxidant defense system and activating H2S biosynthesis
summary: Consumers favor fresh-cut button mushrooms, yet their shelf life is hampered by rapid quality decline. This research investigates the effects of a 0.5 g/L D -cysteine ( D -Cys) application on the quality and physiological responses of fresh
content: Consumers favor fresh-cut button mushrooms, yet their shelf life is hampered by rapid quality decline. This research investigates the effects of a 0.5 g/L D -cysteine ( D -Cys) application on the quality and physiological responses of fresh-cut button mushrooms. Findings reveal that D -Cys application notably postponed the mushrooms browning, curtailed weight reduction, and decreased malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, lipoxygenase (LOX) activity, and increase the levels of reducing sugars. Concurrently, it boosted soluble protein content. Moreover, D -Cys mitigated the generation of superoxide anions (O 2 − ) and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) while reducing catalase (CAT) activity. It also enhanced the activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione reductase (GR), and phenylalanine ammonia-lyase (PAL), and diminished those of polyphenol oxidase (PPO) and peroxidase (POD). Furthermore, treatment with D -Cys significantly stimulated the endogenous production of hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) in fresh-cut button mushrooms. This effect was accompanied by an enhancement in the activity of enzymes AbCBS, AbCSE, and AbMST, which are crucial in the metabolic pathways associated with sulfur metabolism. However, the beneficial effects of D -Cys were significantly diminished when mushrooms were co-treated with 1 mmol/L propargylglycine (PAG). Additionally, transcriptome sequencing analysis revealed that the genes with differential expression in the D -Cys group were mainly associated with oxidation–reduction process, cysteine metabolic process, cysteine biosynthetic process, oxidoreductase activity, POD activity, and sulfur metabolism. Collectively, these results indicate that D -Cys maintains the quality of fresh-cut button mushroom by regulating the antioxidant enzyme activity, converting to endogenous H 2 S, and converting to L- cysteine ( L -Cys).

title: Isolation, Characterisation, Simultaneous Quantification and In Vitro Cytotoxicity Assessment of Iguratimod and Its Degradation Products
summary: ABSTRACT Iguratimod (IGU) is a novel cytokine inhibitor clinically approved for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. The structural features of the drug reveal several potential labile sites, including the sulphonamide group, formamide mo
content: ABSTRACT Iguratimod (IGU) is a novel cytokine inhibitor clinically approved for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. The structural features of the drug reveal several potential labile sites, including the sulphonamide group, formamide moiety and aryl–aryl ether linkage, all of which are susceptible to hydrolytic cleavage. The current study is undertaken with the objectives of developing a stability‐indicating high‐performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) assay for simultaneous quantification of IGU and its degradation products (DPs), characterisation and cytotoxicity assessment of the DPs. The present study investigates the forced degradation behaviour of IGU under various stress conditions. The DPs were separated and characterised by high‐resolution mass spectrometry and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. A possible degradation mechanism was proposed. A selective stability‐indicating HPLC assay was developed for the quantification of the drug and its DPs. In vitro cytotoxicity of the DP was assessed using the MTT cell viability and DNA ladder assays, whilst DNA damage markers were monitored by western blotting. The drug was susceptible to degradation under acidic and basic conditions, yielding two DPs. The acid DP exhibited a distinct capacity to compromise genomic stability. These results suggest that the conversion of IGU to its DP under acidic conditions confers significant DNA‐damaging properties. Given that the acid degradant is also a major metabolite of IGU, a thorough toxicological evaluation is warranted. Owing to the facile formation of the acid DP, the developed method can be applied to monitor IGU and its degradation during processing with acidic excipients and dissolution testing samples in an acidic medium. The method can also be modified to monitor IGU and acid degradants from plasma samples.

title: Polyfluorene Containing Dibenzothiophene‐ S,S ‐Dioxide and Benzothiadiazole Units for Fluorescent Response to Metal Ions
summary: ABSTRACT The green light‐emitting polymer (PF‐SO10‐BT1) was prepared by the Suzuki polycondensation method, during which dibenzothiophene‐ S,S ‐dioxide (SO) and 2,1,3‐benzothiadiazole (BT) units were incorporated into the polyfluorene (PF)
content: ABSTRACT The green light‐emitting polymer (PF‐SO10‐BT1) was prepared by the Suzuki polycondensation method, during which dibenzothiophene‐ S,S ‐dioxide (SO) and 2,1,3‐benzothiadiazole (BT) units were incorporated into the polyfluorene (PF) backbone. Both the SO and BT units possessed strong electron‐deficient ability in PF‐SO10‐BT1, which can form a donor/acceptor structure with the fluorene unit, exhibiting intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) characteristics. The number‐average molecular weight ( M n ) of PF‐SO10‐BT1 was 36.5 kDa with a polydispersity index (PDI) of 2.08. This molecular weight was beneficial for dissolution in polar solvents while also being able to achieve green light emission through the ICT effect. The photoluminescence quantum yield ( Φ PL ) of PF‐SO10‐BT1 in N,N ‐dimethylacetamide solution was as high as 77.6%, which can provide sufficient fluorescence signal intensity under low concentration conditions. PF‐SO10‐BT1 exhibited cross‐sensitivity under gradual addition of metal ion solutions with multiple mixing cycles, whereas distinct response behavior was observed after the direct addition of metal ion solutions with a single mixing cycle. The limit of detection (LOD) of PF‐SO10‐BT1 for Fe 3+ was 20.7 µM. These results provide insights into the structure–property relationships of conjugated polymers incorporating the SO and BT units and valuable guidance for the further structural design of analogous conjugated polymers.

title: IFT–Wettability Interplay and Force-Regime Transition in Chemical EOR: A Mechanistic SI/FI Diagnostic Approach
summary: Despite the crucial role of enhanced oil recovery (EOR) in meeting rising energy demands, interpretation of chemical EOR (CEOR) performance is limited by reliance on interfacial tension (IFT) and contact angle (CA) data. Most studies correl
content: Despite the crucial role of enhanced oil recovery (EOR) in meeting rising energy demands, interpretation of chemical EOR (CEOR) performance is limited by reliance on interfacial tension (IFT) and contact angle (CA) data. Most studies correlate IFT and CA with core flooding results, masking the contribution of capillary and gravity forces. The study introduces a force-isolation workflow that distinguishes capillary-, viscous-, and gravity-governed recovery by combining spontaneous imbibition (SI) and forced imbibition (FI) experiments conducted on clay-rich Bandera Gray sandstone cores. The key novelty is a modified Amott cell that applies controlled hydraulic pressure heads (10–30 cm) during the FI experiment, which allows measuring the lowest pressure to trigger oil displacement in every fluid system. Four injection systems—high-salinity (HS) brine, low-salinity (LS) brine, an anionic surfactant (sodium lauryl sulfate, SLS), and a cationic surfactant (cetyltrimethylammonium bromide, CTAB)—are selected to induce interfacial conditions. SLS generates high capillary pressure and a near-zero contact angle, promoting capillary-assisted viscous FI at the lowest pressure threshold, achieving 41% SI recovery and an SI/FI ratio of ~80%. By contrast, CTAB produces a low IFT but insufficient capillary pressure, resulting in gravity-driven SI with 5% recovery and viscous-dominated FI, with an SI/FI ratio of ~9%. The brine systems exhibit viscous-assisted capillary recovery, requiring the highest entry pressure. The SI/FI ratio classifies the force regimes, confirming that capillary support governs mobility control under SI and FI conditions. This force-regime approach provides a more reliable basis for CEOR formulation design than IFT and CA screening alone.

title: Biophysical characterization and antibacterial activity of green-synthesized silver nanoparticles from pomegranate (Punica granatum) peel extract against multidrug-resistant clinical isolates
source: Journal of Medical and Health Studies
summary: For several common infections, the spread of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria has narrowed the range of usable antibiotics. Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are one candidate replacement, and making them with plant extracts keeps both the cos
content: For several common infections, the spread of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria has narrowed the range of usable antibiotics. Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are one candidate replacement, and making them with plant extracts keeps both the cost and the use of toxic reagents low. We set out to make AgNPs with pomegranate peel extract, describe their properties, and see how well they act on MDR isolates from patients and how toxic they are to Vero cells. An aqueous peel extract, with no other reducing agent, was added to 1 mM silver nitrate. The resulting particles were characterized using UV–visible and FTIR spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, dynamic light scattering and zeta-potential measurement. Five patient isolates were tested by agar well diffusion, broth microdilution (MIC/MBC) and time-kill experiments; Vero cell toxicity was measured by MTT. SPR peak at 425 nm, almost unchanged after 30 days at 4 °C. FTIR band shifts (phenolic O–H, C=O) implicated extract polyphenols in reduction and capping. TEM: spherical particles, 22.5 ± 6.1 nm; DLS: 38.6 nm, PDI 0.21; zeta potential −28.4 mV. The lowest MIC (8 µg/mL) was recorded for Escherichia coli and the highest (32 µg/mL) for both methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Klebsiella pneumoniae. At 2× MIC, viable counts dropped by 3 log₁₀ within 8 h (E. coli) and 12 h (MRSA). The Vero IC₅₀ was 112.4 µg/mL (selectivity index 3.5–14.1). The peel-derived AgNPs were bactericidal against MDR isolates at concentrations under the Vero IC₅₀. Topical rather than systemic use looks like the most realistic application.

title: Synthesis of SnO2 and TiO2 Semiconductor Quantum Dots for Hydrogen Gas Evolution through Water Splitting Reaction
summary: This paper reports on the synthesis, characterization of tin dioxide (SnO2) as well as titanium dioxide (TiO2) quantum dots (QDs) and compare their potential production of hydrogen gas (H2) through photocatalytic water splitting reaction. O
content: This paper reports on the synthesis, characterization of tin dioxide (SnO2) as well as titanium dioxide (TiO2) quantum dots (QDs) and compare their potential production of hydrogen gas (H2) through photocatalytic water splitting reaction. One pot synthesis of SnO2 QDs was prepared through thermal pyrolysis of tin stearate under non-hydrolytic approach. On the other hand, synthesis of TiO2 QDs was prepared through the mild condition of TiCl4 with the use of icy bath. According to HRTEM image, the shape of SnO2 QDs is almost quasi-spherical and TiO2 QDs is almost spherical in shape. Both nanoparticles have diameter ranged in 1-10 nm, while XRD patterns are matched well with standard pattern of SnO2 and TiO2 QDs, respectively. Optical studies reveal that both SnO2 and TiO2 are of UV-active compounds and hence, can be selected as the candidates for hydrogen production through UV activated photocatalytic water splitting reaction.

title: Influence of 6‐Trifluoromethyluracil Versus Chloride Counterions in the Properties of Bis‐(1,10‐Phenanthroline)chloridecopper(II) Motif: Spectroscopic and In Vitro Biological Activity Assays
summary: Copper(II) metallonucleases have emerged as a promising class of compounds to serve as alternatives to the platinum drugs. Here, we evaluated how different counterions, 6‐trifluoromethyluracil (6tfmu) and chloride, impact the biological act
content: Copper(II) metallonucleases have emerged as a promising class of compounds to serve as alternatives to the platinum drugs. Here, we evaluated how different counterions, 6‐trifluoromethyluracil (6tfmu) and chloride, impact the biological activity of copper(II) complexes containing the bis‐(1,10‐phenanthroline)chloridecopper(II) motif. Compounds were characterized by chemical and spectroscopic measurements. Crystallographic studies were conducted for [Cu(phen) 2 Cl]6tfmu (1), while data from complex [Cu(phen) 2 Cl]Cl (2) were previously described. In vitro antiproliferative assays demonstrated that both complexes exhibited lower IC 50 values than cisplatin, with melanoma A375 cells as the most sensitive, being 1.3 and 0.9 µM 1 and 2, respectively. Both compounds bind DNA to an indistinguishable extent, through a hybrid mode combining minor‐groove recognition with partial intercalation of a single phenanthroline ligand. Molecular dynamics performed on the common [Cu(phen) 2 Cl] + cation and microplate fluorophore assays converge on this mode. The main reactive oxygen species generated by complexes 1 and 2 were ·OH and H 2 O 2 , respectively. Substrate depletion assays in a human Topoisomerase‐I‐mediated DNA relaxation experiment indicated the preference of the [Cu(phen) 2 ] 2+ motif for degrading the DNA substrate over directly inhibiting the enzyme itself. The counterion modulates antibacterial potency and identity of the dominant reactive species, while leaving DNA recognition by the shared cation essentially unchanged.

title: Electrosprayed dry powder formulations of paclitaxel/carboplatin for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer
summary: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for about 85% of all cases. Current emerging treatment options still show limited clinical benefit, making chemotherapy a
content: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounting for about 85% of all cases. Current emerging treatment options still show limited clinical benefit, making chemotherapy an important part of NSCLC management. Although multiple clinical trials have demonstrated the efficacy of carboplatin combined with paclitaxel in patients with NSCLC, adverse reactions and safety concerns associated with traditional chemotherapy administration remain significant, highlighting the need for alternative drug delivery strategies. Pulmonary drug delivery enables direct drug deposition in the lungs with reduced systemic exposure. Dry powder formulations provide an alternative to liquid aerosol systems for pulmonary drug delivery, with electrospraying offering a flexible approach for preparing inhalable dry powder particles. In this study, electrosprayed particles based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and chitosan were developed and optimised for the pulmonary delivery of paclitaxel and carboplatin. The particles were characterised using electron microscopy, laser diffraction, and next-generation impactor, and their biological performance was evaluated in A549 and Calu-3 cells. Despite a primary particle size below 1 μm, particle aggregation led to volumetric and aerodynamic diameters within the optimal range (1-5 μm) for pulmonary deposition. The formulations showed low moisture content (<3% w/w) with good aerosol performance, achieving over 80% emitted dose and the highest effective fine particle fraction of 58.61 ± 0.83%. Both drugs were successfully encapsulated with a rapid release of 70-90% within the first 2 h. Chitosan coating increased particle adhesion and cell interaction, and cell viability studies confirmed cytotoxic effects against A549 cells over 72 h.

title: Ambitious emission reductions maintain Earth resilience, conditional on climate and carbon feedbacks and tipping points
summary: Earth resilience is a guiding principle for navigating safe futures in the Anthropocene, but operational quantification remains limited. We introduce a path-based resilience indicator estimating the probability of returning to a safe Holoce
content: Earth resilience is a guiding principle for navigating safe futures in the Anthropocene, but operational quantification remains limited. We introduce a path-based resilience indicator estimating the probability of returning to a safe Holocene-like state by 2100 via the share of trajectories that fulfil not only temperature-but also dynamic warming rate-and tipping safety demands, rendering it effective for analyses of overshoot. It is conditioned on emission scenarios and analysed considering uncertainties in climate and carbon sensitivity and tipping dynamics. We find that a net-zero-by-2050 scenario has an estimated resilience of 34%, in contrast to <1% for current policies. To gain ∼10%pt resilience, emissions need to be cut by 35% in 2035 compared to an NDC scenario. On average, 7.3%pt are gained with every 5 years of decarbonising earlier than 2050. Therefore, early decarbonisation can hedge against the risk of tipping and strong climate and carbon feedbacks.

title: Evaluating CMAQ Representation of Wildfire PM₂.₅ in California (2008–2018): Regime-Dependent Performance and Nonlinear Error Structure
summary: Abstract We evaluated daily paired Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) estimates and observations during California fire seasons (June–October), 2008–2018, using conventional metrics, classifications at 12 and 35 µg m⁻³, two case studie
content: Abstract We evaluated daily paired Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) estimates and observations during California fire seasons (June–October), 2008–2018, using conventional metrics, classifications at 12 and 35 µg m⁻³, two case studies, and a leakage-resistant Random Forest diagnostic. After quarantining 18 CMAQ total PM₂.₅ values above 557 µg m⁻³ without capping, the primary analysis contained 187,051 records. Observed and modeled means were 10.69 and 9.29 µg m⁻³; Pearson r was 0.502 (r² = 0.252), mean bias was − 1.40 µg m⁻³, and RMSE was 9.96 µg m⁻³. CMAQ detected 45.4% of observed events at the descriptive/former annual level of 12 µg m⁻³ and 40.8% at the current 35 µg m⁻³ 24-hour standard level. At 35 µg m⁻³, CMAQ produced more events overall but missed 1,273 of 2,151 observed events because modeled and observed events often did not coincide by site-day. The Random Forest excluded observed PM₂.₅, CMAQ total PM₂.₅, and the no-fire component from its primary features. In an untouched site-year test partition (n = 37,430), R² was 0.711, RMSE was 5.82 µg m⁻³, and MAE was 3.44 µg m⁻³; fire-only CMAQ PM₂.₅ was the dominant predictor. CMAQ remains useful for regional and multi-year analyses, but paired-event detection and localized extreme-smoke estimates require explicit uncertainty treatment.

title: Synergistic graphene immobilization and electrolyte engineering enables durable lithiated organic cathodes
summary: Lithiated small-molecule organic carbonyl compounds are promising cathode candidates for lithium-ion batteries yet suffer from severe electrolyte dissolution and low electronic conductivity, which severely compromise their cycling stability
content: Lithiated small-molecule organic carbonyl compounds are promising cathode candidates for lithium-ion batteries yet suffer from severe electrolyte dissolution and low electronic conductivity, which severely compromise their cycling stability and rate capability. Herein, we propose a synergistic strategy combining graphene immobilization and localized high-concentration electrolyte (LHCE) regulation to overcome these limitations. Specifically, a typical lithiated cathode, 8 O-4Li, is uniformly anchored on graphene via π–π interactions, constructing a conductive composite (8 O-4Li@G) with inhibited molecular dissolution and accelerated electron transfer. The LHCE further suppresses solvent-induced active material loss. The integrated design enables the 8 O-4Li@G composite to deliver a high reversible capacity of 219 mAh g −1 at 0.02 A g −1 with a high average discharge voltage of 3.5 V, achieving a remarkable energy density of ~760 Wh kg −1 based on the mass of 8O-4Li. Furthermore, it achieves impressive cycling stability with 96% capacity retention over 300 cycles at 1 A g −1 and superior rate capability. This work presents an effective strategy to unlock the full potential of lithiated organic cathodes for high-energy-density batteries.

title: Self-aggregation separation of microplastics from water induced by topological cationic organogels
summary: This work reveals a novel functionality and mechanism for the electric field-induced self-aggregation separation of microplastics from water, mediated by a topological cationic organogel. Nine self-synthesized topological cationic organogel
content: This work reveals a novel functionality and mechanism for the electric field-induced self-aggregation separation of microplastics from water, mediated by a topological cationic organogel. Nine self-synthesized topological cationic organogels were adopted as model probe materials, and analysis of their structure–activity relationships revealed that the densely secondary-crosslinked poly(amine salt) gel (PMASG) exhibited a superior treatment capacity of 2426.80 mg/g for polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs), significantly outperforming most reported analogous materials. Furthermore, PMASG maintained a stable treatment performance in different water environments and for various types of other microplastics (PET, PVC, PTFE), and achieved efficient removal in ultra-dilute systems with microplastic concentrations as low as 0.01 mg/L, demonstrating excellent practical application potential. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated that the post-treatment residue can be completely thermally degraded under an inert atmosphere and possesses favorable combustion characteristics in air (ignition temperature: 328.96 °C, burnout temperature: 761.9 °C, comprehensive combustion characteristic index: 3.39 × 10 −5 ), enabling the elimination of post-treatment solid waste and achieving a green cycle for valorization. Based on kinetic/thermodynamic behavior studies and multi-spectroscopic micro/mesoscopic structural evolution analysis, a novel localized electrostatic-induced nucleation-driven self-aggregation (LEIN-SA) mechanism was established. In this mechanism, the topological cationic network of PMASG generates a localized electrostatic field that destabilizes and captures nearby microplastics, leading to the formation of a critical PMASG–PS composite cluster (nucleus). and subsequently driving the rapid aggregation of microplastics in water. In summary, this study develops a new strategy for water microplastic pollution remediation that combines ultra-high efficiency and total environmental friendliness.

title: Smog effects on health and traffic accidents before & during COVID-19 in Faisalabad, Pakistan
source: Journal of Environmental Science Health & Sustainability
summary: Smog is a seasonal environmental and public health concern in urban regions where interactions between atmospheric conditions, anthropogenic activities, and human exposure may influence health and safety outcomes. This study investigated th
content: Smog is a seasonal environmental and public health concern in urban regions where interactions between atmospheric conditions, anthropogenic activities, and human exposure may influence health and safety outcomes. This study investigated the associations between seasonal smog conditions, health outcomes, and visibility-related traffic risks in Faisalabad, Pakistan, during the smog season (September–November), comparing pre-COVID (2016–2019) and COVID-19 (2020) periods. An integrated dataset comprising hospital records, community questionnaire surveys, visibility observations, and traffic accident statistics was analyzed to evaluate multiple dimensions of smog-related impacts. Hospital records from outpatient and emergency departments were examined for respiratory tract infections, bronchial asthma, allergic conjunctivitis, stroke, and ischemic heart disease. Hospital records showed temporal variation across study years, with fewer recorded visits during the 2020 COVID-19 period. Survey responses indicated that urban residents generally experienced more frequent smog-related symptoms than rural residents, particularly respiratory discomfort and eye irritation. Visibility analysis demonstrated an inverse association between reduced visibility and traffic accident severity, with lower visibility levels corresponding to higher numbers of accident victims and casualties. Because direct measurements of ambient pollutants were unavailable, the observed changes cannot be attributed solely to variations in air pollutant concentrations. Instead, these findings represent the combined influence of environmental conditions, social changes, mobility patterns, and healthcare-seeking behavior during the COVID-19 period. This study provides an integrated evaluation of seasonal smog impacts by linking medical records, community-level health perceptions, visibility conditions, and traffic accident patterns in Faisalabad. Unlike previous studies that primarily examined individual components of air pollution impacts, this approach provides a broader understanding of the environmental and societal consequences associated with seasonal smog episodes.

title: Quantitative 2D HSQC with Non-Uniform Sampling for the Determination of Paracetamol in Compound Preparations
summary: Paracetamol (APAP) is a common active ingredient of compound cold preparations, and its routine one-dimensional 1H-NMR quantification is compromised by overlap with the aromatic signals of co-formulated caffeine and chlorpheniramine. A rapi
content: Paracetamol (APAP) is a common active ingredient of compound cold preparations, and its routine one-dimensional 1H-NMR quantification is compromised by overlap with the aromatic signals of co-formulated caffeine and chlorpheniramine. A rapid method based on two-dimensional 1H−13C HSQC combined with non-uniform sampling (NUS) was established: with DMSO-d6 as the extraction solvent and 1,4-dinitrobenzene (δH = 8.45 ppm) as internal standard, the cross-peaks at δH/δC = 7.33/121.26 and 6.67/115.44 ppm serve as two independent quantitative channels, requiring neither chromatographic separation nor an analyte-matched reference standard. Under the optimised conditions the acquisition time per sample was 26′35″, one quarter of that of uniformly sampled HSQC (108′25″). The method was linear over 0.625–40.0 g•L−1 (R2 = 0.9999) with LOD 0.397 g•L−1 and LOQ 1.20 g•L−1; precision was 0.5 %–0.74 % RSD, 48 h stability 0.83 % RSD, and recovery 98.15 %–99.89 %. The results for ten commercial preparations (capsules, tablets and a granule) deviated from the pharmacopoeial HPLC method by less than 4 % — Bland–Altman bias +0.93 % with 95 % limits of agreement of −2.1 % to +3.9 % and no significant systematic bias (paired t-test, p = 0.09) — and from the label claims by less than ±2 %; the lowest content verified experimentally was 1.2 % w/w, and lower contents were not examined and should not be extrapolated. The method is simple to operate, determines APAP in compound preparations rapidly and accurately, and provides a reference for the quality control of manufacturers and regulatory authorities.

title: A subnational approach to energy transition costs in Venezuela
summary: Venezuela's prolonged electricity crisis, characterized by frequent blackouts and deteriorating generation assets, has received renewed attention amid recent geopolitical tensions. Systematic analysis of the power sector remains severely co
content: Venezuela's prolonged electricity crisis, characterized by frequent blackouts and deteriorating generation assets, has received renewed attention amid recent geopolitical tensions. Systematic analysis of the power sector remains severely constrained by data scarcity, limited transparency, and the absence of reliable state-level generation statistics. This study addresses these constraints by adopting a state-based framework and reconstructing electricity generation capacity by converting annual energy figures into required capacity using generic capacity factors, based on historical infrastructure development and fuel availability. With this reconstructed dataset, we evaluate three investment scenarios and their associated economic outcomes. Results show that maintaining the current system without new investment minimizes short-term costs but fails to resolve reliability failures. In contrast, targeted investments yield heterogeneous benefits. States with existing gas infrastructure favor natural gas generation, while resource-rich regions achieve lower costs through renewable deployment. Leveraging existing infrastructure and localized resource endowments is essential for stabilizing Venezuela's electricity system under institutional and data limitations.

title: The First Computed Snugness — a parameter-free occupancy, so carbon, iron and gold finally have values
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Paper 75 §3 named the missing object exactly: "a first-principles cavity definition that computes for arbitrary nuclei from the packing geometry — carbon, iron and gold have never had a computed value, only defaults." After P69/D20 every sn
content: Paper 75 §3 named the missing object exactly: "a first-principles cavity definition that computes for arbitrary nuclei from the packing geometry — carbon, iron and gold have never had a computed value, only defaults." After P69/D20 every snugness number in the corpus is the measured mass relabelled. This paper supplies the first definition that provably is not, because nothing measured goes in — no masses, no binding energies, no fitted coefficients. Only the zeros of spherical Bessel functions, the same mode table as the three-peaks derivation. The definition, declared before any value: fill A nucleons bottom-up through the cavity's modes (degeneracy 4(2l+1) per level, levels ordered by Bessel zero); divided by the cumulative capacity of every level touched. exactly at a closure; it dips just after. This record holds one paper on its own and is refreshed every couple of months. The complete deposit, 10.5281/zenodo.21788037, holds every paper with its code and data and is updated first; for the newest version of this paper, go there.

title: Allergic sensitization to airborne pollens in Brazil
summary: Introduction: Pollen-induced respiratory diseases represent a growing health burden in Brazil, influenced by environmental exposures and climate change. Despite their clinical relevance, pollinosis and pollen sensitization remain underdiagn
content: Introduction: Pollen-induced respiratory diseases represent a growing health burden in Brazil, influenced by environmental exposures and climate change. Despite their clinical relevance, pollinosis and pollen sensitization remain underdiagnosed and poorly characterized across the country’s diverse ecosystems. Objective: To review the epidemiology, clinical relevance, and diagnostic challenges of allergic sensitization to airborne pollen in Brazil, with an emphasis on regional perspectives to support personalized treatment. Methods: The ASBAI Committee on Allergens conducted a narrative review of studies published through February 2026 using the PUBMED, LILACS, and SCIELO databases. Studies addressing aerobiology, pollen sensitization, the prevalence of pollinosis, molecular diagnosis, and allergen immunotherapy in Brazilian populations were evaluated. Thirty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Results: Reported sensitization rates ranged from 12 to 45%, depending on the geographic region and population studied. The most relevant allergenic source was Lolium multiflorum (L. multiflorum) pollen, particularly in southern Brazil, where well-defined pollen seasonality has been associated with respiratory symptoms and may be influenced by climate change and agricultural practices. Evidence from other regions remains limited, although sensitization to tropical grasses and cashew tree pollen has been documented. Advances in component-resolved diagnosis have improved the identification of genuine sensitization patterns and may help guide indications for allergen immunotherapy. However, the characterization of relevant Brazilian pollens and the standardization of allergen extracts remain insufficient. Conclusions: Allergic sensitization to airborne pollen in Brazil is heterogeneous and strongly influenced by regional flora and environmental conditions. Addressing current knowledge gaps requires establishing a national aerobiological monitoring network and modernizing allergen immunotherapy through molecular standardization, thereby aligning clinical practice with advances in precision medicine.

title: In Vitro Determination of the Antibacterial Activity of AgNPs using Syzygium Aromaticum Against Streptococcus Mutans
summary: Objective: To evaluate the antimicrobial activity of AgNPs with clove extract against Streptococcus mutans and determine their MIC and MBC Study Design: Controlled, in vitro laboratory experimental studyPlace and Duration of Study: This stu
content: Objective: To evaluate the antimicrobial activity of AgNPs with clove extract against Streptococcus mutans and determine their MIC and MBC Study Design: Controlled, in vitro laboratory experimental studyPlace and Duration of Study: This study was conducted at the Department of Basic Sciences, College of Dentistry, Al-Qadisiyah University, Qadisiyah Governorate, Iraq, from 14th Jan 2025 to 20th September 2025. Methodology: Biosynthesis of SA AgNPs and characterization using UV-Vis, FTIR, XRD, and SEM. The antibacterial activity was determined by the agar well diffusion method then estimate the MIC and MBC. Results: The XRD pattern of the pure silver sample has a closely match JCPDS card No. 04-0783 with four sharp, visible diffraction peaks appeared at specific 2Ɵ angles. FTIR spectroscopy of SA AgNPs identified the specificfunctional groups. High absorption of AgNPs appeared at 421nm in the UV-Vis spectrum. SEM analysis showed a crystalline nature and quasi-spherical form of AgNPs with dimensions 14 - 32 nm. The zones of inhibition for AgNPs synthesized using Syzygium aromaticum were determined using agar well diffusion method. SA AgNPs at a concentration of 20 mg/mL displayed the most potent antibacterial action, producing the largest zone of inhibition measuring 19 ± 0.8 mm. The inhibitory activity was initiated at 0.32 mg/ml, while the MBC was 1.25 mg/ml. The calculated MBC/MIC ratio was determined to be approximately 3.9 (∽4). Conclusion: The results suggested that Ag nanoparticle synthesis with Syzygium aromaticum can be used as an effective inhibitor of bacterial growth.

title: Exploring flexible sensing strategies toward embodied intelligence
summary: The field of embodied intelligence emphasizes the adaptive development of systems through interactions with their environments, with perceptual capabilities acting as a core enabler. Accordingly, flexible sensors are increasingly integrated
content: The field of embodied intelligence emphasizes the adaptive development of systems through interactions with their environments, with perceptual capabilities acting as a core enabler. Accordingly, flexible sensors are increasingly integrated into embodied intelligence systems, owing to their conformability to complex morphologies and adaptability to dynamic movements. Despite the great potential of such sensors, improving their performance to further advance embodied intelligence presents cross-disciplinary challenges. This article reviews flexible sensing strategies for embodied intelligence at both the device and system levels, highlighting the path toward the synergy between hardware and software. The foundational elements underpinning the advancement of flexible sensors in embodied intelligence are introduced from both hardware and software perspectives. At the device level, various approaches for developing flexible sensors are examined for enhancing their mechanical performance and augmenting their functionalities. At the system level, the integration of flexible sensors into embodied intelligence systems is analyzed with respect to implementation approaches and the resultant intelligent behaviors. Finally, the future outlook of flexible sensing strategies for embodied intelligence systems is discussed.

title: Probing Inclusion Complexation of a Biologically Potent Molecule With α‐Cyclodextrins by Crystal Diffraction Studies
summary: ABSTRACT The crystal structure of the 1:1 inclusion complex of α‐cyclodextrin (with Rhodanine) was established by x‐ray diffraction. This complex crystallizes in hexagonal crystal system with the space group P6, characterized by a head‐to‐t
content: ABSTRACT The crystal structure of the 1:1 inclusion complex of α‐cyclodextrin (with Rhodanine) was established by x‐ray diffraction. This complex crystallizes in hexagonal crystal system with the space group P6, characterized by a head‐to‐tail channel‐type packing arrangement. Co‐crystallized water molecules are also partially present in eight lattice point. The guest molecule Rhodanine is placed inside the α‐cyclodextrin cavity.

title: Quantum Control of Molecular Photodissociation Reactions with Intense Laser Fields
source: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
summary: Abstract Quantum control of molecular reaction dynamics has been a challenging subject of research for many years. Here, a new control scheme is proposed to modify the fragment distributions of molecular photodissociation reactions. The sch
content: Abstract Quantum control of molecular reaction dynamics has been a challenging subject of research for many years. Here, a new control scheme is proposed to modify the fragment distributions of molecular photodissociation reactions. The scheme is applied to the A-band photolysis of CH3I, which is simulated using a realistic wave packet model. The control scheme applies a single moderately intense (1010–1013 W cm–2) pump pulse to excite CH3I. This pulse produces light-induced conical intersections (LICIs) between the ground and excited electronic states, that reshape the natural diabatic potentials, generating new adiabatic light-induced potentials (LIPs). The new LIPs lead to different photodissociation dynamics, producing different fragment distributions compared to the weak-field regime. Complete inversion of the branching ratio I*(2P1/2)/I(2P3/2) between the two dissociation channels is achieved, with the previously dominant I*(2P1/2) channel practically suppressed, and the minor I(2P3/2) channel becoming the dominant one. Experimental implementation of the scheme appears straightforward and of universal application to photodissociation processes.

title: Dispersive Micro‐Solid‐Phase Extraction of Some Parabens From Fruit Juice Using Yolk−Shell ZIF‐8‐based Material (ZnO@SiO 2 @C/Ni)
summary: ABSTRACT Parabens are widely used as antimicrobial preservatives in food, cosmetics, and industrial products due to their stability and practicality. Long‐term exposure to parabens may pose risks to human health and ecosystems. Dispersive m
content: ABSTRACT Parabens are widely used as antimicrobial preservatives in food, cosmetics, and industrial products due to their stability and practicality. Long‐term exposure to parabens may pose risks to human health and ecosystems. Dispersive micro‐solid‐phase extraction (D‐µSPE) is a fast and effective sample preparation method used for cleaning complex matrices and enriching analytes, ensuring reliable analytical results. To enhance analytical selectivity and sensitivity, it is essential to design sorbents with high surface area and selective adsorption properties for target analytes. Zeolite imidazole framework‐derived porous carbon materials, ZnO@SiO 2 @C/Ni, were used as the adsorbent in this study, featuring a yolk‐shell porous structure with high surface area, chemical stability, and efficient adsorption performance for parabens extraction from food samples. To characterize the ZnO@SiO 2 @C/Ni composite, various characterization techniques were employed. In this study, D‐µSPE was integrated with high‐performance liquid chromatography coupled with ultraviolet detection. A series of experimental parameters were systematically evaluated to enhance the extraction performance of parabens, including sample pH (6), extraction duration (20 min), elution solvent type and volume (methanol, 600 µL), breakthrough volume (20 mL), sorbent mass (10 mg), desorption time (4 min), and salt amount (in the absence of salt). Following optimization, the analytical method demonstrated strong linearity for methylparaben (MP), ethylparaben (EP), and propylparaben (PP) across a concentration range of 0.1–800 µg L −1 . The method also achieved low limits of detection of 0.03 µg L −1 for each analyte, confirming its suitability for trace‐level analysis. Also, relative standard deviations ranged from 2.3% to 6.2%, indicating consistent precision across replicate measurements. Extraction recoveries varied between 46.8% and 82.6%, and coefficients of determination for MP ( R 2 = 0.9967), EP ( R 2 = 0.9907), and PP ( R 2 = 0.9970) confirmed excellent linearity and reliability of quantification. These findings support the method's suitability for trace‐level detection of parabens in fruit juice matrix.

title: Radiolabeling and Preclinical Evaluation of [77Br]hGTS13, an xCT-Targeted Small Molecule
summary: Abstract System xc– is an amino acid antiporter overexpressed in numerous cancers, including glioma, pancreatic, and lung cancers. Different glutamate derivative radiotracers allow for the imaging of system xc– by positron emission tomograp
content: Abstract System xc– is an amino acid antiporter overexpressed in numerous cancers, including glioma, pancreatic, and lung cancers. Different glutamate derivative radiotracers allow for the imaging of system xc– by positron emission tomography (PET), such as [18F]hGTS13. Our goal was to radiolabel hGTS13 with the therapeutic Auger electron emitter bromine-77 (77Br) and determine if system xc– tolerates the substitution of fluorine-18 (18F) by 77Br. [77Br]hGTS13 was radiosynthesized by a nucleophilic aliphatic radiobromination. Its uptake in the nonsmall cell lung cancer cell lines H460 and A549 showed a high and sustained uptake. A competition assay with the natural substrates of system xc– and a synthetic inhibitor proved the specificity of [77Br]hGTS13. It remained 100% intact in human serum after a 1 h incubation at 37 °C. Ex vivo biodistribution studies in H460 tumor-bearing nude mice and rats showed similar tumor-associated radioactivity for [18F]hGTS13 and [77Br]hGTS13, but [77Br]hGTS13 was not stable, and the tumor uptake must therefore be interpreted with caution. The in vitro results prove that system xc– tolerates the substitution of the imaging radioisotope by a therapeutic one; however, in vivo stability requires careful consideration.

title: Targeting a MYC-directed metabolic vulnerability sensitizes tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy with selectivity
summary: Abstract A key strategy for precision therapy lies in identifying and targeting tumor cell-specific metabolic vulnerabilities to develop effective combination treatments. In this study, we demonstrate that vandetanib, a multi-kinase inhibit
content: Abstract A key strategy for precision therapy lies in identifying and targeting tumor cell-specific metabolic vulnerabilities to develop effective combination treatments. In this study, we demonstrate that vandetanib, a multi-kinase inhibitor, acts as a potent transcriptional repressor of the serine synthesis pathway (SSP) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLCs). Mechanistically, vandetanib acts by suppressing the oncogenic transcription factor MYC, which exerts a greater regulatory weight on SSP transcription than the canonical GCN2–ATF4 adaptive amino acid response (AAR) axis. This MYC-directed SSP blockade impairs tumor adaptation to serine/glycine (SG) deprivation, inducing cooperative cytotoxicity both in vitro and in vivo. Crucially, normal cells rely on the GCN2–ATF4 pathway rather than MYC for SSP regulation, thereby sparing them from toxicity. The combination of vandetanib with SG restriction achieves potent tumor suppression with an improved safety profile. Our work establishes a “metabolic sensitization” paradigm wherein targeting oncogene-specific transcriptional nodes disrupts tumor metabolic adaptability, offering a highly selective strategy to overcome TKI resistance.

title: Red–blue light ratios shape growth, physiological responses and leaf metabolic profiles in tissue-cultured Zingiber officinale plantlets
summary: Light quality regulates in vitro plant development, but the integrated responses of ginger plantlets to different red–blue light ratios remain unclear. Tissue-cultured Zingiber officinale Roscoe plantlets were exposed for eight weeks to whi
content: Light quality regulates in vitro plant development, but the integrated responses of ginger plantlets to different red–blue light ratios remain unclear. Tissue-cultured Zingiber officinale Roscoe plantlets were exposed for eight weeks to white light (W), red light (R), blue light (B), or combined red–blue light at 1:1 (RB11), 1:3 (RB13), or 3:1 (RB31). Morphological traits, physiological and biochemical parameters, and untargeted leaf metabolic profiles were analysed. R primarily promoted stem elongation (mean stem length 46.0% higher than W) but produced relatively fewer buds, leaves and roots. B increased soluble sugar and protein contents and produced the lowest malondialdehyde level (19.7% below W). RB31 showed high catalase and peroxidase activities together with relatively low malondialdehyde. RB13 produced the highest bud and root numbers (root number 21.3% above W), maintained a high leaf number, enhanced carotenoid accumulation, and was associated with candidate responses involving lipid, phenylpropanoid, flavonoid, glutathione, polyamine and carbon–nitrogen metabolism. Only linoleic acid metabolism in B versus W remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Overall, the treatments induced distinct growth, physiological and metabolic response patterns. RB13 showed the most balanced response among the combined red–blue treatments and may be suitable for improving in vitro ginger plantlet quality.

title: Microstructural refinement and stability of Si-containing (Al,Mo,Ta,V,W)-carbide coatings
summary: Many ceramic coatings suffer from grain coarsening and mechanical softening during high-temperature exposure, which limits their performance in extreme environments. High-entropy carbides (HECs), while thermodynamically metastable, offer op
content: Many ceramic coatings suffer from grain coarsening and mechanical softening during high-temperature exposure, which limits their performance in extreme environments. High-entropy carbides (HECs), while thermodynamically metastable, offer opportunities to enhance kinetic microstructural stability through compositional complexity. Here, we investigate the effect of Si addition on sputtered (Al,Mo,Ta,V,W)C coatings. Increasing the Si content from 0 to 7 at.% systematically refines the columnar grain width from ~500 nm to ~20 nm and promotes a pronounced (200) texture. Upon annealing at 1200 °C, nanoscale SiC precipitates form preferentially along grain boundaries while the fcc carbide phase and nanocrystalline morphology remain largely preserved. These precipitates effectively impede grain-boundary motion and dislocation glide, resulting in only a moderate hardness decrease from 28 to 24 GPa and an indentation modulus of ~390 GPa upon annealing. The results demonstrate that low-solubility, strong carbide-forming elements can enhance microstructural coarsening resistance in metastable HEC coatings by promoting boundary-precipitation strengthening, providing a promising strategy for designing thermally robust ceramic coatings.

title: Less Filler, More Fight: A Graphene Oxide–Carbon Nanotube Hybrid Outperforms Carbon Nanotube Alone at an Identical Low Loading in Epoxy Dental Composites
summary: BackgroundAmalgam's retreat under mercury regulation leaves a mechanical gap that composite resins and glass ionomers have not fully closed, keeping nanofiller-reinforced epoxy systems in contention.Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and graphene oxid
content: BackgroundAmalgam's retreat under mercury regulation leaves a mechanical gap that composite resins and glass ionomers have not fully closed, keeping nanofiller-reinforced epoxy systems in contention.Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and graphene oxide (GO), tested separately at high loadings, each strengthen epoxy in a dose-dependent manner.It is unknown whether using both CNT and GO, at the same total filler amount, gives better mechanical properties than CNT alone. AimsTo compare the tensile, compressive, and nanoindentation properties between a low-loading CNT-only epoxy composite and an iso-loaded GO+CNT hybrid carrying the same total nanofiller content, and to characterise CNT dispersion and fracture-surface morphology on field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM). Settings and designIn vitro, laboratory-based comparative experimental study across two collaborating institutions. Materials and methodsEpoxy nanocomposites were cast in 12 g batches of Araldite GY 250 resin with Aradur 951 hardener, as either 0.5 wt% multi-walled CNT alone (CNT group; 0.06 g CNT) or a combined 0.25 wt% CNT + 0.25 wt% GO hybrid (0.03 g CNT + 0.03 g GO) -both carrying an identical total loading of 0.5 wt%.Tensile and compressive testing used a universal testing machine (n=5 per group); nanoindentation used a Berkovich diamond indenter (n=5 per group; 25 indents total); fracture-surface morphology was examined by FESEM. Statistical analysisWith five independent specimens per group, results are reported as mean ± standard deviation and group differences were tested by independent-samples t-test (α=0.05),supplemented with Cohen's d given the small sample size.Tensile strength, compressive strength, and strain at peak differed significantly between groups; reduced elastic modulus and hardness did not reach significance at this sample size, though both carried moderate-to-large effect sizes (d=0.60 and 0.83) with post-hoc power of only 13% and 21%, respectively. ResultsThe GO+CNT hybrid outscored the CNT-only composite on every parameter measured despite an identical total filler loading: tensile strength (27.48 ± 0.45 vs. 25.20 ± 0.51 MPa, ~9% higher, t=7.50, p=0.0001), compressive strength (172.46 ± 1.87 vs. 167.06± 1.16 MPa, ~3% higher, t=5.49, p=0.0006), reduced elastic modulus (5.89 ± 0.58 vs. 5.54 ± 0.58 GPa, ~6% higher, t=0.96, p=0.37, d=0.60), and hardness (0.26 ± 0.04 vs. 0.23 ± 0.04 GPa, ~14% higher, t=1.32, p=0.22,d=0.83).FESEM of both composites showed carbon nanotube pull-out and crack-bridging at the fracture surface; the GO+CNT hybrid additionally carried a visibly more textured matrix background consistent with co-dispersed graphene oxide nanosheets, dispersion remaining generally uniform with no large-scale agglomeration in either group.

title: Comparative mechanical, microstructural, durability performance and life cycle assessment of pectin and inulin versus xanthan gum in loam soil stabilization
summary: Microbial xanthan gum (XG) is a well-known stabilizer for loam soil, however plant-derived biopolymers such as pectin and inulin may offer better performance due to their distinct stabilization mechanisms. This study therefore compares thes
content: Microbial xanthan gum (XG) is a well-known stabilizer for loam soil, however plant-derived biopolymers such as pectin and inulin may offer better performance due to their distinct stabilization mechanisms. This study therefore compares these plant-derived biopolymers with XG to evaluate their effects on the strength, durability, microstructure, and LCA of loam soil, using treated samples tested after 1, 7, 28, 56, and 90 days by UCS, ultrasonic pulse velocity, F-T cycles, and microstructural analyses. Compared with inulin and XG, 1% pectin after 28 days provided the highest compressive strength, increasing the strength of loam from 230 to 5102 kPa. Pectin also exhibited the best performance under F-T cycling. This improvement was associated with the formation of a dense hydrogel network that coated mineral surfaces and reduced pore spaces. Although pectin provided the greatest mechanical and durability enhancements, the comparative LCA showed that inulin achieved the highest overall environmental performance, with MPPI scores of 0.67, 0.60, and 0.50 for inulin, XG, and pectin, respectively, under scenario S2. These results indicate that pectin and inulin can improve the performance of loam soil compared with XG; however, inulin emerged as the best performing biopolymer when structural integrity and environmental sustainability were considered simultaneously.

title: A Novel Voltammetric Approach for the Rapid Quantification of Rosmarinic Acid in Origanum micranthum and Origanum minutiflorum
summary: In this study, rosmarinic acid (RA) was isolated and quantitatively determined in extracts obtained from Origanum micranthum and Origanum minutiflorum using complementary analytical techniques. Following the isolation of RA from the ethyl a
content: In this study, rosmarinic acid (RA) was isolated and quantitatively determined in extracts obtained from Origanum micranthum and Origanum minutiflorum using complementary analytical techniques. Following the isolation of RA from the ethyl acetate subextract of O. micranthum, spectrophotometric analyses were performed to evaluate its distribution in different solvent fractions, revealing a pronounced enrichment in ethyl acetate extracts of both species. In addition, an electrochemical strategy based on differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) was established for the rapid quantification of RA employing a boron-doped diamond (BDD) electrode. Under optimized experimental conditions, the method exhibited linearity over the concentration range of 0.2-80 µM with a detection limit of 0.061 µM. The applicability of the proposed approach was validated by successful analysis of plant extracts, yielding recoveries of 100.62% for O. micranthum and 100.74% for O. minutiflorum. The combined use of isolation, spectroscopic evaluation, and electrochemical quantification provides an efficient analytical framework for the determination of RA in the investigated Origanum extracts.

title: Multifunctional green nanocomposites of poly(GMA-co-MA)/nanoclay with Ag/Zn nanoparticles bioreduced using Morus alba extract for dye removal and antibacterial activity
summary: This work investigates the development of a series of functional nanocomposites based on nanoclay and a copolymer (PGM), synthesized via in situ radical polymerization of glycidyl methacrylate (GMA) and maleic anhydride (MA). Four formulati
content: This work investigates the development of a series of functional nanocomposites based on nanoclay and a copolymer (PGM), synthesized via in situ radical polymerization of glycidyl methacrylate (GMA) and maleic anhydride (MA). Four formulations (NC-10, NC-30, NC-60, and NC-85) with increasing polymer content were prepared to evaluate their adsorption and antimicrobial properties.
