The preservation of anhydride groups was designed to enhance cationic dye affinity, achieving a maximum methylene blue (MB) adsorption capacity of 294.12 mg g −1 (Langmuir model) for NC-10 within just 20 min. To introduce antibacterial functionality, Ag, Zn, and AgZn nanoparticles were biosynthesized using mulberry leaf (MNPs) extract and incorporated into the NC-10 matrix. Structural and morphological characterizations were performed using FTIR, XRD, XPS, SEM, and EDS analyses. The incorporation of MNPs slightly decreased the MB adsorption capacity while introducing antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones ranging from 12 to 25 mm against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. These results demonstrate the potential of the developed NC-10/MNPs as multifunctional materials for simultaneous dye removal and antimicrobial applications.

title: IoT-Enabled Real-Time Outdoor Monitoring of Perovskite BIPV System under Real Climatic Conditions
summary: This study presents a first-of-its-kind IoT-enabled outdoor investigation of perovskite Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) subsystems under real environmental operating conditions at Peshawar, Pakistan. Two architecturally distinct per
content: This study presents a first-of-its-kind IoT-enabled outdoor investigation of perovskite Building-Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) subsystems under real environmental operating conditions at Peshawar, Pakistan. Two architecturally distinct perovskite modules, namely Module A (300 cm2) and Module B (500 cm2), were independently integrated within a common BIPV envelope using separate load configurations of 200 Ω with a green LED and 1 kΩ with a red LED, respectively. An IoT-based monitoring framework incorporating INA219 current–voltage sensors, SHT31 temperature–humidity sensing, TSL2561 irradiance monitoring, DS3231 real-time clock synchronization and SD card data logging was developed to continuously acquire synchronized electrical and environmental datasets from October 2025 to January 2026. During the transition from autumn to winter, solar irradiance decreased from approximately 48–59 mW cm−2 to 32–35 mW cm−2, while ambient temperature declined from nearly 30–32°C to 13–14°C, accompanied by an increase in relative humidity from ∼25–36% to ∼64–66%. Under these conditions, Module A exhibited substantial degradation, with conversion efficiency decreasing from ∼4.8% to ∼2.18%, primarily due to environmental exposure, moisture ingress and encapsulation related instability associated with its segmented multi-cell architecture. In contrast, Module B demonstrated comparatively superior operational stability, maintaining efficiencies between ∼7.34% and ∼6.12% owing to its monolithic structure, enhanced encapsulation integrity and improved resistance to humidity-induced degradation and low-irradiance operation. The findings highlight the critical interplay between environmental conditions, device architecture and encapsulation quality in determining the long-term outdoor stability of perovskite BIPV systems, and demonstrate the practical feasibility of integrating semi-transparent perovskite solar windows into sustainable energy-efficient buildings.

title: Lateral Transshipment Application in TunisAI: A Case Study of the Company "SODEA"
source: International Journal of Finance Insurance and Risk Management
summary: Purpose: This study examines the role of lateral transshipment in optimizing the export of Tunisian oranges to the French market.Particular attention is given to the consolidation of orange shipments from multiple Tunisian producers and the
content: Purpose: This study examines the role of lateral transshipment in optimizing the export of Tunisian oranges to the French market.Particular attention is given to the consolidation of orange shipments from multiple Tunisian producers and the contribution of this logistics practice to transport efficiency, product quality, shipment reliability, and the competitiveness of Tunisian citrus exports.Design/Methodology/Approach: The study adopts a logistics and supply-chain perspective to analyse the contribution of lateral transshipment to the organization of Tunisian orange exports.The analysis focuses on the consolidation of shipments before export, including the pooling of volumes from different producers, coordination among producers and exporters, shipment planning, traceability, refrigerated storage, and modern packaging operations.The case of SODEA, a Tunisian company established in 1995 and active in the packaging, pre-packaging, and export of fruits and vegetables, is used to illustrate the practical application of these logistics practices, particularly in the export of Maltese oranges to France.Findings: The analysis indicates that lateral transshipment can improve the efficiency and reliability of Tunisian orange exports by consolidating shipments before loading and reducing the incidence of partial shipments, transportation costs, and logistical delays.Shipment pooling also facilitates more regular deliveries to export ports and contributes to maintaining the freshness and quality of oranges during international transportation.In addition, the practice supports improved coordination among producers and exporters, strengthens traceability and shipment planning, and enables exporters to respond more effectively to fluctuations in production and market demand.The SODEA case further illustrates how refrigerated storage, fruit sorting and sizing, and modern packaging facilities can support compliance with international quality requirements and contribute to the positioning of Tunisian oranges in the French market.Practical Implications: The findings suggest that lateral transshipment can constitute an effective logistics strategy for improving the competitiveness of Tunisian citrus exports.Producers and exporters can benefit from shipment consolidation through lower logistics costs, improved capacity utilization, better delivery reliability, and reduced product losses.Strengthening coordination among producers, exporters, logistics providers, and exportport operators could further improve the efficiency of the Tunisian citrus supply chain and enhance its ability to serve European markets.

title: THERMAL ANNEALING - INDUCED CHANGES IN POLYETHERSULFONE (PES) MEMBRANES: STRUCTURAL, MECHANICAL, AND FLUX CHARACTERIZATION
source: Journal of Chemical Technology and Metallurgy
summary: Polyethersulfone (PES) membranes are known for their outstanding chemical and thermal resistance, making them suitable for various separation processes. However, enhancement in mechanical properties anremaination efficiency remains necessar
content: Polyethersulfone (PES) membranes are known for their outstanding chemical and thermal resistance, making them suitable for various separation processes. However, enhancement in mechanical properties anremaination efficiency remains necessary for achieving optimal membrane functionality. This study investigates the influence of thermal annealing treatment at low temperature of 60°C and 70°C on the morphology, chemical structure, mechanical performance, and pure water flux of PES membranes, compared to none - thermal annealing membranes. Commercial membranes were subjected to thermal treatment for 60 s using a laboratory oven. Characterization techniques included Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT - IR) for functional group analysis, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) for morphological assessment, tensile testing for mechanical evaluation, and dead - end filtration for pure water flux measurement. None - thermal annealing membranes exhibited a tensile strength of 7 MPa, elongation of 43 %, and a water flux of 100 LMH. Annealing at 60°C enhanced pore compactness and uniformity, increasing tensile strength to 9 MPa, elongation to 50 %, and flux to 125 LMH. In contrast, treatment at 70°C further increased water flux to approximately 300 LMH but reduced tensile strength to 6 MPa and elongation to 37 %, indicating a more rigid and brittle structure. FT - IR analysis confirmed no chemical degradation, with enhanced hydrophilic group intensities suggesting improved molecular orientation due to the thermal treatment. The results demonstrate that thermal annealing, particularly at 60°C, can effectively improve PES membrane performance relative to none - thermal annealing membranes while preserving structural integrity, offering a practical approach for advanced membrane - based separation technologies.

title: A higher serum lactate dehydrogenase to creatine phosphokinase ratio after exertional heat illness is associated with short-term heat intolerance
summary: Heat intolerance (HI) after exertional heat illness (EHI) is assessed by heat tolerance testing (HTT), but predictive biomarkers are lacking. We evaluated whether the serum lactate dehydrogenase to creatine phosphokinase (LDH/CPK) ratio, me
content: Heat intolerance (HI) after exertional heat illness (EHI) is assessed by heat tolerance testing (HTT), but predictive biomarkers are lacking. We evaluated whether the serum lactate dehydrogenase to creatine phosphokinase (LDH/CPK) ratio, measured early after collapse, is associated with short-term HI. We conducted a case-control study of 78 Israel Defense Forces soldiers with EHI who underwent HTT within six months and had LDH and CPK measured within 12 hours of collapse. Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios, with Firth penalized regression as a parallel robustness analysis. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis. Nineteen (24.4%) were heat intolerant. The HI group had a higher ratio (median 1.14 vs. 0.69, p = 0.003). After adjustment, a higher ratio was associated with HI (OR 2.66, 95% CI 1.42 to 5.91); the penalized estimate was 2.23 (1.28 to 4.52). The area under the curve was 0.73 (0.59 to 0.85), better than either enzyme alone, but no cut-point was usable in isolation (sensitivity 63%, specificity 75% at 0.97). The ratio did not differ between heat stroke and heat exhaustion (p = 0.44), and remained associated with HI in those with altered mental status (OR 2.63, 1.31 to 7.35). A higher LDH/CPK ratio shortly after EHI is associated with short-term HI. The tissue source of the LDH elevation was not determined; central nervous system involvement remains one possible explanation, though it cannot be verified. The ratio is a candidate adjunct to return-to-duty assessment, and requires external validation.

title: Emissions of Methane, Ethane, and VOCs from the Denver-Julesburg Basin from airborne studies in 2023: Improved Quantification with Independent Wind Observations
summary: Oil and natural gas (O&G) operations emit substantial methane (CH 4 ), ethane (C 2 H 6 ), and other volatile organic compounds (VOCs), yet their fluxes and trends remain uncertain. We conducted airborne mass balance measurements of CH 4 and
content: Oil and natural gas (O&G) operations emit substantial methane (CH 4 ), ethane (C 2 H 6 ), and other volatile organic compounds (VOCs), yet their fluxes and trends remain uncertain. We conducted airborne mass balance measurements of CH 4 and C 2 H 6 in the Wattenberg Field of the Denver-Julesburg Basin during four flights in October -November 2023. An updated framework integrates mobile lidar wind profiles with modeled winds to better resolve wind speed and planetary boundary layer height, two dominant sources of uncertainty, improving confidence in derived fluxes. Expanded VOC analysis distinguishes agricultural CH 4 emissions from concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs), assessing acetic acid (CH 3 COOH) temperature sensitivity following freezing conditions and ethanol as a potential CAFO tracer. CH 3 COOH shows temperature sensitivity, but enhancements remain sufficient, supporting its use as a robust CAFO tracer. Tracer analysis using C 2 H 6 and CH 3 COOH attributes 66 +/- 17% of CH 4 emissions to O&G sources, with the remainder dominated by CAFOs. Total CH 4 emission rates in 2023 (26.0 +/- 7.5 t hr -1 ) are consistent with prior measurements from 2012—2023 despite increased O&G production, while C 2 H 6 emission rates (3.2 +/- 0.6 t hr -1 ) have declined. Production-normalized CH 4 and C 2 H 6 emission intensities have decreased substantially since earlier studies, although most of the decline occurred before 2021, with little change observed between 2021 and 2023. Expanded flights, coverage, and platforms improve confidence in emission intensity estimates.

title: Evaluating Proactive Social Responsibility and the Potential for Responsible User Behaviour in Riverfront Development: Abu-Nuwas Street, Baghdad as a Case Study
summary: Riverfronts are significant public spaces, promoting belonging, social interaction and collective use. This study seeks to evaluate how proactive social responsibility is reflected in riverfront planning and assess how spatial quality indic
content: Riverfronts are significant public spaces, promoting belonging, social interaction and collective use. This study seeks to evaluate how proactive social responsibility is reflected in riverfront planning and assess how spatial quality indicators may provide conditions that support responsible user behavior, focusing on Abu-Nuwas Street in Baghdad as a case study. PSR is considered a planning and administrative framework embedded in design decisions, while responsible user behavior is a potential outcome. The study adopted a quantitative descriptive-analytical approach through two five-point Likert scale questionnaires. The first surveyed users and visitors of the recreational riverfront area (n=143), while the second surveyed architects and built-environment specialists regarding the road expansion project (n=47). Data were analyzed using means and standard deviations. Users reported high levels of place identity and attachment, safety and comfort, social interaction, and aesthetic and visual quality, in contrast accessibility, walkability, and environmental quality received moderate evaluations. Specialists reported moderate performance across PSR indicators, with stronger spatial connectivity but weaker place identity, pedestrian priority, environmental impact, and long-term social sustainability. The findings indicate that the recreational riverfront provides spatial conditions that may support positive collective use and place attachment, whereas the road expansion project prioritizes traffic-functional performance over social-environmental objectives. The study develops a descriptive-analytical framework for evaluating how proactive planning and riverfront environmental quality may foster conditions supporting socially responsible user behavior.

title: Experimental Evidence of Reaction‐Driven Fracturing and Ultramafic Rock Weakening Induced by CO 2 Mineralization
summary: Abstract Carbon sequestration in mafic and ultramafic rocks offers a pathway to mitigate emissions, while mineralization could precondition rocks for critical mineral extraction. However, the reaction‐driven fracturing processes that increa
content: Abstract Carbon sequestration in mafic and ultramafic rocks offers a pathway to mitigate emissions, while mineralization could precondition rocks for critical mineral extraction. However, the reaction‐driven fracturing processes that increase permeability and weaken rock remain underexplored. Here, we expose serpentinized dunite samples to ‐rich Mg(OH) 2 ‐brine at 90°C and 3.5 MPa for up to 32 days, using X‐ray computed tomography and digital volume correlation to quantify morphological evolution and 3D solid displacements. Results reveal tensile microfractures nucleating within 11 days, progressing to core disaggregation, with localized damage concentrated along pre‐existing veins and flaw tips. Calculated crystallization pressures exceeding 100 MPa, together with fracture mechanics modeling, support magnesite formation within brucite‐filled veins as the primary driver for reaction‐driven fracturing. Raman spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy help identify mineral changes. These insights into spatiotemporal dynamics of reaction‐driven fracturing can inform strategies for injection and mineralization in ultramafic formations.

title: Flexural and Shear Performance of GGBS-Silica Fume Blended Geopolymer Concrete
summary: This study provides an experimental characterization of the flexural and direct shear behavior of ambient-cured ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS)–silica fume (SF) blended geopolymer concrete. It targets a gap in material-level fle
content: This study provides an experimental characterization of the flexural and direct shear behavior of ambient-cured ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS)–silica fume (SF) blended geopolymer concrete. It targets a gap in material-level flexural and shear data for this class of binder. A total of ten mix designs spanning five GGBS-SF blending ratios (100:0 to 0:100) and two alkaline activator solution (AAS) ratios (1.5 and 2.0) were investigated. Four-point bending tests under closed-loop deflection control and modified JSCE direct shear tests were conducted on plain prismatic specimens at 28 days. Complete load-deformation responses were captured, including post-peak softening. These were used to evaluate flexural strength (f r ), shear strength (f v ), initial and secant flexural stiffness (K i and K s ), peak-to-cracking deformation ratio (µ δ ), pre-peak flexural toughness (T), brittleness index (BI), and normalized pre-peak shear work (Gs). GGBS-rich systems achieved the highest absolute peak f r and f v of 3.59 and 4.52 MPa, respectively, under AAS = 2.0. These systems also exhibited the most balanced post-peak fracture response under higher AAS ratio (higher silica availability), in contrast to SF-rich systems, which became increasingly brittle as SF content increased under AAS = 2.0. Within Group A, G50S50 showed the most balanced fracture behavior, with the lowest brittleness index in its group. K s correlated exponentially with splitting tensile strength (f sp ), with R² = 0.93. This is a dataset-specific association and does not establish a causal relationship. Preliminary, dataset-specific empirical correlations for f r and f v were developed and benchmarked against codified provisions. Microscopy analyses within Group A indicated that the Ca/Na ratio tracked the transition between C–A–S–H- and N–A–S–H-dominated microstructures and the associated mechanical performance hierarchy.

title: Purity is not proof: an air-corrected mud-gas hydrogen purity alone cannot demonstrate a natural hydrogen accumulation
summary: Six natural hydrogen wells have been announced with headline purities of 73% to 97%, each from gas released during drilling, with air, or oxygen and nitrogen, removed by calculation; two operators say testing is still needed. A purity recor
content: Six natural hydrogen wells have been announced with headline purities of 73% to 97%, each from gas released during drilling, with air, or oxygen and nitrogen, removed by calculation; two operators say testing is still needed. A purity records composition, not quantity or source, so alone it cannot show a recoverable accumulation. In the contractor’s public records, the interval behind Ramsay 2’s 86% is one the contractor labelled a “Likely artefact”, just below a casing shoe; its hydrogen before air correction (0.98%), its purity (86.26%) and a relative per-rock index match or exceed two events it attributed to the formation. At Ramsay 1 the real-time log at the 73.3% depth was at background. A drilling study’s carbonate samples, re-analysed, held at most 249 ppmv of drilling-made hydrogen, which reads up to 82% with oxygen and nitrogen excluded but under 1% on an oxygen-based correction. Coding of the 20 announcing documents finds confirmation or discovery wording in 14 of 20 headlines, attached mostly to presence and purity and never to a quantity. Gas rates since reported for two headline wells, about 3 to 360 m3 a day, come from other or wider intervals, so no headline interval yet has a hydrogen rate; on a six-tier evidence ladder the headline figures are Tier 1, a show in drilling returns. The paper does not argue that these wells lack accumulations, only that their purities cannot tell; a registered forecast expects their first flow tests to give under 1,000 m3 of hydrogen a day.

title: Isotopic Insight Into Nitrate Sources and Cycling in Polar Sea Ice
summary: Abstract Sea ice alters nitrate (NO 3 − ) availability in polar oceans, yet the influence of sea‐ice type on NO 3 − sources and cycling remains poorly constrained. We analyzed NO 3 − concentrations and isotopic compositions ( δ 15 N, δ 18 O
content: Abstract Sea ice alters nitrate (NO 3 − ) availability in polar oceans, yet the influence of sea‐ice type on NO 3 − sources and cycling remains poorly constrained. We analyzed NO 3 − concentrations and isotopic compositions ( δ 15 N, δ 18 O, Δ 17 O) in Antarctic one‐year and Arctic multi‐year sea ice to investigate NO 3 − sources and transformation processes. Mean NO 3 − concentrations were substantially higher in Antarctic one‐year sea ice (3.89 ± 17.75 μmol L −1 , with the large standard deviation driven by a few bottom‐layer samples with elevated concentrations) than in Arctic multi‐year sea ice (0.50 ± 0.22 μmol L −1 ). Δ 17 O‐based source apportionment showed that atmospheric NO 3 − contributed 37% ± 11.64% in Arctic multi‐year sea ice, compared with 4% ± 2.69% in Antarctic one‐year sea ice. Despite much lower total NO 3 − concentrations, Arctic multi‐year sea ice exhibited a higher atmospheric NO 3 − contribution, indicating better preservation of atmospheric NO 3 − . Non‐atmospheric NO 3 − , derived from in situ nitrification and/or underlying seawater, accounted for 96% ± 2.69% and 63% ± 11.64% of the NO 3 − pool in Antarctic and Arctic sea ice, respectively. Isotopic compositions and nutrient concentrations indicate the occurrence of microbial NO 3 − cycling in both Antarctic one‐year and Arctic multi‐year sea ice, with more pronounced cycling in Antarctic one‐year sea ice. Collectively, these results suggest that sea‐ice type influences NO 3 − concentrations, sources, and cycling, highlighting the role of sea ice in NO 3 − availability in polar marine environments. We acknowledge that nitrite (NO 2 − ) in sea‐ice samples could introduce a degree of uncertainty into isotope interpretations; however, given the relatively low NO 2 − /(NO 2 − + NO 3 − ) fractions, this uncertainty is unlikely to have affected our main conclusions.

title: Antarctic Circumpolar Current slowdown precedes an abyssal overturning decline in response to added meltwater
summary: Ice melt around Antarctica threatens to dramatically alter the Southern Ocean circulation, and thus disrupt the global redistribution of heat, freshwater, nutrients, and carbon. Past research has linked Antarctic ice melt to weakening of th
content: Ice melt around Antarctica threatens to dramatically alter the Southern Ocean circulation, and thus disrupt the global redistribution of heat, freshwater, nutrients, and carbon. Past research has linked Antarctic ice melt to weakening of the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC) and Antarctic Bottom Water (AABW) formation, but their relationship and regional timeline of response remain unclear. Here, we assess a high-resolution ocean projection applying future atmospheric and ice-melt forcing to quantify the response time scales of the ACC and AABW. We find that ACC weakening precedes AABW decline by ∼ 20 years, driven by different regional responses to meltwater. Along the West Antarctic sector west to Adélie Land, meltwater advected northward along near-surface isopycnals alters density gradients controlling ACC strength through a near-immediate barotropic response, while surface water mass transformation and AABW formation also decline rapidly. In contrast, global AABW decline lags because it is delayed by the dynamically stable Weddell and Prydz Bay sectors, despite surface freshening there. These results suggest ACC strength may serve as an early sign of future Southern Ocean overturning change. Plain Language Summary The ocean surrounding Antarctica is vital to our climate system. Vast quantities of water sink into the abyss via the overturning circulation, carrying dissolved carbon, oxygen, and anthropogenic heat into the deep ocean. The world’s strongest current, the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC), circles Antarctica, isolating cold waters to the south from the rest of the ocean. Recent studies show that both the overturning circulation and the ACC may slow due to Antarctic ice melt, but the connections or timeline between these processes remains unexplored. Here, we assess a high-resolution ocean simulation forced by 50 years of future climate change including Antarctic meltwater. We find the ACC declines a full two decades before a global overturning slowdown is detected, because the ACC responds quickly to meltwater-induced density changes, while the global overturning signal only emerges once all sectors decline. This delay is driven by the Weddell and Prydz Bay sectors, which show little slowdown until the simulation’s final years, despite some local freshening. The West Antarctic sector west to the Adélie, by contrast, efficiently channel meltwater to the ACC and display a faster abyssal decline. Assessing these regional contributions is essential to understanding the Southern Ocean’s future response to climate change, and measuring the ACC may provide an early warning sign of impending overturning decline.

title: Ionic lipid–surfactant complex based on phosphatidylcholine and sodium dodecyl sulfate for enhanced curcumin encapsulation and sustained delivery
summary: Developing stable, efficient nanocarriers for hydrophobic anticancer agents remains a major challenge in pharmaceutical nanotechnology. In this study, we engineered a novel ion-pair amphiphile through electrostatic complexation between zwit
content: Developing stable, efficient nanocarriers for hydrophobic anticancer agents remains a major challenge in pharmaceutical nanotechnology. In this study, we engineered a novel ion-pair amphiphile through electrostatic complexation between zwitterionic phosphatidylcholine and the anionic surfactant sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), forming a phosphatidylcholine–SDS (P-SDS) ionic complex with enhanced hydrophobicity and self-assembly capability. The resulting hybrid amphiphile was further stabilized with Tween-80 and formulated into nanoscale micellar structures to encapsulate curcumin. 1H-NMR and FT-IR spectroscopy confirmed the formation of the P-SDS ionic complex, while DSC analysis showed the disappearance of crystalline curcumin, indicating successful amorphous dispersion within the micellar core. Fluorescence spectroscopy revealed a low critical micelle concentration (CMC) of 3.1 × 10−4 M, suggesting favorable thermodynamic stability of the self-assembled system. Dynamic light scattering measurements showed an average particle size of approximately 239 nM with a strongly negative zeta potential ranging from −37 to −44 mV, indicating good colloidal stability. The optimized formulation achieved 19% drug loading with an encapsulation efficiency of 39.8%. In vitro release studies showed a biphasic release profile: an initial moderate burst followed by sustained curcumin release over 72 h. Morphological analyses using ESEM and TEM confirmed the formation of spherical nanoscale assemblies with relatively uniform morphology. The developed P-SDS nanoassembly is a simple, scalable, and biocompatible platform for delivering hydrophobic therapeutic agents. The ion-pair engineering strategy proposed in this work provides a versatile approach to tuning amphiphilicity, self-assembly behavior, and drug-loading capacity in lipid-based nanocarriers, with potential applicability for passive tumor targeting through the enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect.

title: Plasmon-like Optical–Thermal Coupling in Nano-Engineered Solar Absorber Coatings Integrated Structural, Spectral, and Photothermal Analysis
summary: This work involves preparing photothermal absorber coatings with nanoparticle additives and their characterization for photo-thermal conversion applications. It includes the correlation between additions of metallic and metal oxide particle
content: This work involves preparing photothermal absorber coatings with nanoparticle additives and their characterization for photo-thermal conversion applications. It includes the correlation between additions of metallic and metal oxide particles, the optical properties of the composite coatings and their photo-thermal conversion characteristics. Coatings incorporating Ni, Fe3O4, CuO, NiO, and MnO₂ are characterized using SEM–EDS, UV–Vis spectroscopy (200–1000 nm), specular reflection measurements. The coatings are also subjected to time-resolved photothermal analysis. Ni-incorporated coatings exhibited the highest measured thermal performance among the investigated coatings. A maximum surface temperature of 93.93 °C and stored thermal energy of 213.10 J with a peak heating rate indicator of 0.360 are obtained corresponding to a visible absorption peak at approximately 540 nm. A high spectral absorptance (AUCα) of about 1.717 and a low reflectivity of 4.6% are also obtained. The results are in agreement with the proposed plasmon-like absorption behavior in metallic Ni nanoparticles that can lead to the transformation of photons into heat. The Fe3O4- and CuO-incorporated coatings show competitive performance due to broadband absorption mechanisms. The NiO- and MnO2-incorporated coatings are found to exhibit lower efficiency due to UV-dominated absorption. Despite its high absorptance, the primary coating thermal response remains limited due to the absence of conductive pathways. Correlation analysis indicates that no individual spectral parameter alone governs photothermal performance. The results demonstrate that effective photo–thermal conversion requires the combined effect of broadband absorption, plasmon-assisted or defect-mediated mechanisms in addition to suitable microstructural characteristics.

title: Indoor Air Quality and Environmental Safety in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit in Al-Najaf, Iraq: A Cross Sectional Study of Incubators and Surrounding Air
summary: Objective: To measure selected indoor air quality parameters within neonatal incubators and neonatal intensive care unit rooms using a calibrated digital monitoring device Study Design: Descriptive analytical cross-sectional studyPlace and
content: Objective: To measure selected indoor air quality parameters within neonatal incubators and neonatal intensive care unit rooms using a calibrated digital monitoring device Study Design: Descriptive analytical cross-sectional studyPlace and Duration of Study: This study was conducted at the neonatal intensive care unit of Al-Zahraa Teaching Hospital in Al-Najaf, Iraq, from 1st October 2024 to 31st March 2025. Methodology: The study included 12 active neonatal Incubators and two neonatal intensive care unit rooms. Air quality parameters including temperature, relative humidity, particulate matter (PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10), carbon dioxide, formaldehyde, and total volatile organic compounds, were measured using a portable monitoring device. Measurements were conducted during peak working hours at different locations within the rooms and incubators. Results: The research results demonstrated that the majority of air quality indicators met international standards for acceptable levels. The temperature and carbon dioxide levels met the recommended values, but relative humidity fell below the recommended threshold. The PM2.5 and PM10 levels remained within acceptable range while formaldehyde and total volatile organic compounds gaseous pollutants appeared at extremely low levels. The two rooms showed no significant statistical differences between them (P>0.05). Conclusion: The neonatal intensive care unit indoor air quality assessment showed acceptable results although the facility needed humidity level improvements. The establishment needs continuous air quality assessment together with control systems to maintain protection for neonates

title: An Analytical Investigation of the Energy Performance of Double-Skin Façade Systems in a Mild-Humid Climate: The Trabzon Case
summary: This study quantifies the effect of Double-Skin Façade (DSF) systems on building energy performance and indoor thermal comfort under temperate-humid, diffuse-radiation climatic conditions, using Trabzon, Turkey, as a case study. A four-stag
content: This study quantifies the effect of Double-Skin Façade (DSF) systems on building energy performance and indoor thermal comfort under temperate-humid, diffuse-radiation climatic conditions, using Trabzon, Turkey, as a case study. A four-stage methodology was applied: (i) climatic characterization using Climate Consultant; (ii) BIM-based geometric modeling in Autodesk Revit 2024; (iii) coupled Revit Insight–EnergyPlus energy simulations; and (iv) comparative performance analysis between a multi-story DSF-equipped office building (S1) and a geometrically identical single-skin reference building (S0). Simulation results show that the DSF configuration reduced annual heating energy consumption by 15–22% and cooling energy consumption by 12–18%, corresponding to an overall annual energy performance improvement of 14–20%, while the proportion of thermally comfortable indoor hours increased by 10–14% relative to S0. These gains originate from the dual seasonal behavior of the façade cavity, which acts as a thermal buffer zone in winter and as a stack-driven natural exhaust channel in summer. Unlike prior DSF studies, which are concentrated in hot-arid or cold climates, this work provides quantitative, climate-specific evidence for temperate-humid, diffuse-radiation regions, offering transferable design criteria for cavity configuration, ventilation strategy, and glazing selection in similar climates.

title: Nitrogen release–demand synchrony governs the productivity–environment trade-offs of organic nitrogen substitution
summary: Partial replacement of mineral nitrogen (N) with manure is widely promoted to improve nutrient circularity and reduce N losses, yet its agronomic and environmental outcomes vary widely among sites and seasons. Because manure N becomes plant
content: Partial replacement of mineral nitrogen (N) with manure is widely promoted to improve nutrient circularity and reduce N losses, yet its agronomic and environmental outcomes vary widely among sites and seasons. Because manure N becomes plant-available only through microbial decomposition, its performance depends on how release kinetics align with crop N demand under prevailing soil and climatic conditions. Here, we calibrated APSIM Next Generation against a winter wheat–summer maize field experiment in eastern China, explicitly representing manure decomposition and N mineralisation. We then simulated 0–100% substitution of mineral N with sheep manure across contrasting initial soil N, growing-season rainfall, and historical (1991–2020) and future (2041–2060; 27 CMIP6 models) climates. The model reproduced crop phenology (RMSE = 6.45 d), grain yield (R² = 0.79), soil mineral N (R² = 0.70) and cumulative N₂O emissions (R² = 0.73). Under the baseline climate, 15–45% substitution maintained grain yield within 0.6% of mineral fertiliser while reducing greenhouse-gas intensity by 14–41% in wheat and 9–25% in maize. Complete substitution achieved the largest emission reductions but reduced yield by up to 7.3%, increased interannual yield variability and raised the energy footprint. Rainfall most clearly determined the direction of yield–GHG trade-offs and explained 39–51% of the variance in simulated yield, whereas initial soil N mainly shifted response magnitude; GHG variance was dominated by rainfall in wheat (52%) and by substitution rate and climate scenario in maize (40% and 31%). Under SSP5–8.5, net N mineralisation increased by 167% in wheat and 70% in maize, whereas crop N demand changed by −1% and −47%, respectively. This widened the seasonal gap between N release and demand through crop-specific pathways: off-peak mineralisation in wheat, and earlier, truncated demand in maize. By quantifying how N release and crop demand diverge under warming, these results explain why no single replacement ratio is likely to remain optimal across crops and climates. Substitution strategies should therefore be designed for release–demand synchrony, matching the timing of plant-available N supply to crop demand, rather than for a fixed replacement fraction.

title: Instrumentation and real-time hygrothermal monitoring of a double-layer Cob prototype and condensation risk assessment
summary: Earthen construction is becoming increasingly popular as a low-carbon alternative to conventional materials, but it’s in situ hygrothermal behavior in instrumented prototypes remains poorly documented, particularly regarding the combined mo
content: Earthen construction is becoming increasingly popular as a low-carbon alternative to conventional materials, but it’s in situ hygrothermal behavior in instrumented prototypes remains poorly documented, particularly regarding the combined monitoring of temperature, humidity and heat flux across multiple wall orientations. As part of the CobBauge project, a prototype with a two-layer wall (structural material and insulation) was built in Normandy and continuously monitored across its four orientations. Analysis of two three-day periods, selected in summer and winter, shows that, in the absence of heating, the indoor temperature remains stable between 23-29°C in summer and 13-15°C in winter, despite outdoor variations of 13-33°C and -4 to 11°C respectively, while indoor relative humidity remains between 50 and 60%. Temperature profiles across the wall thickness reveal a marked contrast between the four facades (which differ in orientation and thickness), with the east and west facades exhibiting the highest temperature amplitudes. The interior and exterior superficial thermal resistances, estimated from these profiles, remain generally consistent with the standard’s default values, with more pronounced deviations on the exterior side, likely influenced by local wind and solar radiation. An assessment of the risk of condensation using the Glaser method reveals no risk, either on the surface or within the structure. A result that contrasts, however, with the relative humidity recorded in the insulation of the north-facing wall, reaching 90% in winter, exceeding the commonly accepted mold risk threshold of 80%. This discrepancy highlights the limitations of the Glaser method when applied to hygroscopic materials and it underscores the necessity of combining theoretical analyses with in-situ measurements to reliably assess the hygrothermal behavior of earthen structures.
