title: The Best of Both Worlds? Probing the Feasibility of Acquiring High-Energy and -Stability LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2–LiFePO4 Materials through Mechanofusion Dry-Coating
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Abstract Microsized polycrystalline Ni-rich LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC) was dry-coated with 2–4 wt % nanosized LiFePO4 (LFP) through a mechanofusion process. The effect of the surface modification was investigated by physicochemical and elect
content: Abstract Microsized polycrystalline Ni-rich LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC) was dry-coated with 2–4 wt % nanosized LiFePO4 (LFP) through a mechanofusion process. The effect of the surface modification was investigated by physicochemical and electrochemical characterization, focusing on cycle life and thermal stability. Cross-section SEM/EDS confirms the presence of a LFP coating on the NMC surface. Electrochemical characterization shows that both the NMC bulk and the LFP coating are electrochemically active and that both uncoated NMC and LFP-coated NMC have similar rate capabilities up to 4 wt % LFP coating in half-cell configuration. Long-term testing in full cells balanced against graphite shows that the uncoated NMC and LFP-coated NMC have similar initial electrochemical performance and cycle life characteristics. The reference NMC and coated NMC–4 wt % LFP respectively retain 83% and 84% of their 0.1 C capacities after 367 cycles, with post-mortem analysis confirming the preservation of the LFP coating. DSC measurements reveal that the LFP coatings do not affect the onset of the thermal decomposition. Increasing the amount of coating material to 6–10 wt % did not improve the electrochemical stability further. The ineffectiveness in improving the cycling and thermal stability is attributed to the porous character of the LFP coating and the inadequate coverage across the wide NMC particle size distribution.

title: Assessing the health and economic burden of sick leave associated with long-term fine particulate matter exposure: a 13-year analysis using German health claims data
summary: Background Ambient fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) is a major environmental health risk, yet its contribution to sick leave and related productivity losses remains insufficiently quantified. We therefore examined the association between P
content: Background Ambient fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) is a major environmental health risk, yet its contribution to sick leave and related productivity losses remains insufficiently quantified. We therefore examined the association between PM 2.5 exposure and all-cause sick leave days and estimated the corresponding model-based burden and productivity losses. Methods Using routine health insurance data from AOK Baden-Württemberg for 2010–2022, we fitted generalized additive models with penalised splines to estimate the exposure–response curve between monthly PM 2.5 exposure and all-cause sick leave days. Models were adjusted for long-term trends, seasonality, temperature, sex, the COVID-19 period, NO 2 , vacation days, and lockdown days, and accounted for spatial heterogeneity using a postal-code-based Markov random field. Model-based exposure contrasts were derived from predicted sick leave days at selected PM 2.5 concentrations. Productivity losses were estimated using the human capital approach. Results PM 2.5 showed a positive non-linear association with sick-leave days (p < 0.001). Compared with 5 µg/m 3 , adjusted predicted sick-leave days were 9.56% higher at 10 µg/m 3 (95% CI 9.09–10.00) and 15.00% higher at 20 µg/m 3 (95% CI 14.20–15.80), while little change was observed between 10 and 15 µg/m 3 (+0.04%, 95% CI − 0.30 to 0.38). The overall non-linear association was supported across additional analyses, although its magnitude and precise shape varied with temporal coverage and covariate adjustment. PM 2.5 concentrations above the WHO guideline of 5 µg/m 3 corresponded to 105 model-attributable excess sick-leave days per 1,000 working-age inhabitants per year, equivalent to approximately 5.31 million excess sick-leave days and €1.56 billion in annual productivity losses in Germany. Conclusion Higher PM 2.5 exposure was associated with a relevant model-attributable burden of sickness absence and productivity losses. These findings suggest that ambient PM 2.5 may be an important population-level correlate of work absence, although causal interpretation is limited by the ecological study design and residual confounding.

title: Living Anionic Polymerization of 1-Cyclohexyl[3]dendralene
summary: Abstract Anionic polymerization of 1-cyclohexyl[3]dendralene (1CH3D) proceeded with potassium naphthalenide (K-Naph) or diphenylmethylpotassium (Ph2CHK) in tetrahydrofuran (THF) at –78 °C. Poly(1CH3D)s with the predicted molecular weights a
content: Abstract Anionic polymerization of 1-cyclohexyl[3]dendralene (1CH3D) proceeded with potassium naphthalenide (K-Naph) or diphenylmethylpotassium (Ph2CHK) in tetrahydrofuran (THF) at –78 °C. Poly(1CH3D)s with the predicted molecular weights and narrow molecular weight distributions (MWD, Mw/Mn < 1.1) were quantitatively obtained. The polymerization of 1CH3D was attempted using sec-butyllithium (s-BuLi) in toluene to investigate the effect of solvent polarity. Sequential copolymerization of 1CH3D and 2-vinylpyridine was conducted using Ph2CHK to afford a poly(1CH3D)-b-poly(2-vinylpyridine) with well-defined chain structures, indicating the living character of the polymerization. Various nuclear magnetic resonance measurements revealed that the microstructure of poly(1CH3D) prepared in THF consisted of the 4,6-structure (80%) and 4,3-structure (20%). Meanwhile, the 4,6-structure content reached 94% in the polymer obtained in toluene. These results indicate that 1CH3D underwent propagation not only via conjugated addition mode but also via vinyl addition mode. The hydrogenation of poly(1CH3D) having a high 4,6-structure (>91%) was attempted to obtain an alternating copolymer, poly(ethylene-alt-1-butenylcyclohexane). The poly(1CH3D)s showed glass transition temperatures between 1 and 16 °C and a cross-linking property by heating over 270 °C.

title: Bio‐Based Deep Eutectic Solvent for Catalyst‐Free Synthesis of Xanthenediones
summary: ABSTRACT We developed an environmentally friendly and efficient method for preparing xanthenedione derivatives via a multicomponent Knoevenagel–Michael cyclocondensation reaction in a bio‐based deep eutectic solvent (DES). The reaction comb
content: ABSTRACT We developed an environmentally friendly and efficient method for preparing xanthenedione derivatives via a multicomponent Knoevenagel–Michael cyclocondensation reaction in a bio‐based deep eutectic solvent (DES). The reaction combined aromatic or heteroaromatic aldehydes with dimedone in a DES prepared from lactic acid, maltose, and amla juice at room temperature without an added catalyst. Among the DES systems tested, a 3:1:3 mixture of lactic acid, maltose, and amla juice performed best, yielding xanthenedione derivatives in 64%–98% yields within 1–5 h. The method accommodated aldehydes bearing electron‐donating and electron‐withdrawing groups, as well as selected heteroaromatic aldehydes. Mechanistic considerations suggest that the DES activates the aldehyde and promotes dimedone enolization through hydrogen bonding and acidity, facilitating Knoevenagel condensation, Michael addition, and cyclodehydration. The DES was reused for five cycles, although its efficiency gradually decreased. Fourier‐transform infrared (FT‐IR) and proton nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 H NMR) analysis after the fifth cycle showed that the DES retained its main spectral features. Green chemistry metrics, including atom economy, the E‐factor, reaction mass efficiency, and process mass intensity, support the sustainability of this approach. Overall, this study demonstrates that bio‐based DES systems can serve as recyclable solvents and catalytic media for multicomponent organic synthesis.

title: Keratinolytic fungi mediated composting of chicken feather waste and its potential for promoting growth of vegetable crops
summary: The poultry industry produces millions of tonnes of chicken feather waste annually. Improper disposal of this waste may contribute to environmental pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, and proliferation of insects and pathogens, thereby pos
content: The poultry industry produces millions of tonnes of chicken feather waste annually. Improper disposal of this waste may contribute to environmental pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, and proliferation of insects and pathogens, thereby posing environmental and public health concern. Chicken feathers are a valuable source of keratin with considerable potential for conversion into value-added agricultural resources. This study evaluated the ability of Aspergillus spp. to convert chicken feather waste into feather-amended substrate and assessed their effects on the growth of vegetable crops. Chicken feather waste was subjected to aerobic composting for 60 days in a soil-amended system, using Aspergillus niger and Aspergillus gorakhpurensis. Maturity and phytotoxicity were determined using the seed germination index (GI). Physicochemical characteristics were measured to characterise nutrient profiles. Agronomic performance of spinach, cabbage, and brinjal was evaluated through morphological assessment and analysis of photosynthetic pigments. Composted feather-amended substrate produced using A. gorakhpurensis achieved a germination index (GI) of 62%, reflecting partial maturity and reduced phytotoxicity. Additionally, the substrate exhibited improved physicochemical characteristics, with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 2.08 dS·m − 1 and C/N ratio of 7.22. Total nitrogen and sulfur contents were 0.23% and 0.18% respectively, in contrast to 0.07% nitrogen and 0.03% sulfur in the control soil, consistent with nitrogen and sulfur mineralisation during composting. Higher germination, improved morphological traits, and enhanced chlorophyll and carotenoid contents were observed after application of composted feather substrate in the tested crops. The present study showed that A. gorakhpurensis produced a composted feather-amended substrate with the most favourable physicochemical profile and agronomic performance under the experimental conditions. These findings suggest that fungal-mediated feather composting may represent a promising approach for converting chicken feather waste into nutrient-enriched soil amendment. Not applicable.

title: Microwave and whey protein synergistically regulate the formation of steadied starch-fatty acids-protein-VB1 complexes: Structure, mechanism, digestion, and VB1 release properties
summary: This study is the first to incorporate water-soluble vitamin B 1 into a starch-fatty acid-protein ternary system, constructing a starch-lauric acid-protein-vitamin B 1 quaternary complex (MRS-LA-WP-VB 1 ) that enables VB 1 encapsulation and
content: This study is the first to incorporate water-soluble vitamin B 1 into a starch-fatty acid-protein ternary system, constructing a starch-lauric acid-protein-vitamin B 1 quaternary complex (MRS-LA-WP-VB 1 ) that enables VB 1 encapsulation and controlled release. Low-moisture, short-duration microwave pretreatment (700 W, 60 s) increased amylose content and altered starch surface hydrophilicity, thereby creating conditions favorable for the encapsulation of guest molecules. WP binds to starch through hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions and, in synergy with microwave pretreatment, enhances the structural order and stability of the system. LA and VB 1 primarily enter the helical cavity via hydrophobic interactions. Encapsulation efficiency measured after selective disruption by NaCl, urea, and SDS revealed that the hydrogen-bonding-to-hydrophobic interaction ratio shifted from 7:3 to 5:5 from binary to quaternary complexes. The MRS-LA-WP-VB 1 increased resistant starch (RS) by 35.93% and exhibited excellent controlled release under in vitro simulated digestion, extending VB 1 release to 11 h showing potential for small-intestinal sustained release.

title: Major volcanic eruptions episodically disrupted the continuity of polar warming through aerosol forcing
summary: Abstract The polar regions are warming rapidly, exceeding the global average due to greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. Using CMIP6 simulations, HadCRUT5 data, and MERRA-2 aerosol records, this study shows that major 20th-centur
content: Abstract The polar regions are warming rapidly, exceeding the global average due to greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. Using CMIP6 simulations, HadCRUT5 data, and MERRA-2 aerosol records, this study shows that major 20th-century volcanic eruptions, Agung (1963), El Chichón (1982), and Pinatubo (1991) temporarily offset polar warming through sulfate-induced cooling. The Agung eruption suppressed Arctic surface air temperature anomalies for approximately 4–5 years (1964–1968), El Chichón for a similar duration (1983–1987), and Pinatubo for about 4–5 years (1992–1996), demonstrating a consistent multi-year cooling response following each event. Without these eruptions, Arctic surface air temperature anomalies would have increased by up to 0.5 °C, whereas volcanic activity caused short-term cooling ranging from −0.07 °C to −0.4 °C. Arctic minimum temperatures ( $${T}_{\min }$$ T min ) are rising faster than maximum temperatures ( $${T}_{\max }$$ T max ), indicating asymmetric warming. In contrast, Antarctic responses were weaker, moderated by oceanic and atmospheric dynamics. Collectively, these eruptions produced episodic multi-year cooling that temporarily interrupted the ongoing Arctic warming trajectory, with warming resuming as volcanic aerosol forcing diminished. Spatial patterns reveal pronounced warming in the central Arctic, Greenland, and Siberia in the absence of volcanic forcing, highlighting the role of eruptions in modulating polar warming and providing insights relevant to future geoengineering considerations.

title: Cryogenic mechanical properties of low thermal expansion ZrW2O8 /epoxy composites and their application in impregnated REBCO superconducting coils
summary: Abstract Rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) coated conductor (CC) tapes are promising for high-energy and high-field applications. In epoxy-impregnated REBCO superconducting windings, during the cooling process, the delamination induced
content: Abstract Rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) coated conductor (CC) tapes are promising for high-energy and high-field applications. In epoxy-impregnated REBCO superconducting windings, during the cooling process, the delamination induced by thermal mismatch stress significantly threatens stable operation due to the weak c-axis strength of REBCO CC tapes. Therefore, reducing the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of the impregnation material will serve as an effective measure to enhance the structural safety of impregnated REBCO superconducting coils. In this research, a series of ZrW2O8/epoxy composites were fabricated by doping different proportions of negative thermal expansion powders into epoxy. The CTE within the temperature range of 4.2–285 K, along with the tensile and shear properties at room temperature and 77 K, were examined. Moreover, high temperature superconducting coils (HTS) were impregnated with optimized improved epoxy composite material, and the Voltage-Ampere characteristics at 77 K in self-field were explored. The results indicate that ZrW2O8/epoxy resin as an impregnation material effectively mitigates the thermal mismatch stress of superconducting coils and enhances their structural stability at extremely low temperatures. Finite element simulation provides supporting evidence of the experimental results. This study will offer an important foundation for optimizing the impregnation materials of high-field superconducting magnets and is highly significant for enhancing the performance and reliability of superconducting magnets.

title: Toward Durable Prosthetic Feet: Mechanical and Tribological Evaluation of Polyurethane Elastomers
source: Advance Sustainable Science Engineering and Technology
summary: Elastomeric materials play a crucial role in determining the durability, comfort, and service life of prosthetic feet. Although various elastomers have been explored for this application, systematic evaluation of polyurethane formulations t
content: Elastomeric materials play a crucial role in determining the durability, comfort, and service life of prosthetic feet. Although various elastomers have been explored for this application, systematic evaluation of polyurethane formulations that integrate mechanical and tribological performance remains limited. This study investigates two types of polyurethane elastomers (A70 and A80) with different polyol–isocyanate ratios to identify an optimal formulation for prosthetic foot applications. Mechanical properties were evaluated through tensile, tear, hardness, and density tests, while friction and wear behavior were assessed using a pin-on-disk tribometer. A commercial prosthetic foot elastomer available in the Indonesian market was used as a benchmark. The results show that A80-based formulations generally provide superior tensile and tear strength compared to A70 variants. Among all specimens, A80-3 exhibits the lowest wear volume and stable friction performance, while maintaining hardness comparable to the commercial product. Although its density remains higher than the benchmark, the improved wear resistance indicates potential for extended service life. These findings offer practical guidance for durability-oriented material selection in the development of cost-efficient prosthetic feet.

title: REVERSE SUPPLY CHAINS IN THE TEXTILE INDUSTRY: A BIBLIOMETRIC STUDY
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: This study analyzed the evolution and intellectual structure of scientific production on circularity in the textile industry through a bibliometric approach based on the Scopus and Web of Science databases.The analysis encompassed indicator
content: This study analyzed the evolution and intellectual structure of scientific production on circularity in the textile industry through a bibliometric approach based on the Scopus and Web of Science databases.The analysis encompassed indicators related to temporal evolution, geographical distribution, scientific journals, co-authorship networks, and keyword co-occurrence, using the VOSviewer software for the construction and visualization of scientific networks.The findings revealed significant growth in publications from 2022 onward, indicating the recent consolidation of the topic within the international research agenda.A decentralized geographical distribution was identified, with notable contributions from India, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Australia.The co-authorship network exhibited low collaborative density and high structural fragmentation among researchers, suggesting that the field remains at a dispersed stage of scientific consolidation.The co-occurrence analysis identified Circular Economy as the central conceptual axis connecting discussions related to textile waste management, circular supply chains, traceability, digital technologies, and circular fashion.The findings highlight both the interdisciplinary nature and the rapid expansion of the literature, while also revealing gaps concerning the integration of governance, sustainability, and supply chain management.This study contributes to the systematization of scientific knowledge on circularity in the textile industry and provides strategic directions for future research aimed at strengthening the theoretical and operational dimensions of the circular transition within the sector.

title: Rotatiridoid, a rare iridoid from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen and its anti-inflammatory activity
summary: A rare iridoid featuring an unusual 3-O-8 bridged ether bond, named rotatiridoid (1), was obtained from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen, along with five known analogues. Its structure was established by means of HRESIMS, 1D
content: A rare iridoid featuring an unusual 3-O-8 bridged ether bond, named rotatiridoid (1), was obtained from Phlomoides rotata (Benth. ex Hook.f.) Mathiesen, along with five known analogues. Its structure was established by means of HRESIMS, 1D and 2D NMR experiments, and ECD calculations. When evaluated in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages, compound 1 displayed anti-inflammatory activity, suppressing the production of pro-inflammatory mediators such as NO and ROS at 7.5 μM.

title: Ultrasound as a Multifunctional Physical Platform for Whole‐Grape Valorization: From Field Management to Green Extraction, Quality Modulation, and Intelligent Scale‐Up
source: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
summary: The grape and wine industry faces prolonged barrel aging, microbial spoilage, protein haze, chemical additives, and inefficient by-product valorization. These challenges motivate nonthermal technologies that reduce chemical inputs. Ultrasou
content: The grape and wine industry faces prolonged barrel aging, microbial spoilage, protein haze, chemical additives, and inefficient by-product valorization. These challenges motivate nonthermal technologies that reduce chemical inputs. Ultrasound operates in two mechanistically distinct regimes: sensing, based on acoustic propagation, reflection, and echo detection, and processing, driven mainly by acoustic cavitation and its physical and chemical effects, including microjets, shock waves, localized hotspots, and reactive radicals. These complementary modes provide a versatile physical platform. This review covers ultrasound across the grape-wine continuum: acoustic imaging for precision viticulture; postharvest preservation with green activated water; green extraction enhanced by natural deep eutectic solvents; grape protein modification for ingredient assembly; modulation of wine color, aroma, and colloidal stability; selected aging-associated reactions involving 1-hydroxyethyl radicals; selective microbial inactivation and fermentation modulation; and scale-up based on energy characterization, continuous-flow reactors, and data-driven modeling. Current evidence indicates that ultrasound is evolving from an empirically optimized unit operation toward a mechanistically informed and quantitatively characterized physical-field platform. Reported effects include accelerated aging-related transformations, modified protein structure and stability, and selective microbial responses, although they depend on treatment conditions and matrix properties. Absorbed energy density supports quantitative comparison of treatments, but reliable scale-up also requires acoustic-field distribution, residence time, temperature, and reactor geometry. Future progress will require standardized energy reporting, pilot- and continuous-flow validation, physics-informed data-driven modeling, and integration of process analytical technologies with closed-loop control. These advances would support more reproducible, scalable, and sustainable ultrasound processing in the grape and wine sector.

title: Distribution, Host Association, and Dissemination of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in the Water-Receiving Area of the Middle Route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project
summary: Rapid urbanization has created heterogeneous aquatic niches in megacities; however, how functionally distinct water bodies shape the environmental resistome remains poorly understood. To elucidate this, we analyzed 30 surface-water metageno
content: Rapid urbanization has created heterogeneous aquatic niches in megacities; however, how functionally distinct water bodies shape the environmental resistome remains poorly understood. To elucidate this, we analyzed 30 surface-water metagenomes from four waterbody types in Beijing during summer and autumn. A total of 1 380 antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) subtypes belonging to 28 classes were identified. Our results demonstrated that urban rivers sustained the highest average ARG burden (average of 0.536 copies per cell), whereas relatively isolated urban lakes exhibited the lowest (0.199 copies per cell). Notably, the receiving waters linked to inter-basin diversion maintained an intermediate ARG load (0.328 copies per cell), but displayed the strongest coupling between ARGs and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) ( R 2 = 0.965). This indicated an elevated mobilization potential at these hydrological interfaces. Seasonal succession displayed a significant reduction in ARG abundance (from 0.441 to 0.227 copies per cell), and the characteristic spatial distribution patterns remained consistent across sampling campaigns, with community turnover acting as the primary driver of resistome variation. Variance partitioning analysis (VPA) and partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) revealed that ARG variation was jointly shaped by microbial composition, MGEs, and environmental factors with high explanatory power ( R 2 = 0.91~0.97). In summer, the shared effect of the microbiome and MGE composition accounted for the largest explained fraction (25.69%), and PLS-PM highlighted MGEs as the strongest direct predictor of the resistome (path coefficient = 0.76). Genomic binning identified that the resistome was phylogenetically concentrated within Pseudomonadota, with Enterobacter being a core high-risk host harboring co-localized ARGs and virulence factors. Thus, urban water networks act as connected yet selective resistome environments, while providing a foundational ecological framework for understanding the transport and dissemination of antimicrobial resistance and informing risk-oriented management of complex megacity aquatic systems.

title: Production of alpha-amylase from a novel strain of Bacillus licheniformis on low-cost substrates
summary: Amylase is an industrially important enzyme that can be utilised in various industrial processes, including those in the food, animal feed, pharmaceutical, detergent, textile, and paper industries. In this study, the isolate SHB17_28, which
content: Amylase is an industrially important enzyme that can be utilised in various industrial processes, including those in the food, animal feed, pharmaceutical, detergent, textile, and paper industries. In this study, the isolate SHB17_28, which exhibited the highest α-amylase production among the isolates obtained through garden soil screening, was identified as Bacillus licheniformis based on its phenotypic characteristics and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Six agro-industrial wastes, namely beet molasses, brewer’s malt, grape waste, corncob, wheat straw, and wheat bran, were evaluated as substrates for α-amylase production. Optimal conditions for α-amylase production by the strain were pH 8, 35°C, 48 h of incubation, and a shaking speed of 120 rpm. Of the agro-industrial waste material, grape waste (1.5% w v-1) and beet molasses (2% w v-1) yield the greatest α-amylase as carbon sources. Amylase was stable at 50°C, pH 8, and in a medium containing 5 mM of various metal ions. Overall, it was concluded that α-amylase from a new strain of Bacillus licheniformis could be produced at a low cost using agro-industrial waste materials, thereby eliminating the need for expensive growth factors.

title: Perovskite-Integrated Hybrid CPV–TEG Solar Module with Graded Optics: Toward Comprehensive Design
summary: Solar energy is vital for affordable and clean energy (SDG-7) alongside with reducing carbon emissions, but traditional solar panels struggle with inefficient sunlight capture and heat-related performance losses. To overcome these issues, w
content: Solar energy is vital for affordable and clean energy (SDG-7) alongside with reducing carbon emissions, but traditional solar panels struggle with inefficient sunlight capture and heat-related performance losses. To overcome these issues, we designed a compact hybrid solar module combining a graded-index (GRIN) lens to focus sunlight, a high-efficiency perovskite solar cell, a thermoelectric generator (TEG) to convert waste heat into electricity, and an air-cooled heat sink for simple thermal management. Unlike complex systems relying on active sun-tracking, large concentrators, or energy-intensive water cooling, our design is space-efficient and eliminates the requirement of solar tracking. Using COMSOL Multiphysics for optical and thermal modeling and SCAPS-1D for the solar cell modeling, we simulated the system under a 4.25 times sunlight concentration. The perovskite cell achieved a theoretical simulated efficiency of 47.76% under concentrated steady-state conditions, the TEG added 0.015% from recovered heat, and the overall module reached 48.34% efficiency under the specified steady-state simulation conditions. This compact system, structurally designed for non-tracking capabilities, shows strong potential for electrical output and heat management, offering a clear path for prototype development. Key factors like concentration ratio, wide incidence angle, solar cell thickness, and heat-sink performance were identified as critical for future improvements, guiding the way toward efficient, real-world solar solutions.

title: Plant biomarkers and elemental compositions reveal transport changes on the Iberian margin across the late Neogene
summary: To reconstruct Iberian Margin paleoclimate and the effects of Mediterranean gateway restriction during the late Miocene, International Ocean Discovery Program Expedition 401 drilled Site U1609 on the southwestern Portuguese Margin (37º22.62
content: To reconstruct Iberian Margin paleoclimate and the effects of Mediterranean gateway restriction during the late Miocene, International Ocean Discovery Program Expedition 401 drilled Site U1609 on the southwestern Portuguese Margin (37º22.6259’N, 9º35.9120’W; 1660 m water depth) in the path of Mediterranean Overflow Water (MOW). We present a multiproxy study of plant waxes, lignin phenols, palynomorphs, and X-ray fluorescence. From 11.5–9.5 Ma, hemipelagic sediments have high Ca and dinoflagellate:pollen ratios. Between 9.5 and 6 Ma plant proxies (e.g., alkanes and lignin) and terrigenous elements (e.g., Ti) become more abundant, with more land-based flux attributed to tectonic uplift and the initiation of MOW. Sediments from 6–2.5 Ma indicate relatively stable elemental proportions, although precessional pacing of Ti/Ca occurs throughout the record. Plant wax n -alkane δ 13 C and δD values indicate C 3 vegetation and Atlantic storm tracks, like modern, occurred throughout the warmer Tortonian–Zanclean climates. In contrast, lignin indicates greater variability across the record. High lignin transport and low syringyl/vanillyl ratio suggest riverine export from high-elevation conifer forests in the SE Iberian Peninsula, followed by lateral ocean current transport transport, with fluxes increasing as MOW strengthened at 4.5 Ma. During the Messinian Salinity Crisis, when MOW ceased, lignin delivery was reduced and restricted to lowland riverine inputs from SW Iberia, where angiosperms today dominate the exported woody biomass. We find river-exported gymnosperm lignin to be a valuable tracer of distal advection tracking the history of MOW across the Messinian gateway reorganization.

title: Robust perovskite lattice for durable and efficient pure-red light-emitting diodes
summary: Metal halide perovskite light-emitting diodes are rising as promising candidates for next-generation display technologies. The bromine-iodine mixed halide perovskites contribute to straightforward emitters for pure-red emission, however, su
content: Metal halide perovskite light-emitting diodes are rising as promising candidates for next-generation display technologies. The bromine-iodine mixed halide perovskites contribute to straightforward emitters for pure-red emission, however, suffering from limited electroluminescent durability and efficiency due to highly sensitive optical properties to the featured soft lattice. Here, we report robust perovskites by intrinsically reinforcing the lattice with synergistic rigid ring ammonium and dedicated electrostatic polymer. We reveal the mechanism of enhanced lattice stiffness by sequentially clarifying the rigid cation-induced high atomic packing factor and the electrostatic polymer-derived strong octahedral Coulomb force. The resultant perovskites exhibit more than 100% improvement in bulk modulus and over 75% decrease in bond angle fluctuation under a high electric field of 107 V m−1. The robust perovskite lattice strongly suppresses the electric field-induced lattice distortion and ion migration, and strengthens the carrier radiative recombination. Consequently, we demonstrate durable and efficient pure-red PeLEDs with a long lifetime of 343.3 h and a high external quantum efficiency of 31.3%. Moreover, we reveal good compatibility of this approach in boosting the blue and green device performances. Mixed-halide perovskites enable pure-red displays but suffer from poor durability and efficiency because their soft lattices distort. Zhou et al. stiffened the lattice with rigid ammonium rings and an electrostatic polymer, producing durable, efficient devices.

title: Southern Solutions to Fill Gaps in Global Development and Climate Finance: How the World’s Most Vulnerable Countries Are Deepening a Fourth Wave of Public Banking
summary: This article addresses the question of what financial resources are available to the world’s most climate exposed and vulnerable countries, and how this fits within and contributes to the broader South-South financial landscape. It presents
content: This article addresses the question of what financial resources are available to the world’s most climate exposed and vulnerable countries, and how this fits within and contributes to the broader South-South financial landscape. It presents original empirical data and institutional analysis to show new trends where emerging Southern-led public banks and financial institutions are deepening and broadening the global financial architecture, and why they feel compelled to do it. Using data from the IMF, UNCTAD, and the FICS/Peking University Institute of New Structural Economics Public Banks Database the article argues that the most climate-exposed and vulnerable countries have the least available finance and pay the highest prices for it. These countries did not cause the climate crisis, they are among the most impacted by it, and they have the least resources to confront it. Nonetheless, this does not mean they can do nothing; this article aims to show how developing countries are taking the reins into their own hands in an effort to fill gaps and limitations of the global financial architecture. It maps the public development banks owned by the 74 members of the Vulnerable-20 grouping, alongside complementary, innovative, instruments and mechanisms being created by V-20 and a broader, overlapping, group of net borrower countries. The article identifies and nests these within a maturing “fourth wave” of South-South initiatives that began in the mid 2010’s with the largest BRICS economies. The incipient Borrowers Platform, launched in 2026 by net borrowing countries, could, if successful, represent the peak thus far in this evolution.

title: Ship-shore energy systems for maritime electrification: Voyage-energy provision, configurations and resilience
summary: Maritime decarbonisation requires a shift towards low- and zero-emission energy systems, while the viability of electrified vessels depends on how voyage energy is provided onboard and replenished externally. Existing reviews mainly organis
content: Maritime decarbonisation requires a shift towards low- and zero-emission energy systems, while the viability of electrified vessels depends on how voyage energy is provided onboard and replenished externally. Existing reviews mainly organise the field around technologies, vessel configurations and replenishment solutions, with less attention to how energy provision and system constraints shift across the ship-shore system. We reviewed literature published primarily from 2000 to 2026 on onboard capability, external replenishment, ship-shore coordination and resilience, and synthesised these areas through the perspective of voyage-energy provision. The review identifies two energy-supply pathways. Shore-electric operation relies on sustained external electricity supply, while fuel-carried electric operation relies more on onboard fuel storage and conversion. Four representative configurations are distinguished as battery-dominant shore-electric, range-extended hybrid, power-buffered hybrid and fuel-dominant electric. Three illustrative case studies examine how replenishment conditions and onboard capability affect operational feasibility across representative vessel services. As reliance shifts from external supply towards onboard autonomy, the main constraints move from replenishment access and port-side supply capacity towards onboard energy storage and conversion capability. These dependencies also shape vulnerability to physical and cyber disruptions and the continuity of energy services. These findings can support early assessment of likely deployment constraints under different operating and infrastructure conditions and help coordinate vessel and shore-side energy planning.

title: Progress in organic nanomaterials mediated healthcare biosensing
summary: Deteriorating food quality and stress-ridden professional commitments have severely affected the health quality and physical efficacy, making it mandatory to monitor the food quality for cautiously limiting the intake of processed eatables.
content: Deteriorating food quality and stress-ridden professional commitments have severely affected the health quality and physical efficacy, making it mandatory to monitor the food quality for cautiously limiting the intake of processed eatables. With exposure to debilitating environmental toxins remaining unabated, regular checkups have emerged as essential for adopting timely cautions. In this context, nanomaterials (NMs) are progressing as current focus for accurate and cost-effective screening of pathogens, environmental and industrial contaminants posing health risks. Progress in functionalization assays and characterization methods has improved the understanding quantum effects and combinatorial functioning in NMs for their biosensing applications. Diversified into organic, inorganic and carbon based textures, NMs provide innovative remedies through their size-morphology graded physicochemical properties and enhanced surface area-enriched chemistry. This article focuses on healthcare-biosensing utilities of organic NMs, with thrust on the structural correlations and comparative aspects for a sustainable future. Illustrations herein comprise the recent use of polymer nanocomposites, dendrimers, hydrogels, thin film-assemblies and molecularly engineered polymers. The discussion on biosensing probe-attributes of these NMs could reinforce their modifications for enhanced accuracy and functionality.

title: Toward iron upcycling for green hydrogen: target engineering for powder-derived iron-based nanoparticles by laser ablation in water
summary: Developing sustainable and cost-effective oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts is urgently required to overcome the cost and critical raw material status of the benchmark iridium and ruthenium-based catalysts. To address this ch
content: Developing sustainable and cost-effective oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts is urgently required to overcome the cost and critical raw material status of the benchmark iridium and ruthenium-based catalysts. To address this challenge, iron-based nanostructures represent promising alternatives due to their abundance, low cost and potential catalytic activity. Herein, we propose a proof-of-concept study toward future iron upcycling approaches through the synthesis of iron-based nanoparticles by pulsed laser ablation in water. Custom-made iron targets were fabricated from commercial iron (Fe) powders and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) employing different Fe:PMMA weight ratios. A bulk iron target was employed as a reference material. A comprehensive physicochemical characterization revealed a strong influence of the target composition on nanoparticles formation and phase evolution. While nanoparticles generated from the bulk target predominantly exhibited the hematite phase, the powder-based targets produced mixed-phase iron-based nanoparticles. Electrochemical investigations demonstrated a competitive OER activity with the nanoparticles obtained from Fe:PMMA 1:2 target showing an overpotential of 335 mV at 10 mA/cm 2 with a deposited total mass loading of ∼47 µg cm −2 . These findings demonstrate the feasibility of tailoring iron-based nanostructures through a versatile powder-based target engineering approach, providing a promising route toward circular manufacturing through iron upcycling for green hydrogen applications.

title: Targeted nanomedicine for ischemic cardiomyopathy
summary: Ischemic cardiomyopathy remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The therapeutic efficacy of conventional pharmacological interventions is constrained by poor bioavailability, limited myocardial targeting capacity, and
content: Ischemic cardiomyopathy remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The therapeutic efficacy of conventional pharmacological interventions is constrained by poor bioavailability, limited myocardial targeting capacity, and systemic adverse effects. Nanomedicine has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome these limitations by enhancing drug stability, prolonging blood circulation time, and enabling precise delivery to diseased tissues. In the setting of ischemic cardiomyopathy, active targeting approaches-particularly those functionalized with tannic acid and cardiac-targeting peptides-have been extensively investigated to boost the delivery efficiency of therapeutic agents and halt disease progression. Moreover, the ischemic microenvironment (IME), characterized by inflammation, redox imbalance, and enzymatic dysregulation, not only drives pathological progression but also creates unique opportunities for site-specific therapeutic intervention. Systematic comprehension and evaluation of these targeting strategies are critical to advancing the clinical translation of myocardium-targeted nanomedicines. In this review, we summarize recent advances in myocardium-targeted nanotherapeutic strategies, with a special focus on tannic acid-based systems, cardiac-targeting peptides, reductive microenvironment-responsive platforms, and enzyme-responsive delivery approaches. We also discuss the current limitations and future perspectives of such strategies, aiming to offer insights into the rational design and clinical development of next-generation therapeutics for ischemic cardiomyopathy.

title: CHEMICAL-TECHNOLOGICAL PRECONDITIONS FOR DIGITAL TWIN IMPLEMENTATION IN POLYMER PROCESSING: A DOCUMENTED TECHNOLOGY BASELINE FROM BULGARIAN PLASTICS
source: Journal of Chemical Technology and Metallurgy
summary: Digital Twin technology is increasingly proposed for polymer processing, yet the chemical-technological conditions that make a twin useful, and the equipment baseline required to build one, are rarely examined together against documented in
content: Digital Twin technology is increasingly proposed for polymer processing, yet the chemical-technological conditions that make a twin useful, and the equipment baseline required to build one, are rarely examined together against documented industrial evidence. This paper establishes why polymer processing is a favourable domain for Digital Twin implementation and then tests how far the necessary preconditions are met in a national producing sector. The argument proceeds from polymer physics. Because melt viscosity is strongly shear- and temperature-dependent, and because thermal history governs crystallization, shrinkage and residual stress, a fixed set of machine settings does not reproduce a fixed process state when polymer grade, recycled fraction, moisture content or additive level varies. A twin is valuable in this domain precisely because the state variables that determine part quality cannot be measured directly in production. Against this background, a technology inventory was compiled for a census of 29 Bulgarian plastics manufacturers (NACE 22.2x), of which 20 firms have documented process-level evidence. Extrusion is documented at 13 of the 20 firms, injection moulding at 5 and internal recycling at 4, with thermoforming, coating and blow moulding at 1 - 2 firms each; 7 of the 20 firms disclose named equipment. Sensor-level process instrumentation is documented at no firm, and no firm provides evidence of an ERP, MES or SCADA system, or of a Digital Twin. On the classification applied here, no firm falls in the confirmed Digital Twin category and three fall in the Digital-Twin-ready category. The binding constraint in this sector is therefore not modelling capability but the absenceof the in-process measurements – melt temperature, melt pressure, cavity pressure and screw torque - from which any twin state estimate must be constructed. Firms processing recycled feedstock have the strongest technological case for instrumenting first.

title: Oleic acid suppresses NLRP3 inflammasome activation to prevent dermal macrophage death and limit imiquimod-induced psoriasis
summary: Psoriasis is associated with altered lipid metabolism, including reduced expression of fatty acid metabolism genes and decreased circulating oleic acid. Here we report that oral oleic acid supplementation normalized serum oleic acid levels
content: Psoriasis is associated with altered lipid metabolism, including reduced expression of fatty acid metabolism genes and decreased circulating oleic acid. Here we report that oral oleic acid supplementation normalized serum oleic acid levels and protected from skin thickening and epidermal hyperplasia in a imiquimod mice model of psoriasis. These effects were associated with preserved skin-resident macrophage numbers and reduced expression of key psoriasis-associated inflammatory markers. Mechanistically, imiquimod induces dermal macrophage death via NLRP3/caspase-1 inflammasome activation, while adoptive transfer of dermal macrophages attenuates psoriasiform inflammation. Oleic acid rescued macrophages from imiquimod and nigericin-induced death in vitro by suppressing NF-κB and NLRP3/caspase-1 signaling, lowering IL-1β and reactive oxygen species production, and restoring mitochondrial homeostasis, independently of TLR7. Together, our results position dermal macrophage survival as a previously unrecognized checkpoint in psoriasiform inflammation, and suggest that restoring lipid metabolic fitness, rather than solely targeting downstream inflammatory mediators, may offer an additional mechanism-based strategy to limit tissue- damaging inflammation.

title: Schizotrins B-E from the Cultured Cyanobacterium CCIBt3280 - Unique Biosynthetic Signatures and Evidence for an Antibacterial Target
summary: We report the discovery and chemical structures of schizotrins B-E (1-4) isolated from cultures of Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280. These peptides were identified by spectroscopic and spectrometric analyses. Their absolute configuration was establ
content: We report the discovery and chemical structures of schizotrins B-E (1-4) isolated from cultures of Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280. These peptides were identified by spectroscopic and spectrometric analyses. Their absolute configuration was established by Marfey’s and advanced NMR analysis, computational modeling, and Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280 genome analysis. Conserved A- and B-type ketoreductase motifs revealed a stereochemical control of αketoreduction in polyketide natural products. Phylogenomic analyses placed Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280 within the Floridanema family-level clade, indicating that its current assignment to Phormidium should be reassessed. Genome mining uncovered numerous previously unknown schizotrin-like biosynthetic gene clusters in publicly available genomes. The antibacterial activity of peptides 1-4 were also investigated. Schizotrin B inhibited the growth of Bacillus anthracis Sterne at 1 µM. Whole-genome sequencing of spontaneous resistant mutants of B. anthracis revealed a loss-of-function mutation in psd (phosphatidylserine decarboxylase), implicating membrane phospholipid homeostasis in schizotrin B activity. Our results expanded the chemical diversity of the schizotrin family, provided new insights into the biosynthesis of αcarbonyl-containing amino acids, supported the placement of the schizotrin-producing lineage within a potentially novel cyanobacterial genus, and provided insights into the potential mechanism of schizotrins antibacterial resistance.

title: Intelligent Identification of Key Nutrient Loss Nodes in Topsoil Stockpiling Based on ST-GCN and Multi-Source Heterogeneous Data Fusion
summary: Stripped topsoil from power transmission projects faces continuous nutrient degradation during stockpiling, compromising subsequent vegetation restoration. This study proposes an intelligent method to identify key nutrient loss nodes by fus
content: Stripped topsoil from power transmission projects faces continuous nutrient degradation during stockpiling, compromising subsequent vegetation restoration. This study proposes an intelligent method to identify key nutrient loss nodes by fusing Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Networks (ST-GCN) with multi-source heterogeneous data. Indoor simulations monitored physical, chemical, and biological indices of Shandong brown soil, Jiangxi red soil, and Tibetan alpine meadow soil under varying storage conditions. An ST-GCN model predicted spatio-temporal nutrient evolution, while a sliding-window algorithm detected mutation points. Results indicated that alpine meadow soil suffered the most severe decline (39.3% chemical factor loss), followed by brown soil (25.0%) and red soil (17.6%). Strip stacking best preserved physical structure (78.9% retention), while tarpaulin covering maximized biological activity retention (64.0%). Coupling analysis revealed that physical degradation precedes biological response, triggering chemical loss. Under the optimal combination (strip stacking plus tarpaulin), key loss nodes were identified at 30–60 days for alpine meadow soil and red soil (with a delayed peak in the latter), and 60–90 days for brown soil.This method accurately captures differential nutrient attenuation patterns, providing a scientific basis for precise topsoil conservation management.

title: Genital Involvement in Female Patients With Congenital Type 1 Plasminogen Deficiency: A Case Series and Updated Literature Review
summary: INTRODUCTION: Congenital type 1 plasminogen deficiency (PLGD1) is an ultra-rare disorder characterized by the formation of fibrin-rich pseudomembranes on mucosal surfaces across multiple organ systems. In affected females, ligneous lesions
content: INTRODUCTION: Congenital type 1 plasminogen deficiency (PLGD1) is an ultra-rare disorder characterized by the formation of fibrin-rich pseudomembranes on mucosal surfaces across multiple organ systems. In affected females, ligneous lesions may involve the genital tract. AIM: We aimed to characterize the clinical manifestations and therapeutic approaches associated with genital involvement in females with PLGD1. METHODS: A structured literature review was performed to identify previously reported females with PLGD1 and genital lesions. In addition, PLGD1 patients followed at Padua University Hospital were included. RESULTS: A total of 57 females with genital manifestations consistent with PLGD1 were identified, including 4 cases from our institution, 8 patients enrolled in a phase 2-3 clinical trial, and 9 cases described before recognition of the association with plasminogen deficiency. Reported plasminogen activity levels ranged from < 2% to 50%. Pseudomembranous lesions involved the vagina, cervix, endometrium, ovaries, and fallopian tubes. Genital involvement represented the sole clinical manifestation in 13 of 57 patients (22.8%). The most common symptoms included dysmenorrhea, vaginal discharge, post-coital bleeding, and infertility (18/38 cases, 47.4%). Surgical excision was associated with a high rate of recurrence. Data on topical and systemic treatments for genital involvement were limited and largely empirical. The most effective therapeutic approach was replacement therapy with human Glu-plasminogen concentrate and fresh frozen plasma. CONCLUSIONS: Genital tract involvement in PLGD1 is not uncommon and may represent the sole manifestation of the disease, with potential implications for fertility. Glu-plasminogen replacement therapy has shown promising results, although its availability remains limited worldwide.

title: From accurate AI to sustainable AI: A lifecycle computational framework for resource-efficient, explainable, and trustworthy artificial intelligence in energy systems
summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to improve forecasting, optimization, control, and decision support in energy systems, yet much of the literature remains dominated by accuracy-centric evaluation. This critical review argues tha
content: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to improve forecasting, optimization, control, and decision support in energy systems, yet much of the literature remains dominated by accuracy-centric evaluation. This critical review argues that such evaluation is insufficient for sustainable energy transitions because AI models also impose computational, environmental, operational, and governance costs across their lifecycle. Rather than descriptively summarizing prior work, the paper comparatively examines major groups of studies, including AI for renewable-energy forecasting, smart-grid optimization, energy management, Green AI, explainable AI, and trustworthy AI, to identify where their assumptions, metrics, and deployment priorities converge or conflict. The review shows that existing research often treats model performance, computational efficiency, carbon footprint, explainability, robustness, privacy, and accountability as separate concerns, leaving a gap in integrated lifecycle assessment. To address this gap, the paper proposes a lifecycle computational framework for sustainable AI in energy systems, covering data acquisition, model design, training, inference, deployment, monitoring, retraining, and governance. The framework supports multi-dimensional evaluation of AI systems in terms of accuracy, resource efficiency, carbon impact, transparency, reliability, and real-world deployability, offering a pathway from merely accurate AI toward sustainable, explainable, and trustworthy AI for energy applications.

title: Oxide Scale Decomposition‐Driven Intergranular Oxidation in Hot‐Rolled Hot Stamping Steel: Mechanism and Process Control
summary: Intergranular oxidation (IGO) in 22MnB5 steel degrades automotive component performance, yet oxygen supply mechanisms under low oxygen potentials remain unclear. This study reveals that IGO occurs exclusively below 900 °C, with the depth ex
content: Intergranular oxidation (IGO) in 22MnB5 steel degrades automotive component performance, yet oxygen supply mechanisms under low oxygen potentials remain unclear. This study reveals that IGO occurs exclusively below 900 °C, with the depth exhibiting a C‐curve temperature dependence with a 751 °C nose temperature. Depth evolution follows logarithmic kinetics rather than Wagner’s parabolic law due to grain boundary diffusion channel blockage. Crucially, the oxide scale decomposition‐driven oxygen supply mechanism is systematically quantified for the first time: Under vacuum, oxide scale decomposition releases oxygen that propagates IGO to 26.4 μm after 8 h at 750 °C—a 136% increase over conventional oxidizing conditions—causing monotonic depth growth deviating from classical C‐curve behavior. Focused ion beam–energy‐dispersive X‐ray spectroscopy reveals a core–shell oxide structure (SiO 2 core/Cr 2 O 3 inner shell/MnO outer shell) governed by selective oxidation thermodynamics and diffusion kinetics. Industrial validation confirms 15 μm IGO depth in hot coil slow‐cooling zones, matching laboratory FeO decomposition results. Accordingly, optimized processing—lower coiling temperatures, front‐stage laminar cooling, and forced post‐coil cooling—was validated to suppress IGO below 5 μm. This work establishes a thermodynamic–kinetic framework for IGO in hot stamping steels, bridging fundamental mechanisms with industrial practice to resolve surface quality degradation through targeted process control strategies.

title: Air pollution sensing to urban air quality insight: review of spatially interpolated data products from sensor networks
summary: Air pollution adversely impacts health globally, disproportionately affecting urban populations. Regulatory monitoring is often too spatially coarse to capture true intra-urban variability, needed to prioritize and guide localized intervent
content: Air pollution adversely impacts health globally, disproportionately affecting urban populations. Regulatory monitoring is often too spatially coarse to capture true intra-urban variability, needed to prioritize and guide localized interventions and policies. High-density lower-cost sensor (LCS) networks, mobile monitoring, satellite-derived products, and advanced interpolation techniques are emerging to support higher spatial resolution characterization. However, results from related studies are varied, disconnected across different fields, and as yet with no defined standards or guidance. This review examines the literature from 2005-2025 to systematically compare data collection and modeling pipelines for accuracy and application to the intra-urban challenge. 166 studies from regional to neighborhood scale were analyzed quantitatively on monitoring network characteristics (geographic location, spatial density, target pollutants, study duration) and interpolation modeling approaches (algorithms, predictive covariates, performance metrics). Studies from Europe, Asia, and North America dominated the literature, with particulate matter being the most studied pollutant. While 95% of studies had measurement density below 20,000 km2/device (metro scale), none had sufficient resolution for capturing intra-urban heterogeneity. Modeling approaches shifted over time from primarily geostatistical methods toward increasingly sophisticated machine learning and deep learning techniques incorporating diverse covariates, including meteorology, land use, traffic patterns, and satellite data products. More than measurement density or model complexity, strategic use of both static and dynamic covariates in data driven models was most consistently associated with performance improvement for interpolation of both PM2.5 and NOx. However, major gaps remain including (1) imbalance in data availability geographically, temporally, and across pollutant species, leading to major challenges in assessing and achieving transferability of models globally, (2) limited data availability at appropriate intra-urban scale for most metro areas, (3) lack of evaluation and reporting standards necessary to truly compare performance of different data-model pipelines, and (4) general lack of generating or reporting uncertainty quantification on model outputs, critically needed for interpretability and sensitivity analyses. These gaps point to an urgent need for not only interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation but also discipline-wide guidance that will enable objective assessment of model performance and state-of-the-art, including shared benchmark datasets, standardized evaluation metrics, mandatory unit reporting, and guidelines for complete model specifications.

title: Brassinosteroid Enhances Thermotolerance by Improving Photosynthesis and Membrane Stability Under Reproductive‐Stage Heat Stress in KDML105 Rice ( Oryza sativa L.)
source: Journal of Agronomy and Crop Science
summary: ABSTRACT Brassinosteroids (BRs) are plant steroid hormones known to enhance tolerance to abiotic stress, including heat stress (HT). This study investigated the effects of foliar application of BRs (0, 0.05, 0.1, and 0.5 nM) on the physiolo
content: ABSTRACT Brassinosteroids (BRs) are plant steroid hormones known to enhance tolerance to abiotic stress, including heat stress (HT). This study investigated the effects of foliar application of BRs (0, 0.05, 0.1, and 0.5 nM) on the physiological performance and yield of the tropical photosensitive rice cultivar KDML105 at the reproductive stage under HT (42°C for 7 days). Experiments were conducted at booting and 50% flowering stages under controlled HT in greenhouse and naturally HT exposure in field conditions. Heat stress significantly impaired physiological performance by increasing electrolyte leakage (EL) and malondialdehyde (MDA), indicating reduced membrane stability. It also reduced photosynthetic pigments, PSII efficiency, stomatal conductance and transpiration rate, leading to a decrease in assimilate production and grain yield. Brassinosteroids application improved physiological performance by maintaining membrane stability, preserving photosynthetic pigments and enhancing PSII efficiency and CO 2 gas exchange. These factors may be associated with better assimilate translocation and grain filling, resulting in higher yield under HT. Brassinosteroids mainly enhanced reproductive traits, including total number of grains/panicle, number of filled grains/panicle, and grain yield. At the 50% flowering stage, greater heat sensitivity was observed compared to the booting stage, while 0.5 nM BR showed the best physiological improvement. These results suggest that BRs enhance thermotolerance in KDML105 rice by protecting photosynthetic function and membrane stability during the reproductive stage.

title: Realizing Reversible Photo‐Charging via Stacked 1T/2H MoS 2 Bifunctional Cathodes for Photo‐Rechargeable Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Photo‐rechargeable batteries that integrate solar energy harvesting, conversion, and storage in a single device are able to efficiently utilize sustainable energy. However, current photo‐batteries based on bifunctional (photovoltai
content: ABSTRACT Photo‐rechargeable batteries that integrate solar energy harvesting, conversion, and storage in a single device are able to efficiently utilize sustainable energy. However, current photo‐batteries based on bifunctional (photovoltaic conversion and energy storage) cathodes could only achieve photo‐assisted charging, whereas light‐only photo‐charging remains incomplete and irreversible. Particularly, in absence of a photo‐charging circuit, the observed charging phenomena are pseudo photo‐charging due to side reactions. To realize genuine photo‐charging, we design a bifunctional cathode of MoS 2 by integrating photo active (2H) and energy storage (1T) phases. Nickel oxide is introduced to improve the interface conductivity and stabilize the 2H/1T phases of MoS 2 . Additionally, we employed an external resistance to balance the self‐discharge current and the photo‐charging current under illumination. For the first time, we demonstrate Zn 2+ photo‐batteries that can be reversibly photo‐charged for over ten times, and the deposition of zinc at the anode is visualized. The photo‐rechargeable batteries could realize a photo‐charging capacity ratio of 100% by2 h illumination, with a specific capacity of 110.55 mAh g −1 . Furthermore, we assemble a sustainable energy harvest‐conversion‐storage mini‐system that could practically provide energy to portable electronics.

title: Enhancing hydrogen embrittlement resistance in a non-equiatomic Fe0.5CoCrNi high-entropy alloy via Mo alloying: A Combined First-Principles and Experimental Study
source: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
summary: This study employs first-principles calculations combined with experiments to investigate the effect of Mo alloying on the hydrogen embrittlement resistance of the non-equiatomic Fe 0.5 CoCrNi high-entropy alloy. The results indicate that M
content: This study employs first-principles calculations combined with experiments to investigate the effect of Mo alloying on the hydrogen embrittlement resistance of the non-equiatomic Fe 0.5 CoCrNi high-entropy alloy. The results indicate that Mo addition improves the hydrogen embrittlement resistance of the alloy. First-principles calculations show that Mo suppresses H2 dissociation and weakens atomic H adsorption on the alloy surface, as reflected by the increased H 2 dissociation energy and the raised H adsorption energy, an effect arising from the Mo-induced modification of the surface electronic structure combined with the local chemical environment. Surface work function and density-of-states analyses further indicate that Mo doping promotes electron delocalization and raises the work function, thereby improving the surface electrochemical stability. In addition, Mo converts the hydrogen dissolution energy at grain boundaries from a negative value (-0.135 eV) to a positive value (+0.089 eV), suppressing hydrogen dissolution at grain boundaries. Experimental results confirm that Mo enables the alloy to maintain excellent mechanical properties in hydrogen environments, exhibiting a mixed fracture mode combining ductile and brittle fracture characteristics. The experiments also verify that Mo effectively mitigates the weakening effect of H on grain boundary cohesive strength. This study elucidates the hydrogen embrittlement resistance mechanism of Mo at the atomic scale, providing a theoretical basis for the rational design of high-entropy alloys with superior hydrogen embrittlement resistance.

title: Influence of Adaxial and Abaxial Leaf Surface Wax Alkanes and Free Fatty Acids of Lagenaria siceraria on Short‐Range Attraction and Oviposition‐Site Selection in Helicoverpa armigera
summary: ABSTRACT Larvae of Helicoverpa armigera (Hübner) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) can cause complete defoliation of Lagenaria siceraria (Molina) Standl., commonly known as bottle gourd, resulting in substantial yield losses in India. Female moths o
content: ABSTRACT Larvae of Helicoverpa armigera (Hübner) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) can cause complete defoliation of Lagenaria siceraria (Molina) Standl., commonly known as bottle gourd, resulting in substantial yield losses in India. Female moths oviposit exclusively on the abaxial leaf surface, rather than the adaxial leaf surface, suggesting that abaxial leaf surface wax (ABLSW) chemicals serve as a short‐range attractant and cues for oviposition‐site selection. This study investigates the role of ABLSW chemicals, specifically alkanes and free fatty acids (FFAs), from three bottle gourd cultivars—ANKUR AMIT (AMIT), KSP‐1720 (KSP) and ANKUR GOLU (GOLU)—as short‐range attractants and cues for oviposition‐site selection by H. armigera females. Twenty n ‐alkanes ( n ‐C 14 to n ‐C 36 ) were identified in both adaxial and abaxial leaf surface waxes of these three cultivars. In the adaxial leaf surface waxes (ADLSW), 14 and 13 FFAs within the range of C12:0 to C22:0 were detected in AMIT and KSP, and GOLU, respectively. In contrast, in the ABLSW, 13 and 14 FFAs were detected in AMIT and GOLU, and KSP, respectively. In the ABLSW chemicals, heptadecane and palmitoleic acid were the predominant n ‐alkane and FFA, respectively, in these cultivars. Females exhibited attraction and oviposition on 0.25 leaf equivalent of crude ABLSW from these cultivars compared to solvent controls (petroleum ether), as demonstrated by Y‐tube olfactometer and oviposition assays. Synthetic blends replicating the composition of 0.25 leaf equivalent of crude ABLSW—comprising heptadecane, pentacosane, heptacosane, palmitoleic acid and stearic acid for AMIT; hexadecane, heptadecane and palmitoleic acid for KSP; and heptadecane, palmitoleic acid and stearic acid for GOLU—functioned as candidate active compounds for short‐range attraction and cues for oviposition‐site selection in H. armigera . Females displayed comparable egg‐laying responses to all three synthetic blends when tested against each other. Therefore, these blends may serve as effective lures for baited traps in pest management strategies.

title: Perspectives of Biomaterial‐Based Sustainable Integrated Micro‐ and Nanophotonics
summary: ABSTRACT Biomolecular photonics is emerging as a pathway toward sustainable alternatives to fully semiconductor‐based devices, leveraging the unique optical properties and solution processability of proteins, nucleic acids, and other biogen
content: ABSTRACT Biomolecular photonics is emerging as a pathway toward sustainable alternatives to fully semiconductor‐based devices, leveraging the unique optical properties and solution processability of proteins, nucleic acids, and other biogenic molecules. This review covers recent advances in nano‐ and microscale biophotonic devices, spanning biopolymer waveguides (with optical losses down to 0.24 dB cm −1 ), bio‐organic LEDs and lasers (luminous efficiencies up to 130 lm W −1 ; lifetimes >3600 h), biohybrid photovoltaics (PCE up to ∼20%), photodetectors, and optoelectronic memristors. We critically examine interfacial engineering challenges, such as stability, charge separation, and hybrid integration with semiconductor solid‐state platforms, as the central bottleneck to be overcome in translating laboratory breakthroughs into consumer‐grade photonic integrated circuits. We argue that, while biomaterial‐based devices generally trail their inorganic counterparts in efficiency and lifetime, the unique biocompatibility, specificity, and broadband tunability of biogenic molecules provide decisive advantages in well‐defined niches: implantable and wearable diagnostics, point‐of‐care biosensors, and emerging quantum bio‐photonic platforms. Moreover, clear evidence indicates that inexpensive, stable, and easy‑to‑handle biopolymers and composites, available for large‑scale production from biomass, can become essential for building, improving, and stabilizing waveguide and photovoltaic structures. By bridging molecular biology and photonic engineering, biomaterials offer a pathway toward scalable, biocompatible, and energy‐efficient photonic technologies.

title: MoS 2 ‐Modified Jute Fibers: Synergistic Enhancement of Tribological Properties in Brake Material via Interface Compatibility Optimization and Surface Modification
summary: ABSTRACT Asbestos and copper fibers are increasingly restricted in brake materials due to health and environmental hazards. Jute fibers (JF) are promising sustainable alternatives, yet their poor interfacial compatibility with polymer matri
content: ABSTRACT Asbestos and copper fibers are increasingly restricted in brake materials due to health and environmental hazards. Jute fibers (JF) are promising sustainable alternatives, yet their poor interfacial compatibility with polymer matrices limits mechanical and tribological performance. Herein, MoS 2 nanosheets were grown in situ on JF via a facile hydrothermal method to fabricate dual‐functional JF/MoS 2 hybrid reinforcements for polymer‐based brake materials. The 4 wt.% JF/MoS 2 hybrid increased the hardness by 99%, the compressive strength and modulus by 40% and 14%, and the impact strength by 21%, and reduced the wear rate by 36% while delivering a more stable friction coefficient than the unfilled control. Compared with the physically mixed JF and MoS 2 , the hybrid improved the compressive strength and modulus by 70% and 47% and reduced the wear rate by 30%. The grafted MoS 2 strengthens interfacial adhesion through mechanical anchoring and, upon sliding, forms a low‐shear, high‐load‐bearing transfer film that mitigates abrasive and adhesive wear. These results are based on laboratory‐scale dry sliding tests and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of full‐scale braking performance. This strategy addresses interfacial adhesion and lubricant dispersion, offering a new paradigm for sustainable, high‐performance, asbestos‐free friction materials.

title: Human attractiveness to Aedes albopictus : sweat amino acid associations and functional screening of skin volatiles
summary: BACKGROUND: Human-derived chemical cues are central to mosquito host-seeking and may provide candidates for odor-baited surveillance and attract-and-kill tools. However, the factors associated with inter-individual attractiveness to Aedes a
content: BACKGROUND: Human-derived chemical cues are central to mosquito host-seeking and may provide candidates for odor-baited surveillance and attract-and-kill tools. However, the factors associated with inter-individual attractiveness to Aedes albopictus (Skuse) and the behavioral activity of corresponding skin volatiles remain incompletely characterized. RESULTS: metrics were not significantly associated with attraction. In a subset of nine volunteers, total sweat amino acid concentration was inversely associated with attraction (r = -0.812, P = 0.008). Headspace solid-phase microextraction gas chromatography-mass spectrometry detected 28 skin volatiles, including 5 compounds present in all volunteers and 10 volunteer-specific compounds selected with the common compounds for functional screening. Electroantennography showed significantly greater responses to all five common compounds than to liquid paraffin and to crotonaldehyde than to n-hexane. Dual-choice bioassays identified six compounds with positive directional responses after Holm-Bonferroni correction: decanal, nonanal, tricyclodecenyl acetate, tetradecanol, tridecane and (E)-2-dodecen-1-ol. CONCLUSION: The integrated chemical, electrophysiological and behavioral workflow identified an inverse association between sweat amino acid concentration and human attractiveness, and defined six skin volatiles as priorities for dose-response, blend and semi-field evaluation toward Aedes albopictus lure development. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: One‐Step Fabrication of Lightweight PLA Foam Boards With Enhanced Compressive Performance and Thermal Insulation
summary: ABSTRACT An integrated foaming and molding strategy was developed to produce lightweight poly(lactic acid) (PLA) foam boards from pellets modified with dicumyl peroxide and trimethylolpropane triacrylate (TMPTA) using supercritical CO 2 . T
content: ABSTRACT An integrated foaming and molding strategy was developed to produce lightweight poly(lactic acid) (PLA) foam boards from pellets modified with dicumyl peroxide and trimethylolpropane triacrylate (TMPTA) using supercritical CO 2 . Torque, spectroscopic, gel content and rheological analyses provided indirect evidence consistent with crosslinked structure formation, while increased complex viscosity and elastic response suggested improved melt strength. Concurrent pellet expansion and interparticle bonding enabled board formation within a single foaming cycle, eliminating separate secondary molding. At 135°C and 15 MPa, PLAD T0.75 achieved the highest volumetric expansion ratio of 32.80 and the lowest density of 0.038 g cm −3 . PLAD T0.5 exhibited balanced cellular morphology and functional performance, with an expansion ratio of 30.76, a density of 0.041 g cm −3 , a compressive stress of 2.51 MPa at 80% strain and a thermal conductivity of 0.037 W m −1 K −1 . It also exhibited the lowest compressive creep strain among all samples at 100°C and 0.2 MPa after 1 h. Increasing TMPTA to 1 wt% caused cell coarsening and reduced overall performance. These findings demonstrate the importance of balancing the extent of reactive modification with cellular structure. They provide a practical, simplified route to PLA foam boards combining low density, compressive load‐bearing capacity and thermal insulation.

title: Effect of Water Content on the Tribological Properties of Grease
summary: ABSTRACT In mechanical lubrication systems, grease can become contaminated with water due to seal failure and high ambient humidity. Water can alter the fibrous network of the thickener in grease, leading to base‐oil separation, reduced con
content: ABSTRACT In mechanical lubrication systems, grease can become contaminated with water due to seal failure and high ambient humidity. Water can alter the fibrous network of the thickener in grease, leading to base‐oil separation, reduced consistency and abnormal oil bleeding. In this study, experiments were combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the tribological behaviour of lubricating systems with different water contents, together with changes in parameters such as density distribution and system height. The aim was to clarify the short‐term effects of water on grease structure and lubrication performance. The results show that the system with 5% water exhibits the best lubrication performance. Compared with the anhydrous system, the maximum wear‐scar depth decreased by 0.142 μm and the maximum stress decreased by 29%. These findings suggest that a moderate amount of water forms hydrogen bonds with the polar groups of the lithium soap thickener, strengthening the soap‐fibre network. This interaction stabilizes the emulsion formed by water, base oil and thickener, resulting in the highest resistance to compression. In contrast, excessive water increases the intermolecular spacing between thickener molecules, weakens the structural integrity of the thickener network, promotes lubricant‐film rupture and reduces load‐carrying capacity. The experimental results are consistent with the MD simulations.

title: Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition and Substrate Engineering of Low-Resistivity Ultrathin MoCx Films for Advanced Interconnect Applications
summary: As Copper (Cu) interconnect dimensions continue to shrink, conventional tantalum/tantalum nitride (Ta/TaN) liner/barrier layers occupy an increasing fraction of the available interconnect volume and introduce additional electrical resistanc
content: As Copper (Cu) interconnect dimensions continue to shrink, conventional tantalum/tantalum nitride (Ta/TaN) liner/barrier layers occupy an increasing fraction of the available interconnect volume and introduce additional electrical resistance because of their relatively high resistivity. Therefore, a key challenge is to develop ultrathin liner/barrier materials that can maintain low resistivity while providing effective Cu diffusion-barrier performance. In this work, we demonstrate MoC x as a liner-free barrier material using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD). For this PEALD-grown film, cycloheptatriene molybdenum tricarbonyl, (η 6 -C 7 H 8 )Mo(CO) 3 , was first introduced as a precursor to synthesize ultrathin molybdenum carbide (MoC x ) films. The effects of plasma reactants, plasma power, deposition temperature, film thickness, and substrate types were systematically evaluated to clarify how PEALD process conditions and substrate chemistry influence the electrical performance of ultrathin MoC x films. We observed nucleation differences during the growth based on the substrate; MoC x films deposited on Al 2 O 3 consistently exhibited lower resistivity than those grown on SiO 2 .
