Using the optimized deposition process, amorphous MoC x films thinner than 5 nm showed resistivities as low as ~230 μΩ·cm without any post-deposition annealing. For reference, current Ta/TaN liner/barrier layers typically exceed 500 μΩ·cm resistivity in the sub-5 nm thickness regime. Sub-5 nm MoC x film also showed good Cu adhesion and effective Cu diffusion-barrier behavior after thermal annealing of up to 500 °C. These results demonstrate the potential of ultrathin amorphous MoC x as a low-resistivity liner-free barrier material for advanced Cu interconnects.

title: Biodegradable Monometallic Manganese Nanoparticles for Multimodal Tumor Therapy
summary: ABSTRACT Synergistic therapeutic nanoplatforms are of considerable interest in tumor therapy, but their translational potential is often limited by complex multicomponent designs and unknown in vivo degradation behavior. Herein, we show a d
content: ABSTRACT Synergistic therapeutic nanoplatforms are of considerable interest in tumor therapy, but their translational potential is often limited by complex multicomponent designs and unknown in vivo degradation behavior. Herein, we show a degradable, single‐component manganese nanoparticles (Mn NPs) using liquid‐phase exfoliation of commercial bulk manganese powder for cancer therapy. In the acidic tumor environment, Mn NPs react with H + to generate Mn 2+ and H 2 and raise the local pH. The released Mn 2+ drives Fenton‐like reactions to produce ROS, while H 2 causes mitochondrial damage, which together lead to tumor cell death. In addition, Mn 2+ activates cGAS‐STING signaling and initiates antitumor immunity. Moreover, Mn NPs inhibit tumor growth in CT26, 4T1, and B16F10 mouse models and show better effects than Mn 2+ alone. Transcriptomic analysis further reveals activation of multiple immune‐related signaling pathways following Mn NP treatment. In a bilateral tumor model, unilateral injection of Mn NPs triggers a systemic antitumor immune response, leading to effective inhibition of distant, untreated tumor growth. Collectively, this study identifies Mn NPs as a simple, biodegradable, single‐component nanoplatform that offers a promising new route for multimodal tumor therapy.

title: Improving Transparency in Guided Wave Testing: Aligning Long-Range Ultrasonic Inspection with Conventional UT Reporting Principles
summary: Guided Wave Testing (GWT) has become a widely used long-range ultrasonic screening technique for pipelines and industrial structures. The method enables inspection of tens of meters from a single probe location and is particularly useful fo
content: Guided Wave Testing (GWT) has become a widely used long-range ultrasonic screening technique for pipelines and industrial structures. The method enables inspection of tens of meters from a single probe location and is particularly useful for insulated, buried, or otherwise inaccessible piping systems. Despite its widespread adoption, a significant challenge in current GWT practice is the lack of transparency in inspection reporting. In many field applications, results are presented using highly compressed long- range plots, log-scaled amplitude displays, or Distance Amplitude Correction (DAC) curves without calibrated amplitude scales. These approaches often rely heavily on field interpretation and can obscure defect signals or limit the ability of inspectors to verify indications. Because guided wave testing is fundamentally an ultrasonic inspection method, reliable reporting requires three essential calibrations: distance calibration to accurately locate reflectors, amplitude calibration to express signal strength as reflection coefficient (%), and attenuation calibration to compensate for signal loss over distance. This paper discusses how these three calibrations form the technical foundation for transparent GWT reporting, proposes a methodology that aligns guided wave inspection with conventional ultrasonic testing principles, and demonstrates how Time-Corrected Gain (TCG) plots with calibrated amplitude axes significantly improve the reliability and credibility of guided wave inspection results.

title: Boosting Efficient Water Oxidation via Photothermal‐Enhanced High‐Entropy Oxides With Dual AEM and LOM Pathways
summary: ABSTRACT High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism
content: ABSTRACT High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. By combining theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations, we reveal that Fe doping optimally tailors the adsorption/desorption energetics of intermediates along the AEM, while simultaneously introducing oxygen vacancies that modulate the metal‐oxygen electronic environment and promote LOM participation. This dual‐pathway activation, enabled by the high‐entropy rock‐salt structure, enhances catalytic activity. In addition, the photothermal effect of (FeMgCoNiCuZn)O 1−x can accelerate interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and facilitate OOH * deprotonation. Under Xe‐lamp irradiation, Fe doping lowers the apparent activation energy for OER from 15.3 to 11.2 kJ mol −1 , and the catalyst achieves oxygen evolution current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm −2 at overpotentials of 159 and 247 mV. More importantly, it exhibits outstanding long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for over 1500 h at 1 A cm −2 . These findings underscore the potential of Fe‐doping hexanary HEOs as a highly efficient candidate for electrocatalytic water splitting.

title: Overview of the Belgian Corrosion Programme in the Framework of the Supercontainer Design for the Final Disposal of Vitrified High‐Level Radioactive Waste and Spent Fuel
summary: ABSTRACT In Belgium, deep geological disposal was proposed as the solution in principle by a Royal Decree in 2022. A societal debate in 2023–2024 broadly confirmed this option. A new Royal Decree is being prepared to define the staged proce
content: ABSTRACT In Belgium, deep geological disposal was proposed as the solution in principle by a Royal Decree in 2022. A societal debate in 2023–2024 broadly confirmed this option. A new Royal Decree is being prepared to define the staged process for siting and implementation. ONDRAF/NIRAS currently considers disposal in poorly indurated clay as the reference for its R&D programme. The supercontainer concept is being considered as reference design for disposing of vitrified high‐level waste and spent fuel. It establishes an engineered environment around a metallic overpack, ensuring favourable chemical conditions where corrosion remains slow and predictable, thus supporting long‐term safety no specific rock has been selected yet as host for geological disposal in Belgium; the repository design itself is still generic to a large extent. Moreover, future changes in cement formulations may also influence environmental conditions around the overpack. ONDRAF/NIRAS' programme currently aims at understanding the general trends related to the corrosion behaviour of carbon steel in different environments. The development of novel materials for the overpack are also monitored.

title: A Sustainable, Robust, Soft‐Gated Janus Bio‐Membrane for High‐Flux Aromatic Recovery From Saline Industrial Wastewaters
summary: ABSTRACT The selective recovery of aromatic pollutants from saline wastewater remains a central challenge in sustainable chemical engineering. We present a bio‐derived Janus membrane that couples a sorption‐active, mechanically robust wood
content: ABSTRACT The selective recovery of aromatic pollutants from saline wastewater remains a central challenge in sustainable chemical engineering. We present a bio‐derived Janus membrane that couples a sorption‐active, mechanically robust wood scaffold with an ultrathin polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) layer for soft‐gated aromatic transport. Spectroscopic, molecular, and free‐volume analyses support transient hydroxyl‐mediated phenol capture, favorable interfacial association, and onward diffusion through PDMS. The membrane achieves an overall phenol mass‐transfer coefficient of 36.9 × 10 −7 m s −1 and 99.4% salt rejection under ambient conditions, with sustained performance in petrochemical and offshore oilfield wastewaters. It combines a tensile strength of ∼70 MPa with consistent separation performance across a meter‐long sheet. Life‐cycle and national‐scale analyses indicate over 85% reductions in environmental impact and over 42 000 tons of CO 2 ‐equivalent mitigation annually. This work establishes a scalable bio‐derived membrane architecture that bridges molecular transport design with aromatic resource recovery, advancing the valorization of saline industrial wastewaters.

title: Strain Rate Triggered Network Locking in Shear‐Stiffening Gel/Wood Fibres Composites for Adaptive Impact Protection
summary: ABSTRACT Lightweight structural materials capable of simultaneously sustaining mechanical load‐bearing and dissipating extreme impact energy remain a long‐standing challenge, as conventional systems are constrained by the intrinsic trade‐of
content: ABSTRACT Lightweight structural materials capable of simultaneously sustaining mechanical load‐bearing and dissipating extreme impact energy remain a long‐standing challenge, as conventional systems are constrained by the intrinsic trade‐off between stiffness and toughness under dynamic loading. In this work, we address this limitation by introducing a strain rate triggered network locking strategy that enables adaptive mechanical reconfiguration in poplar fibres (PFs) and shear stiffening gel (SSG) composites (PSCs). PSCs are constructed by integrating PFs networks with SSG, forming a hierarchical interpenetrating architecture in which interfacial interactions and dynamic bonding jointly govern the mechanical response. Under low strain rate loading, PSCs enabled efficient stress distribution, achieving a flexural strength of 58.88 MPa with a balanced toughness. Under high strain rate loading, PSCs reached an energy absorption per unit thickness of 2.04 J·mm −1 and a force per unit thickness of 377.80 N·mm −1 . Notably, a steel projectile impacting at 153.4 m·s −1 rebounded, further demonstrating its potential as a scalable biobased adaptive impact‐resistant panel. This strain‐rate adaptive design principle provides a general pathway for structural materials, enabling them to simultaneously achieve static load‐bearing capacity and dynamic impact protection, and offers a scalable route for the development of biobased adaptive impact‐resistant panels.

title: Unlocked Covalent Competition in Asymmetric La/Sr‐O‐Fe Motif Activates Lattice Oxygen for Selective Methane Oxidation
summary: ABSTRACT Controlling lattice‐oxygen reactivity in transition‐metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars‐van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM 1 ‐O‐TM 2 bridges suffer from covalent competition between adja
content: ABSTRACT Controlling lattice‐oxygen reactivity in transition‐metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars‐van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM 1 ‐O‐TM 2 bridges suffer from covalent competition between adjacent redox‐active cations, which generates site heterogeneity and degrades selectivity. Herein, taking Ruddlesden–Popper LaSrFeO 4 (A 2 BO 4 ) as a model, we demonstrate that constructing asymmetric A‐O‐B motifs (i.e., La‐O‐Fe and Sr‐O‐Fe) provides a distinct route to overcome this limitation. Combined experiments and DFT calculations reveal that the A‐O‐B configuration could convert redox‐inert A‐site cations into direct electronic contributors to oxygen, which unlocks the covalent competition, substantially enabling promoted electron density over oxygen and enhanced Fe─O bond covalency. Consequently, LaSrFeO 4 displays much lower methane activation barrier (∼1.24 eV) than its perovskite counterpart, LaFeO 3, with an Fe‐O‐Fe motif (1.90 eV), ultimately affording a 2.35‐fold increase in syngas yield with 97% selectivity. This discovery reveals that asymmetric A‐O‐B coordination may serve as a promising structural strategy, distinct from B‐O‐B modulation, for modulating the electronic properties and reactivity of lattice oxygen.

title: Mimetic tissue models for accurate lipid quantitation in fibrotic mouse heart by MALDI-MSI
summary: Accurate spatial quantitation of endogenous biomolecules is paramount to rationalize disease progression in tissues and translate findings into clinical use. In this contribution, we present a streamlined and quality-controlled spatial quan
content: Accurate spatial quantitation of endogenous biomolecules is paramount to rationalize disease progression in tissues and translate findings into clinical use. In this contribution, we present a streamlined and quality-controlled spatial quantitation pipeline for accurate quantitative mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) of lipids. By creating miniaturized mimetic tissue models (MTM) spiked with stable isotope labelled standards (SILS) matching the tissue used for MSI, calibration and MSI experiments are performed from the same sample slide minimizing measurement variabilities. By determining the absolute SILS concentrations and lipid annotations via LC-MS/MS in the same MTMs as used for MSI, measurements are intrinsically quality controlled and quantitation results via MSI can be reported in units of µglipid/mgprotein commonly employed in lipidomics. We present an in-depth comparison of spatial quantitation via MSI and bulk LC-MS/MS for the same samples, i.e. mouse heart tissue, yielding good overall agreement between both quantification modalities for 95 endogenous lipids. Furthermore, we demonstrate the capability to capture heterogenous lipid expressions during disease progression quantitatively by charting lipidomic changes upon myocardial infarction-induced tissue remodeling. Our workflow reports absolute spatial quantitation results for 10 lipid classes and identifies 19 regulated lipids that are in line with known cellular remodeling events in fibrotic heart tissue.

title: Oxygen‐Controlled Structural and Defect Engineering of Magnetron‐Sputtered ZnO Thin Films for Photosensing
summary: ABSTRACT Zinc oxide (ZnO) thin films with a wurtzite structure were deposited by direct current magnetron sputtering under controlled O 2 :Ar ratios and nominal oxygen partial pressures to investigate the influence of oxygen‐controlled defe
content: ABSTRACT Zinc oxide (ZnO) thin films with a wurtzite structure were deposited by direct current magnetron sputtering under controlled O 2 :Ar ratios and nominal oxygen partial pressures to investigate the influence of oxygen‐controlled defect evolution, particularly involving oxygen vacancies (V o ) and zinc interstitials (Zn i ), on structural and ultraviolet photosensing properties. ZnO‐based UV photodetectors remain limited by the complex interplay between surface charge transfer and bulk carrier recombination. Increasing oxygen availability modifies the defect landscape and promotes preferential c‐axis orientation, reduced grain size (∼130 to ∼90 nm), decreased film thickness (∼445 to ∼105 nm), and enhanced E 2 (high) Raman characteristics. Photoluminescence measurements further indicate stronger near‐band‐edge emission and reduced defect‐assisted non‐radiative recombination in the oxygen‐rich film. The film deposited at the highest investigated O 2 :Ar ratio (3:2) exhibits the best overall photoresponse, associated with improved preferential c‐axis orientation, reduced defect‐assisted recombination, and the continued contribution of surface oxygen adsorption–desorption processes. This results in an enhanced ultraviolet photoresponse with ON/OFF ratio of ∼1.33, sensitivity of ∼97.65%, responsivity of ∼6.64 A/W, detectivity of , and external quantum efficiency (EQE) of ∼2243%. These findings demonstrate that oxygen‐controlled growth effectively tunes the structural, defect‐related, and surface charge‐transfer processes governing ultraviolet photosensing in ZnO thin films.

title: Dual‐Pronged Strategy for Practical H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis: Cross‐Scale Engineering of Nanocarbon Catalysts
summary: ABSTRACT Both the atomic‐/molecular‐scale active sites and the mesoscopic mass transfer properties jointly govern the overall performance of catalytic materials. In this work, we propose a dual‐pronged strategy that integrates heteroatom do
content: ABSTRACT Both the atomic‐/molecular‐scale active sites and the mesoscopic mass transfer properties jointly govern the overall performance of catalytic materials. In this work, we propose a dual‐pronged strategy that integrates heteroatom doping with micro/nano‐scale structural design, thereby optimizing surface carbonaceous active sites and mesoscale mass transport, ultimately enabling the development of a mesoporous carbon‐based catalyst for practical electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis. Impressively, the optimized nanocatalyst exhibits high electrocatalytic activity and selectivity (> 95% at pH 13 and > 90% at pH 7) toward H 2 O 2 , facilitating the production of H 2 O 2 solution at industrial‐related current densities in flow‐cell systems and making it suitable for applications such as pulp bleaching and medical‐grade disinfection. Mechanistically, we propose that sulfur heteroatoms modulate the binding energy of *OOH intermediates on the carbonaceous surface, thereby enhancing H 2 O 2 formation; besides, the mesoscopic geometric structure with a hollow interior and mesoporous channels ensures sufficient O 2 supply and a hydrated environment, supporting mass transfer‐enhanced H 2 O 2 generation. The dual‐pronged strategy presented here offers a new framework for designing catalytic platforms aimed at cross‐scale process intensification in the electrocatalytic small molecule conversion.

title: Enhancing Rate Capability and Cycle Life of TiNb2O7 Anodes: The Synergistic Role of Compositing with Carbon Nanofibers and SDS Morphological Tuning
summary: TiNb 2 O 7 (TNO) has attracted considerable attention as a promising anode candidate for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) due to its favorable properties, including high theoretical capacity, moderate operating voltage, and multi-electron redox
content: TiNb 2 O 7 (TNO) has attracted considerable attention as a promising anode candidate for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) due to its favorable properties, including high theoretical capacity, moderate operating voltage, and multi-electron redox capability, but its poor intrinsic electronic and ionic conductivity limits its practical use. This study presents a dual-modification strategy that combines carbon nanofiber (CNF) compositing with sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS)-assisted morphological regulation through a one-pot solvothermal synthesis. In addition, the influence of SDS concentration on the morphology of TNO/CNF composites is systematically investigated to identify the optimum composite architecture. Varying SDS concentrations (2×, 10×, and 20× the CNF amount) revealed the 10× ratio as optimal, yielding a well-connected CNF scaffold uniformly decorated with fine TNO nanoparticles, minimizing agglomeration and facilitating electron/ion transport. This composite delivered an initial discharge capacity of 290 mAh/g at 1C, retaining 61% after 200 cycles—outperforming pristine TNO (225 mAh/g) and SDS-free TNO-CNF (272 mAh/g). It also maintained ∼85 mAh/g at 20C, attributed to the synergistic CNF network and SDS-mediation effects. Finally, ternary composites incorporating reduced graphene oxide (rGO) were synthesized using the same procedure. SDS significantly improved morphological homogeneity, creating well-integrated TNO/CNF/rGO networks with uniform nanoparticles distribution across the conductive scaffold. These ternary SDS-modified nanocomposites showed superior high-rate performance at 10–20C. However, they exhibited reduced low-rate capacities and cycling stability (from 255 to 141 mAh/g at 1C over 200 cycles) due to rGO's tortuous pathways that impede bulk Li⁺ diffusion.

title: Re(I)‐Based Molecular Actuator‐Equipped Nanomotors for Integrated Photodynamic and Photomechanical Therapy of Solid Tumor
summary: The dense stromal barrier of solid tumors severely hinders intratumoral distribution and therapeutic performance of conventional nanomedicines, and such limitation further compromises oxygen-dependent photodynamic therapy. Herein, through m
content: The dense stromal barrier of solid tumors severely hinders intratumoral distribution and therapeutic performance of conventional nanomedicines, and such limitation further compromises oxygen-dependent photodynamic therapy. Herein, through molecular engineering, we develop a Janus nanomotor (Re1@NMs) that integrates a three-dimensional rhenium(I)-based molecular actuator (Re1) with glucose oxidase (GOx)-powered propulsion. Owing to the Janus structure, asymmetric GOx-catalyzed glucose consumption generates local chemical gradients that fuel autonomous motility, thereby enhancing intratumoral distribution. Upon light activation, the engineered Re1, screened from six Re(I) complexes, functions both as a dual Type I/II photosensitizer generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) to induce oxidative stress and as a molecular actuator whose Y-axis motif undergoes E/Z photoisomerization and torsional deformation, thereby contributing to membrane permeabilization. The resulting integrated mechano-photodynamic action coordinately activates ferroptosis and pyroptosis. In a murine tumor model, Re1@NMs-mediated phototherapy achieves superior tumor suppression with excellent biosafety and further elicits robust antitumor immunity, as evidenced by enhanced dendritic cell maturation, increased tumor-infiltrating T cells, elevated effector cytokine expression, and damage-associated molecular pattern release. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first integration of a deliberately engineered metal-complex-based three-dimensional molecular actuator with a tumor-microenvironment-adaptive nanomotor, establishing a new paradigm for overcoming tumor barriers.

title: The SlHYL1 ‐ SlRBP1 module integrates gibberellin metabolism to promote plant height in tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum )
summary: SUMMARY Plant height is an essential agronomic trait that significantly influences crop yield and quality. The HYPONASTIC LEAVES 1 (HYL1), a core component of microRNA biogenesis, remains poorly understood in terms of its regulatory mechani
content: SUMMARY Plant height is an essential agronomic trait that significantly influences crop yield and quality. The HYPONASTIC LEAVES 1 (HYL1), a core component of microRNA biogenesis, remains poorly understood in terms of its regulatory mechanisms on agronomic traits in tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum , Sl). In this study, we demonstrated that CRISPR/Cas9‐mediated knockout of SlHYL1 caused dwarfism, and partial suppression of SlHYL1 in tomato cultivar “Ailsa Craig” (AC) via RNA interference (RNAi) increased internode number but reduced internode length, resulting in a semi‐dwarf phenotype, confirming the role of SlHYL1 in regulating plant height. Cytological analysis showed that SlHYL1 suppression decreased both cell number and size within internodes. Yeast two‐hybrid screening identified that SlHYL1 interacted with another tomato RNA‐binding protein 1 (SlRBP1). Knockdown of SlRBP1 resembled the SlHYL1‐RNAi semi‐dwarf phenotype. Further studies revealed that the SlHYL1‐SlRBP1 module additively promotes the expression of gibberellin (GA) biosynthetic genes, thereby facilitating GA accumulation. Additionally, the dwarf phenotypes of both SlHYL1‐RNAi and SlRBP1‐RNAi plants were partially rescued by exogenous GA 3 application. Notably, unlike SlHYL1, SlRBP1 did not affect the biogenesis of most miRNAs. In summary, our findings demonstrate that the SlHYL1‐SlRBP1 module regulates tomato plant height by enhancing GA accumulation.

title: Opposite Effects of Removing Ethylene Carbonate from the Electrolyte on Ni-Rich Layered Oxide and Mn-Rich Olivine Phosphate Cathodes
summary: Ethylene carbonate (EC)-free electrolytes are promising for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, their benefits have been demonstrated primarily for layered oxide cathodes, while their effects on olivine phosphates remain unclear. H
content: Ethylene carbonate (EC)-free electrolytes are promising for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, their benefits have been demonstrated primarily for layered oxide cathodes, while their effects on olivine phosphates remain unclear. Here, we show that EC removal accelerates the degradation of LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 (LMFP64), in contrast to LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811). Experiments and first-principles calculations suggest that these opposite responses reflect distinct degradation pathways associated with transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) covalency. On NCM811, strongly hybridized O 2 p states near the Fermi level favor EC dehydrogenation, initiating degradation; EC removal eliminates this pathway. In contrast, olivine models exhibit weaker TM 3d–O 2 p hybridization, more ionic TM–O bonding, and stronger PF 6 − adsorption at TM sites. Without EC, experiments on LMFP64 reveal salt decomposition before cycling and accelerated degradation; EC otherwise limits anion access to TM sites. These findings show that the effect of EC removal is cathode-dependent and can be rationalized by TM–O covalency.

title: Water-free dyeing of polypropylene fabrics in supercritical CO2 with functional dispersants for eco-friendly textile applications
summary: Owing to rising environmental awareness, the textile dyeing and finishing industry faces increasing pressure to reduce water consumption and chemical wastewater generation of conventional aqueous dyeing processes. Supercritical carbon dioxi
content: Owing to rising environmental awareness, the textile dyeing and finishing industry faces increasing pressure to reduce water consumption and chemical wastewater generation of conventional aqueous dyeing processes. Supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO₂) dyeing, a water-free dyeing method, conserves water resources and prevents water pollution. Polypropylene (PP) fabrics are promising eco-friendly textile materials owing to their simple structure, low carbon emissions, and less weight. High crystallinity and lack of polar functional groups in their molecular structure makes them difficult to dye. PP fibers are commonly colored via mass pigmentation. However, limited flexibility in masterbatch formulations restricts color mixing and shade modification. In this study, a series of styrene–maleic anhydride (SMA) copolymers grafted with long-chain alkyl amines were synthesized and used as dispersing agents in scCO₂ dyeing systems to enhance the disperse dye uptake of PP fibers. When applied to a disperse yellow dye (JY) and blue dye (JB), the SMA dispersants significantly improved dyeing performance under scCO₂ conditions. For a JY with an SMA dispersant, the Kubelka–Munk function (K/S) value increased by approximately 27.7%, whereas levelness (ΔE*) decreased by 47.1%. For a JB with an SMA dispersant, the K/S value increased by 39.7%, and ΔE* decreased by 42.6%. In a mixed-dye system, the SMA dispersant addition resulted in a 39.5% increase in K/S and 20.5% reduction in ΔE*. This study demonstrates the feasibility of using SMA–alkylamine polymeric dispersants to improve the dyeing performance and surface hydrophobicity of PP fabrics under water-free scCO₂ dyeing conditions without the use of fluorinated additives.

title: Trees rely on both root‐based ‘do‐it‐yourself’ and mycorrhizal‐based ‘outsourcing’ adaptations to shifting soil nutrient availability during forest stand development
summary: Abstract Soil nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) availability generally decrease with forest stand development, yet how tree species acclimate to this decline remains largely unclear. The functional coordination hypothesis proposes that trees
content: Abstract Soil nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) availability generally decrease with forest stand development, yet how tree species acclimate to this decline remains largely unclear. The functional coordination hypothesis proposes that trees concurrently improve leaf nutrient recycling and root nutrient acquisition to cope with nutrient deficiency. Conversely, the resource limitation hypothesis posits that trees prioritize either strategy, as simultaneous employment of both strategies is resource costly. To test these conflicting hypotheses, we leveraged a chronosequence of Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica stands with six age classes ranging from 16‐ to 62‐year‐old. We measured a comprehensive set of 70 plant and soil variables including needle nutrient retranslocation and resorption, and root architectural, morphological, physiological and mycorrhizal traits to assess the response of needle nutrient recycling and root nutrient acquisition to changes in stand nutrient status. Stand development reduced soil N and P availability and caused a shift from N to P limitation as evidenced by increasing needle N:P ratios and decreasing N:P‐acquisition enzyme ratios. There was no evidence of N or P retranslocation from old to young needles, and nutrient resorption efficiency was independent of soil nutrient availability, indicating that adjustments of needle nutrient recycling contribute little to mitigating nutrient deficiency. Root length density decreased exponentially with stand development, whereas cord‐forming ectomycorrhizal fungi (EMF), root phosphatase activity and rhizosphere effects on plant‐available soil P logarithmically increased, implying a shift from root nutrient scavenging to combined EMF nutrient scavenging and root P mining. Synthesis . Our findings suggest that tree species do not necessarily rely on both improved recycling and acquisition to acclimate to soil nutrient scarcity with stand development. However, trees can simultaneously depend on physiological adaptations of absorptive fine roots themselves, as well as on a constrained selection of EMF. This reveals that complex sets of adaptations, both root‐based ‘do‐it‐yourself’ and mycorrhizal‐based ‘outsourcing’, can be effectively used by trees to cope with changes in soil nutrient availability.

title: Plant species' distribution patterns, functional traits, and range shifts along an elevation gradient
summary: Knowledge about species' distributions is essential for understanding biodiversity patterns and predicting responses to climate change. The shapes of species' density distributions reflect how their performance varies across their range – s
content: Knowledge about species' distributions is essential for understanding biodiversity patterns and predicting responses to climate change. The shapes of species' density distributions reflect how their performance varies across their range – shaped by environment, biotic interactions, and dispersal. Because these distributions reflect emergent properties of populations, they may reveal deterministic processes underlying species' past and future ranges and range shifts. Yet, distribution shape parameters (DSPs) are rarely considered in this context, leaving their potential largely unexplored. We addressed this gap by asking: 1) How do DSPs vary and covary among mountain plant species? 2) How are DSPs related to plant functional traits? 3) Can DSPs and functional traits explain recent range shifts? We quantified DSPs for 283 species across 626 plots spanning a 2000‐m elevation gradient on the Calanda massif, Graubünden, Switzerland, extracted functional traits from the TRY database, and compared DSPs and functional traits to range‐shift rates from two complementary data sources. We found that observed range shapes formed a subset of all possible shapes, suggesting trade‐offs in the drivers of distribution shapes. For example, we found that species abundant at higher elevations had shorter upslope and longer downslope distribution tails, consistent with abiotic stress limitation. Range limits and optima were also correlated with functional traits and distribution skew with species' dispersal distance. Finally, both distribution shapes and functional traits correlated with ongoing range shifts – DSPs outperformed functional traits, but considering both provided greater explanatory power. Overall, our results demonstrate that DSPs offer promising directions for future research into the factors influencing range shifts and our ability to predict them. Specifically, the drivers of DSPs and the relevant temporal scales over which they operate should be explored, potentially providing further insights into species' range shifts.

title: Metabolomic and Transcriptomic Characterization of Actinokineospora bangkokensis 44EHWT: Enhancing Anti-anthracnose Production Through N-Acetylglucosamine Supplementation
summary: N -acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) serves as a key carbon source and regulatory signal for secondary metabolism in actinomycetes, yet its role in Actinokineospora remains poorly understood. Here, genome mining, transcriptomics, and untargeted me
content: N -acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) serves as a key carbon source and regulatory signal for secondary metabolism in actinomycetes, yet its role in Actinokineospora remains poorly understood. Here, genome mining, transcriptomics, and untargeted metabolomics were integrated to investigate GlcNAc-supplemented Actinokineospora bangkokensis 44EHWT. Genome mining revealed 35 biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) and multiple GntR-family regulators. Untargeted metabolomics identified 2,705 features, with 493 uniquely induced by GlcNAc. Molecular networking showed significant enrichment of cyclic peptides and polyketides, including a significant increase in the relative abundance of thailandin B (fold change = 2.004, p adj = 0.00012861). In contrast, thailandin A showed only a modest and statistically non-significant change in relative abundance (fold change = 1.105, p adj = 0.390). The GlcNAc-supplemented crude extract showed a 25.92% increase in production yield compared with ISP2 alone and exhibited the largest inhibition zone against Colletotrichum gloeosporioides DoA c1060 (22.31 ± 0.50 mm), followed by C. gloeosporioides DoA c2434 (20.42 ± 0.54 mm) and Fusarium oxysporum DoA c0761 (17.06 ± 0.08 mm). Transcriptomics revealed 2,577 differentially expressed genes, though BGC regulation was heterogeneous. Notably, the Thailandin BGC was transcriptionally downregulated at Day 5 despite increased metabolite accumulation, indicating temporal offsets likely supported by precursor supply. Overall, GlcNAc acts as a context-dependent modulator that selectively triggers specific bioactive pathways rather than globally activating all BGCs. This study highlights the power of multi-omics to expand chemical diversity and harness the natural product potential of Actinokineospora .

title: Gastroprotective effects of Sapodilla fruit powder against ethanol‐induced gastric injury in Sprague–Dawley rats: In silico prediction and in vivo validation
summary: Abstract Background Gastrointestinal disorders are rapidly increasing worldwide due to the disturbance of mucosal defenses. Manilkara zapota possesses significant therapeutic attributes to improve individual well‐being. Objectives The curre
content: Abstract Background Gastrointestinal disorders are rapidly increasing worldwide due to the disturbance of mucosal defenses. Manilkara zapota possesses significant therapeutic attributes to improve individual well‐being. Objectives The current study was conducted to evaluate the antioxidant activity, phytochemical characterization, and in silico and in vivo gastroprotective potential of Manilkara zapota fruit powder (MZFP) in ethanol‐induced gastric injury in Sprague–Dawley rats. Methodology Antioxidant activity and phytochemical profiling of MZFP were investigated via DPPH and FRAP assays, alongside TPC and FTIR analysis. The in silico study was carried out via molecular docking and Discovery Studio Visualizer. Furthermore, efficacy was determined by procuring Sprague–Dawley rats, which were administered ethanol (5 mg/kg body weight) to induce peptic ulcer. Rats were sacrificed after 28 days, and blood and serum were collected for hematological and serological examination. Results The methanolic extract has the highest antioxidant potential due to the maximum TPC (116.63 ± 2.47 mgGAE/100 g). The FTIR analysis revealed the presence of aliphatic C–H and ester/aldehyde C=O groups, demonstrating phenolics, flavonoids, and carbohydrate moieties. The in silico study predicted the gastroprotective potential of MZFP, with apigenin demonstrating maximum activity, i.e., the binding affinity of −7.4 kcal/mol. Furthermore, the gastroprotective activity was validated by in vivo rodent modeling. The findings indicated that all the markers were negatively influenced in T1, which were improved in T4. The histopathological examination also confirmed the potential of MZFP in attenuating the progression of PUD. Conclusion In a nutshell, these findings revealed that MZFP (500 mg/kg BW) has a significantly higher protective effect against ethanol‐induced gastric injury.

title: Dopant‐Enhanced Inhibitory Negative Photoconductance and Hetero‐interfacial Switchable Synaptic Response in CsPbI 3 Perovskite
summary: ABSTRACT All‐inorganic halide perovskites, particularly CsPbI 3 , are excellent candidates for neuromorphic devices owing to their unique defect‐tolerant electronic structure and mixed ionic‐electronic transport. Here, we demonstrate that t
content: ABSTRACT All‐inorganic halide perovskites, particularly CsPbI 3 , are excellent candidates for neuromorphic devices owing to their unique defect‐tolerant electronic structure and mixed ionic‐electronic transport. Here, we demonstrate that the inherent synaptic plasticity of CsPbI 3 can be modulated by cationic doping and heterojunction engineering. By introducing transition metal dopants (Cu, Mn and Zn) into the perovskite lattice, we modify the trap‐state density and charge‐carrier dynamics. CsPbI 3 naturally exhibits negative photoconductance (NPC) due to its defect‐mediated charge dynamics and Mn‐doping increases this effect manifold. First‐principles calculations reveal that Mn‐substitution creates highly localized states within the bandgap, significantly amplifying light‐activated charge trapping kinetics. This manifests as a robust negative photoconductance, enhancing biomimetic inhibitory responses with a high paired‐pulse depression index of 188%. Also, we show that the polarity of the optical synaptic response is not merely a bulk property but can be inverted via interfacial charge‐transfer at the CsPbI 3 /ZnO heterostructure. This transition from inhibitory to excitatory behavior underscores the role of material interfaces in controlling synaptic polarity. These findings establish a materials‐based strategy for developing CMOS‐compatible, dual‐mode neuromorphic architectures on monolithic substrates.

title: Detection of Tiludronic Acid in Equine Hair and Its Segmental Analysis Following Administration
summary: A method for the detection of tiludronic acid in equine hair was developed and applied to investigate its distribution in hair following administration of Tildren®. Hair samples collected from seven horses at 2-7 months post-administration
content: A method for the detection of tiludronic acid in equine hair was developed and applied to investigate its distribution in hair following administration of Tildren®. Hair samples collected from seven horses at 2-7 months post-administration were analysed using ultra-performance liquid chromatography tandem high-resolution mass spectrometry (UPLC–MS/HRMS). The method achieved an estimated limit of detection of 0.1 pg/mg. Tiludronic acid was detected in all hair samples collected following administration. Segmental analysis revealed non-uniform distribution along the hair shaft, with the highest concentrations observed in discrete segments corresponding to the time of drug exposure. The position of the concentration peak shifted towards distal end with increasing post-administration time according to the normal hair growth rate. These findings demonstrate the incorporation of tiludronic acid into equine hair via systemic circulation and suggest that segmental hair analysis may provide information regarding the timing of bisphosphonate exposure in horses.

title: Strontium cations guarding chabazite zeolite windows for selective deuterium recovery
summary: Abstract Deuterium is indispensable for nuclear fusion and isotopic labeling; however, the separation of high‐purity deuterium from hydrogen isotope mixtures (D 2 /H 2 ) remains challenging due to their nearly identical physicochemical prop
content: Abstract Deuterium is indispensable for nuclear fusion and isotopic labeling; however, the separation of high‐purity deuterium from hydrogen isotope mixtures (D 2 /H 2 ) remains challenging due to their nearly identical physicochemical properties. Herein, we report a strontium‐cation‐guarded chabazite (CHA) zeolite that exhibits a combined effect of favorable diffusion kinetics and tailored equilibrium adsorption for the quantum sieving of D 2 /H 2 . Strontium cations positioned at 8‐membered ring windows facilitate preferential D 2 diffusion and enrichment during adsorption, while simultaneously enabling rapid H 2 release during desorption. This decoupling of adsorption–desorption dynamics results in exceptional D 2 /H 2 performance. At 40 K, the optimal adsorbent achieves a dynamic D 2 /H 2 selectivity of 3.10 and a D 2 capacity of 6.60 mmol g −1 . Breakthrough tests followed by a two‐stage desorption process (direct purging and subsequent heating) yielded D 2 recoveries of 52.7% and 47.3%, with corresponding purities of 73.3% and 98.9%, respectively.

title: Probing the dimensionality of confinement in soft nanoreactors through plasmonic nanoparticles nucleation
summary: Soft nanoscale confinement fundamentally alters the thermodynamic and kinetic landscape of chemical reactions, yet a predictive understanding of how nanoreactor geometry dictates reactivity remains elusive. In this work, we demonstrate that
content: Soft nanoscale confinement fundamentally alters the thermodynamic and kinetic landscape of chemical reactions, yet a predictive understanding of how nanoreactor geometry dictates reactivity remains elusive. In this work, we demonstrate that the dimensionality of soft confinement governs the onset of nanomaterial formation. By systematically tuning the water-to-surfactant molar ratio () in self-assembled lecithin reverse micelles, we decoupled the geometry of the host template from its chemical composition. We utilized the in situ nucleation of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) as an active optical and structural probe across isotropic, anisotropic, and bulk-like spatial domains. Correlating UV-Vis spectroscopy with small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) analyses, we reveal that confinement dimensionality acts as an ON/OFF switch for the reduction of gold ions. Under extreme isotropic confinement (), where the interfacial water network is severely restricted, AuNP formation is suppressed for at least 30 days. Conversely, a hydration-induced structural transition toward anisotropic, wormlike domains () coincides with the onset of AuNP nucleation and yields the highest reaction extent. Finally, further expansion into bulk-like regimes () dilutes the gold precursor within the aqueous domains, attenuating the reaction yield. We rationalize these trends within a phenomenological framework based on classical nucleation theory, highlighting confinement dimensionality as a design parameter for soft nanoreactors and tailored plasmonic nanomaterials.

title: Servitization in the Era of Digitalisation and Circular Economy: A Four‐Decade Bibliometric Investigation (1988–2025)
summary: ABSTRACT The study maps and synthesises the intellectual, conceptual and social structure of product–service Systems (PSS) and Servitization research spanning from 1988 to 2025. For a bibliometric review of 1492 Scopus–indexed documents, we
content: ABSTRACT The study maps and synthesises the intellectual, conceptual and social structure of product–service Systems (PSS) and Servitization research spanning from 1988 to 2025. For a bibliometric review of 1492 Scopus–indexed documents, we use the R‐bibliometrix package and VOSviewer to conduct bibliographic coupling, co‐word citation, co‐authorship and thematic evolution analyses. The findings reveal a rapidly amalgamating research field with PSS and Servitization at its conceptual core. Scholarly attention has fundamentally shifted from manufacturing and operational efficiency to digital enablement, sustainability, and circular economy‐driven business models. By providing a holistic, 37‐year mapping of this study, this study recognises critical thematic clusters and proposes a forward‐looking research agenda to advance the theory, practice and policy.

title: Interfacial charge‐regulated peroxide pathway enables visible‐light‐driven oxidative coupling of methane to ethane
summary: Abstract Controlling oxygen activation while suppressing overoxidation remains a central challenge in photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) under mild conditions. Herein, we report an interfacial charge‐regulated strategy for s
content: Abstract Controlling oxygen activation while suppressing overoxidation remains a central challenge in photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) under mild conditions. Herein, we report an interfacial charge‐regulated strategy for selective visible‐light‐driven methane coupling to ethane over an In 2 O 3 ‐synergized Au/TiO 2−x photocatalyst. The introduction of In 2 O 3 establishes a built‐in electric field at the In 2 O 3 /Au/TiO 2−x heterointerface, enhancing charge separation and driving directional photogenerated electron migration along the pathway of In 2 O 3 → TiO 2−x → Au and resulting in electron‐enriched Au sites under irradiation. These sites fundamentally alter the oxygen activation pathway by promoting the formation of mild peroxide species (O 2 2− ) while suppressing highly oxidative oxygen species. The resulting O 2 2− species activate CH 4 to form *CH 3 intermediates, which undergo selective C–C coupling on Au. As a result, the catalyst achieves an ethane formation rate of 304.6 ± 7.6 μmol·g −1 ·h −1 with 99.4% selectivity under visible‐light irradiation. The rate increases to 32.9 ± 0.5 mmol·g −1 ·h −1 under full‐spectrum irradiation.

title: Applications of Active Infrared Thermography Methods in Civil Engineering : Reinforced Concrete and CFRP
summary: The accessibility of active infrared thermography methods depends on the heating sources. The paper presents the application of three active infrared thermography methods in civil engineering. The first method with a Laser system was applie
content: The accessibility of active infrared thermography methods depends on the heating sources. The paper presents the application of three active infrared thermography methods in civil engineering. The first method with a Laser system was applied to detecting the absence of adhesive in CFRP which is commonly used for strengthening different structures (such as columns, beams, slabs). The second method with halogen lamps was also applied to detect the defect in CFRP. The last method with microwave heating source (frequency of 2.45 GHz) was applied to detect reinforcement bars in a reinforced concrete wall, and to detect the defect in CFRP. The results showed the efficiency of the active thermography methods for civil engineering structures. More particularly, the microwave thermography was also used to study the durablity (defects with aging) of the CFRP.

title: Reactivity of a Pacman Chlorophosphane Toward Ammonia and Azide: Formation and Characterization of a Diamino‐ and a Diazidophosphane
source: Zeitschrift für anorganische und allgemeine Chemie
summary: The halide substitution reactions of the Pacman chlorophosphane Pac(PCl) 2 with NH 3 and AgN 3 provide straightforward access to the corresponding diamine Pac(PNH 2 ) 2 and diazide Pac(PN 3 ) 2 , respectively, both of which were isolated in
content: The halide substitution reactions of the Pacman chlorophosphane Pac(PCl) 2 with NH 3 and AgN 3 provide straightforward access to the corresponding diamine Pac(PNH 2 ) 2 and diazide Pac(PN 3 ) 2 , respectively, both of which were isolated in good yields. Multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, including 1 H, 31 P, and two‐dimensional 1 H– 31 P/ 1 H– 15 N HMBC experiments, revealed that both compounds exist as mixtures of endo–exo and exo–exo isomers in solution and enabled their unambiguous structural assignment. Density functional theory reproduces the experimentally observed structural features and identifies pronounced differences in intramolecular donor–acceptor interactions between the endo and exo hemispheres of the Pacman framework. Although donor–acceptor interactions are significantly weaker within the sterically confined Pacman cavity, the endo–exo isomers are predicted to be thermodynamically favored for both derivatives. The combined experimental and computational investigations provide a detailed understanding of the structural and electronic properties of these new phosphorus‐amino and phosphorus‐azido Pacman compounds and establish a basis for their future application as versatile precursors in main‐group chemistry.

title: Ambient Pressure Drying of Aerogels for Structure Preservation and Multifunctional Applications
summary: Ambient-pressure drying (APD) is attractive for scalable aerogel manufacturing because it avoids the pressure vessels used in supercritical drying and the low-temperature vacuum equipment required for freeze-drying. Its principal limitation
content: Ambient-pressure drying (APD) is attractive for scalable aerogel manufacturing because it avoids the pressure vessels used in supercritical drying and the low-temperature vacuum equipment required for freeze-drying. Its principal limitation is the liquid-gas meniscus generated during evaporation, which couples solvent surface tension, wetting, pore size, drying rate, and skeleton strength to shrinkage and cracking. This review establishes a process-structure-property framework for APD-derived aerogels. After defining the scope of APD and distinguishing it from the broader category of subcritical drying, we quantitatively analyze capillary pressure using the Young-Laplace relationship and discuss the absence of a universal critical contact angle or pore size. Physical, chemical, and hybrid crosslinking are compared in terms of synergistic reinforcement and possible competition caused by densification, brittleness, or blocked mass transport. The structural outcomes of APD are benchmarked against supercritical and freeze-drying, with emphasis on density, porosity, specific surface area, shrinkage, and mechanical integrity. Application sections then connect pore architecture and interfacial chemistry to thermal insulation, adsorption, energy storage, electromagnetic shielding, acoustics, and biomedical functions. Finally, environmental fate, solvent safety, reporting standards, and continuous manufacturing are identified as priorities for translating APD aerogels from laboratory demonstrations to reproducible products.

title: Sonication‐assisted green extraction and functional characterization of dietary fiber from a novel PD2LV65 oat ( Avena sativa L.) cultivar
summary: Abstract This study explored the oat cultivar PD 2 LV 65 as a native source of dietary fiber (DF) and optimized its extraction using response surface methodology. A three‐factor three‐level design assessed the impact of time (10, 20, and 30
content: Abstract This study explored the oat cultivar PD 2 LV 65 as a native source of dietary fiber (DF) and optimized its extraction using response surface methodology. A three‐factor three‐level design assessed the impact of time (10, 20, and 30 min), temperature (20°C, 30°C, and 40°C), and amplitude (60%, 70%, and 80%) on the extraction efficacy. It was observed that time and temperature significantly ( p ≤ 0.0001) influenced DF yield, whereas amplitude had a minor effect ( p ≤ 0.05). Infrared spectroscopy confirmed the presence of soluble, insoluble, and total DF fractions. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed lack of crystallization or melting phases which indicates purity, whereas X‐ray diffraction showed patterns between 15° and 25°. Sonication enhanced extraction efficiency, surface area, and pore size, thereby caused an increase in DF’s bioactivity as an absorbent. Overall, sonication proved to be a green and economical technology, improving both yield and functional properties, positioning PD 2 LV 65 DF as a promising nutraceutical ingredient.

title: Complementary Rejuvenation of Aged Asphalt by Waste Cooking Oil and Waste Wood Pyrolysis Oil: Experimental Characterization and Molecular Dynamics Insights
summary: To address the difficulty of simultaneously restoring the molecular mobility and structural stability of aged asphalt using a single bio-oil rejuvenator, a dual-source bio-oil composite rejuvenation system consisting of waste cooking oil (W
content: To address the difficulty of simultaneously restoring the molecular mobility and structural stability of aged asphalt using a single bio-oil rejuvenator, a dual-source bio-oil composite rejuvenation system consisting of waste cooking oil (WCO) and waste wood pyrolysis oil (WWO) was developed based on the concept of component-specific functional division. According to their compositional characteristics, WCO primarily serves to replenish light fractions and restore molecular mobility, whereas WWO is used to enhance the regulation of interactions among polar components and asphaltene aggregation behavior. Compositional and microstructural characterization, rheological testing, and molecular dynamics simulations were employed to investigate the rejuvenation effectiveness and molecular interaction characteristics of the different rejuvenation systems. The results showed that, compared with aged asphalt, the composite-rejuvenated asphalt exhibited a 33.92% increase in aromatic content, a 32.20% decrease in asphaltene content, and a 22.50% increase in the colloidal stability index, together with fewer surface cracks and improved morphological continuity. The composite system reduced the stiffness of aged asphalt, enhanced its low-temperature stress relaxation capacity, and maintained favorable resistance to permanent deformation at high temperatures. Its creep stiffness at −12, −18, and −24 °C decreased by 41.03%, 51.87%, and 45.71%, respectively. Molecular dynamics simulations further showed that the peak value of the asphaltene–asphaltene radial distribution function decreased by 17.48%, while the fractional free volume increased by 20.00%, indicating suppressed asphaltene self-aggregation and increased molecular mobility within the system. These findings demonstrate that WCO and WWO exhibit functional complementarity in replenishing light fractions, restoring molecular mobility, and regulating asphaltene aggregation, thereby providing a theoretical basis for the component-oriented design of waste bio-oil-based composite rejuvenators.

title: The Synergistic Antibacterial Activity of Curcumin and Quercetin Against Nocardia seriolae and Evaluate Their Therapeutic Effects in the Infected Largemouth Bass
summary: ABSTRACT Nocardia seriolae is an important bacterial pathogen causing chronic granulomatous disease in cultured fish, and effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study aimed to identify natural compounds with synergistic antib
content: ABSTRACT Nocardia seriolae is an important bacterial pathogen causing chronic granulomatous disease in cultured fish, and effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study aimed to identify natural compounds with synergistic antibacterial activity against N. seriolae and evaluate their protective effects in largemouth bass ( Micropterus salmoides ). A structure‐guided screening strategy targeting N. seriolae isocitrate lyase (ICL) was performed using molecular docking, ADMET prediction, and in vitro antibacterial assays. Curcumin and quercetin were selected as candidate compounds based on their predicted interactions with ICL and antibacterial activity. The combination of curcumin and quercetin exhibited a synergistic effect against N. seriolae , with a fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) of 0.25 at a fixed 1:1 ratio, reducing the effective concentration of each compound eightfold compared with individual treatments. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable interactions between the two compounds and the ICL model, while enzyme activity analysis showed that the combination significantly reduced intracellular ICL activity. Furthermore, the combined treatment inhibited bacterial growth, decreased metabolic activity, and caused severe disruption of bacterial cell envelope integrity, as demonstrated by transmission electron microscopy and alkaline phosphatase leakage assays. Acute toxicity evaluation showed that the 96‐h LC 50 of the curcumin‐quercetin mixture in largemouth bass was 24 mg/L, indicating relatively low short‐term toxicity at the therapeutic concentration. In an experimental infection model, immersion treatment with the curcumin‐quercetin combination reduced bacterial burden, alleviated granulomatous lesions in visceral organs, and improved survival of infected fish. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that curcumin and quercetin provide a promising natural‐compound combination for controlling N. seriolae infection and provide a potential strategy for managing fish nocardiosis.

title: Effects of Graphene Oxide Addition and Carbonitriding on Metal Injection Molding Low Carbon Steel
summary: The effect of adding 1 wt.% graphene oxide (GO) to a low-carbon steel feedstock processed by metal injection molding (MIM) was investigated in terms of its thermal behavior, chemical composition after sintering, microstructure, and response
content: The effect of adding 1 wt.% graphene oxide (GO) to a low-carbon steel feedstock processed by metal injection molding (MIM) was investigated in terms of its thermal behavior, chemical composition after sintering, microstructure, and response to carbonitriding followed by quenching and tempering. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) revealed a shift in the melting peak of the polymeric binder system from 158 to 161 °C and a decrease in its apparent melting enthalpy from 112 to 98 J/g, indicating changes in the thermal behavior of the feedstock rather than melting or phase transformation of the steel matrix. Thermogravimetric analysis showed a shift in the onset of mass loss from approximately 325 to 310 °C, with additional decomposition events occurring between approximately 420 and 450 °C. After sintering, the carbon content increased from 0.118 to 0.219 wt.%, accompanied by higher Cr, Ni, and Cu contents. The GO-containing material also exhibited a finer ferritic grain structure and a higher pearlite fraction, together with indications of increased residual porosity and local microstructural heterogeneity. Following carbonitriding, quenching, and tempering, surface microhardness was substantially higher than core microhardness, and the 5% polymer solution produced the highest cooling intensity and surface microhardness among the evaluated quenching media. Overall, the results indicate that GO addition modified the thermal behavior of the polymeric binder system and was associated with changes in the chemical composition, microstructure, and response of sintered MIM low-carbon steel to carbonitriding and subsequent heat treatment.

title: Carbon Dot-Coated Bambusa vulgaris Fibers: Structural, Photoluminescent, and Antibacterial Properties for Sustainable Functional Applications
summary: Cellulose-rich natural fibers provide a renewable platform for developing sustainable functional materials. This study investigated carbon dot-coated Bambusa vulgaris fibers prepared through a simple dip-assisted coating approach to introdu
content: Cellulose-rich natural fibers provide a renewable platform for developing sustainable functional materials. This study investigated carbon dot-coated Bambusa vulgaris fibers prepared through a simple dip-assisted coating approach to introduce optical and antibacterial functionalities. X-ray diffraction revealed a semi-crystalline structure with a crystallinity index of 16.9%, while FTIR analysis identified oxygen-containing functional groups consistent with possible non-covalent interactions between CDs and the cellulose surface. The coated fibers exhibited a tensile strength of 196.95 ± 2.82 MPa, strain at break of 0.062 ± 0.004, and Young’s modulus of 4.13 GPa. Photoluminescence analysis showed broad visible emission from 410–710 nm, with maximum intensity of 4892 a.u. at 548 nm. CLSM qualitatively confirmed fluorescence distributed along the coated fiber surface. Antibacterial testing at 100 μg mL⁻¹ produced inhibition zones of 15 mm against Escherichia coli and 14 mm against Staphylococcus aureus , corresponding to 78.9% and 82.4% of the activity of the 10 μg streptomycin control, respectively. These findings demonstrate successful optical surface modification and antibacterial activity of carbon dot-coated Bambusa vulgaris fibers for sustainable functional material applications. The limitations of this study is the absence of quantitative CD loading and coating-stability measurements, direct antibacterial mechanistic assays, and cytotoxicity and biocompatibility evaluations, which currently limits confirmation of long-term biomedical applicability.

title: Associations of gut microbial and serum metabolic features with metabolic comorbidities in patients with NAFLD
summary: Introduction Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) coexists with dyslipidemia or impaired fasting glucose (IFG), but gut microbial and serum metabolic features remain incompletely characterized. Objectives We aimed to compare gut microb
content: Introduction Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) coexists with dyslipidemia or impaired fasting glucose (IFG), but gut microbial and serum metabolic features remain incompletely characterized. Objectives We aimed to compare gut microbial beta diversity, taxonomic profiles, predicted microbial functions, and serum metabolites across healthy controls (HCs) and NAFLD subgroups; evaluate omics-based classifiers and exploratory integrated classifiers distinguishing subgroups from HCs; and assess metabolic responses to Dialister invisus supplementation in mice. Methods Fecal microbiota and serum metabolites were profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing and targeted UPLC–MS/MS, respectively, in 41 HCs and 222 NAFLD patients. Patients were stratified into three subgroups by dyslipidemia and IFG: NAFLD_N (neither dyslipidemia nor IFG), NAFLD_DLP (dyslipidemia without IFG), and NAFLD_IFG (IFG irrespective of lipid status; HbA1c/OGTT unavailable). Random-forest classifiers were developed for each omics layer and for post hoc integrated multi-omics panels to distinguish each NAFLD subgroup from HCs, with performance evaluated in the held-out set. Dialister invisus was administered to high-calorie diet-fed mice, and metabolic and hepatic outcomes were assessed. Results NAFLD patients showed lower Dialister invisus abundance and higher abundance of the GTDB placeholder taxon Phascolarctobacterium_A sp900545025, with increased predicted menaquinone biosynthetic potential. Microbial and serum metabolite profiles differed significantly among subgroups. Microbiome classifiers achieved AUROCs of 0.71, 0.58, and 0.73 in the held-out internal evaluation, whereas metabolome classifiers achieved AUROCs of 0.89, 0.83, and 0.93 for NAFLD_N, NAFLD_DLP, and NAFLD_IFG. Post hoc integrated panels yielded descriptive AUROCs of 0.92, 0.89, and 0.96 in that subset. Dialister invisus supplementation reduced body weight, serum ALT, AST, triglycerides, fasting blood glucose, and ipGTT AUC in high-calorie diet-fed mice. Conclusion This study identifies shared gut microbial and serum metabolic alterations across NAFLD patients irrespective of IFG or dyslipidemia, alongside subgroup-specific signatures. The Dialister invisus findings support its potential role in metabolic regulation and warrant mechanistic investigation.

title: Linking Corrosion Product Morphology to Impedance Response Across Immersion and Salt Spray Testing of Coated Steel
summary: ABSTRACT Neutral salt spray and immersion testing are both routinely used to assess coated‐steel corrosion, yet rarely compared at the level of the corrosion product itself. This work examines whether electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
content: ABSTRACT Neutral salt spray and immersion testing are both routinely used to assess coated‐steel corrosion, yet rarely compared at the level of the corrosion product itself. This work examines whether electrochemical impedance spectroscopy differences between natural immersion, artificially aerated immersion, and neutral salt spray trace back to corrosion product architecture rather than to the test method. Bare steel and zinc‐rich and epoxy‐only scribed powder‐coated systems were characterised by EIS, imaging, and SEM. Natural immersion produced the highest impedance and a compact product; neutral salt spray produced the lowest impedance and a porous, cracked product; aerated immersion was intermediate. The same ranking was reproduced in coated systems, where the corrosion product at the defect dominated the response. Zinc rich primer coating's impedance advantage over epoxy coating was reduced under aeration, suggesting zinc's cathodic‐protection mechanism is itself oxygen‐sensitive. EIS indicators from different accelerated tests should not be assumed directly comparable.

title: Multiple Phase Transition Behavior of Silver Thiophenolates with Rigid Aromatic Rings and Flexible Alkoxy Chains
summary: Silver thiolate coordination polymers (CPs) exhibit diverse structures and physical properties, although thermal behavior of silver thiophenolate CPs has rarely been investigated. In this study, we investigated the effects of ligands contai
content: Silver thiolate coordination polymers (CPs) exhibit diverse structures and physical properties, although thermal behavior of silver thiophenolate CPs has rarely been investigated. In this study, we investigated the effects of ligands containing rigid aromatic rings and flexible alkoxy chains on the thermal phase transitions of silver thiophenolate CPs. A series of para -alkoxy-substituted silver thiophenolate CPs (AgSAr-OCX, where X denotes the number of carbon atoms in the alkoxy chain) were prepared through ligand exchange reactions. Structural characterization revealed that all AgSAr-OCX derivatives formed layered crystal structures and that the conformational order of alkyl chains increased with increasing chain length. DSC analysis showed that the number and temperatures of the thermal transitions strongly depended on alkyl chain length, with longer-chain derivatives exhibiting multiple thermal events. Variable-temperature powder X-ray diffraction measurements revealed two successive lamellar-to-lamellar transitions followed by transformation into a hexagonal columnar phase for the longer-chain derivatives. Variable-temperature FT-IR measurements further indicated conformational disordering of the alkyl chains during the reversible low-temperature transition. These multiple phase transitions may arise from the combination of rigid aromatic rings that stabilize the layered structures and flexible alkoxy chains that provide thermal responsiveness through conformational changes.

title: Smart‐Release Ion‐Exchanged Ca‐Montmorillonite for Corrosion Protection of AA2024 Aluminium Alloy
summary: ABSTRACT This study reports the development of smart‐release anti‐corrosion pigments based on ion‐exchanged montmorillonite (MMT) for the protection of high‐strength AA2024 aluminium alloy. Zn 2+ ‐ and Mn 2+ ‐modified MMTs were synthesized
content: ABSTRACT This study reports the development of smart‐release anti‐corrosion pigments based on ion‐exchanged montmorillonite (MMT) for the protection of high‐strength AA2024 aluminium alloy. Zn 2+ ‐ and Mn 2+ ‐modified MMTs were synthesized by liquid‐phase ion exchange. XRD and SEM/EDX confirmed the preservation of the montmorillonite structure and incorporation of the modifying cations. The inhibiting performance of the pigments was evaluated in acid rain using potentiodynamic polarization, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and gravimetric measurements. Zn‐modified MMT provided the highest protection, reducing the corrosion current density from 1.2 × 10 −6 to 7.9 × 10 −8 A cm −2 after 168 h and achieving inhibition efficiencies of 93.4%, 93.7%, and 91.8% by polarization, EIS, and gravimetric measurements, respectively. Mn‐modified MMT showed lower inhibition efficiency (47%–54%), whereas Zn–Mn‐modified systems provided intermediate protection (75%–90%). The superior performance of Zn‐MMT may be associated with the release of Zn 2 + cations from montmorillonite interlayers and their possible interaction with OH − ions generated during cathodic oxygen reduction. These processes may favor the formation of sparingly soluble zinc‐containing species, potentially including Zn(OH) 2 , which could contribute to the development of a protective surface layer and reduce the electrochemically active area. Zn‐modified MMT therefore shows strong potential as an environmentally safe inhibiting pigment for anti‐corrosion coatings.

title: Hydrogen retrofitting for regional freight Decarbonization: vehicle-level feasibility and energy system implications
summary: Regional freight transport remains difficult to decarbonize due to high daily mileage, operational variability, and limited charging flexibility, which constrain the suitability of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) for medium- and long-dista
content: Regional freight transport remains difficult to decarbonize due to high daily mileage, operational variability, and limited charging flexibility, which constrain the suitability of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) for medium- and long-distance delivery missions. This study proposes a multi-scale framework to assess hydrogen retrofitting of existing diesel light commercial vehicles (LCVs) as a decarbonization strategy for regional freight transport. A real-world case study based on four representative delivery routes in the Rome metropolitan area is used to evaluate retrofit feasibility using commercially available fuel cell systems, lithium-ion batteries, and 350 bar hydrogen storage. The proposed fuel cell hybrid electric vehicle (FCHEV) achieves an estimated operational range exceeding 290 km while reducing capital expenditure (CAPEX) by approximately 40–50% compared with new hydrogen-powered LCVs. Vehicle-level results are extended to estimate fleet-scale hydrogen demand, electricity requirements, and infrastructure implications, providing decision support for freight fleet transition and regional transport decarbonization.

title: Electrolyzer Sizing and Techno‐Economic Assessment of Small‐Hydropower‐Based Green Hydrogen Using 3 Years of Hourly Generation Data
summary: ABSTRACT Small hydropower can provide a comparatively persistent renewable‐electricity profile for water electrolysis, but electrolyzer sizing requires a compromise between renewable‐energy capture and equipment utilization. This study eval
content: ABSTRACT Small hydropower can provide a comparatively persistent renewable‐electricity profile for water electrolysis, but electrolyzer sizing requires a compromise between renewable‐energy capture and equipment utilization. This study evaluates a planned green‐hydrogen system at Miryang Dam, Republic of Korea, using 26,280 h of measured generation data from two 650 kW units during 2021–2023. A 1 MW PEM electrolyzer was simulated by hourly load following, and capacities from 300 to 1200 kW were screened using an equal‐weight ideal‐point criterion and marginal hydrogen‐production gain. The planned 1 MW configuration captured 98.11% of available hydropower energy, achieved a 59.93% capacity factor, and produced 93.75 t‐H 2 /year. The criterion identified 600 kW as the technically balanced capacity, with 84.71% capture, 86.25% capacity factor, and 80.95 t‐H 2 /year. Incremental hydrogen gain declined from 7.03 t/year for the 500–600 kW increase to 3.82 t/year for 600–700 kW. At a PPA price of KRW 160/kWh, audited operating and full LCOH were KRW 20,137/kg‐H 2 and 27,209/kg‐H 2 . The results show that sizing based solely on peak hydropower output can overestimate the electrolyzer capacity required for efficient system utilization.

title: Occupational Airborne Pollutant Exposure and Hematological Outcomes in Workplace Settings: A Systematic Review
summary: Occupational exposure to airborne pollutants poses a significant risk to hematological health. This systematic review aims to evaluate the associations between workplace airborne pollutants and key blood parameters, as well as the modifying
content: Occupational exposure to airborne pollutants poses a significant risk to hematological health. This systematic review aims to evaluate the associations between workplace airborne pollutants and key blood parameters, as well as the modifying roles of age and body mass index (BMI) among adult industrial workers. Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search across Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Medline identified studies published over the last five decades. The search strategy incorporated terms related to occupational air pollution and airborne pollutants, including particulate matter (PM), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and heavy metals (HMs). Studies evaluating occupational exposures and reporting hematological outcomes-hemoglobin concentration, mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH), mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC), and anemia prevalence-were included. Methodological quality was assessed using study design-specific JBI critical appraisal checklists. Out of 1855 retrieved records, 55 studies (predominantly from developing and industrializing countries) met the eligibility criteria. Findings reveal that workplace exposure to VOCs, HMs (e.g., lead), and PM is consistently associated with subclinical hematological alterations, characterized by lower hemoglobin levels and altered red blood cell indices (MCH and MCHC). Notably, despite high workplace pollutant concentrations, linear correlations between pollutant levels and hematological indices were often weak, indicating complex exposure-response dynamics. Analysis of modifying factors showed that higher BMI was positively associated with hemoglobin levels, potentially suggesting a protective buffering pattern, whereas age exhibited weak associations, likely reflecting a "healthy-worker effect" in exposed populations. The complexity of these findings underscores the necessity of moving beyond single-pollutant assessments toward evaluating mixed workplace exposures. Integrating routine hematological surveillance and nutritional screening into occupational health programs is crucial for mitigating workplace hematotoxicity.

title: Accelerating interfacial charge transfer via spin polarized Ni-doped Co3O4 for high-performance zinc-iron flow batteries
summary: Interfacial charge-transfer critically governs Zn plating/stripping kinetics and determines the electrochemical performance of zinc‑iron flow batteries. However, the regulation of electron-transfer pathways at the spin-level remains unexplo
content: Interfacial charge-transfer critically governs Zn plating/stripping kinetics and determines the electrochemical performance of zinc‑iron flow batteries. However, the regulation of electron-transfer pathways at the spin-level remains unexplored. Herein, we propose a micro-interface spin engineering strategy using Ni-doped spinel Co 3 O 4 as a model catalyst and reveal that the local spin configuration serves as a fundamental descriptor for regulating interfacial electron transfer pathways during zinc deposition. Guided by the Mott two-current model, Ni doping modulates the spin structure of spinel Co 3 O 4 , creating asymmetric spin-dependent channels and establishing a dominant low-resistance spin transport pathway. As a result, Ni-doped Co 3 O 4 markedly lowers the apparent activation energy for interfacial Zn/Zn 2+ charge transfer from 23.61 kJ·mol −1 to 12.79 kJ·mol −1 and exhibits the lowest charge-transfer resistance. The optimized spin-dependent transport pathway further promotes uniform Zn nucleation and surface diffusion, effectively suppressing dendrite formation. Benefiting from these advantages, the zinc‑iron flow battery maintains an energy efficiency above 80% at 100 mA·cm −2 and sustains over 600 cycles with negligible capacity decay. This work establishes a mechanistic framework linking local spin polarization with interfacial electron-transfer pathways, offering new insight into spin-regulated Zn deposition kinetics and providing a rational strategy for designing high-performance zinc-based flow batteries.

title: Enhanced Quantum Simulations Reveal Conformation-Controlled, Site-Resolved Proton Binding in Biliverdin
summary: For a molecule with several titratable sites, a measured pKa reports a change in the number of bound protons, but not the population of each tautomer. The biological chromophore biliverdin (BV) is a longstanding example: the protonation of
content: For a molecule with several titratable sites, a measured pKa reports a change in the number of bound protons, but not the population of each tautomer. The biological chromophore biliverdin (BV) is a longstanding example: the protonation of its four pyrrole nitrogens controls its photoactivity, yet the reported pKa values vary by about two units, and ring C is typically assumed deprotonated in neutral BV without a site-resolving measurement. BV is also flexible, so its protonation microstates and its conformers form coupled ensembles: the shape of the molecule changes how tightly it binds the proton. Here, we compute the macroscopic pKa of BV in explicit water and the populations of its four neutral tautomers, from the site-resolved pKa of the four rings. Enhanced quantum-mechanical simulations follow a proton into bulk water, and the free energies of proton transfer between rings and of ring rotation connect all protonation states in one thermodynamically consistent network. In the locked-helix conformation that dominates in water, BV has a macroscopic pKa of 4.0, and its four nitrogens are almost equally basic (site pKa values of 4.5 for rings B and C and 4.9 for rings A and D). No single tautomer dominates: the tautomers deprotonated at rings B and C each make up 36% of neutral BV, and those deprotonated at rings A and D 14% each.
