content: Introduction Plant-associated microbiomes can shape host phenotypes, yet plant breeding programs rarely incorporate microbiome data into their selection criteria. For example, multi-location trials are central for studying genotype-by-environment interactions, yet the microbiome is a poorly characterized component of environmental variation. Methods This study sought to better understand effects of region, irrigation and nutrient management, and scion on variation in the cacao-associated soil microbiome within a multi-location breeding trial. Samples were sent for amplicon sequencing from four regions of Brazil and represented two cocoa scions and an irrigation trial comparing drip-irrigated and rainfed plots. Results Samples clustered by region for both prokaryotes and fungi, though the effects were not significant due to low statistical power and differences in multivariate dispersion. A conserved core microbiome was identified that included a complete prokaryotic nitrogen-cycling functional core as well as two omnipresent fungal ASVs belonging to the genus Fusarium . Irrigation and nutrient management explained 13% of fungal beta diversity and affected the relative abundance of 156 irrigation-responsive taxa across taxonomic levels. Depletion of irrigation-sensitive prokaryotes was linked to lower alpha diversity in drip-irrigated/fertigated plots relative to rainfed plots receiving surface-applied fertilizer, while fungi were more resilient to the effects of irrigation. Scion genotype did not affect alpha or beta diversity of the soil microbiome. Discussion Together, these findings can be used to guide incorporation of microbial variation in plant breeding models and inform management strategies that support productive and sustainable agroecosystems.

title: Ignition Enhancement by Repetitive Pulsed Discharge Plasma in a Methane/Air Mixture with Barrier Discharge Igniter and J-Hook plug
summary: Methane, the main component of natural gas and biogas, is widely used in internal combustion engines as a low-carbon fuel. The stability of methane ignition under lean-burn and diluted conditions remains challenging for achieving high effic
content: Methane, the main component of natural gas and biogas, is widely used in internal combustion engines as a low-carbon fuel. The stability of methane ignition under lean-burn and diluted conditions remains challenging for achieving high efficiency and low emissions. Repetitive pulsed discharge plasma offers a promising solution by enabling rapid energy deposition. In this study, a repetitive sub-microsecond pulsed discharge (RMPD) ignition system was developed and applied to a barrier discharge igniter (BDI) and a J-Hook plug. Their ignition characteristics were compared with conventional transistorised coil ignition (TCI) in a constant-volume combustion chamber. Methane/air mixtures with stoichiometric and lean conditions, λ = 1 and λ = 1.8, were tested at 2 bar and 298 K using high-speed Schlieren images and spectroscopic measurements. The lowest pulse number for successful ignition of RMPD systems was two, corresponding to the apparent discharge energy of approximately 6 mJ for BDI-RMPD and 32 mJ for J-Hook RMPD. For J-Hook TCI, the corresponding lowest tested energy was 45 mJ. BDI-RMPD exhibits the best ignition performance across all test conditions. However, J-Hook RMPD shows a strong dependence on pulse number, with “increase-decrease” non-monotonic behaviour at λ = 1 and improved ignition with increasing pulse number at λ = 1.8. Schlieren results indicate that the flame kernel with RMPD is synergistically governed by thermal effect and local plasma-induced jetting. Spectroscopic measurements of Hα (656 nm) and O (777 nm) emissions from the J-Hook RMPD show greater shot-to-shot variability under lean conditions, suggesting that the early ignition process is sensitive to local mixture conditions near the plug.

title: Daytime Idle Energy Reduction in Radiotherapy Simulation Computed Tomography: A Prospective Workflow‐Based Evaluation
summary: ABSTRACT Introduction Previous computed tomography (CT) energy‐saving studies have primarily focused on after‐hours shutdown or idle energy use in diagnostic CT. Radiotherapy simulation, however, includes preparation and immobilisation step
content: ABSTRACT Introduction Previous computed tomography (CT) energy‐saving studies have primarily focused on after‐hours shutdown or idle energy use in diagnostic CT. Radiotherapy simulation, however, includes preparation and immobilisation steps that may prolong daytime non‐acquisition periods. This study quantified daytime energy use in radiotherapy simulation CT and evaluated the contribution of power‐saving operation. Methods In this prospective single‐centre study, electrical power consumption was directly measured using a three‐phase power logger during five baseline and five power‐saving weekdays (08:00–18:00). Power measurements were integrated with patient in‐room intervals and simulation procedure categories. Staff perceptions of workflow impact were assessed using an anonymous questionnaire, and carbon implications were estimated from the measured energy reduction. Results Mean directly measured clinical‐hour energy consumption decreased from 38.7 to 36.5 kWh/day with power‐saving operation, a 5.8% reduction. Non‐acquisition time during patient presence varied markedly by procedure, from 56.5% for respiratory‐gated four‐dimensional CT to 97.1% for head‐and‐neck simulation. Power‐saving operation shifted daytime power use towards a lower‐power state, corresponding to an estimated reduction of 0.84–1.01 kg‐CO 2 per clinical day across the emission‐factor sensitivity range. Twenty of 21 staff (95.2%) reported no impact on patient throughput. Conclusion Power‐saving operation reduced daytime energy consumption without meaningful workflow disruption. Radiotherapy simulation CT has prolonged, procedure‐dependent idle periods arising from radiotherapy‐specific preparation workflows, highlighting a practical and previously undercharacterised opportunity for energy reduction.

title: ASSESSMENT OF GLOBAL SUSTAINABILITY
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset is associated to Deliverable 3.5, produced within the framework of the EU-HORIZON project TRANSITION https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101069665 This dataset contains the input parameters, and sectoral vector changes used to
content: This dataset is associated to Deliverable 3.5, produced within the framework of the EU-HORIZON project TRANSITION https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101069665 This dataset contains the input parameters, and sectoral vector changes used to represent the deployment of different carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies in European NGCC power plants within an input-output modelling framework. The dataset includes technology-specific characteristics, operational assumptions, investment and operational expenditure allocations, modifications to economic demand vectors, emissions reduction assumptions, and associated scenario definitions. The data support the estimation of economic, environmental, and value-chain impacts of CCS implementation under alternative deployment pathways

title: Environmental suitability and climate-informed spatial prioritization of Opuntia ficus-indica (L.) MILL. in India using MaxEnt and the analytic hierarchy process
summary: Climate-informed diversification of water-limited farming systems requires identifying environmentally suitable areas that remain favorable under future climate conditions. This study assessed the current and future environmental suitabilit
content: Climate-informed diversification of water-limited farming systems requires identifying environmentally suitable areas that remain favorable under future climate conditions. This study assessed the current and future environmental suitability of cactus pear ( Opuntia ficus-indica ) across India and developed a spatial prioritization framework for dryland agricultural planning. MaxEnt models using 138 spatially thinned occurrence records and climatic, soil, and land-use/land-cover predictors were projected to the 2050s and 2070s under four RCP scenarios using the BCC-CSM1-1 global climate model. MaxEnt-derived suitability was integrated with selected soil and land-surface criteria through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Future suitability persistence was quantified using the Climate Persistence Index (CPI) and combined with current integrated suitability to derive the Climate-smart Opuntia Priority Index (COPI). Current Moderate-to-Optimum integrated suitability covered approximately 1.085 million km 2 , of which 73.41% (796,315 km 2 ) retained at least Moderate suitability across five or more of eight future scenarios. COPI identified 549,070 km 2 (16.80% of the analyzed area) as High or Very-high priority, primarily in western India, with additional opportunities in peninsular regions. Five independently reported Indian experimental locations corresponded spatially with High or Very-high COPI classes; however, observed differences in survival and productivity demonstrated that model-derived suitability does not directly predict crop performance. The principal limitations include reliance on a single climate model, predefined MaxEnt regularization and AHP weights, static soil and land-use assumptions, and limited field correspondence. Thus, COPI provides a preliminary biophysical decision-support framework for prioritizing genotype evaluation, agronomic trials, and climate-smart dryland diversification rather than direct evidence of cultivation success or agricultural resilience.

title: Sustainable soil practices for improving soil health, greenhouse gas mitigation and climate resilience of rice cropping systems
summary: Climate change is threatening rice yields more and more, which undermines global food security. Traditional agricultural practices further endanger the ecosystem by causing carbon emissions, soil degradation and wasteful water usage. Despit
content: Climate change is threatening rice yields more and more, which undermines global food security. Traditional agricultural practices further endanger the ecosystem by causing carbon emissions, soil degradation and wasteful water usage. Despite some progress in this area, local adaptation, soil quality improvement and mitigation remain insufficient. This review emphasises the importance of sustainable soil management in enhancing the climate resilience of ecosystems. Conservation tillage can reduce carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions by 25–40% and production costs by 20–35%. Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) and the System of Rice Intensification (SRI) reduce methane emissions by 40–70% whilst increasing water retention capacity by 25–65%. Organic amendments can increase soil organic matter content by 25–40%, while the use of biochar can increase drought resilience by 15% and grain yield by 10% in stressful conditions. Integrated practices can reduce total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 30–50%. This study also suggests the development of climate-resilient rice varieties that can cope with climate change, and new soil amendments, such as biofertilisers that have been enhanced by nanotechnology and designer biochars. Moreover, digital agriculture such as using artificial intelligence to monitor soil health and precision application technologies. This review highlights the urgent need to make these practices mainstream in order to ensure long-term productivity and ecological stability.

title: AI Model Energy and Carbon Disclosure: A Source-Audited Study of 103 Releases (2024-2026)
summary: AI model cards and release documents are supposed to help people assess models. For energy and carbon, they often leave out the number a reader needs, or print figures that cannot be compared directly. I built the Release Energy Ledger, a s
content: AI model cards and release documents are supposed to help people assess models. For energy and carbon, they often leave out the number a reader needs, or print figures that cannot be compared directly. I built the Release Energy Ledger, a source-traceable record of 161 distinct developer releases, and audited a selected set of 103 dated 2024-2026 releases that passed a page check. On the designated release document, 85 (82.5 percent) print no energy, carbon or compute figure, 1 prints compute only, and 17 (16.5 percent) print an energy or carbon-related figure: 16 training-specific and 1 life-cycle footprint. None prints release-specific inference energy. Meta accounts for 10 of the 17; without Meta, the count is 7 of 93. The figures differ in method, unit, equipment boundary and emissions accounting, and only 8 of the 17 state a basis, a boundary and a method together. Changing the unit of analysis gives 11 of 80 documents, 10 of 59 model families and 7 of 23 developers. The strict-quote subset (5 of 74) is a different evidence frame, not a lower bound. A page re-read confirmed the printed figures for all 17; blinded AI coding agreed with the ledger on 91.9 to 100 percent of fields, and a separately instructed AI adjudicator agreed on 42 of 42 selected cells. These results describe the documents in this selected set, not actual emissions, the universe of releases or legal compliance. No human has validated any label. The ledger and counting script are released with the paper as a versioned data record (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23808341).

title: Energy dependence, industrial structure, and growth in the EU
summary: This research examines how industrial structure influences the relationship between energy security and economic growth within the European Union. The analysis is based on Eurostat data for EU member states covering the period from 2000 to
content: This research examines how industrial structure influences the relationship between energy security and economic growth within the European Union. The analysis is based on Eurostat data for EU member states covering the period from 2000 to 2024. To explore these relationships, the study employs two-way fixed-effects regression and System GMM estimation, while using cluster analysis to group countries based on their structural characteristics. The results indicate that the impact of energy security on growth depends on a country's industrial structure: a larger industrial share can mitigate the adverse growth consequences of energy dependence. Investments show a positive and stable relationship with growth, whereas the impact of inflation is negative. The roles of trade openness and renewable energy are more moderate and less robust. The cluster analysis identifies three groups of countries that differ in terms of growth performance, energy dependence, and economic openness. The findings emphasize that efforts to reduce energy dependence and transition to a cleaner energy system should be supported by policies tailored to the specific industrial characteristics of individual member states. From a policy perspective, the findings support differentiated measures tailored to Member States’ industrial structures and levels of energy dependence. Energy diversification should therefore be combined with policies that strengthen energy efficiency, investment, and industrial adaptability.

title: Eco-social pedagogy through outdoor learning in early childhood education: Teachers' outdoor practices in northern Spain
summary: Early childhood education is increasingly recognised as a critical space for cultivating climate awareness, care, and agency through embodied and relational learning, with outdoor education emerging as a particularly powerful context for th
content: Early childhood education is increasingly recognised as a critical space for cultivating climate awareness, care, and agency through embodied and relational learning, with outdoor education emerging as a particularly powerful context for this development. This mixed-methods study examines how educators in regular schools in the Basque Country (Northern Spain) describe the role of sustained engagement with nearby ecosystems in supporting eco-social pedagogies and education for sustainability in early childhood settings. Data were collected through questionnaires completed by educators representing schools participating in the Forest School Network (n = 28 schools), complemented by 21 semi-structured interviews with teachers who regularly engage in outdoor learning in nearby ecosystems. Findings indicate that outdoor environments function as emotionally secure and pedagogically generative spaces where children engage in place-based practices such as tree planting, litter collection, habitat creation, monitoring invasive species, measuring water and air temperature, participating in citizen science initiatives, and using local ecological knowledge, including Basque species names. Educators described these everyday practices as fostering eco-social dispositions grounded in care, relational ethics, agency, and shared environmental responsibility. Teachers described a professional shift from transmitting environmental knowledge toward facilitating inquiry, empathy, and collective forms of environmental care. At the same time, many educators identify gaps in institutional support and climate-related training within teacher education programmes. By situating these insights within current debates on early childhood climate education, the study contributes grounded empirical evidence on how educators perceive the relationship between eco-social pedagogy, outdoor learning and environmental education in early childhood settings. It suggests that outdoor education, when framed as emotional, agential, ethical, and community-oriented engagement, is perceived by educators as creating opportunities to encourage dispositions associated with environmental responsibility, care, and sustainability.

title: The ESG Paradox: Reconciling Financial Performance, Rating Divergence, and Market Realities
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
summary: ESG-labelled assets have expanded rapidly, transforming from a niche ethical strategy into a cornerstone of global capital allocation. Yet, this rapid growth encounters profound structural friction: regulators pull in opposite directions re
content: ESG-labelled assets have expanded rapidly, transforming from a niche ethical strategy into a cornerstone of global capital allocation. Yet, this rapid growth encounters profound structural friction: regulators pull in opposite directions regarding mandates, and rating providers fiercely disagree on which firms qualify as sustainable. This review asks whether capital allocation guided by ESG metrics actually improves risk-adjusted corporate financial performance or instead masks agency frictions and greenwashing. The review synthesizes peer-reviewed meta-analyses, identified econometric studies, and rating-provider datasets published between 2001 and 2024, analyzing mechanisms across the environmental, social, and governance pillars. Meta-analyses overwhelmingly report non-negative ESG–financial performance associations. Identified studies trace this value to highly specific channels: lower financing costs, stronger human-capital productivity, and thinner downside risk tails. However, aggregate effect sizes remain modest, and portfolio-level evidence demonstrates weaker, regime-dependent returns. Rating divergence compounds this problem. Six major ESG providers correlate at only 0.54 on average, primarily due to fundamental disagreements over scope and measurement. Industry materiality, firm size, and varying regulatory regimes explain much of this heterogeneity. Corporate boards must tie ESG compensation strictly to audited, material metrics; asset managers must triangulate specific underlying indicators rather than trusting composite scores; and regulators should urgently prioritize disclosure comparability over additional subjective ratings.

title: The Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty: A Just and Equity Agreement to Ending Fossil Fuels Era
summary: To face the current and interconnected climate, ecological and socio-economic crises a radical change in our societies which starts from an immediate energy transition from fossil fuels is required. Undoubtedly, the global fossil fuels indu
content: To face the current and interconnected climate, ecological and socio-economic crises a radical change in our societies which starts from an immediate energy transition from fossil fuels is required. Undoubtedly, the global fossil fuels industry is the major driver of climate change. In fact, it is responsible for about 90% of the global carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions into the atmosphere ( SEI et al. 2023 ). Since 2019, the implementation of a proposed international agreement, the Fossil Fuels Non-Proliferation Treaty, which is patterned after to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, stems from a global articulation of climate justice movements, indigenous and civil society organisations. The three fundamental pillars of the treaty are based on: the development of a just transition based on international cooperation between states, non-proliferation (immediate cessation of exploration and expansion into new fossil fuels reserves) and a fair phase-out. The adherence of various nation states across four continents (17), 10 Indigenous Amazon nations, numerous municipalities (135) and organisations (3.995) underlines that this initiative is now the most effective and mature mitigation agreement to ensure that the quantities of fossil fuels essential to achieving global climate governance goals are left in the ground ( Howard et al. 2022 ).

title: Decarbonization as a neo-colonial policy in Africa? Rethinking development priorities in global climate governance
summary: Global climate governance presents a fundamental paradox: while Africa contributes less than 4% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, the continent suffers disproportionately from climate impacts, resulting in annual financial losses am
content: Global climate governance presents a fundamental paradox: while Africa contributes less than 4% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, the continent suffers disproportionately from climate impacts, resulting in annual financial losses amounting to billions of dollars. Although existing scholarship has largely critiqued Western-influenced climate governance, understanding decarbonization as a neocolonial policy to moderate Africa’s development priorities remains underexplored. Employing a qualitative multi-method design and drawing on the thesis of climate colonialism, this study critically dissects the colonial erasures within Western-centric decarbonization policies and examines how global green transition mandates conflict with Africa’s developmental priorities. Findings reveal a disconnect between carbon market narratives and the rising emission levels of advanced economies. Despite this double standard, African states are made to comply with green transition mandates without adequate financial or technological support from major historical emitters. This article makes a case for a restructured climate justice system that respects Africa’s low historical carbon footprint, prioritizes its developmental needs while still contributing meaningfully to global climate goals.

title: Beyond Pollutant Removal: Solar-Driven Photo-Oxidation Pathways for Circular and Intelligent Wastewater Treatment
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Although the photo-oxidation process is often portrayed as a technology for pollutants destruction,yet the future of it relies on its ability to remove pollutants from real wastewater, in a process that requires minimal external energy, is
content: Although the photo-oxidation process is often portrayed as a technology for pollutants destruction,yet the future of it relies on its ability to remove pollutants from real wastewater, in a process that requires minimal external energy, is capable of recovering useful products, maintains controlled toxicity levels, and has measurable environmental benefits. This review critically assesses photolysis routes from photon absorption to the generation of reactive-oxygen-species, as well as from the reactor to the post-treatment, recovery of the resources and intelligent control. It discusses semiconductor photocatalysis, photo-Fenton chemistry, photoelectrocatalysis, heterogeneous oxidants, and hybrid solar–biological trains and the difference between removal, transformation, mineralization, detoxification and circularity. Special emphasis is placed on the occurrence of matrix effects, catalyst deactivation, photon utilization, mass transfer, energy demand, secondary pollution and reliability of reported kinetic parameters. The review reveals significant differences between well optimized laboratory experiments and working systems: most studies are conducted with synthetic water, short batch tests, single contaminant solutions, incomplete mass balances, and inconsistent energy accounting. The proposed circular-intelligence framework involves: (1) solar photo-oxidation, (2) online sensing, (3) mechanistic-datadriven modeling, (4) predictive control, (5) catalyst recovery, (6) product quality checking and (7) life cycle assessment. The review finds that future progress will neither be made by achieving maximum removal percentages nor will it be made by achieving a process that is easy to execute in the lab, but difficult or impossible in practice.

title: Long-term outcomes of globe-sparing surgery combined with adjuvant radiotherapy for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma
summary: Purpose To evaluate long-term outcomes of radiotherapy after globe-sparing surgery for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) and compare different radiotherapy protocols. Methods This retrospective comparative case series included
content: Purpose To evaluate long-term outcomes of radiotherapy after globe-sparing surgery for lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) and compare different radiotherapy protocols. Methods This retrospective comparative case series included 97 patients with LGACC treated with globe-sparing surgery followed by postoperative radiotherapy between November 2003 and April 2023. Patients received one of four protocols differing in clinical target volume (CTV) expansion and radiation dose. Primary outcomes included locoregional recurrence, distant metastasis, locoregional recurrence-free survival (LRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), progression-free survival, and overall survival. Results The median age was 38 years, and median follow-up was 7.2 years. The overall 5-, 10-, and 15-year LRFS rates were 80.2%, 74.5%, and 74.5%, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified R2 resection (HR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.53‑11.35, P = 0.005), cribriform histology (HR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.08‑0.81, P = 0.020), and smaller CTV expansion (≤0.5 cm; HR = 4.06, 95% CI: 1.41‑11.67, P = 0.009) as independent predictors of local recurrence. Patients treated with ≤0.5-cm CTV expansion and ≤54 Gy had significantly lower 5-, 10-, and 15-year LRFS rates (55.2%, 40.5%, and 40.5%) than those treated with 1-cm CTV expansion and 60-80 Gy (90.5%, 90.5%, and 90.5%; P < 0.001). DMFS did not differ significantly between groups ( P = 0.599). Best-corrected visual acuity of 20/20-20/40 was preserved in 35.1% of patients. The 5-year risk of radiation retinopathy was 25.1% and 43.6% ( P = 0.057) in the no extended-margin and extended-margin groups, respectively. Conclusions Radiotherapy with 1-cm CTV expansion and a dose of 60 Gy after globe-sparing surgery provided favorable locoregional control for LGACC. Distant metastasis remained the predominant cause of treatment failure.

title: High-pyrolysis-temperature acidified straw biochar improves soil hydrological functioning and increases maize yield in saline soils
summary: Biochar contributes to the restoration of soil fertility and crop productivity in saline-affected farmlands. Soil hydrological functioning is a key indicator for assessing the degradation and rehabilitation of saline soils. However, the mec
content: Biochar contributes to the restoration of soil fertility and crop productivity in saline-affected farmlands. Soil hydrological functioning is a key indicator for assessing the degradation and rehabilitation of saline soils. However, the mechanisms by which acid-modified maize straw biochar produced at different pyrolysis temperatures regulates the hydrological properties of saline soils remain unclear. In this study, a four-year soil amendment experiment was conducted in moderately saline soils of the Hetao Irrigation District in China to evaluate the effects and underlying mechanisms of acidified biochar produced at three pyrolysis temperatures (C1: 300 °C, C2: 500 °C, and C3: 700 °C) and applied at two rates (T1: 10 Mg ha - ¹ and T2: 20 Mg ha - ¹) on soil hydrological properties. The results showed that: (1) application of acidified biochar significantly decreased soil salinity, pH, and bulk density, while increasing soil water content and organic matter. Moreover, it markedly enhanced crop yield and biomass; (2) acidified biochar markedly improved soil hydrological properties (0–40 cm), with the C3T1 treatment performing best, increasing soil saturated water-holding capacity, field capacity, soil water storage, and saturated hydraulic conductivity by 17.35%, 27.91%, 14.31%, and 26.92%, respectively; (3) Principal component analysis (PCA) and Mantel test results indicated that soil hydrological properties were positively correlated with crop yield, biomass, clay content, soil organic matter, and total porosity (p < 0.05), but negatively correlated with bulk density, electrical conductivity, and sand content (p < 0.05). Random forest analysis further highlighted that improvements in soil hydrological properties were primarily driven by changes in biomass, SOM, bulk density, clay content, and total porosity. Overall, this study demonstrates that acidified biochar produced at a high pyrolysis temperature (700 °C) and applied at 10 Mg ha - ¹ effectively enhances the physicochemical and hydrological properties of saline soils, thereby improving their productivity. These findings provide important guidance for developing biochar-based strategies to rehabilitate saline-affected agricultural soils.

title: Does the carbon emission trading scheme enhance enterprises’ green total factor productivity? Evidence from China
summary: With growing global attention to climate change and sustainable development, the green and low-carbon transition has become a key pathway to advancing high-quality economic development. However, whether the carbon emission trading scheme ca
content: With growing global attention to climate change and sustainable development, the green and low-carbon transition has become a key pathway to advancing high-quality economic development. However, whether the carbon emission trading scheme can enhance enterprises’ green total factor productivity while simultaneously achieving emission reductions still requires further investigation. Utilizing relevant data of Chinese A-share listed companies spanning from 2011 to 2023, the present study conceptualizes the carbon emission trading scheme as a quasi-natural experiment and establishes a Difference-in-Differences (DID) model to scrutinize its impact on enterprises’ green total factor productivity (GTFP). The findings reveal that the carbon emission trading scheme notably elevates enterprises’ GTFP, with the outcomes retaining robustness even after addressing endogeneity concerns and conducting rigorous robustness checks. Mechanism tests elucidate that the carbon emission trading scheme primarily propels enterprises’ GTFP by alleviating financing constraints, curtailing agency costs, and promoting digital transformation. Moderating effect tests demonstrate that market competition plays a pivotal role in amplifying the positive influence of the carbon emission trading scheme on enterprises’ GTFP. Heterogeneity analysis suggests that the policy effects of the trading scheme are more noticeable among non-state-owned enterprises, pollution-intensive enterprises, and enterprises situated in the eastern region. Furthermore, an examination of economic consequences unveils that the carbon emission trading scheme not only elevates their GTFP but also fosters their high-quality development. These research outcomes not only diversify the theoretical literature concerning the trading scheme and its economic consequences but also furnish vital theoretical guidance and policy recommendations for refining the carbon emission trading scheme, advancing the construction of the trading market, and bolstering enterprises’ GTFP.

title: High-Efficiency Multistimuli Responsive Carbon Dots with Near-100% Photoluminescence Quantum Yield for Anticounterfeiting Technologies
summary: Abstract With the rising demand for information security and anticounterfeiting, developing intelligent luminescent materials responsive to external stimuli is crucial for enhancing encryption and anticounterfeiting technologies. Herein, a
content: Abstract With the rising demand for information security and anticounterfeiting, developing intelligent luminescent materials responsive to external stimuli is crucial for enhancing encryption and anticounterfeiting technologies. Herein, a facile one-pot solvothermal strategy was developed to prepare multistimuli responsive carbon dots (CDs), which exhibit solvent-responsive, concentration-responsive, and pH-responsive properties, along with a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) approaching 100% in aqueous dispersion. Systematic investigations reveal that the high PLQY of the CDs originates from the cross-arranged nonextended conjugation of perylene-based backbones in the CDs core, which prevent further π–π stacking. In addition, surface functional groups regulate solvent-dependent luminescence behavior through polar interactions and hydrogen bonding. As the concentration increased, enhanced intermolecular interactions induce the emission from monomer-dominated to aggregate-dominated states. Furthermore, under different pH conditions, reversible protonation and deprotonation of surface functional groups enable dynamic modulation of the electronic structure, thereby regulating the fluorescence emission. By combining with polymers, multicolor high-brightness polymer powders with PLQY approaching 100% were successfully prepared. These composite materials demonstrate excellent performance in handicraft decoration and anticounterfeiting systems. This work not only provides a theoretical basis for the design of highly efficient luminescent CDs but also expands their potential in intelligent materials and photonic applications.

title: Financing Education for Sustainable Development: How Relevant Is the Role of Institutions?
summary: This study examines the effect of government expenditure on education on environmental degradation, proxied by carbon dioxide emissions, across a panel of 17 Sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries from 2005 to 2024. It also examines whether th
content: This study examines the effect of government expenditure on education on environmental degradation, proxied by carbon dioxide emissions, across a panel of 17 Sub-Saharan African (SSA) countries from 2005 to 2024. It also examines whether the institutional environment in SSA influences this relationship. Applying the Lewbel two-stage least squares method to address endogeneity and omitted variable challenges, the study finds that government expenditure on education reduces environmental degradation in SSA, whereas the poor institutional environment increases it. The results further show that the poor institutional environment in SSA reverses the beneficial effect of government expenditure on education on the environment. These findings suggest that policymakers in SSA can rely on government educational finance to promote environmental sustainability; however, efforts should be geared towards strengthening the institutional environment to realise the positive environmental gains of government educational finance.

title: TOURISM, GROWTH, AND INCLUSION IN THE WORLD’S LEADING MUSLIM-FRIENDLY DESTINATIONS
summary: This study examines whether Muslim-friendly tourism is associated with economic growth and whether growth is linked to unemployment and income inequality across the 20 leading destinations in the Global Muslim Travel Index 2024. The study f
content: This study examines whether Muslim-friendly tourism is associated with economic growth and whether growth is linked to unemployment and income inequality across the 20 leading destinations in the Global Muslim Travel Index 2024. The study further explores the indicative role of economic growth as a transmission channel linking tourism performance with socio-economic outcomes. Annual panel data spanning 2010–2024 are analyzed using the Panel Pooled Mean Group Autoregressive Distributed Lag approach to estimate both short-run and long-run relationships among the variables. Additional mediation analysis is conducted to examine the indirect role of economic growth in linking Muslim-friendly tourism with unemployment and income inequality. The findings reveal that Muslim-friendly tourism exhibits a significant positive long-run association with economic growth (θ = 0.5829). Tourism expansion is also negatively associated with unemployment (θ = -0.4273) and income inequality (θ = -0.2154), indicating inclusive development linkages. Economic growth further shows a negative relationship with unemployment (θ = -0.3064) and income inequality (θ = -0.2149), suggesting that growth functions as a transmission channel through which tourism development is linked to socio -economic welfare. In the short run, tourism expansion is positively associated with economic growth, whereas inflation tends to intensify inequality pressures. In addition, foreign direct investment appears to support productive capacity and inclusive economic expansion across Muslim-friendly tourism destinations. The findings suggest that Muslim-friendly tourism is closely associated with inclusive and sustainable development. Tourism expansion, when accompanied by macroeconomic stability and supportive investment conditions, is linked to better employment conditions, lower income concentration, and stronger long-term economic inclusiveness across leading Muslim-friendly tourism destinations.

title: OpenAlex-derived data and code for persistent ties and asymmetric change in China-US low-carbon technology research
summary: This release contains the OpenAlex-derived component of the study "Persistent ties and asymmetric change in low carbon technology research between China and the United States". It includes processed topic-year publication counts, climate an
content: This release contains the OpenAlex-derived component of the study "Persistent ties and asymmetric change in low carbon technology research between China and the United States". It includes processed topic-year publication counts, climate and benchmark topic definitions, matching inputs, parsed public bibliographic identifiers and institutional/author affiliation metadata, partner portfolios, funding-organisation metadata, query provenance, derived analytical outputs, figure source data and Python code. The main climate corpus covers 23 topics and 16,255 China-US joint publications during 2008-2025. Broader topic counts cover 2005-2025; a separate historical snapshot is retained for sensitivity checks. This is a deliberately scoped OpenAlex release, NOT the complete manuscript replication package. OECD patent and OECD/Scopus bibliometric extracts and corresponding numeric outputs are excluded pending dataset-specific redistribution clearance. Figure 6 is not included. The original October 2026 OpenAlex API response cache is unavailable; parsed records and the query manifest are included. Fresh retrieval from OpenAlex may differ from the historical snapshot. No synthetic observations are introduced in this release. The core offline runner operates on the supplied processed inputs; plotting code produces figures 2-5 and 7 plus the graphical abstract from archived outputs. Extended scripts are provided for methodological transparency, but some require excluded OECD inputs or the excluded combined numbers.json and are not part of the runnable public workflow. Observational panel contrasts should not be read as identified causal policy effects; scenario calculations are conditional accounting rather than forecasts or policy targets. Publication and patent measures do not measure realised emissions reductions. Original derived data and documentation are CC BY 4.0; original code is MIT. See README.txt, FILE_CATALOG.csv and licence files for details.

title: Towards a green China: energy policy, technological innovation, and green investment as drivers of environmental sustainability
summary: China’s pursuit of environmental sustainability has become one of the defining policy experiments of the twenty-first century, combining an ambitious dual-carbon pledge with the world’s largest deployment of clean-energy technology and gree
content: China’s pursuit of environmental sustainability has become one of the defining policy experiments of the twenty-first century, combining an ambitious dual-carbon pledge with the world’s largest deployment of clean-energy technology and green capital. This review synthesizes recent scholarship to examine how three interlocking levers, energy and climate policy, technological innovation, and green investment, jointly shape China’s transition toward a lower-carbon and more resilient development path. Drawing on a structured reading of peer-reviewed research published predominantly between 2019 and 2025, the article develops an integrated framework in which policy sets direction and incentives, innovation lowers the cost and expands the frontier of abatement, and investment mobilizes the capital required to translate intent into installed capacity. The evidence indicates that target-based governance, embodied in successive Five-Year Plans and the 2030/2060 carbon commitments, has been reinforced by market-based instruments such as the national emissions trading system, and by an expanding architecture of green credit and green bonds. Technological progress in solar photovoltaics, wind power, batteries, and electric mobility has driven steep learning curves, allowing renewable additions to exceed fossil capacity additions by wide margins in recent years. Green finance is shown across numerous provincial and firm-level studies to reduce carbon-emission intensity, chiefly by catalyzing green technological innovation and by reallocating capital away from pollution-intensive activities. Nevertheless, persistent tensions remain, including coal lock-in, energy-security concerns, uneven regional capacity, intensity-based rather than absolute caps, data-quality risks, and the danger of greenwashing. The review argues that the effectiveness of any single lever is conditional on its coherence with the others, and that spatial spillovers and regional heterogeneity mediate outcomes in ways that generic national narratives obscure. Case evidence is integrated throughout to ground the analysis in concrete provincial, sectoral, and corporate experience. The article closes by identifying priorities for policy design and an agenda for future research on the policy–innovation–investment nexus.

title: Developments in the EU Emissions Trading System and Their Effects on CCU Pathways
summary: ABSTRACT The analysis presented in this article focuses on provisions of the European Union (EU) emissions trading system (ETS) for carbon dioxide that is captured in stationary installations for chemical utilization (CCU). The evolution in
content: ABSTRACT The analysis presented in this article focuses on provisions of the European Union (EU) emissions trading system (ETS) for carbon dioxide that is captured in stationary installations for chemical utilization (CCU). The evolution in EU ETS legislation over more than two decades has led to challenges for CCU pathways with regard to monitoring, reporting, and allowance surrender obligations. This article attempts to trace the development from an engineering perspective. A look ahead suggests that CCU strategies could benefit from the formal expansion of the scope of the EU ETS, which has recently begun to take shape.

title: Determinants of (over)use and de-implementation of low-value infection prevention practices and care procedures that carry infection risks in hospitals: a scoping review
summary: Introduction Infection prevention (IP) practices are critical to patient safety. However, some IP measures or care procedures associated with a risk of infection are used inappropriately or excessively. This overuse can be considered low-va
content: Introduction Infection prevention (IP) practices are critical to patient safety. However, some IP measures or care procedures associated with a risk of infection are used inappropriately or excessively. This overuse can be considered low-value care (LVC) as it contributes to potential negative health outcomes for patients, unnecessary healthcare costs, and environmental strain. This scoping review aims to identify determinants of (over)use and de-implementation of LVC general IP measures and non-surgical care practices linked to infection risk in hospitals. Methods We conducted a scoping review following Arksey and O’Malley methodology. A systematic search was performed in OVID/Medline, Embase.com, Elsevier/Scopus, and Ebsco/CINAHL up to January 29-February 2, 2026. Study selection was supported by the artificial intelligence tool ASReview using the SAFE-procedure. Data was charted using a piloted extraction form including type of study, type of LVC practice, and determinants of (over)use or de-implementation. Determinants were categorized according to Augustsson's de-implementation framework. Results A total of 13,738 records were retrieved of which 57 studies were included. Most included studies were empirical and focused on care procedures with an infection risk ( n = 40), predominantly urinary catheter use ( n = 37). Other studies addressed general IP measures ( n = 17), mainly glove use, sometimes combined with gowns/aprons ( n = 5) with two studies also including isolation practices. Across studies, determinants mainly related to professional-, patient-, and inner-context, and were primarily associated with continued (over)use rather than de-implementation. Many studies described situations of (over)use rather than explicitly probing the underlying motivations driving these behaviors. None of the studies explicitly labeled the examined care practices as LVC, and several did not specify criteria that distinguished appropriate from inappropriate use. Conclusions Current literature on determinants of (over)use and de-implementation in infection prevention focuses predominantly on urinary catheter and glove use, with a strong emphasis on determinants driving (over)use. Systematic study of overuse in infection prevention and subsequent development of effective de-implementation strategies is hindered by studies not clearly defining care practices as LVC. Advancing this field requires more theory informed and context-sensitive approaches to better characterize overuse, identify barriers and facilitators to reduce overuse, and to support the development of targeted de-implementation strategies.

title: Net-carbon intelligent control for water-energy-carbon synergy in wastewater treatment plants - an accelerated digital-twin kernel
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Wastewater treatment plants emit greenhouse gases, yet the official IWA benchmark platform bsm2-python has no process greenhouse-gas model, so water-quality–energy optimisation ignores direct N₂O emissions and can push operation into high-e
content: Wastewater treatment plants emit greenhouse gases, yet the official IWA benchmark platform bsm2-python has no process greenhouse-gas model, so water-quality–energy optimisation ignores direct N₂O emissions and can push operation into high-emission regions. We present an open-source plant-level digital-twin kernel that couples an energy model and an hourly grid-emission-factor module with a two-step nitrification N₂O overlay superimposed on the validated ASM1/Takács model without perturbing its nitrogen balance. The kernel reproduces the official implementation: the three energy terms agree exactly and the effluent quality index differs by 0.54%. Compiled with numba it runs at 16507 steps/s, 18.4 times faster. A 40-day scan of 261 setpoint combinations yields 199 distinct feasible operating points and an 11-point Pareto front; at high nitrate setpoints more aeration lowers the N₂O emission factor from 0.79% to 0.58%.

title: A study of the impact of climate transition risk on the profitability of commercial banks
summary: Abstract Climate transition risk has become an increasingly important challenge for commercial banks during the low-carbon transition process. Using carbon dioxide emissions from six carbon-intensive industries and industry-level bank loan
content: Abstract Climate transition risk has become an increasingly important challenge for commercial banks during the low-carbon transition process. Using carbon dioxide emissions from six carbon-intensive industries and industry-level bank loan data, this study constructs a climate transition risk indicator for Chinese listed commercial banks from 2010 to 2022 and examines its impact on bank profitability. Employing a two-way fixed effects model, heterogeneity analysis, moderating effect tests, and a series of robustness checks, the study finds that climate transition risk significantly reduces bank profitability. The negative effect is more pronounced among state-owned and large commercial banks, while it is relatively weaker for joint-stock banks, regional banks, as well as small and medium-sized banks. Further analysis reveals that bank size and non-performing loan ratios partially mitigate the adverse impact of transition risk on profitability. The findings suggest that banks with high exposure to carbon-intensive industries should strengthen climate-related risk management and gradually optimize their credit structure during the green transition process. The study also provides evidence for regulators to implement differentiated climate finance policies across different types of banks.

title: Precession and meltwater control of greenhouse gas emissions from terrestrial sources during the last glacial period
summary: Abstract. Changing vegetation patterns in response to shifting climate over the last glacial period could explain variations in the long-term global carbon cycle, as recorded in trace greenhouse gas (GHG) concentrations in polar ice-core da
content: Abstract. Changing vegetation patterns in response to shifting climate over the last glacial period could explain variations in the long-term global carbon cycle, as recorded in trace greenhouse gas (GHG) concentrations in polar ice-core data. However, existing geological records provide only fragments of the vegetation cover history, and the evolution of corresponding carbon stocks and fluxes remains uncertain. Using a comprehensive Earth system model we simulate global transient trajectories of the coupled climate–vegetation–carbon system over 130000 years of the late Quaternary, including intervals with interactive marine biogeochemistry and dynamically coupled ice sheets with iceberg calving. Our aim is to understand how vegetation changes may explain orbital and sub-orbital scale variations in the global carbon budget. According to proxy-based evidence and previous modelling applications, we find that the experiments adequately reproduce known patterns. We focus on how natural land cover transitions and productivity changes contribute to simulated terrestrial emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4). We classify the strength of vegetation changes and locate highly dynamic regions, found closely around monsoon margins, which respond strongly to orbital precession on a multi-millennial timescale, as well as to meltwater discharge in the North Atlantic on sub-orbital timescales. Other regions, however, respond mainly to CO2 fertilization. During the strong meltwater pulses of the last deglaciation, in a simulation with interactive marine biogeochemistry, land biosphere changes are capable of causing marked atmospheric CO2 jumps of close to 10 ppmv within several centuries. The simulations together highlight continental regions where interactions between shifting climate and carbon cycle components most likely contributed to GHG variability of the last glacial cycle.

title: Prevalence of Local Emissions in Arctic Carbonaceous Aerosols Revealed by Dual Carbon Isotopes and Atmospheric Transport Modeling
summary: Abstract Carbonaceous aerosols in the Arctic are mainly attributed to long‐range transport from lower latitudes, but direct observational data over the central Arctic Ocean, particularly in summer, remain limited. We present a cruise‐based
content: Abstract Carbonaceous aerosols in the Arctic are mainly attributed to long‐range transport from lower latitudes, but direct observational data over the central Arctic Ocean, particularly in summer, remain limited. We present a cruise‐based study conducted during the eighth Xuelong Arctic expedition across the central Arctic Ocean. Using dual carbon isotope analysis (δ 13 C– Δ 14 C), molecular organic composition, and black carbon (BC)‐atmospheric modeling, we provide quantitative insights into the sources of Arctic marine aerosols. Our findings show significant spatial differences in aerosol composition between the North Pacific and Arctic Ocean. Fossil fuel–derived carbon contributes 55.5 ± 17% (0.49 ± 0.39 μg m −3 ) of total carbon in Arctic summer aerosols. While model simulations closely match BC concentrations outside the Arctic Ocean, they underestimate BC levels in the inner Arctic by a factor of two, suggesting gaps in local source representation. These findings emphasize the need for better representation of local emissions, especially from shipping, in models to improve understanding of aerosol‐driven climate effects in the Arctic.

title: Asymmetric N,O-Centered Stable Diradical Nanoparticles for NIR-II Fluorescence Imaging-Guided Photothermal Tumor Therapy
summary: Abstract Stable organic radicals provide distinctive open-shell platforms for near-infrared fluorescence, but their use in NIR-II fluorescence imaging-guided photothermal therapy remains limited. Herein, we report an asymmetric N,O-centered
content: Abstract Stable organic radicals provide distinctive open-shell platforms for near-infrared fluorescence, but their use in NIR-II fluorescence imaging-guided photothermal therapy remains limited. Herein, we report an asymmetric N,O-centered Blatter−phenoxyl diradical (BP) and its nanoparticle formulation (BP-NPs), a water-dispersible nanoplatform prepared by encapsulating the BP by an amphiphilic polypeptide P(OEGMA)23−PLys15. BP combines the oxygen-centered phenoxy and the nitrogen-centered Blatter radical units in an asymmetric scaffold, distinguishes it from many carbon-centered radical and symmetric diradical systems, and shows an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 0.73%. Variable-temperature 1H NMR, high-resolution mass spectrometry, and variable-temperature EPR spectroscopy were employed to characterize the molecular structure and temperature-dependent open-shell behavior of BP. After encapsulated, the BP-NPs retained broadband visible-to-NIR absorption and NIR-II emission, with an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 0.41% in water. Under 808 nm irradiation, BP-NPs showed good photostability and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 27.3%. In vitro studies reveals that the BP-NPs exhibit low dark cytotoxicity but strong light-induced 4T1 cell killing, while the in vivo NIR-II imaging showed efficient tumor accumulation, with the maximum fluorescence signal and tumor-to-background ratio (TBR ≈ 9.3) observed at approximately 24 h post-injection. Photothermal therapy at this window markedly suppressed the tumor growth without obvious treatment-related body-weight loss during the observation period. This work highlights asymmetric phenoxy−Blatter N,O-centered diradical nanoparticles as promising open-shell platforms for NIR-II imaging-guided photothermal therapy.

title: When Does Transparency Matter for Consumers’ Circular Decisions? Visibility and Traceability in Closed-Loop Supply Chains
summary: Markets are increasingly demanding greater supply chain transparency, yet this remains a significant challenge for many companies. Understanding whether and what type of information to disclose represents a significant challenge for compani
content: Markets are increasingly demanding greater supply chain transparency, yet this remains a significant challenge for many companies. Understanding whether and what type of information to disclose represents a significant challenge for companies, particularly when the information pertains to circular initiatives, such as those involved in closed-loop activities. This study, grounded in signaling theory, explores the effect of disclosing closed-loop supply chain information on consumers' intentions. We selected consumers as our unit of analysis for the active role they can play when referring to companies’ closed-loop initiatives, such as purchasing recycled products or participating in take-back programs. To test the hypotheses, two scenario-based experiments are conducted. The primary aim of the studies is to operationalize supply chain transparency through its visibility and traceability components in a closed-loop supply chain context. A second objective is to examine the effectiveness of transparency in closed-loop supply chains, analyzing how the two components influence consumer outcomes across different phases of the customer journey. The findings contribute to the growing literature on supply chain transparency, identifying the boundaries of signaling theory and offering insights for managers on strategic investments in transparency.

title: Persistent declines in forest‐dependent birds following active restoration of logged tropical forest in Borneo
summary: Abstract Tropical forest restoration is critical for mitigating biodiversity loss and climate change, including in forests impacted by selective logging. Active restoration through liana cutting and enrichment tree planting can substantiall
content: Abstract Tropical forest restoration is critical for mitigating biodiversity loss and climate change, including in forests impacted by selective logging. Active restoration through liana cutting and enrichment tree planting can substantially accelerate carbon recovery, potentially reducing economic pressures to convert logged forests. But its long-term biodiversity impacts remain largely unknown. Using over two decades of bird survey data from Borneo’s largest logged-forest restoration project, we quantified occupancy patterns for 176 species across primary, naturally regenerating, and actively restored logged forests spanning a 30+ year post-logging chronosequence. Forest-dependent, threatened and near-threatened species generally declined through time in actively restored areas, whereas many species in naturally regenerating forests progressively recovered toward primary forest levels. Between 17–40% of 66 threatened or near-threatened species had consistently lower occupancies in actively restored than in naturally regenerating forest. Across species of global conservation concern, median occupancies in restored areas remained ∼22% below primary forest even 50 years after harvests, compared with only ∼6% lower under natural regeneration. Arboreal insectivores, frugivores, and predatory species appeared most negatively affected by active restoration, with 27-49% of arboreal gleaning insectivores (of 62), 13-30% of arboreal frugivores (of 40), and one-third of predatory species (of 15) showing higher occupancy in naturally regenerating forests. Sallying insectivores also showed a possible but uncertain response, whereas ground-associated frugivores and insectivores were largely unaffected by restoration treatment. Concerningly, even 50 years post-logging, up to 52% of 50 high forest-dependency species retained distinct occupancies in actively restored compared with primary forest, suggesting persistent negative impacts of vine-cutting and/or tree planting activities on avian populations. Synthesis and applications . Our findings indicate that despite substantial carbon benefits, active restoration within selectively logged forests may impede the recovery of forest-dependent biodiversity. This challenges the common assumption embedded within nature-based climate solutions that carbon and biodiversity outcomes will necessarily align. Nonetheless, despite the persistent declines in bird communities, actively restored forests continued to provide key habitat for many species. Active interventions may thus still contribute to broader biodiversity conservation objectives if they protect logged areas from conversion, potentially via carbon payments.

title: What’s on the menu? Quantifying the greenhouse gas emissions and water footprint of the food service procurement within elite male & female football teams
summary: Abstract Background: The global food system contributes approximately 34% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) and exerts substantial pressure on freshwater resources, yet the environmental impact of food provision within profes
content: Abstract Background: The global food system contributes approximately 34% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) and exerts substantial pressure on freshwater resources, yet the environmental impact of food provision within professional sport remains unexplored. Addressing this evidence gap, this study quantified the environmental footprint of food service provision across four professional football clubs in England, representing the English Premier League (EPL), English Football League Championship (EFL Champ), English Football League One (EFL L1), and Women’s Super League (WSL). The primary aims were to determine total and relative GHGE, water footprints, and the contribution of individual food categories to each environmental metric. Methods: A seven-day cross-sectional design was employed using reference-standard life cycle assessment methodology via the Nutritics Foodprint Carbon Footprint Functionality . A bottom-up analytical approach assessed 289 individual food and beverage items across 52 categories. Data were analysed descriptively, with comparisons made using 95% confidence limits to preserve interpretive transparency. Results: Marked inter-team variation was observed in relative nutritional provision and environmental impact. The EFL L1 team demonstrated the highest energy (2,272 ± 27 kcal·d⁻¹), carbohydrate (228 ± 3 g·d⁻¹), protein (138 ± 3 g·d⁻¹), and fat (90 ± 2 g·d⁻¹) provision per cover per day, as well as the GHGEs (7.17 ± 0.14 kg·CO₂·eq) and water footprint (6.01 ± 0.11 kL·eq). The EPL, EFL Champ, and WSL teams followed in descending order for both energy and environmental measures. Across all clubs, meat - particularly beef - was the largest contributor to total GHGE (~ 38%) and water footprint (~ 36%), with dairy (~ 16%) and vegetables (~ 18%) representing notable secondary contributors. Beverages, primarily bottled water, accounted for 22% of total GHGE in the EFL L1 team, underscoring how both menu composition and operational practices influence environmental outcomes. Conclusion: This study provides the first evidence that professional football food services differ markedly in their environmental impact, with higher energy and protein provision - particularly from ruminant meat and dairy - driving greater GHGEs and water use. Practical strategies such as moderating overall protein provision, particularly from red meat procurement, while increasing plant-based protein inclusion, and replacing bottled water and dairy with filtered and plant-based alternatives could substantially reduce emissions without compromising performance nutrition. Embedding these actions within FIFA, UEFA, and EPL sustainability frameworks would align football with global climate goals and position the sport as a leader in advancing sustainable nutrition practices.

title: Plasma etch process optimization for photonic-grade diamond-on-insulator substrates and thickness evaluation using colorimetry
summary: Diamond color-center qubits integrated with photonic circuits can be initialized, manipulated, entangled, and read individually with high fidelity, making them attractive for large-scale modular quantum computers, quantum networks, and dist
content: Diamond color-center qubits integrated with photonic circuits can be initialized, manipulated, entangled, and read individually with high fidelity, making them attractive for large-scale modular quantum computers, quantum networks, and distributed quantum sensing. However, the limited size of heteroepitaxially grown single-crystal diamond (SCD) and photonic-grade diamond-on-insulator (DOI) substrates remains a challenge for integration with existing manufacturing processes. Here, we develop a plasma etch recipe to thin direct-bonded (100) SCD membranes (<50 $μ$m) into large-area, thin-film DOI substrates, and demonstrate free-standing photonic chiplets fabricated from the resulting DOI. The ICP-RIE recipe preserves diamond bonding, provides sufficient micromasking and surface-quality control, and enables thin-film DOI manufacture. We thin a 10 $μ$m diamond plate bonded to SiO$_2$/Si and obtain a photonic-grade DOI substrate with diamond thickness $\leq$300 nm. The DOI film is around 300 nm thick over 0.5 $\times$ 0.5 mm$^2$, with surface roughness < 0.5 nm, while the bonding interface remains intact. Diamond photonic chiplets are fabricated on this DOI substrate using a standard two-step lithography process, without complex thin-film transfer, under-etching, or pedestal formation. We also present a colorimetric study of diamond visibility on SiO$_2$ and quantify color differences across thicknesses in common colorimetric spaces. This analysis enables automatic diamond-thickness extrapolation from standard optical microscope images with 5 nm resolution, in good agreement with white-light interferometry (WLI) measurements. The DOI substrate and colorimetric thickness-evaluation method provide an effective fabrication platform and reliable validation route for scalable manufacturing of diamond nanophotonic devices, opening a path toward large-scale integrated quantum systems.

title: Could local climate, forest site and stand conditions mitigate the defoliation in European beech stands? – The case of southern Belgium
summary: Although climate change has been a major factor in the declining health of European beech (Fagus sylvatica L.) stands since the end of the 20th century, it seems that local site and stand conditions may play a key role within the beech’s cl
content: Although climate change has been a major factor in the declining health of European beech (Fagus sylvatica L.) stands since the end of the 20th century, it seems that local site and stand conditions may play a key role within the beech’s climax region by exacerbating or mitigating this phenomenon. In this study, we assessed crown defoliation in 1,515 dominant trees distributed across 101 mature beech stands, located along bioclimatic and ecological gradients in the Ardenne region (southern Belgium) during July and August 2022. A large dataset covering past and present climate, local forest site and stand conditions was analysed using a Random Forest model, combined with a variable selection (VSURF) and interpretated by the Shapley values method. The final model explained 45% of the observed variability in stand defoliation and identified five key drivers. Warmer spring conditions and moderate increases in temperature during the growing season were associated with reduced crown damages, reflecting climate conditions that remained suitable to beech. Local site conditions also modulated the health status of beech: stands located on well-drained plateaus and soils with a high available water capacity showed lower defoliation, while the presence of waterlogged or shallow soils increased damage level. The stand structure also played an important role, as higher canopy density limited crown damages, probably due to a buffering effect on the forest understorey’s microclimate. These results provided practical guidance for adaptive forest management aimed at increasing the resilience of beech forests to current climate change.

title: Pectinase-Based Bioprocesses for Circular Bioeconomy and Sustainable Industrial Development.
summary: Pectinases play a vital role in the degradation of pectic part of the plant cell wall and are considered in the group of hydrolytic enzymes. In the present scenario, demand of economically feasible and environment friendly techniques and ap
content: Pectinases play a vital role in the degradation of pectic part of the plant cell wall and are considered in the group of hydrolytic enzymes. In the present scenario, demand of economically feasible and environment friendly techniques and approaches has significantly led the research on the microbial production, standardization of process parameters and improvements of pectinases. The development of pectinase-based bioprocesses has been found to promote sustainable industrial practices by reducing the use of chemicals, energy, and waste, thereby supporting eco-friendly production systems. The unique aspect of this review is that it explains traditional methods of pectinase production alongside novel methods, which include solid-state and submerged fermentation, recombinant DNA techniques, heterologous gene expression, protein engineering, CRISPR/Cas genome editing technologies, enzyme immobilization, and nanobiotechnological methods, which improve the production, stability, and performance of pectinases. It further demonstrates the increasing importance of the use of pectinases in sustainable manufacturing through decreasing the use of chemicals and energy, as well as reducing waste production from industry. It illustrates that innovations in microbial strain engineering, process optimization, and utilization of low-cost substrates have significantly increased the economic viability and efficiency of producing pectinases. Yet, some issues associated with commercialization, standardization of production processes, recovery, and stability of enzymes still exist. Overall, this review paper gives an overview of the recent advancements and limitations of next-generation pectinases.

title: Management rather than climate and biodiversity shapes long-term delta15N dynamics in grassland soils
summary: The bulk soil δ 15 N signature in grassland soils serves as a fingerprint of nitrogen inputs, turnover and losses, reflecting the influence of land management, climate, plant biodiversity and abiotic soil properties.Although natural abundan
content: The bulk soil δ 15 N signature in grassland soils serves as a fingerprint of nitrogen inputs, turnover and losses, reflecting the influence of land management, climate, plant biodiversity and abiotic soil properties.Although natural abundance δ 15 N has been proposed as an indicator for these factors, previous studies yielded mixed results regarding the importance of its drivers.In this study, we quantified changes in soil δ 15 N across 72 German grassland sites after 12 years (2011 vs. 2023) and analysed relationships with detailed records of land use intensity, plant biodiversity, climate, and soil properties.Land use intensity was quantified on a continuous scale based on mowing, grazing and fertilisation.In the top 10 cm of soil, δ 15 N changes ranged from -0.86 to + 2.49‰, equating to an average increase of + 0.35‰ per decade.Over two-thirds of our study sites showed a long-term increase in δ 15 N associated with high land use intensity.Our findings indicate that fertiliser application and grazing are the dominant drivers of δ 15 N increases, while a biodiversity-mediated decrease via reduced N losses was not observed.The slow decadal-scale shifts suggest that single soil δ 15 N measurements without known initial values are only informative for long-term management processes and not for assessing recent management impacts.

title: Sustainable Non-Sterile Glove Use for Injections: A Scoping Review of Practices, Attitudes, and Behavioural Drivers
summary: Abstract Background Inappropriate non-sterile glove use presents patient and healthcare worker safety risks and contributes to healthcare waste and emissions. Existing guidelines suggest gloves are not routinely required for intramuscular a
content: Abstract Background Inappropriate non-sterile glove use presents patient and healthcare worker safety risks and contributes to healthcare waste and emissions. Existing guidelines suggest gloves are not routinely required for intramuscular and subcutaneous injections however practices may vary. This review aims to describe the practices and attitudes of nurses and midwives regarding glove use during injections. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Bibliographic databases (MEDLINE and CINAHL), Google Scholar and expert-identified grey literature were searched. Data extracted included evidence type, setting and location, glove use practices and attitudes, and information on related concepts including hand hygiene, risk assessment, sharps safety, and sustainability. Data were synthesised and mapped to the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation-Behaviour framework. Results A total of 31 articles from 9 countries were eligible and included primary research, clinical guidelines, educational resources and editorials. Research demonstrated substantial practice variation and provided evidence that glove use during injections contributed to poorer hand hygiene and cross-contamination. Guidelines stated that gloves were not routinely required, while educational resources presented mixed messages. Identified behavioural drivers of glove use were an understanding of infection prevention principles (capability), social and professional context (opportunity), and perceived safety (motivation). Conclusion Practice variation is common and may arise from misalignment between policy, education, and professional attitudes. Understanding behavioural drivers can inform the development of clear and consistent resources to support sustainable and safe glove use for injections based on risk assessment.

title: Antileishmanial and antimalarial activities of synthetic marine endoperoxides
summary: Synthetic samples and analogs of marine endoperoxides derived from mycaperoxides and plakortides were screened for their antileishmanial and antimalarial activities. It was found that these compounds exhibited significant activity against b
content: Synthetic samples and analogs of marine endoperoxides derived from mycaperoxides and plakortides were screened for their antileishmanial and antimalarial activities. It was found that these compounds exhibited significant activity against both parasites in the micromolar range. However, mycaperoxide analogs also exhibited high cytotoxicity against both cancer and healthy mammalian cell lines in the micromolar range. By contrast, ethyl plakortide Z showed minimal to no cytotoxic activity, leading to interesting potential against P. falciparum (IC50 = 2.90 ± 1.13 µM, SI > 62) and L. major (IC50 = 16.87 ± 2.04 µM, SI > 5.9). The specific cytotoxicities of mycaperoxides might be attributed to the carboxylic acid functional group, which is absent in ethyl plakortide Z.

title: Monitoring and evaluating the just transition : reflections on a theory of change for Scotland, with lessons for beyond
source: Strathprints: The University of Strathclyde institutional repository (University of Strathclyde)
summary: Just Transitions policies are gaining pace worldwide including a range of national, sub-national and sectoral Just Transition plans, with Scotland as a leading voice. The Scottish Government continue to develop a raft of strategic and polic
content: Just Transitions policies are gaining pace worldwide including a range of national, sub-national and sectoral Just Transition plans, with Scotland as a leading voice. The Scottish Government continue to develop a raft of strategic and policy responses to Just Transition. In the absence of finalised and fully funded plans, such as the final Energy Strategy and Just Transition plan, however, the Scottish Just Transition is largely positioned within a policy framework that is not yet fully functional or operational. Moreover, the Scottish Government is grappling with establishing operationalizable Just Transition monitoring and evaluation approaches. This reflects a core challenge in the literature: whilst the conceptual origins and framework for a Just Transition are well-accounted for and many empirical case studies exist, very few contributions set out how to determine whether Just Transition policy is being effective, if at all; approaches are unproven; data is complex, partial and overlapping, and what constitutes a Just Transition is contested. Reporting on mixed-methods research conducted alongside the Scottish Just Transition Commission, this paper begins to fill this gap with specific, measurable outcomes for the Scottish Just Transition. In so doing, we provide a Theory of Change framework for upcoming national, sectoral, and regional plans and evaluations. As core contributions, we justify the necessity of this conceptually, give context to the Scottish case, set out an approach relevant to other contexts, and, in reflecting on planned versus actual impacts, share experiential learnings for other researchers and practitioners developing and operationalizing monitoring and evaluation approaches.

title: When Embodied AI Infers Too Much
summary: As embodied AI systems enter homes, hospitals, and public spaces, they introduce a new class of privacy risks—not by recording more, but by inferring more. Drawing on modalities such as thermal imaging, radio-frequency sensing, chemical ana
content: As embodied AI systems enter homes, hospitals, and public spaces, they introduce a new class of privacy risks—not by recording more, but by inferring more. Drawing on modalities such as thermal imaging, radio-frequency sensing, chemical analysis, and pressure mapping, these systems can construct rich behavioural and physiological models of individuals, often without explicit user awareness or consent. While each signal may appear innocuous in isolation, sensor fusion can enable powerful inferences about health, habits, and emotional states.
