This article examines how current legal frameworks only partially address this shift from observation to inference, and explores how sensor design, regulatory oversight, and user-facing transparency can mitigate the risks. We argue that safeguarding privacy in the age of embodied AI requires recognising inference itself as a site of regulation and design—before silent insights become structural intrusions.

title: Technology Focus: Flow Assurance (November 2026)
summary: Digital frameworks and autonomous operations are transforming the future of flow assurance. Recent developments in flow assurance feature three core trends: infrastructure optimization for decarbonization, autonomous well interventions, and
content: Digital frameworks and autonomous operations are transforming the future of flow assurance. Recent developments in flow assurance feature three core trends: infrastructure optimization for decarbonization, autonomous well interventions, and hybrid modeling. The industry encounters persistent challenges regarding uncertainties in multiphase flow measurement, pipeline integrity for CO2 under transient conditions, and scale management in deepwater environments. Overcoming these limitations necessitates a transition from reactive empirical correlations to proactive digital frameworks and autonomous operations. Paper SPE 225871 details a real-time process twin for a large-scale network for carbon capture and storage. By forecasting critical thermodynamic parameters, continuous surveillance allows operators to optimize the transport of dense-phase CO2 and prevent accelerated corrosion during unplanned shutdowns. Paper OTC 36149 presents an autonomous methodology for the chemical treatment of inorganic scale in ultradeepwater carbonate reservoirs. Using existing completion rig infrastructure instead of conventional stimulation vessels reduces operational costs, logistical complexity, and the emission of carbon equivalents. Paper SPE 228033 introduces a neural network constrained by fundamental physical laws to solve Navier-Stokes equations for multiphase flow measurement. Embedding mass and momentum conservation directly into the training process improves prediction accuracy across varying flow regimes and minimizes reliance on empirical calibration.

title: Dampak Kesulitan Keuangan terhadap Indikasi Praktik Greenwashing: Analisis Peran Mediasi Inovasi Hijau
summary: Greenwashing has become a critical issue in corporate sustainability implementation; however, research on the impact of financial distress on greenwashing remains limited and yields inconsistent results. This study addresses this gap by exa
content: Greenwashing has become a critical issue in corporate sustainability implementation; however, research on the impact of financial distress on greenwashing remains limited and yields inconsistent results. This study addresses this gap by examining the role of green innovation as a mediating variable in the relationship between financial distress and greenwashing, drawing upon legitimacy theory and stakeholder theory. The study focuses on energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2020 to 2024, utilizing a sample of 87 companies (comprising 267 observations after outlier removal). Secondary data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and path analysis. The results indicate that financial distress has no significant effect on either greenwashing indications or green innovation. Similarly, green innovation does not significantly affect greenwashing indications. Conversely, firm size was found to have a significant positive effect on greenwashing indications. These findings suggest that financial distress does not influence corporate greenwashing practices, and green innovation does not mediate the relationship between financial distress and greenwashing

title: PENGUATAN PRODUKTIVITAS EKOSISTEM MANGROVE PANGLIMA BULANG TANJUNGPINANG MELALUI REHABILITASI, EDUKASI, DAN BIMBINGAN KELEMBAGAAN
summary: Kawasan Mangrove Panglima Bulang di Kota Tanjungpinang berfungsi sebagai pelindung pantai, habitat biota, penyangga kualitas perairan, serta ruang potensial bagi pembelajaran lingkungan dan ekowisata berbasis masyarakat. Namun, pengelolaan
content: Kawasan Mangrove Panglima Bulang di Kota Tanjungpinang berfungsi sebagai pelindung pantai, habitat biota, penyangga kualitas perairan, serta ruang potensial bagi pembelajaran lingkungan dan ekowisata berbasis masyarakat. Namun, pengelolaan kawasan masih menghadapi persoalan berupa pemeliharaan pascatanam yang belum terjadwal, pencatatan rehabilitasi yang terbatas, belum tersusunnya standar edukasi pengunjung, serta penguatan kelembagaan Pokdarwis yang masih diperlukan. Kegiatan ini bertujuan memperkuat produktivitas layanan ekosistem melalui rehabilitasi berbasis data, edukasi partisipatif, dan bimbingan kelembagaan. Pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan partisipatif-kolaboratif melalui sosialisasi, Focus Group Discussion (FGD), pemetaan kebutuhan, penyampaian materi, diskusi terarah, serta evaluasi pengetahuan menggunakan pre-test dan post-test. FGD mempertemukan Pokdarwis, pemerintah kelurahan, masyarakat, pemuda, mahasiswa, dan praktisi konservasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan terbentuknya pemahaman bersama bahwa keberhasilan rehabilitasi perlu didahului oleh pemilihan lokasi yang sesuai, pemeliharaan, penyulaman, dan monitoring. Layanan edukasi membutuhkan narasi interpretasi, aturan keselamatan, kebersihan, dan pemandu lokal, sedangkan keberlanjutan memerlukan pembagian tugas, SOP, logbook, rencana kerja, dan jejaring kemitraan. Evaluasi 18 lembar pada masing-masing pengukuran menunjukkan rerata pre-test 95,56% dan post-test 87,78%; post-test tetap didominasi oleh skor tinggi, tetapi heterogen pada sebagian kecil peserta sehingga pendampingan berulang tetap diperlukan. Kegiatan menghasilkan Paket Tata Kelola Layanan Ekosistem Mangrove Panglima Bulang yang mengintegrasikan rehabilitasi, edukasi, monitoring, dan kelembagaan sebagai dasar pengelolaan berkelanjutan.

title: How Green Policy and Investment Drive Sustainable Transport Infrastructure Development in Iraq
source: Journal of Engineering and Sustainable Development
summary: Developing sustainable transport infrastructure is a critical challenge in emerging economies. This study examines how green transport policy effectiveness and investment in green transport infrastructure contribute to sustainable transport
content: Developing sustainable transport infrastructure is a critical challenge in emerging economies. This study examines how green transport policy effectiveness and investment in green transport infrastructure contribute to sustainable transport infrastructure development in Iraq through environmentally sustainable practices and technological advancements in transport. Data were collected from 272 transport managers, engineers, and sector experts and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Statistical tests of reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, model fit, predictive relevance, and hypothesis testing were applied. Findings indicate that green transport policy effectiveness and investment significantly enhance environmentally sustainable practices, which subsequently promote technological advancement in transport. Both environmentally sustainable practices and technological advancements were found to positively influence sustainable transport infrastructure development. The results further support significant sequential mediation effects, demonstrating that environmentally sustainable practices and technological advancements jointly transmit the effects of policy effectiveness and investment on sustainable infrastructure outcomes. In addition, digital infrastructure readiness strengthens the relationship between technological advancement and sustainable transportation infrastructure development. This study contributes to the sustainable transportation literature by validating a comprehensive mediated–moderated framework in an emerging economy and providing practical guidance for aligning policy initiatives, investment decisions, and technological innovation to achieve sustainable transport development

title: Integrated planning of casualty transportation and medical supply distribution in the post‐disaster relief network: a Q‐learning‐based multi‐objective robust optimization approach
summary: Abstract In recent years, natural disasters have become more frequent and destructive, causing major infrastructure damage and significant loss of life. The unpredictable number of casualties and their rapidly changing conditions after a di
content: Abstract In recent years, natural disasters have become more frequent and destructive, causing major infrastructure damage and significant loss of life. The unpredictable number of casualties and their rapidly changing conditions after a disaster pose significant challenges to the post‐disaster relief efforts. Considering the uncertain number and dynamic condition of the casualties, we investigate an integrated relief planning problem of emergency facility locations, casualty transportation routes, and medical supplies distribution. A robust optimization approach is employed, and the concept of dynamic casualty death probability resulting from the treatment delays is introduced. Then, a tri‐objective optimization model is formulated to minimize the casualty death probability, the latest arrival time of medical supplies, and the total operational costs. To solve the model, a multi‐objective particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed, which is enhanced with Q‐learning to guide the search direction by dynamically adjusting the inertia weights. Moreover, a local search mechanism is incorporated to improve the population diversity, resulting in a Q‐learning‐based multi‐objective particle swarm optimization algorithm with local search. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated through a set of numerical experiments. A case study of the Yushu Earthquake further demonstrates the model's practical applicability.

title: Using building management system data to reduce energy use and improve maintenance visibility in acute hospitals: a review, national data analysis and practical framework for NHS estates
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Acute hospitals are among the most energy-intensive public buildings, and most already have a building management system (BMS) whose data are used mainly for basic control and alarms. This paper reviews evidence on using BMS data to reduce
content: Acute hospitals are among the most energy-intensive public buildings, and most already have a building management system (BMS) whose data are used mainly for basic control and alarms. This paper reviews evidence on using BMS data to reduce energy use and improve the visibility of maintenance needs in hospitals, and analyses national Estates Returns Information Collection (ERIC) data for English acute trusts from 2023/24 to 2025/26. Acute trusts used 10.07 TWh in 2025/26, 76% of it as heat. Energy intensity across 215 general acute hospital sites varied almost twofold between the 10th and 90th percentiles (310–591 kWh/m²) and was not associated with estate age (Spearman ρ = 0.04, p = 0.60). Studies in commercial buildings report median savings of 3% from energy information systems and 9% from fault detection and diagnostics; applied to acute trusts, these rates suggest 0.30–0.91 TWh, £32–95 million and 55–165 kt CO2e a year. Hospital evidence centres on operating theatre ventilation setback, and evidence linking BMS data to maintenance management is limited. A six-stage framework is proposed covering data checks, schedule optimisation within HTM 03-01, alarm rationalisation, fault-to-work-order links and verification. Evaluation in NHS hospitals is needed.

title: Elevated atmospheric CO2 reshapes soil metal(loid) mobility and stress responses in Enchytraeus crypticus: a multi-level analysis from molecular to population endpoints
summary: Projected increases in atmospheric CO 2 may alter soil properties and modify the ecotoxicity of metal(loid)-contaminated soils, yet their combined effects on invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study evaluated how elevated atmosphe
content: Projected increases in atmospheric CO 2 may alter soil properties and modify the ecotoxicity of metal(loid)-contaminated soils, yet their combined effects on invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study evaluated how elevated atmospheric CO 2 (600–1000 ppm), encompassing levels projected under future IPCC scenarios by 2100, influences soil physicochemistry, metal(loid) availability, and the biological responses of Enchytraeus crypticus in control and metal(loid)-contaminated soils, relative to standard CO 2 conditions (400–500 ppm). A multi-level approach integrated soil parameters, metal(loid) bioaccumulation, molecular and biochemical responses, and survival and reproduction following 2- and 21-d exposures. Elevated CO 2 was associated with higher soil pH and element-specific shifts in metal(loid) mobility, particularly higher water-extractable Pb and Zn after 2 d. In contaminated soil, higher water-extractable Pb under elevated CO 2 was accompanied by higher body Pb, reaching significance at 1000 ppm CO 2 . Elevated CO 2 was also associated with lower total RNA content, higher MT1 and CAT1 expression at 1000 ppm CO 2 , and lower Hsp70 expression, while ETS activity showed limited variation and lipid peroxidation remained stable. Adult survival remained high across CO 2 conditions, whereas reproduction was strongly constrained by soil contamination. In control soil, juvenile production was lower at 600 ppm CO 2 than under standard conditions, but not at 800 or 1000 ppm, indicating no consistent concentration-dependent reproductive response. Overall, elevated atmospheric CO 2 modified soil metal(loid) mobility and elicited pathway-specific molecular and biochemical responses without a consistent effect on population-level endpoints. These findings highlight the importance of considering climate-driven changes in contaminant exposure and biological responses under future atmospheric conditions.

title: Green Investment, Environmental, Social and Governance Disclosures, and Corporate Social Responsibility: The Case of Nigerian Companies
source: International Review of Management and Marketing
summary: Existing research provides little evidence that investments with an environmental focus promote better corporate social responsibility (CSR) practices or are simply symbolic actions in weak institutional environments. Hence, this study inve
content: Existing research provides little evidence that investments with an environmental focus promote better corporate social responsibility (CSR) practices or are simply symbolic actions in weak institutional environments. Hence, this study investigated the effect of green investment and ESG disclosures on the CSR performance of listed companies in Nigeria. The research was grounded in stakeholder and institutional theories to explain the relationship between environmentally driven investments and corporate social outcomes. Secondary data was collected from annual reports of selected listed companies for ten years and analysed using the Feasible Generalised Least Squares (FGLS) and Driscoll-Kraay Standard Error (DKSE) estimation techniques. The findings revealed that green investment has a positive and significant impact on CSR practices (Z = 4.849, p < 0.01). This implies that companies with higher green investment practices have more participation in environmental protection, community development, and responsible governance. The results also suggested that supporting factors such as green capital expenditure, ESG initiatives, green technological innovation, and carbon emission reduction efforts have an influence on the success of green investment. The study found that green investment improves CSR performance; however, its effect may be reduced to a legitimacy tool where institutional structures are weak. The research indicates that policymakers should tighten sustainability regulations and foster transparent ESG reporting. At the same time, companies should connect green investment to long-term environmental and social strategies to achieve meaningful CSR outcomes.

title: Parasocial Interaction and Perceived Value as Determinants of Intention to Buy Made-in-Thailand Products through Live- Streaming Personal Shoppers
source: International Review of Management and Marketing
summary: This research investigates the rising trend of live shopping and jasa titipan (jastip) in Southeast Asian digital commerce, focusing on the growing popularity of Made in Thailand products among Indonesian consumers. Livestream commerce has
content: This research investigates the rising trend of live shopping and jasa titipan (jastip) in Southeast Asian digital commerce, focusing on the growing popularity of Made in Thailand products among Indonesian consumers. Livestream commerce has changed consumer behaviour by offering immediacy, interactivity, and immersive digital experiences that lessen psychological distance between sellers and buyers. In Indonesia, live personal shopper sessions have become a key method for cross-border purchases of Thai cosmetics, fashion items, herbal supplements, and packaged foods, which are widely viewed as authentic and high-quality. Despite the market's rapid growth, previous research has mostly examined individual aspects like interactivity, trust, or entertainment, with limited attention to understanding the combined psychological factors influencing purchase intentions in livestream shopping. This study develops and tests a structural equation model (SEM) that includes social presence, parasocial interaction, perceived trust, perceived value, and perceived enjoyment to explain Indonesian consumers’ willingness to buy Thai products via live personal shoppers. The model captures both utilitarian and hedonic evaluation aspects, showing how relational bonding, immediacy, credibility cues, and experiential enjoyment collectively reduce uncertainty in cross-border transactions. This work contributes to theory by providing a comprehensive framework for understanding purchase intention formation in livestream commerce. Practically, the findings suggest strategic approaches for personal shoppers and digital platforms to enhance credibility and build consumer trust. Additionally, the study supports SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) through sustainable digital trade and inclusive economic participation.

title: Modelagem de Dados para Descarbonização Industrial: Um Framework de Indicadores Ambientais
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A descarbonização industrial constitui um desafio técnico e gerencial que exige integração entre dados operacionais, governança informacional e decisões orientadas por evidências.Este artigo propõe um framework de modelagem avançada de dado
content: A descarbonização industrial constitui um desafio técnico e gerencial que exige integração entre dados operacionais, governança informacional e decisões orientadas por evidências.Este artigo propõe um framework de modelagem avançada de dados para estruturar indicadores intrafábrica associados ao consumo energético, ao consumo hídrico e à geração de resíduos, convertendo registros operacionais dispersos em diretrizes quantitativas para apoio à redução da pegada de carbono.A pesquisa caracteriza-se como aplicada, exploratória e descritiva, com abordagem quali-quantitativa, combinando revisão bibliográfica sistematizada, modelagem relacional de dados e aplicação empírica em contexto industrial automotivo.Os resultados indicam que a arquitetura proposta amplia a visibilidade operacional, qualifica a rastreabilidade dos indicadores ambientais, favorece a governança de dados e sustenta estimativa preliminar de redução de 5,46% nas emissões operacionais de CO2 equivalente.Conclui-se que a modelagem de dados, quando articulada a práticas de Engenharia de Produção, ecoeficiência e tecnologias associadas à Indústria 4.0, constitui infraestrutura analítica relevante para a transição sustentável de sistemas produtivos.

title: Strategies for R&D investment in chemical companies to achieve Net-Zero
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: Achieving net-zero emissions in intensive sectors requires not only technological solutions, but also strategic reconfiguration of corporate innovation efforts under conditions of uncertainties.This study examines how chemical companies mob
content: Achieving net-zero emissions in intensive sectors requires not only technological solutions, but also strategic reconfiguration of corporate innovation efforts under conditions of uncertainties.This study examines how chemical companies mobilize research and development (R&D) investments in response to decarbonization challenges, considering differences in organizational maturity.Using qualitative data from the Carbon Disclosure Project and applying thematic analysis, the study develops a typology of R&D investment strategies in the chemical industry.Six clusters of meaning were identified and aggregated into three strategies: reactive behaviours, organizational capability building, and innovative transformation.The findings show that these strategies are distributed across maturity levels, generating asymmetric innovation dynamics within the sector.While a limited group of firms integrates R&D into core values and invests in transformative technologies, most remain anchored in reactive or incremental regimes.By linking firm-level innovation strategies to system-level transition dynamics, this study offers a diagnostic framework to assess why decarbonization efforts in hard-to-abate industries progress unevenly and remain misaligned with net-zero objectives.

title: Urban and peri-urban agriculture in the Global South: Nexus and policies to reduce territorial inequalities and improve social welfare
summary: In the Global South, rapid urbanization intensifies pressures on natural resources, food security, and social equity, progressively displacing agriculture toward vulnerable peri-urban areas. Urban and peri-urban agriculture (UPA) has emerge
content: In the Global South, rapid urbanization intensifies pressures on natural resources, food security, and social equity, progressively displacing agriculture toward vulnerable peri-urban areas. Urban and peri-urban agriculture (UPA) has emerged as a strategic approach not only for food production but also for strengthening social cohesion, climate resilience, and territorial integration. Despite growing relevance, the literature lacks systematic understanding of how Nexus frameworks are operationalized in UPA research and how they inform inclusive policy design. This study aims to systematically review UPA-Nexus research to identify emerging trends, regional patterns, governance arrangements, and policy pathways for reducing territorial inequalities in the Global South. Following the PRISMA protocol, a systematic literature review was conducted in the Scopus database (2017–2024) using Boolean operators related to UPA and Nexus frameworks. Of 92 identified documents, 49 met inclusion criteria (peer-reviewed, open-access, English-language, explicit UPA-Nexus focus). Data were systematically extracted on Nexus categories, territorial scope, governance arrangements, implementation scale, and reported outcomes. An inductive thematic analysis identified patterns and gaps across the reviewed literature. The review reveals three major contributions. First, we identify 17 distinct Nexus categories—demonstrating substantial conceptual diversification beyond the traditional Water-Energy-Food (WEF) Nexus, with emerging frameworks incorporating health, waste, climate, and social dimensions. Second, comparative analysis shows a marked regional divergence: Global North research emphasizes technological efficiency, optimization, and participatory innovation, while Global South literature addresses structural constraints, subsistence strategies, and institutional fragmentation, with studies concentrated in Africa, Asia, and Iran. Third, the analysis identifies critical governance gaps: despite policy recognition, implementation remains fragmented, with regulatory instruments ranking most effective yet predominantly locally focused, limiting territorial integration. UPA-Nexus approaches can reduce territorial inequalities when supported by enabling institutional frameworks, participatory governance, and context-sensitive policies. The review advances a conceptual framework integrating Nexus configurations, territorial dynamics, and institutional arrangements to inform integrated policy design. Findings highlight the need for strengthened institutional coordination, secure land tenure, and inclusive governance mechanisms to realize UPA's potential for advancing the SDGs in the Global South.

title: An Ecosystem Perspective to Manage Scope 3 GHG Emissions: Evidence from the Manufacturing Sector
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: Mitigating scope 3 emissions is a systemic challenge, yet current OSCM literature remains trapped in technocratic and dyadic paradigms.To bridge this orchestration void, this study adopts the 'ecosystem-as-structure' lens to investigate how
content: Mitigating scope 3 emissions is a systemic challenge, yet current OSCM literature remains trapped in technocratic and dyadic paradigms.To bridge this orchestration void, this study adopts the 'ecosystem-as-structure' lens to investigate how 969 global manufacturing firms align multilateral partners.Analysing CDP disclosures, we reveal that focal firms must evolve into 'Ecosystem Strategy Architects'.By building partner capacity, balancing regulatory governance with financial incentives, and proactively instrumentalising transparency and alliances, these firms dictate the institutional rules of the net zero transition.This paper provides an architectural blueprint for collaboratively constructing sustainable value beyond hierarchical control.

title: SUEWS validation and SUMO queue-dissipation calibration
summary: Road-transport electrification is widely recognized as central to sustainable urban transport transitions. Fifty cities worldwide were selected to cover diverse economic levels, climates, traffic volumes and grid carbon intensities. A multi
content: Road-transport electrification is widely recognized as central to sustainable urban transport transitions. Fifty cities worldwide were selected to cover diverse economic levels, climates, traffic volumes and grid carbon intensities. A multidimensional framework was developed to assess road-transport carbon dioxide-equivalent (CO2e) emissions, urban air temperature, traffic noise, energy consumption and operational efficiency. Differences in urban environmental benefits were compared across five electrification rates: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%. In these controlled scenarios, ICEVs were proportionally replaced by BEVs while traffic demand and road-network structure were held constant. Comparisons were also conducted using observed 2025 BEV shares and projected 2050 shares. Under the controlled full-electrification scenario, the model estimates average reductions of 45.8% in road-transport CO2e emissions, 0.74 °C in near-surface air temperature, 2.91 dB(A) in traffic-noise source levels, and 70.1% in final energy consumption, alongside a 1.06 km h-1 (2.42%) increase in network-wide average operating speed. Variation in urban environmental benefits was driven by grid carbon intensity, vehicle stock, vehicle type, annual energy consumption level and road density. Differences in economic development shaped electrification trajectories, grid carbon intensity and the scale of traffic activity. As a result, higher environmental benefits from road-transport electrification were generally obtained by high-income cities.

title: BIOINOCULANTS OF AZOTOBACTER VINELANDII NBIMCC 1619 - PHYSIOLOGICAL, KINETIC, AND TECHNOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS
source: Journal of Chemical Technology and Metallurgy
summary: Considerable attention is now being paid to environmentally friendly agricultural practices that reduce reliance on chemical inputs while maintaining high crop productivity and preserving soil health. Among the most promising sustainable ap
content: Considerable attention is now being paid to environmentally friendly agricultural practices that reduce reliance on chemical inputs while maintaining high crop productivity and preserving soil health. Among the most promising sustainable approaches is the use of plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR), which are essential components of sustainable agriculture and integrated nutrition management practices. Among them, bacteria of the genus Azotobacter have attracted scientific and commercial interest because they combine efficient atmospheric N2 fixation with numerous plant growth-promoting (PGP) properties.The present study focuses on Azotobacter vinelandii NBIMCC 1619 PGP characteristics and the formulation of a bioinoculant preparation. A systematic fermentation and processing strategy was developed under controlled conditions to address the key challenges of producing effective N2-fixing PGPR bioinoculants. The biochemical profile of the strain revealed simultaneous expression of N2 fixation, phytohormone biosynthesis, siderophore production, phosphate solubilization, and extracellular enzyme production. An optimization process resulted in the development of a nutritionally balanced, agriculturally relevant N-free medium and a cultivation regime with DO2 of 30 %, a temperature of 29°C, and a pH of 7.1. A fed-batch strategy of continuous substrate feeding over a 12 h period was implemented to result in high biomass production and N2-fixing performance of the bioinoculant. Its stability at 4°C and in freeze-dried form with cryoprotection was proved. Thus, the physiological, kinetic, and technological characteristics of A. vinelandii NBIMCC 1619 demonstrate its potential for large-scale production under economically satisfactory conditions as a bioinoculant to increase crop productivity.

title: White matter damage across frontal–subcortical circuits in carbon monoxide intoxication: Insights from fixel-based analysis
summary: Background Carbon monoxide intoxication (COI) can cause white matter damage through neurotoxic effects. This study investigated these abnormalities within frontal–subcortical circuits and their association with cognitive impairment. Methods
content: Background Carbon monoxide intoxication (COI) can cause white matter damage through neurotoxic effects. This study investigated these abnormalities within frontal–subcortical circuits and their association with cognitive impairment. Methods 91 COI patients at chronic stage and 20 heathy controls were enrolled. Patients were divided into 3 severity groups (normal cognition; mild cognitive impairment, MCI; and dementia). Voxel-based morphometry and fixel-based analysis were evaluated between patients, as well as across different severity subgroups, and healthy controls. Regression analysis was conducted between the fixel derived metrics and the cognitive composite scores. Significance was set as family-wise error-corrected p < 0.05. Results White matter damage can be detected across frontal–subcortical circuits at chronic stage of CO intoxication. Compared with healthy controls, damage in COI patients with normal cognition can be found in the cingulum even without significant grey matter lesion. The COI-MCI group showed sporadically localized white matter abnormalities in motor, dorsolateral prefrontal and anterior cingulate circuits, whereas the COI-Dementia group demonstrated deficits involving multiple major white matter tracts, including the anterior limb of the internal capsule and anterior thalamic radiation, as well as basal ganglia, temporal and occipital lobes. Reduced fixel derived metrics in periventricular and frontal bundles, including the internal capsule, superior corona radiata and cingulum were highly correlated with cognitive performance in executive function (Pearson's r up to 0.674). Conclusions Damage in the frontal–subcortical circuits can be found in patients with carbon monoxide intoxication, which was correlated to the severity in the affected cognitive domains.

title: A COMPARATIVE NARRATIVE REVIEW OF GEOLOGICAL RISK ASSESSMENT OF HYDROGEN AND CO2 IN DEPLETED RESERVOIRS IN THE UNITED STATES
source: Magna Scientia Advanced Research and Reviews
summary: Depleted oil and gas reservoirs are increasingly considered for carbon dioxide (CO2) sequestration and large-scale hydrogen (H2) storage, due to their established geological characterization, infrastructure, and capacity to retain hydrocarb
content: Depleted oil and gas reservoirs are increasingly considered for carbon dioxide (CO2) sequestration and large-scale hydrogen (H2) storage, due to their established geological characterization, infrastructure, and capacity to retain hydrocarbons. However, storage strategies developed for CO2 are being applied to H2 without sufficient accounting for their physical, geochemical, and microbiological behaviors. This creates uncertainty about whether depleted U.S reservoirs can safely support both decarbonization pathways. A narrative comparative review was conducted to synthesize evidence on fluid behavior, trapping mechanisms, reservoir suitability, risk factors, and monitoring for both gases. Covering fluid behavior, trapping mechanisms, reservoir suitability, risk factors, and monitoring for both gases. The findings show that H₂ is considerably less dense and more diffusive than supercritical CO₂, making it more buoyant, prone to migration through microfractures and legacy wells. Unlike CO₂, which can utilize multiple trapping mechanisms, H₂ primarily remains in the gas phase and depends heavily on structural containment. Its storage performance may also be affected by microbial activity and mineral reactions that could form methane or hydrogen sulfide. Hence, H₂ storage requires more stringent evaluation of caprock, fault, and wellbore integrity, alongside specific hydrogen sensing systems. It is concluded that depleted reservoirs in U.S. may support both applications, but reliable H₂ storage requires tailored site selection, monitoring, and risk management frameworks, which are significant to guide safer project design, limit leakage and gas losses, inform hydrogen-specific regulation and commercial use.

title: Closing the loop on Precision Fermentation: Recycling and Upcycling Spent Media and Biomass
summary: Precision fermentation (PF) offers a flexible method for producing high-value food ingredients, but it generates large volumes of spent media and microbial biomass, which pose environmental and economic challenges. This article explores str
content: Precision fermentation (PF) offers a flexible method for producing high-value food ingredients, but it generates large volumes of spent media and microbial biomass, which pose environmental and economic challenges. This article explores strategies for recycling spent media into fresh fermentation inputs and upcycling microbial biomass into food ingredients. Focusing on yeast and fungal fermentations, we examine case studies involving widely-used chassis strains. Case studies indicate that recycling can reduce wastewater emissions by 70% or more, and reduce operating cost by nearly 30%. Spent media contains valuable nutrients such as amino acids, organic acids, lipids, vitamins, and minerals, but also includes solids and growth inhibitors that must be removed or inactivated. While dilute biomolecules in spent media are unsuitable for food applications due to costly water removal, spent biomass shows promise for upcycling. Yeast and fungal biomasses are rich in proteins, lipids, micronutrients, bioactives, and structural polymers like mannoproteins, β-glucans, and fungal chitins. These materials can serve similar roles to brewing yeast derivatives, though they require stricter safety protocols and exhibit greater variability. The variability presents an unexplored landscape of opportunity for new flavours, structural ingredients (emulsifiers, gelling agents, etc.) and biofunctionality. Recycling and upcycling PF byproducts can deliver significant financial and environmental benefits that support the sustainable growth of the industry.

title: Composite energy geo-structures for building decarbonization
summary: Energy geo-structures (EGs) integrate heat-exchange loops into geotechnical structures to provide heating and cooling using shallow geothermal energy. However, the contribution of standalone EGs to building thermal demand may decrease in la
content: Energy geo-structures (EGs) integrate heat-exchange loops into geotechnical structures to provide heating and cooling using shallow geothermal energy. However, the contribution of standalone EGs to building thermal demand may decrease in large-scale applications and can be accompanied by seasonal ground thermal imbalance. To overcome the limitations of standalone EGs, a composite EG system integrating energy tunnels (ET), energy diaphragm walls (EDW), energy piles (EP), and boreholes (BHE) is proposed. A three-dimensional numerical model of a composite energy geo-structure system was established and evaluated against experimental or published benchmark data for the component subsystems. The model was used to investigate the short- and long-term thermal performance of the composite system. The results show that, despite localized reductions in the heat flux in length of EP and BHE, the composite EGs achieved a higher total heat exchange capacity—1.90, 2.70, 11.24, and 24.87 times greater than those of standalone ET, EDW, EP groups, and BHE arrays, respectively. Over the ten-year simulation, ET and EDW showed limited interannual variation, while the EP-BHE subsystem approached a repeatable seasonal response after the first complete annual cycle. Additionally, under the prescribed building-load conditions, circulating flow rate and soil thermal conductivity mainly altered the local ground-temperature field, whereas annual heat exchange was primarily determined by the imposed building demand and the COP-dependent ground-side load. Compared with coal-fired heating and electric air-conditioning under the same building load, the composite system reduced annual operational emissions by 49.80% (962.03 t CO 2 -eq), demonstrating its potential for efficient and low-carbon building thermal supply.

title: COP31 : The Climate Change Burden on Women and Children–From Vulnerability to Leadership and Action

title: A modified Sharpe framework incorporating carbon exposure
summary: This study proposes the Carbon Adjusted Standardized Sharpe Ratio (CASSR), which combines standardized Sharpe ratios and portfolio carbon exposure using parameters estimated from the feasible portfolio distribution. For Bitcoin, gold, and t
content: This study proposes the Carbon Adjusted Standardized Sharpe Ratio (CASSR), which combines standardized Sharpe ratios and portfolio carbon exposure using parameters estimated from the feasible portfolio distribution. For Bitcoin, gold, and the S&P 500, CASSR reduces calculated carbon exposure by 33.28% relative to Sharpe optimization, with a 3.51% reduction in the Sharpe ratio. The optimal allocation remains unchanged under the alternative emission estimates examined but varies with gold valuation and investment horizon. In a separate application to eleven S&P 500 sectors using a common carbon metric, CASSR reduces carbon exposure by 93.20%, with a 13.56% reduction in the Sharpe ratio. Moving-block bootstrap results indicate lower average portfolio carbon exposure under CASSR. Comparisons with alternative carbon-optimization approaches place the CASSR solution on both the carbon-efficient and mean-variance-carbon efficient frontiers. The findings are conditional on the selected investment universe and carbon-accounting assumptions.

title: Strategic Value Chain Analysis of Baiada Poultry: Enhancing the Industrial Value of Ross Breeders in South Australia
summary: The Australian poultry industry is undergoing a significant transformation driven by rising protein demand and stringent standards for animal welfare and biosecurity. As a market leader, Baiada Poultry plays a pivotal role in the upstream R
content: The Australian poultry industry is undergoing a significant transformation driven by rising protein demand and stringent standards for animal welfare and biosecurity. As a market leader, Baiada Poultry plays a pivotal role in the upstream Ross breeder sector in South Australia. This study evaluates Baiada’s strategic positioning and operational efficiency to identify how vertical integration and value chain optimization enhance industrial value. Using a descriptive qualitative case study approach, this research utilizes Value Chain Analysis (VCA) and SWOT analysis. Data were gathered through field observations at South Australian breeder facilities, in depth interviews with management, and comprehensive documentation of biosecurity protocols. The analysis reveals that Baiada’s robust vertical integration and adoption of automated climate-controlled housing significantly reduce operational costs while maximizing the genetic potential of Ross breeders. Strategic mapping places Baiada in a "Growth" quadrant, indicating that its internal strengths particularly in biosecurity and brand differentiation (e.g., Lilydale and Steggles) are well positioned to exploit market opportunities despite global feed price volatility. The study concludes that integrating technical biological excellence with adaptive strategic management is fundamental for sustaining competitive advantage and driving value creation in the international poultry landscape.

title: Melting ice of Antarctica, sustainable development & policies
summary: In this article, the author endeavors to explain the role of Antarctica in stabilizing sea ice & current, environmental protection and biodiversity in the polar region as well as in the global climate scenario. Due to global warming Antarct
content: In this article, the author endeavors to explain the role of Antarctica in stabilizing sea ice & current, environmental protection and biodiversity in the polar region as well as in the global climate scenario. Due to global warming Antarctica’s ice sheets are melting at higher rate which has alarmed the planet. The paper studied the causes of melting of Antarctica and its successive impacts on sustainable development goals, environmental damages, and existence of coastal regions of Antarctica and its habitats. The policies of saving Antarctica, sea level rise and discussions on relevant issues were also exemplified in this article lucidly.

title: Satellite Systems and Sensors: Foundations and Innovations for Sustainability Monitoring
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Satellite Earth Observation (EO) has become a cornerstone for planning, monitoring, and verifying sustainability policies under the 2030 Agenda, the Paris Agreement, the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, and the Convention on Bi
content: Satellite Earth Observation (EO) has become a cornerstone for planning, monitoring, and verifying sustainability policies under the 2030 Agenda, the Paris Agreement, the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, and the Convention on Biological Diversity. This chapter presents a design-to-indicator framework that links satellite mission architecture to the quantitative, auditable indicators needed for water, food, climate, ecosystems, and risk applications. EO is cast as an estimation problem in which geophysical state variables are inferred from multi-sensor measurements through explicit forward operators and error covariance, enabling rigorous treatment of Minimal Detectable Change (MDC), confidence intervals, latency, and spatio–temporal aggregation. We review space-segment choices (orbits, constellations, platform classes) and payload options (optical, thermal infrared, SAR, LiDAR, microwave radiometry, GNSS reflectometry, and emerging sensors) emphasizing their complementarity and information synergy. Ground-segment design, calibration and validation strategies, uncertainty propagation and quantification, and data-fusion and digital-twin approaches are discussed as integral parts of the mission. Four end-to-end case studies — irrigation and evapotranspiration, forest carbon, floods, and methane emissions — illustrate how specifically designed constellations and miniaturized sensors can be engineered to deliver robust indicators, traceable from the pixel to the policy decision.

title: High‐Throughput Design of Efficient Dual‐Atom Catalysts Anchored on C 2 N for Electroreduction of CO and NH 3 to Acetamide via Atomic Modeling and Machine Learning
summary: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic C–N coupling technology provides a new approach for green acetamide synthesis, which is achieved via direct reduction of carbon monoxide (CO) and ammonia (NH 3 ). However, efficient, stable catalysts urgently need
content: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic C–N coupling technology provides a new approach for green acetamide synthesis, which is achieved via direct reduction of carbon monoxide (CO) and ammonia (NH 3 ). However, efficient, stable catalysts urgently need to be developed, and their reaction mechanisms elucidated. In this study, density functional theory is employed to systematically screen a series of homonuclear (TM 2 ‐C 2 N) and heteronuclear (CuTM‐C 2 N) copper‐based transition metal (TM) dual‐atom catalysts (DACs). After comprehensively evaluating their stability, catalytic activity, and selectivity, five candidates with excellent performance are identified: Cu 2 –C 2 N, CuTi–C 2 N, CuV–C 2 N, CuCr–C 2 N, and CuMn–C 2 N. The limiting potential for acetamide synthesis over the DACs is linearly correlated with the Gibbs free‐energy change (Δ G ) of the *CO → *CHO step. Exploring the intrinsic relationships between the binding energies of different intermediates reveals a linear scaling relationship, indicating their correlation and potential to limit catalytic performance. The synergistic effect between heteronuclear TM pairs successfully overcomes this inherent limitation, significantly reducing the Gibbs free energy difference between the *CO and *CHO intermediates. Machine learning is adopted to explore the structure–activity relationship of the identified DACs, and the sure independence screening and sparsifying operator method is employed to construct a robust descriptor system, enabling accurate prediction of the maximum uphill Gibbs free‐energy change among the elementary steps of a given reaction pathway (Δ G max , eV). This study elucidates the reaction mechanism underlying the electrocatalytic synthesis of acetamide from CO and NH 3 , providing theoretical guidance for highly efficient DAC design.

title: IMPLEMENTAÇÃO DE DECLARAÇÕES AMBIENTAIS DE PRODUTO NO SETOR DA CONSTRUÇÃO CIVIL NA AMÉRICA LATINA: UMA REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA E CRÍTICA ORIENTADA À SUSTENTABILIDADE
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: Resumo: As Declarações Ambientais de Produto (EPD em inglês) vêm se destacando como instrumento para comunicação em sustentabilidade em diferentes setores.Este estudo se centra no cenário latino-americano, com o objetivo de analisar os desa
content: Resumo: As Declarações Ambientais de Produto (EPD em inglês) vêm se destacando como instrumento para comunicação em sustentabilidade em diferentes setores.Este estudo se centra no cenário latino-americano, com o objetivo de analisar os desafios associados ao desenvolvimento e à adoção de EPDs com foco no setor da construção civil.A metodologia estruturou-se em uma Revisão Sistemática da Literatura (RSL) realizada em março de 2026 nas bases Web of Science e Scopus aplicando o modelo PRISMA.De forma complementar, uma revisão documental sobre políticas e governança regional de operadores de programa de EPDs também serviu para complementar a análise crítica.Dos 831 documentos iniciais, apenas 56 artigos seguiram para a análise detalhada.Evidenciando-se que Brasil e México lideram o setor de EPDs na América Latina; no entanto, os números são limitados frente ao mercado europeu.Como fatores limitantes se destacam a escassez de bases de dados nacionais para apoiar o desenvolvimento das EPDs, desafios econômicos regionais diversos, o desconhecimento e capacidade técnica insuficiente e a baixa demanda de mercado por EPDs dentro da região-alvo.Também, a ausência de regulamentações que exijam as EPDs na contratação pública (ou de serviços públicos) foi um destaque.Superar essas limitações é fundamental para potencializar a competitividade e avançar na produção e consumo mais sustentáveis na América Latina.

title: Construcción modular en América Latina: desempeño, logística y sostenibilidad
summary: La construcción modular y la prefabricación fuera de obra trasladan actividades del cantero a entornos industriales con la promesa de reducir plazos, estabilizar la calidad y disminuir impactos ambientales; no obstante, su desempeño real en
content: La construcción modular y la prefabricación fuera de obra trasladan actividades del cantero a entornos industriales con la promesa de reducir plazos, estabilizar la calidad y disminuir impactos ambientales; no obstante, su desempeño real en América Latina está poco documentado. Esta revisión sistemática tuvo como objetivo sintetizar críticamente la evidencia sobre productividad, calidad, logística, seguridad, costos y desempeño ambiental, con énfasis regional. Conforme a PRISMA 2020, se analizaron 29 publicaciones (2006–agosto de 2026): nueve fuentes latinoamericanas y veinte estudios internacionales de contraste. Ante la heterogeneidad de sistemas y métricas, se aplicó una síntesis temática y configuracional, sin metaanálisis. Los resultados muestran ventajas consistentes en compresión del cronograma, control dimensional, reducción del trabajo húmedo y de residuos y menor exposición a riesgos en obra, pero no sustentan ahorros universales de costo ni de carbono, que dependen de la escala, el transporte y los límites del análisis. En la región, la adopción se concentra en experiencias aisladas de Brasil, Ecuador, Chile y Perú, y enfrenta fragmentación normativa, baja escala fabril, contratación tardía, restricciones de transporte y escasa trazabilidad. Se concluye que la vía más viable es una adopción gradual basada en plataformas de producto configurables, BIM, certificación de interfaces, compras por valor de ciclo de vida y redes regionales de manufactura. El estudio aporta un marco de condiciones habilitantes e indicadores comparables, transferible con cautela al Caribe y Centroamérica; sus limitaciones derivan de un corpus regional reducido y concentrado y de posibles sesgos de publicación.

title: AVALIAÇÃO ESTATÍSTICA DA QUALIDADE DO AR E CORRELAÇÃO ENTRE POLUENTES EM VOLTA REDONDA (RJ)
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A qualidade do ar destaca-se como uma das principais preocupações ambientais contemporâneas, devido aos seus impactos sobre a saúde humana e os ecossistemas.A poluição atmosférica é um problema urbano complexo, resultante da interação entre
content: A qualidade do ar destaca-se como uma das principais preocupações ambientais contemporâneas, devido aos seus impactos sobre a saúde humana e os ecossistemas.A poluição atmosférica é um problema urbano complexo, resultante da interação entre emissões de fontes fixas e móveis, transporte de poluentes, características topográficas e transformações físicoquímicas na atmosfera (Leoni; Sampaio; Corrêa, 2017).Nesse contexto, o monitoramento sistemático torna-se essencial para avaliar a exposição da população, identificar tendências temporais e verificar a eficácia das políticas de controle ambiental (Ministério do Meio Ambiente, 2019).Entre os principais poluentes regulamentados estão o monóxido de carbono (CO), dióxido de enxofre (SO₂), dióxido de nitrogênio (NO₂), ozônio (O₃) e partículas totais em suspensão (PTS), cujos limites são definidos pela Resolução CONAMA nº 03/1990 (Martins et al., 2017).A exposição a esses poluentes está associada a efeitos adversos à saúde, especialmente em áreas urbanas densamente povoadas (Liu et al., 2025; Šulc et al., 2022).O comportamento dos poluentes está relacionado à dinâmica urbana, industrial e às condições ambientais, sendo influenciado por fatores como uso do solo, crescimento urbano e atividades industriais (Zhao et al., 2022).Estudos também indicam que reduções nas emissões veiculares e industriais podem resultar em melhorias significativas na qualidade do ar (Srivastava, 2021; Nakada; Urban, 2020).Em regiões com forte presença industrial, a exposição prolongada a poluentes pode intensificar efeitos crônicos à saúde, reforçando a necessidade de monitoramento contínuo (Hrebniak; Fedorchenko, 2019).Nesse contexto, destaca-se o município de Volta Redonda (RJ), caracterizado por intensa atividade industrial, com destaque para a Companhia Siderúrgica Nacional (CSN), e elevada circulação de veículos, fatores que contribuem para a emissão de poluentes atmosféricos (Souza et al., 2019).Diante disso, este artigo tem como objetivo analisar estatisticamente as concentrações de SO₂, NO₂, CO, O₃ e PTS nas estações de monitoramento do INEA localizadas nos bairros Vila Santa Cecília, Retiro e Belmonte, no período de 2013 a 2022, por meio de estatísticas descritivas, análise temporal e avaliação das correlações entre os poluentes, com base nos limites estabelecidos pela Resolução CONAMA nº 03/1990.
